Make Her Stop!
I See Why You Humans Treasure Poetry
Feeding on Others' Gazes
Who Performs for Your Life

Why learn from humans when cats will do? You place Lady Becky before the crystalline being... the creature hesitates—but the cat is already rubbing against its ankles.
Light erupts where they touch, swirling through its mirror-like form—splintering, scattering like fireworks. Revelation, not in words, but in shared joy. The secrets of life, understood. Gratitude floods you.
When the glow fades, a second cat sits there—same breed as Lady Becky, but with different markings. They sniff each other, tails twitching in mutual curiosity.
And so you gain a new pet. It refuses to explain further, of course. You are but a foolish human, a servant to scoop its litter. It is the superior being now. The true ruler of this world. A very cute one.

You commanded Seliman to guard you as you studied the mirror-born creature—yet the crystalline form already reflected his face. Slowly, visions surfaced: the Consort’s visage, the Sultan’s face… As Seliman recoiled in dread, the creature drank them in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—forging itself anew. Hair, armor, weapons emerged, a human’s guise. Then a human’s voice: "Shall I learn his loyalty or his treachery? A pity—I excel at neither, nor do I care."
The newly shaped warrior laughed, brushing aside Seliman’s blade, and took position at your other flank—poised to guard or strike.

When the nameless swordsman met the mirror-born creature, his burning eyes became constellations in the reflection—merging with the crystal’s glow. You saw it then: the fall of his highland kingdom... royal blood overflowing, fire and ash beneath starlight... Drinking it all in, the creature forged a face of hard lines, armor of ornate steel—adorned like a man, and speaking like one:
"Ah, you wish me to play the grieving swordsman of a fallen realm? Don’t look so startled. The stars always insist on sharing their tales... and I don’t despise the role. Only pray you’re less tiresome than they are."

So this was the fabled monster that could mimic adventurers! Jabal's eyes gleamed with anticipation—what better sparring partner than a copy of himself? The mirror-like surface drank in his eager face, while the shimmering aura behind it shifted into deserts, battlefields, dense jungles... Feasting on these adventures, the creature began reshaping itself—muscles, armor, leather straps—arming itself like a man, speaking like one: "I've seen places no mirror has ever reflected. Fascinating. Human, you'd better deliver on these experiences... Shall we depart at once?"
Fortunately, Jabal welcomed all comers—be they rivals or allies.

The crystalline being laughed at Adila's wariness... It's surface warped like a carnival mirror, reflecting a grotesque Adila—twisting through the female warrior's stances in rapid succession: ferocity, then rage, anguish, helplessness, endurance, confusion... Drinking in these faces—perhaps even thoughts and memories—the creature reshaped itself. Hair, cloth, armor, and weapons emerged, arming itself as human do. Then came a human's voice:
"Like this female warrior... Hunting the grandest songs, challenging only the deadliest prey, laughing in fate's teeth... Yes, I begin to see."
The newly forged fighter crossed blades with Adila—steel kissing steel as they circled, arms weaving, eyes locked—until the creature found the perfect balance for the weapon's weight.

A pack of hunting dogs, large and small, circled the strange mirror-born creature, barking wildly... and within the creature's form, their reflections twisted—merging with Faris’ face... then swallowed whole, reforged into skin, fur, and armor. Adorned like a man, it spoke like one: "You mean to be like the man, not his dogs, yes? Though his soul is tangled too deep with theirs—hounds leading the hunter, not the hunter choosing their prey... Woof, I think I understand."
The newly shaped warrior crouched, letting the hounds lick and fawn over him—much to Faris’ chagrin.

Shama mistook it for some artful contraption meant to break a Extravagance Card. She tilted her head, studying, appraising… unaware her own reflection had begun to shift—the mirror warping, cracking, blooming: bodies tangled in different ways, dances to unheard music, pain and pleasure twisting together… The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice: "What a peculiar creature you are! Always full of surprises… Ah, and this gift." Even as it sculpted its face to match Shama’s tastes, the mirror-born thing drew something forth from its waist—long, crystalline… and when fear prickled your skin, it took shape at last: a sword.

This was the foul sorcery Gulis feared most—the wicked shamans of the tribes stealing souls through mirrors! He grumbled, yet pride kept him at your side. As if answering his curses, the mirror-born thing began shaping its form—lithe and powerful as Gullis himself... The creature stretched its slender frame, flesh still half-crystal, and in the reflection, Gullis' face twisted into an arrow—loosed straight through the warrior’s resolve. With stolen thoughts and memories, it forged armor, straps, a face, arming itself as men do, then spoke: "Patient as a hunter? I assure you, no hunter has a mirror’s patience." 
The newborn warrior took its place beside Gullis, who—with a wary glare—puffed out his chest in challenge.

You let these brigands test the mirror-born creature—they were expendable, after all. As if sensing your thoughts, the mirror twisted its greedy, ugly face... conjuring visions of gold and jewels tumbling within its crystalline form. Bewitched by the sight, [s2.name] raised weapon high, intent on shattering this mirror vessel of riches.
The creature drank in the greed, malice, and violence—forging itself in an instant: a swifter, crueler, deadlier thug.
With a brutal twist of [s2.name]'s arm, wrenching a pained groan from [s2.name]'s throat, the newly shaped warrior seemed pleased with what it had learned.

You let these brigands test the mirror-born creature—they were expendable, after all. As if sensing your thoughts, the mirror twisted its greedy, ugly face, conjuring visions of gold and jewels tumbling within its crystalline form. Bewitched by the sight, [s2.name] raised weapon high, intent on shattering this mirror vessel of riches.
The creature drank in the greed, malice, and violence—forging itself in an instant: a swifter, crueler, deadlier thug.
With a brutal twist of [s2.name]'s arm, wrenching a pained groan from [s2.name]'s throat, the newly shaped warrior seemed pleased with what it had learned.

The crystalline figure lifted its hand, extending it towards the girl, whose face was a mix of hidden fear and curiosity. Overwhelmed by fear, the girl squeezed her eyes shut and uttered a jumble of prayers from her homeland. In that moment, a faint beam of starlight pierced through the window, diving into the fluid form of the mirror. [s1.gender] seized it, shaping it into a flexible sword and wielding it delicately. With a persistence that had endured long past its prime, and a determination mingled with confusion, the figure reshaped itself. Hair, cloth, armor, and weapons emerged, arming itself as humans do, and releasing a soft sigh as humans would.
"So, innocent. So naive. And so powerless, attempting to wield such a meager power to protect anything... Heh, I understand now."
This newly shaped warrior walked towards you, passing by the flushed Anita, disregarding her futile attempt to appear intimidating.

Habib wondered why you had brought him before this crystalline figure. He studied its form—what bones lay beneath that luminous shell, what flesh gave it motion? What hue would its blood spill if cut? His musings, along with his shadow, seeped into the mirror’s depths... layer by layer, from within, shaping the mirror-born thing. As if something primal had been stirred, The creature let out a shuddering moan before slowly, almost gleefully, weaving itself garments like a man’s. Then it spoke, its voice uncannily human: "I have mirrored countless lives, yet today I learn what lies beneath their skin. Well done, mortal—you’ve roused my curiosity."

Iman accompanied you to meet the unnatural thing, and even he seemed drawn to the crystalline figure's beauty.
As he approached, his reflection shimmered within the mirror-born creature... twisting... dissolving... until only his scars remained—those sacred wounds offered to the Purist! Even healed, they still held divine power. Cracks spread across the flowing crystal, phantom scars turning real.The creature's sculpted composure faltered at last. In haste, a flesh-and-blood form burst from the fractured shell—panting, trembling, speaking now with human voice:
"It seems not all things can be learned through mirrors. Then I shall learn them in this body instead."

Alim circled the crystalline figure warily, eyeing the creature's bare, glowing form... What strange noble's bauble was this? [player.name]'s tastes grew stranger by the day... His shadow stretched long in the mirror, twisting like Dark Alley’s crooked paths, his face fracturing into many—robbed nobles, spared pups, turf-war thugs, sniveling street rats... The creature drank them in—faces, thoughts, memories—weaving hair, cloth, a visage... adorning itself as men do, then speaking in their tongue: "Ah, like this old thief? Skilled in survival, sticky-fingered yet clear-minded? Scorned by fools, hiding wisdom behind? I think I understand."
Alim scowled at this rogue—too much like himself—and slunk to your side, muttering curses under his breath.

Lumera reached out to touch the crystalline figure, each press of her fingers making tiny stars bloom within its flowing form... The starlight mirrored in her eyes, a glittering constellation... Drinking in this radiance, the creature shaped itself—human features, hair, garments—adorned now like flesh and blood, speaking as they do: "Like her? To be a true sage, disinterested in human yet enthralled by their hoarded knowledge... for she knows these truths already existed in the world—humans merely dragged them into the light. Yes. I shall be as she is."
Then the creature took Lumera's hand and led her to the study, where questions began to flow between them...

Had you not held her back, Mahir would have charged forth with her little hammer ready to strike. Her boisterous reflection swirled within the crystalline figure, morphing into gears, mechanisms, and Aetheric circuits... For a fleeting moment, these intricate parts assembled and whirred as if forming something entirely alien—until its host forcibly halted the transformation. The creature reshaped itself in human likeness and spoke with human irritation: "What madness dwells in this woman's mind! How bizarre... yet fascinating all the same."
You laughed and told it that most humans say the same.

Inal believed this to be mere maintenance of precious artifacts! The crystalline being played along, remaining motionless as a statue beneath her cloth... Each gleaming surface reflected Inal's movements—some bending low, some stretching tall, some humming forgotten melodies, others pouting at random thoughts drifting through her mind... Absorbing these expressions and forms, the creature began crafting features after her departure—cheeks, hair, garments - adorning itself in human fashion. Finally it spoke with human voice:
"Would you have me as meek and compliant as that child? Prepare for disappointment - her mind overflows with far more intriguing notions! To shackle precious things as servants... this reveals human's dull and detestable nature."

Badriyyah rejoiced in this wondrous being, circling the creature while chanting hymns to the hidden gods of her sect, seeking to stir dark tides within that chaotic mirror...
Phantoms of demons flickered in and out—each one grotesque and dull, unworthy of the mirror's approval. At last, all shadows were cast aside, leaving only the traces of Badriyyah's tattoos reflected in the glow, merging with the creature's radiance—Along those patterns, a thinking human was carved out, its form fixed, and it spoke with human tongue:
"Would you have the forsaken, the exiled powers claw at this world? A pity... they find no refuge in this mirror. Show me instead something of human."

As his fingers traced the ancient golden motifs in wonder, the crystalline mirror captured his visage—and in the flickering candlelight, visions arose: a once-fair homeland consumed by flames, countless treasures trampled into dust, fate itself torn asunder like fine silk. No artisan's hand, however deft at repairing gold and jade, could mend such a rending wound!
The mirror's essence absorbed these phantoms—perhaps even thoughts and memories—gradually fashioning itself: hair, features, pupils, until at last it opened human eyes and spoke in human tongue: "As vulgar as he, as opportunistic, and just as practiced in concealing his true nature... Tsk. Mortals—you would do well to devise fresh diversions for your guests."

Filled with sheer excitement, Asal hurried to examine your treasure, completely captivated by the crystal sculpture... He even retrieved his sketchbook and filled several pages with sketches, attempting to capture this otherworldly object.
As he immersed himself in his parchment, the crystalline surface reflected numerous words and pages, resembling a cocoon enveloping the shifting life within.
When Asal lifted his gaze once more, the creature of the mirror emerged from its cocoon! Countless words surged towards Asal, knocking the curious human unconscious. "You humans tend to record everything on paper, while only mirrors truly reflect the world's essence..." This newly shaped scholar picked up Asal's parchment, swiftly tearing out the pages filled with records.

You brought Maggie before the crystalline figure... Enthralled by its shimmering glow, she stepped closer, her hand reaching out unbidden.
The creature mirrored the gesture, their fingers intertwining with Maggie's. The light fractured like disturbed water at their touch, revealing countless faces swirling within its depths: Maggie laughing, Maggie weeping, Maggie raging, Maggie enduring, Maggie rejoicing... The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"Like your wife then? Like her love of verse and art? Like her mercy for every suffering soul? Like her... remarkable forbearance toward you? She is a most advantageous model, but I don't scorn your cunning. Human will be human." At first the voice was Maggie's own. Then it shifted—growing rasping, sardonic. You departed without gaining another wife. Part of you mourned while part of you was glad.

Nayla gazed greedily at the crystalline figure, lavishing praise upon its beauty and radiance. She pressed you with honeyed words, teased you with lingering touches—all to bend you to her will. Her hunger, her pride, her schemes... all reflected in the mirror's surface. The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"As insatiable as her? To understand human through such dull means..." Then it struck Nayla across the face, the very image of how she herself disciplined servants.

You brought Fardak before the luminous being of the mirror—its mercurial power stirred him, planting dangerous hopes in his heart... and his gaze, of course, was captured within that crystalline form.
As it moved, Fardak's face shifted within—hatred, hope, ambition, duty, fear... The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice: "Like this young man? Learning to bow low, hiding ambition, nursing grudges in silence... Is this how nobles play their game? How dull. I did not wake for such tedium. Pray your little schemes... make my tale worth telling."
Then the creature smoothed its expression, becoming as composed, quiet, and patient as Fardak himself.

You brought Qais before the crystalline figure, declaring him human's chosen envoy to this unknown being.
The honor struck him like a blow—the mirror drank in his flinching retreat, his terror, his shame, his stubborn pride... The mirror-being feasted on these expressions—thoughts and memories too, you'd wager—slowly shaping itself: hair uncoiling like vipers, silken fabrics slithering about its form, gold and gems blossoming like pox upon noble skin.
For one trembling moment, Qais found courage. He grasped [s1.gender]'s hand. "A wonder! I'll teach you our ways as a father—" The newborn noble struck like a scorpion, hand lashing out as its mouth twisted into Qais' own sneer, dripping venomous words.

You kicked Jawad toward the crystalline abomination, eager to witness its reaction—if it devoured him, no great loss; if it copied him, a hundred Jawads would still not trouble you...
The wretch nearly soiled himself in terror, yet the creature caught him with shimmering arms... Within its translucent form swirled Jawad's panicked visage—his greedy leer, his venomous spite, his groveling masks—all consumed. The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"You would have me become... this shamless one?" The first words dripped with disdain for its template. Already it refined itself—sculpting sharper cheekbones, a prouder bearing... yet kept Jawad's deft hands. "Ah, but these know their craft. See how they count coins and twist power... Very well. I understand."
Before you stood the perfect courtier—every treacherous instinct honed to razor's edge.

You summoned Fatuna to behold this wonder, and indeed, it ensnared her utterly. She circled the crystalline figure, studying every facet as her myriad reflections danced across its surface—the widow's solitude, the killer's detachment, the smoldering passion, the mother's longing... The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"Mother. Wife. Woman. How mortals love to cage themselves with masks—we mirrors know this dance well." With predatory grace, it glided between you, mirroring Fatuna's own poise—that perfect, terrifying composure that never cracks.

Imagine the fun of showing Jalila her true colors! You smooth-talk her into approaching the crystalline figure. Treating it as a mere prize, Her Majesty carefully appraises its beauty... until her own proud, discerning face stares right back from the surface.
The reflection twists and warps with shimmering light, yet stubbornly reforms itself each time... The creature drinks it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it speaks with a human voice.
"So even without mirrors, mortals find ways to hide behind the unreal body... You surprise me." With that, it snatches the whip from Jalila's stunned grasp, testing its weight with familiar ease...

You brought Raed the crystalline figure... She scoffed at noblemen's pretentious whims even as her fingers drummed against its glassy surface—until something in the reflection made her recoil.
The spiked club was already swinging when you grabbed her arm—only for another hand to seize the weapon's haft too. There stood a lordling, all grace and poise. What bizarre mirror had plucked from Raed's soul to forge such courtly bearing?

Out of curiosity, you brought Aziz—what could a slave laborer possibly show the mirror-creature?
When his calloused fingers brushed the crystalline form, the glass showed another man: younger, fairer, bedecked in jewels astride a charger, golden spear gleaming as he raced across the grasslands... In Aziz's stunned silence, The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice: "A clumsy metaphor. Must mortals always give before taking? Even looking-glasses know better—they take and give in equal measure. Still... your presentation amuses me. Do maintain this standard."
The vision of nobility stepped over Aziz's trembling form, walking to your side with grace.

You brought Zephyr to gaze upon the strange wonder... Oblivious to your purpose, he moved with exaggerated caution, terrified of damaging what appeared to be a priceless treasure. Unaware of how his face twisted and fractured in the crystal's depths—the woman who had sold him, the woman who would buy him, even one he himself would one day purchase, all shimmering among shards of light like scattered coins... Regret. Shame. Dread. The mirror-creature drank them all, savoring each flickering expression as it absorbed his changing visage, tasting the essence of his life... It slowly reshaped itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"Men believe fate is a circle, but I say fate is merely a mirror —which is why I differ from him. I shall be master of my own reflection." With the casual grace of highborn nobility, the creature reached out and patted Zephyr's head.

Amur thought this another dark ritual. Trembling, he approached the crystalline figure as you assured him—no bloodletting required, no incantations to chant.
Yet blood came all the same, a crimson tide surging within the glass, drowning his reflection—and in turn, reality betrayed him. An unseen force hauled him aloft like a drowning man, his body convulsing as he spewed liquid from his lungs like drowning... but it was blood that came, not water.
The faces of sacrificed girl emerged from the mirror, clawing at him, biting into him... Savoring this hatred, this curse, the creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice: "So this is the stuff of nobility. A most... instructive specimen." The last shards of mirror melted from its form. The visions, the blood-sea, the vengeful wraiths—and Amur's wretched life—vanished with them. Only a worthless corpse remained, collapsing to the ground.

The crystalline being studied the two identical versions of you... Within its form, countless more reflections shimmered and fractured, rippling like light upon water...
The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"Like you? Skilled at pretty words for powerful ears? Master of the art of calculated retreats? As cursed—and as blessed—as yourself? Or perhaps... convenient enough to play your double’s double? Is that too greedy of you?" It turned, examining its new form in another mirror. "I've barely awakened, and already mortals bore me. Let us hope your little game... makes my tale somewhat less tedious."
The last shifts of it stilled. Before you stood perfection—a flawless courtly noble, every inch as polished as [player.name].

To Jenna, human were but fixed texts—she could only add brief passages to adorn them.Until she met this crystal figure that could be reshaped freely.
Countless lines of faces, countless jewels, arms and hands of every fashion... The mirror-creature changed at her whim, until she grew faint with excitement. "So this is poetry? I knew nothing of its pleasures in the mirror... Today she taught me rhythm—it seems this 'life' may prove amusing after all." Shaped by this cadence, the poet adjusted its silks with careful hands, making them fit the tastes newly learned from Jenna.

You led Zaki to behold the mirror-creature. As their gazes met, Zaki's reflection twisted and shifted... So many possible futures! A mighty warrior, a rich merchant, a cunning courtier... all manner of great men... The creature drank it all in—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with a voice with human voice:
"Are your kind always so... hopeful? So endlessly hungry? Small wonder mirrors show only truth, while men spin fantasies from nothing. Let us hope what follows proves at least half as diverting as these pretty dreams."

One look at the mirror-creature, and Nabhani understood. He arched his back in a dancer's stance, sending ripples of color through the crystal.
Lust, war, poetry. The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with a voice with human voice:
"Like him, braiding both hair and words into intricate patterns? Like him, gazing at women with poetry in his eyes? Like him, willing to die for romance... I think I understand.”
Nabhani delighted in this praise, shouting for servants to bring wine so he might share a drink with this marvelous being whose beauty rivaled his own.

You took Junah to see that exquisite crystal figure... At first glance, she fell for its form, pressing close, kissing deep... Soon her reflection filled the crystal's surface, letting the mirror-creature consume it, refine it, slowly shaping features, hair and garments. It had human lips now, yet Junah choked its breath—not in flesh, but in the illusion, in the crystal's reflection of destructive desire... So between transformation and struggle, it claimed human form through lethal passion.
When the final shaping was done, the mirror-image faded, leaving it gasping... while Junah, overcome by that deadly ecstasy, lay unconscious in the new poet's arms.

You took Faraj to see the crystal figure... and the wondrous creature observed him in turn. Under his gaze, the reflections twisted and surged—first himself, then light, then fire, then you... Yet all these visions shattered one by one, ascending toward higher, more ethereal forms, until they nearly surpassed what the mirror could contain. At last, the mirror-creature abandoned its pursuit of his limits. Instead, it savored this elusive rhythm, slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice: "An ideal...? Never has such a thing appeared in the mirror-world. How curious. If you have the skill... then show me."

Your poet circled the glittering figure, spouting wild comparisons—the night sky, autumn lakes, moonlit seas of bioluminescence, a maiden's eyes... The glassy creature finally clapped a hand over his mouth, yet the words kept coming, alive and wriggling through its fingers into its translucent body! Like minnows, mice, songbirds, they darted madly through its mind... Slowly, color bloomed across its form—face, hair, garments shaped by poetry. When it finally spoke, every word carried rhythm: "Like this... poet? Ah, I see. Must I find art in worms writhing? See heaven through wine's haze? Very well. Since I'm awake now..."
With that, it sucked in its belly—Hassan's beer gut vanishing—and bowed with perfect grace.

Malkina took one look at the crystalline figure and immediately began conjuring visions of cosmetics and gowns. Her imaginings flooded into the mirror's surface, warping its form through endless contortions... Only when Malkina finally nodded in approval did the exhausted creature slump into a vaguely human shape, panting from the ordeal. "When can we do this again?" Malkina demanded, eyes gleaming with anticipation.

You bid [s2.name] face this unknown peril... and she hadn't beheld such treasures in ages. As her gaze drank in the crystal and its radiance, her reflection surfaced in the glass—along with all she'd lost: dignity, station, a father's love, gold, comforts, the power to bite others, unblemished hands... All shattered into fragments within that mirrored realm, scattering like shards of ice... The crystal figure drank deep of this essence, shaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice: "So this is human’s delight—savoring pain you need not endure. Madness and ruin too, perhaps. Is this what you'd have me harvest from her?"
The newly-fashioned poet reached out, brushing tears from the once-favored girl's cheek. With fresh-made tongue, it began to taste.

You led Salwiyah to behold the luminous crystal figure—she thought it merely another trinket for her collection! That greedy, eager face of hers was caught in the mirror... then fractured as you pulled her between flattery and scorn. The shards drew forth more faces from her depths—the admiration of others, their envy, their whispers, their longing, their hunger, their scheming... Like a yawning abyss, she contained nothing within, defining herself only by what she drew from those around her. Nourished by this hunger, the mirrored creature shaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke with human voice:
"Ah... It’s hard to find one's own reflection so repulsive. You've planted thoughts in me no being should harbor, mortal."

You brought Arzuna before the mirror-born creature, its crystalline form catching her fair features before stretching forth slender arms, swaying its waist—a silent invitation to dance. Phantoms shimmered in that eldritch glow: candlelit trysts, silken veils drawn aside, glories beyond counting, sorrows too deep for tears... The creature drank it all in—faces, perhaps even thoughts and memories—slowly reshaping itself. Hair, cloth, gold, and gems adorned it, and it spoke human voice: "All dances demand their songs... Tell me, does the tale that woke me merit singing?"
And so the wondrous creature lived on, forever in the form of a cat... Perhaps the best outcome? At least it is clever, sweet, and never leaves your side.

5000303.title: Your name
strings: Your name
You have awakened this ancient being from its long slumber, shaped it in form. Now it demands something deeper... something of the soul.
Does the Mirror reveal your true face?
Or do you decide what the Mirror shows?
Some things may be helpful in crisis
This is a battle of wills. The loser becomes the other's slave.
Resist the Mirror-Dweller's dominion!
The number of dice provided by your Wisdom and Magic is affected by the opponent's Charisma and Magic.
You need at least 4 Success to resist the dominion.
It Begins to Reweave Reality
You're Free of the Game...
You Dragged It into Chaotic Fate
It Demands a Duel
You Claimed the Trophy
Let It Lecture……
You Followed the Truth
Subdued by Wisdom
It Stands Above You...
"Be my servant, [player.name]."
You Think You’re More Awful than Sultan?

Humans do not perceive the world as it is, but glimpse its truth through songs, poems, and written words. Just as a magical mirror may twist the images it reflects, so too does this poet from beyond the mirror now ensnare minds in new ways...
The creature conjured from the azure glow an instrument you had never seen—some mixed or refined instrument of mortal craftsmanship. Then it began to play, and to sing... a song of you, from the hour of your birth...

So your life was rewoven—now you were the poet's childhood friend! Together you vowed to wander distant lands, to behold the wonders of foreign realms... For this shared dream, you'd sell your estates and servants, cast off burdensome kin and titles... These duties, these thoughts, were all stitched into your mind with the music. And as the melody played, those dark threads—the Sultan's Game's curse—loosened their grip, no longer binding your fate.
More and more souls, drawn by the song, came to your courtyard. They embraced this tale, offering gifts and blessings for your journey...

The music began unraveling the tale of your life, thread by thread, weaving its own strands into the fabric... You were the poet's childhood friend! Together you vowed to wander distant lands, to behold the wonders of foreign realms... For this shared dream, you'd sell your estates and servants, cast off burdensome kin and titles...
Wait—no! You fought back in your mind. Shattered memories and truths clashed, a storm of broken threads as the music grew shrill, desperate to tear fate itself apart—until the darkest, most unyielding strands ensnared the intruder. The Sultan's Game's curse, the fate you could never escape, now coiled around the mirror-poet like a noose... The creature shrieked, cursing the treachery of black magic—but you knew the truth. The Sultan's Game—no, your game—had claimed another piece.
Now, name the creature. Like the wise who bind demons with their true names, make it yours to command.

For reasons unknown, you cannot refuse this challenge— the creature must have struck something deeper within you... With every clash of steel, your spirits and wills collide, seeping into one another...

At last, your weapon slipped from your grasp as something pierced your heart, plunging you into darkness.
When the world righted itself, your childhood sparring partner hauled you upright—the five-hundredth bout between you, still evenly matched... But none of that mattered now. You had sworn to wander distant lands together, to behold the wonders of foreign realms... For this shared dream, you'd sell your estates and servants, cast off burdensome kin and titles... Even the Sultan's Game—every memory and curse that might shackle you—had died in that final duel. Now reborn, you stood unshackled.

The creatue struck not at the flaws in your technique, but the chinks in your soul! Each move that bound you twisted not just your limbs, but your very thoughts and memories.
Countless shadows rose in your mind—visions of past duels, battles fought side by side... No more. You ceased matching your opponent's rhythm, feigned imbalance, left your heart deliberately exposed—and the creature lunged greedily for the killing blow... only to impale itself upon your blade.
The world shattered like a mirror. No blood spilled, no steel drawn—yet the warrior born of reflections lay panting at your feet.
Now, name the creature. Like the wise who bind demons with their true names, make it yours to command.

Most people cannot discern truth, they follow only authority. Yet this sage before you now casts an authoritative glow upon your very soul... Through the creature's words, you transcend the mundane, wandering the sacred realms of spirit and wisdom...

Epiphany and enlightenment... Those rare sparks of wisdom that once flickered only in your darkest nights now blaze like festival fireworks. What joy—to know truth at last. What freedom—to hold the key to transcendence.
When this sage begins to walk, you follow without hesitation—you will traverse mountains and rivers with it, spreading it's wisdom across the realms of huhuman! More and more hear it's words, kneeling to offer gold and treasures, or their very selves to join your growing host...

Epiphany and enlightenment... Those rare sparks of wisdom that once flickered only in your darkest nights now blaze like festival fireworks. What joy—to know truth at last. What freedom—to hold the key to transcendence. Then, like a foul stench, the taint within you seeps forth—taint left by the Sultan’s games and curses, like nails piercing the bubble of your ecstasy, defiling this sacred moment.
When the illusion shatters, you see the truth: the one before you merely parrots old platitudes, a mirror with no substance of its own. With your wisdom, you dismantle its words with ease, each victory dimming their light further... Until, like a defeated monster, the mirrored creature kneels—subdued. Now, name the creature. Like the wise who bind demons with their true names, make it yours to command.

You tell the mirror-creature that mere adornments do not make a noble—a noble requires an unbroken lineage, deeds of inheritance, titles recognized by the crown... And as you speak, the truth dawns upon you: is not the one before you a scion of an ancient royal bloodline? Its lands are vast and fertile, its rule was just and wise—even the Sultan dares not trespass upon its domain...

Yes, what a glorious realm it is... A sanctuary where you may thrive, your talents unshackled, your days filled with honor and peace—no more cowering in fear! Damn the Sultan’s game! Renounce him truly, and the curse of his dominion will shatter like glass. More and more are drawn to this lord’s renown, trailing in your wake, weeping, begging—offering all they possess just to earn a place at its side, to reach that distant paradise...

The creature must have forgotten who you are! You are [player.name], the one who dared defy even the Sultan! True power and tyrants could not cow you—what then are hollow titles and forged grandeur? You laugh at the folly before you, and with your mockery, something dims within the mirrored creature. The sound of shattering glass echoes in the void... Like the heroes of old who bound demons with wit alone, you have unraveled its deceit. Now, seal its fate with a name!

When people gaze upon this enchanting artist, their minds recall its works... But only you see the truth—the flickering light between illusion and reality, shimmering amidst the flowing melodies and exquisite makeup.

When people gaze upon this mighty warrior, their minds recall its valor and deeds... But only you see the truth—the flickering light between illusion and reality, shimmering amidst the sinew and steel.

When people gaze upon this solemn sage, their minds recall its words and tomes... But only you see the truth—the flickering light between illusion and reality, shimmering amidst the knowing eyes and gilded scrolls.

When people gaze upon this noble lord, their minds recall its power, lands, and gold... But only you see the truth—the flickering light between illusion and reality, shimmering amidst the stern face and rich adornments.

5000304.title: Mirror a Man
strings: Mirror a Man
[xiaochou.name] wishes for you to introduce one of the male lovers you’ve spoken of before—it has questions about desire, and it seeks his perspective.
The Mirror
Your male lover
Only a man with Passion will suffice
This one might offer most intriguing reference points.
This one is merely among the masses of ordinary.
Wound of Sin
He is Just a Kid
Faraj’s Type?
Certainly, Shama Counts as a Man

Iman’s gaze lingers between you and [xiaochou.name] for a moment before he kneels opposite you, lifting a cup of jasmine tea to his lips.
"Desire is sin," he murmurs, as if already knowing [xiaochou.name]’s unspoken question. "Greed is sin. dishonesty is sin. Indulgence is sin. Even... existence itself is sin." His head bows slightly, lips moving in silent prayer. There is more he might say, but the words remain unspoken. With a deferential nod, he rises—only then do you see it: a wound, split open along his spine.
And only now does [xiaochou.name] whisper in confusion, "Why is his wound... pure white?"

At first, Qais seemed utterly bewildered—how could he not recall a close friend like [xiaochou.name]? But soon, his expression grew distant, and then he was chatting eagerly with [xiaochou.name], as if reuniting with an old friend.
After a torrent of hollow talk—ideals, realm, politics—[xiaochou.name] abruptly shifted the tide: "What do you think of desire? What kind of partner do you most enjoy indulging with?"
You stiffened. Such a question was far too brazen for Qais—yet what stunned you more was how casually he answered.
"Of course, a kindred spirit... Better yet, a learned beauty. She must understand me, support me, share noble aspirations... and have ample bosom."
Even he froze then, as if startled by his own words. Was this truly what lay in his heart?
Once the unsettled guest had departed, [xiaochou.name] turned to you with a knowing blink. "Pitiful creature," [xiaochou.name] scoffed, disdain dripping. "His flesh is whole, but his heart? Hollowed by darkness, twisted beyond his own recognition."

"Man or woman?" Zaki didn't care when you'd gained a friend to share such intimate topics with. After only a moment's confusion, he laughed again, carefree. "As long as it brings joy, does it matter?"
Because he was young, he didn’t understand the cost of pleasure or responsibility. You shrugged, indifferent, while [xiaochou.name] shot you a glance and remarked, not without edge:"Some men never grow up."

As you settled into the cushions and met those eyes fixed unwaveringly on you, you did something rare—you reached for [xiaochou.name], shaking your head at it.
[xiaochou.name]’s gaze flickered between you and him, then curved into a knowing, mocking smile.
Faraj, baffled but ever the gracious host, dutifully steered the conversation, filling the room with warmth. You played your part too, tossing in opinions, waxing eloquent. Only the mirror knew—only the mirror saw your cowardice. You didn’t want to know. You didn’t dare learn what kind of heart lay beneath that thick, amber-honeyed crust.

After receiving your invitation, this beautiful nobleman went out of his way to don a suit of men's attire, swept his lush hair back, and swapped his sweet incense for the cologne favored by aristocratic men. He likely assumed you were planning a game of a different sort, so when his gaze fell upon the third person in the room—[xiaochou.name]—he paused, if only for a fleeting moment.
Under [xiaochou.name]'s watchful eye, Shama swiftly dismissed the slight oddity... With a graceful smile, he bowed to you both, and soon you were gathered around the hookah and goblets, deep in conversation.
[xiaochou.name] politely inquired about Shama's views on desire, and Shama, as if prepared for the question, spoke with eloquence.
"I excel at indulging desires, so your question is quite apt... In my opinion, sex is the dullest of affairs. Imagine if men were stripped of their faces, bodies, attire, and jewels—reduced to nothing but walking with, well... cocks. Where’s the fun in that? Who’d even want to bed them? Sex is merely a doorway, a means to explore oneself. Oh, just a door! And what lies beyond... well, that’s a treasure to be uncovered slowly..."
The words left you baffled, but [xiaochou.name] seemed thoroughly pleased.

After a few cups of wine, [xiaochou.name] steered the conversation toward "the desires of men." [s2.name] vividly described his myriad fantasies, even confessing to the inappropriate objects of his longing...
Had these words been recorded and spread, they would have dealt a heavy blow to [s2.name]'s reputation. He was not usually one to speak recklessly, and today’s indiscretion could only be blamed on [xiaochou.name], who had been egging him on.
Your revelry lasted until midnight. [s2.name] departed with a hint of unease, as if struggling to recall what he had said. As for [xiaochou.name]... "Humans are so tedious." The creature found it all rather dull.
Gazing into the Mirror

The next day—you cast a casual glance at the ancient silver mirror hanging in your hallway, its surface worn by time, once capable of reflecting only faint, ghostly shapes. But now, the figure in the mirror stares back at you with unsettling clarity. A shiver runs down your spine as you realize it must be [s1.name]. It offers you an inscrutable smile, then, in the blink of an eye, the mirror reverts to its usual state—as if it were nothing but a trick of the light.

[s1.name] joined the little gathering you had arranged—perhaps due to the magic, but in any case, Maggie voiced no objections to the guest's sudden appearance. Not even when [s1.name] bluntly asked what kind of person she fancied did Maggie take offense.
"You ask too late, don't you think?" She chuckled behind her hand. "I already have a husband now."
Even [s1.name] could pry no further from her. You couldn't say whether you were satisfied or disappointed.

Badriyyah had no qualms about sharing her answer! With a giggle, she told [s1.name] that desire was simply a path to pleasure—nothing more.
"Men are fine, of course, but in this world, if you rely entirely on them for anything, you’re in for trouble!" She winked at you both. "We have our own ways of finding delight."
She prattled on and on, still brimming with words even as she took her leave.

"Oh, I do adore men," Nayla answered without hesitation after hearing [xiaochou.name]'s words. With elegant fingers, she plucked a nutty mille-feuille from the table, a sweet smile curling at her lips. "Men are utterly delightful—each has his own... delicious qualities."
She eagerly shared her extensive expertise on the subject with [xiaochou.name], her insights so thorough they left even you wide-eyed, feeling thoroughly outmatched.

At [xiaochou.name]'s question, Fatuna’s usual composure seemed to crack ever so slightly.
"Once, I too had unrealistic expectations of a partner—love, loyalty, and such..." She lifted her teacup, blowing away the rising steam before speaking plainly. "Desire, marriage—they’re merely tools, nothing more."

Upon learning that the woman you recommended had once worked in the House of Delights, [xiaochou.name] resolved to "see" her answer firsthand—for a mirror, even under its own magic, could never be trusted with words shaped by throats and tongues.
As the wine blurred Junah’s eyes into a glistening haze, the Mirror itsef finally glimpsed Junah’s past through her small, fragile "mirrors"...
The nights steeped in debauchery, the swaying bed curtains, the sheen of exhausted sweat, the fading bruises layered anew, and, occasionally, tears for unknown reasons...
Too many fragments folded into the reflection of her gaze. And the longer the Mirror stared back, the deeper the disappointment in humanity grew. In the end, [xiaochou.name] looked away.

Upon learning that the woman you recommended had once worked in the House of Delights, [xiaochou.name] resolved to "see" her answer firsthand—for a mirror, even under its own magic, could never be trusted with words shaped by throats and tongues.
Luckily, Jalila’s chambers, much like her former "workshop," were lined with countless mirrors. [xiaochou.name] moved freely among them, watching. It observed bare flesh, glistening fluids, skin pulled taut—night after sleepless night (Jalila was diligent; she worked until dawn). Rarely did the Mirror witness true "sexual intercourse”. Instead, it bore resemblance to the tortures the Mirror had idly glimpsed elsewhere...
Could pain and desire entwined brew an intoxicant? [xiaochou.name] felt, indeed, a sharper insight into humanity.

Upon learning of Shama’s origins, [xiaochou.name] remained pensive—until the moment it finally met her and posed a question you’d never considered:
"You were born noble. So why did you become a Lady of Delights?"
Shama paused, then smiled faintly. In her mirror-bright eyes, [xiaochou.name] glimpsed her past—and her answer.
Her chamber in the House of Delights was unique: perfumed with rare incense, adorned with poetry and wit, all artfully disguising the monotony of copulation. Naturally, men cared little for such things unless bedding was the goal.
And like these refinements, her male organ was the cherry atop the cake. With the guests’ tacit consent—even anticipation—she wielded it, embracing it as part of her nature. Only here, in the House of Delights, was she accepted as both man and woman.

[xiaochou.name] was taken aback by your decision to bring your sister along—so much so that it discarded the questions prepared in advance. It glanced between your face and Arzuna’s, so eerily alike, before finally asking Arzuna why she desired you.
After a brief pause, Arzuna turned to you: "You may not know this, [player.name], but since childhood, I was taught to watch you—your blood is my blood, your face mirrors mine, yet our fates could not be more different. Observing you was like gazing into a mirror only to find it had come alive. Some would flee from such a sight. Others would pretend not to see. But I... I was the one drawn to the spectacle."
[xiaochou.name] studied her for a long moment, then gave a slow, thoughtful nod.

"Where does desire come from? Is it truly so hard to grasp?" Mahir needed no prompting from [s1.name]—she answered with blunt honesty, if anything baffled by the question itself. "A poet must recite their verses. An actor craves an audience. Shouldn’t I test the fruits of my own labor? How else would I spot flaws, refine designs, or draw fresh inspiration? Ah, speaking of which—" She clapped your thigh, then thumped her chest in earnest assurance. "I’m already gathering data. When the upgraded Rod of Life is ready, you’ll be the first to know, mark my words!"
You had absolutely no interest in this!!!

At your summons, Inal crept forward and knelt, trembling—more timid, more dull than she had ever been as Maggie’s slave.
You signaled [s1.name] to proceed, and so [s1.name] posed the prepared question: "What do you think of desire?"
Inal froze, then pressed her forehead to the floor. "It is for Master [player.name] to decide." Her voice quivered. "To fulfill... to fulfill your wishes is my duty."
Of course—she was your newest concubine. You nodded, satisfied, and turned to [s1.name]. Meeting your gaze, it’s expression darkened. In that moment, it saw clearly how one soul could be utterly plundered by another.

At the mention of Salwiyah’s name, [s1.name] let out a knowing sound. "I know her. She spends more time before a mirror than anyone I’ve ever met."
It then recounted how closely it had observed the girl’s dazzling beauty: the way she practiced expressions before the glass, lingering over each as if selecting the most alluring, the most beguiling. She fussed endlessly with that single lock of hair at her brow—arranging it to seem artlessly fallen, yet perfectly placed to shadow her forehead, contour her cheeks, and deepen the violet of her eyes.
[s1.name] relished the memory, for it was the first time the Mirror had pondered that strange, unsettling quality Salwiyah exuded: a pure, unadulterated desire, honed into a weapon, a shield, a venom.
Finally, [s1.name] declared, "You won’t keep her." Well... fine. Even if you bristled at the thought, there was no arguing it aloud.

After a few cups of wine, [xiaochou.name] steered the conversation toward "the desires of men." [s2.name] shyly described her myriad fantasies, even confessing to the inappropriate objects of her longing and tricks...
Had these words been recorded and spread, they would have dealt a heavy blow to [s2.name]'s reputation. She was not usually one to speak recklessly, and today’s indiscretion could only be blamed on [xiaochou.name], who had been egging her on.
Your revelry lasted until midnight. [s2.name] departed with a hint of unease, as if struggling to recall what she had said. As for [xiaochou.name]... "Humans are so tedious." The creature found it all rather dull.
Gazing into the Mirror

The next day—you cast a casual glance at the ancient silver mirror hanging in your hallway, its surface worn by time, once capable of reflecting only faint, ghostly shapes. But now, the figure in the mirror stares back at you with unsettling clarity. A shiver runs down your spine as you realize it must be [s1.name]. It offers you an inscrutable smile, then, in the blink of an eye, the mirror reverts to its usual state—as if it were nothing but a trick of the light.

5000306.title: See a noble
strings: See a noble
[xiaochou.name] wishes for you to introduce one of the noble lovers you’ve spoken of before—it has questions about desire, and it seeks his perspective.
The Mirror
Your noble lover
Only a noble with Passion will suffice

[s1.name] joined the little gathering you had arranged—perhaps due to the magic, but in any case, Maggie voiced no objections to the guest's sudden appearance. Even when [s1.name] bluntly asked her thoughts on power and desire, she took no offense. Instead, she smiled—at you: "Did [player.name] put you up to this?"
Without waiting for an answer, she continued, "Men love to complicate simple things, give them strange names, then claim women don't understand. But is that really so?"
"Take us, for example. Perhaps—just perhaps—my marriage began as a union of convenience, a merging of houses for mutual gain. But what has carried us to this day? Could it be anything other than the two of us?"
You broke into a cold sweat, as if you'd dare say no.

Iman’s gaze lingers between you and [xiaochou.name] for a moment before he kneels opposite you, lifting a cup of jasmine tea to his lips. When [xiaochou.name] posed the question of power and desire, he paused briefly, then offered his answer.
"What is forbidden only grows stronger. That is where sin takes root." His eyes flicked toward you, cool and knowing. A light too bright repels some while drawing others—he understood the logic well, just as he was not blind to your deliberate closeness, your tainted hunger.
But, as he himself had said—was his desire for you any purer?

"Oh! Is that so?" After hearing [s1.name]’s question about "power and desire," Nayla twirled a lock of her pretty curls around her finger, pausing—uncharacteristically—to think. But soon, she shrugged it off with a careless laugh. "I’ve met plenty of men who groveled at my feet. If they pleased me, I rewarded them. If they displeased me... well, who did they think they were?" She spun tales of these men without hesitation, much to [xiaochou.name]’s amusement.
Clearly, in her eyes, such lowly creatures could never threaten her lofty station—not even for a moment. What a vain, foolish woman.

At first, Qais seemed utterly bewildered—how could he not recall a close friend like [xiaochou.name]? But soon, his expression grew distant, and then he was chatting eagerly with [xiaochou.name], as if reuniting with an old friend.
After a torrent of hollow talk—ideals, realm, politics—[xiaochou.name] abruptly shifted the tide: "What do you think of desire? Some say it’s tied to power."
"I disagree," Qais dismissed the idea without hesitation. "Otherwise, wouldn’t the Sultan be the most desired man in the land?"
Well... you had no idea how to respond. Gais, too, seemed to realize his blunder. The gathering ended awkwardly in the sudden chill, with only [xiaochou.name] thoroughly pleased. Mirrors do love secrets.

At [xiaochou.name]'s question, Fatuna’s usual composure seemed to crack ever so slightly.
"I see no issue with it," she said, lifting her teacup to gently blow away the rising steam. "Those with power inevitably relish its privileges, while those without naturally gravitate toward it, offering tribute in exchange for protection. It’s not just desire—this is how the world turns."

Zaki could hardly be called "powerful" in your presence. The overly young boy had tasted desire, but the "world of adults" remained far beyond his grasp.
Soon, [xiaochou.name] lost interest, and discontentedly believe that you were merely humoring it.

The moment "power" was mentioned, Mahir’s eyes flashed.
"Power ruins everything—it’s like an impurity left in a flask, tainting whatever it touches!" She wrinkled her nose in disgust. "Fathers push you to marry, mothers force you to learn household rule—every parent shoves their children into molds carved by their fathers, all for the sake of a name and a sliver of power. Like pots fired by a potter. So dull! So dull!"
Her sudden outburst had [xiaochou.name] nodding fervently, seizing her hand as if it found a kindred spirit...

You settled onto the cushions, sharing wine and idle chatter, drifting through trivial matters. Under [s1.name]’s guidance, the conversation soon turned to desire and power.
Faraj had little passion for power—otherwise, he wouldn’t have acted more like a humble servant in your presence. He refilled your empty cup before speaking. "The other day, my father sent another letter urging me to return home."
Faraj had never complained of such things to you before. You straightened, listening intently.
"He’s grown old, always insisting I take over the family business, inherit the lands—not ‘waste time’ trailing after [player.name]. But I told him, no man’s effort, however tenfold, could match serving a wise master. They call me mad. I say they don’t understand."
When he looked at you, his eyes held that familiar, eager need for approval. Without thinking, you clapped his shoulder. No more words were needed.
As for [xiaochou.name]… watched it all, thoughtful.
Gazing into the Mirror

The next day—you cast a casual glance at the ancient silver mirror hanging in your hallway, its surface worn by time, once capable of reflecting only faint, ghostly shapes. But now, the figure in the mirror stares back at you with unsettling clarity. A shiver runs down your spine as you realize it must be [s1.name]. It offers you an inscrutable smile, then, in the blink of an eye, the mirror reverts to its usual state—as if it were nothing but a trick of the light.

5000307.title: Desire and Love
strings: Desire and Love
Love is the most perplexing thing of all to [xiaochou.name]! It wishes to meet the one you love, for it has many questions to ask!
The Mirror
The one you love
Only a character with Passion and Bond of Fate will suffice
Never Fall in Love with Clients

[s1.name] joined the little gathering you had arranged—perhaps due to the magic, but in any case, Maggie voiced no objections to the guest's sudden appearance. At last, [s1.name] cautiously voiced the confusion about love, and Maggie, after a moment's thought, sighed and said, "Love is a glass bead that resembles a gem—or a gem that resembles a glass bead. At times it is noble, at times cheap. You cradle it carefully, yet cannot help but doubt its worth. Still, you strive to protect it, driving away thieves who would steal it and brutes who would shatter it... You have no choice, for it is there, yours, a part of you."
You gently drew Maggie into your embrace, letting her lean against your chest. Now you had no mind to spare for what [xiaochou.name] might think.

Iman’s gaze lingers between you and [xiaochou.name] for a moment before he kneels opposite you, lifting a cup of jasmine tea to his lips. In the soft silence, [xiaochou.name] asked him about love.
Iman frowned slightly, lowering his eyes to the drifting petals in the teacup, then slowly offered an answer: "Love is pain," the devotee of the Immaculate Purity mused, "but not like the pain of prayer."
"But if it is pain, why do people seek it?" [xiaochou.name] pressed, bewildered.
"Because it is not a choice."

"Love?!" Under [xiaochou.name]'s impassive gaze, Badriyyah burst into laughter, even knocking over the pastries on the tea tray onto the carpet. "Oh, apologies, apologies!" She wiped tears from the corners of her eyes and turned to you. "Where did you find such a naive friend? Listen, love doesn’t exist at all!"
She picked up a nut biscuit, popped it into her mouth with a careless shrug, and tapped [xiaochou.name]’s furrowed brow with her other hand. "Life is full of troubles—so many that one might wish for death, no? To convince yourself to keepBadriyyah living, you must tell yourself you still love this world, that someone in it loves you. What else can you do?"
[xiaochou.name] grew even more perplexed. "If the reason to live is a lie, then why live at all?" "Now you’re asking the right person! Listen—"
Badriyyah launched into her usual tirade about death being the end of toil, but you swiftly stuffed a dainty yet choking pastry into her mouth—lest she accidentally convert [xiaochou.name] into a cultist!

"Oh, of course I love [player.name]—he’s the most adorable person in the world." After hearing [xiaochou.name]'s words, Nayla didn’t hesitate to loop an arm around your neck and plant a firm kiss on your cheek.
You wiped the lipstick from your face with a scowl, reproaching her for her lack of seriousness. Nayla giggled, daintily picking up a nutty mille-feuille from the table, her lips curling into a sweet smile. "See, love is just like this. It’s a lie… or maybe there’s a tiny bit—just this much—truth hidden in it. What do you think?"
She winked at you, beautiful as an ever-elusive riddle.

At first, Qais seemed utterly bewildered—how could he not recall a close friend like [xiaochou.name]? But soon, his expression grew distant, and then he was chatting eagerly with [xiaochou.name], as if reuniting with an old friend.
After a torrent of hollow talk—ideals, realm, politics—[xiaochou.name] abruptly shifted the tide: "What do you think of love?
To your surprise, Qais tilted his head in profound confusion, as if the word held no meaning for him. "Perhaps you mean... respect? Admiration? Or...?" His voice trailed off, growing strangely faint. You watched as something swiftly darkened his pupils into an abyssal black. Then, in an eerie, fervent tone, he declared with absolute certainty, "—I love you."
[xiaochou.name] gave a pitying shake of its head and remarked, flat and without judgment, "You've ruined him."

At [xiaochou.name]'s question, a crack appeared in Fatuna’s ever-composed demeanor, and she blurted out, "But that’s a child’s game."
She stared at you in disbelief, as if unable to fathom you calling her "beloved," forcing her to reassess what lay between you. In her eyes, you caught a fleeting glimpse of guilt, hesitation, or something even heavier… but none of that so-called "love." Her head bowed in silent resentment—why had fate not let you meet sooner?

Zaki didn’t care in the slightest when you’d gained a friend to share such intimate matters with. Without hesitation, he nodded: "Love? Of course I—" His voice abruptly faltered. Under [xiaochou.name]’s piercing gaze, he suddenly couldn’t recall how to pronounce the word. Frantically, he racked his brain—why did the more he thought of it, the more alien it became?
The Mirror withdrew its gaze in disappointment—it had seen, yes, it had seen Zaki utter that word so many times, to so many people. But in truth, the boy’s heart had no idea what it meant.

[xiaochou.name] could hardly believe your beloved was the lowliest of Lady of Delights. It studied Junah with deep suspicion, asking: "What do you know of love?"
Junah lowered her head shyly, unwilling to reveal the longing in her eyes. "It is the most precious thing in the world," she murmured, utterly certain.
[s1.name]’s brow furrowed as it stared intently at Junah, eyes gleaming with an eerie light—it saw behind her the frail sapling of fate, the tangled branches all leading to the same withering end. Only here, did Junah stand like a fresh bloom.
"I will watch," [s1.name] ground out through clenched teeth, the words forced and jagged, twisting its expression into something almost savage. "I will watch how this ends for you.”

[xiaochou.name] could hardly believe your beloved was a Lady of Delights—it even deepened its doubts about the very definition of "love."
And Jalila’s answer only confirmed its suspicions. "Love is nothing but dead weight," she said. "Of course we tell clients we love them, but we don’t believe it—because if you do, you’re finished. Your body, your emotions, your life, your work… everything you are will be ruined, and then you’ll have no choice but to die."
Her tone was detached yet sorrowful, as if she’d witnessed countless such tragedies firsthand. And you—you couldn’t prove you were the exception. But at least, once you left this room, once the magic faded, you and Jalila could pretend these words had never been spoken.

[xiaochou.name] could hardly believe your beloved was a fallen Lady of Delights. [s1.gender]It studied Shama with deep suspicions2.name], asking: "What do you think of love?"
Shama paused, then answered coolly, as if detached from the matter. "Love... Oh, it exists, of course. But it comes with conditions—you must fit the other’s tastes and expectations."
Seeing the gravity in [xiaochou.name]’s expression, Shama pursed her lips and added with practiced ease, "—Which is why every Lady of Delights knows how to please her clients." With elegant, practiced hands, she poured you a drink. In its lingering bitterness, you tasted something like tears.

[xiaochou.name] was taken aback by your decision to bring your sister along—so much so that it discarded the questions prepared in advance. It glanced between your face and Arzuna’s, so eerily alike, before finally asking Arzuna what she thought of… well, love.
"Love and desire are the same thing," Arzuna mused. "Sometimes you don’t even know what you want from the other person, so you say you want love. But in truth, it’s just the shadow of an insatiable desire… utterly ugly."
The answer left [xiaochou.name] looking oddly deflated, as if it wanted to press further—but then, strangely, the Mirror hesitated, and said nothing at all.

"I know, I know!" Mahir needed no prompting from [s1.name]’s magic, eagerly sharing her thoughts on love. "I love everything I create! Because I brought them into this world—they are questions, answers, reflections, fragments of my soul and wit… I love each one!"
Wait, that’s not the kind of love we’re talking about, is it? You glanced at [xiaochou.name], only to find it nodding as if profoundly moved. Later, [xiaochou.name] even told you that Mahir possessed a rare potential… and coming from the Mirror, that was high praise indeed.

At your summons, Inal crept forward and knelt, trembling—more timid, more dull than she had ever been as Maggie’s slave.
You signaled [s1.name] to proceed, and so [s1.name] posed the prepared question: "What do you think of love?"
Inal froze, then pressed her forehead to the floor. "I don’t know—I don’t know what it is. Perhaps I once had it, but I… I have utterly failed it."
Tears fell from the girl’s trembling eyes, darkening the thick-woven rug. [xiaochou.name] couldn’t help but touch the damp stain, then her pale cheek. Through those translucent pupils, it saw a past of simple, fleeting joy—now shattered, leaving only endless regret and pain. She kept whispering apologies, over and over.

You settled onto the cushions, sharing wine and idle chatter, drifting through trivial matters. Under [s1.name]’s guidance, the conversation soon turned to love and desire.
Uncharacteristically, Faraj fell silent for a moment before speaking in a low voice, "Love is an incurable sickness. It hollows out the soul, gnaws at reason, and is never satisfied." He sighed faintly, staring down at his cup, his brow shadowed with helpless frustration—yet he dared not meet your gaze.

"Everyone wants love, just like they want prettier, rarer gems!" At [s1.name]’s question about love, Salwiyah answered without hesitation. Her delicate fingers twirled through soft curls, violet eyes flickering with practiced charm, lips curved in a meticulously crafted smile—her makeup flawless under the light. "Love is a fashionable commodity, and I can give them the very best."
Her voice carried a fierce, almost prideful arrogance and ambition. [xiaochou.name] took it all in.
Fixes and Patches

For days afterward, every time you saw [s1.name], it was wielding a tiny hammer, attempting to inlay minuscule gemstones into a long belt.
When you asked, it readily explained—that was a technique once taught to princes and lords’ sons, meant to temper the arrogance of future rulers with its grueling patience.
"Every time I muster the patience to understand humans better, I find you’re all so gifted at tormenting your own kind," [s1.name] declared, tossing aside the mangled belt.

5000308.title: What to See...?
strings: What to See...?

The things you refuse to speak, the feelings words fail to capture—[xiaochou.name] has ways of knowing. All you need do is provide a vessel. Come now, you wouldn’t be so stingy as to deny even that, would you?
The Mirror
You recall things not meant for others' ears...
Perhaps something peculiar has stirred your desires...
What’s Wrong with Loving a Kitten?
Rhino or Real
In the Deep Dark
Desire Higher than Lust

That night, [s1.name] slipped effortlessly into your dreams.
The Mirror watched it all unfold in silence: how you laid out the softest, most luxurious rug, lured the kitten into your chamber with treats, then scooped it up and buried your face in its downy chest fur, nuzzling without a care—no need to fret over Carnality Card in this dream! No guilt, no shame, just earnest strokes and gentle pats until the kitten purred softly. Oh, the finest creation ever wrought! Each time, it soothed your restless soul.
Countless mirrors reflected your boundless joy, until dawn’s light roused you... Ah! If only Lady Becky truly curled in your arms!

Truth be told, you’d rather not recall what happened that day—when the Carnality Card snapped, you lost far too much... But in this dream, you truly became a rhino... Drawn by gaze and scent, you found your fated mate.But you remembered you were playing the Sultan’s game—what luck! A bull rhino unbound by rut, yet you must find a Gold tier mate without delay!
And so you ran, frantically, searching across the savanna until the sun dipped low, until your strength failed, until—you jolted awake. Every mirror in your chamber reflected your sweat-drenched face. [s1.name] had witnessed every detail of the dream, yet it seemed unwilling to face you for now.

That night, [s1.name] slipped effortlessly into your dreams, bearing witness to your profane couplings with the creatures of the dark.
They toyed with you freely, assuming forms impossible in the waking world—yet in this realm of dreams, you were the master, and you toyed with them in turn. Thus did you wade through rivers of blood, of agony and ecstasy, parting flesh and bone, sinew and vein, seeking richer feasts in the darkness. To their senseless howls, their mocking wails, you demanded answers—of pleasure, of death.
The Mirror watched in silence. But of the Cultic God, it had nothing to share.

That night, [s1.name] slipped effortlessly into your dreams, bearing witness to all your rebellious treacheries and ambitions. Through the fractured prisms of countless shattered mirrors, it glimpsed the myriad forks of fate—shouts, hopes, blood spilled into flames, heavy or resolute steps ascending the golden throne. Supreme power, more gratifying than any carnal pleasure, yet once seized, would it leave you emptier than the fading throes of desire?
In the end, you awoke, the faint dawn light revealing your cold, weary face in the mirror. The executioner's blade drew nearer still.

That night, [s1.name] slipped effortlessly into your dreams, reflecting a lightless evening. You wandered alone across the desolate plains, shivering in the bitter wind, unsure which path would not lead to the cliff’s edge. At last, you found it—a strange, tiny flame, flickering weakly in the night breeze without fuel. Instinctively, you stepped forward, cupping it in your hands—and through your eyes, the mirror saw much in that fire: those you had betrayed, those you had scorned, those you had answered, those you had honored. Your dark thoughts, your obsessions, your kindness, what you could not grasp, what you yearned for—and this heart of yours, wrapped in tangled desires, was the fuel for this flame. Together, you and the fire lit a corner of the darkness, like a newborn sun.

That night, [s1.name] slipped effortlessly into your dreams.
It saw cards of every kind swirling around you, and you examined them, deciding the fate of each—determining the life and death, the glory and disgrace of those around you. For the first time, you wielded such unchecked power! Like a Sultan, like a god, the world revolved around your choices, twisting into impossible shapes, like a turning kaleidoscope—what if you did this? Try it, just try it! Last time, he died; this time, let it be her. Maybe, you can make another choice this time; now, pick something different. No need for guilt—it’s just a game, isn’t it?
[s1.name] watched the dream in silence, observing your monstrous desires, waiting to see how your game would end.
Gazing into the Mirror

The next day—you cast a casual glance at the ancient silver mirror hanging in your hallway, its surface worn by time, once capable of reflecting only faint, ghostly shapes. But now, the figure in the mirror stares back at you with unsettling clarity. A shiver runs down your spine as you realize it must be [s1.name]. It offers you an inscrutable smile, then, in the blink of an eye, the mirror reverts to its usual state—as if it were nothing but a trick of the light.

5000309.title: Desire and Progeny
strings: Desire and Progeny
[xiaochou.name] seeks to understand more about desire and progeny. You may introduce it to those you deem fit to share their thoughts.
The Mirror
Those who care about progeny
Only a few characters can offer insights of worth.

You had the servants set up a charming tea party in the garden—pomegranate tea, shade, mild hookahs even the ladies enjoyed, and plenty of sweet, dried fruits and candied treats.
Maggie cradled her teacup, sharing her thoughts on heirs with [s1.name].
"Children... well, they're a blessing if you have them, a Purist's gift, a balm for parents' hearts." She took a sip, her eyes downcast. You'd never heard her broach the topic before, so you listened intently. "But I think... if one spends their life in misery for lack of a child, that seems unnecessary. Living is about happiness first—your own happiness, before you can bring it to others. If embracing the one you love brings joy, then even if it doesn't lead to a child... I'd still want to hold them a hundred, a thousand times."
Her cheeks flushed, and she hid her shyness behind her cup. Her words made your heart itch—you longed to embrace her right then, quite literally—if not for [s1.name]'s uncanny magic, you might never have heard such words from Maggie.
[s1.name] studied both your faces, then nodded thoughtfully.
"Thank you, Lady Maggie," it said. "I, too, hope you and your beloved may embrace day and night."

You found the wandering swordsman in a tavern, predictably draped over a beautiful prostitute, leaning in to sip from her cup.
[s1.name]’s eyes lit up, and it seized the moment to sit across from the swordsman, asking his thoughts on progeny.
The swordsman gave it a withering look, but after a brief stare, his annoyance faded. “If I lack the strength to protect a child, or the means to give them a decent future, I won’t even consider it,” he said with a mocking grin. “Bringing someone into this world just to suffer—what a sin.”
You glanced pointedly at the woman beside him, sneering. “Fine words. But how is this responsible? If you truly believe that, why not take up with a few male whores—”
The swordsman gaped at you, speechless. But [s1.name], as if seeing or knowing something, burst into laughter. The meeting ended in discord, with the Mirror’s uncontrollable giggles ringing in your ears. Still, as you left, you noticed the swordsman muttering and pressing extra coins into the girl’s hand…

You steeled yourself before finally inviting Jawad to your home, but you’d underestimated his enthusiasm for the topic!
Without a word, he dragged you and [s1.name] to a lavish mansion, leading you down a corridor lined with enormous paintings—not of ancestors or rulers, but of his beloved little Arumina.
Jawad proudly regaled you with trivial tales behind each portrait, from her babbling infancy to her delicate maidenhood. At last, you couldn’t help but ask: Why not hang these at home? His face crumpled. “Oh… oh, well… little Arumina says it’s disgusting and embarrassing. Really? Really?” He seized you, launching into a lament. You gave his shoulder a solemn pat, then turned on your heel and left. Hah. Given another chance, you’d never bring up Arumina again. As for [s1.name], it lingered with Jawad until sunset, returning with the air of someone who’d struck gold…

[s1.name]'s question left Fatuna stunned. The ever-graceful noblewoman, for the first time in your presence, knocked over her teacup. She had never pondered why one should have a child—every girl wed, then bore one child or many. Her mother had, her friends had, all girls did, becoming "mothers" while still young and innocent, stepping onto a path the world deemed inevitable. But why?
She fell into a long silence, lost in thought, before finally sighing and offering [s1.name] an apology. "I fear I must reflect on this," she said, a bitter smile touching her lips. "Had someone asked me this sooner... I might have known there was another choice."
You watched her retreating figure, the weight of her words leaving you all wordless.

At [s1.name]'s question, Qais let out a bitter laugh. He told you his mother had urged him, both openly and subtly, more than once.
“She’s always wanted me to settle down quickly—because children mean responsibility and ties, don’t they? With a wife and child, you can’t act so recklessly, so thoughtlessly.” He shook his head helplessly. “I’ve worried her too much.”
On that point, you couldn’t help but agree. Then again, it occurred to you—since you’d rescued Qais and brought him under your banner, he had grown less reckless with his tongue.

“Shouldn’t this question be asked of our parents?” Arzunal sneered, her radiant face twisting with rare venom. She spoke through clenched teeth: “Bearing a child is the basest, most shameful escape—when one lacks the courage or strength to do what must be done, the final solution is to spawn some poor wretch to bear that cursed hope! They perform their suffering and sacrifice, but what does the child gain? Why should the kid carry the burden?”
Every eye in the room, every goblet, every mirror reflected the fury she’d buried deep. [s1.name] pressed it lips tight. Yes, yes—this was the tale it knew too well. What wretched creatures humans were!

You received two distinguished guests in the parlor—[s1.name] and Faraj. By the time you stepped in, they were already sharing a hookah, their conversation warm and easy.
“Hmm? Thoughts on children? Well… I’ve seldom pondered it. The elders in the family do nag, true, but I think…” Faraj dabbed the wine from his lips, considering carefully. “Desire is one thing; children are another. Children are a kind of desire—ah, ah, not that sort!—they’re the continuation of a parent’s life, the embodiment of human’s hunger to live forever, no? But for me… I’ve no such hunger. If I can serve loyally, if I can prove my worth, I’d rather burn bright… and vanish.”
He refilled your cup, and the talk meandered elsewhere.
Amid the clinking of glasses, you caught [s1.name] watching you thoughtfully. This meeting with Faraj had clearly deepened it understanding of human desires.

Shama met you at the most fashionable Perfume shop in the capital. The air was thick with intoxicating scents, shelves lined with exquisite bottles carved like gemstones and crystal. And when Shama stood among them, the tiny reflections dancing across her cheeks…
“You ask my thoughts on carnality and progeny?” She smiled at [s1.name]’s question, lifting a small vial carved from obsidian. She held it beneath [s1.name]’s nose, then gestured for you to inhale as well. “Fresh, clean, elegant, no? Yet this is the essence of poppy, blended with the scent of barley grains… Poppy’s other gift is the madness of dreams, they say, and it’s addictive—but it smells divine, doesn’t it?”
She paid the shopkeeper five gold coins and tucked the vial away.
“So here is my answer, my lords. Desire carries the sweetest, most addictive fragrance. To savor it, one cannot escape the delirium it brings. And that, I believe, is progeny. What madness drives one to drag an innocent child into this world? What arrogance makes one wish to replicate oneself? How deeply must love delude, to crave a kin mingled with another’s blood?
