My contempt, scorn, and arrogance toward humans have only driven me further from them. I toyed with your hearts, believing I understood you—when all I did was ‘see.’"
"I apologize, [player.name]. I will continue to explore these human questions, but now, I shall do so in a more ‘human’ way. Command me as you would any of your followers." With that, [s1.name] bowed again—just as a true human might.

You spoke these words to your brother. Countless mirrors reflected your identical faces, and in a daze, you could no longer tell which were your reflections and which was your true brother—did he even exist? A shudder ran through you.
"That won’t do," he replied—or perhaps, the countless versions of you in the mirrors did. "This is your fate, and mine." The voices layered upon each other, an endless echo crashing down. Through the forest of mirrors, you glimpsed a swirling black mist coiled behind you both—and in that instant, a familiar presence... a chilling one, shattered every mirror. Before you could discern what it was, the dream ended. You jolted awake to an indescribable warning, finding every mirror in your home reduced to dust.
The Mirror had failed. It demanded you choose another one.

In the labyrinth of night, a blade clattered at [s2.name]’s feet. The mirrors encircling [s2.name] flickered with scenes of betrayal and abandonment, blood spilling freely across their surfaces—soon, your blood would join it, mingling with visions that had not yet come to pass, yet were no less real for it.

Seizing this rare moment, the Mirror savored the ebb and ruin of your life through your heart and [s2.name]’s hand, relishing the intricate, fleeting emotions in its mind… until the next day, when it returned to you in human guise, announced by servants, and bowed with practiced courtesy.
"I hope you don’t mind my little trick," it said. "I wanted to taste death, but a mirror cannot die—shatter it into a thousand pieces, and it remains a mirror. So... I borrowed your heart."
"Thanks to your earlier aid, I better grasp why humans are so... unlikable. Bound by flesh, gifted with complex minds yet trapped in frail bodies. You strive for the unattainable; every desire comes with pain. You beg the Mirror for wishes, scrutinize your reflections, and are never satisfied... So, I despise you.”
Then [s1.name] paused, then smiled. "But you are also... fascinating. Yes, fascinating."
With a careless shrug—yet offering no further insight—[s1.name] concluded: "[player.name], I admit, these days have been more entertaining than mere observation. I suppose I’ll linger by your side a while longer—though I intend to experience things in a more... human way." 
Having settled on this conclusion, [s1.name] bowed once more. When it straightened, the last glimmer had faded from its eyes. Now, it looked entirely, utterly human.

How effortlessly one can manipulate hatred and spur a self-righteous vengeance! Regardless, the Mirror was pleased with the outcome.
You jolted awake, pushing yourself upright—only to find your wounds gone. In the dawn’s light, only a faintly gleaming shield lay beside you, faithfully reflecting your face—no mockery, no jest, no emotion.
And so, you realized: the Mirror had left you. It had found the answer it sought. This shield was its parting gift—a final act of mercy for the pitiful creatures called human.
Forged from an eternal thing once bent to your will, the shield gleams mirror-bright. In certain moments, you fancy it still watches you.

5000343.title: The Coin’s Turn
strings: The Coin’s Turn
When you returned home, [xiaochou.name] was undergoing a strange transformation…
The creature of the mirror finally makes a crucial change...
This was the result of the long, winding choices you had made.
I Shall Merge with the River of Mortals

[xiaochou.name]’s body radiated a golden glow. Coins tumbled from its hair, sleeves, cascading onto the floor in an unending, ever-quickening clatter.
You sensed something amiss and seized [xiaochou.name]’s hand—only to grasp a fistful of gold. [xiaochou.name] smiled and told you it had come to understand wealth, but not yet humanity. It would become something greater, something eternal, flowing through the world, witnessing all that humans do.
[xiaochou.name]’s form crumbled faster now, and with a final leap, it shattered into countless tiny coins, scattering through your window into the streets below. Passersby cried, “[player.name]’s breaking the cards again!” and scrambled for the sudden fortune raining from the sky.
Now, no one could hoard this creature of the mirror. [xiaochou.name] would be spent, traded, passed from hand to hand—to the empire’s edge and beyond. Only a heap of coins remained before you, indistinguishable from those minted by the Sultan—save for the faint, perhaps imagined, smile on each blurred face.

5000344.title: Mind Over Matter
strings: Mind Over Matter
When you returned home, you found a eunuch already there, ready to greet his "master".
The creature of the mirror finally makes a crucial change...
This was the result of the long, winding choices you had made.
The Royal Archivist

You had never heard of such a position—no, you were certain it didn't exist. Everyone knows the Royal Archives and the Royal Library have absolutely nothing to do with each other! But the eunuch from the palace tittered, "Truly, they say Lord [player.name] is a jester, a master of feigned ignorance... and now I see it's no exaggeration."
He bowed deeply to [xiaochou.name], who had just approached, and recited the Sultan's decree—commanding [xiaochou.name] to return at once to the Royal Archives and fulfill [xiaochou.name]'s ancestral duty of organizing the books. Clearly, without anyone noticing, the once-obedient creature of the mirror had arranged a new fate for itself...
Days later, you found the Royal Archives—a repurposed nobleman's mansion in another corner of the city, hastily refurbished. Servants were still sweeping and dusting as you entered. The place was crammed with books. Books everywhere—and mirrors everywhere—and there, at the far end, sat the illustrious Archivist. "I've decided to linger awhile. After all, you mortals only live a century or so. When you die, I'll move on to other stories," [xiaochou.name] said, flipping pages without looking up. "Try to live longer. Say, two hundred years. By then, I might finish reading what's here." You didn't argue about the lifespan just yet. Instead, you asked: "Didn't you despise humans? Why live among them now?" "Ah, because of what you showed me—those people, those events... especially that last dream." [xiaochou.name] marked the page with a finger and finally met your gaze. "It made me realize that merely watching and listening through the mirror isn't enough to understand your kind—so incompetent, yet so stubborn; so fleeting, yet your thoughts endure; so wasteful, yet so enamored with restraint..." [xiaochou.name] sighed and returned to the book. "Anyway, come find me if you need something. Otherwise, don't bother. You know where this place is now—and remember: live two hundred years, or I'll make you regret it."

5000345.title: Amusing Humans
strings: Amusing Humans
When you returned home, you knew—the being of the mirror had slipped free once more... [xiaochou.name] now touched every mirror, every human thought, without needing your leave...
The creature of the mirror finally makes a crucial change...
This was the result of the long, winding choices you had made.
Most Amusing Human

"Do you know?" [xiaochou.name] smiled at you, its voice bypassing the air, slipping straight into your mind... To resist this intrusion, you steeled yourself, mustering every ounce of will... Yet no further assault came.
"When I peer through all mirrors at once, humans are like flickering mist—chaotic, senseless..." [xiaochou.name] knelt, taking your hand. "But when I gaze through only your mirror... I see patterns, fascinating ones. [player.name], my master, allow me to serve you still. Let me witness more of these wonders!"
You felt it then—a new pact forged between you. Binding until your last breath. Until this game—no, this cycle—reaches its end.

5000346.title: The Archivist
strings: The Archivist
In this self-fashioned sanctuary of books, [xiaochou.name] lives in comfort, yet it still takes leisure to recommend you intriguing volumes—and, incidentally, to check if you yet draw breath.
Rewards different number of books based on the roll check
[xiaochou.name]'s Favor
Its Wisdom and Sociability determine your full dice count.
You need at least 1 Successes to get books
Curious Gift
Still Breathing?
[xiaochou.name] sent you two books—lately, it has been reading swiftly, effortlessly, and wished to share this good fortune with you.
[xiaochou.name] sent you a book—the only one it found worth reading of late.

[xiaochou.name] visited your manor, glimpsed you from afar and left. It could have just used a mirror to check! It seems [xiaochou.name]’s thoughts have grown stagnant lately, truly in need of a walk.

5000347.title: A Song from Afar
strings: A Song from Afar
[xiaochou.name] has left this city, journeying to distant lands. Occasionally, it thinks of you and sends a letter.
The Wandering Poet

In the letters, [xiaochou.name] sketches the sights, the sounds, the wonders it has witnessed and praised. These words, distilled into verse, are read and sung by you—and countless nameless souls beyond.

5000348.title: The Strings of Thousand Harmonies
strings: The Strings of Thousand Harmonies
The day you awoke, something felt amiss... Sitting by your bed, gazing into the mirror, you suddenly realized—the tether that bound [xiaochou.name] to your side had vanished.
The Mirror wants to make one last attempt

[xiaochou.name] was gone.
Not only that, when you asked the servants if [xiaochou.name] had visited today, they stared at you in bewilderment. "Who?" they asked. You understood then—only you remembered that name, only you recalled the visitor from the mirror.
Ah, yes—the mirror!
You rushed to the dusty storeroom. Where the mirror once stood, now lay an object wrapped tightly in eastern silk. A lute, its surface shimmering like polished glass. When plucked, its notes flowed like mountain springs, slipping effortlessly into every heart... On its back, tiny characters were carved: “Each heart hears their own joy, plays their own unique melodic ploy."
This, perhaps, was [xiaochou.name]'s parting gift. Such an extraordinary being was never meant to linger long in your world. Maybe it sought a more comfortable place to rest, or perhaps it had grown weary of unraveling human tales.
Yet those who hold this instrument will forever remember the poet called [xiaochou.name].
Forged from an eternal thing once bent to your will, the lute's strings shimmer with silvered light—like frozen moonlight on still water.

5000349.title: The Crown of Mirror
strings: The Crown of Mirror
Tonight, [xiaochou.name] returns to your dreams...
The Mirror’s final wish is about to be fulfilled
This is [xiaochou.name]’s decision, you cannot interfere
The Crowned One

"[player.name]," [xiaochou.name] calls your name.
"I must thank you, human. You've shown me things I've never known... But to be human—too loud, too cumbersome for me." As [xiaochou.name] speaks, its form begins to dissolve, fading. "Let me stay with you in a quieter way. My final gift. Prove yourself worthy of it—show me more wonders."
In the dream, [xiaochou.name] scatters into dust of glass. When you jolt awake, a coronet rests upon your brow—heavy as gold, smooth as a mirror, reflecting all around you.
Forged from an eternal thing once bent to your will, it gazes now with ruler's eyes—upon the world, and into the dark corners of your soul.

5000350.title: Human is Mirror
strings: Human is Mirror
A weary traveler arrives at your door... It is none other than the long-lost [xiaochou.name]!
How fares [xiaochou.name] out there?
This was the result of the long, winding choices you had made.
Renewal

"To walk among humans, to govern them—it is too weary, too foul!" [xiaochou.name] spoke, shaking off the dust of the road—the first time you noticed its clothes and form could even be soiled. "I am not fit for such labor alone. These burdens are best borne by one like you. Let me stay by your side! This way, I may still taste the world without its weight."
As [xiaochou.name] spoke, it clasped your hand again... A cold fire ignited where your skin met, swiftly cleansing [xiaochou.name]'s form and raiment—anew. Once more, the creature of the mirror bound itself to you. It seems [xiaochou.name] will haunt you for a long while yet.

5000351.title: Abandoned
strings: Abandoned

5000352.title: Reinforcements from the Mirror
strings: Reinforcements from the Mirror

Your army is about to cross a bridge. The sun has just risen, and golden shards dance upon the river’s surface—yet in the reflection of the bridge, [xiaochou.name] stands, smiling at you... Suddenly, you realize the once-murky waters now gleam like polished glass. Perhaps this is no ordinary gift...
[xiaochou.name]
Your Troop
Protagonist
Through the Mirror’s power, your mightiest army’s numbers shall double.
You Journey Together through the Same River

When [s2.name] crosses this bridge, in the reflection upon the water's surface, the same company marches silently. Each time a warrior's feet touch the soil of the far bank, another soldier appears beside him—identical in resolve, identical in strength, as if born brothers, united in their march to overthrow the tyrant.

5000353.title: That Shore
strings: That Shore
Reading can improve yourself, so develop a habit of reading.
Currently Reading
The reader.
Would such words truly stir people's hearts?
They should know—what's truly precious isn't some distant future beyond reach.
Praise the shore we shall all reach in time!
She Saw Through the Trick of This Poem
To Read it, One Need not Even Know Letters
This peculiar craft of weaving magic into words to sway and whisper into the minds of readers, a skill from which Lumera had profited greatly.

The maiden on the cover murmured in [s2.name]'s ear, guiding [s2.gender(him,her)] to chant the incantation with its eerie cadence. The world will awaken at last, for this life is not worth clinging to—the god promise us more at the end!

5000501.title: Haunted Mansion
strings: Haunted Mansion

Your fingers brush over the weathered mud bricks of the abandoned mansion. Dust falls. An ancient, ominous air rises with it. It is said that none who dare enter escape certain doom. What makes you think you would be any different?
You must attend the appointment in person.
You have to dispatch a follower.
A Conquest Card of the Bronze tier or below, or a Bloodshed/Carnality Card befitting the follower's tier
You can try putting some items on it, maybe it will be useful.
Depending on the Sultan Card used, you will approach the Haunted Mansion differently.
If using a Carnality card, the target must have Passion.
You can proceed and explore normally without a Sultan Card.
They torment your nerves, leaving you feeling weak and dizzy. You cannot go on like this. You know you have to get out of here, before the fire goes out, before you are consumed by hatred...
Your Magic and Charisma determine your full dice count.
3 Success will offer better results.
Missing key card(s) or passion to trigger the event
I won't go with you!
This person does not meet the required tier to resolve the Sultan Card.
So you wanted to go to this place
What are you thinking? I won't go!
This person does not meet the required tier to break the Sultan Card.
Terror Arouses Passion
Alone With My Shadow
Abandoned Mansion
At some point, the Carnality Card has broken
You break a Sultan Card in an extremely unclean moment
Calling for Blood
Finally, enough blood has been shed
You discover something...

You have brought [s2.name] with you to this abandoned mansion. It took a lot of persuasion, but fortunately you have the perfect excuse: the Sultan Cards. How else could you justify those ridiculous things you do?
The mansion is empty. You shout. There is no response... The eerie atmosphere and unnatural chill make you and [s2.name] huddle closer together...

Passion sparks like fire, igniting your desires and awakening that which was sleeping in the room... As you caress [s2.name]'s body, the darkness in the room stirs. The shadowy shapes on the walls, floor, and ceiling slither and hiss as if excited by the rubbing and squeezing of your hands. As you kiss and moan and yearn, from within the walls, sounds the slamming of bodies against bodies...

Such unnatural sights should terrify you… But the strangeness enthralls you both. The moon has risen. From your intertwined shadows, an uncanny specter emerges to join your bliss. Its long tongue licks over where your bodies meet. Its sharp claws trace runes through your sweat. Its voice guides your rhythm...

Under its control, in unison, you reach climax. A flood washes out from between [s2.name]’s legs... You jolt awake as the moonlight is suddenly devoured by dark clouds, and from where you are joined, foul, tar-black blood gushes out like tides of a poisoned sea. [s2.name]'s eyes roll back as if possessed, a horrid gurgling crawls out of [s2.gender(his,her)] throat... You pick [s2.gender(him,her)] up and flee in terror, drenched in blood...
Clearly, you have awakened the evil that has taken residence in the abandoned mansion, and it has left a dark stain on your souls.
Upon hearing of this, the Sultan eagerly asks for details. But both you and [s2.name] are still in shock, and your muddled, stammering accounts leave him disappointed.

"This is the place." Upon entering, Badriyyah smiles with recognition. She moves cheerfully through the hall, her fingers brushing the dust-covered stone table where moonlight reveals dark stains unmistakably like blood... The blood seems to animate, coiling eagerly around her fingers before she playfully waves it away.
You approach nervously as she embraces you affectionately. Badriyyah extracts from your clothing the card you planned to break here, examines it with narrowed eyes, then giggles, "Oh, how delightful! I've never played quite this way before!"
In the darkness, dust falls gently while countless shadows writhe across walls, floor, and ceiling... watching you with resentful gazes. But Badriyyah remains unbothered. She guides you, whispering and moaning like a serpent in your ear, these sounds echoing through the empty house, layering upon themselves as if countless women were being enjoyed by you simultaneously upon this blood-soaked stone bed...

After your passionate encounter, you recall few details. When you awaken, sunlight streams into the dust-filled abandoned mansion, dispelling the night's strange atmosphere. You rouse Badriyyah with a yawn - is it your imagination, or has the crescent tattoo on her forehead darkened, as if having absorbed all the mansion's darkness?

Through the mess of stains on the stone bed, you glimpse a sublime vision - pure devotees kneeling before the true god. In ancient times, a god was condemned for unauthorized embellishment of the world - now, through your vision and the game's unholy stains, Their name shall be sanctified again, returning to glory.

"This is the place." Upon entering, Badriyyah smiles with recognition. She moves cheerfully through the hall, her fingers brushing the dust-covered stone table where moonlight reveals dark stains unmistakably like blood... The blood seems to animate, coiling eagerly around her fingers before she playfully waves it away.
You approach nervously as she embraces you affectionately. Badriyyah extracts from your clothing the card you planned to break here. As she examines it with narrowed eyes, before she can register surprise, countless cold, vengeful hands emerge from the darkness, seizing your dagger and driving its thin blade into her throat.
Blood flows down, mingling with the stone bed's ancient stains. Badriyyah laughs - countless women's voices laugh through her shattered throat, layered and lingering. They kiss your hands, swirl around you, then gradually fade. In this dust-covered abandoned mansion, only you remain, hands stained with cultist's blood, heart pounding violently.

In the moment the card breaks, through the splattered blood, you glimpse a sublime vision - angels serving at the god's side. In ancient times, a god was condemned for unauthorized embellishment of the world - now, through your vision and the game's unholy stains, Their name shall be sanctified again, returning to glory.

From the moment you laid eyes upon the haunted mansion, the Bloodshed Card began trembling. It moaned, conjuring up visions of crimson. Its edges sharpened – reminding you of its existence. One evil attracts another... A slaughter committed here will surely be rewarded. As if compelled, under the pretext of a joined adventure, you brought [s2.name] here.

Your footsteps echo in the empty hallways. As soon as [s2.name]'s back is turned, countless shades emerge from the darkness, guiding your hand, guiding your dagger… They point to [s2.gender (his, her)] weak spots. A stab through the spine, some say. A cut through the artery, others whisper.

The shades suddenly vanish when [s2.name] turns to smile at you. You planned to shrug off the illusions and leave immediately... But you realize from [s2.gender (his, her)] stiff expression that [s2.gender] saw those illusions... and received the same instructions to kill you. You cannot turn back now, as a dagger likely awaits your back should you retreat...

Finally, you steel your resolve. You pull out your dagger and plunge it into [s2.name]'s throat. As if guided by fate itself, your blade severs [s2.gender (his, her)]'s artery and throat in one clean strike...

The dead of night is filled with a silent drip. Drip, drip, drip, goes the blood on the floorboards. The illusions, ghosts, and shades are all gone. None of the evil things are here to share your guilt. The choice of bloodshed is yours alone.

On floor, walls, ceiling... strange symbols twist and coil, as if someone carefully writes with [s2.name]'s blood. The killing is chosen; the Sultan Card rises into the air, breaking itself under darkness's silent watch.

On floor, walls, ceiling... strange symbols twist and coil, as if someone carefully writes with [s2.name]'s blood. The killing is chosen; the Sultan Card rises into the air, breaking itself under darkness's familiar gaze.

"This is the place." Upon entering, Badriyyah smiles with recognition. She moves cheerfully through the hall, her fingers brushing the dust-covered stone table where moonlight reveals dark stains unmistakably like blood... The blood seems to animate, coiling eagerly around her fingers before she playfully waves it away.
She extracts from your clothing the card you planned to break here, examines it with narrowed eyes, then laughs without restraint: "Well, I know exactly what to do now."
Her fingertips dip into darkness, tracing patterns nearly identical to the ancient bloodstains in the hall.
Countless screams of fear and hatred layer throughout the empty house, transforming into a sweet rhythm that Badriyyah drinks in. The crescent tattoo on her forehead darkens, as if absorbing the mansion's every shadow... The Conquest Card breaks as moonlight floods the dwelling.
After explaining the night's events to the Sultan, the haunted house you purified naturally becomes yours, regardless of its previous owner - this is "conquest."
Bad luck is just an excuse for the weak. You broke into this decaying mansion, torch in hand, to light everything up, and – if necessary – burn everything down.

Deep inside the mansion, the wet stench of rust and blood smothers you like a chthonic kiss. A cold wind blows from deeper within, and the flickering candlelight illuminates a corner of the heavy, moth-eaten curtains. Bloodstains meander. Before your eyes, is a crime scene.

No, not only that... As you stare at the crimson – so wantonly painted all over – the color twists and struggles as if alive. An endless cacophony of screams and cries echo in your skull, begging you, cursing you, rejecting you, binding you...
You do not recognize the symbols, but there is no doubt they form part of some evil ritual. Perhaps a scholar would be able to discern what they mean and how to disrupt them.
And these trapped, vengeful souls... You do not know how to set them free.
You flee from the haunted mansion in a panic. In the thick, morning fog, you feel a chill in your bones, as if you are on the edge of an abyss. Despite your efforts, it clings to you...
You successfully escaped the haunted mansion. The first rays of sunlight gently caress you, melting away the coldness that was seeping into your soul. You again walk in the world of the living.

The Sultan cannot care less about your fright. You have not even suffered a scratch; you are just scaring yourself. However, he still permits you to break this Conquest Card, as he eagerly awaits your next card – hopefully of a higher tier – and the even bloodier adventure it would bring.

5000502.title: Unsolved Murders
strings: Unsolved Murders
Bloodstains. Footprints. Hints to heinous crimes. Is it too late to find the truth?
You must send a follower, or handle this yourself.
You can assign an additional follower to help.
You can place consumables here to help you achieve your goals.
Having Influence greater than 5 will reduce the difficulty of the check.
If the investigation fails multiple times, this Event will disappear.
After pulling down the heavy curtains, the pale sunlight finally shines into the decaying mansion. You sneak in quietly again, in search for truths that have yet to fade away...
Your Stealth and Sociability determine your full dice count.
You need at least 2 Successes to get the truth. If the Influence is high enough, 1 Success instead.
You rely on your Influence

You are quite influential in the city. On the day of the investigation, a servant who claims to have served in that mansion comes to you. He divulges certain secrets in you and provides you with an irrefutable piece of evidence, asking only that you... you are the only one who can give justice to the young women who perished there, for the culprit behind all this is in fact the well respected judge...

Footprints still fresh, strips of clothing torn off from a struggle, a discarded weapon… Slowly, you piece together the truth. You have irrefutable evidence, all pointing towards the well-respected Legal Official…
Endless resentment forced to remain silent under the sun, bloody messages left undeciphered… Unfortunately, you make no progress towards uncovering the truth.

Endless resentment forced to remain silent under the sun, bloody messages left undeciphered… Unfortunately, you make no progress towards uncovering the truth. Anxiety stirs. You have a feeling that if you fail to gain any new insight next time, the truth shall elude you forever.
It is too late. It is all gone. You have worked in vain.

No matter how careful an investigation is, it will leave traces. You know this to be a race against time. You must make a strong enough case before the culprit is alerted to your presence and disappears into the darkness forever.

5000503.title: Rest in Peace
strings: Rest in Peace
Restless wraiths remain trapped in this world, endlessly wailing and weeping…
You can send the Priest, the Occultist, the Old Judge, or any other follower to perform this ritual.
You can use the murderer's head or a sacred relic from the temple to complete the ritual.
There are many ways to exorcize the vengeful spirits here, leading to different rewards.
Out of arrogance or indifference, you decide to have your followers forcefully expel the vengeful spirits. But, can you manage it?
Your Magic and Charisma determine your full dice count.
You need at least 2 Successes to put her to rest.
The sinner is dead
Radiant Purity
Rest Now
Absorb
Let the sinner bear the backlash of his own evil magic
You succeeded
You failed

The tendrils of darkness drape themselves around the severed head, draining moisture and life from its skin and flesh. They wither away, leaving behind a pallid skull, its hollow sockets staring blankly into the void.

Finally, the darkness is sated. Light and wind again flow through this room, once filled with blood and resentment. In a haze, you seem to see the girls curtsying to you, bowing their heads in gratitude, before disappearing into thin air, hand in hand. And you realize it is already sundown. You come to your senses, your chest warm, and the unnatural frigidity is gone from this mansion.

Death, too, is a gift from God. Why then this resentment, this refusal to return to Him? In the blinding light emitted by the relic, all the lingering souls are silenced and unmade. As for sins... they are for God to judge and punish.
The grand ceremony, presided over by [s1.name] personally, has finally brought peace to the dead and struck fear into the Cultists who cower in the darkness.

The cold wind whistles, stinging your skin. Is it an illusion? You smell the sweetness of endless fear and hatred intertwined. The Badriyyah smiles and raises her staff. In silence she chants her obtuse spell. Then, silence falls like death. This is how it should be. Only the gem inlaid on top of her staff gleams scarlet, red as a maiden's lips, pure as blood.

Look, you have brought their most welcomed guest! Endless hatred rushes the old legal official. He screams and struggles, but he could not defy them. They take back what he has taken from them – the youthful body, the skin and flesh that do not age – the breath of life that do not belong to him. Before your very eyes, life drains from this man at an astounding speed. He becomes gaunt, withered, and weak, a pile of bones wrapped in loose skin.
Even so, he lives. He opens his mouth, but could not make a sound. He moves his eyes, but could not focus his gaze. He flails his arms, but – like a worm – he could not support his body.
His living soul is trapped in a dead body, unable to return to his earthly delight, and equally unable to plead his case with his false good deeds before God.
Let him enjoy this inescapable immortality! This is the most vicious curse left for him by the girls who died under his evil spell to prolong his life.
The powerful magic silenced all the voices of hatred and curses, and peace finally returns to this mansion.

You mobilize your magic and attempt to dispel the foul presence. But it is not enough, far from it. You tremble and stutter, unable to utter your spells, unable to resist the terror assaulting you from the depths of your soul. The only thought remaining: Flee.

5000504.title: The Real Culprit
strings: The Real Culprit
You have solid evidence that the Legal Official has committed a crime, and this is also the leverage you can use to control him and make him work for you.
You have the whereabouts of the Legal Official Amur.
Option 1: You can send a follower, or kill the culprit yourself.
Option 2: To blackmail the Legal Official into doing your bidding, you can send any follower, or talk to him yourself.
You must place the item Valid Evidence
Depending on your choice, different subsequent rituals may be initiated.
What are you going to do with the Judge?
You decide to kill this sinner...
Make him an asset...
Amur cries bitterly before the evidence you show him, begging for your forgiveness. However, those who had the right to forgive are long dead, and all that you can do is send him to them.

Amur cries bitterly before the evidence you show him, begging for your forgiveness. His old eyes are filled with disbelief, rancor, and fear, but as you expected, there is not a trace of remorse. Which is just fine. You need no remorse, you need his submission.

The judge bows his trembling head and tells you all you wanted to know, from what the evil ritual in the mansion is meant to achieve, to the whereabouts of the Occultist who could preside over the ritual...

5000505.title: Court Execution
strings: Court Execution
At your request, the Sultan agrees to let you execute Amur, thereby offsetting a Bloodshed Card.
Legal Official Amur is brought to the palace, trembling as he awaits your execution.
You must place a Bloodshed Card worthy of the Legal Official.
This Event happens as the consequence of a choice you made. You cannot change or cancel it.

Amur kneels at the foot of the long steps, his lips trembling, but not a word of pleading is uttered. He knows that there is nothing to be done now. He is not dying to his crimes – he did not commit any. The slave girls are but commodities: he has the right to deal with them as he pleases. He is dying to you, to the card in your hand. Even as his head rolls on the ground, his eyes remain open. He nails his eternal hatred to you. He curses you with his immortal soul: may you sink in the quagmire of misfortune, for all eternity!

5000506.title: In the Name of God
strings: In the Name of God
The High Priest of the Purists asks you to find and capture cultists operating secretly within the city.
Those judged heretical, living or dead
Your devout faith, or the one who delivers cultists
There are many targets that could satisfy the Priest's demands.
You brought Mahir's head over
You brought Mahir over
Cultist's Offering
Witch Hunter
Witch Captive
Temple Trap
False Accusation

You inform the priest that Mahir dared peer into the stars' secrets and the dwelling place of gods - undeniably heretical! You've already purified her on their behalf.
"This woman repeatedly attempted to steal sacred objects," the priest acknowledges, nodding gratefully. When you inquire about these "sacred objects," he falls silent. You depart with your reward and lingering questions.

You denounce Mahir to the priest for daring to peer into the stars' secrets and the dwelling place of gods - undeniably heretical! Mahir stares at you in disbelief, struggling desperately before guards restrain and remove her.
"This woman repeatedly attempted to steal sacred objects," the priest acknowledges gratefully. When you inquire about these "sacred objects," he falls silent. You depart with your reward and lingering questions.

You deliver the cultist to the church. Before you can speak, an agonized wail erupts. The young man clutches his fractured stone, emitting inhuman howls. As the stone crumbles to dust in the pure light, he collapses lifeless.
Thus the follower of the strange god is purified by the Purists' power. The priest silently nods in appreciation.

The priests recognize Badriyyah's face immediately. This detestable woman attracted numerous ignorant commoners from Dark Alley as followers, and several elimination attempts had failed... for various reasons.
They acknowledge your achievement with appropriate compensation.

The priests recognize Badriyyah's face immediately. This detestable woman attracted numerous ignorant commoners from Dark Alley as followers, and several elimination attempts had failed... for various reasons.
They acknowledge your achievement with appropriate compensation. Badriyyah is dragged away, hurling vile curses at you, the priests, and even the Immaculate Purity until the very end.

The moment Badriyyah stepped into the temple, the trap was sprung.
Confusion flickered across her face, twisting into disbelief—then into wild, hysterical laughter. The priests recognized her instantly. This detestable woman attracted numerous ignorant commoners from Dark Alley as followers, and several elimination attempts had failed... for various reasons.
They acknowledged your deed and rewarded you as promised. Badriyyah was seized and dragged away, spewing curses until her voice broke—at you, at the priests, and even at the Immaculate Purity itself.

When [s1.name] is dragged away by waiting temple guards, the entire sanctuary echoes with protestations of innocence and curses against you. The priests state they will provide your reward after obtaining concrete evidence of heretical crimes.
Clearly, you're unlikely to receive that reward.

5000507.title: Night's Shelter
strings: Night's Shelter

Amid swirling mist, you tread through Dark Alley's smoke and dust, finding this old clay-brick house. The colored tiles above the windows have long since faded and fallen away, wind and sand having rendered the heavy curtains dirty and dim. Still, you discern blurred dark shapes matching your memory. This is the place. Before knocking, you consider once more: why have you come?
You're certain the evil Occultist is hiding here
Option 1: You are prepared to send followers, or go apprehend this cultist yourself
Option 2: You are quite interested in the cultist's dark arts. You are prepared to send followers, or go and talk to her in person
You can bring consumables to help you arrest the cultist. If you have a White Honey Amber Orb, it will all be very simple
Using the item the Priest gave you can lower the difficulty of this check.
Different choices will lead to different plots and Events.
Your hand, hidden behind your back, quietly holds the dagger tight...
Your Combat and Magic determine your full dice count.
You need at least 1 Success to capture her.
It's rare to get the best of both worlds, and you can only step on one path with one pair of feet.
Witch Capture
You are attracted to the Darkness

Having made up your mind, you calmly knock on the door. No response. But you are certain and patient. Finally, the door opens. From within a thick darkness, you see a pale and youthful face. The woman's eyes are cold and alert, bright as a sharpened blade.

Without preamble, you present the White Honey Amber Orb.
It emits gentle radiance - a poet might compare its pure wetness to moonlight during the rare rainy season. It easily illuminates this confined space, banishing all darkness.
Before you now stands merely a weakened woman stripped of power. You capture her with ease.

All of a sudden, you find her inexplicably, extraordinarily beautiful. Her eyes are the darkest nights, her full lips poppies in full bloom. Your breaths are filled with a strange fragrance, the sweetness of apple dripping honey, hiding its hollowed out core, where a snake had been. You are lost in it. You have become the core. You want to return whence you came... Distantly, camel bells chime. A blinding sunrise pierces your dull eyes. You find yourself on top a sand dune, almost buried in the sand, without knowing how and when you got here. You are lucky a passing caravan rescues you. A narrow escape – for you. As for the pale and beautiful Cultist... she has long disappeared.

All of a sudden, you find her inexplicably, extraordinarily beautiful... No, something is wrong. Alarm bells scream in your heart and, almost subconsciously, you draw your dagger.
You have imagined countless possibilities and prepared countermeasures for each of them, all to capture this evil cultist. Your efforts are not in vain. Before the sun rises, you have succeeded and left the Dark Alley behind. The thick fog covers everything.
No one will notice the disappearance of a reclusive woman. Regardless, it is the Dark Alley. Who cares?

This isn't the woman. You immediately realize the person you seek isn't this tired, aged, utterly ordinary woman. Under persistent questioning, she reveals the dwelling's original occupant left just last night.
You've missed the Occultist; she's beyond your reach now.

For some inexplicable reason, you suddenly find her extraordinarily beautiful.
You find yourself confessing everything to her - how your heart is drawn to that mysterious darkness.
"Oh, it seems our master has taken a liking to you," she says, laughing merrily as she listens, taking your hand. "Look, my master has acknowledged you." You discover a black mark on your palm - like a small mole or ink drop. Gazing at it, you involuntarily recite an ancient incantation guided by Badriyyah's voice.
Darkness answers your call, bestowing some yet-unknown desire upon your head. Thus you learn the name of that ancient, banished Cultic God and the forbidden knowledge.
"I am Badriyyah," her voice carries unmistakable intimacy, "welcome, fellow traveler."

5000508.title: Divine Assistance
strings: Divine Assistance
The unusual evil atmosphere in the Haunted Mansion is disturbing. Perhaps you can seek help from the Purist Order.
The Priest of the Purist Order
If you want the Order's help, you must hand in the Traces of Black Magic.
You must send a follower, or go to the Order yourself. People who are diplomatic and charming always get better results.
You can try putting some items on it, maybe it will be useful.
Perhaps... Oh God, forgive a man's insatiable greed... Such beautiful orbs... Perhaps you are entitled to two of them?
Your Sociability and Charisma determine your full dice count.
2 Successes will offer better results.
Wait!
Haven't the priests of the Purist Order already turned against you? They won't help you - better consider other options.

You draw the runes you glimpsed deep in the mansion from memory. They are crooked and incomplete, but High Priest Iman recognizes them at a glance – they are part of some kind of sorcery spell.
These dark apostates dare to sacrifices to the devil so blatantly by the royal capital. The temple cannot tolerate such blasphemy.
But in order to catch them all in one fell swoop, Priest Iman cannot make a move himself. He hands you a White Honey Amber Orb, hoping that you can find the cultists hidden in the city.
You know that such an orb can dispel all evil forces, just as the Purists banished the Cultic God into the void. Before it, the vengeful spirits of the mansion will have nowhere to hide. Even the magician behind it all will have no choice but to surrender.
However, blessed though it is, it is still of this earth. If darkness stains it, even just by a little, it will lose its purity and perfection. It will lose its power and grow dim, becoming just an ordinary rock...

Iman looks at you evenly, his amber eyes as calm as an ancient well. They suddenly make you feel so ashamed. Oh, how could you have fallen to greed in such a holy place, facing such a holy gem?!

You immediately apologized – confess in penitence – to him, and promise that you will resolve matters at the mansion and bring in those cultists. You will bring them here to face God and teach them a lesson they would never forget.

Iman looks at you evenly, his amber eyes as calm as an ancient well. You are ready to face any questioning, your reasons sufficient, but without uttering a word, as if having already seen through them all, he simply gives you another holy orb.

You happily thank him, promise that you will resolve matters at the mansion and bring in those wretched cultists. You will bring them here to face God and teach them a lesson they would never forget.

You draw the runes you glimpsed deep in the residence from memory. They are crooked and incomplete, but the Priest of Purists recognized them immediately—they were part of a sinister ritual circle.
Those dark oath-breakers have dared to offer sacrifices to devils so brazenly around the royal city! The priest thanked you with a grave expression and gave you an Orb, said to possess the power to dispel all evil, just as the Purists had banished the Cultic Gods into the Void. They had no time for further questions, however. They were already preparing a purge against the Cultists within the city. Still, if you wish to lend your strength to this holy war, the Priests of the Purist would welcome you with open arms.

5000509.title: Evil Clues
strings: Evil Clues
Those twisted bloody symbols deep in the Haunted Mansion are disturbing. What are they?
You can send a follower, or go in person. A person who is good at negotiation and knowledgeable is often more helpful in investigation.
You must bring Traces of Black Magic with you to conduct relevant investigations.
You can try putting some items on it, maybe it will be useful.
If this investigation fails, you can try again.
You draw from memory the runes you glimpsed deep in the mansion. They are crooked and incomplete... but perhaps someone can recognize their origin?
Your Sociability and Wisdom determine your full dice count.
You need at least 1 Success to find a clue.
My Creation
Investigation failed

"Found it in the abandoned eastern house, right?" Badriyyah smiles. "That ritual extends life. Want to know the client's identity? Sorry, I can't tell you."
Well, that seems to be all you'll get from her.

After a day of meticulous investigation, you finally uncover a clue - someone saw similar symbols somewhere in Dark Alley... Isn't that where Badriyyah lives? You find her, and she cheerfully admits: "Found it in the abandoned eastern house, right? I drew those... The ritual extends life. Want to know the client's identity? Sorry, I can't tell you."
Well, that seems to be all you'll get from her.
Judge Amur has revealed the Occultist's hiding place. If you're prepared to face darkness, horror, and death, you may investigate.

After a whole day of careful investigation, you finally catch a clue. Someone has seen a similar symbol somewhere in the Dark Alley. She marks the location for you on the map. If you feel that you are ready – ready to face the deepest darkness, terror and death – you can go investigate.
A whole day of hard work, a whole day of nothing.

5000511.title: Untraceable Crime
strings: Untraceable Crime
You have used every possible means and finally obtained solid evidence on the identity of the murderer, but...
Valid Evidence
The sinner is dead

The evidence you obtain points to Judge Amur, whose evil deeds cause an uproar in the city. Unfortunately, he has died before receiving his due punishment or redeeming his sins. Countless kindhearted citizens, poets, and painters flock to the Dark Alley to mourn the seventy-seven slave girls who die for his greed. They praise their beauty, depict their torture, and sing of their sufferings. People grow rich and famous from these works, and some even gain noble patronages. After they leave, the Dark Alley slowly returns to its usual desolation, as if nothing has happened. As for justice? No one cares. How can these resentful souls be appeased? Certainly not through any of this.

5000512.title: Avenge Them
strings: Avenge Them
The only way for Amur to pay for his crimes is death.
Amur realizes that he is doomed
The time to act is now.
You can take this to break a Bloodshed Card that matches the Judge's tier
Certain items can be useful in combats.
This is a life-and-death battle
If you feel that combat is too difficult, you can try other means, such as reporting him to the Sultan.

When he realizes that you are unmoved by pleas and tears, Amur puts away the pointless performances.

He stands up straight. You suddenly discover that he is not as old as his age would suggest – few people in the Sultan's cities live pass seventy. A life is so easy to take, by the climate, poverty, sickness – but Amur looks young. Neither hunched nor gaunt, this body that should be close to death is full of an ominous vigor.

He stares at you fiercely with his clear eyes and draw a dagger from his waist: "You asked for it."

Your mind darts back to the Haunted Mansion, the evil ritual you still lack understanding of... And you realize that this fight may not be as easy as you imagined.
The number of dice provided by your Physique and Combat is affected by the enemy's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 1 Success to win.
You cursed your opponent right to death with vicious language! You've won!
You have applied poison to your weapon, and you only need to make a small cut, and then you can wait for victory! With that stratagem, you've won!
Report his crimes to the Sultan

The blade pierces through his chest. A dirty scarlet soaks through the layers of silk, and is cooled by the night breeze. Death comes as quietly and irresistibly as the night, petrifying his final expression of anger and fear. Amur's eyes slowly lose focus, until they are as dull as stone. You calm your breathing, still ragged from the fierce combat, and after a while, you pull out your scimitar and cut off Amur's head.

The vengeful spirits entrenched in that mansion would appreciate this gift.

You bring the news of the Legal Official's death to the palace, along with a matching Bloodshed Card that you present to the Sultan's desk. Amid the nervous murmuring of your colleagues, a smile tugs at your king's lips. How he love to see your hands covered in blood, just as his are, just as you despised.
Your actions inevitably left traces.

You should not have underestimated the enemy. He is not an ordinary old man, and you should have known that. Incredible power controls his body. You can almost see it: underneath his healthy, smooth skin, there is a monster. It is agile, quick, powerful, fearless, and inexhaustable. You lose. Sweet blood gushes out of your wounds and the flow curves into a mysterious symbol. Unfortunate avenger, you, too, have become food for the monster.

5000513.title: The Call of Darkness
strings: The Call of Darkness
You frequently dream of returning to that perilous mansion, following blood trails from a fallen dagger deeper into darkness. Something awaits you there, calling you.
Traces of black magic can help you find clues
You must handle this issue personally
You can find a wise person for help
Certain items can help you uncover more clues during conversations
You can keep trying.
You look for a mentor who can give you answers.
Your Sociability and Wisdom provide you with the full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes.
In the lingering shadows, you hear mocking laughter. But daylight breaks, and the dream dissolves into nothing.
A Woman Found

Her shelter is crude, burning strange incense, with no light penetrating the worn tapestries. Her jewelry emits a moon-like glow, outlining her entrancing silhouette, her garments parted like a doorway inviting entry into darkness.
It leads you into a fog-filled labyrinth where you wander in circles until morning light breaks through. You awaken exhausted to the sound of fading sighs.

5000514.title: Badriyyah
strings: Badriyyah
I am Badriyyah, she smiles. Her black fingers brush and tingle your chest, perhaps to calm you, or to provoke you further.
She can teach you forbidden knowledge no longer spoken of
You must attend the appointment in person.
This is an enticing woman; you can take this to break a Bloodshed or Carnality Card.
Use a Sultan Card appropriate for your needs.
You can know her without needing a Sultan Card.
Peering into Darkness
Dark Communion
Pain's End
Unholy Ritual

Effortlessly, you confide your recent experiences, earning her high praise. "You completed my unfinished ritual through blood and followed the remaining guidance to find me... You have remarkable talent, both in magical aptitude and your cold heart." She laughs joyfully, taking your hand. "Look, my master has acknowledged you." You discover a black mark on your palm - like a small mole or ink drop. Gazing at it, you involuntarily recite an ancient incantation guided by Badriyyah's voice.
Darkness answers your call, painting your head with the blood and hatred of your sacrifice. Thus you learn the name of that ancient, banished Cultic God and the forbidden knowledge bestowed upon humanity.
"Welcome," she squeezes your hand with obvious affection. "Our god favors you. We're fellow travelers now."

Before speaking to her, you presented a Carnality Card. Words weren't necessary, physical connection brings one closer to the truth—besides, you were aware of your hunger. She laughed, holding the hand with the Carnality Card, mimicking the card posture, pressing your lower bodies together. What is more important than joy or merriment? In the entanglement, your blade pierced through the longstanding delusion—life is a scam, an endless toil. The divine guiding our joy is exiled, yearning to return and end this ancient suffering. Recalling forbidden knowledge sealed for eons, as you and Badriyyah recited the Cultic God’s honorifics, you both reached the peak of joy."Welcome, fellow traveler." She laughed playfully, squeezing your hand with evident affection, "Our god likes you well."

Before speaking to her, you first present a Bloodshed Card.
Unexpectedly, she smiles and grasps your hand holding the Sultan Card, mimicking the depicted posture, using the card to slice her own throat. That massive wound becomes her true lips, truth flowing like blood, which you instinctively respond to with lover-like kisses and drinking - through this gift, you learn an ancient secret - life is merely deception, a meaningless arrangement of endless toil, the god guiding us toward pleasure was banished, and followers await Their return to end the world's eternal suffering!
The forbidden knowledge buried for eons resurfaces, the Cultic God's name escapes your lips, and in that moment, you look up to find her entrails consumed by your teeth, her remains vibrant and beautiful, supremely elegant.

In the moment the card breaks, through the splattered blood, you glimpse a sublime vision - angels serving at the god's side. In ancient times, a god was condemned for unauthorized embellishment of the world - now, through your vision and the game's unholy stains, Their name shall be sanctified again, returning to glory.

In the moment the card breaks, through the splattered stains, you glimpse a sublime vision - pure devotees kneeling before the true god. In ancient times, a god was judged evil and banished for unauthorized world-alteration - now, through game-created stains and your vision, Their name will be sanctified anew, returning once more.

5000515.title: White Honey Amber Orb
strings: White Honey Amber Orb
According to Purist Order priests, the White Honey Amber Orb possesses curse-banishing powers.
The Cursed One
The orb emits cleansing light, driving away the resentment and curses clinging to [s2.name].

5000520.title: Lost Treasures
strings: Lost Treasures

You must find a Tyrian golden statuette for the Sultan before your time runs out, but Tyria is an unfamiliar name to you. Time is if the essence, perhaps you can ask that merchant who sells exotic goods.
Treasure of a Lost Kingdom
If this Ritual is not completed within the time limit, the game will end.

The deadline has arrived, yet you still haven't presented the Sultan with satisfactory collections. 
Trembling, you kneel on the palace's cold stone floor, begging for mercy and forgiveness. 
The Sultan smiles ambiguously without speaking. The silence weighs so heavily on your spine, making you feel infinitely small and insignificant. 
You sense death's veil lifting slightly at the corner, but all you can do is wait hopelessly. 
The Sultan taps his throne lightly, jewels and gold making a soft "click." He smiles, having thought of a good idea. 
"Princess Ansuya, if you beg me, I'll spare his life. How about it?" He finally speaks, but not to you. 
You can't help raising your head slightly, glimpsing mild disgust fading from Ansuya's eyes. 
 She bows to the Sultan: "As you wish." 
In that moment, you see a perfect, white god statue collapsing instantly, tumbling from a snowy peak, becoming useless stones. It was just a matter of one sentence... You didn't have to die! You madly jump up, cursing this woman, then the Sultan waves his hand, and you're dragged away. 
Everything that once attracted you now pushes you into an irredeemable abyss. She merely stares coldly through you, through the Sultan, gazing at the immense reflection of this world's arrogance, desire, and hypocrisy.

The Sultan toys with the small golden statuette, rubbing the scratches and old dings caused by years of worn. Its lines and contours are unusually delicate and soft. The pagan god lowers its brows, merciful and compassionate.
Tyria.
He thinks of that feeble tribe again. The gods they served had the same repulsive temperament as they did. Though their princess was somewhat interesting.
The Sultan casts a glance at Consort Ansuya who stood quietly beside him.
Except for the first year she came, this woman had been so quiet and inconspicuous that he almost forgot her name. But now, he recalls the lingering gratification torturing her brought him. She is a lioness hiding her claws. He wants to break her again.
The Sultan casually throws the statuette into the golden plate beside him, like throwing away a used wine glass. It makes a sharp clink. He turns to you: "What's with the ruby ​​on the statue's forehead?"
You quickly present the prepared speech with just the right amount of servility and flattery: "Your Majesty is wise... The Tyrian tribe has long been destroyed under the iron hooves of your troops. I went through all the merchants in the city, only to find this damaged figurine, excavated from ancient ruins, apparently a relic of the Tyrian tribe. But how could I present Your Majesty with something defective? Therefore, I took the initiative to order a craftsmen to repair it as much as possible..."
"Gilding the lily." The Sultan's voice reveals no signs of satisfaction or anger. The weight of his presence makes you bow down even more.
You purposely ordered for the ruby inlay, intentionally ruining the minimalist gentle harmony of the Tyrian style. You are betting that the Sultan did not order for this statuette to appease Consort Ansuya.
Who in the world is worthy of the Sultan's appeasement? He is above all likes and dislikes. He conquers everything he sees with an unparalleled desire for destruction.
You lowered your posture even more, "Please forgive me..."
The Sultan waves his hand and smiles cruelly, "You are dismissed. Your reward shall be delivered to your mansion this evening. Isn't that right, Consort Ansuya?"
Consort Ansuya hides a hint of annoyance under her lashes. She bows. "As you wish."

5000521.title: Consort Ansuya's Visit
strings: Consort Ansuya's Visit

As the Sultan promised before the court, Consort Ansuya arrives in your courtyard. Wearing the cold twilight, she is as solemn and silent as ever, indifferent to the prying eyes of others. As you wish, she is now at your disposal.
Ansuya arrives, as promised.
You choose to indulge with her
You choose to have a long talk with her
If you and Ansuya share the same goal, she will help you.
You need to choose carefully
If you can prove that you and Ansuya share the same ideals, she will help you.
You have to make a choice
Tonight, you claim Consort Ansuya
You entered the consort's body, and her mind
You look forward to a luscious display between your wife and the consort
You conspired with the consort
You didn't do anything

You have claimed the coveted Ansuya, the most unique jewel of the Sultan's collection.
You toyed with her like toying with a broken statuette: its grace, dignity, compassion, resolve and divinity snuffed out alongside the candlelight. You write your victory with the tears she finally shed – no longer caring if you ever got close to that bitter heart.
Later, you hear that Consort Ansuya's palace caught fire one night. The fire raged until dawn, reducing everything to ash. In the flames, the night wind carried a handful of pure white sand away into the vast, unsullied sky.

In between kisses, you exchange cold and hard convictions. You beg her to help you.
"You want to kill the Sultan?" Dark fire burns in Ansuya's eyes. She holds your face in scrutiny, determining whether you truly are companions on the same dark path. "What do you want me to do?"
You reveal an unformed plan in hushed tones. You tell her that you need her to help you steal the Sultan's ring. It is a powerful magical artifact that has foiled foolproof assassinations and erased tribes from the surface of the earth. Your only hope of success depends on the ring being removed from the Sultan. And except in a moment of true intimacy, the Sultan will never take it off. 
A ray of hope lights up Ansuya's gray eyes. She reaches the summit in your description of regicide. "I will help you." She promises in the afterglow, steadying herself to sit up straight. "After I return to the palace, I will try to win the Sultan's favor and look for a good opportunity. However, I am afraid I will need your support."
She gives you a token and tells you to seek her in the harem some time later. It is a string of old bells woven together with colorful ropes. You shake them gently and find that they are all mute, making no sound.

You order your wife to change, and then find yourself the most comfortable seat facing the large bed, ready to watch the two gorgeous women pleasure each other. Your wife is shy, but she, too, must have countless fantasies about the consort’s beautiful body?

You hear the sound of silk and jewelry falling to the floor, feel soft skin pressing against your back... and then a dagger slits your throat.

As you slowly fall, you see the consort, her smile radiant.

You take Ansuya to a quiet room and dismiss everyone. "Please forgive me for the way I arranged for our private meeting," you apologized to Ansuya, "but only you can help me with this matter."

You need her to help you steal the Sultan's ring, which is a powerful magical artefact. It has helped the Sultan resist all assassination attempts. It has erased a tribe from the surface of the earth in an instant. Except for in moments of true intimacy, the Sultan will never take it off. And only by taking it from him does your regicide plot have any hope of success.

This ray of hope lights up Ansuya's eyes. Through the hard frost, you can almost touch the humiliation, recalcitrance, and hatred she has suppressed in the deepest part of her soul. "I will help you," she looks at you and promises, with the solemnity of swearing an oath, "Upon my return to the palace, I shall endeavor to regain the Sultan’s favor and await the right moment to act. However, I must confess – I will require your support."

She hands you a token of trust and asks you to find her in the harem after some time has passed. It is a string of old bells woven together with colorful threads. You shake them gently and find that they are mute and make no sound.

You bring Ansuya to a quiet room and dismiss everyone else. You dare not make any sudden moves, as if even breathing a little heavier would be blasphemous.
In the awkward silence, you serve wine for the two of you, trying to find something to talk about. Ansuya simply listens, responding sparingly.
As the wine flowed, you soon became drunk. When you wake up, Ansuya has already left. You can only recall a few scattered words and Ansuya's calm and gentle eyes. A beautiful dream, dissipating in a sigh.

You ask the servant to bring Ansuya to your room, but you have no intention of going there yourself.

You have no lust for desecrating the Sultan's consort. You merely need another way to break that damn card with its depiction of a pair of loving couple. You still remember the day you wedded Maggie. You swore an oath of loyalty to her. You will never have her shed a single tear for you.

It is strange that after so many years, your chest still warms when you think of Maggie's eyes, so full of affection, of love. 

You cannot help knocking on Maggie's door. Taking her into your arms, you kiss her. You know not how long this love you share can sustain you in this terrible game. But at least in this very moment, it still beats in your hearts, alive and strong.

You have your servant bring Ansuya to your room, but you don't intend to go there yourself.

It isn't your desire to defile the king's consort; you simply need a way to break that damned card engraved with the image of lovers. That's all.

Afterwards, when Ansuya sometimes appears in court, she speaks a few words in your favor.

5000522.title: Ansuya's Request I
strings: Ansuya's Request I

Ansuya agrees to help you steal the Sultan's ring, but she must first gain the Sultan's trust and favor, before she will even have an opportunity to enter his bed chamber. This is no easy task... Right now, she needs money to take care of matters in the palace.
Ansuya needs your support
Mute Bells
Requires 10 Gold Coins.
You can do this job yourself, or send any of your followers to do it.
You can either pay 10 Gold Coins to bribe the guard, or utilize the prepared Harem Secret Passage.
Some things can help in infiltration
Some friends who frequent the harem would be very helpful in this task.
It's obviously difficult to get into the Sultan's harem, but you don't have any better option. Pray... Pray that you can succeed.
Your Stealth and Physique determine your full dice count.
You need at least 1 Success to sneak successfully.

Either you can't, or you don't want to, in short, you ignore Ansua's plea for the time being. Ansuya is very disappointed in this, there are some things that she can't do alone, and she needs your support for your common goals.

You ask the Court Physician to bring the money Ansuya requested into the harem, which is a simple task given his position.

Ansuya is very grateful to you. She will use this sum and her savings to arrange for some bold, new outfits.

The Sultan will surely notice her change. In his hubris, he will think that this woman – who has always held her head high in a defiant silence – has finally resigned herself to the master of her fate, broken by a searing lesson in humiliation.

You ask the Jeweler to bring the money Ansuya requested into the harem, which is a simple task as she is a familiar face at the palace.

Ansuya is very grateful to you. She will use this sum and her savings to arrange for some bold, new outfits.

The Sultan will surely notice her change. In his hubris, he will think that this woman – who has always held her head high in a defiant silence – has finally resigned herself to the master of her fate, broken by a searing lesson in humiliation.

Bharat sneaked into the palace at night and knocked on Ansuya's window.
So many years had passed, but when Ansuya opened the window, he still found himself back in Tyria's humble town—he had once knocked on her window just like that, pouring out his "trophies" onto her desk.
What useless things they had been! Beautiful feathers, shiny stones, and sometimes even shabby wood carvings he had made himself... Ansuya would smile softly and gather those worthless little gifts into the most beautiful jewelry boxes.
They had been so young back then. Now, so many years had gone by, and that warm smile had long since vanished from Ansuya's lips.
She accepted the money Bharat brought and thanked him politely, as if she no longer remembered her childhood playmate.
She had long since sorted those trinkets away—counting her own savings, planning how to exchange some for new, floating jewelry and fresh garments.
The Sultan would surely notice her change. In his hubris, he would think that this woman—who has always held her head high in a defiant silence—has finally resigned herself to the master of her fate, broken by a searing lesson in humiliation.

Bharat sneaks into the palace through the secret passage and finds Consort Ansuya, now the darling of the harem.

She has moved to a resplendent palace, wears more extravagant gowns, and dusts her cheeks with a thin layer of rouge, like a bud that blooms once in a lifetime atop a snowy mountain peak. No one can resist such beauty – not even the Sultan.

Ansuya asks Bharat to tell you that as soon as the time is right, she will steal the magic ring for you. Her tone is light and nonchalant, but there is no underplaying the risk she is taking. A single misstep would cost her her life.

For a moment, Bharat wants to take her away, far away. Away from all of this – the truths, the lies, the debts owed, and the vengeance due.

But he cannot.

He sees the fierce flame deep in Ansuya's eyes. All her concessions, her resentment, her forbearance – her entire self – are fuel for this inferno. She will not leave until she sees death and destruction raining down on the faithless, heartless tyrant.

Bharat is unsure whether he should hate you for pushing Ansuya into the pyre of revenge or be grateful to you for granting her wish. He is worried, uncertain. In the end, he can only sigh and implore you to make sure the time for regicide is truly ripe before you ask Ansuya to steal the ring. Otherwise, as soon as the Sultan realizes something is amiss, you know what fate awaits you all.

5000531.title: Search for Tyrian Relic
strings: Search for Tyrian Relic
The name Tyria is unfamiliar to you, but perhaps not to Bharat, the merchant under your roof, who is always selling exotic goods. If you ask him, you might learn something useful.

You find Bharat, explaining your purpose and predicaments. Of course... Well, there is no need for that. The absurd stories about you and those Sultan Cards always spread like wild fire from the court to every corner of the city.
Bharat, who always greets people with a smile, stares at you with an uncharacteristically cold expression. He holds on to the door frame tightly, as if he has used up all his willpower not to punch you in the face.
"Why did you do this? How dare you -" He growled like an angry beast, "You dare to come ask me if I know anything – let me tell you, I know nothing about Tyria. Let the Sultan take your insolent and shameless head!"

A heavy shadow looms over you. The fear of the Sultan, the fear of death, coldly climbs up your spine and neck. You tremble, enduring the seething, impotent rage: "Yes, I will die. Everyone dies, so what? From his consort to the ants on the ground, who can guarantee that they will live to see another day?"
"And that's why you defiled Consort Ansuya? You despicable coward!" Bharat sneers.
"Naturally I had my reason in seeking her out. I-" you stop short, suddenly feeling how pointless your struggles and justifications are. You chuckle weakly. "I want to kill the Sultan, and only she can help me. How about you that? Go and tell that to the Sultan."
Bharat is stunned. He opens his mouth, instinctively looks around the empty street outside, and then pulls you into the house. "How dare you utter such words in the streets, you have a death wish?!"

You find his attitude peculiar. "You... as well?"
Bharat does not answer directly, but inquires into your plan. Seeing you eyeing him without a word, he finally takes a step back as a gesture of faith.
He tells you that the Tyrian tribe had long been destroyed by war... When Tyria were surrounded by enemy forces, the chief reached out to the Sultan for help, and gave his only daughter to the Sultan. The Sultan accepted his offerings of gold and beauty, but after expelling the enemies, he also gladly accepted this modest piece of land as his own. 
The Tyrian people were unwilling to serve such an dishonorable monarch, but after several violent crackdowns and expulsions, the tribe withered, leaving behind nothing but a barren wilderness that the Sultan soon cast aside.
Bharat takes a deep breath and reveals a golden statuette from within a sealed shrine – it has been hidden from the light of day for a long time. Depicting the pagan gods in art is a crime. But it remains sacred. Perhaps divinity only dies when the last believer dies. 
"Listen, I don't want your money. I want you to swear before our God that you will kill the Sultan." Bharat stares at you with burning eyes, "If you renege on your oath, I will haunt you for the rest of my days."
You give Bharat your words and accept this relic of Tyria. Inexplicably, you feel a tremor in your soul, as if you were branded. The ancient eyes of the statuette gleam subtly, as if glancing at you. But upon closer inspection, it was just a trick of the light.

You sense his unusual rage and the fear, buried deep beneath that anger... The fear of the Sultan, the fear of death, coldly coils around his spine, spitting vitriol to you. You laugh, your tone blithe and friendly: "Yes, I will die. Everyone dies, so what? From his consort to the ants on the ground, who can guarantee that they will live to see another day? Especially you... my dear tenant. You are a Tyrian, no? Save your denials. You know the truth." Veins bulge on his arm as he grabs onto the door, but he does not – dares not – close that door. Your theory confirmed, you feel more at ease. "Think about it, with the Sultan's 'clemency', will he allow a rat like you to live in his city? What good is my death to you? You will lose the only friend in this city who dares to lend you a roof over your head." "What kind of a friend are you?" Bharat stares at you sharply. You shrug, "Up to you. I don't mind company on the gallows." Bharat takes a few deep breaths, suppressing his urge to punch your face in here and now. He scratches his hair and finally relents. He pulls you into the house, vexation clear on his face, and shuts the doors and windows. "I have something. I can save your worthless life. On one condition," he pauses, then seems to have made a decision, "you have to help me meet with Ansuya...Consort Ansuya." "Oh? Should I perhaps arrange for your carriage, pack your luggage, and fill your pockets with gold? And even secure the two of you a safe house, then personally escort you out of the city?" You whistle glibly, your tone laced with derision. Bharat blushes and growls: "I have no desire to – it is none of your business! Make an oath, swear that you'll keep your promise, and I'll sell you my treasure. Otherwise, go bother someone else!" You nod and agree. Why not? A promise is but a make belief, based on nothing other than one's conscience. Bharat reveals a golden statuette from within a sealed shrine – it has been hidden from the light of day for a long time. Depicting the pagan gods in art is a crime. But it remains sacred. Perhaps divinity only dies when the last believer dies. Bharat stares at you with burning eyes, "If you renege on your oath, I will haunt you for the rest of my days." You accept this relic of Tyria. Inexplicably, you feel a tremor in your soul, as if you were branded. The ancient eyes of the statuette gleam subtly, as if glancing at you. But upon closer inspection, it was just a trick of the light.

A heavy shadow looms over you. The fear of the Sultan, the fear of death, coldly climbs up your spine and neck. You tremble, enduring the seething, impotent rage: "Yes, I will die. Everyone dies, so what? From his consort to the ants on the ground, who can guarantee that they will live to see another day?"

Bharat watches you with a cold sneer, those eyes, filled with a unfamiliar disdain, pierce through your lies and excuses like a sharp blade. Without gracing your despicable display with another word, he slams the door. You hear the clunk of the lock being turned, and you know you will have to find another way.
