The expedition team rushes into the canyon under the protection of [s2.name]'s spell, only to find a griffin nesting there, awakening to the sound of its next feast...
 [s3.name] draws the bow and shoots, but the griffin's claws are faster. In the chaos, the team scrambles forward as each one of their comrades is torn apart...

The expedition plunges into the canyon under the protection of [s2.name]’s magic. A griffon nests here, and you are the feast that has stumbled willingly into its jaws…

But [s3.name] is quick – an arrow takes its left eye. Then Jabal strikes, driving steel deep into the beast’s heart. Though it reeks of musk and carrion, the path ahead is clear now.

Amidst the black stone forest sculpted by storms, you struggle to trudge on...
Countless snakes emerge from the shadows, slithering to catch up with you.
At this moment, [s4.name] steps up, igniting [s4.gender(his, her)] cloak to fend off the snakes, while the rest of you hasten forward, not wasting the precious time [s4.gender] bought.

[s2.name]’s magic is spent. Jabal vanishes into the howling dust. The rest press forward, searching for his tracks, but only smears of blood stretch into the storm.
The wait is a slow death. The wind buries half the party before the world stills, before silence falls like a heavy shroud.
Then – the sky clears. And there, in the distance, Jabal runs toward you, something brilliant clutched in his hands.

[s2.name]’s magic is spent. Jabal vanishes into the howling dust. The rest press forward, searching for his tracks, but only smears of blood stretch into the storm.

At last, [s5.name] finds him beneath a slab of rock, barely conscious. [s5.name] then drags the band out of the canyon, almost dying in the process. From his sickbed, Jabal swears he will return. But you are unsure if you can afford another loss like this.

[s2.name] tears the winds apart, watching as Jabal charges toward the canyon’s end. The rest stumble forward in pursuit, until a boulder falls, sundering their path.

If we have the support of [Intelligence], we will have a better chance of winning.

[s2.name] does not walk to the altar by choice. His hollow eyes meet those of his old companions. A shadow writhes into the cavity of his opened belly, gorging itself on warm, living flesh. The others seize the moment, taking the relic the spirit once guarded.

The adventurers choose to fight the darkness. Alas, their magic is too feeble before the encroaching shadow. As the monster collapses – reeking, glistening, bleeding bile – the exhausted warriors turn to count their loses, only to see the remains of [s5.name], dissolving into a pool of rank, bubbling filth.

The adventurers choose to fight the darkness. Alas, their magic is too feeble before the encroaching shadow. The darkness devour them one by one... Only Jabal makes it back, by luck. He swears he will have his revenge, but would anyone join his fight now?

The adventurers choose to fight the darkness. Alas, their strength is too feeble before the encroaching shadow. The darkness devour them one by one... Only Jabal makes it back, by luck. He swears he will have his revenge, but would anyone join his fight now?

The adventurers choose to fight the darkness. They have come prepared, their magical barrier holding firm against the dark miasma. The monster's brute force is no match for the battle-hardened adventurers... As the monster collapses – reeking, glistening, bleeding bile – the Shadow Compass emits a brilliant purple light. The powerful artifact calls to its new master.

5000705.title: Forest of the Jinn
strings: Forest of the Jinn

Legends say the jinn are as beautiful as they are cruel, yet many claim to have won the Jinn Queen's treasures through wit and deceit... Jabal’s notes speak of a wager: triumph, and the jinn will be trapped to serve you... You wonder what the cost of failure would be.
Will the adventurous general come here this time?
A guide, with at least 4 in Survival.
A bulwark, with at least 4 in Combat.
To deal with the jinn's trickery, you need someone clever, with at least 4 in Wisdom.
To engage the Jinn Queen, you need a messenger with at least 4 in Charisma.

The entrance to the Forest of the Jinn is covered with bitter briars. A single scratch, and your mind is drowned in its worst pains. [s2.name] parts the thorns with cautious hands, clearing the way. At the path’s end, the flowering branches stir, twisting like hungry serpents, but Jabal seizes them with his bare hands.
He weeps long after the party's escape. But he does not share what the thorns made him remember.

The entrance to the Forest of the Jinn is covered with bitter briars. A single scratch, and your mind is drowned in its worst pains. [s2.name] parts the thorns with cautious hands, clearing the way...
At the end of the path, the flowering branches stirs, suddenly coming to life, and trips your guide. He stumbles, lost among the thorns... Even as the party flees, [s2.name]'s screams linger.

A tiny jinn the size of a pea stops the adventurers, demanding a wrestling match with not just one but two of you at a time. Jaball and [s3.name] both surge forward, only to see the jinn blow on his own thumb, growing into a giant three times taller than a person in an instant. He plays with the party's strongest warriors as if they were toys.
Suddenly, [s3.name] seizes an opportunity and stabs the jinn's bulging belly – the jinn deflates like a balloon, and is blown away in a spray of foul-smelling gas. The expedition seizes this chance to proceed.

A tiny jinn the size of a pea stops the adventurers, demanding a wrestling match with not just one but two of you at a time. Jaball and [s3.name] both surge forward, only to see the jinn blow on his own thumb, growing into a giant three times taller than a person in an instant. He easily defeats the party's strongest fighters.
The jinn grabs [s3.name], and opening his enormous mouth, swallows him whole with a guttural gulp...
Just when you think all is lost, a dagger pierces out from his belly... [s3.name]'s final strike.
the jinn deflates like a balloon, and is blown away in a spray of foul-smelling gas. The expedition seizes this chance to proceed.

The next challenge is a game of chess. The jinn sage smiles, whispering that the price is sanity itself. [s4.name] steps forward with glee. The jinn twist the rules at will, but he twists them back, trapping the creature in its own contradictions. In the end, the sage wearing a big hat swells – bloats – bursts like a fire cracker. An erudite smell fills the air.

The next challenge is a game of chess. The jinn sage smiles, whispering that the price is sanity itself. [s4.name] plays well, but the jinn twist the rules at will. Soon, he loses his king. And something else. The twisted laws of the game have lodged deep in his mind... Fortunately, you are allowed to continue forward. But [s4.name] – [s4.name] must be watched, lest he start smearing feces upon his own skin.

Through trial and torment, you reach the Jinn Queen. There is no wager here – only her favor, or the lack of it, depending on her mood.

[s5.name] flatters her beauty, her wisdom with passion and poetry. Yet her gaze lingers on Jabal's handsome features instead...

She lifts a hand. The brave warrior’s eyes fill with devotion, with love. He falls to his knees like a loyal hound, worshipping at the queen's feet. And the rest of you receive your prize: a lantern, and the jinns trapped within.

Through trial and torment, you reach the Jinn Queen. There is no wager here – only her favor, or the lack of it, depending on her mood.

[s5.name] is struck by inspiration and entertains the queen with tales about the Sultan's Game. The queen rewards the party with mercy. She gifts them with a Jinn Lantern, through which she can now watch the stories unfold with her own eyes.

5000706.title: Jabal's Friendship
strings: Jabal's Friendship

Legend has it, guided by the Shadow Compass and the Jinn Lantern, the hero will pass through the distant oasis and open a path with the Amulet of Wind, embarking on a journey to save the world... You have braved these trials, yet there is no world in need of saving...

Jabal, however, is delighted. At the very least, his ancestors’ notes were not entirely fraudulent.

From now on, he will fight by your side and help you win this cruel game.
Jabal is waiting for you.
Appropriate Conviction.
The General regards you as a close confidant. He will become your Follower in a few days time without need of further input.
Placing the appropriate Convictions can change some details.
You show him the Sultan's evil

After remaining silent for a long time, Jabal promised that if one day you faced the Sultan in battle, he would stand by your side.
 Considering that his family has guarded the Sultan for generations, this promise is very valuable.
 As a result, on the day of the final battle, the Sultan's Champion will be reduced by one.

You reveal the truth to him. The world moves inexorably towards the awakening of the Lord of Darkness, who slumbers in the depths beneath. Alas, he is not one to heed the call of truth. Or perhaps the weight of his education, the chains of reason, keep him from joining you... Jabal leaves without a word. Perhaps the next time you meet, it would be with blades drawn.

5000709.title: Sword Duel
strings: Sword Duel
Jabal demands a public duel with you; as so inclined the intention of the Sultan.
Glory-Long-Gone General
You must do it yourself.
You can take this to break a Bloodshed Card that matches the Jabal's tier
Consumable
This is a life-and-death battle
Draw your sword.
The number of dice provided by your Physique and Combat is affected by the enemy's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 3 Successes to win the duel.
You avoided this duel, but do you really think death can be evaded?
You should realize that with your current [Physique] and [Combat], it's nothing but suicide.
If we have the support of [Intelligence], we will have a better chance of winning.

Jabal falls beneath your blade.
No one cheers, except for the Sultan, whose laughter echoes through the court.
"Since he loved fighting so much, let him fight to the death. This is the reward I grant him," the Sultan says with a smile. "Now, clean up the floor."
Only then do the courtiers follow with weak applause. Like frightened quails, they dart furtive glances your way, silently counting their secrets and dreading which might become your weapon.

Jabal's blade pierces your heart.
Through fading vision, you see the Sultan descend from his throne to inspect your fate. He smiles, poking your body with his finger.
"Well done, Jabal. From now on, the Sultan's game is yours to play."

Yet, the final breath you draw is a sigh of relief.

You circle the pillar, dodging while hurling venomous words to distract Jabal. Finally, you seize the moment when his guard drops and plunge your blade into his heart.

Jabal falls.

No one cheers, except for the Sultan, whose laughter echoes through the court.

“What an interesting fight! It's the reward he deserves,” the Sultan chuckles. “Well, clean up the floor.”

You coat your weapon with poison. A small, shallow cut is all it takes. Then comes the wait for victory.
Jabal falls.
No one cheers, except for the Sultan, whose laughter echoes through the court.
“He loved fighting so much, yet he couldn’t even die like a warrior. What a perfect punishment,” the Sultan says, clapping for you with a smile. Only then do the courtiers follow with weak applause, more like sighs of sorrow than celebration.

The floor of the court is overflown in the General's sprouting nectar. Though hastily as his life slipped from him, that his death seeped into the tongues of hypocritical commoners and atomistic balladeers.

5000710.title: Guardian
strings: Guardian

You fell an insignificant wench – still, although the rules of the Sultan's Game protect you, Nabhani mourns her still. He demands a duel to the death with God as witness, vowing revenge for his friend.
You've seen fools dueling for a prostitute's body or favor, but this is the first time you've seen someone duel for a prostitute's life.
You may fight the battle yourself, or choose a noble follower to fight on your behalf.

The most handsome swordsman in the capital has died, his eyes full of resentment. But his last words were: I pity your soul, poor friend.
The most handsome swordsman in the capital has died, his eyes full of resentment, looking in your direction, whispering... The onlookers are too noisy, you can't hear...

You strike his sword from his hand and corner him in the arena. The crowd roars – half shouting for you to kill him, half begging him to surrender. 

“However you wish to mourn her, it ends here.” you tell Nabhani. “She might be pleased to see you fight for her, but if you die here, she will still weep.” 

Thus, you turn your back to the avenger...
And as you reach the edge of the arena, he admits his defeat.

Your fighter placed the blade against Nabhani's neck, a neck longed for by countless noblewomen... The spectators are shouting, they crave romantic blood, and this unparalleled swordsman should die for love in the arena.
But you always love to go against the tide, you raised your hands in a gesture of forgiveness and left the scene amid everyone's surprised gazes.
His blade pierced through your heart, you saw sympathy in his eyes, you heard him praying for your soul, you heard the crowd cheering... but everything became blurred.

He killed your warrior, instantly turning away, apparently abhorring the crowd. 
At least for you, it's over, though from now, you've lost a friend and gained an enemy in the court.
Nabhani spits on you, people despise you, and from now on, in the palace, you lose a friend and gain an enemy.
You cursed your opponent right to death with vicious language! You've won!
You cursed him into running away in disgrace! You've won!
You have applied poison to your weapon, and you only need to make a small cut, and then you can wait for victory! With that stratagem, you've won!
Although you don't want to kill him, the poisoned weapon leaves you no choice! You've won! Even without using a Bloodshed Card, he is doomed.

5000712.title: An Interesting Incident
strings: An Interesting Incident

Nabhani – the most gorgeous swordsman in the capital, and the most adept user of his other sword come nighttime callings – knocks on your door. You don't know what he intends to do... surely he didn't come just to mock himself?
The Most Handsome Swordsman in the Capital
You can entertain him personally or let Maggie do it
Either you or your wife, someone must welcome the guest.

Unlike the rumored frivolity, he was courteous and graceful in his every move – of course, these are all told to you by your wife afterward. You can see she highly approves of the man, even needing her to tiptoe with her words to avoid giving you any bad impressions.
But that's not important. The key point is that as an excellent Swordsman, Nabhani expresses sympathy for your plight and is willing to lend a helping hand whenever you need it.

Nabhani spent half the evening mocking you, but unlike those who prey on your misfortunes, he shows genuine interest in the Sultan's Game:
"From now on, should there be any adventures or other interesting activities, you may consider Nabhani your ally."
After saying this, he quietly leaves, stealing your best bottle of wine on his way out.

5000713.title: Unreliable Ally
strings: Unreliable Ally

Clearly, in Nabhani's imagination, the Sultan's Game should be full of skirmish, sex, and scandals. His sword should be clanging steels, but the only clanging that echoed was the clanging of accounted Gold Coins, counting days after days, after days... This obviously couldn't satisfy his restless heart. Soon enough, he returned to his former life of debauchery. Perhaps once he's bored, he will come back to check if you're still alive every now and then.
Nabhani is dashing outside
Find a female with enough Charisma to go get him... or a bottle of wine.
Can the Sultan's card bring him some new excitement?
He plays around and comes back to see you once a week.
Only a female with Charisma in 5 or higher can call him back to help you next time. A bottle of wine may work, too. Wait... Perhaps using a Sultan Card?
Using different Sultan Cards leads to entirely different storylines, but the cards don’t always get broken immediately.
Nabhani returns with unsteady steps.
Already played~
Not today ~
Already proved myself here ~

You look at him with concern, ready to ask, but he simply waves his hand, sighs deeply, and stays silent.
Not long after, Nayla comes to see you. She is in high spirits, helping herself to the juiciest grapes off your table. "I could never understand it," she complains, "Nabhani has slept with almost every woman in the capital, yet only now has he finally spent the night with me.” Then, with a playful smile, Nayla cups your face in her hands. "Thanks to you, my dear [player.name], I finally ate him. Oh, he's so delicious!! Not only in... well, that sense, but he's so sweet too. His tongue is absolutely a treasure of this empire!"
You couldn't think of anything new to bring Nabhani back.
You couldn't think of anything new about carnality to bring Nabhani back.
Clearly, Nabhani has long lost interest in "conquest."
While you struggle to survive, Nabhani is out having fun.
Nabhani had someone leave a note for you, asking you to prepare good wine as he would return tomorrow.
Only beauties or fine liquor can motivate Nabhani, but only for a short while.
You show him a Carnality Card
Show Nabhani the Conquest Card.
Temporal Matters
Fortunate Timing
Time to go, [player.name]~!
Have fun to your heart's content
Enough is enough
House of Delights remains closed; Carnality must wait

Nabhani returns to your courtyard with great enthusiasm.

He winks at you mysteriously: "Have you heard that the House of Delights has been trying out something new lately? Let's go together–but remember to bring your best cloth; we are in the presence of men."

You're full of doubt: you've always heard of the Lady of Delights wearing heavy makeup and competing for attention to greet guests, but it's the first time hearing that guests need to dress elaborately. However, you calmly nod, indicating that you agree.

Nabhani fiddles with the card you brought and bursts into laughter: "Worried about this card? Oh, good friend, I have a brilliant idea!"

He cheerfully leaves with your card, and seeing him like this, you suddenly have doubts... showing him the Conquest Card might not have been a good idea...
Seeing the card, Nabhani ruefully shakes head: “I do know of a luxurious spot, but sadly, recent flames burnt that very slave market to the ground.”
Seeing your card, Nabhani suddenly remembered something: "Did you know that the slave market we visited last time was completely burned down?"
You show him an Extravagance Card, and Nabhani happily comes back to you. He winks at you, "Great, time to spruce up our activity varieties a little!"

You had [s2.name] summon Nabhani back to help. But of course, neither of them knows that a dagger awaits this playboy... Always with eyes only for beauty and indulgence, Nabhani finally shifts his gaze to you. Those eyes are heavy with pity, devoid of hatred, as if he still seeks to offer you comfort. But the blood filling his throat silences him.
Although there has been no conflict between you before, you really can't stand his frivolous attitude... So let a duel under God's gaze mettle the resolve you two carry.

You send someone to track down Nabhani at the House of Delights, where chaos has broken out.

 A paying customer has been waiting far too long for the girl he requested, but was left ignored. Frustrated, he stands up, pulls aside the veil, and sees that most of the girls are fawning over Nabhani in the inner chamber. The man, furious at being ignored, challenges Nabhani, the center of attention. Two men head to the open ground in front of the House of Delights, ready to settle the matter. 

When you and [s2.name] arrive, a familiar girl hurries over and pleads with you, as a powerful minister, to mediate the duel. If any patron were to die there, it would spell disaster for everyone in the House of Delights.

You responded to his summons in time

Abdul is very pleased with your courtesy. Half a candle burns down in empty prattle. Then, he casually mentions that Murtaz did not appear at the court today. Abdul smiles, but there is a malicious glint in his eyes. "Murtaz is the Sultan’s most trusted courtier. You should talk to him. I hope to see him at the Sultan's golden palace tomorrow – and every day after that. Don’t disappoint me."

Abdul is very pleased with your courtesy. Half a candle burns down in empty prattle. Then, he casually mentions that Murtaz did not appear at the court today. Abdul smiles, his tone a veiled threat, his eyes hold a malicious glint. "Murtaz is the Sultan’s most trusted courtier. You should talk to him. I hope to see him at the Sultan's golden palace tomorrow – and every day after that. Don’t disappoint me."

5000721.title: Absent Courtier
strings: Absent Courtier

You are sent to the house of Murtaz. When you arrive, you see a priest stepping out of his doorway. Murtaz himself looks exhausted, hollowed out. In the silence, you catch the scent of musk, camphor, and borneol. A funeral, without question. You remember him now. His wife and father both perished in the Sultan’s Game.
Murtaz has just come out of a funeral.
You can handle this yourself, or send a follower to do it.
You can comfort him with 3 Gold Coins.
If you mess up, there’s still a chance to fix it. But if you never try, there’s no chance at all.
You can offer him some consolation with gold.
You can also achieve your goal leveraging on your Infamy or Influence, if you have at least 5 in either.
Abdul was displeased with the delay in hearing from you. He had another nobleman do it for him, and that nobleman went around condescendingly proclaiming your incompetence because of it.
You chose to coerce him
You choose to comfort him

After you explained the purpose of your visit, Murtaz nearly throws you out in rage. He leaps to his feet, cursing the Sultan’s cruelty, cursing your callousness. Has he not suffered enough? And yet here you are, pressing him further. He pours his grief and fury onto you, and when there is nothing left, he collapses to his knees. He sobs as he agrees to your request.

He will attend the court tomorrow morn, because the Sultan demands it, because he lacks the spine to refuse. Because you both know the truth: when the Sultan wanted to break those cards, it was Murtaz himself who delivered his wife and father to the palace doors.
After you explained the purpose of your visit, Murtaz throws you out in rage. You will have to make another visit.

Murtaz tells you that his mother had been ill for a long time, crushed by the weight of sorrow. Last night, she breathed her last. A family was shattered, all for a game.
Murtaz complains bitterly, cursing the Sultan with the harshest of words. But when you tentatively bring up the possibility of rebellion, he jumps up and turns his fury and profanities on you, as if not doing so would prove his own impotence.
Your sympathy and pity turn to dust. Finally, you lose patience and cut him off, "Don’t think I don’t know! You yourself sent your wife and father to the palace, to the Sultan and his cards!" You harshly inform him that the Sultan wants to see him tomorrow before leaving, not giving him a second glance. Will Murtaz attend court? He will. You have no doubt.

Afterward, Vizier Abdul is quite satisfied. He believes the Sultan will finally notice the deep-seated resentment that Murtaz has been harboring at court. 

You, however, find it all ridiculous – the kingdom's vizier has been reduced to nothing more than a court jester.

5000722.title: Report to the Vizier
strings: Report to the Vizier
Abdul has ordered Murtaz to attend the court every morning, without fail. He asks you to bring back Murtaz’s promise of compliance.
Murtaz's Promise
If you fail to fulfill Abdul’s request, you will be punished for your incompetence.
You failed
You succeeded
You failed to bring back Murtaz’s promise of compliance. And so, for the time being, you replace him as the one people side-eye and snicker at.

Abdul is pleased. Good. Now the Sultan can sit in his palace and enjoy the sight of Murtaz – his rage and hatred buried beneath layers of his own impotence.

You, however, find it laughable. The Vizier of the kingdom, reduced to nothing more than a court jester arranging performances.

5000723.title: Audience with the Vizier
strings: Audience with the Vizier
Abdul sends another servant, summoning you to his residence. It may not be that urgent, but he does not like being ignored.
Abdul is furious.
You must go in person
If you do not go, you may face criticism from the Vizier in the palace later.
Abdul hates being ignored, it makes him feel very humiliated. He will surely seize every opportunity to slander you to the Sultan in the palace. Be careful.

You suspect Abdul has come to see you about Murtaz, and you are correct. Somehow, that coward has found the audacity to threaten vengeance against the Sultan. A drunken boast, perhaps, but Abdul –ever the Sultan’s most faithful servant – will never tolerate such treason. He has chosen you to teach Murtaz a lesson. A lesson he will never forget.

5000724.title: How Dare the Worm?
strings: How Dare the Worm?

You take Abdul’s hint. He wants you to kill Murtaz, the prancing fool who dares claim vengeance against the Sultan. But more pressing is the question: how does he plan to do that? What gave the coward the nerve to rebel? You should find him, see if his newfound courage has any worth – any value you might claim for yourself.
Murtaz is drowning in delusions.
You can handle this yourself, or send an ally.

Abdul is repulsed with the lack of news from you, feeling that his prestige as a Vizier is being challenged. You don't know what he did, but during that time, you became the subject of whispers in the court.

When you visit Murtaz's residence again, you find it completely changed.
The living room is covered by tapestries with strange totemic embroideries. Lanterns flicker in the sunless room. A neurotic fervor gleams in Murtaz's shifty eyes. He does not even notice your arrival, mumbling in prayers that you can barely make out, words like "condemnation" and "Sultan"... It seems he has no intention of rebellion. This coward has placed all his hopes for revenge on some obscure deity.
How awfully disappointing. Now, you are faced with a choice. Will you kill him and report back to the Vizier, or spare this poor soul?

5000725.title: End the Pain
strings: End the Pain
You decide to kill this pathetic person and end the despair and pain he dares not end.
Murtaz is praying to the devil
Anyone can kill him, anyone at all.
Murtaz’s life can be used to break a Bronze or Stone Bloodshed Card.
You can use a Bloodshed Card, but it would change the nature of this action.

Abdul is repulsed with the lack of news from you, feeling that his prestige as a Vizier is being challenged. You don't know what he did, but during that time, you became the subject of whispers in the court.

You judge this wretched soul, proclaiming his sins for all to hear. The priests arrive, destroying the strange totems. The people argue – were they truly conduits to demons, or merely a coward’s desperate delusions? As for Murtaz’s meager belongings, you pocket them while no one is watching.

You kill Murtaz and offer his death in exchange for breaking a single Bloodshed Card. But rumors spread like rot in the dark. Some say the wicked totems were your doing, that you orchestrated this to seize what little wealth Murtaz had left.

The Vizier is very pleased with the outcome. He examined the pale head, sneering at the pitiful hatred that it would never act upon. How could anyone dare to attract the Sultan’s attention with such means? How shameless...
You listened to Abdul’s muttering, and the hidden emotion in his slightly squinting eyes sent a chill down your spine.

5000726.title: Report to the Vizier
strings: Report to the Vizier
Abdul asked you to teach Murtaz a lesson. He expects you to bring back Murtaz’s head, but are you really willing to do his dirty work?
You must present Murtaz’s head, or get his promise.
If you fail to fulfill Abdul’s request, you will be punished for your incompetence.

Abdul grows impatient with your silence. He takes your delay as an insult, an affront to his authority as the Vizier. You do not know what he has done in response, but for a time, the court whispers and snickers, and all its tales are about you.

The Vizier is very pleased with the outcome. He examined the pale head, sneering at the pitiful hatred that it would never act upon. How could anyone dare to attract the Sultan’s attention with such means? How shameless...
You listened to Abdul’s muttering, and the hidden emotion in his slightly squinting eyes sent a chill down your spine.

The Vizier listened to your report impassively, appearing unsatisfied. Things had gotten to this point, and he couldn't find a pretense to target that poor man any further – but wait, why? Murtaz posed no real threat to him... You left the Vizier’s mansion lost in thought, unable to understand what it all meant.

5000727.title: Spare him
strings: Spare him

You decide to spare Murtaz. He is nothing more than a man driven mad by the Sultan's cruelties. You will try to dissuade him from speaking so openly of his schemes – it is not wise, and you will have something to satisfy the Vizier.
Murtaz is praying to the devil
You can meet with him yourself, or send a follower.
Perhaps there is something that can help you.
To persuade him, you need sufficient Charisma and Sociability.
Can you persuade Murtaz?
Your Charisma and Sociability determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to persuade him.

Abdul is repulsed with the lack of news from you, feeling that his prestige as a Vizier is being challenged. You don't know what he did, but during that time, you became the subject of whispers in the court.

You try to tell him not to go around screaming his hatred for the Sultan. He looks at you in shock, his face turning red as he stammers, finally swearing he has never said anything of the sort publicly. You immediately realize that it was likely a word of jest among drunken friends, that was later betrayed...
You are left speechless and can only warn him not to speak of such blasphemy to anyone again. Murtaz opens his mouth, but in the end just nods silently. Only when he escorts you out does he finally say, "You know, I really heard voices from the void. I will succeed, just wait and see. I curse the Sultan. He will pay for all this...!"
Twisted, dark currents of madness flicker in the gloomy depths of his eyes.

You try to reason with him, to warn him against his folly. His face burns red with anger. "You understand nothing!" he shouts before throwing you out. Through the door, you hear him sobbing, whispering frantic prayers. This madness is all he has left, his only hope.

The Vizier listened to your report impassively, appearing unsatisfied. Things had gotten to this point, and he couldn't find a pretense to target that poor man any further – but wait, why? Murtaz posed no real threat to him... You left the Vizier’s mansion lost in thought, unable to understand what it all meant.

5000728.title: Audience with the Vizier
strings: Audience with the Vizier
Abdul sent a servant to summon you to his residence. His matter may not be important, but he does not like being ignored.
Vizier Abdul is summoning you
You must go in person, or send a follower.
If you do not go, you may face criticism from the Vizier in the palace later.
You do not visit him
Abdul despises being ignored. It wounds his pride. He will seize every opportunity to slander you before the Sultan. You would do well to tread carefully.

Abdul is very pleased with your courtesy. Half a candle burns down in empty prattle. Then, he finally comes to the point. A young widow Fatuna has inherited a small fortune from her late husband. But it is improper for a woman to hold such wealth. Abdul wants you to take it from her. How? He does not care. Threats, slander, disgrace. Whatever it takes.

5000729.title: Fortune Scattered
strings: Fortune Scattered
Abdul covets the wealth Fatuna inherited. He sends you to take what was never yours to claim – by whatever filthy means necessary.
Fatuna's husband is dead.
You can handle this matter yourself, or send a follower.
Maybe there is something that can help you persuade them.
You can leverage your Influence or Infamy to coerce Fatuna. Otherwise, you must persuade her with your Charisma and Sociability.
You knock on Fatuna's door, unsure of how to start this conversation...
Your Charisma and Sociability determine your full dice count.
You need at least 1 Success to persuade her. 3 Successes will yield the best result.

You fabricate and spread a barrage of filthy rumors, leaving Fatuna with no way to defend herself. In the end, unable to endure the shame, Fatuna dies by her own hand. You claim her wealth with ease. But the people are not blind. They see you for what you are. And they spit on your name.

You inform Fatuna of Abdul's plot and urge her to part with some of her wealth. She is shaken by your grave expression and hurriedly producing a chest of gold and jewels, begging for your help. And so, under your careful orchestration, news spread of how the Vizier has drained her of her wealth. The scavengers withdraw, their appetites sated.

You inform Fatuna of Abdul's plot and urge her to part with some of her wealth. She wavers, uncertain, but at last, worn down by your persistence, she relents. She gives you a small sum and asks you to leave her be.

You inform Fatuna of Abdul's plot and urge her to part with some of her wealth. She scoffs, unimpressed, and has you thrown out. A woman who shows even the slightest weakness will be devoured by wolves. She knows this all too well.

5000730.title: Report to the Vizier
strings: Report to the Vizier
Abdul has asked you to plunder Fatuna's fortune for him.
Abdul has an estimation of Fatuna's wealth. You need to give him at least 10 Gold Coins.
If you fail to fulfill Abdul’s request, you will be punished for your incompetence.

Abdul grows impatient with your silence. He takes your delay as an insult, an affront to his authority as the Vizier. If you cannot squeeze Fatuna, clearly you should have taken some gold out of your own coffer. Whatever he has done, for a long time, the court whispers and points to you, as if you have committed an unforgivable crime.

The Vizier accepts the money you bring, no question asked. He cannot care less about Fatuna or where the gold came from.

He only smiles, letting the coins spill through his fingers. You hear him murmur that the Sultan has been considering a campaign against a tribe, but the military fund was short. And yet, how fortunate! His most loyal, most resourceful servant – Abdul – has so effortlessly solved the problem.

You do not ask if Abdul will mention your name to the Sultan. You already know the answer. The Sultan does not care where his gold comes from either.

5000731.title: Project Investment
strings: Project Investment

A female craftsman who calls herself an inventor came to your door, eagerly and enigmatically introducing you to her latest research project. She assured you that the development had reached its final stage and that she just needed a little more sponsorship to complete this unprecedented great invention – an instrument capable of unveiling secrets beyond the starry sky.
Artisan Mahir
You can assist Mahir personally or send a follower.
Mahir hopes you can sponsor 5 Gold Coins.
You can break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower
Some items may be useful during the research.
Wisdom lays the foundation, and gold brings success.
Invention carries risks, so invest cautiously.

Moved by Mahir's words, you give her a significant sponsorship. The mysteries of the firmament, the celestial abode of the divine... you aspire, you crave, you anxiously await the day Mahir completes her work...
Your Wisdom and Gold Coins provide you with the full number of dice rolls.
You need at least 5 Successes to complete the research.
If you don't have time, I will come to you later! – A female artisan who has waited for many days without a response

You invested a significant amount of money in an unknown craftsman, and the Sultan allowed you to resolve a Sultan Card for it. Mahir used the excess funds to build an observatory. She drags you over with the promise of an unforgettable night together. She shows you a complex and magnificent instrument, with intricate patterns conforming to some natural logic and rhythm. Through the lens, you peer into the distant starry sky, the timeless gleam of faraway starts captured in your eyes, while Mahir's excited voice echoed in your ears.
"I knew it... You know, I always felt that we are all governed by a force, just like these stars, moving in definite trajectories. I want to discover the laws governing that force, governing everything. That is my dream."
"I think people call that foce 'God,'" you reply instinctively. The realm of God is quietly shedding its veil of mystery. Now, you have gleamed it. In the future, you will reach it.

Mahir has completed the project. She shows you a complex and magnificent instrument, with intricate patterns conforming to some natural logic and rhythm. Through the lens, you peer into the distant starry sky, the timeless gleam of faraway starts captured in your eyes, while Mahir's excited voice echoed in your ears.
"I knew it... You know, I always felt that we are all governed by a force, just like these stars, moving in definite trajectories. I want to discover the laws governing that force, governing everything. That is my dream."
"I think people call that foce 'God,'" you reply instinctively. The realm of God is quietly shedding its veil of mystery. Now, you have gleamed it. In the future, you will reach it.

You invested a large sum in an nobody artisan. The Sultan allows you to break an Extravagance Card with this. However, people's mockery turn into prediction. Mahir could not overcome the technical challenges, despite her best efforts. The completion of the project has been indefinitely postponed. She forces a smile, saying, "I've always felt that everything is governed by an unseen force. I want to discover the laws governing that force, governing everything, but..." She shakes her head, sighs, and hands you a pair of crystal glasses. "They can help you see the world more clearly. I hope they would be of use to you."

Mahir could not overcome the technical challenges, despite her best efforts. The completion of the project has been indefinitely postponed. She forces a smile, saying, "I've always felt that everything is governed by an unseen force. I want to discover the laws governing that force, governing everything, but..." She shakes her head, sighs, and hands you a pair of crystal glasses. "They can help you see the world more clearly. I hope they would be of use to you."

5000732.title: Project Investment II
strings: Project Investment II

Mahir is again inspired. She touts a new elixir that can grant the body limitless vigor and unleash the deep-seated powers of the soul. It would be a groundbreaking achievement, if it can actually be made. But... the chances sound slim...
Mahir is inspired again.
You can assist Mahir personally or send a follower.
Mahir hopes you can sponsor 5 Gold Coins.
You can choose to break an Extravagance Card or Bloodshed Card of Bronze tier or lower.
Some items may be useful during the research.
Wisdom lays the foundation, and gold brings success.
Invention carries risks, so invest cautiously.
Mahir's vision persuades you. You give her a significant sponsorship. Abundant vigor, eternal life... you long for it, you yearn for it, anxiously waiting for the day Mahir completes her work...
Your Wisdom and Gold Coins provide you with the full number of dice rolls.
You need at least 5 Successes to complete the research.
If you don't have time, I will come to you later! – A female artisan who has waited for many days without a response

Mahir brings you three vials of impossibly clear liquid, indistinguishable from water – yet tests reveal a vitality pulsing within. She tells you how these tinctures have saved the dying, halted a plague, reversed the decree of death itself. But they must never meet open flame. The concentrated essence, distilled to its purest form, would unleash all its energy in an instant.

You accept her gift. And while she speaks, elated, unguarded, you drive a dagger into her heart. Her words falter, her pupils glaze, the light within them arrested and then dispersed.

The Water of Life does not save her. You regard the blasphemer’s corpse with cold detachment – eternal stars, eternal life, these are the dominion of the divine. She has paid in blood for her trespasses.

Mahir has failed. Something has gone wrong in the distillation – her process yields only disappointment. At last, she arrives at your door, head bowed, burdened by defeat. With a wan smile, she lifts a few bottles for you to see. "At the very least," she says, "I can promise this is the strongest liquor you'll ever taste."

You take the gift. And while she stands there, unguarded, you drive a dagger into her heart. She stares at you, stunned, unable to comprehend what has just happened.

Foolish blasphemer. Did she not know? The devout do not drink for pleasure. She not only dared to stain your faith, but also dared to reach for the heavens – the domain of the divine. And for that, she must pay in blood.

You invested a large sum in an nobody artisan. The Sultan allows you to break an Extravagance Card with this. Your lavish investment fuels progress. Soon, Mahir brings you three vials of impossibly clear liquid, indistinguishable from water – yet tests reveal a vitality pulsing within. She tells you how these tinctures have saved the dying, halted a plague, reversed the decree of death itself. But they must never meet open flame. The concentrated essence, distilled to its purest form, would unleash all its energy in an instant. No mortal could withstand that blast.

You accept her gift, offering words of comfort. And so, for a night, you share the spirits Mahir has brought – thick, heady, burning through thought and sense alike. It scours away the failure and regret, leaving only laughter and cheer, dissolving all things into a blissful, primal oblivion.

5000733.title: Recruit Mahir
strings: Recruit Mahir
After two projects of collaboration, Mahir considers you her best partner and hopes to establish a closer, more stable, long-term relationship with you.
Mahir wants to become your companion.
Mahir wants to become your follower.
You can arrange for her to continue her researches by placing her in the "Methinks" area.

Mahir has become your follower. She is not concerned with what deity you follow or what ideals you hold; she is here because of you. In you, she finds a long-lost trust – despite being a noble, she faced much scorn and ridicule for her obsession with crafts and tools, but you are different... You are willing to support her dreams, finance her endeavors and – most importantly – you believe in her.

5000734.title: Long-Term Research
strings: Long-Term Research

After two projects of collaboration, Mahir considers you her best partner. She hopes to form a closer, long-term relationship with you, just like before – you invest, she conducts research, and happiness is that simple.
Mahir is confident and brimming with inspiration.
You can assist Mahir personally or send a follower.
Mahir needs at least 5 Gold Coins for research funding.
Some items may be useful during the research.
Most research requires Aether support
Wisdom provides foundation, Aether brings success.
Since you have established a long-term collaboration, the Sultan no longer allows you to break Extravagance Cards through these investments.
Invention carries risks, so invest cautiously.
You provide Mahir your sponsorship. What new ideas does she have this time? Will she succeed?
Your Wisdom and Gold Coins provide you with the full number of dice rolls.
You need at least 5 Successes to complete the research.

Without Aether infusion, Mahir's experiment predictably failed, but it is a minor set back. She brings you some interim results. She shares with you her failures, the challenges she wrestled with, and lastly, she shares with you a bottle of liquor while cunningly persuading (tricking) you to procure some Aether for her.

Mahir comes to you excitedly, announcing her success! She enjoys success, enjoys researching new things and overcoming new challenges. Most of all, she enjoys sharing both the hard work and the joy it brings with you.

Mahir has failed, but it is a minor set back. She brings you some interim results. She shares with you her failures, the challenges she wrestled with, and lastly, she shares with you a bottle of liquor, because you are her most trusted partner.
Perfect Match
Inspiration Flash
Catastrophe Coming
As Religious Leader, I decide
Aether Requisition
Potential Use
Before you can intervene, Mahir has already drawn out the magic within, reducing the ancient Highlord's Effigy to irreparable sand.
Mahir seems to have another strange new idea.
The Purist Order's Aether supply is completely depleted. Where will future research lead?
You tell Mahir she needn't secretly take Aether anymore—the vault can be completely open to her. Mahir has never admired you more; her joy resembles a mouse fallen into a rice bin.
"Let's go! Please, these things sitting unused in the church is simply wasteful!" Mahir keeps insisting.
Before leaving, Mahir stops you, handing over a tattered schematic.

strings: Volcanic Dragon – Final Battle
An Extremely Difficult Boss Battle
Volcanic Demonic Dragon
Dragonslayer
Use your secret weapon!

If you do not defeat it today, it will wipe out all life on earth!
Final Battle, the Volcanic Dragon!

5000736.title: Into the Darkness (Abandoned)
strings: Into the Darkness (Abandoned)

The young, pallid lady leads you by the hand. Dim candlelight flickers, illuminating an altar steeped in darkness and blood. She watches you with a knowing smile, her voice warm with encouragement. She urges you to offer tribute, to step into the night, to become her companion. And that great, unknowable presence will surely turn His gaze upon you, drawn by the scent of blood.
The Occultist Badriyyah is willing to guide you.
You must personally oversee this ritual.
You must offer a living human as a sacrifice
You can take this to break a Bloodshed Card or Carnality Card
Sacrificing the life and blood of a living person will grant you dark powers.
You can take this opportunity to break either a Bloodshed or Carnality Card. You can only ever break one Carnality Card through this Ritual.
The Sultan Card's tier must not exceed that of the sacrifice's.
You still were not ready to start a ritual, and Badriyyah ran out of patience. She and her dark secrets vanished without a trace, leaving no sign behind.

Badriyyah instructs you, step by careful step, in the art of sacrifice.
You bind the offering tightly to the black stone altar and slit open the veins at their wrists. Their blood runs hot over your fingers, and at that moment – a cold shiver climbs up your spine. A pair of unseen hands, deathly chill, settle over yours, guiding you to trace sigil after sigil, each more intricate than the last.
Whispers coil around you, layer upon layer, a chorus of voices speaking mysteries too vast to comprehend. Hunger rises from the depths of your being, coursing through your veins like fire. You kneel before the offering, staring into the black void that was once eyes – eyes that held only despair and agony, eyes that now churn in an entropy as deep as the starry skies. You bow your head to the night and offer up your name.
Badriyyah smiles. “Worship, my friend. Worship our Lord of Darkness. He shall grant us strength, so long as we offer Him death and blood...”
Something foreign takes root within you. Your heart hardens, colder, stronger.

You suggest adding some sensuality to the ritual. Badriyyah shrugs and leaves you to it. What a forgiving god.
You secure the sacrifice to the black stone altar, savoring her pain and pleas. In that perfect, weightless moment, you let the blade slip across her wrists. Their blood, rich and scalding, spills forth. Exquisite. You dip your fingers into the heat, and then – cold. A cold shiver climbs up your spine. A pair of unseen hands, deathly chill, settle over yours, guiding you to trace sigil after sigil, each more intricate than the last.

You bow your head to the night and offer up your name.
Badriyyah smiles. “Worship, my friend. Worship our Lord of Darkness. He shall grant us strength, so long as we offer Him death and blood...”
Something foreign takes root within you. Your heart hardens, colder, stronger. You proclaim your deeds to the world, unashamed, and the Sultan listens with rapt attention, pressing for details. The priests cry blasphemy, the people shudder at your excesses, but what of it? You smile and break the Sultan Card.

You dare speak no further.

He warns you sternly with a look, as if not drawing his sword is already extraordinary courtesy.
He leaves without finishing his tea. How rude.
You expend considerable effort persuading the Roaming Swordsman, but he merely shrugs: unfortunately, he already has his own god.

When you try persuading him, Habib immediately perks up. First he asks if those legendary otherworldly monsters truly exist, then wonders how their meat tastes... Good heavens, what normal person would eat such things?! You hastily send him away, fearing he might serve you some questionable dish next moment.

Jenna constantly writes and sketches in her inspiration notebook, seemingly attentive. You're uncertain whether she's merely humoring you... but ultimately she closes her book and agrees to join your cult, which is enough.

Facing High Priest Iman, you cannot utter a single word of your prepared cult sermon despite long contemplation.
Iman merely glances at you, then departs with a slight bow, as if already knowing what you intended to say - don't. Don't push your relationship to an irreparable precipice.
Jabal's typically languid eyes suddenly grow alert, sharp as a wolf's. Facing you, he slowly draws his scimitar.
Nayla is naturally attracted to darkness and blood... who could be more suited for cultist?

At first, you pretend this is just an ordinary small gathering.

Patiently, you discuss familiar topics with him: officialdom, law cases, statutes... Gradually, the conversation slides into deeper darkness, but out of respect and trust for you, he notice nothing. Finally, you see his expression go blank for a moment, like parchment waiting for the first stroke of ink.

You have successfully corrupted him.

During a usual small gathering, you discuss familiar topics with him: the Court, precedents, laws... However, when trying to steer the conversation towards deeper darkness, his eyebrows knit in caution, eyeing you suspiciously. 

You laugh it off as a joke. Seems now is not the time.

After repeatedly confirming this faith requires neither payment nor donations, Jawad finally nods with a smile, his insincere attitude making you roll your eyes. Nevertheless, you briefly imagine his aging face wearing that disgusting Purist priest expression and decide his current demeanor is preferable.

You try convincing Adila to follow the Cultic God while she's maintaining her sword with tung oil - it's the only time she has patience for your lengthy sermons. She finishes polishing, flourishes the blade skillfully, then sheathes it before looking at you: "What gods can give me, I can take myself. What I cannot take, no god can give me."
Ah, the toughest marks for any con artist are people like this.

You showed Fatuna some secrets of the Creator, the Lord of Darkness. To your surprise, she was already familiar with these doctrines — once they were confirmed by you, she eagerly desired you to teach her more.
You slowly drip the dark secret into a glass, telling Zaki it is what he lacks, and even what his father lacks... Without hesitation, he drinks the dark remedy.

Hearing your words, Nabhani widens his eyes in shock, examining you repeatedly. He cannot believe you've descended into darkness's abyss, powerless to help... His face turns ashen, then he pours you wine, serving himself as well. After this drink, he never returns to your side.

Before you can mention the foul deity lurking in darkness, Faris's dogs suddenly begin howling madly. He apologizes repeatedly, frantically calming his dogs, and you lose your opportunity to continue.
Junah is compliant. Whatever you give her, she accepts.
Jalila shows interest in the Cultic God you describe.

Shama has read many cult records and rumors in books. Clever as she is, she naturally knows their cruelty and horror... yet her comfortable position reading in her study relies entirely on your assistance. Thus, she merely sighs lightly, not refusing you.
Therefore, Shama kneels obediently on the floor, forehead touching the ground, exposing her slender, vulnerable neck. "If you wish to deprive me of this too, please kill me."

You tell Alim how wonderful your Cultic God is, how they bestow unimaginable pleasure... oh, and wheat cakes too, certainly.
Alim strokes his chin, looking curious, somewhat longing, somewhat doubtful, then suddenly something occurs to him. He claps his hands firmly with an enlightened "Ah! I understand - I've heard you gather regularly? Don't forget to invite me."
Gullis firmly refuses you.

This conversation is an absolute disaster. For every statement you make, Lumera asks three probing questions, leaving you confused and speechless: who knows how gods work, what is faith's essence, where divine power originates, how monster summoning functions, whether the otherworld is immaterial or physical... You part ways unhappily.

“However you wish to mourn her, it ends here.” you tell Nabhani. “She might be pleased to see you fight for her, but if you die here, she will still weep.”

Your fighter placed the blade against Nabhani's neck, a neck longed for by countless noblewomen... The spectators are shouting, they crave romantic blood, and this unparalleled swordsman should die for love in the arena.
But you always love to go against the tide, you raised your hands in a gesture of forgiveness and left the scene amid everyone's surprised gazes.
His blade pierced through your heart, you saw sympathy in his eyes, you heard him praying for your soul, you heard the crowd cheering... but everything became blurred.

He killed your warrior, instantly turning away, apparently abhorring the crowd. 
At least for you, it's over, though from now, you've lost a friend and gained an enemy in the court.

Adila holds the severed head, turning it over in her hands with careful scrutiny. Her fingers trace the edges of the wound, unbothered by the blood staining them.

"Clean and precise – the prey didn't suffer a moment of needless pain. This is truly masterful work," she says, her voice filled with admiration. "You did this, didn't you? You're even more skilled than I thought."

You give a modest response, explaining how you and Jabal worked together to hunt the beast.

Adila pauses thoughtfully. "That adventurous general – I've heard of him! He once searched the lands far and wide for dragons at the Sultan's behest, but..." She trails off. Then, her eyes brighten as she looks at you. "Oh, you're not just brave but honest and humble too! Next time there's a hunt like this, please take me with you!"-
He excitedly carries the head through the streets, proudly showing it off to everyone he meets, whether they care to see it or not – a walking celebration of your acclaim.

She and her son are both shocked by the giant wolf's head. The boy, cheeks flushed with excitement, asks if you could mount it in his bedroom, hoping it would inspire him to become as brave a warrior as you. 

Fatuna, pleased with this scene, rewards you generously.
