This sinful card makes Iman frown. 
He coldly, unhesitatingly rejects you: "Please don't call divine blessings 'extravagance'." With distaste, he orders priests to escort you out. 
Perhaps their god is pure, untarnished, and inviolable, yet at this moment, under this brilliant sky, you distinctly sense an otherworldly glance toward you and your card. Only your connection remains insufficient; you haven't yet received divine blessing... that's all.

This sinful card makes Iman frown. He coldly, unhesitatingly rejects you: "Please don't call divine blessings 'extravagance'." With distaste, he orders priests to escort you out. Yet in this moment, under this brilliant sky, you sense an otherworldly glance toward you, then every white stone around you subtly vibrates, your card shatters, and divine light concentrates on your forehead like a simple mark or brand - He has noticed you. Yes. HE - HAS - NOTICED - YOU. Everyone witnesses this sudden miracle; believers and priests prostrate themselves, loudly praising the Immaculate while Iman stands frozen, eyes reflecting profound anguish and confusion. Finally, he kneels before you, head bowed, voice tearful: "Please guide me."

No one anticipates a dagger here; even the divine doesn't vigilantly protect its faithful. Iman collapses bleeding, crimson quickly staining surrounding spring water. You're genuinely surprised at your easy success... 
Priests quickly identify the culprit, protesting to the Sultan, who fortunately pre-pardoned your game-related transgressions - besides, who's to say the Sultan disapproves?

This sinful card deeply disturbs Iman; its depictions of love and desire would contaminate his eyes with a second glance. Predictably, priests and believers chase you from the temple. 
Why so serious? Just let me indulge briefly. You grumble, retrieving your Sultan Card from the mud. Just then, something stirs within - looking skyward, you sense a hasty celestial glance. Only your connection remains insufficient; you haven't yet received divine blessing...

This sinful card deeply disturbs Iman; its depictions of love and desire would contaminate his eyes with a second glance. Predictably, priests and believers grab your arms to eject you, but suddenly, under this brilliant sky, you sense an otherworldly glance, then every white stone around you subtly vibrates, your card shatters, and divine light bathes you, marking your forehead - They have noticed you. Yes. HE - HAS - NOTICED - YOU. Everyone freezes at this sudden miracle; believers and priests eventually prostrate themselves, loudly praising the Immaculate while Iman stands paralyzed, eyes reflecting profound anguish and confusion - why? He will dispassionately brush aside his pristine white hair, directing you to use this stone knife to cut his gold-dusted, scarred back, and amidst blood and pain, he'll whisper one pure word.

[s2.name]'s spiritual impurities are thus expelled, just as [s1.name]'s flowing blood is washed from white stones without leaving traces.

Iman leads you to a secluded garden planted with elegant foliage surrounding a massive central white stone pillar. Looking upward, you can't determine its height, only seeing neat inscriptions disappearing beyond sight. 
Iman remains silent, contemplative, waiting until you lower your gaze before speaking.

You hand him your broken Extravagance Card. Iman traces its sharp edge, feeling unmistakable pain from its concentrated sinfulness, furrowing his brow. 
"Is something wrong?" you ask. 
He brushes aside his hair, again revealing his extensively scarred back - layered, accumulated, heart-wrenching. 
"Having received blessing, you understand that only in pain, only when experiencing nothing but pure pain, can priests hear the divine voice and convey pure words to supplicants." He speaks softly as his cloak resettles, white stone ornaments tinkling, "This ritual forms Purist faith's foundation - just a little blood, and our god manifests frequently, quite generous, yes?" 
"But your card... what does it mean?" he whispers, puzzled, nearly making you miss the faint mockery in his earlier words, "Why would miracles appear now?... What have you done?"

You laugh softly, placing the card in his gold-dusted palm. Iman feels its cold surface, sensing evil and sin; any spiritually sensitive person would reach identical conclusions. 
"Is something wrong?" you ask. 
He brushes aside his hair, again revealing his extensively scarred back - layered, accumulated, heart-wrenching. 
"Having received blessing, you understand that only in pain, only when experiencing nothing but pure pain, can priests hear the divine voice and convey pure words to supplicants." He speaks softly as his cloak resettles, white stone ornaments tinkling, "This ritual forms Purist faith's foundation - just a little blood, and our god manifests frequently, quite generous, yes?" 
"But your card... what does it mean?" he whispers, puzzled, nearly making you miss the faint mockery in his earlier words, "Why would miracles appear now?... What have you done?"

You lack conceptual imagery of the divine; to you, its power represents merely a small fate-altering die. You use it to achieve desired outcomes, nothing more. Such theological discussion would certainly get you expelled, so you wisely remain silent. 
Iman sighs softly, realizing his absurdity - he's the Purist High Priest, responsible for guiding believers, not you... 
He shakes his head slightly, returning your card, and departs, dispirited.

You candidly share that through repeated contemplation, dreams, suffering, and struggle, you've touched goodness's phantom, heard god whispers... essentially every Purist priest's journey...

You confess that in darker moments, temptation surrounded you; evil kissed you, demonic hands gripped you...

You desperately grasp Iman's hands, seeking guidance.

You suddenly grasp Iman's hands, fixing the Immaculate's most devoted high priest with your stare: "They shall return." With eerie intonation, you capture his spirit: "They shall return. I have witnessed Their true face - " 
He's shocked by your mental image - you've accepted destiny, bringing the Creator-King, Demon-Lord, Lord of Darkness into this world.

You laugh abruptly, exhausted and melancholic. You explain to Iman that perhaps this stems from uncovering the exiled ancient god's true visage - beneath creation's appearance lies merely putrid, foul, viscous ink... Intent on smearing, devouring, and ultimately destroying this world. 
Iman appears profoundly shocked by your revelations. But then comes the crucial question - what should we do? How stop Him? Pray to the Immaculate? 
But who guarantees... that pristine white robe, that light beam drawn by your sinful card... aren't merely another deceptive veil, like "the "Creator"?

Without clear answers, the miracle's anomaly seems attributable solely to your exceptional devotion, the Immaculate's special favor. 
Iman quietly listens without offering encouragement, comfort, or gentleness. Instead, his concerned gaze reminds you that approaching divinity brings danger - witness his scars - though this peril hasn't yet manifested for you.

Iman appears to understand. Perhaps this unusual blessing occurred because They perceived your dream-torments. "Fear not, [player.name], nor abandon hope," he softens his voice - for the first time, you hear warmth rather than coldness, even slight consolation - "Each pain represents your battle for Them, and They... remain ever with you." 
The breeze rustles grass, producing hushed sounds. Their whisper lingers, trembling with what might be... fear.

These evil omens nearly drive you mad; your lips tremble uncontrollably while tears fall - is it remorse, fear, something else? You yourself cannot say. Your only certainty - you need help. From the Immaculate, from Their most devoted High Priest... a desperate, hopeless plea. 
The god responded thus to your cry, and Iman grasps your cold hands. Suppressing his terror of that incomparable dark lord, he promises: "We can devise purification methods, ways to stop Him."

But then you smile slyly. 
"Your god must have erred somehow." You whisper malevolently near Iman's ear, "I follow the exiled Cultic God - master of darkness, creation, and mysteries." 
Seeing the High Priest's shocked expression, you laugh satisfactorily. 
How interesting! God light manifests on an evil card - doesn't this prove the Immaculate submits to evil and sin?

Have you grown overconfident? Consider your location and audience. When revealing the Cultic God's vision, your evil philosophy to Iman, realize this constitutes provocation, even declaration of war - but what's wrong with that? A magnificent new world approaches; all hypocritical pretenses will be rewritten. How could the pathetic Immaculate compare with your ancient lord? You depart the nauseating white temple with arrogant stride.

You humble yourself, kneeling before him as when seeking blessing. He studies your face before silently nodding, proceeding deeper into the garden. 
Of course he agrees - this carnal act has god approval and blessing! 
You follow his steps contentedly.

You humble yourself, kneeling before him as when seeking blessing. He studies your face, maintaining cold silence. 
Well... even with god approval, you cannot win his favor. You retreat gracefully.

He nods, bowing slightly before departing. The garden's foliage quickly obscures him; strangely, you sense his burden of doubt and exhaustion, making him resemble hollow driftwood. 
Surely this impression is false; Iman's blessings always prove remarkably effective.

You use your most cautious, troubled, desperate tone when probing Iman's attitude toward this Carnality Card, while he silently studies you. His gaze resembles purest water, making you slightly ashamed. 
But doesn't water's purpose include purifying filth? If this card represents sin, if god revelation aims to rescue you from evil, shouldn't he assist? 
"Please follow me," he says, taking your card deeper into the garden.

You use your most cautious, troubled, desperate tone when probing Iman's attitude toward this Carnality Card, while he silently studies you. His gaze resembles purest water, making you slightly ashamed. 
You accept your card back from him, dropping the subject.

If your god has subdued his, what should you fear?
You produce the Carnality Card, brazenly tapping his handsome face: "Esteemed High Priest, care to correct me?" 
Iman's face shows no humiliation; he merely gazes at you steadily, pure as gold: "As one who walks crooked paths yet hears god voices... perhaps this explains the miracle's unusual manifestation... Please follow me." He bows slightly, proceeding deeper into the garden. 
Well, that's precisely what you wanted.

If your god has subdued his, what should you fear?

Then was the heavenly light truly blessing? It shattered this evil card - couldn't this represent anger toward betrayers, purification of sinful objects? Perhaps this interpretation proves correct!

His neck arches higher through this pain, throat emitting hoarse whimpers like pleas or prayers, gradually transforming into stranger murmurs from his chest... you recognize this previously heard... god pure words explosively resound in your ears; in this strange, sacred observation, cold moist air lifts your soul cloudward...

You've desecrated the Purists' High Priest... the Sultan's Game witnesses this depravity. The moment the card breaks, bloody marks suddenly appear across your back, like the merciless scourging priests inflict during self-judgment... Yet you feel no pain - quite opposite, waves of ecstasy flow through you - in this unjust game, you've atoned in God's place for the world's carnal sin.

strings: Divine Light Trial

Afterwards, his father speaks poorly of you at court. What is this about? Becoming a priest is a great honor and privilege, isn't it?

His light equals a small cat, vibrant and lively, stronger than everyone else combined. But you remain silent, exactly what this youth desires. His gaze holds gratitude; afterwards, he sends you a heavy bag of gold.

He becomes emotionally overwhelmed, tears glistening, as if never experiencing such glory. What a blessing to offer his useless body and powerless blood to the great God and Their followers! He thanks you repeatedly.
His light is too weak; his Pure Word barely provides healing effect. You deliver your harsh assessment, and he simply lowers his head, quickly adjusting to offer a smile: "I-I'll continue trying."

Such pure eyes, such pure light... though slightly inferior to the nobleman, he's still young!
Hearing your praise, the boy's face flushes with excitement and embarrassment. He immediately turns, searching the crowd, likely seeking parents to share his joy.
Tears immediately fill his eyes, pure droplets rolling down as he breaks into loud sobbing among the crowd. You must frantically console him before he finally leaves, still sniffling.
Time proves your choice correct; you truly are divinely favored. The priests respect you completely.

strings: Awakening
You wake within your dream... the heavens shimmer for you alone.
You've crossed into the extraordinary realm
They Come

As if seeing stars for the first time - no longer cold points of light, but beings with emotions... embodiments of desires, crafts, and kingdoms... 
The stars, feeling your gaze, respond with joy. 
They pulse slowly, descending, yearning to bridge the distance between you. 
Suddenly, a great star falls, its blinding white light overwhelming the sky. 
In answer, a black mountain rises from earth like a spear, threatening the lingering stars. 
In your dream, all other stellar voices fall silent.

5004802.title: The Depths Call
strings: The Depths Call
Something summons you, guiding you to this abandoned mine...
What summons you?
Heart of Darkness

You dismiss your servants and venture alone into the tunnel depths. Ancient Cultic God worshippers would dig downward until the earth warmed and strange gems appeared - merely the first step of their journey. 
Crawling through, soil filling your nostrils, ominous water sounds surrounding you, you question your sanity - if you don't return, will servants have to retrieve your corpse? 
Wedged between massive boulders, dizziness overtakes you... perhaps this is the necessary path to transcendence - approaching death brings you closer to divinity. You abandon what must perish to approach what endures! A sensation unlike any before - your thoughts become a rope whose other end someone violently seizes! Something pulls desperately at your heart, soul, and magical essence! 
The rope tightens, nearly dragging you into unfathomable depths... As you struggle, the vibrating cord creates a rhythm, revealing a path to hear the alluring voice more clearly. 
Your servant awakens you... The mine, darkness, rope - all gone. Was it mere hallucination? As you wonder, the voice from the depths echoes in your ears once more.

5004803.title: Inner God
strings: Inner God
You've often dreamed of this garden... It feels intimately familiar, as if you've always been dreaming, as if life itself is merely a dream.
It has called to you for ages, now seeking you directly
Darkness Incarnate

It arrives. You sense a powerful presence. Your garden fades - flowers, clouds, soil, insects, buried secrets... No, not everything vanishes - intense darkness fills everything instead! That fog-like darkness shrouds your mind, consuming your thoughts, memories, even your flesh... 
You cannot resist laughing, weeping, prostrating yourself, offering your life... This is the greatest of banished cult deities, the primal creator of god and earth, king of demons, master of darkness and the underworld...

5004804.title: God Visage
strings: God Visage
In your dream, before the Creator... countless times you kneel in submission - just as you serve the Sultan while awake. Finally, with gathered strength, you raise your head...
Speak with the God
This isn't your true face, is it, my lord?

As you raise your head, your garden returns—your beloved carpet, water pipe, preserved fruits, flowers, and hand-washing basin—all forming your sanctuary. You realize: you are no longer mortal. The dark mist solidifies amid hearty laughter... A handsome dark-haired man in crimson leather appears. Heavy gold adorns his body, enormous gem rings flash on every finger. Their floor-length hair forms countless braids decorated with star-like jewels. Their overwhelming scent borders on foulness. "You're remarkable... I never expected such capability," they walk across your carpet, looking down at you: "Now you've seen my true face. How many mortals achieve this? You should look happier!" They smile, almost approachable... Like a host, you offer the water pipe, taking turns enjoying it. "How are your tasks going? Are the rituals difficult? Need more gifts?" Their smile fades as one hand traces their milk-white skin while others—a third, a fourth—rummage through pockets, carelessly tossing items to the ground: giant millipedes, bizarre demons, thrones, riches, palaces... scattered like insignificant debris. You remain silent. Finally, finding something in their trouser pocket, their voice turns cold: "This is what you want, yes? Unlike that pretender, I've always embraced my true form, need no disguise... Look!" Instantly, they reveal something, and this false form distorts—endless dark tides overwhelm you. Garden, carpet, all submerged in darkness, the world filled with black ooze, leaving you floating as the sole light source. "I am contamination, fullness, deadly abundance, unrelenting pleasure!" You finally understand—this is an ink bottle, the speaking liquid around you is black ink... Once perhaps the essence of creation, now decayed to viscosity and stench, unable to write a new, more wondrous world...It was all a deception.

5004805.title: Light's Discipline
strings: Light's Discipline
To clear your mind and understand these thoughts... you choose the most primitive method: asceticism.
What seeks to guide me?
Divine Experience

Emulating devout Purist followers, you pour ice water over yourself, then scorch with fire, then accept flagellation. Through cycles of mortification, you remain expressionless. Pain merges with your soul - unimaginable to exist without it. Your birth brought your mother pain, your growth brought pain to lessers, your nobility brings pain from the Sultan. Pain defines existence - no joy exists without it, so we should venerate pain as we do pleasure! You've never felt anything like this - your thoughts become a rope whose other end someone violently seizes! Something pulls desperately at your heart, soul, and magical essence! 
The rope tightens, nearly dragging you into unfathomable depths... As you struggle, the vibrating cord creates a rhythm, revealing a path to hear the sacred voice more clearly. 
Servants rush in, witnessing flames and hearing thunder... terrified by the phenomena you've triggered. They should fear, for you've received holy instruction.

5004806.title: God Revelation
strings: God Revelation
You've often dreamed of this garden... It feels intimately familiar, as if you've always been dreaming, as if life itself is merely a dream.
God Countenance
Radiance Incarnate

They arrive. You sense a powerful presence. Your garden fades - flowers, clouds, soil, insects, buried secrets... No, not everything vanishes - everything transforms into purest white - all around you becomes perfect opal, merging with the sky in brilliant light. Within this whiteness, a gaze descends, judging your worth... This is the world's guardian, demon-vanquisher, master of light and flame, most immaculate lord...

5004807.title: A manifestation of the True God.
strings: A manifestation of the True God.
In your dream, before the Immaculate Purity... countless times you kneel in submission - just as you serve the Sultan while awake. Finally, with gathered strength, you raise your head...
The Immaculate Purity
This isn't your true face, is it, my lord?

As you raise your head, your garden returns - your beloved carpet, water pipe, preserved fruits, flowers, and hand-washing basin - all forming your sanctuary. The opal light slowly coalesces into human form - surprised at your presumption, it begins expanding limitlessly, growing larger, more imposing, making your garden insignificant... But just as both blazing sun and twinkling stars are celestial bodies, you too are no longer mortal. Finally, the massive illusion vanishes like bubbles, and a familiar voice speaks behind you. "Come sit, [player.name]." Turning, you see a white-robed priest, who nods, then raises their hand, examining their form as if finding it novel. Their vague, ordinary face - like an average of all Purist priests you've seen, utterly featureless - is another phantom created by your mind. Seemingly perceiving your inner contempt, their face trembles, mimicking either human anger or a smile? Finally abandoning words and gestures, they rise, shed this inadequate shell, and fill you. Your flowers, carpet, water pipe transform again into opal, rapidly losing all texture in blinding white light... You become opal, then your eyes, face, palm lines are erased, until finally you hear the sacred sound hidden within the white radiance, that indescribable, ineffable hum... "Words profane purity maturity profanes innocence life profanes death possession profanes loss all is profanation is profanation is profanation... purify everything all buildings are abscesses humans are maggots foolish maggots who would crown themselves unacceptable... complete purification my duty before the master who created all returns... puripurify/destroydestroydestroy..." This voice emerges from within you, inscribing understanding upon your heart: It has gone mad, incapable of bringing a pure realm, It will destroy everything.

5004808.title: Sacred Encounter
strings: Sacred Encounter
What a spectacle - two deities appear before you in succession...
The Mightiest Cultic God
The Purifying Truth God
Convergent Paths

Creator and Purifier regard each other coldly; clearly, gods dislike reunions or chance meetings. Before you can decide what to ask of them, your mind shrinks... the space where gods dwell becomes cramped - no, your mind isn't shrinking - both deities freely expand their transcendent forms - growing larger, nearly filling your will entirely... One side of your mind craves pain, feeling utterly defiled, wanting to flay your skin, burn what lies beneath with acid, scrape away all filth - while your other mind cannot resist urges to kill, destroy, witness holy men's debauchery, roast virgins on spits! Clutching your head, you writhe in agony. The true god claiming to purify all, the Cultic God claiming to liberate all - face to face, how similar their inflicted suffering! You see nothing, your mind's eye blinded, completely filled with God power, you should never have done this, how could you allow these opposing gods simultaneously - "Destruction!" This voice erupts in your mind. "Destruction! Destruction! Destruction!" Your eyes widen, seeing nothing. Tears flow, each drop laden with divinity and malice. You understand - no savior exists - deities bring only one thing to the mortal world... "Destruction!" If any difference exists between them, it's merely in their methods, means, and aesthetics of world destruction, but the result remains: Destruction! Destruction! Destruction! With sudden clarity, you close your eyes... again seeing the two deities standing face to face... Standing behind the Creator, you glimpse the Immaculate Purity's true face. Their countenance bears nothing... They desire everything to vanish, return to blank slate... Then circling behind the Immaculate Purity, you glimpse the Creator's true face. Like churning black mud, urgent ink droplets, wanting to blacken everything, eliminate distinction between pain and pleasure... They suddenly turn to regard you. Time to awaken, mortal - you've learned enough about divinity.

When you awaken from your hysteria-like release, you see Maggie unconscious - now skeletal, corrupted by the darkness you secreted... Though she says nothing, you know this loving woman can accept no more.

Finally, the time comes, you make your demand... Maggie responds only with an embracing smile. Her flesh barely retains warmth, only enough life remains to soothe your agitation... Following her guidance, you tear open her neck, chest, abdomen... 
Amid death and ruin, you don't know if you've released madness, or become one with it.

You pull him to madness's edge - just as he pulls you toward rationality's border. 
In this struggle, you remember nothing, but know only someone deeply beloved would endure such ugly behavior... What hurts him isn't your scratching, violence, or raving - but seeing his most respected person reduced to this state.

When you reach for him again, his smile speaks of desperation. What more can this worn vessel offer? What comfort remains in his fractured soul? His dagger, meant to free you from torment, finds his own heart in the struggle. 
As lifeblood flows, your mind clears one last time... But is this clarity, or have you simply become the darkness?
He hungers for your essence, your divine purpose fulfilled as his guide. "Take, drink of my blood; take, eat of my body." Your earthly form fades while your influence grows!
The moment draws near. What remains of you in this world is but a final anchor. Your essence - branches, blossoms, fruits - nourishes him now. You both sense the coming transition.

Your physical existence ceases. No earthly power, arcane force, or god authority contains you now. Consumed and possessed, your light shines through him. Rebirth awaits within his form - but not today, not within these pages.

Your consciousness hangs in balance: joy weighs against madness and emptiness. 
Though collapse looms inevitable, today you still possess treasures to place on the scale - precious insights crystallized from your long journey.

You wear Mahir's creation - lightning captured in form - the perfect storm to either purify or devastate your mind. 
Whatever comes, you embrace it.

Teetering at madness's edge, you study this painting intently, examining each creative decision that brought it into being. 
The process anchors you, restoring fragments of reason.
When madness binds your thoughts ever tighter like a rope, suddenly, a thought... a pair of calm eyes helps you break free.

A potent stench enveloped you, unrelenting. You felt dizzy, numb, trembling, and nauseated, unable to move as darkness flickered at the edge of your vision, as if each breath drained life itself... At last, before you lost consciousness, the maddening thoughts that tormented you crawled away from your mind.
Roughly hewn, it hints at a female torso. Some primal life seems to slumber within it...

You foolishly seek to resolve your spiritual crisis through the absurd gods of the cultists. 
You pray, plead, beg... only to be answered by cold laughter from the darkness. 
Perhaps you still need to prove your worth to the chaotic gods.

You seek the Purist's grace to quell the storm in your mind...
A blinding flash lances through your consciousness and down your spine, a jagged bolt of pure agony. This is the Purist's answer to your plea.
"Unworthy," the pain whispers. "Ask not what the light can do for you, but what you can offer the light."
It "assists" your meditation for a grueling while before the sensation finally ebbs away.

Cruel fate ensnares you, wrapping like precious silk, layer upon layer, slowly suffocating you... 
But suddenly, a breeze caresses your face and reveals a startling truth - wasn't all this your choice? You could have remained silent, followed the crowd, even eagerly licked the Sultan's boots and encouraged him to cast misfortune onto others! 
Yet you chose to stand and oppose him. Every step was your decision... 
You recall those emotions - the sense of duty, that unbearable anger... in that moment, you took pride in yourself. 
You open your eyes, mind crystalline with clarity. Having chosen this path yourself, complaints become meaningless. 
You're prepared to challenge fate now, and if necessary, to seize it by the throat. 
Your destiny belongs to you alone, not to heaven.

In painful contemplation, you suddenly remember your original purpose. 
You're caught in this cruel fate because you chose to stand and counsel the Sultan, because you couldn't remain a silent witness. 
You ask yourself: would you become a villain - someone who revels in the Sultan's cruel games - just to escape this fate? 
The answer shines clear. Fate may batter and torment you, but it cannot twist your essence. Given another chance, you would stand against the Sultan again. 
Understanding this brings profound relief, even drawing soft laughter from your lips.

As fate's painful barbs subside, sudden exhilaration grips you. 
Playing the Sultan's game may ultimately cost your head, but before that happens, couldn't you justifiably remove many other heads? You could indulge in pleasures under the Sultan's banner, exploit others' fear of the game for wealth, and taste imperial authority! 
This will certainly be a magnificent game, and you intend to enjoy every moment! 
The thought makes you hum cheerfully to yourself.

You watch this pitiful figure trembling before you. 
Your fate rests in the Sultan's hands, yet you hold the fate of many others in yours... doesn't this mean the game grants you Sultan-like power? 
You spread your palms, studying them intently. A slave can only control his own hands, but a royal courtier controls vastly more... 
The sensation of dominance feels strangely intoxicating, not unpleasant at all. 
You're ready to fully embrace the Sultan's game.

The world's malice pours down like black rain, drenching you completely. You curl inward, arms tight around your body, defenseless. 
As pain torments you, Maggie gently embraces you. Her slender frame shields you from much of the cruelty... 
"None of this is your fault, my love," Maggie whispers in your ear. "If the world punishes you for doing what's right, then the world itself is wrong." 
You hold each other, tears mingling... This greatly eases your suffering. Yes, if the world stands wrong, then you must correct its error. Even if you die trying, at least you can say, "I did nothing wrong."

You suddenly recall what Nabhani said when you first entered this game, as he stood beside the Sultan... 
"So you've become the protagonist now, haven't you?"
You had no time to consider his words then, but looking back, Nabhani's view of the game has remained remarkably consistent. 
He sees each encounter as merely a chapter in a story - enemies as backdrop, friends as decorative flowers - everything exists to highlight himself as the protagonist. Therefore, nothing warrants complaint! 
You smile wryly. Perhaps Nabhani is right... Now that you've become this game's protagonist, you should deliver an unforgettable performance for your audience. 
With this thought, you straighten your posture, roll your stiff shoulders and neck, then glance at your reflection. 
The curtain has risen, and the protagonist has taken the stage!

Your thoughts turn to the cultists. 
Isn't their daily existence just like living in the Sultan's game? Sometimes starving, sometimes feasting, sometimes beaten by Purist priests, other times pressed against warm flesh in darkness... They never know where tomorrow finds them, whether they'll survive; they can only accept, then accept again. 
Ah... they understand the truth. 
This is the way of the world, the nature of life - whoever attempts to predict their path is a foolish sage; whoever expects to control their future is a blasphemous saint! 
Understanding this, you feel the burden on your shoulders suddenly vanish. Stop questioning why this fate befell you - such destiny awaits everyone. "Unpredictability" forms fate's very essence.

Could it be... that all this is some deity's arranged trial? That the Sultan's game is dark as pitch so humanity's faint light within shines like stars... 
Is this god waiting for you—Their follower, Their lamb, Their lost bluebird—to find the crack in cruel fate and lead others from this game? Everything has cracks; that's how light enters. Just look upward—find the channel through which true divinity descends! 
You suddenly understand those Purist followers who find pleasure in self-torture... The path given by divinity isn't torture but blessing.
Rebuking Darkness
Ancient Enmity
Spiral of Destruction

You dare invoke the most unholy name before the Immaculate Purity! 
They thunder through your mind, Their light a spear piercing heaven and earth, a ruler lashing the world... 
Until the next day's sunset, whenever your focus wavers, everything before you shatters into light and flames... This divine punishment They foretell... fortunately, They cannot execute it immediately.

Darkness boils as you mention Their enemy's name before a god. 
Their anger transforms into a dark forest, intending to make you lost forever... Fortunately, you still pray for light in your heart. This beam, like a faint lamp, illuminates your path back to the mortal realm... it also reveals the monstrosities the evil god created from your fears. Masterpieces crafted from your inner terrors... about death, betrayal, failure, love... After waking, these images linger.

Two rival gods, who both want nothing more than to end the world, keep running into each other in the back of your mind.
It's a perfect little battlefield where they can tear each other apart, and your mind along with it... for all eternity.

Even your favorite treats and wines don't do it for you anymore; death is the only thing on your mind. You look at the frail and the sick and see yourself in their shoes...
It's a bit of a downward spiral, and you know it, but you're powerless to stop it.
You just keep thinking and thinking... and you'll probably still be at it when your time finally comes.

You find actual nails and pin a thread from your clothing to the wall. 
You pluck the thread, feeling its tension, watching it return to position... You experiment with many threads, one after another. 
Each thread behaves differently. Some break easily, like costly silk; others endure significant disturbance and return unchanged - like coarse threads in servants' garments. 
Life's dimensions extend beyond era and family to include yourself - the thread itself. Your material, quality, and resilience determine fate's boundaries. 
This childish experiment brings surprising comfort. 
You resolve to be a thread strong enough to endure.

Lost in contemplation, you unconsciously take up your sword and practice while your mind works... 
Drenched in sweat, clarity strikes you. 
No matter how eloquent an enemy or complex a situation, with sufficient strength... you can simply cut through! 
Strength solves all puzzles. Might transcends cunning, force breaks deadlock. Fortunately, you possess this strength. 
You raise your sword skyward. If the gods favor you, let your blade cleave whatever fate awaits! No challenge can withstand sufficient strength. If defeated, it merely proves your weakness - and the weak should accept their end gracefully, shouldn't they? 
A cool breeze dries your sweat and eases your fatigue. 
Perhaps god approval of your warrior's resolve.

You contemplate so deeply that you begin to enjoy the very process of thought. 
Your mind soars, exploring every avenue. What is fate? A series of events, or confluence of people? Do our actions manifest through body, so does fate target body or soul? Are we vessels executing fate's design, or fools lured astray? 
Following these thoughts, you gather philosophers' works, reading aloud in your study... Then enlightenment arrives: 
Whether fate is fixed or fluid, whatever awaits - a sage who masters thought will overcome with wisdom. Let fate challenge you more fiercely! More riddles, more obstacles, more intricate games! Let fate's cruelty increase! 
As this realization forms, everything around you softens and warms, as if leaning against a glossy-furred beast... The sensation passes instantly - perhaps god acknowledgment of your insight?

You contemplate Zaki and his mother. 
Whatever the young man does, his mother silently observes. Hasn't Fatuna woven Zaki's fate herself? She arranged his meeting with you, provided his affluence, determined his birth, accent, heritage, strength... 
For a son, mother becomes fate's goddess; for the mother, wasn't her own mother the god force shaping her destiny? 
You exhale deeply. Suddenly fate seems less terrifying - you can calmly face it, confront that silent watchful gaze.

You think of Lumera. 
What destiny awaited her? Street wandering until starvation claimed her? 
Her clean clothes, warm meals, beloved books - all exist because of your momentary thought... those gold coins between your fingers. 
How malleable is human fate! Even if some call such encounters "destined," fate remains fundamentally unpredictable. Your fingers changed Lumera's destiny. Might someone else's touch similarly alter yours? 
Reflecting on how you rescued a brilliant girl from death's grasp... your turmoil temporarily subsides.

You examine the Sultan Card in your hands...
If fate resembles cards dealt by the Magician, then... though fate deals randomly, choice remains yours, doesn't it?
You decide who bears this card's burden. You could sacrifice yourself—that's fair. If fate treats you cruelly, deny it a puppet to manipulate.
You clutch the card, laughing silently. This unprecedented feeling—holding your fate while directing others'!
You've endured more than your ancestors ever understood about destiny. The question of predetermined fate now seems trivial, beneath you.
You set aside the question entirely.

As you contemplate, a voice tempts you persistently. 
Isn't chaos fate's true beauty? 
Predetermination cannot exist... fate shifts constantly, though not necessarily improving. 
Embrace chaos, embrace frenzy, embrace the unknowable! 
... 
Fate isn't predetermined, but its uncertainty is. This conclusion eases your spiritual anxiety immediately.

When deeply considering this question, light floods your mind - not directing but overwhelming everything in uniform whiteness, making all indistinguishable... 
Fate is predetermined. 
Fate leads to a pure, peaceful world. 
Everyone must strive toward this end. 
This is your destiny. 
Your fate is fixed. 
... 
You cannot resist this light. Believing in predetermined fate lightens your mental burden... reduces choice's pressure. You surrender a piece of yourself for momentary peace. 
Later, when bloodshed becomes necessary, your hand will be steadier, your step more certain.

Who created good and evil? Surely humans invented these concepts themselves? 
Perhaps virtue and vice are merely standards humans impose on themselves... rewarding desired behaviors with "Renown," punishing unwanted actions with "Infamy." 
Like twin strings controlling a suspended ball - drift too far left, the right string pulls; too far right, the left restrains. Ultimately, these are reward systems driving most people along a middle path, neither extreme. 
You sigh with relief. Your confusion resolves: good and evil aren't predetermined - they're human constructs evolving with each generation. Naturally, you may establish your own moral standards.

You must be inherently good - born virtuous. 
You've earned this claim. When the entire court remained silent, you alone confronted the Sultan. 
You've defined your own goodness; you're already that singular light in darkness. 
Now you must burn brighter, illuminating others with your radiance! 
Your spirits lift, finding courage to face tomorrow.

Only fools believe anything predetermined - except that the weak inevitably fall to the strong. 
Sultan, gods, demons - all simply greater forms of violence. If violence embodies evil, then power is evil, wealth is evil, everything pleasurable or exciting is evil! 
Becoming more corrupt than they... you could defeat them, claim their power, even replace them!
As this ambition surfaces, darkness spreads through your heart... like distant ink drops falling into your soul's ocean. 
The stain shifts, revealing everything you desire - power, wealth, authority, pleasure, even destruction itself.

You consider Faraj. 
He worships you almost blindly, but does he understand your essence? Even as you wield the Sultan Card, even committing unforgivable acts, doesn't he follow faithfully? 
For Faraj, "good" simply means "what [player.name] does," and "evil" is "what [player.name] wouldn't do." These concepts didn't exist before he met you and apply to no one else - they're even imposed upon you. You can only remain his idol, however imperfect. 
This realization lifts your burden. Each person appears as unbearable filth to some eyes, yet perfect treasure to others.

You contemplate Nayla. 
No one would call her "good," and she likely cares nothing for the word. Yet people acknowledge her beauty. Many far kinder than her possess much less allure. 
Evil doesn't contradict beauty, then. Nor strength, nor happiness... Perhaps least of all, "justice." 
You smile, observing courtyard flowers tended by your servants. They root in foul manure yet adorn ladies' hair as treasures. 
Good and evil matter little - or rather, distinguishing between them matters not at all.

Weighing your actions, you realize the boundary between good and evil may never have existed - rendering the struggle to distinguish them pointless. 
Serving the Sultan loyally should represent virtue. Yet when his actions harm people and country, opposing him becomes righteous. Contemplating rebellion - is this virtuous or wicked? Impossible to determine. 
The issue isn't morality, you realize... but whether you follow your inner truth, unwavering despite temptations, solely pursuing your heart's purpose. 
As for what this "purpose" might be... each person, each god likely holds their own understanding.

You beseech the ancient darkness for answers. 
At your first forbidden prayer, dark visions overwhelm your imagination. 
You witness the Sultan stripped of power as you write sacred words determining his fate. 
You see the Magician torn apart by darkness, shifting forms - dog, viper, sea monster, enchantress - begging mercy through countless guises, repeatedly tortured and erased by your hand... 
This coveted power arrives. In the dark vision, ink droplets fall from heaven like sweet rain... You joyfully open your mouth, letting darkness penetrate your essence...

You purify yourself, light incense, recite prayers... seeking the Immaculate Purity's guidance. 
As meditation deepens, reality fades, but enlightenment remains distant - darkness surrounds you. 
When confusion and terror overcome you, the yearned-for light finally descends. 
They rebuke your weakness while lamenting mortal foolishness. A mighty hand grips your heart, transmitting icy will, like iron tongs locking your bones, igniting purifying flame to forge your courage. 
Upon waking, physical pain accompanies a strange icy calm.

You struggle not to rebuke them openly. Their noise overwhelms... Even the whispered schemes of those plotting evil reach your ears, though spoken softly, though miles distant!

You seek the Purist's grace to quell the storm in your mind...
A blinding flash lances through your consciousness and down your spine, a jagged bolt of pure agony. This is the Purist's answer to your plea.
"Unworthy," the pain whispers. "Ask not what the light can do for you, but what you can offer the light."
It "assists" your meditation for a grueling while before the sensation finally ebbs away.

Evil disregards others' wishes; virtue considers them. 
Virtue doesn't presage vice, nor does vice equal strength. Humanity requires both - without one, we lose warmth from others; without the other, we become prey in life's wilderness. They complement each other like opposite sides of a coin. 
Contemplating this, you idly take a gold coin, turning it between your fingers...
You toss it high. 
It falls leftward as if wind-blown, then sharply right before landing... 
Despite careful searching, you cannot find where this glinting coin fell... nor which face landed upward.

No... impossible! Virtue could never herald vice - virtue opposes vice absolutely. You understand this clearly. 
When virtue's light shines, power naturally gathers; you entered this game alone but now have followers. This light may not burn as hot as corruption's fire initially, but never extinguishes, springing from humanity's deepest dreams... 
Humans naturally desire to treat others well. Uncorrupted by society and hardship, we remain virtuous. 
You and your companions firmly believe this. You correct twisted reality bit by bit, remembering the philosopher: "One may be lowly as dust, but never twisted as a maggot." 
As clarity arrives, you unconsciously reach toward the night sky... feeling something within your grasp... 
Opening your hand reveals golden dust motes that dramatically disperse... Your spirit strengthens, power filling your body. 
Perhaps some virtue-loving god rewards you, though you never sought god favor.

Indeed, virtue heralds vice - you understand now. 
Virtue is a mirage created by the powerful to deceive the weak. Come here, free from cruelty, insult, plunder - this paradise is "goodness"! Then lambs follow the illusion, falling into the jaws of those who created the mirage. An effortless feast. 
Even occasional virtuous acts by the wicked serve self-gratification. Charity brings worshipful looks; mercy demonstrates life-and-death authority. Vice forms virtue's foundation - without vice, would virtue be noticed? 
Understanding brings perfect contentment. You draw from your water pipe... 
Rich power flows through the mouthpiece... You cough briefly, then feel invigorated, energized, clear-minded - perhaps reward from some god favoring vice.

You consider Alim. 
This pickpocket feeds orphans with stolen money. Without his "transfers," these children would starve. 
Are Alim's actions virtuous or wicked? 
All moral systems denounce theft - but how do they address poverty and hunger? They merely urge the wealthy to donate scraps... They praise generosity but wouldn't seize purses from the unwilling as they would sever a thief's hand! 
What else could Alim do? 
He commits wrong to achieve right. His hands, blackened by sin, are brushed with gold... 
These hands play fate's melody, harmonizing virtue and vice. 
This insight brings relief; morality isn't black and white - mostly gray areas exist, like Alim, like yourself.

You reflect on Qais. 
When confronting the Sultan, didn't he anticipate imprisonment? Didn't he know his family would suffer?
Yet he acted anyway, revealing virtue as sacrifice. Those worshiping virtue love sacrifice, yearning to offer themselves so others might flourish. Being remembered and honored provides life's greatest satisfaction. 
Frighteningly, self-sacrifice appears among humanity's deepest desires. Throughout history, haven't countless people died for religion, rulers, love, even to prove existence? Often our brightest, strongest, most remarkable specimens! 
Revelation strikes. The path to virtue requires self-harm, meaning vice precedes virtue, not vice versa! 
Jasmine fragrance inexplicably appears, invigorating you. Some unseen god apparently appreciates your conclusion.

You contemplate Jawad. 
He never questions his actions' righteousness. He simply wants wealth, finding loopholes in rules to acquire it. 
Who deserves blame? Jawad who exploits the loophole, or the rule containing it? 
If rules are designed this way, doesn't it suggest rule-makers encourage such behavior? The Sultan enables nobles' corruption, securing their support. The Purist allows priests to extort offerings, ensuring children enter the church. The Cult permit followers' revelry, gaining sacrifices! 
You suddenly understand. 
Good and evil don't exist. Abandon moral judgment, instead carefully discerning the rules beneath your feet; then dance with them - one, two, three steps - then twirl.

Moral contemplation exhausts you. You collapse onto your carpet. A mouse scurries past - a cat pounces, stunning it with one paw, then scratching it awake to play with it. 
Watching this predatory game, you find your answer. 
Which is virtuous or wicked - cat or mouse? Such distinctions don't exist. The cat derives pleasure, developing sharper claws and hunting skills. The mouse is merely sacrifice, summoning this game through its existence. Who would call a rodent virtuous? It simply lacks choice. 
Yes, morality is meaningless because we lack true choice. Pleasure matters - enjoying the game matters! 
You laugh aloud. The cat regards you with emerald eyes and golden pupils, seemingly sharing your amusement...

Morality is necessary precisely because it serves as a flexible instrument - resilient and effective, never wearing out, available for your own use.

Of course morality is necessary - what would the world become without it? 
Everyone pursuing maximum self-interest would ensure mutual harm. No cooperation, no trust, no expectations, nothing beyond immediate gratification. Clearly, a world without moral constraints would quickly become unsustainable. 
Your conviction solidifies. You desire moral constraints, embrace them - these limitations lift you skyward like winds beneath a bird's wings. 
Your steadfast belief earns god approval from some unseen power. Jasmine fragrance fills your mansion. Servants instinctively kneel before you, recognizing you as godly touched.

You recall a mischievous philosopher who imagined a cat sealed in a box with poison - without opening the box, one cannot know whether the cat triggered the poison and died; for the observer, the cat exists simultaneously alive and dead. 
Morality resembles this paradox. 
An action is simultaneously virtuous and wicked, depending on who observes; morality both exists and doesn't exist, depending on whether you currently need it. Understanding this brings unprecedented freedom... Nothing constrains you anymore. You've placed your conscience in that box, sharing space with the cat. 
The Cultic God apparently appreciate your metaphor, including the cat portion - sending a hot wind carrying complex scents of soil, meat, and animal musk, clearly conveying: everything predates morality, rendering morality meaningless.

You think of Faris. 
Doesn't he regularly whip his hunting hounds? Yet they depend on him, trust him, view him as their sole master... 
Do these hounds follow morality? Are they born more loyal and noble than the finest aristocrats? Hardly! They merely follow animal instinct, which we misinterpret as "morality"! 
Isn't everything similar? Humans are merely naked apes, our so-called morality merely survival strategies evolved through instinct? 
As you contemplate this, darkness seems to produce soft laughter... Something appreciates your reasoning.

You consider Mahir. 
Are her actions virtuous or wicked? Impossible to define - the god never anticipated someone earning livelihood through "invention," just as they struggle to judge the Sultan's game. 
The god isn't omnipotent, morality isn't necessary. The world advances too rapidly to categorize every novelty. 
This brings relief... Finding the doctrinal space blank, you're free to inscribe your own interpretations.

Strangely, recalling Maggie's displeasure during spiritual turmoil brings comfort - like a dying traveler in the desert spotting a fearsome crocodile. The crocodile terrifies, yet signals life-saving water nearby. 
Though Maggie's displeasure alarms... it means morality matters because it affects those you care about. 
Sharing this insight with Maggie brings her gentle smile. She's always known you as a decent, moral husband. 
This exceeds any god blessing.

You stare at the soil by your feet. Worms writhe below, bird corpses slowly decay. 
When facing unanswerable spiritual questions, you long for answers from below, from chaos... 
They gladly respond. 
Closing your eyes, ecstasy floods your body. Tremendous force yanks you back and forth. You collapse, nearly vomiting, yet paradoxically joyful from this power. 
Money exists to be spent. 
Love exists to be betrayed. 
Life exists to end. 
Morality exists to experience transgression's pleasure. 
Isn't it simple?
Hee hee hee, hee hee hee, hee hee hee ha ha ha ha ha... 
This is Their answer.

Looking skyward, during spiritual confusion you hope for supernatural guidance... 
They answer.
You close your eyes, allowing sacred thought to fill you... This rewards your soul-searching prowess, for not everyone receives god wisdom for their questions... 
Morality is necessary because I desire it. 
What I desire is necessary. 
Therefore morality is necessary. 
Their answer is this simple. 
You open your eyes, doubts vanquished.

Closing your eyes smiling, before sleep you consider adding a small stream to your courtyard gardens, curious how worms and crickets might respond...

You had thought of those Ladies of Delights, finding yourself time and again unable to resist seeking them out. Were you fascinated by them themselves—or by how they had accommodated you?
Perhaps "obsession" had always derived from the joy of shaping others. You had molded them to appear infatuated with you, genuine or otherwise—and that illusion, though false, had proved irresistible.
On closer thought, hadn't all intoxicating things worked the same way? Alcohol had shaped drunks into self-imagined men of importance; swords had turned warriors into life-and-death arbiters. The Sultan had reshaped courtiers into toys and slaves. Watching another human soul bend through your own actions—nothing had ever enticed you more.
You had shivered slightly then, not from cold, but from the dark, approving laughter that rippled through the void.
"Precisely," They said. "I appreciate your insight."
...Have you ever heard Their whispers so clearly before?

You think of Nayla.
She is a creature of pure appetite—craving the finest fabrics, the brightest jewels, and the most exotic spices. She demands to be the envy of all, standing above the rest, wanting everything and then some!
And yet, the world remains under her spell. Her greed is her greatest charm; shaped by a constant stream of tribute from men and indulgence from women, she has become a force of nature.
But what is the root of this infatuation?
Reflecting on your moments with her, you find the answer: desire. Nayla's allure is born from her sheer, pulsing hunger. It's the spark of survival—the urge to feast, to drink, to embrace. The more she wants, the more blindingly alive she appears, a trap for every shallow soul with a weak will.
But right then, an icy thought strikes you, sending a shiver down your spine.
"Indeed. Desire is the ultimate filth—vile, hateful, and begging to be purged," They say. "Follow me and purify your heart of all desire."
...Have you ever heard Their whispers so clearly before?

You recall moments bringing happiness—that incomparable sensation surpassing any sensory pleasure or material delight.
Only while happy can you enjoy life's sweetness without guilt; only while happy can you proudly continue existing; only while happy can your soul's reservoir store additional water against inevitable future droughts.
Perhaps your magical fascination stems from happiness found in wielding power, which protects what brings you happiness.
Life represents a one-way journey seeking happiness. You regret nothing.
But wait... a paradox emerges. You concentrate intensely... god whispers and visions never brought pure "happiness." Do They scorn human fascinations, or... cannot achieve them?
You gain deeper understanding of existence.

You rub the ink stain on your palm, summoning Them to answer your inner question. 
They respond immediately, as if eternally awaiting your call. 
They show you an enormous boiling cauldron... massive beyond comprehension, filled with thick black broth, stirred by a she-demon with two pairs of breasts. 
Hands lift you up. You kick and flail uselessly, held like a grasshopper between a child's fingers - then thrown into the cauldron! 
...Remarkably, nothing burns. No, that's incorrect - it isn't cool, but your magic protects you. Watching other victims scream agonizingly in the boiling broth, the she-demon repeatedly submerging their briefly emergent heads with her ladle. They swallow filthy broth, intestines cooking from within - but you? Your magic forms a beautiful protective shield. The demon's ladle avoids you, broth cannot touch you, even heat remains distant. 
You understand Their message. Your magical fascination exists because it allows you to safely navigate the Sultan's game, witnessing others' suffering while remaining unscathed. 
How captivating. 
... 
You awaken refreshed, slightly proud. Perhaps next time, ask whether the Cultic God might grant you this she-demon. Her appearance wasn't unpleasant...

You relax, allowing god will to fill you... This experience feels wonderful, effortless, like a child returning to mother's embrace... 
They guide you to immaculate stairs ascending beyond sight. You climb each step, requiring significant effort. To continue upward, you must summon all your strength, even your magic... 
Ah, you understand Their intended answer: your magical fascination stems from devoted Purist faith. You know greater power qualifies you for higher steps, making you more valuable to the god... 
As if rewarding your insight, the staircase's end suddenly appears - a magnificent celestial palace. You cannot see its inhabitants, only pairs of pure, gold-dusted bare feet. 
... 
The dream ends, leaving you deeply satisfied.
Rebuking Darkness
Ancient Enmity
Spiral of Destruction

You dare invoke the most unholy name before the Immaculate Purity! 
They thunder through your mind, Their light a spear piercing heaven and earth, a ruler lashing the world... 
Until the next day's sunset, whenever your focus wavers, everything before you shatters into light and flames... This divine punishment They foretell... fortunately, They cannot execute it immediately.

Darkness boils as you mention Their enemy's name before a god. 
Their anger transforms into a dark forest, intending to make you lost forever... Fortunately, you still pray for light in your heart. This beam, like a faint lamp, illuminates your path back to the mortal realm... it also reveals the monstrosities the evil god created from your fears. Masterpieces crafted from your inner terrors... about death, betrayal, failure, love... After waking, these images linger.

Two rival gods, who both want nothing more than to end the world, keep running into each other in the back of your mind.
It's a perfect little battlefield where they can tear each other apart, and your mind along with it... for all eternity.

Can you discover the key this keyhole yearns for? Can you pass through the doorway into realms forbidden to mortal steps?

In this unnatural emptiness, only you and the door exist.
Glancing down, you find yourself dressed in formal court attire. This revelation suggests you can carry worldly influence into the void.
What will you bring through? What could shield you eternally in the unknown?
Not gods, not companions, not weapons... but rationality. You yearn for an ever-clear, sharp mind; you aspire to become thought's keen edge, slicing through the mists that would deceive you.

You've repeatedly opened that door within your consciousness. 
Nothing happens. 
The mundane grayness of reality extends on both sides, and neither you nor any part of you feels elevated. 
Suddenly, something catches your attention. You rush eagerly to investigate... 
A vast hole - bottomless and endless - lies just beyond the door. You swear you've never seen anything like this before; it exists neither in your imagination nor your memory... 
A strange attraction pulls you forward. You crawl over, peering inside... 
It's filled with your own broken corpses. You burned, dismembered, beheaded, poisoned... All the versions of you who died in countless cycles of the Sultan's Game, buried here... 
They reach up, grabbing at your throat, wanting you to join them in death. 
You wake trembling, drenched in sweat, lips blue, palms bloody from your own nails. Now you cannot face any "holes" - even pastries with centers terrify you. You're especially frightened by people's ears and nostrils, ordering everyone in your household to cover these openings - stuffing your own with cotton, opening your mouth to breathe, asking people to write instead of speak. 
"The master has gone mad playing the Sultan's Game," people say throughout the city.

The realization came to you in a dream. 
In that dream, you were surrounded by darkness, instinctively climbing upward through a cocoon. Breaking through an opening, you encountered light - you unfurled damp wings, letting them dry in the gentle breeze before taking flight, joining countless other butterflies. As evening approached and the air cooled, you settled on a saffron petal, calmly thinking: a butterfly's life is nearly complete. 
You awoke suddenly as a servant brought your water pipe, its smoke infused with saffron spice curling through the room. 
Understanding dawned - passing through the door was like being a butterfly dreaming it was human; remaining on this side was like being human dreaming of butterfly form.

You had a dream. 
Morning came, and you woke to fragrant air as your maid brought strong tea and breakfast to your bedroom. Maggie chatted casually with you as you ate, discussing last night's dreams. 
Together you walked to the sitting room where her personal maid waited, having prepared your day's attire. While Maggie applied cosmetics and arranged her hair, you gazed absently through the window at your beautiful garden, meticulously maintained, where birds shook morning dew from their feathers, creating tiny rainbows. 
Then you visited your territory together. You checked the harvest, spoke with representatives of your people; you proposed building stone roads, receiving eager support, with merchant guilds voluntarily offering financial backing. 
Afterward, you returned home. Dinner was sumptuous, dancers performed, your friends played drums and sang. The wine rivaled anything in the Sultan's cellars... 
The Sultan? Yes... weren't you playing the Sultan's Game? 
The moment your thoughts touched "the Sultan's Game," you awoke. You remained in bed, the game's countdown continuing. 
How long since you'd experienced such a pure, gentle dream? Not requiring supernatural satisfaction, grand miracles or blessings - just living slowly, enjoying peacefully, finding contentment... 
This dream was the world's answer: having crossed that threshold, you could no longer be viewed as an ordinary human; consequently, you could no longer possess a simple life. When immersed in such existence, you never treasured it - now, you couldn't help but weep.

You had a dream. 
In it, you stood alone in a dark garden unlike any you'd seen - devoid of plants but filled with strange structures. You rode a wooden horse, joining dozens of others moving up and down while circling a central point. 
The horses' mouths emitted intermittent music, an unfamiliar melody resembling both a lullaby and cultists' summoning chants... 
Everything remained shrouded in darkness, occasionally illuminated by strange flashing lights outlining unfamiliar symbols... The air smelled sweetly of honey and grain. Lost and confused, you wondered how long these crudely painted wooden horses would continue circling. Just as you prepared to jump off... 
The horse broke free from its pole. Without mechanical assistance, its stiff legs awkwardly extending, it carried you into the darkness. You screamed for help, struggled desperately, but your legs seemed trapped in the stirrups... 
You jolted awake, terrified. 
This dream was the world's answer: having crossed that threshold, you could never again be considered merely human. The horse beneath you represents your power, uncontrollable, carrying you into unfathomable darkness.

You had a dream. 
In it, you stood surrounded by corpses - all your victims, as you well knew. 
You wandered among them, carefully recalling each killing. When memories failed, you tapped a corpse's shoulder, gesturing it to rise and reenact its death. 
You witnessed a beautiful woman pushed from a cliff by your hand. 
You saw an aged man forced into a lake at your command. 
You watched a young child begging you for mercy. 
You observed faithful servants refusing to believe you'd harm them. 
Walking onward, the reanimated corpses followed in a procession as you crossed the threshold. 
Looking back, they had vanished. 
You awoke. 
This dream foretold your future. How much blood has already stained your journey beyond the door? And what price will crossing the next threshold demand? 
The meaning of crossing matters less than the truth: a murderer must continue killing.

You had a dream.
In it, you were a sword, wielded by a hero on the battlefield. You cleaved countless skulls before your bearer was struck down and you fell to the ground.
Seasons passed while you waited with countless remains. Daily, thin layers of dust settled upon you until you were buried completely. Resting against the hero's skull, tangled in his dried hair, weeds, shrubs, and trees grew above you... You were entirely forgotten.
Countless years later, someone excavated the land—a pioneering farmer's family, driven from their home, seeking survival on the barren ancient battlefield. A child pulled you from the soil. You expected the child to wield you, to kill—but after examining your damaged form, the child simply tossed you into a bucket.
You were taken to a blacksmith.
Your ornate decorations vanished, gold filigree carefully scraped away as payment for your reforging. Your blade became unnecessary, your guard superfluous—only your steel mattered now...
You were reforged into a hoe.
The farmer's child used you to till the earth. Too heavy for the child now, but soon they would grow, and you would become a perfectly balanced tool in their hands.
You awoke.
This dream revealed the world's answer: beyond that door, you might be reforged, your edge wielded by others; yet you remain yourself, malleable. Heroes and farmers alike are merely temporary wielders.

You had a dream. 
In it, you were a bookworm living in an encyclopedia. 
Daily you devoured the pages before you, first consuming "Prophets," then "Philosophers," then "Salted Mutton"... You ate and ate and ate, whether gods, excrement, or virtuous maidens - nothing deterred your appetite. The only distasteful parts were gold-dusted illustrations, which you carefully nibbled into delicate patterns, like flower petals decorating a lady's forehead. 
Then you encountered a delicious obstacle: the leather cover, soft and supple. You feasted insatiably, your small, resilient teeth working without rest, hardly sleeping! The intricately carved cover and world knowledge became waste in your belly, which you smeared across sacred texts - a bookworm's dominion over the world. 
Afterward, something unprecedented shocked you, filling you with fear, confusion, tension - you saw light! 
Beyond the encyclopedia, the real world bathed in sunlight, birds peered from trees, dust filled the ruined library, snakes and cats prowled nearby... 
You, a mere bookworm, gazed hopelessly at a world you could never consume. 
You awoke. 
This dream answered your question: crossing the threshold meant leaving the familiar world for the true realm. You believed you had devoured all mysteries, yet they watched you intently, like a woodpecker eyeing a worm.

You had a dream. 
In it, you anxiously awaited something. Your companions lurked in darkness, equally impatient. 
Your vision encompassed the entire night sky. Occasionally stars flickered, their light spreading into beacons, prompting people to leap toward them. Others followed, fighting and tearing at each other until the victor touched the light. 
You watched blood rain from above, broken limbs and bruised eyes quickly healing in darkness amidst curses. Nothing mattered except capturing those beacons, the paths to power... the promise of a feast lasting millennia. 
A beacon illuminated, and you instinctively rose - suddenly understanding it was the cultists' ritual, and you were the impure deity they summoned. 
You awoke. 
This dream was likely the Cultic God's reward, revealing truths meant only for initiates. If you continue advancing in His service, perhaps one day... this dream will become reality.

You had a dream. 
In it, your limbs couldn't move, nor could you turn your head. Your blood seemed frozen - you had become stone. 
People approached you one by one, disrobing completely, displaying their bodies before you. Your forward-fixed eyes penetrated their skin, observing their muscles, organs, thoughts. 
The pale priest harbored death wishes. 
The fragrant noblewoman nursed lion-like ambitions. 
The gold-adorned beauty possessed a spider's soul. 
The book-carrying beggar filled his heart with stars. 
You witnessed so many that souls nauseated you. How you longed to close your eyes, to let them become stone too, ending this torturous insight into human hearts... 
Your wish came true as darkness gradually enveloped you. Only at the final moment did you realize - you were the white stone in the deepest chamber of the Purist Temple. 
You awoke. 
This dream was the Purist's answer: beyond that door, you transcend worshipper, priest, or patriarch, surpassing mortal limitations. But this means surrendering freedom and joy, becoming a sacred stone for deities to tread upon.

Contemplating death makes it feel increasingly imminent. 
You recall reading about a creature called the shared-fate bird in some ancient tome - two heads sharing one body, taking turns sleeping. When the right head slept, the left head ate a wonderfully fragrant flower. Upon waking, the right head detected the scent and believed the left had deliberately eaten without sharing. In revenge, while the left head slept, the right ate a poisonous flower, killing both heads and their shared body. 
While you sleep, might your soul seek revenge against you? Perhaps your other self drinks poison or undertakes impossible challenges... Your fear intensifies until you dare not sleep. You dread nightfall, closing your eyes, losing consciousness... Yet the longer you stay awake, the briefer your lucidity becomes. You drink the strongest tea, stab yourself with knives, soak in ice water - anything to stay awake... 
Even you realize you're approaching complete madness.

You contemplate calmly: life and death represent existence's greatest themes, never offering many mysterious answers - only one conclusion: 
You will die, as will the Sultan, as will Maggie, as will everyone you love or hate. 
What is there to fear? 
Without death, you would witness everyone around you aging and dying... experiencing endless farewells and funeral processions. You'd sink deeper into isolated thoughts, eventually becoming an incomprehensible elder, a monster frightening children. 
Timely death is life's deserved blessing; eternal existence would be death's mockery! 
Having found your answer, your mind grows peaceful. Even if death arrived in the next moment, you wouldn't beg for reprieve. 
You discover each exploration represented overcoming difficulties. Challenges demand greater power, using greater power brings satisfaction, this satisfaction unconsciously leads you toward the next challenge... and greater power. 
Without challenges or risk of failure, no greatness exists. You've gained so much merely to repeatedly verify you possess so much. 
Understanding this brings weariness yet spiritual calm. 
Even if you're merely a donkey chasing a dangling carrot, at least you understand the trick's nature.

You release your thoughts, cutting them loose, allowing them to fall limply around you. 
Then you gently push these ideas forward with maximum benevolence. Every matter, every person, every encounter... You'll fight for survival but, like a tiger, won't kill unnecessarily or force your prey to dance in despair for your amusement. 
Thus, death becomes a vessel woven from kindness. You board it, lie down, covered by loved ones' blessings and lamentations, accompanied by your achievements and pride. Water gently carries you forward, onward... until stone gates appear. 
Your vessel passes through, while red-winged birds circle overhead, singing in unison: 
"Behold - behold - it is [player.name] - one who lived without regret!" 
You wake from this shallow dream feeling refreshed, fearing nothing.

You do fear death, not your own extinction, but posthumous attacks on your reputation and retribution against your loved ones. After all, you're hardly the most virtuous person... at least not the best, correct? 
Then your furrowed brow relaxes, and you smile... The answer seems obvious - how foolish not to have seen it! 
Having gained such power and strength, having walked so far through the soul's garden - surely you can eliminate all enemies before death claims you? 
Satisfied, you light another water pipe. Nothing merits fear, for evil's reward is power over life. Even in death, you'll become the Styx's ferryman, deciding who lives and who accompanies you across!

You think of Bharat, who sells heritage for profit - homeland heritage, ancient world heritage, dead people's heritage. These legacies were once new, representing the dream of rebirth their creators envisioned. 
After your death, will people similarly consume your legacy? Your hoarded coins, accumulated treasures, your thoughts, your character... 
Like new gods devouring old gods' aspects, like new Sultans licking blood from old Sultans' wounds. 
You silently resolve to plunder as much as possible from the dead before facing your inevitable end! 
Afterward, you'll place a pure gold coin beneath your tongue, which supposedly pays the ferryman's fare. 
As these thoughts form, a subterranean presence suddenly attacks you - seemingly furious yet excited. It urges you to plunder not just from the dead, but from the living - especially other living deities! It demands fierce attacks, passionate curses, until life becomes death, until - until... 
Exhausted, you sigh, understanding divinity a little better.

You think of the Roaming Swordsman. 
His past died, yet he emerged from ruins. Rooted in decomposing noble corpses, his swordsmanship originated there; breathing fresh air blown from new winds, his robust physique developed. 
Yet he remains a sharp sword, capable of severing anything, whether old or new. 
Isn't death a blessing for someone like him? 
Isn't death a blessing for all of us? 
The Roaming Swordsman wielding his reborn blade can face death proudly - as can you. After all, you've both fought with everything you possess. 
...No, that's wrong. Your past remains unkilled, requiring more from you... 
God thoughts seize you, immobilizing your limbs as sacred voices pour into your crown. 
...I can kill everything, or rather, purify everything... 
...Only when your path behind lies utterly blank may you rightfully die... 
...Advance, fight, in my name, for sublime purity... 
... 
He releases you, having spoken with perfect clarity. 
You collapse, then crumple weakly. Today, your understanding of divinity deepens further.

You examine the Sultan's suspicion toward you, pondering. 
The Sultan granted you power, not genuinely relinquishing authority but demonstrating his ultimate power - the power to bestow power. 
Then he watched you play the game, suffer, rise and fall. 
You clearly understand: if you die, he'll simply designate another to repeat the cycle... The game never ends, its history continues unbroken. As long as strong rulers exist, the game continues, history writing itself. 
Human death seems so insignificant against institutional power... Individual fate represents mere ripples. 
Even the gods, regardless which one, cannot disrupt this game, can they? 
Ha... Even the gods - even the gods! Human-created systems, traditions, institutions, laws - even gods watch helplessly as their mortal vessels dance within these frameworks! 
You collapse, overwhelmed by complex emotions. 
They remain silent.

Relaxing, your mind clears, casting out all fear, doubt, and restraint. Your soul is an empty hall, awaiting the divine to fill it.
He answers your call.
Black winds and mist swirl within you, forming fascinating things: seductive She Who Slithers, phallic images, sizzling roast pigs running wildly, newborn calves arise armed.
These illusions share a trait that chills you...
"Face."
Yes, the serpent has your face, genitals too, calves, roast pigs all. Fantasies all relate to [player.name] yet remain detached.
You tremble, covering your eyes. It's divine seduction...
"Serve me, I'll grant you courage against death; not immortality, but endless rebirth. You won't bother with physical differences, your soul eternal, with me!"
You fling to the ground, those faces linger in your mind...angelic seduction is addictive; an eternal follower seems too mundane...should've foreseen...
A bug crawls before you; suddenly thinking...look closely, does it have a human face, an immortal soul?
He laughs softly.

You concentrate your thoughts, praying toward your soul's extremity. 
You extinguish all desires - even desires for righteousness, for loved ones, for responsibility. While praying, only the Purist's words deserve your longing. 
They respond. 
Patiently They flow through your bloodstream, through every vessel, every muscle, every pore. This reminds you: all this will decay; but before decay, all can serve Their purpose. 
Eyes closed, you feel divine touch, gradually understanding Their message... 
Until decay claims you, you remain His pristine instrument. 
While you remain useful, They will preserve you from corruption... 
Resisting death is wrong, unless serving higher purpose. 
Your god tempts you... You, a mere mortal, merit Their personal bargaining... 
You kneel in profound gratitude. They linger briefly before departing this world.

Their anger transforms into a dark forest, intending to make you lost forever... Fortunately, you still pray for light in your heart. This beam, like a faint lamp, illuminates your path back to the mortal realm... it also reveals the monstrosities the evil god created from your fears. Masterpieces crafted from your inner terrors... about death, betrayal, failure, love... After waking, these images linger.

Two rival gods, who both want nothing more than to end the world, keep running into each other in the back of your mind.
It's a perfect little battlefield where they can tear each other apart, and your mind along with it... for all eternity.

strings: Battle of the Mind XII

Every great battle is one of the soul...
You are riddled with wounds. Guilt and self-examination, fear and anticipation carve a giant, ugly scar in your soul.
It bleeds and twitches, its contorted image constantly reels within your mind... resulting in fluctuating delusions.
Upon waking from these visions once more, realization dawns — it must be rendered into art, stabilized by indelible ink and pigment, avoiding further wound deterioration.
Evil?
Good?
