At first, the General thought he had misheard the order, but the Sultan never repeated himself. 
The courtiers remained silent, as if all their sound had been swallowed by a quicksand. Only the sound of rustling fabric was heard. 
The General collapsed, seemed too weak to bear his armor. He crawled forward to his master, eyes full of despair – he did not beg for mercy, for he had seen the endings of many who begged... 
When he finally began to lick the body of the Sultan, the courtiers turned away, could not bear to see. Later, some said he accidentally vomited and committed suicide out of guilt, while others said the Sultan personally punished him for his disrespect. None of them was willing to speak the truth. 
Nonetheless, the Magician announced it was a wonderful act of Carnality.

As someone close to the Sultan, the Royal Guard had seen too many absurd things. On the other hand, he was not without desire for the Sultan's divine body...
However, he did not expect it to happen in such circumstance.
Under the gaze of the courtiers, the Royal Guard had lost his mind... He took off his pants, raised his buttocks high, and buried his head in the soft carpet, awaiting the judgment of fate.
He heard the voices of his shocked comrades, the mocking of the noblewomen... He didn't know what had entered his body. Was it the Sultan's scepter or his sheath?
Everyone knew what had happened, except him. But he would not dare to ask this question in his life...

The noble Vasir asked the Sultan to allow him to serve at night so that he would be fully prepared to bring joy to the mornach.
That night, it is said that he brought several women to the Harem, including his wife, daughter, sister, and niece... Perhaps he thought this could quench the desire of the Sultan.
Unfortunately, everyone, including himself, disappeared in the Harem and were never seen again.

The Scribe recorded this order in his book before calmly asking the Sultan to allow him to return home to inform his family and cleanse himself for the serving. 
That night, people found that the Scribe hanged himself in his study. His children took his notes and escaped the city. 
The Sultan said nothing, but he asked the guards to bring the body to the Harem. 
The next day, the Magician announced that the Sultan had completed this Carnality Card.

The consort tenderly came to the Sultan's side. If not her, who else could be worthy of this card of love?
Soon, her smile froze. "I thought I would bed you tonight?" she bit her lip uneasily. Sultan did not answer and gave her a silent smile.
The dress slowly slid down on the clean and silky-smooth marble floor, revealing her noble and beautiful body in the bright sunlight. The courtiers all knelt and lowered their heads, yet the painful and intimate sounds kept echoing in the vast palace.
It is said that on that day, many courtiers voluntarily gouged out their eyes and cut off their ears to prove their untainted loyalty and to show that they had never had any improper desire about the consort.

Overwhelmed by sudden public favor, the woman forgot something important: the Sultan loves to watch women fight for him, but he does not like being used as a trophy for boasting.

She swaggered to the Sultan's seat proudly, her voluptuous body pressed against him, her silk hair rubbed against his skin. During their pleasure, she flaunted enviously at other consorts, basking in the aged concubine jealousy; she even left claw marks on the noble Sultan with long nails... finally, her actions bored the Sultan.

The next moment, on the golden throne, the woman struggling in panic as if a disobedient ram being throttled.

At last – peace, she quells. Her empty eyes reflected courtiers' figures that gradually blurred, faded – perhaps because the court was dismissed, or perhaps because her life had ended.

5005102.title: Gold Bloodshed Card
strings: Gold Bloodshed Card

"I see, this game certainly makes pastimes more thrilling," the Sultan seemed in high spirit, "very intriguing." Silence fell over the Lapis Lazuli palace. People held their breath. The fear had clutched their hearts. Their expensive silk robes were drenched in cold sweat.
The Sultan toyed with the card in his fingers. Who would he choose?
Put the card representing the Sultan here
Put any Gold tier bloodshed target here
Put the Gold Bloodshed Card here
Place the Sultan, the Bloodshed Card, and the target of bloodshed into corresponding slots to open the Event.
The Gold Bloodshed Card can only target Gold Characters.
A high-tier Sultan Card cannot target a low-tier character.
I see, this is how the game is played.
Your Majesty! I am loyal...
I am willing to die for you, your Majesty...
...I am not noble enough, Your Majesty, unworthy of this game.
Is this your plan...?
Your Majesty, I am not of royal blood; I may not qualify.
Too absurd... no, I said nothing.
Your Majesty... this joke scared me.
Your Majesty, please... don't look at me like that, I can't do this...
I would die for that Gold tier…
The Sultan chose the General as the target of bloodshed
The Sultan chose Vasir as the target of bloodshed
The Sultan chose the Aged Consort as the target of bloodshed

He was the Sultan's most loyal comrade. They used to had each other's backs on the battlefield... Since when did he diminish himself into a foolish coward, clapping his hands for the Sultan's every decision?
Going back twenty years, he would draw his sword and cut down the magician that had swayed the monarch.
But now he was lying on the ground like a broken sack, waiting for soldiers to drag him into the death row cell...
Going back twenty years, more than half of the soldiers would defend him with their lives, even from the great Sultan. But now, he was dragged away like some livestock by his own men. The courtiers quickly made way for their fallen collegue.

Vasir was the Sultan's uncle. He was a greedy and cunning old man! The young monarch's ambition of diligence and governance had all been gradually worn away in his court tricks...
The other courtiers were speculating whether this game is a plot, a smart way to eliminate his political enemy... The look of the courtiers made the Sultan disappointed. They didn't realized that he was just too bored.

She loved the Sultan deeply. After all, the Sultan had killed her parents and brothers to ascend the throne, yet she still chose to become his consort. She never feared him, because this man was her only love in all her life.
But she also knew that fear had quietly corroded her loved one's soul. Sometimes, He would wake up with a start in the middle of the night or keep rubbing his "bloodstained" hands in his sleep. When he talked about succession, his eyes were cold, as if he was talking about an enemy.
Unfortunately, these final thoughts would never be heard. The poets would soon start singing a thousand versions of the teardrops on her execution day.

5005103.title: Stone Extravagance Card
strings: Stone Extravagance Card

For the Sultan, completing the Stone Extravagance Card would be effortless. But he would not want to ruin this rare entertainment by simply giving a few Gold Coins away to his guard. 
The couriters went to great lengths to find a beggar. They must not be too dirty, that would displease the Sultan. Nor could they look too clean and neat to be real.
Now, the Sultan was going to reward this beggar in person. To the Sultan, it was a trivial gift, but for the beggar, it was a turning point in his life.
Put the card representing the Sultan here
Nameless Beggar
The Sultan's wealth and women can all be given as rewards
Put the Stone Extravagance Card here
Place the Sultan, the Extravagance Card, and the selected rewards into corresponding slots to open the Event.
Everything the Sultan owns, be it people or possessions, can be used as rewards.
The Stone Extravagance Card is the lowest tier. Any rewards can satisfy its requirement.
Greed or Lust
A small reward, with unexpected surprise...
Your Majesty!
Shit, I do not meet the requirement!
This... makes no sense?
I am willing to die for you, but I am not qualified.
This violates the rule, doesn't it?
Your Majesty! It can't be right.
Your Majesty... this joke scared me.
Your Majesty, I love you!
If this is my fate…
Sultan gave the beggar 5 Gold Coins
The Sultan gave his noble, Aged Consort to the beggar
The Sultan gave his favorite, most Seductive Consort to the beggar
The Sultan gave a slave to the beggar

Everyone praised the Sultan for this show of benevolence.
Someone said 5 Gold Coins were enough to feed a family for a week, only to be immediately ridiculed by another who claimed a poor man could never earn 5 Gold Coins in a year. Someone suggested he could buy a head of livestock and live off it; others argued that he could invest the money in a small business, growing his fortune...
While they were imagining the offspring of the nameless beggar would repay the Sultan tenfold, a hundredfold, and even more, the beggar had his throat slashed in a dark alley in the lower town. His fingers were mangled because he held onto those coins so tight. Those coins were supposed to change his fate...

Without saying a word, the consort followed the beggar, vanishing at the palace's gate. Everyone hoped this was some jest.
The Sultan was not pleased, as the consort showed no emotion.
He ordered his High Constable to track them and recount their tale.
Years later, an old storyteller returned, narrating the beggar and consort's journey.
Even as cities fell to sands over millennia, their tale lived on, adapted and celebrated.

Upon realizing it wasn't a joke, she cried openly before the court, scratching guards and hitting their armors, cursing all courtesans and slaves and all who surrounds her.

When she was about to scold the Sultan himself, he darted his eyes toward his guards, who executed her post-haste. Of course, the corpse was still a reward that begger could not refuse.

It's said that the begger carry the beautiful corpse and left, no one knew where he went and what was next.

Long time after, people said that in the unknown graveyard outside the city, there is a gravestone with blossoming flowers, that was her grave. The stories about it, some of them terrifiying, some of them sexual, some of them brave, some of them all of it.

The beggar accepted the Sultan's gift. However, he did not take the slave's collar chain. He asked the Sultan to free the Slave Girl and allow them to marry.
The Sultan found the idea amusing. And the courtiers, in order to please the Sultan, gave many wedding gifts to the couple on the spot. It is said that the couple made full use of the wife's knowledge of the Palace, started running a small store for a benevolent noble lady, and lived a prosperous life ever after.

5005104.title: Bronze Conquest Card
strings: Bronze Conquest Card

There was a prosperous city near the Sultanate, that had been trading treasures and spices with an Eastern Empire for decades, if not centuries... They also made a lot of money, maybe too much money from the Sultan. It was about time for them to pay the price.
Once the target of conquest was decided, the melancholy that had shrouded the court during these games was swept away. The courtiers began to talk about the inevitable victory enthusiastically. There was only one question left – whom the Sultan would send to take the loot.
Choose a leader for the army
Sultan's Army
Place Tactics Intelligence to gain attribute boosts and rerolls during expeditions.
A prosperous, unguarded town
Place the Bronze Conquest card here
Place the commander and the Conquest Card into corresponding slots to open the event.
This event requires an attribute check. Please focus on the Characters's Combat and Physique attributes.
You can use Equipment to strengthen the character who will set off on an expedition (put the card there to equip).
Open Character details and click the Equipment Card behind the illustration to remove it.
Tactics Intelligence can boost attributes and provide rerolls.
The tier of the Conquest Card matches the conquest target's tier. The tier of the character executing the conquest is irrelevant. You can dispatch a character in any tier for this ritual.
Glory to the Sultan!
The number of dice provided by your Combat and Physique is affected by the enemy town's Combat.
You need at least 1 Success to win.
That's what I'm looking for.
This is my opportunity to get promoted.
If I fail... No, I won't fail.
The battlefield is not my forte.
You should choose characters with higher Combat and Physique attributes.
I'm not made for war.
Your Majesty, please don't joke around.
Am I competent for this? I have always wanted to become a general since I was a kid...
This... is beyond my wildest imagination, Your Majesty.
An easy victory

The Sultan's army beheaded the town's guardian, though merely months ago, the Sultan had promised them autonomy. At that time, the guardian had knelt and kissed the Sultan's feet in gratitude. Nevertheless, the Bronze Conquest Card is resolved.

"What fascinating thrills, those last two days were," The Sultan nodded at the Magician, "Your game is good, I understand it now. Come, let's continue playing."

[s1.name] recklessly challenged the enemy in a duel and was unfortunately cut down... the Sultan’s army retreated. However, the Sultan could not tolerate such a defeat. There could be only one winner and it must be him! He led a massive army and razed the town to the ground... Amidst the blood and ashes, he snapped this Conquest Card in half. Now, he had mastered all the rules of the game.

5006001.title: Dealing with the Betraying Friend
strings: Dealing with the Betraying Friend

You detest ungrateful people the most. Even though you once drankr under a tree together, this person is no longer your friend! This wasn't your choice – it was his. He chose to become your enemy, and now, he must pay the price for it.
The Betraying Friend is at your mercy.
In this situation, you should step in personally.
You can use this opportunity to discard a Bloodshed Card or a Carnality Card
Perhaps, you can use a Carnality card?
Or, use a Bloodshed card!
Or, just let him go.
You decided to indulge in Carnality.
You decided to relish in Bloodshed.
You decided to forgive this former friend.

You drag this man out of the cellar and slap a Carnality Card on his face.
Has the poor guy finally realized what's going to happen? He frantically tries to escape your restraint, but due to the torment he endured over the past three days, he's unable to resist your advances. As you brutally pierce him, his weak and pale face no longer holds the prideful expression it once had. Only the gemstone ring you didn't take from his finger remains, a most ironic epitaph to the event.
You break the card as desired, and the man has learned his lesson and will never appear before you again.

You drag the man out of the cellar and slap a Bloodshed Card onto his face.

Does this poor thing finally realize what's about to happen? He panics, desperately trying to escape your grasp, but after three days of torment, he's far too weak to resist. As the blade pierces his chest, that weak and pallid face finally loses its once-proud expression. Only the gemstone ring on his finger – one you couldn't even bother to take – remains as his final, ironic burial token.

Just as you wished – you break the card, and the man will never appear before you again.

These three days were enough to teach him a profound lesson. You drag this man out of the cellar and tell him he can go. He looks at you suspiciously, confirming it's not a joke, and then bursts into tears of joy, kneeling and hugging your legs as if you were the greatest saint in the world...
Not long after, he voluntarily returns all the money he owed you.

5006002.title: As You Wish
strings: As You Wish

Your neighbor -a fool who always competes with you – beat his own wife's face just to warn her not to talk to someone like you [a man who commits adultery with women using sorcerous cards]. Since the mud has already been flung at you, you decide to accept it and make the most of it.
Abused Woman
Carnality cannot be delegated
You can use this opportunity to discard a Stone Carnality Card
If you happen to have a Carnality Card, you can announce to the world that you are indeed capable of such deeds.
Maggie would be unhappy about this.

You show your neighbor that his suspicions were absolutely correct. However, not because you are a lecher who goes wild at the sight of women, but to give him a memorable lesson.
After this incident, no one dares to speak ill of you anymore.

You show your neighbor that his suspicions are completely unfounded. You're not a lecher who goes wild at the sight of women – of course, it's not because you're afraid of Maggie's reprimand either – it's just that, to be honest, his wife's looks don't hold a candle to Maggie's!

5006003.title: I Want It All
strings: I Want It All

A swindler – or maybe not a swindler – approaches you with a heap of trinkets, claiming they are ancient relics belonging to your family. With a grand gesture, you generously declare that you will take them all in.
You can handle this yourself, or send a follower to do it.
10 Gold Coins, not a single cent less.
You can take this opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower.
Spend a large sum of money to buy jewels.
You can take this to break an Extravagance Sultan Card

The person was overjoyed and tried to run away with your money. However, maybe out of fear of trouble from you, he sneakily handed you something just before leaving. When he had gone far away, you opened your hand to find a piece of jewelry bearing the royal insignia...
It's better not to ask how he got it.

You concealed the royal jewelry and pretended to be heartbroken, lamenting about how you were swindled into buying a pile of worthless items. Honestly, people always enjoy seeing others suffer. The Sultan gladly granted you permission to break this Extravagance Card.

5006004.title: I Only Want the Best
strings: I Only Want the Best
Among the antiquities that this swindler – or perhaps not a swindler – was selling, there were indeed some things worth noting. You picked them out, and although reluctantly, he gave you a price.
You can handle this yourself, or send a follower to do it.
3 Gold Coins are enough.
It won't cost a lot of money; it's a matter of face.

After some bargaining, you bought them at a very reasonable price. Though these little things have little value, with a bit of maneuvering, they can enhance your prestige, letting everyone know how illustrious your ancestors were.

5006005.title: A Day's Good Dream
strings: A Day's Good Dream
Thanks to your thoughtful comfort, Maggie's uneasiness and anxiety gradually eased.
Wife's Resentment
Your Wife's Resentment will be soothed.
Maggie feels much better.
During your tender embrace, any small disagreements between you both gradually dissipated.

5006006.title: Generous Donation
strings: Generous Donation

Someone beats drums and gongs at your doorstep, singing hymns loudly. As you open the door, a group of children shower you with white flowers and shout 'Hooray' and 'Thank you.' Before you figure out what's going on, they pull out a donation banner 'for the pure children'...
You can do this job yourself, or send any of your followers to do it.
You are certain you want to donate 10 Gold Coins.
You can take this opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower.
Though it costs a lot of money, it can resolve an Extravagance Card.

You generously donate 10 Gold Coins. White petals pour down like rain and the church children cheer your name, loud enough for the whole town to hear. 
Having done a good deed, you sleep well this night. 
Despite the expense, this deed has greatly increased your prestige.

Later, you heard that those priests were imposters, and the 'pure children' were just a scam. They took your money and gleefully left the city that very night...
You provided the palace with the best clown performance, and the Sultan laughed as he permitted you to break an Extravagance Card.

5006007.title: Money to Avoid Disaster
strings: Money to Avoid Disaster

Someone beats drums and gongs at your doorstep, singing hymns loudly. As you open the door, a group of children shower you with white flowers and shout 'Hooray' and 'Thank you.' Before you figure out what's going on, they pull out a donation banner 'for the pure children', making it clear they won’t let you go without money...
You can do this job yourself, or send any of your followers to do it.
3 Gold Coins are enough.
At least no one will scold you for being stingy.

This result isn't the most generous, but it's not bad either. The clerics loudly announced your donation amount, comparing you to those who donated more, trying to pressure you into giving more, but you firmly kept your wallet shut.
Perhaps because of the donation, you had a nice dream that night.

5006008.title: Betting funds
strings: Betting funds

The caravan leaders made all kinds of grand promises, and finally, you were convinced. The distant northern coast is a golden land of commerce. You plan to invest some money, and if you have enough people, you intend to send a trusted friend along... All that's left is to wait for them to return with endless gold and treasures.
The merchants need you to invest at least 20 Gold Coins.
You can do this yourself or send any of your followers along.
Some consumables come in handy during long trading journeys.
The caravan guarantees they will try their best.
The merchant needs Survival and Sociability attributes, as well as some time.
The check result will decide the merchant's profit.
The caravan will leave after 7 rounds.

You've invested a substantial amount of money, and the caravan quickly formed. They chose an auspicious day to depart, with over a thousand camels carrying goods worth a fortune. They will travel north along the desert and valley edges, crossing vast straits... Will they return safely? How many treasures will they bring back?
Your Survival and Sociability determine your full dice count.
5 Successes will yield the highest returns.
Maximum benefit, luxurious return!
Substantial profit!
Encountered difficulties, minor profit.
Met bandits, no profit.

After a difficult and long journey, the caravan successfully reached its destination. Almost without having to say a word, the various spices, ivory, and ceramics they brought from the East were snapped up, traded for slaves, coral, silk, and gold. Your investment brought you unparalleled returns. When the merchants delivered your share, your eyes were filled with genuine joy.

Despite encountering many dangers on the road, the caravan successfully reached its destination. Almost without having to say a word, the various spices, ivory, and ceramics they brought from the East were snapped up, traded for slaves, coral, silk, and gold. Your investment brought you a return beyond expectations. When the merchants delivered your share, your eyes were filled with joy.

The caravan encountered unexpected severe weather, barely surviving but losing many goods. They struggled to sell the remaining spices and ceramics and delivered the profits to your residence according to the investment ratio, along with a small gift to soften the blow. Looking at his worn-out face, you couldn't find any harsh words, accepting the money with a sigh.

Shortly after the caravan set off, it was attacked by unexpected sand bandits. They looted everything and brutally killed many caravan followers and camels. The caravan leader returned dejectedly, bringing a small gift to apologize. You looked at his nervous and fearful appearance and sighed. There's nothing more you can do, so you had to accept this fate.

5006009.title: Gold Bird
strings: Gold Bird
No matter how much you regret it, once the Sultan said it, you had no choice but to buy that damned mechanical bird out of your own pocket!
You can handle this yourself, or send a follower to do it
30 Gold Coins, not a single cent less.
You can break an Extravagance Card of any tier for this
Can you refuse the Sultan's request?
Although it will cost a lot of money, it can eliminate the Extravagance Card.
Gold Birds can be offered to the Sultan in The Grand Game for favor and Influence.
You reluctantly handed over the money while cursing the greedy inventor and the onlooking Sultan in your heart! Thank heavens you didn't go bankrupt!

You squeezed out a few tears to ask the Sultan to let you break an Extravagance Card for it, but the Sultan looked at you mockingly, saying, "Didn't you yourself say it was worth its weight in gold?"
You truly have no one to blame but your own rash words! Anyone can see that the bird is not worth that much! Even if it can tell time, fly, and groom its feathers... any rooster on the street can do that!
Now you've really lost a lot... The tears flowing from your eyes became genuine... Your sorrowful appearance amused the Sultan. After having had enough fun, he finally let you go.

5006010.title: Dispose of the Slave Awaiting Death
strings: Dispose of the Slave Awaiting Death
The time has come. You decide to use the card you drew to deal with the slave who dared to steal from the master.
Slave Awaiting Death, at your mercy.
In this situation, you should step in personally.
You can use this to break a Stone tier Carnality Card or Bloodshed Card
Bloodshed or Carnality? In any case, it is the punishment he deserves!
You decided to indulge in Carnality.
You decided to relish in Bloodshed.
This slave was at your mercy. How could he refuse his master anymore? You had a great night, but the next day, you heard that the slave, dragged from your bedchamber at dawn, had breathed his last.

This slave's life belongs to you; you could have taken it long ago, couldn't you? As he faces your blood-stained dagger, the tortured slave surprisingly calmed down. From then on, he would no longer have to live in fear.

5006011.title: Unclean Material
strings: Unclean Material

Obtaining a corpse... sounds simple, because the deceased themselves won't oppose you, but in reality, it is a grave crime. You don't want to ask Mahir how she got the corpse before you. If you need more...
10 Gold Coins, or a person to serve as material.
A Bloodshed Card, the tier cannot be higher than the character used as material
Mahir is eager to try
Mahir will wait for you up to 10 turns. After 10 turns, she will give up and no longer bother you.
You can choose to spend money or send a person. When sending a person... you can also use a Bloodshed Card.

Committing the real crime of desecrating a corpse for an intangible invention isn't worth it. You reject Mahir's proposal and tell her to leave quickly.
She pesters you again, and you suddenly remember something, calling her back. "So you will still sponsor me, right?"
You point to the foul-smelling box she left in the room.
"Don't forget to take this thing away. If you dare to throw it in my pond, I'll throw you in there as well."
She grumbles, reluctantly leaves.
Haha, my lord, don't joke around...

Money talks. Surely someone would be willing to commit a minor crime for cash. You should be able to find a suburban cemetery-keeper, a coffin-maker, or someone else... The question is, what is the so-called “generous reward”?
“You have much time to ponder this, dear!” Mahir laughed, her face flushed with excitement, hands waving up and down. “Imagine, you will have a tireless servant! It can do anything! Maybe not any highly intellectual tasks because their brains rot first... but moving things, killing people, no problem at all!”
This sounds good... You called a servant, arranged the necessary people, and then gave Mahir the money. Now, you just have to wait for her news.

You gave the victim no chance to resist; a swift and clean death was your final gift.
The corpse was stuffed into a large box by Mahir and taken away. You have no intention of asking about the original corpse’s fate.
Now, just wait for her good news.
People in the Lapis Lazuli Palace talk a lot about your use of the Bloodshed Card, even the Sultan asks, what this “experiment” is, and what results it yielded.
Your actions inevitably left traces.
Since you didn't do this by yourself, you naturally can't break the Sultan Card.

5006012.title: The Sultan's Questioning
strings: The Sultan's Questioning
People in the Lapis Lazuli Palace talk a lot about your use of the Bloodshed Card, even the Sultan asks, what this “experiment” is, and what results it yielded.
Persuader of the Sultan
Consumables helpful for your persuasion
If you succeed, it will increase your Influence.
If you fail, the Sultan will fine you... there shouldn't be any danger to your life.
You have to be vague and evasive to avoid arousing the Sultan's larger interest and wanting more 'experiments'...
Your Sociability and Charisma determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to persuade the Sultan.

You thought this matter could be brushed off, but soon you received a notice from the officials – for the suspicion of desecrating a corpse, the Sultan wants you to pay a hefty fine: after all, that's what he wanted in the first place.

The various terms and parameters learned from Mahir finally prove useful; your explanations make the clever Sultan sleepy and dampen his curiosity about these human secrets – today was another perfect demonstration for the ministers.

The Vizier promptly pointed out that the Sultan Card can exempt you from the crime of Bloodshed, but the subsequent ritual of desecrating the corpse is another crime. You can only promise to use a fine to obtain forgiveness – fortunately, the Sultan did not focus on the technical details.

5006013.title: A Fine
strings: A Fine
Desecration is insignificant; the key is that you must pay the fine.
8 Gold Coin Fine
Pay an 8 Gold Coin fine to resolve the problem.
Note, if you do not pay within 3 days, the Sultan will execute you.
You dared to ignore the Sultan's fine? Your life is now forfeit.
The coins falling into the cloth bag sound similar to the clattering Mahir creates in a person’s stomach... So, this should also suffice to offset the crime of desecration, right?

5006014.title: Witness a Miracle
strings: Witness a Miracle
Mahir hopes you will personally witness the miracle of this investment... but you have heard strange roars and terrible smells coming from her laboratory recently... it feels dangerous.
Reanimated Zombie
Mahir
Requires the Protagonist's personal inspection
She insists on showing it only to you.
Please note, this event carries some danger.
It suddenly reached out and grabbed your neck.
Your Combat and Physique determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to avoid death.

You met Mahir, but behind her was a silent, veiled 'person' on a leash. This 'person' had metal stitching, preservatives, and countless copper pipes placeed into its flesh, as well as an exoskeleton of steel, making it more massive than the strongest soldier.
 “How do you like it? Isn't it great!” Mahir demonstrated by stimulating specific copper pipes to control its movements: “After ether is imbued, nerves and muscles can still remember simple activities, forming reflex actions, meaning it can perform many simple tasks...”
 Suddenly, a copper pipe sparked and emitted a foul, black smoke, and the gigantic humanoid lunged at you...

You pry open the hand of the work... as that copper pipe was utterly burned, it returns to cold, like an artisan repeatedly mimicking the action of strangling air.
"I don't know what happened... maybe because I did similar choking gestures while creating it, or maybe this thing had such memories in life... this issue is full of mysteries, much unexplored! But in any case, it's a success, we've animated a corpse!"
Mahir rejoices in claiming credit from you, and if ignoring the bruise on your neck, this would indeed seem intriguing...

You struggled desperately, and Mahir screamed and pulled out one copper tube after another... The guards arrived, they cut off the pair of cold hands, but the aether liquid still flowing in its blood did not dissipate; as long as there is resentment, these hands will always be powerful.
There's less and less air, and your struggles become weaker and weaker.
Maybe you could also become a good 'creation'.

5006015.title: Corpse Power Workshop
strings: Corpse Power Workshop

A whole new energy! It can drive heavy gears, process grain, hammer weapons, smelt metals, stir the alchemy cauldron, and even do laundry!

The crucial part is that this force does not rely on the Sultan's river, so it is tax-free.

For the first time, you genuinely deem this a great idea. Of course, this core secret must stay hidden; you have Mahir keep the power source diligently covered.
Reanimated Zombie
Mahir
Loopholes in tax laws
You are clearly aware of a tax loophole here.
The tax-free mill turns and turns, and Gold Coins pour into your pocket like magic. Everyone wants this movable power source, and the farmers and city potters almost started a fight for it.

According to the Sultan's law, all mills must give half of their income to the Sultan because they use the wind and water protected by the Sultan's hand.
 Now, your corpse mill is no exception. Without the price advantage, this business is no longer popular.
The joy of evading taxes has attracted the Sultan's Tax Collector

5006016.title: The Gradually Perfected Creation
strings: The Gradually Perfected Creation

Mahir has built a dedicated workshop for her greatest invention. Although it feels more like a slaughterhouse to you  –  dozens of limbs from various body parts are categorized and hung on the walls, some from the living and some intricately assembled from wood and metal.
 Metal wires and rivets have been removed, the corpse's body has turned into a pile of chaotic connections of water pipes and lead canisters, only the spine is soaked in sparkling ether solution, indicating its origins from a once-living human.
 Mahir couldn't wait to start working.
Place the corpse in the workshop to await modifications.
Use a live human to optimize the parts...

When Adila leaves, Maggie comes to find you. Her wine-flushed cheeks makes her look particularly charming. She tells you that Adila has shared a story about how her family is cursed by a dragon, preventing them from ever having male heirs. Adila seems to truly believe in the existence of the dragon and is determined to slay it to end the curse.

As Maggie speaks, a complicated expression crosses her face. She pauses, as if wanting to say something, but in the end, she simply shakes her head and stays silent. Perhaps even she hasn’t figured out what to say.

Maggie greatly appreciates your respect for her. According to the noble tradition, the lady of the house must be present when entertaining unmarried female guests in the inner chambers.

But Adila doesn't consider herself a guest at all. She eats freely, tearing into meat chunks, and drinks heavily. Eventually, she starts talking about her family.

“My ancestors killed a dragon. A real dragon – a massive, winged lizard.”

You nod and tell her that you’ve heard stories about dragons too. The story came from Jabal – the general who was always obsessed with venturing into the unknown. He once told you that, long ago, the Sultan’s armies spent years scouring the land in search of dragons. Yet even with the strength of an entire nation, they never found even a single dragon scale.

Still, Jabal believes that dragons existed – and so do you.

Adila’s eyes widen, clearly not expecting your agreement. Then, with renewed excitement, she dives into the history of her family. She explains that the Adila family had been warriors for generations. They were once extremely prominent, and among every Sultan's grand generals, there was always one from her lineage.

But about two centuries ago, one of her ancestors encountered a dragon. He tracked it relentlessly, following its trail deep into its lair, and ultimately slew it.

“At the time, my old ancestor thought dragons were nothing more than oversized lizards,” she says with a bitter laugh. “Dead is dead, right? Well, it turns out that dragons are far more formidable than that.”

With its dying breath, the dragon cursed the Adila family, ensuring they would never kill another dragon again. The curse manifested in a cruel way: from that day forward, no male heirs were ever born into the family. And a woman's hands were for spinning thread and cooking - not for wielding swords. A family with only women could never slay a dragon.

As Adila recounts this twisted tale of curses and dragons, she toys with the carving knife stuck in her lamb shank. As Adila recounts this twisted tale, she toys with the carving knife in her lamb shank. Her tone is mocking, but her eyes betray a melancholy she can't hide.

“So you see,” she continues, “even though my family has done well for itself, run entirely by women, the moment I said I wanted to take up the sword, my grandmother, mother, aunts, cousins – all of them – jumped in to stop me. They said the dragon’s curse forbids us from touching weapons, and if I dared to try, it would only anger that dead dragon even more! They're... ah, forget it. Just treat it as drunk talk, nothing more."

Her voice trails off, and she downs the last of her wine in a single, fluid motion. From the way she handles the cup, you suspect she isn’t drunk at all. She just needed the courage of the drink to tell you this story.

You invite Adila and Jabal to your residence. Jabal begins introducing his story of searching for dragons under the Sultan's order, but Adila seems uninterested.

"Enough, General." The girl interrupts Jabal's lengthy description by raising her hand, "I have no intention of handing the dragon-killing technique of my family to the Sultan. I intend to kill that creature myself, only then can I lift the curse on my family."

"Why?" Jabal is puzzled, "I mean, why do you have to break this so-called curse? What's wrong with only having daughters? You're a warrior, aren't you? You're strong, I am a general, I know a strong warrior when I see one. Shouldn't we kill the dragon together? Isn't that the most important thing?"

Adila is stunned, and you can see her face turning red.

"Oh... you men, don't understand anything," she mutters, shaking her head.

Jabal looks to you for help.

So, you're left to try and persuade Adila. Even if she is a very strong warrior, finding and killing a dragon on her own is almost an impossible task. Currently, Jabal is the best partner she can find. He has been tracking dragon clues for many years, and his martial prowess is unquestionable.
But Adila still shook her head vigorously: "You simply don't understand." With something like an unspoken issue, Adila turned even redder, "You simply don't understand...!" With that, she clamped her mouth shut, almost burying her head into a barrel of wine, clearly unwilling to discuss the matter further.

Seeing Adila so resistant, you and Jabal exchange a glance and can only shake your heads.

"Perhaps it's for the better," you console Jabal, "If the sultan finds out there's a new way to find the dragon, he'll surely order you – or me – to bring him the dragon's head, or deliver our own heads to him."

Jabal opens his mouth and is ultimately forced to agree with you. He lets out a long sigh, the dissatisfaction in his eyes fading as he stares into his drink. In the end, he can only concede, "A warrior should slay dragons, that's the warrior's mission. At least that's how I see it... but indeed, there's no choice. If the Sultan forced me to deliver a dragon's head in seven days, I could only kill myself. Well… never mind."

You catch a flicker of regret in Adila's eyes, but what really binds her? She's not ready to tell you now, maybe the timing isn't right.

strings: Things Warriors Do Not Need

But… you glance at Adila. After spending so much time with this warrior, you know her heart is set on battles, on honing herself through combats. Could she ever choose someone to marry? You can’t imagine it.

You hesitate under the weight of their expectations. With all eyes on you, you reluctantly begin to list the people you know. Who could possibly be a good match for her? From what you recall, she seems to have grown rather close to Maggie…
Adila is escorted into your lobby by the women

You can proceed without choosing anyone, but you’d better not ignore them.

Honestly, you don't think what they said makes any sense – why should slaying a dragon be tied to a betrothal?

Adila observed your expression and felt more relieved. She turned to the women confidently, saying, "I can slay the dragon myself."

But the women advised her with worried faces, arguing noisily, and finally, Adila's mother made the final decision: "No, I do not agree for you to go alone!"

Adila finally couldn't take it anymore, stood up, and shouted at the women, "The dragon curses us to stop us from slaying it; the reason we can't slay dragons isn't because we're women – it's because we deem women unfit for dragon slaying!"

With that, she stormed out like an angry wind, leaving the women in the room exchanging glances, and they awkwardly bid you goodbye.
It seems this matter will have to be set aside for now.

Adila's jaw drops as she stares at you in shock, while the women whisper among themselves. 

As the heir of an ancient family, a man of power, and a husband who has been married for years, your proposal is both tempting and improper.

“If you are to marry her,” the grandmother finally speaks up, “according to the laws of the Sultan, she will have the same rights as your wife. Am I correct?”

You nod in agreement. Among the nobility, every wife is treated equally, with no distinctions in status. The law demands fairness between them. But fairness is easier said than done… and that is one of the reasons why most men are not willing to marry a second, let alone a fourth, wife.

"Well," she continues, "though becoming a second wife may not be entirely proper, for Adila, with all her scars and unladylike ways... to find such a noble husband who treats his first wife so well – it's not a bad match after all."

The women nod in agreement, and Adila’s jaw drops even further.

“I will marry her,” you declare again.

The women burst into excited cheers. The grandmother wipes her tears, saying that she never thought she would live to see this day – Adila married. The other women chime in, saying Adila is far too unruly – always getting into fights and going on adventures – nothing like a proper woman should be. Since the dragon’s curse made their entire household ladies, they should stay quietly in the inner quarters, leaving all fighting to the men to atone for slaying dragons…

“Enough!” Adila suddenly shouts, standing up. Her entire body trembles, and her fists clench tightly.

“The dragon cursed us so we could never slay another dragon again. But the reason we cannot slay dragons isn’t because we’re women – it’s because we’ve convinced ourselves that women are unworthy of slaying dragons!”

With these words, she storms out of the room like a furious wind, leaving you and the other women behind. The grandmother and the aunts exchange uneasy glances, then awkwardly bid you farewell.

Though a bit regrettable, it seems this matter will have to be put on hold for now.

As soon as Jabal enters, the women begin to stir.

After all, he comes from a warrior lineage – a prestigious family. He's a strong warrior and the Sultan's trusted minister... Who could be a more suitable match for Adila?

Yet, puzzled, Jabal looks at the gathered women and takes you aside: "You mentioned something about finding a dragon here, but what's going on?"

You explain the connection between dragon slaying and marriage.

Jabal scratches his head: "Ah... I see, though I feel we could slay the dragon together regardless of marriage, nobody would lose, right? But... I understand, being a noble, I understand these traditions."

He pauses, then says, "I want to have a private word with Adila, ah, and you, [player.name], let's have a quick discussion, then decide about marriage."

Away from the women's watchful eyes, you move to the next room. Once the servants withdraw and close the door, Jabal speaks: "I've always wanted to slay a dragon. If they truly exist, it should be my destiny to hunt one. But tell me truly – do they exist?"

Adila nods firmly.

"Then I will marry you. But let me be clear – I can't promise to love you, because my heart belongs to the hunt until I've faced the greatest beast alive. I'm not thinking about love or heirs right now. What I can promise is respect, a fighting partnership, and a shared quest to bring down this legendary creature. Would that work for you?"

Adila's eyes light up: "I couldn't ask for a better proposal! Don't worry about love. I never understood what's there to love about men anyway. But fighting alongside you to slay dragons? Now that's the kind of partnership I can appreciate!"

The two clasp hands with the firm grip of fellow warriors.

You breathe a sigh of relief. It seems the match is perfectly made.

When Adiila sees Maggie, she looks startled, but soon, she lowers her head, avoiding Maggie’s gaze.
Maggie gently takes hold of her friend's hand, which habitually grasped a sword, and softly mentions a few names. The women begin chattering noisily: this one’s family isn’t good enough, that one isn’t strong enough… Finally, Adila can’t hold back any longer. She leaps to her feet, her fists clenched tightly. “Enough!”
Her sudden outburst startles Maggie and everyone else. For a brief moment, the room falls silent, only to be filled seconds later by Adila’s furious voice. “The dragon cursed us so we could never slay another dragon again. But the reason we cannot slay dragons isn’t because we’re women – it’s because we’ve convinced ourselves that women are unworthy of slaying dragons!”
With these words, she storms out of the room, pushing you aside as she goes. As she brushes past you, you think you catch a glimmer of tears in her eyes. Perhaps it is just your imagination.

Adila's face lights up with frustration as she sees Maggie. She grabs Maggie’s hand, starting to complaint.

"Maggie, back me up here! Everyone keeps telling me I need to find a husband before I can slay the dragon. But I don't need a husband – what I need is a dumb dragon's head dripping with blood!"

Adila seems to regain all her courage, proudly announcing, "Listen, I know everything there is to know about slaying dragons. Nothing can stop me. I'll track down that dragon and kill it myself!"

Maggie is very worried, comforting her while dissuading her. After all, it’s a dragon, the largest, most cunning, and most terrifying beast in the world...

Perhaps Maggie’s worried look touches Adila, she ponders for a moment, looks up at you, "I don't need a man's help, but... perhaps Maggie is right. I hope that Maggie can help me, would that be all right? "

[s2.name] didn't please the women. They whisper criticisms among themselves, creating a tense air, before the overflowing edge became too much to handle...

"Enough!" Unable to bear it any longer, Adila stands up, shouting at them all.

"The dragon cursed us so we could never slay another dragon again. But the reason we cannot slay dragons isn't because we're women – it's because we've convinced ourselves that women are unworthy of slaying dragons!"

With these words, she storms out of the room like a furious wind, leaving the others behind. The grandmother and the aunts exchange uneasy glances, then awkwardly bid you farewell.

It seems this matter must be set aside for now.

5006033.title: Journey Alone
strings: Journey Alone

Adila is determined to set out and slay a dragon. The Book of Dragonslaying left by her ancestors records the kinds of habitats dragons favor most. She plans to search every possible location near the empire based on these descriptions.

Perhaps because of her fallout with her family, she seems completely unprepared for such a long journey… Maybe you could offer her some travel funds.
Adila is making preparations
Support of 8 Gold Coins
This level of support only requires money.
Adila's money was not enough to support this prolonged exploration, so she had to take on some jobs like escorting caravans and hunting beasts on the way, which greatly slowed the search progress...
You offer financial support to Adila
You don't plan to finance her

When you take out the pouch of gold, Adila repeatedly refuses it. She has already decided not to marry anyone and to prove herself on her own. 

You tell Adila that you are just helping a friend. Whether she uses the money to slay a dragon or not is her decision and has nothing to do with you. Hearing this, Adila thanks you gratefully and sets off on her journey without looking back.

A few days later, she returns, full of excitement, and comes to you first. She tells you that she managed to find traces of a dragon.

According to the Book of DragonSlaying, dragons rarely leave footprints. These giant lizards are cautious, knowing their tracks are too distinctive and could easily be recognized. As a result, they only rest on hard, unyielding stone that won't retain any marks. But even the most careful plans have their flaws – they forget that the sulfurous fumes they breathe can also leave traces behind.

"I found stones bearing these traces near a habitat that matches the descriptions," she says excitedly. "This must be the dragon's lair. All I need to do now is confirm that the creature is inside, and then I can prepare to strike…"

She excitedly outlines her plans, too impatient to wait another moment.

Adila doesn’t have enough money to sustain this long journey – a fact both you and she are well aware of. You think she should suffer for her recklessness and eventually give up, but you are wrong. Along the way, she takes on jobs as a caravan guard or hunting wild beasts. Though these tasks greatly slow her search, not once does she regret her choices, nor does she bow to fate.

5006034.title: Struggling Forward
strings: Struggling Forward

Adila does not return as you expected, bowing to her family or to fate. By the time you think of her again, she has been out of contact for a long time. Perhaps she is still struggling for her dream, or perhaps she has already fallen along the way.
Adila is still on her adventure
Finally, Adila comes back

A long, long time passed – so long that you almost forgot her name. Until one day, Adila knocks on your door. She looks utterly exhausted, her body covered in scars, yet her eyes shine as if cleansed by a torrential storm.

She tells you, breathless with excitement, that after a painstaking search, she has finally discovered traces of the dragon.

According to the Book of DragonSlaying, dragons rarely leave footprints. These giant lizards are cautious, knowing their tracks are too distinctive and could easily be recognized. As a result, they only rest on hard, unyielding stone that won't retain any marks. But even the most careful plans have their flaws – they forget that the sulfurous fumes they breathe can also leave traces behind.

"I found stones bearing these traces near a habitat that matches the descriptions," she says excitedly. "This must be the dragon's lair. All I need to do now is confirm that the creature is inside, and then I can prepare to strike…"

Without regard for her exhaustion, she bids you farewell as soon as she finishes speaking, ready to set off once more. You ask her why she doesn't go home, why she doesn’t take a moment to rest. She simply smiles without answering, as if pausing would cause her to crumble to dust and scatter her name to the winds..

That stubborn smile haunts your dreams night after night. Deep down, you sense that her visit was nothing more than a final farewell to this world. You wake from dreams of the dragon and blood, only to realize you still have a chance to help her...

5006035.title: Dragon Lair Investigation
strings: Dragon Lair Investigation
Adila found a possible lair. She decides to create a hidden base near the dragon lair to scout its exact whereabouts. You think, maybe someone under your command could help her…
Adila is scouting.
You could send an experienced stealth practitioner to assist, which means this person needs at least 4 in Stealth.
Some items can help conceal a form
After completing the investigation, a few days of rest are needed before proceeding to the next step.
As night falls, a sudden gale sweeps over sparse woodland, carrying an unusual scent...
Your Stealth determines your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to avoid the dragon's observation.

Something approaches... Adila hides in her hiding place, holding her breath, her trembling fingers clutching the sword hilt. In the dark, she can't discern the shape of the thing, but she sees a pair of enormous, fire-lit eyes, and smells the acrid sulfur...
It is the dragon, she has found the right place. Amidst the overwhelming wind, tears almost well up for the discovery.

While hiding in the shade of the trees, Adila suddenly feels an overwhelming wave of terror wash over her… For a brief moment, a pair of enormous, fire-lit eyes glance her way. That alone sends shivers down her spine, leaving her feet frozen in place. It takes her several seconds to realize that this is the dragon’s aura of dominance. 
She summons all her strength to break free from the fear and tumbles down the hillside to escape…
She manages to escape the dragon’s wrath, but her reckless flight has left her gravely injured.

She struggles to break free from this unspeakable terror, yet her exhausted, battered body can no longer endure.
In her final moment, with trembling hands, she draws the sharp sword at her waist, then melts together with the blade in the searing dragon's breath. Perhaps, someday, among the windblown sands that sweep across your face, you will meet her again.

You spend a large sum, hiring the best craftsmen, preparing everything Adila needs in a few days. She nervously and carefully reviews these items, highly satisfied with their quality. She solemnly expresses gratitude and tells you she'll set off tomorrow, battling the dragon's curse and embracing her destiny.

How foolish they say, to spend a fortune on such an impossible dream! People mock you, calling it a waste of money – but you're content to let them think so. Your extravagant investment has built quite a reputation for you.

5006038.title: Heroic Act of Dragonslaying
strings: Heroic Act of Dragonslaying
Adila set out with her family's blessings to slay the dragon. At this point, you can no longer intervene in this battle that belongs to Adila.
This is Adila's battle.
Like a beast from another world. Fire burns in its every breath.
The final supplies you prepared for her might be useful in a grueling battle... perhaps.
Having the fireproof robe is crucial to the outcome of this encounter.
In the consuming flames of the dragon's curse, can Adila survive? No one knows…
The number of dice provided by your Combat and Physique is affected by the opponent's attributes.
Without a fireproof robe, Adila needs at least 5 Successes to defeat the dragon and at least 1 Success to return alive.

Adila is back, more scars than skins, less eyes than Djinn, but she is alive. 

In her trembling hand lies a large sulfur-colored gem beyond mortal imagination. Within the gem, flames flow as though beating heartbeats, as if the fury of an entire cosmo had been imprisoned in a palm-sized crystal.

"I exchanged my eye with it." Adila raises the gem in hand, "This is the Dragon's Eye. I couldn't kill it. It escaped into another dimension. My sword couldn't pierce the barrier. But, this world is now without dragons. I succeeded." 

She proudly addresses everyone, "The dragon cursed our bloodline to bear only daughters, thinking it would strip us of our dragon-slaying destiny. But it was wrong – I've proven that a woman can defeat a dragon. We can achieve anything we set our minds to, become whoever we want to be. That curse? It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"

Everyone present – the women, nobles, and anxious onlookers gathered at your home – gasps in awe. That gem seems to be from another world. Its appearance makes even the most skeptical admit that dragons existed, and Adila is the warrior who defeated the dragon and forced it into another dimension.

Refusing all help, she makes her way to you with dignified trudges. Then she kneels, offering the Dragon's Eye gem to you.

"None of this would have been possible without you, [player.name]. You have witnessed my despair, my courage, my struggle, my rise. I dedicate the dominion of the Dragon's Eye gem to you."

Adila is back. She is carried into your mansion, covered in blood and wounds, one eye gone, but she is alive.

In her trembling hand lies a large sulfur-colored gem beyond mortal imagination. Within the gem, flames flow like living fire, as if the fury of an entire world had been imprisoned in a palm-sized crystal.

"I exchanged my eye with it." Adila looks weak, yet immensely strong. She raises the gem in hand, "This is the Dragon's Eye. I couldn't kill it. It escaped into another dimension. My sword couldn't pierce the barrier. However, this world has no dragons now. I succeeded."

It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"

With the support of servants, she struggles to her feet and walks resolutely towards you. Then she kneels before you, offering the Dragon's Eye gem to you.

"None of this would have been possible without you, [player.name]. You have witnessed my despair, my courage, my struggle, and I dedicate the dominion of the Dragon's Eye gem to you."

"I exchanged my eye with it." Adila says, looking desperately weak, as if clinging to consciousness just long enough to reach you, "This is the Dragon's Eye. I couldn't kill it. It escaped into another dimension. My sword couldn't pierce the barrier. However, this world has no dragons now. I succeeded." 

Drawing a deep breath, Adila pauses. The flame that once burned in the dragon's eye now continues to blaze within her own.

 "The dragon cursed our bloodline to bear only daughters, thinking it would strip us of our dragon-slaying destiny. But it was wrong – I've proven that a woman can defeat a dragon. We can achieve anything we set our minds to, become whoever we want to be. That curse? It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"

With the support of servants, she struggles to her feet and walks resolutely towards you. Then she kneels before you, offering the Dragon's Eye gem to you.

"None of this would have been possible without you. You have witnessed my despair, my courage, my struggle, and I dedicate the dominion of the Dragon's Eye gem to you."

Adila is carried into your mansion, unconscious and broken. Her once-proud armor is charred black, her body drenched in blood. Her hair and what remains of her clothing tell a tale of dragon's fire. You immediately summon the best physician, watching helplessly as she battles through days of burning fever. When she finally opens her eyes, nothing is the same.

The dragon took more than just her eye. Her arm and leg are mangled, and the devastating burns have left her confined to bed. She could no longer be a warrior.

"It seems I can no longer serve you," she whispers, her voice barely audible. Yet in the face of this cruel fate, Adila shows neither rage nor despair. No curses for the world, no hatred for the damn dragon. She simply closes her remaining eye, a strange peace settling over her features.

"But it doesn't matter," she says softly. "My daughter... or my daughter's daughter... One day, there will be an Adila stronger and luckier than I ever was. And I will be there for her, just as my mother and grandmother were there for me. What I couldn't finish, she will complete. One day."

Adila never came back.

A nearby shepherd found her sword, her armor, and fragments of a shattered skull. The dragon deliberately left these remains in a place frequented by humans, perhaps as a warning or a threat.

You deliver these remains to Adila’s mother and grandmother. The women take turns holding the charred skull, washing it with their tears.

“We will have daughters again,” says the grandmother, gripping the sword once more. “She will choose to be a warrior. She will face the trials. She will stand against the dragon. Even though I would give my life to bring my little Adila back – our daughters will fight, no matter what!”

They thank you politely before leaving with the remains.

Before they go, they leave Adila’s armor with you.

5006039.title: A King-Sized Gift
strings: A King-Sized Gift
The Sultan allows you to break any Sultan Card, and the task will be completed by him.
You can break any Sultan Card.
Any Sultan Card is allowed!
The Sultan's patience is always limited; he only waits for 3 turns.

For such a non-challenging task, the Sultan waves his hand, and guards drag someone from the street to execute him. Who this unfortunate soul is, whether man or woman, whose family member or friend they are, what dreams they hold or crimes they've committed – no one cares. Everything becomes meaningless with the crisp snap of breaking cards.

For such a non-challenging task, the Sultan glances at the courtiers standing silent with fear, casually calls a name, and strolls away, toying with a searing gem. He has more pressing matters to do, not bothering to witness the bloody scene he leaves behind.

You notice the Sultan's gaze circling above you like a hawk over its prey. You happen to draw a silver tier card…

Cold sweat trickles down as you nearly sink to your knees, but the Sultan shifts his gaze away with a smile, lazily naming another unfortunate soul.

How amusing you must be to him. Toying with the searing gem in his hand, he's loath to kill you.

Had it been before the Sultan had obtained the Dragon's Eye Gem, he might have crafted some amusing ways to break his hard-won golden card, savoring how fear rippled across his courtiers' faces. His surviving relatives—the general, the princess, and Vasir—each met their end in rather creative ways.
But today, the Sultan had found something far grander—the eye of a dragon that fled to another dimension. He could almost see that unconquered, pristine white land, his heart set on reaching it—no longer bound by the petty bloodshed of the mortal world.
He gave a few brief commands to his attendants, breaking the card in half, and leaves the court with unhurried grace. Not long after, you heard of an unassuming aged consort's death in the harem—one who once served a former Sultan, and who, they say, gave birth to a demon.

The Sultan idly slips off a ring and tosses it onto the lapis lazuli floor. The crisp sound echoes through the hall.

The courtiers hesitate for a moment, then descend into exaggerated chaos. They throw themselves into the performance of their lives, faces burning red as they fight over a normal ring, while their master is already gone – toying with the dragon's eye gem as he glides away. You stand amid the chaos, with one simple regret: if only he had thrown away the magical ring instead.

This is no difficult task. The Sultan nods, calls his attendants, gives a few commands, and breaks the card in half.

After court, unease lingers in your heart until you hear of a man in the Dark Alley lured to death by a trail of coins, as pathetic as a foolish bird diving into a trap for a few grains of wheat. Only then does your unease finally settle.

So the game goes: the Sultan's generosity is always accompanied by death. No, Sultan's generosity...should be accompanied by death.

This is no difficult task. The Sultan nods, then lazily gestures toward a courtier, gifting him a chest brimming with gold and jewels.

The man dabs at his forehead and offers his thanks, knowing all too well that the Sultan's generosity comes at a price. In time, he'll pay back ten times over, a hundred times over. The Sultan has suspended a sword above his head, and until it falls, peaceful sleep will elude him.

Everyone knows this truth... yet somehow, they all find themselves wondering – and you're no exception – why him? Why not me? It seems he won't be the only one lying sleepless tonight.

"Hahaha..." The Sultan's laughter echoes through the lapis lazuli palace.

He looks at you with approval, then commands his attendants to draw from the treasury to build a palace – a sacred sanctuary solely to enshrine the dragon's eye.

Soon, hundreds of poets will vie to tell of the Sultan's legendary dragon-slaying triumph, each claiming how effortlessly he triumphed. Countless beauties and heroes will come to behold the sacred dragon's eye, only to bow beneath the Sultan's banner.

And the dragon's eye will watch it all, mock it all, until every soul in this world falls silent, and every stone crumbles to ash.

The Sultan toys with the dragon's eye gem, nodding listlessly before gliding away. Perhaps he goes to his harem for carnal pleasures. Not long after, the magician returns to court and announces that the stone tier Carnality Card has been broken. As for the rest, nothing remarkable.

The Sultan toys with the dragon's eye gem, nodding thoughtfully, and then glides away. Perhaps he goes to his harem for carnal pleasures. Not long after, the magician returns to court and announces that the bronze tier Carnality Card has been broken. Later, you hear that whenever the consorts speak of the dragon's eye gem, a flicker of terror crosses their faces.

The Sultan toys with the dragon's eye gem, glances at you, and smiles thoughtfully. His golden accessories chime delicately as he rises from the throne, approaching you with measured, condescending steps.

In an instant, countless thoughts flood your mind. You recall the folk illustrations and novels, and the treasonous words you once dared to speak... You dread hearing your name pass from his lips, yet cannot deny that faint hope stirring in your heart. If it were merely an act of indulgence, if – just if – you could profane that golden throne in this way, if... You lower your head deeply, unwilling to let your expression be seen by the Sultan’s piercing gaze. 

Then, a broken card clatters to the ground at your feet. The Sultan laughs heartily and glides away. Only after his footsteps fade completely do you find strength to wipe your brow. Of course – you should have known. For one who commands a vast harem, choosing a silver tier consort is not a difficult task.
Presenting this card, you cautiously concealed your ambition in your eyes. There will be a day! Even if not now, eventually, you will leave the Sultan with no choice.

What a non-challenging task! The Sultan waves his hand in boredom, ordering the destruction of a small nearby oasis. 

He keeps no garrison there, because he needs fresh bloodshed to stir the ripples of savagery in his heart. And time and again, people are driven back to this blood-soaked land by the cruel, endless desert, despite its soil stained with death and strewn with broken blades.

What a non-challenging task! The Sultan orders the map to be brought forth, then carelessly flicks a gold coin onto it.

All hold their breath, eyes fixed on the coin as it rolls across the map, finally coming to rest upon a town. "This one," the master of the empire taps the map.

A day later, all inhabitants are slaughtered, though they too lived under the Sultan's rule. Nothing strange about this – the nobles treat their own kept slaves no differently.

Conquest Cards are the Sultan's favorite, the sum of countless bloodsheds, offering more exhilaration beyond carnality and extravagance.

As he receives your card, thoughtfully tracing its etched patterns, all fall silent – fearing the Sultan might turn his bloodlust upon their carefully cultivated territories.

Today, someone's fate is sealed. As long as it's not you, what does it matter who? Let him curse you madly, yet it means nothing: a lord stripped of his domain has no right to stand in this lapis lazuli palace.

Your master burst into laughter. Excellent, very excellent. This golden tier conquest is precisely what he desired.
He already possessed the Dragon's Eye, already possessed the fearsome name of a dragonslayer. Countless beauties and heroes will come, submit under his banner, leaving only his enemies... who still dare be his enemy?
Let them tremble! He will rule the entire continent and oceans, not only that, even the untouched realm where the dragon fled, a brand new, pure white, awaiting conquest...

Wherever she goes, women flock to her, admiring both her and her husband, wishing they were her.

With this gem in her possession, she seems willing to overlook any of your mistakes, perhaps.

You return the dragon's eye to her, unwilling to take the glory that belongs to the dragonslayer – that belongs to her. 

Adila looks at the gem, then at you, and finally bows deeply with sincerity. 

"I accept your gift," she says.

strings: Unmatched Love
You give this unmatched, unique glory to Maggie, enough for her to forget most of your past mistakes.
Past Grudges

The scene of you kneeling, offering the dragon's eye to her, often appears in Maggie's sweetest dreams. In the haze of half-sleep, you faintly feel her tender lips brush against your cheek, a gentle kiss she can't help but give.

strings: One-on-one Sword Training
