Catching your gaze, Adila, unusually shy, tries to hide the sword behind her back. "Is Lady Maggie here? We had an appointment," she asks.
Maggie and Adila have agreed that Maggie will learn swordsmanship from Adila.
Adila is ready to be Maggie's swordsmanship tutor.

You hypocritical man, you broke your promise!
Maggie was obviously displeased, but she said nothing. After that, she never mentions sword training again.
You fully support Maggie learning swordsmanship from Adila.

This day, when you return from the court, you find Adila still in your home.
She's holding Maggie's hand, teaching her the proper sword stance.
Adila wears only a wrap around her torso. Her scarred body, viewed from behind, rivals that of any warrior.
While Maggie, in fine silk with a gauze veil, looks too delicate to wield a sword...
"Just so, keep it steady, get used to the feel of the sword!"
"Oh, oh, it's so heavy..."
"Imagine it as a pot, a kettle, or your husband's head!"
"Ha, then I'd drop it!"
They laugh and continue training, unaware of your presence.

5006043.title: Maggie's Secret Recipe
strings: Maggie's Secret Recipe
Maggie gives you a jar of ointment said to remove scars and protect skin. Maybe you could find someone to test it.
You can test this ointment yourself, or choose any follower to test it on your behalf.
Maggie's Exclusive Secret Recipe
The ointment is usable once and can permanently increase Charisma by 1.

Maggie takes the ointment you offer, a little startled. And you swear to her: there's no other woman worth your pleasing. No other woman whose face you care about. Maggie hears you out. Presses her lips together. Smiles. "Then help me apply it, my dear husband." With that, she takes your hand and leads you behind the bedroom curtains.

You thought Adila would refuse the ointment. After all, she'd said those scars, those marks of battle, were her glory. But she takes it. Happily. Then asks if Maggie sent you... Seeing her like this, so pleased, so smug, you're starting to regret it.
The ointment works very well, [s1.name]'s skin looks better. However, you dare not ask Maggie for more to give to your followers, after all... it's Maggie's secret recipe...

5006044.title: Ways to Rest
strings: Ways to Rest
Maggie brings the maids' handwoven dresses to Adila. You're surprised to see how close they've become. But then you realize – of course everyone would like someone as sweet as Maggie.
Maggie has gone out
Maggie can't stand Adila anymore!

When you see Adila again, your eyes immediately catch the delicate ruffles of silk lining peeking out from the collar of her battle-worn leather armor. Oh, it's Maggie's gift… You look away.

So what? Maggie makes all your clothes and accessories too. She even helped fix your belt before you left this morning... No, wait – why are you suddenly comparing yourself to another woman?

5006045.title: The Purpose of Combat
strings: The Purpose of Combat

Adila is here for Maggie's sword training again. She's waiting for Maggie, eagerly like a puppy with a wagging tail. Though you've already promised Maggie, you find yourself wishing she wouldn't come...
Maggie wants to continue swordsmanship practice.
Adila looks forward to meeting with Maggie.
If Maggie doesn't have time, that'll be the end of it.

They're more invested in this than you expected. You thought it was just another of Maggie's whims... But now at night, when you hold her small hands, you can feel the beginnings of calluses forming on her palms.
"A fight isn't about killing your opponent—it's about staying alive," Adila says, guiding Maggie's stance with a hand on her waist. "That's why defense always comes first."
"Just like love," Maggie says with a smile. "For us women, protecting ourselves matters more than striking first."
You notice Adila's smile, with a hint of shyness...

5006046.title: Book of Dragonslaying
strings: Book of Dragonslaying

An ancient manuscript by the Adila family, filled with secrets of the dragons. Adila entrusts this sacred task to Maggie – decoding the book's mysteries. And you, as the closest man to Maggie, naturally find yourself helping with the work...
Ancient scrolls documenting dragon-slaying techniques.
Adila entrusted this heavy burden to Maggie.
You can offer Maggie some assistance.
You accompany Maggie day and night.
You do not meddle in this matter.

You stay by Maggie's side, telling her you're here to help.

Maggie sighs with relief, hugging you.

Together, you and Maggie study the Book of Dragonslaying, trying to decode its mysteries. The text begins to dance, shake and twist, until you drift into sleep, falling into a wild and barren place...

When you wake, Maggie stands at the room's center, arms raised above her head, frozen in a falling pose.

You embrace her. She relaxes in your arms... then opens her eyes, telling you she faced the dragon in her dream. The dragon asked her a strange question – what was the true purpose of slaying dragons...

"I answered 'freedom'... I want freedom, not just freedom as a woman, but freedom of the soul..." Maggie rubs her temples wearily. "Then the voice faded, and I saw the dragon. I think... I can now fully understand the book."

Adila is amazed by Maggie's dream revelation.

"I'd heard that text written in dragon's blood could connect to their mental realm – I never believed it true," Adila says in wonder. "But it requires extraordinary inner strength. Good thing you were here..."

Maggie gives a soft laugh, shaking her head as she takes your hand. "Without [player.name], I wouldn't have made it. My goodness, you have no idea how terrified I was when the dragon appeared..."

You have many matters to attend to, and with Maggie too distracted to spare any thought for the estate lately, the burden falls even heavier on you.

Maggie understands this and doesn't ask too much of you.

One morning, Maggie suddenly bursts into your room. She looks extremely tired yet unusually excited, clutching ink-stained papers, with ink smudges on her clothes and face.

"I've seen it... I've actually seen the dragon in my dream!" she shouts at you. "I can truly help now – not relying on my husband, not on you, just by myself!"

She laughs with joy and races back to her study to write down her insights – information that could help Adila track the dragon. You stand there bewildered, wondering if you've made a wise decision or not...

Adila is amazed by Maggie's dream revelation.

"I'd heard that text written in dragon's blood could connect to their mental realm – I never believed it true," Adila says in wonder. "But it requires extraordinary inner strength. Good thing you were by my side!"

They exchange a knowing smile – a private moment that has absolutely nothing to do with you.

5006047.title: Necessary Preparations
strings: Necessary Preparations

According to the Book of Dragonslaying, that damned giant lizard breathes scorching heat, and most standard armor in the market offers little protection against flames... Maggie has been worrying about how to solve it.
Maggie decides to handle this matter herself
You estimate that this will cost at least 20 Gold Coins.
You can assist Maggie with this task yourself
You can take this opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of Silver tier or lower.
Maggie calculated that it would take 20 Gold Coins to purchase it.

You refused to help Maggie, so she have to juggle housework while making time to order Adila a set of fire-resistant armor.
You rarely see her; every morning, she goes out, and when you fall asleep, she hasn't returned. You don't know how she visits the blacksmiths and weavers, haggles with merchants, or gathering money for these things. You only see excellent equipments after another arriving at the courtyard, and Maggie checks them herself, the merchants speaking to her carefully without any neglect.
A subtle feeling races through your mind, does Maggie really need you anymore? It seems... Maggie can handle everything without you.

You set aside a large sum of money to support Maggie, telling her that you will handle the household affairs so she doesn't have to worry. Relieved, she embraces you and throws herself wholeheartedly into her own intricate war.
Day after day, she busies herself visiting weavers and blacksmiths, meeting with courtiers' wives, and haggling with merchants. By candlelight, order after order is finalized, and finely crafted equipment steadily makes its way into your courtyard. Maggie examines each piece with sharp eyes, allowing no room for negligence or sloppiness.
Is she pushing herself too hard? You feel a pang of guilt for not helping her more, but Maggie's face glows with happiness. "Oh, you know," she says, "as the lady of the house, my job is all about managing money – how to save it, how to spend it. And honestly? I think I'm doing pretty well!"
She smiles, and with newfound confidence and achievement, she glows more radiantly than ever.

You set aside a large sum of money to support Maggie, helping her negotiate with the merchants in person.
Working together, you see as finely crafted equipment steadily makes its way into your courtyard, leaving no room for negligence or sloppiness. And far from being difficult, these greedy merchants are all too eager to win your favor, offering discounts without hesitation. Though the savings are modest, Maggie still cheers with delight, standing on tiptoe to plant a warm kiss on your cheek.
"I'm so glad you're here with me!" she says, her face bright with happiness. With newfound confidence and achievement, she glows more radiantly than ever.

How foolish they say, to spend a fortune on such an impossible dream! People mock you both, calling it a waste of money – but you're content to let them think so. Your extravagant investment has built quite a reputation for you.

5006048.title: Adila is seeking the dragon.
strings: Adila is seeking the dragon.
The Book of Dragonslaying records the favorite habitats of dragons. Confidently, Adila has already set out to inspect each possible location to confirm the true site of the dragon's lair.
Adila is searching for the dragon's trail.
This is not a difficult adventure – there is no need for you to intervene.
Adila has returned safely

Adila comes straight to you and Maggie, excitedly announcing that she has been lucky enough to discover the dragon's trail.

According to The Book of Dragonslaying, dragons rarely leave footprints. These giant lizards are extremely cautious, knowing their tracks are too distinctive and easily recognized. As a result, they only rest on hard, unyielding rocks that leave no traces. But even the most careful plans have their flaws – they forget that the sulfurous fumes they breathe can also leave traces behind.

"I found stones bearing these traces near a habitat that matches the descriptions," she says excitedly. "This must be the dragon's lair. All I need to do now is confirm that the creature is inside, and then I can prepare to strike…"

5006049.title: Before Departure
strings: Before Departure

Once Adila finishes telling you what she's found, she's eager to get back to her journey. She's practically bouncing with excitement about finding the dragon's trail, ready to rush off right away. 
But Maggie stops her. "I have something for you," she says with a smile, leading her into the courtyard.
Adila is preparing for the next step of her plan.
Maggie prepared the belongings for her.
Maggie hands Adila the fireproof robe she prepared.

Tired and dust-covered from the road, Adila solemnly accepts the equipment and heads out right away. On her journey, she discovered a giant stone marked with sulfurous dragon breath. According to The Book of Dragonslaying, a dragon's lair must be close by. She settles in for what might be a long wait, determined to find concrete evidence of the dragon's trail.

5006050.title: As Marriage Should Be
strings: As Marriage Should Be

You do everything you can to help Maggie. It's like going back to the old days when you first got married, when you were deeply in love – sharing the same dreams, walking the same path. The feeling is beyond wonderful.
If there had ever been any discord between you...
You can take this opportunity to remove 1 Wife's Resentment
On a night when the weight of her burdens has finally been lifted and her tasks completed, Maggie curls up in your arms and sleeps soundly, as if all her worries have vanished.

5006051.title: Adila is on an adventure.
strings: Adila is on an adventure.
Adila is confirming the giant dragon's trail near the dragon's lair...
There's still no news from Adila.

Adila returnes. More scars mark her body; upon asking, she shrug it off, saying she narrowly escaped getting discovered by the dragon while observing its nest closely. Thankfully she overcame the fear and rolled across the mountain then ran away. 
Maggie think this is due to the blessing ritual working. She joyfully embraces Adila, expressing her concerns. Adila looks uneasy too, but in her eyes lies more resolve and excitement: 
"That is truly a dragon! That beast!!" She clutches Maggie's hand tightly. "Maggie, I don't know how to thank you. Listen, I'll slay that dragon and offer its head to you, I promise!"

5006052.title: Blessing Ritual
strings: Blessing Ritual
Maggie seems very anxious lately... She's worried about Adila, so she decides to perform a blessing ritual, praying for Adila's safe return. You promise to help her with the ritual.
You need to take out at least 10 Gold Coins to complete this Ritual.
If you take out 20 Gold Coins, you can break an Extravagance Card of Silver tier or lower.
Pray with sincere devotion
Your sheer stalling angered your wife. Maggie invited monks in person to bless Adila, and she doesn't speak to you, the promise-breaking person, for a long time after that.

You arrange for the Purist Order's priests to come. They perform a blessing ritual, reciting prayers for Adila's safe return and success in her future journey. 
Maggie kneels at the priest's feet and presents her offerings – pomegranates, cheese and syrup. The priest casts them into the sacred flames to honor the gods.

Donations to the church are considered "extravagance" – though the church protests this view, arguing that such charitable acts are righteous and worthy. After all, no price is too high for divine favor.

However, the Sultan considers it a waste of money. He rarely wastes money in this way, but he seems to admire your extravagant spending style.

5006053.title: Maggie, let me ask you...
strings: Maggie, let me ask you...
Adila's sudden disclosure makes it difficult for you to sleep. After tossing and turning for a long time, you can't help it and wake Maggie up...
You really want to ask Maggie.
You tell Maggie everything Adila has said.

Maggie's drowsy eyes suddenly fly wide open at your words. She remains stunned for a moment before coming back to her senses.

"Oh my dear Adila, my goodness... I have no idea she felt this way..." She seems to gradually recall her various interactions with Adila. "She did mention she could never picture herself with a man..."

She sinks into deep contemplation... Adila wants to elope with her after slaying the dragon... What would she think? You watch her anxiously, searching her eyes for any hint of her thoughts.

Almost instinctively, Maggie nods. Then, as if suddenly remembering your presence beside her, she quickly shakes her head.
"I won't give up being the mistress of this mansion to become a femal warrior's... lover. That's too silly, right?"
You had hoped for something more – perhaps a promise of her love – but Maggie simply lets out a small yawn and says, "Go to sleep, my darling."
For now, you'll have to take what comfort you can from those words.
With Adila still away and nothing certain, all you can do is push down the anxiety gnawing at your heart and try to find some rest.

Maggie simply tilts her head in confusion, thinking hard for a moment before confirming this isn't a joke.

"Run away with her? But I don't want to run away with her. How could she say that? I don't have any romantic feelings for her... Oh my goodness, I've never had feelings for anyone but you, never!"

She turns to you, eyes widening. "Wait... you actually thought I...?"

Oh, heavens, you quickly assure her that you've never doubted your relationship and swear to it. Maggie studies your face for a long moment before letting her eyes drift shut. "Alright, darling, go to sleep. It's late."

And with that, the matter is settled. You breathe a small sigh of relief. It's all Adila's crazy talk to blame.

"Ah, how could she say such a thing? To my husband, no less!"

Maggie finally snaps back to her senses, her fists clenched tight. "Marrying you has been the greatest joy of my life. Even through all the torments we endured from the Sultan, I've never once regretted it. How could she – how dare she – think my love for you is so superficial?"

Maggie remains angry for a while before turning to self-reproach, wondering if she had somehow led Adila to misread their friendship. You quickly draw her into your arms, murmuring words of comfort. Together, you sink into each other's embrace, soon drifting off to sleep in the gentle warmth of candlelight.

5006054.title: Heroic Act of Dragonslaying
strings: Heroic Act of Dragonslaying
Adila set out with Maggie's blessing to slay the dragon. At this point, you can no longer intervene in this battle that belongs to Adila.
This is Adila's battle.

It must be a grueling battle. In fact, deep down, you feel this is nothing short of a suicide mission. If there's anyone left in this world who still believes in emerging victorious – bathed in dragon's blood with its head as trophy – it would be Maggie. You've witnessed it yourself: on some quiet evenings, she makes her way to the city gates, her gaze fixed on the distant path Adila left.

Sometimes, you stand beside her. More often, she stands alone atop the city walls, quietly waiting – though hope grows fainter each day – for someone who may never return...

5006055.title: Spread in the evening light...
strings: Spread in the evening light...
One evening, you didn't see Maggie at home.
Adila returned victorious.
Maggie's eager waiting.
How much resentment might a wife feel?

You barely notice her absence at first, much like how we rarely think about our own shadows.
After how upset she's been with you lately, especially about not supporting Adila's dragon hunt, you figure she's just sulking and will be back soon. The second day passes, then the third... but Maggie is nowhere to be found.
Late one night, a knock comes at the door. You think it might be Maggie, but instead, you find a messenger holding a delicate box and a letter.
"My husband, [player.name], I've left. You know, this isn't about loving Adila – she knows that too – but you've brought me nothing but tears and pain, and I can't take it anymore. Adila has given me the courage to begin anew. Please don't try to find me."
Below the letter, there are a few hurried notes, perhaps from Adila:
"I didn't kill the dragon – it escaped to another dimension – but I managed to gouge out its eye. Here's your proof, in this box. Consider it compensation for taking Maggie away. After all, you care more about such things than her, don't you?"
"The dragon cursed Adila's bloodline to bear only daughters, thinking it would strip us of our dragon-slaying destiny. But it was wrong – I've proven that a woman can defeat a dragon. We can achieve anything we set our minds to, become whoever we want to be. That curse? It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"
"Perhaps that's why Maggie chose to leave you in the end. Poor soul, you'll never understand this feeling, will you?"
You open the box and stare at the gem that was once a dragon's eye. Within the gem, flames flow like living fire, as if the fury of an entire world had been imprisoned in a palm-sized crystal. No mortal craft could have wrought this...
You gaze at the gem for a long time. Perhaps you're dwelling on your loss, perhaps a thousand thoughts race through your mind. Or perhaps you're already calculating what fortune this otherworldly treasure might bring you...

You barely notice her absence at first, much like how we rarely think about our own shadows.
After how upset she's been with you lately, especially about not supporting Adila's dragon hunt, you figure she's just sulking and will be back soon. The second day passes, then the third... but Maggie is nowhere to be found.
Late one night, there's a knock at the door. You open it to find Maggie standing there. She's holding an delicate box in her arms and a letter in her hand, saying it's from Adila, meant for you.
"I didn't kill the dragon – it escaped to another dimension – but I managed to gouge out its eye. Here's the proof, in this box."
"Maggie loves you more than she loves me – I've known this all along. So when she wouldn't take my gift, I decided to give this gem to you. At least this way, my greatest triumph will stand guard over my most cherished one, in place of me."
"The dragon cursed Adila's bloodline to bear only daughters, thinking it would strip us of our dragon-slaying destiny. But it was wrong – I've proven that a woman can defeat a dragon. We can achieve anything we set our minds to, become whoever we want to be. That curse? It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"
"Thank you and Maggie for all your help during this time. But in the end, forgive me for no longer being able to serve you, you damned man who won Maggie's heart and yet refuses to treasure it!"
As you read the letter, you glance at Maggie sitting quietly beside you, her face painted with bittersweet memories.
"That day, Adila grabbed me out of nowhere, asking me if I would stay with her. She was drenched in blood – the dragon's and her own... The desperate look in her eyes – it reminded me of you years ago. I stayed with her for a while, but... I couldn't help coming back to you. Those few days, I kept thinking about everything between us. I even thought about walking away forever, convinced it would be better for us both...
"But here I am again, you bastard... My goodness, I hate myself that I still need you!"
You can't resist any longer. You pull her into your arms. Maggie keeps her head down, concealing her tears.

You barely notice her absence at first, much like how we rarely think about our own shadows. The second day passes, then the third... but Maggie is nowhere to be found.

Late one night, there's a knock at the door. You open it to find Maggie standing there. 

She's holding an delicate box in her arms and a letter in her hand, saying it's from Adila, meant for you.

"I didn't kill the dragon – it escaped to another dimension – but I managed to gouge out its eye. Here's the proof, in this box."

"The dragon cursed Adila's bloodline to bear only daughters, thinking it would strip us of our dragon-slaying destiny. But it was wrong – I've proven that a woman can defeat a dragon. We can achieve anything we set our minds to, become whoever we want to be. That curse? It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"

"Take this gemstone – it's my way of thanking you for everything. Though you... What you've given me means so much more."

As you read the letter, you notice Maggie beside you, toying with the gemstone, a soft smile touching her lips.

"That day, Adila grabbed me out of nowhere, asking me if I would stay with her. She was drenched in blood – the dragon's and her own... The desperate look in her eyes – it reminded me of you years ago. I stayed with her for a while...Well, here I am choosing you again.Those few days, I kept telling myself I could manage without you – that everything you do for me, I could do on my own..."

"...But here I am, because deep down, I know you're the one who needs me now, aren't you?"

You answer by drawing her into your arms, your kisses speaking what words cannot.

As expected, you find Maggie at the city gate, with Adila beside her... This female warrior is covered in blood – the dragon's and her own. Her bandaged hands clutch tightly at a massive sulfur-colored gem, holding it up before Maggie's eyes. Within the gem, flames flow like living fire, as if the fury of a world-burning inferno had been imprisoned in a palm-sized crystal ball.

"I didn't kill the dragon – it escaped to another dimension – but I managed to gouge out its eye. The dragon cursed Adila's bloodline to bear only daughters, thinking it would strip us of our dragon-slaying destiny. But it was wrong!"

"I've proven that a woman can defeat a dragon. We can achieve anything we set our minds to, become whoever we want to be. That curse? It backfired – it drove every Adila to take up the sword, to break both the curse and our shackles!"

"Maggie, take it!" Adila declares proudly, her eyes blazing as she presents the gem to the woman before her. "This is my greatest achievement. Would you–"

Maggie seems uncomfortable, averting her gaze only to meet your eyes. Adila notices you too. A flash of embarrassment crosses her face. She turns, hastily shoves the gem into your hands, and with bitten lip, flees the scene.

Maggie comes to your side, gently gripping your arm, clearly shaken. "She actually made it back alive, and wounded such a beast! Heavens... She even asked me to leave with her! But that's impossible – I'm [player.name]'s wife! I love you more than life itself! And then she just... Oh, thank goodness you came. I wouldn't have known how to handle that situation."

Even so, Maggie's eyes are drawn to the magical gem. She stares intently at its shimmering surface, murmuring, "So, she really did it... The dragon is banished to another dimension, and the curse is finally broken. Adila is truly remarkable, despite what just happened... she really is incredible!"

"This gem belongs to her... We should find a way to return it to Adila, shouldn't we?" Maggie says softly.

You pause for a moment before drawing Maggie into your arms, her face nestled against your chest. 

And so, this is how the dragon-slaying tale ends.

5006056.title: Wedding Song
strings: Wedding Song

The wedding of Adila and Jabal is set with unexpected haste. Their noble families find the timing precipitous, yet the couple stands firm in their decision. They desire no grand celebration, inviting only you – their true friend and the one who brought them together.
Bride Adila
Groom Jabal
They invited you or Maggie to the wedding.

For various reasons, you couldn't attend Adila and Jabal's wedding, but fortunately, they don't mind such trifles. It did not affect your friendship.
You only heard much later that Adila's mother, aunts, grandaunts, and even the old maid of the house attended. They donned armor, held swords, and sang an ancient, traditionally-passed war song.
It is probably the only regret of being absent.
You attended the wedding as an invited guest
Then, Adila's kin arrived.

The bride and groom walk in together, their stiff posture revealing their discomfort. During the ceremony, Jabal's relatives recite a few love poems they themselves don't believe in, the atmosphere grows unbearably stiff.

Still, you give them your warmest smile and heartfelt wishes. This union between kindred spirits may have nothing to do with love, but who can say this isn't a more precious kind of happiness?

Her grandmother appears in ancient silver armor, leaning on a cane while gripping a sword. Her mother wears silver chainmail, one hand steadying her mother, the other firmly holding an oak shield. Her aunts, grandaunts, and even the household's old maids – all stand adorned in warrior's gear, slowly approaching together.

Adila freezes in place, and her husband is equally stunned.

"Mother, Grandmother, these outfits... weren't you always against women wielding swords?"

At her grandmother's stern strike of sword against the floor, Adila's kin raise their voices as one, launching into an ancient ballad:

"Two battlegrounds I bear, two battlegrounds I see,
One where I face the dragon, one where mother I'll be.
I could slay the beast with blade in hand,
Or birth a daughter who'll make her final stand.
Soft are my hands, and weak my knees,
My daughter, fierce and strong with warrior's ease.
Her shield rises high, her eyes shine bright,
Ready to win where I lost the fight.
Two battlegrounds I bear, two battlegrounds I see,
I strike, I fight, I break free...
At last I've slain the dragon's might.
That dared to chain my soul so tight!"
Surrounded by women, in the unending song of battle, Adila can't help but cry... while Jabal – her husband – grips her hand tightly.

5006057.title: The Warrior's Union
strings: The Warrior's Union
Adila and Jabal visited you, seemingly having something to say.
Adila visits
Jabal visits
You received Adila and Jabal.

Despite being married, Adila and Jabal still live in their own houses, exchanging polite greetings whenever their paths cross.

Speaking of the wedding, the young female warrior's voice turns emotional: "Turns out every woman in my family is like me... striving to become a warrior capable of slaying a dragon." She sighs, sprawling on the thick carpet with her legs stretched out. "My grandmother, mother, and aunts all failed, unable to withstand the pressure and lacking the combat strength... then they married. Several unmarried aunts died on their dragon-slaying quests – as a child, I thought they had eloped!"

"Truly incredible," Jabal says with genuine admiration.

"Hmm... Mother said she didn't want me to actually slay a dragon because it meant death, but she felt it would be a tremendous honor if her daughter could kill one – that's why she was always so conflicted about it. The dragon must have known mothers would always protect their children. That's why the curse works like this, right?"

"But the dragon never expected someone like you." Jabal nods at Adila's muscles with admiration. "You're the strongest woman I've ever met."

"You're no slouch either, my husband." Adila turns to Jabal with a grin. "Ready to hunt down a dragon?"

They share a knowing smile – the kind only warriors understand.

"So, is there anything I can help with?" you ask them.

Adila lists out what they need to slay the dragon: besides her family's ancestral quenched mithril longsword, they need fireproof gear and special harpoons to keep the dragon from escaping. But before all that, she says, the most important thing is finding the dragon's lair. The location is written in her ancestors' journals, but the crucial details are all in code...

Adila's cheeks flush. "I still need some time to figure it out..."

Seeing her discomfort, you offer to study the book while they focus on what they do best.

Both warriors visibly relax at your suggestion. "Thank goodness," Adila laughs. "That thing gave me such headaches when they made me read it as a kid. My ancestors just couldn't write anything straight."

She hands you the book, promising they'll reward you generously after they succeed in slaying the dragon.

5006058.title: Book of Dragonslaying
strings: Book of Dragonslaying

This ancient manuscript by the Adila family, holds countless secrets about dragons. Adila and Jabal have entrusted you with the crucial task of deciphering its contents, promising to share the spoils with you once the mission is complete.
Ancient scrolls documenting dragon-slaying techniques.
You must decipher this book yourself, but to understand it, you need at least 3 in Magic or 6 in Insight
You try to decode its mysteries.
Until... something blocks your path

The complex characters interweave in mysterious patterns, dancing, trembling, and twisting as you study them, spinning around you in circles.

A wave of exhausting dizziness strikes you, and your consciousness begins to sink. Everything around you fades to a blur, and your sense of self grows sharp as steel – you become like a blade, cutting through the veil between reality and illusion.

You fall... deeper and deeper...

"Human, you don't belong here..." You can't make out its form, only hear its thunderous voice, "Go back, go back!" 

You suddenly wake up in the study chamber, finding yourself hunched over the desk. The Book of Dragonslaying lies open before you, but the words on its pages have settled back into lifeless ink, dull and ordinary. No matter how hard you try to focus, the contents slip from your mind like mist. It seems you won't be able to read this book for a while.

5006059.title: Trial in the Dream
strings: Trial in the Dream
You plunge deeper into the darkness and secrets of the nightmare, but suddenly, a black shadow manifests before you, wielding a massive weapon, forcing you back...
In an ancient, chaotic dream...
How can the would-be dragonslayer justify his righteousness?
If you believe something can help you in your dream, it could manifest within your dream...
Only the righteous can prevail here
If you have ever betrayed your commitment to justice, this trial will be arduous.
Entering the dream requires a certain amount of Magic or Insight, make sure it's your own.
How will you prove your justice?
Your Combat and Magic determine your full dice count, while Infamy appropriately reduces your dice count.
You need 5 Successes to win.

According to the Book of DragonSlaying, dragons rarely leave footprints. These giant lizards are cautious, knowing their tracks are too distinctive and could easily be recognized. As a result, they only rest on hard, unyielding stone that won't retain any marks. But even the most careful plans have their flaws – they forget that the sulfurous fumes they breathe can also leave traces behind.

Adila and Jabal have found stones with these markings near a habitat matching the description, with the dragon's lair nearby. They've sent word back about their next step – confirming the exact location of the lair. If conditions allow, they plan to set up traps and prepare ambushes to give that damn lizard a nasty surprise...

You squeeze your eyes shut, whispering that forgotten name in the midnight shadows. Who dares threaten His followers in His domain – in this realm of darkness and dreams? The darkness surges around you, and you feel that strange, entangling presence being devoured by your master... Was that a chewing sound you just heard?
The god remains silent to your prayers, while the demon of dreams stirs in vengeful awakening.

When he realizes what you're about to do, his lips curl into a twisted smile. He pulls you into an embrace, then bites into your neck with teeth too sharp to be human.

The sudden stabbing pain makes you instinctively try to push him away, but then you feel dizzy... You hear a call filled with desire and longing... Your soul seems to float into clouds. You lose control of your body, leaving two empty vessels on the ground, entwined in primal union...

The voices of others pull you back to reality. Three days gone. The young man has been dead for a long time, a lingering smile frozen on his face. The cracked stone in his arms seems soaked in blood – its scarlet hue glaring and vivid.

You slice his throat, but not a drop of blood flows out... A strange, satisfied smile crosses the young man's face. He laughs heartily, clutching the cracked stone as he chants a name over and over again, until his voice suddenly falls silent.

That name haunts your dreams night after night, robbing you of peaceful sleep. It clings to your soul like a hungry shadow, longing for something, refusing to leave...

You light a purifying incense. With solemn devotion, you perform the ritual and plead to exchange the blood of five hundred livestock for the child. A voice from the void agrees to your request. You can feel that voice almost emerging from your mind.

The minister's gratitude knows no bounds. He seizes the cattle and sheep from every farm without hesitation. For seven days, the stench of blood hangs heavy over the land. The farmers' fate – how they will till their fields or sustain themselves without livestock – are beneath notice.

You ask the minister for seven slaves and slit their throats at seven positions according to the ritual's design, exchanging their blood for the promise concerning the child. An ominous curse surges through their spilled blood, then vanishes into the darkening earth. A sharp voice suddenly pierces your mind. He speaks with greed and force, demanding such bounty of blood each year as His tribute.

The minister agrees without hesitation, clearly valuing his beloved son's life above any number of slaves. He even inquires about the ritual's details. There is no doubt that you have a new accomplice.

A mysterious stranger stuffs an unknown mixture of herbs and plants into your mouth. Paralyzed, you can do nothing but watch as he begins sawing open your chest. He skillfully cuts through your bones, his hands rummaging through the crimson mess of flesh and blood. It feels like a surreal, excruciating nightmare. Finally, he repositions your organs, pieces your bones back together, and stitches your chest shut. He mutters a few words before you slip into a deep sleep. When you finally jolt awake, you find that the wound has miraculously healed. Something's different than before – your mind has never been sharper, as if seeing the world, and yourself, for what they truly are.

After that, [s2.name] is haunted by nightmares for days on end, a devil's possession taking root in her dreams.

5006079.title: Dragon Head's Ownership
strings: Dragon Head's Ownership

As soon as you return to the capital, the Sultan summons you to his palace, showing keen interest in the dragon head you have brought back. He even personally opens the dragon's mouth to verify its authenticity...

Finally, he wipes the blood from his hands with a silk scarf offered by a attendant and looks at you languidly: "My dearest [player.name], I think this will look magnificent above my throne. What do you think?"
You choose to offer the dragon head to the Sultan
Sultan
You choose to keep the dragon head for yourself
Dragonslaying Sultan
There's no time to hesitate, make your choice.
Of course, this is yours, Your Majesty.
Very well, I will reward you generously.
Oh? Are you sure?
Royal Favor

Because you presented this peerless dragon head to your Sultan, you gained great fame and prestige in the city instantly.

The Sultan rewarded you generously – treasures, wealth, his private cellars, his harem, and treasury all laid open before you, and you indulged in them day and night. Though absent from court, none dared impeach you. Wealth poured into your coffers unbidden – no need to manage your estate, no need to tend to your affairs...

Gradually, people got used to it, and later, people no longer cared what absurd things you did, until finally... no one noticed as you faded away into the palace's extravagance, like a drop of water into sand.

Your silence makes the Sultan smile.

"Oh, you don't want to?" he says with a smile, lightly raising a ringed finger, "Then die."

The magic signet ring erupts in brilliant light, yet as it falls upon your body – forged in dragon's blood – it brings no harm.

The Sultan glances at his ring, puzzled for a moment, but he brushes off this little accident without concern

"Very well," he says, rising from his throne. The bright candlelight of the golden palace falls upon his face, making his smile seem far more genuine. Let me see what you've really got."

Your silence makes the Sultan laugh.
"No? You refuse?"
"Good." He rises from his throne, a long, slow unfurling. The bright candles of the golden palace carve deeper shadows across his face. "You've been preparing for this a long time, haven't you?" He strokes the false ring on his finger, the one that won't spark a single flame. And from the shadows, his smile turns uglier, crueler. "Come then. Show me what else you've got."

5006080.title: Face the Sultan
strings: Face the Sultan

The deep shadows and radiant light of the lapis lazuli palace play across the Sultan, casting an enigmatic mask over his face. His throat moves as he swallows – a subtle, primal gesture that betrays a barely concealed and animalistic joy.
Sultan
Even the sunlight and shadows belong to the Sultan
The Monarch-Shattering Blade
He doesn't need protection, but the majesty
The Weak-Crushing Blade
You must witness all this yourself
Relax, the fight hasn't started yet
A Game That Delights the Sultan
For you, he is fully armed
The Beast of Light and Shadow

The thick, metallic stench of dragon's blood fills the vast audience hall. Motionless, you stare at the monarch you have served faithfully for so many years. You watch as he rises from the throne, backlit by candles and torches, his towering shadow stretched across the chamber. The air grows heavy and oppressive, weighing upon your shoulders like lead. You fight against the primal urge to kneel. To end this suffocating silence, you draw your blade with slow, trembling resolve.

The Sultan's eyes narrow as he catches the gleam of your blade. Very well. He reaches for his battle sword, beckons a guard to help him don his armor, then pauses briefly between weapons before choosing another blade – a light, serpentine scimitar. 

During these preparations, you remain still and silent, neither speaking nor charging, as if bound by some unspoken pact, simply waiting for the warrior's duel that is to come.

Finally, the Sultan leaves his long-held throne and descends the stairs toward you, step by step... With each step, his shadow grows larger; with each step, his reflected light becomes more radiant. You focus intently on your opponent, gripping your blade tightly, knowing that only by gathering all your courage and strength can you confront him. You realize: the beast, once chained, corrupted, and tormented, has finally been unleashed by you.

5006081.title: Testing the Edge of the Blade
strings: Testing the Edge of the Blade

With indomitable dragon-forged spirit, you stand unwavering before the Sultan. This clash transcends good and evil, ruler and subject, all known and unknown fates – it is just two warriors testing each other's blades, even if you might cast your life in vain upon the lapis lazuli.
Sultan
Dragonslayer
The dragon's lifeless eyes seem to still watch this battle...

A Showdown
Your swords clash with a resonant clang!

The palace has never felt so empty. The servants and guards have quite consciously withdrawn, leaving your battlefield to the silent witness of the dragon's head – its faded eyes watching what is about to unfold.

You stand at opposite ends, swords in hand. For a rare moment, you catch your own reflection in the Sultan's eyes. Dust dances, veils flutter, breeze whispers, light beams pierce – time freezes at this moment, until –
A Thrilling Battle
The hungry blade still trembles

His strike sends tremors through your blade to your grip. If not for the dragon blood tempering your bone, flesh, and soul, this single blow would have torn the weapon from your hands.

Before the pain can register, an unspeakable joy and thrill surge through you. A chuckle escapes your lips – and you hear the same from the Sultan.

Blades clash like relentless thunder and rain. Blood sprays wild and free, turning into a song of battle that races towards its end with no regret. Until the drumbeat of your hearts strikes its final note, your blade cleaves through the Sultan's chest. His blood, you discover, runs just as hot and red as any other.

Twin blades clatter to the floor, something finally departing the vessel that had confined it for too long. The Sultan's gaze drifts from your face, freezing into one last unbridled smile. 

You have never understood his thoughts, neither when he was monarch nor now, as simply himself. But in this moment, you know – he died as a warrior. Perhaps this is the deliverance he desires most.

Until the drumbeat of your hearts strikes its final note, the Sultan's blade cleaves through the air straight for your face. Yet in that moment before death descends, you catch something in the cruel monarch's eyes – an undertow of regret, perhaps even... compassion...

strings: Elegy of the Defeated
