Without mercy, the blade severs your final tether to this mortal world with brutal precision – as if even the slightest hesitation would be an insult to this battle.

The Sultan wipes his blade clean with his sleeve as the warrior's phantom fades into nothing... His sigh speaks of boredom. Soon, servants will scrub the blood from the floor. Soon, the dragon's head will be just another forgotten piece in his collection. He will return to his golden throne, gazing down at the ant-like crowd below. There he'll sit, wondering how to while away these endless days... None of this concerns you anymore.

However, such compassion is nothing but your illusion. The Sultan's blade arcs towards you with crushing force, merciless and determined – as if the slightest hesitation would be an insult to this battle. In that very moment, a golden sword hurls through the air, knocking the scimitar off course before dissolving into dust.
What was that? There's no time to think. Death's whisper brushes past your hair as you spring backward, away from the Sultan. 
The Sultan makes no pursuit. "Oh?" He watches the newcomer with keen interest.
The assassin – or say, the swordsman, the avenger from the past – steps slowly into the hall. In one fluid motion, he draws a long dagger and surges toward the Sultan with wind-like grace, his blade cutting a deadly arc!
"Ha, perfect timing!" The Sultan's laughter booms as his scimitar dances – a piercing shriek of steel as he steps aside to evade the destined strike, then with a twist of his wrist, brings the blade crashing down upon the swordsman!

You have no idea how long this battle has lasted – all you know is that every bone and drop of blood in your body burns like fire. 
Though you and [s5.name] have rarely fought side by side, an unspoken understanding connects you both – the potential heir to the throne and the prince of the Homeland. A single glance is all it takes to read each other's intentions. You advance and retreat in perfect harmony, balancing offense and defense – yet even so, the Sultan maintains his dominance! 
Your weapons are the first to give in, shattering into two pieces, then two more. In the end, [s5.name] can no longer hold his long dagger. Nearly collapsing from exhaustion, he falls to one knee, allowing the Sultan's blade to pierce through his shoulder. The cold steel reflects the twisted grin on the Sultan's face. He twists the blade cruelly, but as he pulls it back, [s5.name] grabs the blade with his bare hands, holding it in place with sheer will. 
In that fleeting moment of shock, in that single opening, you move silently and muster every ounce of strength to plunge a golden sword into the Sultan's back! This is the Sword of Lament, the Sword of the Homeland, the Sword of Eternal Legacy: forever bound to return to the hands of the ruler willing to wield it! 
The Roaming Swordsman smiles. With great effort, he pulls the curved blade from his body and tosses it to the ground like trash. Blood pours from between his fingers as he clutches his wound, "yet he seems to feel no pain at all. 
You hear him reciting an ancient prayer. Then, a gentle breeze stirs, lifting nine flowing veils that wipe away the blood streaming from his wounds. At last, this man – whose kingdom, kin, and name were all erased by the Sultan – has fulfilled his vengeance.

You have no idea how long this battle has lasted – all you know is that every bone and drop of blood in your body burns like fire. 
Your weapons are the first to give in, shattering into two pieces, then two more, until they are completely destroyed, rendered useless for battle. In that moment, the golden sword unexpectedly reappears in [s5.name]'s hand. This is the Sword of Lament, the Sword of the Homeland, the Sword of Eternal Legacy: forever bound to return to the hands of the ruler willing to wield it! 
The Sultan laughs maniacally, his intricate sword dance ringing with sharp clangs as he forces the Sword of Lament into submission, as though he were hammering an unruly nail into place. Many years ago, he had pulled it out. Now, it still brings him a sliver of joy – but it's not enough, never enough! His overwhelming killing intent shatters lamentation, resentment, and hatred, crushing everything weak, humble, and despicable in its wake. Through the smeared blood, he searches for even the faintest thing that might rouse his interest - but nothing remains, nothing anymore. 
Showing nothing but boredom, he sheaths his scimitar and steps over the scattered corpses. Soon, servants will scrub the blood from the floor. Soon, the dragon's head will be just another forgotten piece in his collection. He will return to his golden throne, gazing down at the ant-like crowd below. There he'll sit, wondering how to while away these endless days... None of this concerns you anymore.

The Sultan's blade arcs towards you with crushing force, merciless and determined – as if the slightest hesitation would be an insult to this battle. 
Yet when death's breeze whispers across your face, the pain never comes. The golden scimitar stops before your eyes as your opponent's gaze shifts toward the palace gates. A tall, slender figure stands stark against the light, drawn perfectly straight – he exposes every weakness and vulnerability, only to raise his short bow, the black arrow trained unwaveringly on the Sultan. 
The arrow seethes with terrible hatred and curses – it seems it would seek the Sultan's heart of its own accord, skilled aim or none. Yet he holds the arrow drawn. Perhaps it carries more power drawn on the string – or perhaps he lacks the courage to loose it, for merely stepping into this battle has already stripped away his resolve. 
The Sultan's mocking laughter fills the air as he sneers at Nawfal's hesitation. His gaze fixes upon the black arrow as if drawn by its deadly promise – this is the very chance Nawfal has bought for you!

One name after another falls from Nawfal's pale lips, heavy with sorrow yet strangely calm. Each name punctuates the ringing clash of blades between you and the Sultan. Yet it feels like an unending prayer, like a ceaseless curse. 
There are so many names – some vaguely familiar, others completely unknown. They weave into threads, ropes, and cages, all straining to hold back the Sultan's savage onslaught. His eyes burn crimson with bestial fury, each swing of his blade punctuated by a thunderous roar. Until he is so overwhelmed by those names that he can no longer hold you down, can no longer respond calmly to your attacks in the midst of his rage.
You trade wound for wound, blood for blood, life for life. Until the final name is spoken, until the black shaft crumbles to ash, unable to bear the surging tide of will – at last, you drive your chipped, nearly broken blade into the Sultan's living throat, letting the flood of blood drown out his every word...
You see the Sultan's furious eyes, as if blaming you, blaming fate, for denying him a warrior's death. Then you turn to find Nawfal slumped on the ground, blood staining his lips, as if the shattering of the arrow had claimed a piece of his life and soul in tribute.
He looks at you, his eyes alone remaining as unyielding as stone. "Those names," he says, "belonged to the mortals the Sultan humiliated and slew."

One name after another falls from Nawfal's pale lips, heavy with sorrow yet strangely calm. Each name punctuates the ringing clash of blades between you and the Sultan. Yet it feels like an unending prayer, like a ceaseless curse. There are so many names – some vaguely familiar, others completely unknown. They weave into threads, ropes, and cages, all straining to hold back the Sultan's savage onslaught. His eyes burn crimson with bestial fury, each swing of his blade punctuated by a thunderous roar. Until, at last, you can no longer withstand the relentless attacks. His blade finds its mark, pinning you to the ground. As your life slips away, all you can hear is a faint ringing in your ears. Your blood mingles with Nawfal's, and the Sultan picks up the black arrow – now dulled, like a piece of rusted iron.
“Interesting, very interesting." His laughter echoes with boundless madness. "Without your little reminder, I might have forgotten all these delightful deeds I've done. As a reward, I shall have your names etched alongside the others."

However, such compassion is nothing but your illusion. The Sultan's blade arcs towards you with crushing force, merciless and determined – as if the slightest hesitation would be an insult to this battle. In that very moment, a golden longsword slams against the Sultan's decisive strike. You see the roaming swordsman standing before you, his back turned to shield you. Meanwhile, you hear Nawfal's voice – he holds his short bow steady with the black arrow trained unwaveringly on the Sultan

One name after another falls from Nawfal's pale lips, heavy with sorrow yet strangely calm. Each name punctuates the ringing clash of blades between [s5.name] and the Sultan.

Some of those names are completely unfamiliar to you, while others feel faintly familiar. Suddenly, a strange illusion overtakes you – as though those names transform, here and now, into shattered cards, fluttering down and spilling drops of blood, each etched with faces of pain, fury, and defiance.

No, it's more than that... You also see something behind this battle:

You see the magician pulling the strings of fate, treating people like game pieces; you see yourself, your companions, your enemies, all who insult and are insulted in turn, all who harm and are harmed. You all sit at her table, trapped in one endless game after another.
A thousand times, ten thousand times you weep, plead, struggle, your mind fracturing, your heart either hardening to steel or shattering into countless pieces, all to beg for one... ending that is not an ending at all. You stand battered, despairing, until...until the black arrow bursts forth, carrying with it countless betrayed souls, their shattered prayers transformed into tiny blessings, pouring into your hands.
In that critical moment, you shoulder the Sultan's heavy blade and, incredibly, begin to overpower him... The cards burn and spin, pulling at the strings of fate, choosing you over the Sultan—perhaps because hope still lives within you, or maybe simply because they find him more despicable.
With this borrowed strength, you drive the blade deep into the Sultan's body, letting his blood warm your toes. At last, you wake from your long illusion; you see [s5.name], battered and bloodied, lying on the ground, gazing up at the wind-stirred veils while murmuring prayers of his homeland. You see Nawfal, barely clinging to life, his eyes dim—as if that arrow, when loosed, had claimed a piece of his life and soul in tribute.
You stagger over, lifting them from the ground, then gently bumping fists. Perhaps this is still not the end, as cards continue brewing darkness somewhere in the world, but this time at least, you all made it through alive.

5006101.title: Shadows of Flowers in the Corridor
strings: Shadows of Flowers in the Corridor
Physician Samir suddenly sends for you. Could it be that your discreet maneuver on behalf of Consort Sadani has been uncovered?
Sultan's Court Physician, Samir
You must meet him in person
Perhaps only the dead can keep your secrets forever.
You couldn't find the time to see Samir, but nothing particular seemed to have happened. Perhaps he only wished to catch up.
Strike First

Samir has once been a trusted friend, yet at a moment when lives hang in the balance you have no other choice.
He surely never expects a dagger to greet him... You do not dare meet your old friend's eyes, but you strike, and then present the killing coldly before the court: you act only to break the Bloodshed Card, nothing more.
The Sultan is displeased. Samir is one of his favored court physicians—a man who once betrayed his ancestral oath to serve the Sultan instead of his fallen kingdom, a living banner of loyalty and power. Still, the Sultan does not move against you. Such loyalty, after all, he can summon as often as he pleases.

When you find Samir he leans against a pillar in the corridor, eyes lowered to the floor.
Seeing you approach, he smiles and points to the shifting shadows.
"When you were still a young noble at court, we spent hours here together. Do you remember?"
Of course you do. The trembling shadows come from dense lilacs, jasmine, and roses planted just outside the arcade. These flowers are meant to please the Sultan and his consorts, yet also a hiding place for idle youths. You and Samir once talked here, read, even dozed; those days feel like yesterday.
"So, my old friend," Samir continues, "when I noticed something strange... I thought I should ask you first, before reporting to the Sultan."
From his robe he draws the register of women who serve the Sultan... Your heart lurches. You expected someone to examine it—perhaps the fat eunuchs who manage the harem, whose eyes are easy to deceive. But Samir? He is far harder to fool.
"This record is... odd, isn't it?" He tucks the book back inside his robe and winks at you. "If the one who tampered with it—whoever that may be—truly wanted to alter it, he should have spoken with his old friend first. I can forget this small matter. But my forgetfulness has a modest price." He hands out a slip of paper covered with names. "There are some people I worry about. Find them—give them food, or money—and then tell me how they fare. In return, my memory will have one of its little lapses. Agreed?"
It is blackmail, yet in this court such gentle blackmail almost counts as help. With a faint sigh you take the list from his hand.

5006102.title: Gold, Crystal, and Mud
strings: Gold, Crystal, and Mud
This ancient residence once belonged to court physicians of the fallen kingdom. Now it stands restored, long since in new hands.
Samir's List
You can go in person or send any follower in your stead.
A consumable that grants you a distinct advantage in negotiations.
If you are a figure of true power, you hardly need tricks.
So you ask, lightly, about the people who used to live here...
Sociability and Charisma determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to get what you want.
You lower his guard.
You fail to lower his guard.

Seeing you arrive, the new owner greets you warmly and leads you inside. He proudly explains that the Sultan granted him the estate after the old kingdom fell. His father had been an officer in the old Sultan's honor guard; on the day the city fell, the man crouched in the mud to let the Sultan's horse step upon his back, keeping the monarch's gold-studded harness from the dirt.
You offer polite praise for the story while surveying the carefully tended garden—once planted with medicinal herbs, perhaps—and the many fountains scattered throughout the grounds. You have never seen so much running water in a noble's house; clearly it once served for treatment. You have come to the right place.

So you casually ask about the previous residents. Wishing to ingratiate himself with a court favorite, the owner gladly offers an address at the edge of the city. The physicians, he says, went there after their expulsion. You nod. Only after accepting his generous invitation to dine do you leave the building that is but a shadow of its former self.

You converse easily. Within a few exchanges he treats you almost as a confidant.
He offers an address at the edge of the city. The physicians, he says, went there after their expulsion. You nod, thank him, and leave the building that is but a shadow of its former self.
He refuses to speak of the old kingdom or of the people he expelled. He claims ignorance of their fate. It seems you will have to try again another time.

5006103.title: Little Guardian
strings: Little Guardian
Following the directions, you reach a cluster of shacks in the Dark Alley said to house the exiled court physicians of the fallen kingdom.
You can handle this in person or send any follower in your stead.
5 Gold Coins improve their living conditions. 10 Gold Coins allow you to break an Extravagance Card.
You can take this opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower.
A small payment can give these outcasts a few days of comfort—at least in theory.
No lackeys of the Sultan allowed here.

Among the rickety huts, one dwelling stands out. It is spotless, as if scrubbed inside and out several times a day. Ink and herbs scent the air—a rarity in a poor quarter like this.
You knock lightly. There is a flurry of movement inside. After a pause, a wary eye peers through the crack. You explain your business, but the door slams shut without a word and the lock clicks...
House after house greets you the same way, as though you have committed some great offense. You leave the street empty-handed—Samir, my old friend, it's not that I won't help you!
When you relay the news, Samir only sighs and shakes his head, saying no more of the altered records.
Lost Blood
You thus break an Extravagance Card.

Among the rickety huts, one dwelling stands out. It is spotless, as if scrubbed inside and out several times a day. Ink and herbs scent the air—a rarity in a poor quarter like this.
Yet the people's suspicion of you, the uninvited guest, is still strong. You knock one door after another; no one answers, not even for gold, not even for goodwill. At last you reach a small door at the far end. A girl no taller than your waist opens it. She wears rough but clean clothes, her hair loose in the style of an unmarried girl of the old kingdom, her face defiant.
"What do you want?" she demands, one hand on her hip, the other on the doorframe. "Grandpa is sick. He won't see anyone, and you can't pay the fee anyway—eh?
She straightens up, taking in your robes, your jewels, your uncalloused hands. Then she extends her palm. "You want to see him? Then pay. By the stars above, I'm saying it—no coin, no entry!"
You cannot help but smile and pour the gold you brought into her hand. The gleam lights up her face; her mouth falls open in amazement. At last she recovers, runs inside calling for the old man, and you naturally follow.

The house is narrow and dim. At the far end an old man lies propped on his bed, a massive book in his hands. Eyes hidden beneath heavy brows and disheveled hair fix on you.
"Lackey of the Sultan," he pronounces. "Why are you here?"
"It's Samir—" you begin, but he cuts you off.
"That disgrace—" He clutches his chest, coughing violently. The girl rushes over with a cup of water, scowling at you.
"Thank you, Anita..." the old man mutters, then glares. "Don't speak his name to me! He and that court favorite can keep licking—"
He glances at the child and swallows the rest of the insult. One can imagine how harsh the rest of the words are.
But that's acceptable to you. You are only a messenger, so you ask if there is anything you can do.
"How laughable. How arrogant! The Sultan's nobles think they can do anything. Then bring back our homeland—kill the Sultan! Can you do that?"
Anita looks anxiously between you and him. She is young, but even she knows such words are dangerous.
"I only regret not finishing my medical codex before death... I have no wish but loyalty to one king, no stain on my name. Not like him. Not like Samir! He even dares to keep the name I gave him! That treacherous cur!"
Another fit of coughing.
"I need more money for Grandpa's treatment," Anita bursts out, holding out her hand. "You said you would help him—then give me money."
"Anita! Don't beg from him!"
"But you need them!"
"I'm a physician. Nothing can help me now!"
They argue before you, then both turn to you.
"You truly want to do good, lackey of the Sultan?" the old man says, gripping Anita's shoulder with surprising strength. "Take her with you. I found her on the street. She's brighter than any noble's child. She knows manners, can read the stars, some medicine, even letters. Give her a future. Don't let her end up like the other women here, big-bellied too soon, gossiping at the well all day."
He pushes the girl toward you. She stares at him in disbelief, then bursts into tears.
You hesitate, asking if there is anything else.
"Nothing. Nothing but this. Don't speak to me of that... bastard. I have no such son. I should have strangled him before he ruined our name."
He turns back to his great book, ignoring you and Anita.
After waiting a moment and seeing he will not change his mind, you lead the crying girl away.

A fistful of gold for some poor girl?
The Sultan questions you with lively interest: What kind of girl? How old? Pretty? What color is her hair? Does she know any intriguing tricks?
He keeps pressing until he realizes you simply handed out money with no "more exciting" arrangement attached. His interest fades at once, replaced by suspicion—after all, the girl appears to be of the fallen kingdom's blood!

5006104.title: Homeland's Blood
strings: Homeland's Blood
You take little Anita by the hand and lead her home, wondering what should be done with her. Perhaps you ought to consult someone, for the girl cries so bitterly that your head pounds with the noise.
Anita
Who will care for her now?
Let her stay with you.
You take Anita to [s2.name]'s place.
You intend to take Anita to [s2.name]'s place.
After all, the old man entrusted her to you. You decide to keep her by your side. Perhaps—when the need arises—she may even serve to break a card or two...

Maggie prepares clean and well-kept clothes for Anita, combs her hair, and finds silver bangles suited to her new station, along with a pendant set with moonstone. The girl stares at her in wide-eyed silence, tears still glistening in her lashes, as though she has never once been treated with such care and has no idea how to respond.
Were it not for that vacant expression, she might pass for the daughter of a noble house. Maggie strokes her head with a smile, then turns to you: "All right, you can go."
Where?
"Samir, of course. Isn't it obvious, my dear?" Maggie chides you with a glance. "That old man is surely Samir's father. Entrusting the child to you is nothing less than entrusting her to his son. Now, quickly—go."
You hesitate only a moment before admitting she is right.
You summon a trusted servant and have the girl brought to the court physician's household.

Maggie prepares clean and well-kept clothes for Anita, combs her hair, and finds silver bangles suited to her new station, along with a pendant set with moonstone. The girl stares at her in wide-eyed silence, tears still glistening in her lashes, as though she has never once been treated with such care and has no idea how to respond.
Were it not for that vacant expression, she might pass for the daughter of a noble house. Maggie strokes her head with a smile, then says softly, "Let her stay here, my dear." There is a shadow of sorrow in her brow. "That old man is surely Samir's father. Entrusting the child to you is nothing less than entrusting her to his son. But..." She breaks off with a shake of her head. You draw her gently into your arms and promise that together you will care for the girl as your own.

In Lumera's presence, Anita quiets at once. She tilts her head back, listening in rapt attention as Lumera reads aloud from her book.
Later, when Anita falls asleep, Lumera slips out to find you.
"If you permit it," she says, "I would suggest... I would suggest sending her to Samir, the court physician—your friend. She longs to be a physician... I think such an arrangement would gladden them both."
You nod and accept her counsel.

In Lumera's presence, Anita quiets at once. She tilts her head back, listening in rapt attention as Lumera reads aloud from her book.
Later, when Anita falls asleep, Lumera slips out to find you. Her cheeks flush, her eyes alight with a small, hopeful spark. You realize she has never had a companion of her own age. With a smile you stroke her hair and ask if she would like Anita to remain here with her.
She nods eagerly.

You bring Anita to Samir and recount the old man's words.
Throughout your talk, Anita gazes with fascination at the vials on Samir's belt, his spectacles, and the physician's signet ring.
"Grandpa always spoke of the court physician... You—you are one, aren't you?" she asks timidly, giving Samir a respect she has never shown you. "How can I become one too?"
Samir bends toward her, then removes his spectacles and sets them upon her face. She stumbles back at once, dizzy from the lenses.
"These are crafted by an artisan. Many physicians must use them, for we spend long years reading countless books, squinting to observe and to distinguish. So we need such things. If you can do that, if you can endure the insults and the scorn—and perhaps even more..." He pauses, then smiles. "No. You need not endure so much. Do you wish to learn? Then come with me. I can give you a place as an apprentice."
Anita lets out a cheer, her grief forgotten, clinging to Samir's hand in delight.
Samir glances back at you. "Thank you, [player.name]... truly."
Then he leads the girl away.
Giving her to Samir would have been the best course. But Samir is dead now. And so, Anita has no one but you.

Alim studies Anita with a tilted head.
"So, little girl... you want to be a thief? Heh... heh... heh... you'd make a fine thief..."
"No." Anita's answer is hard and quick. You and Alim both freeze for a heartbeat.
"I know I'd make a good thief," she says, "but Grandpa told me I can become a good physician. I can always come back and be a thief, but a thief can't become a physician just by trying. So I'm going to be a physician, not a thief. If I can't be a physician later, I'll find you at the market. I know where you and your street friends work."
Hands on her hips, she glares at the two of you until you both burst out laughing. Alim praises her again and again, then urges you to send the girl to the Nursery to study. Once you, he bends to her level and asks gravely, as one adult to another: "When you become a physician, will you treat my street friends? Will you really heal them?"
Anita lifts her chin with pride. "If they respect me and pay my fee, then I'll heal them properly."
Still laughing, you have her taken to the Nursery and settled there.

Alim studies Anita with a tilted head.
"So, little girl... you want to be a thief? Heh... heh... heh... you'd make a fine thief..."
"No." Anita's answer is hard and quick. You and Alim glance at one another, and Alim spreads his hands. "It's not that I won't help you, Lord [player.name]. You see? She refuses to come with me." You sigh. Very well. She stays with you.

"She's a good child." That is Badriyyah's first remark on seeing Anita. "Child, will you come with me?"
Anita shakes her head firmly. "Cultists don't bathe. Grandpa said it's unhygienic
...You have never seen Badriyyah laugh so hard. When she wipes the tears from her cheeks she tells you she believes the girl should be sent to the Nursery; one day she might indeed make a fine physician.
She might be right.

"She's a good child." That is Badriyyah's first remark on seeing Anita. "Child, will you come with me?"
Anita shakes her head firmly. "Cultists don't bathe. Grandpa said it's unhygienic
...You have never seen Badriyyah laugh so hard. When she wipes the tears from her cheeks and says to the child, "Then stay with Lord [player.name]. I've heard he bathes often."
Anita looks at you searchingly and remains silent until you give her a nod.

As soon as you tell Anita who you are bringing her to, she clutches at your sleeve, eyes wide with a fear you have never seen in her. "Don't send me to the Purists. I know what they do. They dunk children in water again and again, they cut them with stones, and then—then—then they chant spells at dinner! Please..."
Seeing her terror, you relent. When you tell Iman, he only curves his lips in a faint smile, then suggests placing Anita in your Nursery. Proper schooling and friends will shape her far better than a stern god.

As soon as you tell Anita who you are bringing her to, she clutches at your sleeve, eyes wide with a fear you have never seen in her. "Don't send me to the Purists. I know what they do. They dunk children in water again and again, they cut them with stones, and then—then—then they chant spells at dinner! Please..."
Seeing her terror, you relent. Very well. She stays with you; after all, you can afford it.

"A little girl? What am I supposed to do with a little girl?"
Adila looks at Anita in confusion, then smacks her forehead.
"I can't, but my mother—my grandmother—my aunts—they'd be glad to take her. If you trust me, I'll bring her home. She's neat and clean—though her arms are too thin to lift a sword. But after some training she could handle a dagger. Look at those eyes!"
You hand Anita over to Adila. The little one seems to like this strong sister; she bites her lip, grips Adila's sleeve, and walks off without a backward glance.
Truly—without a glance. Couldn't she at least pretend to show a little dependence or gratitude?

While you speak with Jawad, Arumina sits outside chatting with Anita—surprising that they have anything to say to each other at all. Perhaps Anita is precocious, or perhaps Arumina is simply late to bloom...
As you struggle to persuade Jawad, Arumina bursts in. "Anita is so clever! Cleverer than me! She must not stay here. Father, pay for her to study medicine abroad. When she returns she will be the finest court physician!" With a few pieces of pastry bought at his own expense she coaxes an easy promise from the miserly man, then drags Anita off to play without a shred of hesitation.
Smiling at the father's dazed delight, you rise and take your leave. You have to admit, this seems a good future for Anita.
The father receives you without spirit. He has lost his own daughter, yes, but that does not mean he wants another. He sees you out with polite indifference. It seems Anita will remain with you.

5006105.title: Samir's disappointment
strings: Samir's disappointment
Word of what you have done with Anita reaches Samir soon enough.
Samir hears of Anita's death.
Samir's List
It pains him deeply.
We are no longer friends.
How can you treat a child this way? He is bitterly disappointed. For a long time he refuses to see you.

Anita was supposed to be a minor piece on the board. You did not expect this: before long Samir is found hanged in his home. Some say he hanged himself after the scandal of a consort's miscarriage; others whisper of exiles from the fallen kingdom breaking into his house... Whatever the truth, the matter ends there.
Perhaps entrusting anything to you was a mistake. He paid dearly for that trust.

5006106.title: Unexpected Guests
strings: Unexpected Guests
Soon after, two unexpected guests arrive at your house.
Anita
Samir
A Favor Once Asked
Samir comes to see you, bringing Anita with him.

The young girl now wears a physician's robe and carries a satchel stuffed with paper slips, her head held high in unshakable pride. Samir smiles gently, his gratitude toward you unmistakable. He presses the girl's head in a respectful bow once, twice, before brushing at the tears glinting in his own eyes and sighing softly.
"We are proud people—too proud... Because we think ourselves learned, capable, resourceful..." he speaks for no apparent reason, his gaze following Anita as she runs into the garden to study a pomegranate tree. "We don't know how to say 'I'm sorry,' or 'please.' How much have we lost because of that? Still, at the end, we manage to hold on to something. Still..."
He tells you that the "trivial matter" from before has long since slipped from his mind; no one remembers, and no one will discover it. As for Anita, he vows to train her into the finest physician—she has the talent.
You sincerely wish them both well.

5006107.title: Samir's Gratitude
strings: Samir's Gratitude
Samir hears about Anita's situation.
Samir
A Favor Once Asked
Your arrangement for the girl seems to please him.
He offers no explanations, only sends a trove of costly gifts. In the note accompanying them, he writes simply: "That matter—I have already forgotten it!"

5006108.title: An Unexpected Visitor
strings: An Unexpected Visitor
An unforeseen guest arrives.
Visitor
You can meet him in person or send any follower in your stead.
A consumable for assistance.
What's the matter?
Sociability and Wisdom determine your full dice count.
You need at least 2 Successes to pry the truth from him.
He comes in Samir's stead to call on you.

With great courtesy he bows and presents two vials of carefully prepared salve. You recognize him: the favorite whom the Sultan gave to Samir as a "wife." The gesture had obvious humiliation in it, yet Samir accepted. All these years he has taken no other man and no woman at all. As an outsider, you cannot tell how much of their bond is for show, but at least on the surface it has always seemed harmonious. You remember glimpsing this man at tea with Samir—a quiet, docile figure with hardly any presence. Now his shoulders tremble slightly, his hands pressed to his sides, as though taut with nerves. After handing you the remedies he turns to leave in haste.
You stop him.
Kapar remains silent.

Whatever makes him falter like this must concern Samir. After a few careful words, you convince him that your questions spring from concern. In this court, in this Empire, "concern" and "friendship" are rare things. He should not shoulder everything for Samir alone.
Kapar bites his lip, hesitating, but your words clearly move him—or perhaps he simply has no one else to turn to.
"My master forbade me to tell you," he blurts at last, dropping to his knees. "He said you would worry and act rashly, but..." And then he tells you everything.
Lately rumors spread through the court that certain consorts are secretly seeking abortifacients. A hidden pregnancy means illicit liaisons in the harem—disgrace that could cost many heads... As the court physician attending these women, Samir naturally draws the heaviest suspicion. He has been placed under soft confinement while the royal guards investigate.
It is a perilous situation. Yet even now, he has sent his trusted servant to tend your injuries... You sigh inwardly, then tell Kapar not to lose hope—you will do what you can. But if you wish to intervene, you will likely have to go to court in person.

Kapar refuses to say a word. His mouth is shut like a clam, no matter how hard you try to pry it open. Clearly, Samir has entrusted him with something—and it surely concerns your ever-cautious old friend. You cannot tell what trouble Samir has fallen into, but one thing offers a sliver of comfort: even as the Sultan's gift, Kapar is fiercely loyal to him.
With that thought, you let him go. Samir does not call upon you, and Kapar says nothing, but that does not mean you are helpless. Do not underestimate yourself—if you step into the court in person, is there truly any secret that can escape your ears?

5006109.title: Execution
strings: Execution
The court announces the sentence: Physician Samir is condemned to death for sheltering a royal consort and supplying her with abortifacients.
The Condemned
Companion in Death

Samir is executed. His blood, his chambers, his manuscripts, every trace of his existence is erased in mere days. All that remains is the male favorite whom the Sultan once bestowed upon him... The judges are still debating his fate when news comes that he has slit his own throat at home. He too is quickly erased from memory, just like Samir.

5006110.title: The Stillborn Affair
strings: The Stillborn Affair
The Sultan commands you to uncover the truth before the deadline expires—or else you shall lose your head.
Your time is running short.
You have one more chance to plead for reprieve—but...
Investigation Results
If you make progress in the case, you gain one chance to petition the Sultan for an extension.
You attempt to beg the Sultan for a few more days...
Sociability and Wisdom determine your full dice count.
You need at least 4 Successes to persuade the Sultan.
You succeeded
You failed
What's with that attitude?
Your earnest diligence, your desperate running about, your pitiful eloquence—these finally amuse the Sultan. Praise the Almighty, most merciful sovereign: your life is spared, for a few more days.
Do you truly expect a king to retract his decree? He may well have long awaited the spectacle of your death.
You do not even make a show of investigation, and already you plead for leniency. Before the Sultan even speaks, his ears are filled with denunciations of you.
He has confessed.
The truth has revealed.
Truth Revealed
Time Expires

You present Samir's written confession, admitting that he sought to curse the Sultan with the corpse of a stillborn child...
Relief ripples through the court. This means the royal consorts are innocent, and all blame falls upon that wretched physician. As for you... so long as your conscience does not torment you, you no longer need to live in fear of execution.

In the end, it becomes clear: the entire affair was a plot against Samir, a revenge by stubborn loyalists of the fallen kingdom against a clever man who had thrown himself into the service of the Sultan. Fortunately, our radiant Sultan sees through every deceit, and Samir's unjust charges are swept away.
Though no one is left alive, the sight of that aged corpse and the pale-faced court physician at his side makes the Sultan smile. He rewards you richly, clearly well pleased with the outcome.

In the end, it becomes clear: the entire affair was a plot against Samir, a revenge by stubborn loyalists of the fallen kingdom against a clever man who had thrown himself into the service of the Sultan. Fortunately, our radiant Sultan sees through every deceit, and Samir's unjust charges are swept away.
The royal guards search the place you indicated and find only the corpse of an old man, dead by poison. The rest of the exiles slip away into the night. Yet after hearing the tale of fathers and sons, and watching the physician's anguished expressions, the Sultan deems the outcome acceptable.

And you say nothing.
Since entering this game, death has circled you like a vulture; now it descends lower, close enough to brush your shoulder. Yet your heart is strangely calm.
Perhaps this sacrifice is meaningless. Perhaps Samir will die regardless. But at least—you have not betrayed your friend.
The Sultan's wrath is palpable without even raising your head. You hear the heavy tread of the royal guards' boots.
"Wait... it was me."
You turn in shock—and even the Sultan stares in surprise—as a pale, trembling figure crawls from the shadows of a column.
It is Kapar, the favorite once gifted to Samir.
"I was jealous that Master Samir spent time with other men, so I sought to avenge myself with the stillborn child... I bought the infant from beggars in the street. It belonged to no woman in the harem... I was foolish, wicked... Please, do not punish anyone else."
His words falter. His body begins to convulse, and his mouth floods with blood. Servants scatter in panic; a eunuch kneels to check his breath, then declares that he had taken poison beforehand.
The wretched man's blood stains the floor, souring the Sultan's mood. Yet the Sultan is fond of crimes of passion, fond of sordid tales. Since this story pleases him, he begrudgingly spares both you and Samir from further blame.

You do not even feign an investigation—what greater affront, what deeper contempt for the Sultan! With a wave of his hand, the royal guards force you down onto the smooth, icy lapis lazuli floor. He wants to see your blood drain here, enough to stain several blue tiles red.
As your mind blurs, you dimly hear someone step forth, trembling, to confess. Is it that fool Samir—or another? You can no longer see, no longer hear. Yet even in your own failing, you know this much: you have not betrayed your friends.
Another day passes, and the ministers regard you with yet more pity.

5006111.title: Inquiry in the Harem
strings: Inquiry in the Harem

Even when commanded by the Sultan himself, even when held by the central fountain of the harem, surrounded by guards, eunuchs, and maids, to question the Sultan's consorts is perilous for any courtier.
Sultan's Consorts
You can only enter the harem in person to pursue this matter.
You have but one chance to speak with a consort.
You hope to draw some clue from Consort [s1.name].
You hope to seek word from [s1.name].
Consorts avoid you entirely.

Ansuya listens calmly.
"So this has happened... I have indeed noticed the servants seem distracted of late, as if in fear of something... But they would not tell me such matters, nor would anyone suspect me." She even smiles as she speaks.
She offers no clues, yet recounts stories from her homeland—tales of her father's harem and its intrigues. The royal guards, entranced, forget themselves until the hour grows late. You remain far beyond the time any man is permitted in the harem, which alone sparks whispers among the nobles of your rising influence...

Sadani shows no sign of agitation. She says coldly that she does not know who committed this vile act—only that it could not be one of the favored concubines. That would be sheer folly. To already bask in the sun's love, then seek another man? Impossible.
She falls into silence, stiff and proud, making clear her distance from the affair.
Gently, you offer your own reasoning: indeed, she may be right. Rumors of women seeking abortive medicine from the court physician are not new. Even the most reckless woman would not dare discard a stillborn child now, at the height of suspicion... Surely this is no accident, but a deliberate trap, a cruel conspiracy... As you speak, you feign distress—the Sultan drives you mercilessly, leaving you so little time.
Sadani listens and nods with solemn care. "Your suspicion is most reasonable," she says. "You should be granted more time to uncover the truth."
It is a promise—and she keeps it.

Zazie never ceases her laughter. She seems to find the death of an infant entertaining.
"Think about it, think about it! Picture how hopeless that stupid woman must be after causing all this... Oh, if only I knew who she was!"
She shakes her head, her gold ornaments glittering, the silken sash at her waist loosening without concern. The royal guards cannot help but steal several glances.
"Ask me no more, my dear lord [player.name], for I think of nothing but pleasing my master. Nothing else can enter my ears—they are blocked by golden rings!"
She prattles with practiced charm, giving you no clue at all. Yet it hardly matters—how many men in all the empire, sound of body, may step into the Sultan's harem and behold his most cherished consort?
Your prestige among the people rises.

Fadia kneels before you with utmost humility, listening as you question her. Yet she knows nothing useful. Still kneeling, she recalls carefully and shares all she dares in front of the royal guards and eunuchs. It does not advance the case, but grants you valuable scraps of intelligence.

They fear you—fear that a careless word may betray them, and that your questions might seal their doom. Too many, too favored, have died for their ties to you. They would rather endure the suspicion of the royal guards than risk your gaze. And so, apart from putting on a show of diligence, you pass another day with nothing gained...

5006112.title: Samir's Request
strings: Samir's Request
Concerning the case of the dead infant found in the court, Samir seems to have already formed his own deduction. He asks you to send someone to help him test it...
Samir
Samir requires an assistant with Stealth 5 or higher.
Time is short. He will not wait forever.
A Duty Unshirked
Sorry, My Friend
Samir is deeply grateful. With your help, his inquiry can proceed far more smoothly.
You cannot spare anyone to assist him. Samir says nothing. After all, this is his burden to bear.
What's done is done

One day, an old man blocks your door, hurling curses. He rails at you for meddling, at the Sultan for sparing Samir, and at his own son for dishonoring their house by serving the Sultan. His fury grows louder until a crowd gathers, eager for scandal—gossip of the Sultan, the court, the fallen kingdom, and a father against his son...
Now everyone knows: a stubborn old man, loyal only to his former homeland, cast the corpse of an infant into the harem—an act born of fury at his son's submission to the Sultan. Such things are all too common in the slums. His aim was to see his own son destroyed, yet his scheme was laid bare by the Sultan's composure and your keen judgment, driving him into a frenzy that ended in madness.
Though the guards rush in at once, the tale has already spread from mouth to mouth, known to all. Before their very eyes, the culprit glares with bloodshot eyes, hands trembling, then suddenly foams at the mouth and collapses. By the time the royal guards drag him to the court physician, the old man has already breathed his last...
Even so, the royal guards breath a sigh of relief. They urge you to bring the body, together with the evidence, before the Sultan. "Now Lord Samir's name will be cleared, right?"

5006113.title: The Physician's Death
strings: The Physician's Death
The Sultan's royal guards storm Samir's house, intent on seizing the guilty man.
Samir
Kapar

The royal guards return with grim news: Samir has already taken poison. His death is beyond doubt—a coward's suicide.
The Sultan shows no satisfaction. To him, it means this traitor betrayed twice: once when he renounced his homeland, and again when he fled the Sultan's justice. As he leaves the Lapis Lazuli Palace, the Sultan orders coldly: drag the body away—and the body of his favorite besides. Feed them to the dogs. Lions and leopards are too precious for such carrion.
This thorny case is closed.
Your colleagues respect your handling of it. Yet, strangely, your reputation among the people is affected.

5006114.title: A Truth Samir Dreads
strings: A Truth Samir Dreads
Samir continues his search for the truth—one he has long refused to face.
Samir
The One Who Assists Samir
The Ones Who Hate Me Most
The Ones Who Hate Me Most, The One Who Loved Me Most

"Just as I thought," Samir comes to you, weary from days of inquiry. "It was the work of those who hate me most, done for no other purpose than revenge. They knew that if scandal struck the harem, the Sultan would have my head at once. They sought my death by his hand."
You ask him: who are they?
Samir gives a hollow smile, then glances around. "How are things with your parents? I suppose... well enough. As for me, my parents were court physicians of the fallen kingdom. My family still clings to that king who has long since rotted to mud. What did they give me but shackles? Because of them I could not practice medicine, could not enter the ranks of nobility, could not even stand tall as a man. We were poorer than dogs in the street. What noble would seek out a court physician of the fallen kingdom? What commoner could pay the fee for a 'court physician'?"
He speaks with strange calm, as if telling another man's story. "But still I wanted to be a physician. So I fled the mire. I went before the chamberlain, declaring myself the son of a court physician from the fallen kingdom, offering to renounce all else and devote myself to the Sultan... Of course they hate me. I betrayed my family, took the Sultan's favor, and accepted the favorite the Sultan bestowed upon me. For wealth and rank, I forsook my pride. They are right to hate me. Sometimes, I hate myself."
Outside, a fine rain falls, and the air grows heavy to breathe. After a pause, Samir shakes his head with bitter humor. "In any case, they confessed. They bought a dead infant from the slums and bribed a lowly eunuch to bury it in some consort's garden." He says, "the man you sent to aid me found them still at work, compiling the medical codex—the last command of the old king. Since childhood, my father trained me for this—compiling entries, writing annotations—and the slightest mistake would earn me the lash of his whip... I despised him for it. Now my family offers me a bargain. If I finish their codex, they will hand me a convincing culprit to close this case. Perhaps it is best—then my debt to them ends..."
His hands, more used to grinding herbs than pleading, fold in awkward entreaty. "I do not know how long it will take, [player.name]. I know I have burdened you too much, far more than the little help I once gave you during the royal hunt... But this, this I cannot do alone. If it is at all possible... could you win me a few more days?"
You assure him you will do all in your power.

You ask him: who are they?

Then his composure breaks. His voice rises, raw with anguish. "But they should not have dragged the innocent into this! To hurt me, they caused so much needless pain! Kapar... I did not love him. I am not drawn to men—nor to women, either. I only wanted to be a physician. I only loved my craft! But what wrong did he commit? He always said he was my stain, my blemish... and he finally found a chance to cleanse it. I was confined in my home, and the royal guards brought back his corpse. My God... my God... he was so deft at grinding herbs—he always worked beside me!" Samir lowers his head and weeps. You do not know how to comfort him, so you place a hand upon his shoulder. Outside, a fine rain falls, and the air grows heavy to breathe. At last, when his sobs subside, he tells you of the bargain he has struck with his kin.
"I have promised to complete the medical codex—the last command of the old king. When it is done, I will thank you for your aid... and I will try, somehow, to do something for Kapar." He bows deeply, then takes his leave.

5006116.title: Medical Codex - Chapter I
strings: Medical Codex - Chapter I
Much remains unfinished in the codex. Many herbs still lack illustrations, and Samir devotes himself wholly to the task.
Samir
Perhaps You Can Aid Him
10 Gold Coins, a follower with Survival or Wisdom of at least 5, or certain books may offer assistance to Samir.
You take out a large sum of money.
You assign [s2.name] as Samir's assistant.
You provide reference texts.
You fail to assist.
Your generous payment summons many artists to your call. You must spend some effort dismissing frauds who cannot draw a leaf properly, but in the end, the work advances much faster thanks to you.
[s2.gender] has a keen eye for herbs and knows how to capture their features. With [s2.gender(his,her)] help, Samir's work proceeds smoothly.
[s2.name] is exactly the material Samir has long sought! It spares him much toil and saves precious time.

Still, Kapar remains at Samir's side. Beyond tending to a court physician who forgets day and night in his labor, he has learned some herb lore by long exposure... With his aid, Samir soon completes this portion of the codex.
All you can do is watch Samir scramble to keep up, wishing he could clone himself to finish this demanding task... Perhaps the toil is a mercy—it spares him from his grief, if only for a time.

5006117.title: Medical Codex - Chapter II
strings: Medical Codex - Chapter II
For the next chapter, Samir requires samples of animal bone...
Samir
Perhaps You Can Aid Him
10 Gold Coins, a follower with Combat or Stealth of at least 5, or certain characters may offer assistance to Samir.
No One Knows Better Than Him
Nothing money cannot solve.
Whose bones do you seek?
You fail to assist.
Habib brings Samir a trove of animal bones, greatly hastening the work. The only complaint is that the guesthouse's kitchen now lacks its usual bone broth—a loss loudly lamented.
Fresh animal bones are cheap; older, rarer specimens... Samir helps you identify them, so you won't be cheated. With your aid, the compilation proceeds far more efficiently!

[s2.name] pounds the chest and declares [s2.gender] can hunt anything—lion or tiger, antelope or stallion. Human bones, however, would be a different matter... Samir says that these are unnecessary. In any case, [s2.gender] keeps the promise, supplying Samir with excellent references.

When Samir becomes completely absorbed in his work, losing track of day and night, Kapar takes care of errands, messages, and other trivial tasks. At one point, Kapar returns with a leather sack brimming with various animal bones. Samir beams with delight, hugs Kapar, then plunges back into the intensive compilation work. Ah...
All you can do is watch Samir scramble to keep up, wishing he could clone himself to finish this demanding task... Perhaps the toil is a mercy—it spares him from his grief, if only for a time.

5006119.title: Last Chapter
strings: Last Chapter

Samir and his assistants are now buried under towering stacks of books, busy with "final collation"—the last step before any great work sees the light of day. If you can send literate helpers, the process could go much faster.
Samir
Help in Compilation
Nobles, followers with Wisdom of at least 5, or certain special characters may offer assistance.
Even Kapar can no longer offer assistance in this stage.
Beyond Human Reach
Finally...
Names Side by Side
Debts That Cannot Be Reckoned
When No One Can Assist

Samir comes to you, weary yet proud, carrying the compiled medical codex.
"From now on, physicians may turn to this book. It gathers the remedies of our time and the most effective cures against pestilence... This is my honor. At last, I have completed it. Truly, I never thought this day would come... Thank you, [player.name]" He smiles sincerely as he places the heavy volume into your hands.
"To be honest, I never imagined this work would bring me such joy... When I was a boy, my father forced me to write these entries—if I erred, he would strike me with a whip, or leave me without food... Back then, I hated him, and I hated this codex. Why else would I have run away?" A shadow crosses his face. Then he shakes his head. "...No matter. That is all behind me."

He gestures for you to open the frontispiece. There, a line of small script reads: "To the one who gave everything. To Kapar."
"Even if I write his name here, it makes no difference. The Sultan will never remember the slave he once gave away, nor the man who died because of me..." Samir smiles with gentle longing. "I know it is a small thing—but still, I must do it. I want others to remember him... His name was Kapar."

Samir then hands you a letter. He urges you to read. It is the confession of an elder sharing his surname, who speaks of his fury at a son who betrayed the family. That anger, mixed with years of poverty, curdled into murder. He describes how he sought out a stillborn child, bribed a servant to bury it in the harem, and longed for his own son to be executed by the Sultan's hand.
When you lift your eyes from the page, Samir is watching you. Quietly, he says, "I still do not know whether it was his doing or that of my kinsmen... But in truth, it no longer matters. I owe them nothing now. Submit it to the Sultan—this should satisfy all parties."
He bows, then departs. You do not stop him. You know what he needs now is solitude.
The collation continues, urgent as ever.

5006122.title: A Quiet Place
strings: A Quiet Place
It is a gentle hill by a clear river. A fitting place for a resting ground.
Construction Cost: 8 Gold Coins
To break the Extravagance Card, another 8 Gold Coins are required.
Can only break Extravagance Cards up to Silver tier.
To break the Extravagance Card, sufficient Gold Coin is required.
They Deserve to Be Remembered
Too Much Zeal

Here you consecrate a burial ground for healers. Be they noble physicians serving statesmen, or wandering doctors handing out herbs to the poor, regardless of rank or gender—if they eased suffering in life, they may rest here in death.
When the grounds are finished, you tell Samir. Soon after, the first body is laid to rest, a coral-stone marker raised above it. Together, you stand beneath the shade of trees, watching people come and go. Many physicians arrive with their kin to see this promised place. Among them are familiar faces, watching with the same wary gaze...
Samir notices some of his own kinsfolk, but does not approach. Instead, he turns and smiles at you. "I have nothing to tell them. In the end, all we have done in this life will be judged beneath the earth. When the time comes, I shall meet them—here, beneath our feet."
The wind sweeps across the hill, carrying no trace of decay—only grass, sun, and the scent of soil. In the stillness beyond the wind's reach, the healers at last find their hard-won rest.

After the cemetery is completed, you quietly order Samir's grave to be moved here as well, and carve his name with your own hand upon a coral stone. A physician unacknowledged by his own kin until death—may he find peace at last in this place.

Here you consecrate a burial ground for healers. Be they noble physicians serving statesmen, or wandering doctors handing out herbs to the poor, regardless of rank or gender—if they eased suffering in life, they may rest here in death.
Also, you assign the finest guards to patrol the grounds, raise a bronze statue of a physician, and even place a copy of the medical codex in the warden's hall at the very center. Nowhere else in the empire can boast a cemetery so splendid.
Yet, such grandeur keeps common physicians away; few dare even to approach the warden to arrange their burial... For a long while, the only grave here is that of an old court physician of the fallen kingdom.
His name is etched upon the coral stone by Samir's own hand. That day, the two of you stood together in the shade for a long time, saying nothing. Only when the moment came to part did he smile faintly and say, "I have nothing to tell him. In the end, all we have done in this life will be judged beneath the earth. When the time comes, I shall meet him—here, beneath our feet."

Have You Gone Mad?
Honor
Not long after, the cemetery warden brings you several medicines. They are gifts from physicians who hope one day to be buried here, and from the families of those already laid to rest.

Your lavish investment in this cemetery even surprises the Sultan. "Has this game driven you to such extremes, my vizier? You are already preparing a tomb for yourself?"
For an instant you truly wonder if he is picturing you lying there, but at last he only laughs and permits you to break this card. After all, you have spent a great sum, and no matter how splendid it may be, it remains nothing more than a cemetery...

The dignity, grandeur, and solemnity of this resting place draw the attention of physicians who serve the nobility and enjoy some means of their own... More than that, it is a cemetery sanctioned by the great Sultan himself!
In the days that follow, you are often stopped by men who discreetly press gifts into your hand, hoping you will reserve a place for them on that hallowed ground...

A restorative tonic gifted by physicians, said to strengthen the body.
You can try the potion yourself or have any follower test its effects.
After drinking the potion, [s1.name] finds even meals taste richer. Hunt five gazelles at once, no sweat!

5006125.title: Precious Sample
strings: Precious Sample
Samir requests a vial of the Water of Life as a sample, so that he may study it more closely.
Samir hopes you will provide him with a vial of the Water of Life.
The Art of Imitation

Samir's messenger arrives once more, bearing a crystal vial filled with a clear liquid. At first glance, it resembles the Water of Life, but under closer inspection its color shows a faint shade of blue.
In his letter, Samir first conveys his gratitude, then writes: "The Water of Life is without question the most fascinating of all samples. I have studied it extensively, analyzed its essence, and attempted what may be a crude imitation. Here is my first draft. Perhaps you could find someone to test its effects? I do not believe it to be poisonous, yet I cannot speak with certainty on how it feels when used. And perhaps its use need not be limited to humans? After all, the principles of life are not so different across creatures."

5006126.title: A Cure for Wounds?
strings: A Cure for Wounds?
Samir's imitation of the Water of Life appears capable of healing wounds—and not only in humans, if rumor is true.
Characters Who Need Treatment
Imitation of the Water of Life

Could a man-made medicine truly heal a creature not of humankind? There is only one way to know.
You unstopper the vial and let a single drop fall upon a wound that radiates an uncanny aura. In an instant, the gash closes entirely—even [s1.name] turns in astonishment, staring long at the bottle in your hand.
That very night, you write to Samir: the imitation works astonishingly well on non-human subjects.

At first touch, the wounded animal cries out in pain so sharp it shakes your resolve. You are forced to pin its body down with all your weight as before your eyes, the hideous wound begins knitting shut at a pace visible to the naked eye...
The remedy works, but at a terrible cost of suffering. You report your findings to Samir exactly as they occurred.
Not long after, Samir comes to visit you in person, followed by several attendants, all trained in the healing arts. He inquires carefully into the trials of the imitation. Then, after some thought, he says, "The Water of Life itself uses the power of renewal to mask the pain of bodily healing. My imitation, however, merely tears muscle and skin together by force, compelling them to mend—hence the terrible pain... I wonder if the addition of some sedatives might help... We must not overlook the harm it causes to the patient."
Behind him, his attendants scribble every word.
"You see, I don't have many people to call on, nor can I conduct enough trials." Samir gestures toward those trailing close behind him. How many of them truly admire his skill, and how many are sent by the Sultan to keep watch over him? "That's why I must trouble you. Perhaps you could ask among the people you know—whether some folk remedy for easing pain has escaped our notice... Our medicine advances too slowly, and the patients I can treat are far too few."
With that, Samir offers his thanks in advance and departs, swept away again by the entourage that shadows his every step.

The clear potion touches the wound, and [s1.name] gasps sharply—"By God, it burns! Too much—!" Before your eyes, the bleeding gash begins to close. The effect may not match the Water of Life, but it is miraculous all the same. Yet [s1.gender] grits the teeth the whole time, cursing through the agony. You have seldom seen [s1.gender(him,her)] in such a state.
Later, you relay [s1.name]'s words to Samir: "It feels like searing the flesh together with a hot iron. Unless one is on the brink of death, I doubt anyone would choose to endure it."
Not long after, Samir comes to visit you in person, followed by several attendants, all trained in the healing arts. He inquires carefully into the trials of the imitation. Then, after some thought, he says, "The Water of Life itself uses the power of renewal to mask the pain of bodily healing. My imitation, however, merely tears muscle and skin together by force, compelling them to mend—hence the terrible pain... I wonder if the addition of some sedatives might help... We must not overlook the harm it causes to the patient."
Behind him, his attendants scribble every word.
"You see, I don't have many people to call on, nor can I conduct enough trials." Samir gestures toward those trailing close behind him. How many of them truly admire his skill, and how many are sent by the Sultan to keep watch over him? "That's why I must trouble you. Perhaps you could ask among the people you know—whether some folk remedy for easing pain has escaped our notice... Our medicine advances too slowly, and the patients I can treat are far too few."
With that, Samir offers his thanks in advance and departs, swept away again by the entourage that shadows his every step.
The potion proves remarkably effective, though you no longer share your findings with him after your falling-out.

5006127.title: Pain Cannot Be Ignored
strings: Pain Cannot Be Ignored
Samir hopes you will inquire whether folk remedies for easing pain exist. Such knowledge may help him refine his imitation.
Ways to Gain Inspiration
You may consult certain characters—or, as ever, coin can buy answers.
A Hefty Reward
You ask Raed if she knows any remedy for easing pain.
You ask Jabal if he knows any remedy for easing pain.
You ask Faris if he knows any remedy for easing pain.
You ask Badriyyah if she knows any remedy for easing pain.
You ask Fardak if he knows any remedy for easing pain.
You ask Iman if he knows any remedy for easing pain.

You know little of medicine, but peasants, herders, fishermen, and soldiers all keep their own cures and secrets.
So you send your servants to the marketplace, offering dates and lamb to any who can present a proven remedy.
By the next evening, you have gathered dozens of methods.

Raed ponders long before she speaks: "When I was a child, my mother's garden held a small grey plant, hardly worth notice, with little white blossoms. Its sap numbs the skin. In those days it was used as an anesthetic. Whether the Sultan's physicians still remember it, I cannot say—but it would be laughable indeed if they did not. The answer lies at hand, yet still the search goes on everywhere else!"
You thank her and record her words.

Jabal's body is covered in scars, proof of his knowledge.
"For pain? Soldiers use a kind of liquor from the frontier. It dulls the nerves, but drink too much and it weakens the will. I never touch that thing."
He explains its making, but makes you swear never to indulge in excess. Only after your promise does he let you go.
You record both the recipe and its danger.

Faris brings over several battered books on veterinary medicine.
"If you can create a cheap and useful salve, spare me some first. No one studies remedies for animals, so I have to treat them myself. Look—these pages describe several painkillers, and bandages—these are vital! Promise me, if you succeed, you will give me some. My hounds are often hurt!"
You give your word and take careful notes.

Badriyyah presses a cup of fragrant flower juice into your hands, smiling as she explains its many uses: drink it, pour it on wounds—or apply it in ways best left unspoken.
Well... You record the juice and her methods.

Fardak's homeland follows a medical tradition entirely unlike the Empire's. Their patients are first made to drink a large bowl of herbal broth—usually bitter and foul-smelling, though at times oddly bitter, sweet, rancid, and fragrant all at once.
"Then we vomit—messily—until all the bad things inside are gone. That's when the physicians say you're already halfway cured," he explains with pride. "For injuries like falls or cuts, there's another brew. Drink it, and the pain dulls, sleepiness sets in..."
He goes on and on about the customs of his people, clearly proud of their knowledge.
You note down the remedy.

Iman tells you that Purists never concern themselves with easing pain—in fact, the more it hurts, the better.
"But," he admits, "sometimes rotten flesh must be cut away. If it isn't, the priest dies. In those moments, we need something to keep the cries from being too unbearable. I remember the elder high priests would bring out a gray powder... They're ashes from a certain spice once it's burned. If this can help you, if it can spare others from needless suffering, then use it."
He hands you some samples, and you record everything he said.
You compile all the findings into a thick packet of notes and send it to Samir, praying they will aid in improving the new medicine.

5006128.title: A New Medicine
strings: A New Medicine
Samir begins work on a new medicine. It is weaker than the Water of Life, more painful to use, yet far cheaper and easier to obtain.
Samir
Mahir, or any character with Wisdom above 5, can lend him a hand.

Samir repeatedly tested the analgesic you mentioned—refining, extracting, purifying—until at last he succeeded. The cheap, effective medicine soon spreaded across the Empire. In any case, he thanked you for your help.

Samir tests every pain-relieving method you have brought him, refining, distilling, and purifying again and again. With Mahir's aid, his efforts grow all the more effective. Mahir brings both skill and enthusiasm, arriving with a full set of instruments—She has long entertained the idea of dabbling with more dangerous potions that could poison a person, or even bring a corpse back to life. Samir, however, tells her such potions are hardly miraculous: they merely speed wound closure, far weaker than the Water of Life and utterly incapable of restoring lost limbs.
Mahir ponders this for a moment and then suggests, "Then—shall we steal some Aether?"
"If you speak like that again," Samir replies gently but firmly, "I shall have to turn you out."
Well... it seems they ought to cooperate quite happily.
Samir tests every pain-relieving method you have brought him, refining, distilling, and purifying again and again. With [s2.name]'s aid, his efforts grow all the more effective.

Soon, [s2.name] comes to you, proudly holding up a vial of the new medicine. It is Samir's invention, refined and perfected with [s2.gender(his,her)] help—and now, at last, it can be produced in quantity.
"The court physician says the name shall be—"[s2.gender] winks at you, "Dew of [player.name]! Sexy, isn't it?"
...Something about it feels a little off to you, but Samir clearly meant well.
Either way, from that day forward, even a fig-seller on the street could scrape together a few coins to buy a bottle that might save a child, a lover, or even themselves. The name Dew of [player.name] spreads quickly throughout the land.

Soon, [s2.name] comes to you, proudly holding up a vial of the new medicine. It is Samir's invention, refined and perfected with [s2.gender(his,her)] help—and now, at last, it can be produced in quantity.
"The court physician has named it Water of Renewal."
This cheap yet potent medicine soon spreads throughout the empire. From this day forward, even a fig-seller on the street could scrape together a few coins to buy a bottle that might save a child, a lover, or even themselves. And as the patron of the Water of Renewal, your name is carried far and wide by physicians and patients alike.

5006129.title: A Midnight Call
strings: A Midnight Call
Deep in the night, your door shakes beneath urgent pounding. "Physician—Lord Samir—he... Lord [player.name], you must help him!"
Samir
You can enter the palace to handle this in person.
Any Consumable
Such summons do not come lightly. The danger is real, or Samir would never risk disturbing you at this hour. Prepare yourself well before you go.
You attempt to parley with the inhuman presence.
Magic and Wisdom determine your full dice count.
You need at least 5 Successes to finish the parley.
Save It for Tomorrow

How could that be? Nothing is ever supposed to happen to Samir inside the palace. And besides, as a man, there is no way you will ever be allowed to slip in the harem at night. Yet when you wake the next morning, the news strikes like thunder—Samir is dead. Together with him fell more than a dozen royal guards, their end said to have been unspeakably grim. Word spreads quickly: it was the work of a demon...
No Time to Explain
Unfortunately, You Fail
Fortunately, You Succeed

You hurry to Samir's chambers in the palace. Normally, the royal guards at his door interrogate every man who passes, but today they look stricken with fear. Without a word, they step aside and open the way. Samir drags you inside. His back presses against the door, eyes darting nervously toward you. Only now do you notice the sweat soaking his face.
"They... they were just here. They spoke—if you can call that speaking. That wasn't a human voice... not even close. Oh God, it was terrifying... I think it's connected to the medicine—the one I gave you. But I—" He freezes, then whispers hoarsely, "Listen! They're here again!"
From outside comes a strange scraping, followed by the startled cries of the guards. Then, a taut, sickening creak—like a rope pulled to breaking...
Silence falls. Then: a knock. Once. Twice. Thrice.
Perhaps a tail. Or a bone. Or an eye. But not a human hand... Something beats against the door, shrieking in a voice beyond comprehension. The echo alone sends chills crawling up your spine...

You steady your mind, wrapping every word and syllable in the power of your Insight. Yet the harder you try, the more the voices shatter your focus. The door groans. A crack splinters across the wood. Darkness floods the room. It swallows you and Samir whole. Your consciousness slips away—yet even the monsters who kill you seem bewildered, as if they had meant to bargain for something else.

You steady your mind, wrapping every word and syllable in the power of your Insight... You try to communicate with beings far beyond Samir's comprehension, from a height he could never reach.
"Ten bottles... at the entrance... we... need... will... give you... reward..."
You wipe the cold sweat streaming down your forehead and shout out loud, promising that you understand—you will make sure Samir prepares the medicine.
A rumbling sound shakes the air again, as if from some enormous belly... or perhaps it is the sound of a wound?
When it passes, Samir collapses to his knees, utterly spent, gazing at you with awe. Outside, the royal guards seem to have just awakened from a dream. They whisper among themselves, spreading tales of your deeds—Lord [player.name] not only pleases the Sultan but can even converse with demons!

5006130.title: The Uncanny Order
strings: The Uncanny Order

You urge Samir to begin immediately on this strange order—when will the mysterious client, never seen before, come to collect it? And if they can't bring enough of this potion next time, what consequences might follow? You, Samir, and the palace attendants who witnessed that night's events—all of you are unwilling to even consider the possibilities.
Samir
Samir requires a helper with Magic above 5, or skill in alchemy.

Seeing you refuse to continue assisting, Samir was forced to work alone at a rush... sadly, before long you heard of his miserable death, and that very night, those strange voices invaded your dreams. All night they gnawed at your thoughts, your memories, rummaging through your soul. You nearly thought you would die because death would be gentler. At last, dawn came. Luckily, they seemed to understand you could not make such a draught, and, having left, did not trouble you further.
A Suitable Helper

The new medicine stands ready, neatly sealed in crystal vials.
When you arrive, Samir is fastening labels to the glass. You lean closer. The words read: "Not for human use."
He wipes the sweat from his brow and turns to you.
"The time is too short, the demand too high... I won't risk giving these to people again... So I marked them—to prevent a mistake."
He exhales, his shoulders finally loosening. Weariness clouds his eyes. "From here, it's in your hands. I can't face them again."

5006131.title: Not for Human Use
strings: Not for Human Use
At nightfall, they will come to claim the medicine. Yet you have another choice—you could break the pact.
You can deliver the vials in person or send any follower in your stead.
You choose to offer this batch to the True Faith.
You choose to offer this batch to the Cultic God.
You choose to fulfill your promise and wait for the nocturnal visitors.
Whatever you decide, the price must be paid.

Why give it to others? Why not keep it yourself? You hurried home with the goods, barred the doors and windows, and portioned everything out. Now you would never have to fear being wounded again! As for the abomination begging for the medicine... well, there are always ways to deal with them.
The Priests of the Purist would probably have liked this.
Since those creatures of the night liked it, there must have been the Cultic God who liked it even more.
You hadn't wanted to take the risk yourself, and the devotee most bound to the Cultic God was already gone... better to let it go.
Perhaps for the First Time, You Take Their Gold Coins
Perhaps the Cultic God's Most Cherished Offering
Unfortunately, Badriyyah Has Already Died

It brings pain—sharp, searing pain. Purists crave it. The priests who receive you are radiant with joy, praising the gift as though it were divine. For them, pain is rebirth, as death is peace. They accept your offering and cry your name aloud, proclaiming your greatness.

Badriyyah sniffs the vials again and again, even tasting a drop. She is thrilled.
"If you pour these into the stone cauldron, no chant is needed—they will come just from the scent! Absolutely! How did you manage to get something so perfect? You are incredible!"
She hands you a small booklet, then hugs you tightly, leaving stains of tattoo ink on your clothes.
Whatever those things knocking at the door are, they must now share—or perhaps fight for—these offerings with the creatures summoned by the cultists...

You do not wish to risk facing them yourself. As you hesitate, twilight deepens—they arrive.
The room fills with thunderous roars and anguished moans, a chill that seeps through your skin, and a dread that needs no explanation... You shove the vials through the door crack and brace it shut. The sounds halt the moment they touch the crystal bottles.
You hear the popping of stoppers,
the pouring of liquids,
the sighs of satisfaction...
then silence.
Long after, you open the door. The corridor is empty. In the garden, your servants huddle beneath the pomegranate trees, trembling. You call them forth. The monsters have taken what they came for and will not return. Relief spreads across their faces...

Nightfall brings them here.
The room fills with thunderous roars and anguished moans, a chill that seeps through your skin, and a dread that needs no explanation... You shove the vials through the door crack and brace it shut. The sounds halt the moment they touch the crystal bottles.
You hear the popping of stoppers,
the pouring of liquids,
the sighs of satisfaction...
then silence.
Long after, you open the door. The corridor is empty. In the garden, your servants huddle beneath the pomegranate trees, trembling. You call them forth. The monsters have taken what they came for and will not return. Relief spreads across their faces...

5006132.title: Punishment for Breaking Your Word
strings: Punishment for Breaking Your Word
If you resolve not to deliver the vials, when they come, darkness presses against every crack of your door and window...
Yourself
A consumable for assistance in battling the creatures.
You brace yourself and face the malevolence head-on!
Magic and Wisdom determine your full dice count.
You need at least 7 Successes to survive.
You lost
Alright, You won
You die—like Samir—because you broke your promise.

With the last trace of malice vanishing, you step over the remnants of evil and breathe deeply.
You have won. Together with the newborn sun, you greet the next dawn.

5006133.title: Tattoo Patterns
strings: Tattoo Patterns
Reading can improve yourself, so develop a habit of reading.
Currently Reading
The reader.
I had seen such patterns—on some people's open palms, and on the backs of the hands of those who held whips.
There was no need to review them—they had long been seared into my heart, heh heh...
What a foul thing.
Interesting facts...
Is there anything worth learning?
It is recorded here...
Let me take a look
The lines were full of mysteries.
