Your fury rises.
You and the dissenter clash, shouting over one another before the throne. Neither of you will yield. And when you both finally fall silent, you realize the Sultan has been watching all along. He smiles.
To him, you are both fools. But fools amuse him. That amusement fades when his eyes return to the coronet. It's beginning to grate on him. With a casual wave, he orders the guards to drag Jenna away and have her executed. Perhaps a touch of her blood would make this coronet even more beautiful.
The Price of Absence
Your absence was interpreted as a blatant defiance of his authority. Under his thunderous wrath, no one dared to speak up for you. You were executed.
At Long Last

As you leave the audience hall, everyone instinctively gives you a wide berth. They've all just witnessed what you're capable of.
Jenna walks out of the palace alongside you, her legs weak, almost needing your support, and she is clearly impressed by your actions.
"This Sultan's game... it's far more terrifying than I ever imagined," she murmurs. "Yet you handled it all with such calm... you must have faced trials like this countless times. Lord [player.name]... my friend... you've endured so much."

5006154.title: The Empire's Finest Jeweler
strings: The Empire's Finest Jeweler
Jenna visits you once more, coming expressly to offer her thanks.
Jenna

Jenna has become the empire's most sought-after jeweler. Her workshop is so busy that the carpets are nearly worn through from all the visitors. None of this, of course, would have been possible without your steadfast support.
"I dare say I could call myself the finest jeweler in the entire empire—yes, the whole empire, not just this city. I've handled the Sultan's crown, polished charms for the poor, and even introduced a new gem unknown to anyone before..." Her voice falters, and her gaze drifts toward the window, lost in thought for a moment before she continues.
"But they're still not enough... far from it! There's still so much I want to do, so many corners of the world I long to see. Even imagining it fills me with joy!" She rises and pulls you into an embrace. No words are spoken. You both know the bond between you is unbreakable.

5006155.title: A Young Man's Commission
strings: A Young Man's Commission
A young man seeking to become a court scribe requested a modestly respectable ornament for his interview; even a tiny amethyst would suffice.
Jenna
Requires 1 additional Gold Coin for other materials.
Proper Gems
The client requests an amethyst.
Even if you offer a more precious gem, he cannot pay any extra.
Insert a proper gem.
This is exactly the gem he needs.
A gem like this would lend him a bit more luster.
Either too lowly, making him hang his head at the interview, or too expensive for him to dare accept.
First Jewel
Use an Emerald
A Lucky Stone

Jenna crafts a delicate amethyst piece to the young man's specifications. One day, he may possess treasures far grander—but this first jewel will remain etched in memory.
The finished piece delights him. Set in silver, the amethyst gleams larger and brighter than he expected, encircled by a silver thread shaped like ocean waves. He hurries to the mirror, eager to see himself adorned. The jewel fills him with confidence, kindling hope for the days ahead. The poor young man can't give Jenna much, so she doesn't have much to share with you either—but she still manages to give you a small reward.

Emeralds are gentle yet profound. Perfect for a court official's attire. Should he step into the palace, this piece could serve him for years.
Jenna nods completely in agreement. Yet the young man is overwhelmed by the jewel's splendor. Time and again, he protests that he cannot even afford a few tiny emeralds. Jenna reassures him that the cost has already been covered by Lord [player.name].
He nearly weeps as he leaves, repeatedly promising he will one day repay the kindness he has received.

You hand Jenna a ruby—a gem of extraordinary brilliance, perfect for a moment such as this, when a young man stands on the threshold of his destiny.
Both you and Jenna sense that this ruby will bring him good fortune.
At first, the young man flees—literally terrified.
He mistakes Jenna's craft for a trap, fearing she will demand payment beyond his means. Fortunately, others at the guesthouse intercept him and bring him back.
Jenna explains patiently that Lord [player.name] has already covered the cost, and no further payment will be expected. The young man is astonished—not only by the unexpected generosity but also by the care and artistry Jenna has poured into a piece for which she earns nothing.
He solemnly dons the jewel, raising a vow to both it and you: he will make a name for himself and return one day to repay this debt of gratitude.

5006156.title: A Couple's Commission
strings: A Couple's Commission
A newlywed couple came to Jenna, requesting two pieces crafted from the finest red carnelian. Among the poor, tradition dictated that wedding jewelry be made from this fiery, passionate stone.
Jenna
Requires 1 additional Gold Coin for other materials.
Proper Gems
The client requests a red carnelian.
Even if you offer a more precious gem, they cannot pay any extra.
Insert a proper gem.
This is exactly the gem the client needs.
A gem like this would lend the newlyweds a bit more luster.
Either too humble for a life event like a wedding, or too expensive for them to dare accept.
May You Walk Together Through Life
May Your Love Shine Eternal
May Your Days Be Free of Worry

Red carnelian is the perfect stone for newlyweds, and you suggest that Jenna incorporate a dove motif. These birds mate for life, tending each other in sickness, mourning one another if parted forever.
Jenna nods and sets to work. Soon, she presents two silver bracelets, each engraved with a lifelike dove whose eye gleams with red carnelian.
The young couple is thrilled. They clasp the bracelets on their wrists, doves facing each other, hands intertwined.
Though they cannot pay much, Jenna still finds a way to give you a modest reward for your support.

You hand Jenna an amethyst, a stone famed in old tales for its hypnotic, intoxicating beauty—much like love itself. You hope the violet haze it brings will linger between the couple, sustaining their affection.
Jenna nods and sets to work. Soon, she presents two copper bracelets.
At first, the newlyweds are a little disappointed—they had expected silver. Then the bride gasps in delight: set into the warm copper is a gleaming amethyst! The groom lifts his own bracelet for a closer look, noticing the delicate silver filigree encircling the stone, snugly held in the copper.
The bracelets are tender and beautiful, precious beyond their size. In the trials of married life, these stones may serve as quiet talismans, lending strength and comfort.
Jenna conveys your explanation of the amethyst and your blessings for the couple. Before your guesthouse, they bow deeply in thanks, promising to carry this gift and its blessing with them throughout their life together.

Emeralds are a rare sight on this street—you've never seen anyone wearing them! You suggest that Jenna try them; such a striking stone will be remembered, and so will she.
Jenna agrees—after all, the gem comes from you.
The silver bracelets set with emeralds leave the newlyweds stunned. The bride almost steps back in surprise, and the groom instinctively reaches to steady her. They can hardly believe they now possess such a precious gem.
After Jenna's gentle persuasion, they understand your intention. Tears glimmer in their eyes as they admire the bracelets, marveling at their brilliance and beauty. Later, if their child falls ill, the husband loses his job, or an elder becomes sick, these two stones might just come in handy.
Grateful beyond words, the couple departs, promising to tell everyone of these wedding bracelets, Lord [player.name]'s generosity, and Jenna's masterful craftsmanship.

5006157.title: A Mother's Commission
strings: A Mother's Commission
A woman about to give birth sent her husband to Jenna, requesting a piece of jewelry to pray for the child's safety.
Jenna
Requires 1 additional Gold Coin for other materials.
Proper Gems
The client requests an agate.
Even if you offer a more precious gem, she cannot pay any extra.
Insert a proper gem.
Yes, she can only afford agate.
A gem better than agate—its blessing might work even better.
This was too precious; it might bring misfortune upon this family.
How About a Red Carnelian?
How About an Amethyst?

Since ancient times, people have believed that an agate wards off illness and calms the mind. Perhaps for this order, an agate is the perfect choice. Jenna nods in agreement and sets to work. She prepares an agate necklace for the child, with barrel-shaped agate beads linked by copper clasps. The pendant is a large, semi-transparent agate stone, patterned with wavy streaks that looks like underwater plants. When the child grows, the chain can be adapted into a bracelet, and the pendant strung on a cord for continued wear.
The poor husband is overjoyed with Jenna's work. He pays a modest fee, cradles the necklace to his chest, and runs home to show his wife.

When you present the red carnelian, Jenna's eyes light up. She looks at you as if she has just found a kindred spirit.Yes, she feels the same way! In ancient tradition, red gems are vessels of sequestered divine flame, capable of scorching disease until it flees in agony.
Days later, Jenna brings forth a striking red carnelian bracelet for the husband. Crafted of copper, the bracelet is adjustable, designed to open as the child grows. At its heart rests a carnelian as red as fire, its veins flickering like trapped flames.
The poor man keeps asking if he may really take such a beautiful bracelet, worrying it must be far too precious. Jenna reassures him, "Don't worry. If Lord [player.name] can feed all who gather, he can surely provide these gems."
He bows deeply and carefully carries the bracelet home.

The true danger to a child is not some dark force that requires a gem to ward off, but poverty itself.
You hand Jenna an amethyst, asking her to craft a charm for the child's protection. Should the child fall ill in the future, selling the gem would likely cover a few visits from a physician.
Jenna takes the gem, gazing at you with a depth that lingers, before promising to create something extraordinary.
Jenna crafts a hefty silver necklace—a large amethyst as the pendant, hung on a chain so solid it feels heavy even for an adult.
When the husband comes to collect it, the sheer weight of the necklace startles him. Jenna feigns impatience, urging him to take it quickly.
"This gem was rejected by Lord [player.name]. He cares nothing for such trifles. As for the silver, I find its color disagreeable—take it back if you wish. And if the child falls ill, do not trust charms or saints. Seek a physician. Sell a segment of silver, and it should buy a small handful of medicine."
Jenna never tells you this herself. You learn it only from the whispers of the street. The coin you gave her could never have bought so much silver—it seems she paid out of her own pocket.
Though tales of the kind-hearted jeweler and her noble master circulate through the city, the two of you never speak of it again.
When you return, you sit in the courtyard with Maggie, sipping tea as you talk about what happened. In the cool evening breeze, she leans in and gives you a soft, gentle kiss.

5006158.title: A Gem Unlike Any Other
strings: A Gem Unlike Any Other

Jenna wants you to help her promote cow-bone jewelry among the nobles, so she hands you a few pieces crafted from bone. Naturally, you're curious—can your reputation and flair convince them that when you call it a gem, it truly is one?
Promoter

Maggie takes the cow-bone piece, eyes lingering on it.
"It feels gentle... elegant, yet a little wild. I think it could catch on." She fastens it onto herself. Truly, it looks stunning.

"Oh—I don't wear the bones of the dead!" Nayla screams, recoiling from your hand and the pale jewelry. You rush to reassure her. "Warriors keep the skulls of their enemies as trophies. Bones show conquest, wildness, strength—doesn't that suit you perfectly? And what thrill is there in wearing the same jewelry everyone else already has? You wear what others wouldn't dare... and you make it look stunning. That's real power."
Nayla inspects it closely. The carvinggs are exquisite, and the gold inlays are delicate.
"...Well... I suppose it is quite lovely." She tests it against her skin, a satisfied smile finally breaking across her face.
You can't help but grin.

The newly ascended noble takes the piece without a word, fastening it around [xiaochou.gender(himself,herself)]. [xiaochou.gender] pulls out a small mirror and study [xiaochou.gender(his,her)] reflection carefully.
"Humans' tastes always shift," [xiaochou.gender] murmurs, lowering the mirror. "You've brought what should remain hidden into the open. I admire that."
And with that, [xiaochou.gender] walks away, the jewelry gleaming against [xiaochou.gender(his,her)] skin.

"Ha! What's this new toy?"
Nabhani eagerly lifts the cow-bone piece from your hand, holding it up and studying it closely for a long while.
"I think it would suit any beauty—those with skin dark as ebony, and those pale as moonlight... really, any beauty. Look how smooth it is... almost alive! And it even clings slightly to the hand, just like... a living touch."
After a cheerful farewell, he tucks the piece away and rushes off, eager to show it to every beauty he can find.

Jabal usually scoffs at trinkets, but you point out that this one is made of bone—and if he wears it well, perhaps he could put his own trophies to use in the same way.
Your words strike a chord. By the time you part ways, Jabal has already fastened the piece onto himself. The empire's martial nobles are sure to notice this subtle but telling change.

Faris laughs as he waves the piece away. "It'd be a waste to let me wear it—my dog would probably try to eat it! Such a shame when the carving's this beautiful!"
You suggest to Faris that he treat it as a little trick to make the dog like someone more—if someone isn't good with animals, just have them wear it, and they'll seem instantly more likable.
As for biting—there's nothing to worry about. Each piece is inlaid with gold, and well-trained hounds aren't so easily fooled. Anyone who can afford this jewelry certainly owns obedient, disciplined dogs. They won't touch it without permission.
Convinced, Faris rubs the piece, his eyes gleaming.
Just as he's about to leave, he asks, "Can the dogs wear it too?""Sure, sure," you reply, letting him have his fun.

Seliman accepts the piece without a word. Carefully, he wraps it in a thin veil of silk and tucks it close to his chest.
There's no need to ask—he clearly intends to smuggle it into the palace as an offering to her.
The women of the court are the keenest arbiters of fashion. It won't take long before they notice this unusual gem.

Lumera takes the ornament from your hand and fastens it on.
"What a curious feeling..." She sets aside her book, fingers brushing over its smooth surface. "It's like putting a veil over a star. Unlike any other jewel I've known."
Later, whenever Jenna promoted her bone jewelry, she would repeat Lumera's words:
Try this piece—wear it, and veil your stars."

Fatuna is uneasy about the bone trinket, calling it ill-omened. "Isn't it only the barbarians who wear such things?"
You raise your voice, insisting she has it wrong. The tribes wear bone for blessings—bone is bound to life, life to the gods, and the gods to mortal fate.
So this piece, too, can bring her blessings: for her children's health, for the years yet ahead, and for much more besides.
Silent now, Fatuna accepts the ornament and fastens it on. She runs her fingertips across it, and a faint smile touches her lips.
"What a warm jewel," she murmurs. "I thought gems were meant to be as cold and unyielding as life itself."

Faraj is only too happy to oblige. He fastens the piece at once, then hurries home to change into something to match it.
The fashion-savvy nobles are bound to notice his change soon.
Qais studies the piece with care. "The carving is exquisite. My mother always said jewelers are the finest of miniature sculptors... she'll love this." He thanks you with solemn courtesy.

Adila laughs as she takes the ornament from your hand.
"Who'd have thought the first piece of jewelry I'd get from a man would come in a place like this—and made of bone! It's gorgeous! Like a warrior wearing her trophy."
She slips it on and immediately asks if the jeweler can craft her other pieces too—knife hilts, sword scabbards, even thumb rings from the same bone.
With her approval, bone jewelry is certain to find a place among the city's fashion.

Whatever you like, Zaki likes as well.
He fastens the ornament proudly, then dashes off to show it to everyone. The delicate carving and subtle gold inlay draw admiration wherever he goes.

"Hmm... the workmanship is... well, not bad," Bharat mutters as he turns the piece in his hands. "Could you give me the address of this remarkable jeweler? I'd like to discuss a supply deal."
Ah, a true merchant indeed.
This single piece of jewelry has won admiration from them all.

5006159.title: Bone Craze
strings: Bone Craze
Thanks to your tireless efforts—and your friends'—bone jewelry sweeps through high society in no time! Jenna comes to see you, her delight impossible to hide.
Jenna visits.
You can meet her in person or send any follower in your stead.
As thanks, Jenna grants this character an extra accessory slot.

"All thanks to you! Bone jewelry is all the rage now! And I tell everyone that, among all the bones, the most expensive are from two-year-old male yellow cattle—they must have been fed on alfalfa and never mated... anyway, I made up a whole hierarchy of who's better than whom, who has the right to look down on whom. And the result? They're even happier to spend! That's the trick with gems, isn't it?"
Jenna laughs, holding the ornament up against [s2.name] as if determined to see it on [s2.gender]. While fussing with it, she presses three warm, ivory-white bones into your hand. "The best stock," she grins, "just as I decreed."

5006165.title: Lustrous Silk
strings: Lustrous Silk
Nayla gives you some silk, and its quality is excellent. But who will you give it to?
Silk
Who are you going to give it to?

When Nayla spots the shimmering fabric wrapped around Maggie's head, her rage nearly boils over. She almost tears it off then and there. Yet just as suddenly, something crosses her mind. A sly smile tugs at her lips as she sinks back onto her cushions, twirling a lock of her own hair. That same evening, a perfumed letter arrives on your desk: "When will it be her turn?"

Nayla looks a bit displeased with your taste in pairing the silk, but draping it over yourself greatly amuses her. She leaves a delicate kiss on your cheek, then giggles and urges you to hurry up and deal with the remaining women.

When you return the silk to Nayla, her brows knit in displeasure. "Do you think my gift beneath you?"
You wave your hands repeatedly, saying that the finest silk, of course, must be paired with the most beautiful woman. She laughs, the sound bright and triumphant, and at once commands her attendants to fashion the bolt into a new veil.
[s2.name] accepts the rare silk with a spark of joy. By the time [s2.gender] leaves, [s2.gender] already figured out how to use it to style [s2.gender(himself,herself)]!

5006166.title: Murder Check
strings: Murder Check
So... after Veesa blessed you, did you actually kill anyone? Really kill them? 'Cause if not? Veesa's gonna be pissed.
It grows stronger or acts out, depending on its mood.
Please frequently use Veesa in battles, or you will be punished.
A Bloody Good Job
Not Yet Enough...
Starving for Slaughter
Jinn's Story

The jinn gleefully lays out its collection before you: teeth, fingernails, eyeballs, half an ear still wearing its earring, and... a scrap of scalp! It's had quite the haul following you around. Master [player.name] you're so good at it! More blood! More kills!
As it revels in the gore, you sense its power swelling with every drop of glee...

Veesa, like a heartbroken child, curls around its favorite toy and rolls across your desk. "I haven't had enough playtime..." If the treasure clutched to its chest weren't a human eyeball, it might almost be convincing.
Perhaps you could try satisfying it next time. After all, jinns are creatures of emotion, and when they're happy, their power grows.

Veesa is thrashing in your hair, desperate, starving for kill, for blood, for battle. And you've given it nothing. Not a drop. The jinn is wilting! You can feel it, the sinking mood, the power draining away. And now, every time you try to talk to someone, it won't stop making lewd shapes under your robe. Gods. Jinns.

That night, the moon hung full and bright again. You'd already gone to bed, but through the window, you caught a glimpse of someone moving in the courtyard.
You stepped outside and saw clearly now: it was Veesa. She floated in midair, arms pillowing her head, mist swirling around her as she gazed contentedly at the moon. She turned, saw you, and smiled. "Come sit with me, Master." A light gesture, and your feet felt lighter too. You could float now.
Once you'd grown used to it, Veesa pointed at the moon, closer now, it seemed. "Queen sealed the three of us in the lamp. It was our punishment." Seeing your hesitation, she counted on her fingers. "Besides me, there's Endry and Iliona. We three committed the same crime, so we were exiled together to this material world."
You tell her you know this. After all, you were the one who brought the lamp back from the jinn's realm.
"What the Queen showed you is not what we truly are. In the magical domain, where no one disturbs, there is no matter. Only spirit. Only wish. Power belongs to whoever holds the strongest wish. Wish is where it all begins, and where it all ends. We don't need bodies to chain us to the ground. We can fly upward until we reach the end of our wishing." She sighed. Then you rose together, drifting higher... When you woke again, you were in your bed. But your clothes were wet with dew, the kind that only gathers in the courtyard.

5006167.title: Body Check
strings: Body Check
So... after Endry blessed you, did you actually indulge in carnality? 'Cause if not? Endry's gonna be pissed.
Endry
Yourself
Judged by the breaking of the Carnality Card
The Scent of Your Pleasure
Out of Steam?

Endry hungrily licks the magical residue of your Carnality Cards from your skin. According to it, the black magic inside the Sultan Card is like a spice to a jinn—irresistible. Though it might be the only one who thinks so.
Either way, you endure its demands with patience, letting it take what it needs. And in return, it breathes stronger Charmed Magic onto your face.

"What, you tapped out? A man who can't perform? Unacceptable. A total waste of the perfect blessing I gave you! Ever heard of 'use it or lose it'?"
Muttering these strange accusations, the jinn uses whirlwind hands and mouth to finish the job for you, until your legs can barely hold you.

That morning, you wake with a stiffness between your legs.
You try to roll out of bed, but something strange brushes against you down there. You throw off the silk sheet and find Endry, shrunk down to fit in a palm, nestled beside that part, poking and rubbing with obvious fascination.
"Ah, Master, you're awake?" She shows no shame whatsoever, beaming up at you. "Go back to sleep. I'm trying to give you a dream. In this material world, my magic works slowly..."
Her words pull you under. Your body grows heavy, as if matter itself drags thought downward.
In the dream, Endry shows her past "games" in full. Dozens of herself, all striving to stir desire in others, to squeeze every drop of pleasure from their bodies. "I was the jinn who understood the material world best. Once." Another Endry presses close, breath warm against your ear. "Because I know: flesh is matter. And the desires flesh breeds? They, too, are rooted in matter. The electricity that spikes along your spine, the signals that make you tremble... all matter." She pulls away, rejoining the others. They all gaze at you. "But our mistress scolded me for this. The jinn's realm despises matter. The mistress is the master of wishes, so she needs only think, and all bends to her will. She needs only speak her wish, and every jinn moves to make it so."

5006168.title: Mortal Gospel
strings: Mortal Gospel
For to everyone who has, more will be given, and they will have an abundance. But from the one who has not, even what they have will be taken away.
It promised a blessing. Now, it comes.
Now That's A Gold-getter!

Look! This is the power of blessing, the magic that only works in the human world. Iliona stares, entranced, at the dust shimmering in sunlight, watches it drift down onto your pile of gold coins, where each speck becomes a tiny, brand-new gold nugget. Later it'll shed its shell, grow larger, become real legal tender... Best. Magic. Ever. And you mean it.

5006169.title: Mortal Gospel
strings: Mortal Gospel
For to everyone who has, more will be given, and they will have an abundance. But from the one who has not, even what they have will be taken away.
Iliona
It promised a blessing. Now, it comes?
Their Mother Is Gone

"So... here's the thing..."
Iliona looks at you, awkward. "I did give you my blessing. Money makes money! Wealth attracts wealth!" It holds up a gold coin helplessly. It twitches, then sneezes out a burst of golden dust, and right before your horrified eyes, shrivels into a crumpled, broken husk. "See? That's human world magic for you. The less you have, the less you get. That's just how the blessing works. Nothing I can do about it."

5006170.title: Iliona's Story
strings: Iliona's Story
You've amassed a good fortune! Good. Maybe you're the one who can actually do this. Maybe you won't let Iliona down.
It's coming for you
A Taste for Grandeur

Iliona holds the cup with the most flawless, impeccable poise, its gaze that of a prince. "I was exiled from our world by a pitiless mistress. She crammed three exiles into one lantern. That alone is cruelty enough, forcing me to share space with those two vulgar, lowbred jinns." It takes another pretend sip of tea, performing aristocracy itself. "My crime? I suggested her displays of magnificence fell short. She was too cautious, too calculating. And the glorious things she possessed were far from enough. I merely offered this observation, and she took offense. A most unsatisfactory response."
You ask about jinn morality. "Morality? We have no need of such things. Our Mistress is the master of wishes. In our world, there is no matter, only thought. Her wishes shaped everything. When she stops wanting, what she once wished for simply collapses. A jinn's power grows with desire. The more we want, the stronger we become. And the stronger we are, the more we can take." It raises a hand, studying its lines, its curve, as if admiring a work of art. "I wanted more than my Mistress could give. How pathetic—I mean her." In silence, you two drained the last of the tea. And naturally, it all ended up in your belly.

5006171.title: Cage for Jinns
strings: Cage for Jinns
Two things can bind a jinn: pure gold, and bones with magic still in them. The graveyard always has some, if you look. Things buried. Forgotten.
Find a stealth ally to dig up the grave
Had the gold been pure, three coins would've sufficed...
Consumable
Avoid exposing the criminal evidence by passing a Stealth and Sociability check
Dig up the grave...
Your Stealth and Sociability determine the pool of dice.
You need at least 4 Success to avoid exposing the criminal evidence.
Mysterious Graveyard

Following the jinn's guidance, you come to a graveyard on the city's edge in that darkest hour just before dawn.
It doesn't belong to the Purist. So only the poor and outsiders without the faith's protection are buried here. You never even knew this place existed.
The jinn blesses your sight. Now you can see the faint glimmers beneath the graves, the shallow earth... You dig. And dig. Ducking behind crumbling headstones whenever the gravekeeper passes with his lantern...
The crumbling headstone, name long worn away. And when you pry open that glowing grave... Bones. Piled deep. Countless. Endless. As if the pit beneath has no bottom. As if you've punched through the crust of the world and glimpsed the peak of some hollow world's mountain.
Fear grips you. The gravekeeper could return any moment. You grab the nearest corpse, the one on top, and flee. The jinn, though, won't stop praising your choice. "Fine quality, this one."
After that, you search again and again. That graveyard is nowhere to be found. And the jinn, try as it might, can never quite explain what happened. To it, it's simple. Obvious. Just the way things are.

Following the jinn's guidance, you come to a graveyard on the city's edge in that darkest hour just before dawn.
It doesn't belong to the Purist. So only the poor and outsiders without the faith's protection are buried here. You never even knew this place existed.
The jinn blesses your sight. Now you can see the faint glimmers beneath the graves, the shallow earth... You dig. And dig. Ducking behind crumbling headstones whenever the gravekeeper passes with his lantern...
The crumbling headstone, name long worn away. And when you pry open that glowing grave... Bones. Piled deep. Countless. Endless. As if the pit beneath has no bottom. As if you've punched through the crust of the world and glimpsed the peak of some hollow world's mountain.
Just then, the gravekeeper comes back. You grab the nearest corpse, the one on top, and bolt. The jinn, though, won't stop praising your choice. "Fine quality, this one."
Days later, the High Constable comes asking about a grave robbery. But neither the man who reported it nor the graveyard they're talking about is the one you went to. And the jinn, try as it might, can never quite explain what happened. To it, it's simple. Obvious. Just the way things are.
Grave Mistakes

Following the jinn's guidance, you come to a graveyard on the city's edge in that darkest hour just before dawn.
It doesn't belong to the Purist. So only the poor and outsiders without the faith's protection are buried here. You never even knew this place existed.
The jinn blesses your sight. Now you can see the faint glimmers beneath the graves, the shallow earth... You dig. And dig. Ducking behind crumbling headstones whenever the gravekeeper passes with his lantern...
When the light fades, you glimpse a name on a stone. The grave of — [player.name]! Panic takes you. You tear the grave open, hands shaking, because the corpse inside... it looks exactly like [player.name]!
The gravekeeper hears. He's running at you now, lantern raised. And in its light, his face is the spitting image of Lord [player.name] when angry! No time to think. You grab the body and run, blind with fear... until, somehow, you stumble back onto familiar streets. By sunrise, the corpse crumbles. All that's left is a ribcage forged of pure gold, a cage, perfect for your needs.
After that, you search again and again. That graveyard is nowhere to be found. And the jinn, try as it might, can never quite explain what happened. To it, it's simple. Obvious. Just the way things are.

5006172.title: The Crossroads
strings: The Crossroads
Every crossroad is a place where fate, wish, and magic meet. Every crossroad is a place where past, present, and future meet.
It waits on the path you are fated to walk
Only those who have walked the same fork countless times may witness it
Jinn
8-Gold-Coin Consumable
The flowers blooming at the crossroads are flames lit by the you of the past.
Her coming was destined in the past, called upon in the present, and promised in the future.
Perhaps it will take the power of other jinns; perhaps not this time...
I already have a flower that belongs to me.
Golden Blossom
Purple Blossom
Green Blossom

Iliona leads you to this place. An ordinary crossroads, it seems, the kind soon to be swallowed by the wilds.
"You know, summoning the Queen might not work on the first try..." The jinn darts irritably around the crossing. "Don't look at me like I'm some kind of swindler! It's about whether you were ready before, and whether the future's ready too. Ah, see that road? No flower there. That's no good. Means 'now' isn't the time to summon her."
Still muttering things you don't understand, it ignites, calling forth flames in the air. The very fire that once held it prisoner in the lamp. The flame drifts down, touching earth. Where it lands, a golden flower blooms, radiant, delicate. And when Iliona emerges from its heart, the spaces between worlds shudder, spilling pure Dew of Aether.
You have no idea what just happened. But Iliona declares the ritual a triumph. Try making sense of jinns.

Endry leads you to this place. An ordinary crossroads, it seems, the kind soon to be swallowed by the wilds.
"You know, summoning the Queen might not work on the first try..." The jinn darts irritably around the crossing. "Don't look at me like I'm some kind of swindler! It's about whether you were ready before, and whether the future's ready too. Ah, see that road? No flower there. That's no good. Means 'now' isn't the time to summon her."
Still muttering things you don't understand, it ignites, calling forth flames in the air. The very fire that once held it prisoner in the lamp. The flame drifts down, touching earth. Where it lands, a purple flower blooms, radiant, delicate. And when Endry emerges from its heart, the spaces between worlds shudder, spilling pure Dew of Aether.
You have no idea what just happened. But Endry declares the ritual a triumph. Try making sense of jinns.

Veesa leads you to this place. An ordinary crossroads, it seems, the kind soon to be swallowed by the wilds.
"You know, summoning the Queen might not work on the first try..." The jinn darts irritably around the crossing. "Don't look at me like I'm some kind of swindler! It's about whether you were ready before, and whether the future's ready too. Ah, see that road? No flower there. That's no good. Means 'now' isn't the time to summon her."
Still muttering things you don't understand, it ignites, calling forth flames in the air. The very fire that once held it prisoner in the lamp. The flame drifts down, touching earth. Where it lands, a green flower blooms, radiant, delicate. And when Veesa emerges from its heart, the spaces between worlds shudder, spilling pure Dew of Aether.
You have no idea what just happened. But Veesa declares the ritual a triumph. Try making sense of jinns.
Three Flowers at the Crossroads

You follow the jinn's guidance to the crossroads. Three vivid blossoms already bloom there, one on each path. You have claimed wish, power, and fate as your own. The roads of the past, present, and future now stand sealed behind you. [s5.name] knows the moment has come, and begins to chant the incantation not of this world.
The three flowers become three flames, converging at the crossroads into a single blossom, larger and lovelier, more vivid than any before. It shall be the Queen of Jinn's body in the material world.

The crossroads [s5.name] has brought you to... This is not your first time here, is it? You have come here countless times before. You will pass through here countless times again. The flowers themselves are proof. And now you walk the path called "present," where the roads meet. You have claimed wish, power, and fate as your own. The moment has come.
[s5.name] chants the incantation, rekindling the flame that once belonged to it, the very flame that held it prisoner in the lamp. In answer, the other two flowers ignite. At the crossroads, their flames converge into a single blossom, larger and lovelier, more vivid than any before. It shall be the Queen of Jinn's body in the material world.

5006173.title: Plead with the Queen
strings: Plead with the Queen
The great Queen of Jinn is coming into this world. Offer her gifts, kneel and kiss her toes, or... set a trap.
The Flame Bearer severs the Queen's magic.
The Wind Wielder shields everyone from the Queen's enchantment.
The Filth Caster breaks the jinn's magic.
The Lamp Keeper completes the seal.
Veesa trembles
Endry is eager to try
Iliona stays quiet
That mysterious vessel
An offering rare enough, or the nectar of the Spirit Realm
Consumable
Either offer a sacrifice, or stand against her!
Confronting the Queen of Jinn head-on requires sufficient Wisdom and Magic manpower, and a well-prepared cage.
The jinns will witness this summoning
Burn the flower to cut off its power

When the Queen's flower blooms at the crossroads, you are ready. The jinn rasps a word, a syllable that cannot exist in the mortal world.
In answer, the flower unfurls with impossible speed. And with it come strange music, drifting lights, strange scents... and thoughts, elegant thoughts, flooding your mind. You reel, overwhelmed, while the jinn kneels before the bloom.
Bud, blossom, harvest... Flower to fruit in a heartbeat. The fruit's skin bristles with thorns. Its calyx hangs heavy. Then, as if exploding, the ripe fruit splits open, flesh crimson and raw, and within, the Queen of Jinn is revealed.
"Who? Who dared to..." The Queen's voice is a harp, a song. Her body fits in a perfume bottle. She floats in the air, borne on the backs of two winged attendants, and gazes down at you with a haughty stare. "What is this? This sticky touch... revolting. You dared summon me to the material world with these lowly creatures? Then die. My wish is this: that you suffer a thousand and a hundred and eleven deaths, each in agony." At last, those eyeless eyes turn to you. Mortals. Are you ready to receive the Queen?

Before defiance can harden into words, the world itself shifts... literally. You stand in a forest. Fireflies drift past. Mushrooms nudge up through the soil. The scent of grass and tuberose surrounds you. "Did you think a queen could only rule from her throne, flesh-bound mortal?" The voice comes from above. You look up. The Queen towers over you now, vast as a mountain, gazing down. "Even here, in this wretched place weighted by flesh, I can crush you effortlessly. And then I will draw out that rebellious mind of yours and stitch it into my bedcurtains. Each night, before I sleep, you will sing me a song of despair."
The others from the summoning ritual fling magic wildly in all directions. But the Queen's will has already carried them to another world. A world shaped entirely by her wish.

Before defiance can harden into words, the world itself shifts... literally. You stand in a forest. Fireflies drift past. Mushrooms nudge up through the soil. The scent of grass and tuberose surrounds you. "Did you think a queen could only rule from her throne, flesh-bound mortal?" The voice comes from above. You look up. The Queen towers over you now, vast as a mountain, gazing down. "Even here, in this wretched place weighted by flesh, I can crush you effortlessly. And then I will draw out that rebellious mind of yours and stitch it into my bedcurtains. Each night, before I sleep, you will sing me a song of despair."
Flowers, trees and shadows all surge wild, lunging to devour the bold summoners. But then [s1.name]'s flame ray lashes out, striking true. Piercing the one weakness: the hidden blossom, the flower that brought her to this world.
As flames consume it, everything snaps back to normal. You stand again in the sickening material world. And the Queen? Now she must fight you fair!

The Queen stirs the light upon herself. It scatters on the wind, settling around you, upon you.
Then every mortal and jinn freezes like puppets with cut strings. One by one, they begin to transform according to the Queen's whims: into pets, trinkets, lotions, and patches of moss upon the ground... And in their hearts, each believes, truly, deeply, that this is what they have been since the dawn of creation.

The Queen stirs the light upon herself. It scatters on the wind, drifting around you... But [s2.name] calls forth a gale, forming a barrier of wind just in time. Now you see it with your own eyes: a tree, touched by that glowing dust, twists and warps into an eyelash curler. The Queen of Jinn remakes the world around her with her own wish, unchecked, unopposed. You have to stop her!

Now the Queen is serious. She wants you dead. She speaks her wishes, one after another.
She wishes air and water and earth and sky to turn against you. She wishes every element to see you as an enemy. She wishes your veins, your eyes, your bones, and your very flesh to be torn apart.
You are merely mortal. Against this endless tide of annihilation, what can you do? And so the foolish summoners crumble to ash beneath her will. The Queen will carry that ash back to her world. It will become a cream for her skin, or a toy for her evening entertainments.

Now the Queen is serious. She wants you dead. She speaks her wishes, one after another.
She wishes air and water and earth and sky to turn against you. She wishes every element to see you as an enemy. She wishes your veins, your eyes, your bones, and your very flesh to be torn apart.
As the world is falling apart, [s3.name] hurls a basin of boiling filth at the Queen. Jinn's magic springs from wishes, taste, and a certain sense of what is beautiful. And this ordure, steeped in concentrated magic, is one of the few things in the world their power cannot touch.
Somewhere, the world groans, a sound like eggshells cracking. And then the visions, the destruction, the glowing dust, all of it shatters beneath that scalding tide.

A pity, you miss the moment when the magic is broken. The Queen of Jinn, with grace you cannot fathom and fury you cannot measure, dances. Sings. Recites. Then she wishes it all into a weapon. An instant.
While all are still lost in the perfection of her dance and song, their heads begin to fall. The Queen herself, in haste, flees this world of filth.

The Queen of Jinn recoils, desperate, dodging your filthy tricks. And in that instant, [s4.name] raises the cage, speaking the incantation.
A sharp crack rings out, ribs snap shut, gold surges and swirls. And so the corpse that existed before, exists now, and will exist always, shall become the Queen of Jinn's eternal vessel.

Veesa lunges forward, unable to wait another second. A sewing needle in hand, it jabs at the Queen's ankle... And then it is lost, utterly lost, in the bliss of sucking at that needle's tip. The Queen's curses are ignored. No, savored by it.
The traces of countless carnality unfurl before the Queen like pages of a book... Wait, hold on. When did it and... Cursed Jinn!
Iliona keeps showering the Queen with golden dust, blessing after blessing after blessing. It has been craving for this forever.

Of course you prepared a gift for the Queen. Only a fool trusts jinns and picks a fight with a powerful being from beyond.
You kneel, arms raised, offering it up. The Queen taps the servant beneath her foot, just lightly, with her toe. The servant darts forward at once and accepts your tribute. The moment the tiny creature touches your gift, it begins to shrink... until its size fits the Queen perfectly.
"This is a mortal world thing? This... sinking feeling in my hand... What is this feeling? Ah. Weight. Is this what they call weight?"
The Queen turns your gift over in her hands as her gaze slides across your face. She's playing with you, weighing you. It feels like a thousand arms pressing against you, like hips and breasts the size of mountains crushing in...
You're about to break. Fall apart. Suffocate. Then the Queen looks away. "Good. I'm pleased. An amusing trinket. I could draw out the thoughts within and place them in my museum... Yes. You are forgiven, mortals who summoned me."
Before leaving the material world, the Queen casts her wish upon Veesa. It will serve this world now, forever and ever, bound through past and future alike. Its fate has been rewritten.
Before leaving the material world, the Queen casts her wish upon Endry. It will serve this world now, forever and ever, bound through past and future alike. Its fate has been rewritten.
Before leaving the material world, the Queen casts her wish upon Iliona. It will serve this world now, forever and ever, bound through past and future alike. Its fate has been rewritten.

Veesa sprawls beside the Queen's cage, gazing long at the mistress it once served. Veesa looks utterly happy, chattering on and on about battles, about this and that. The Queen turns her back, ignoring Veesa.
This scene plays out again and again, but Veesa never tires of it.

To show its gratitude, Endry approaches the cage and sheds the mortal clothes from its body, baring the jinn's desire...
The Queen watches coldly, giving nothing in return. And this is exactly the response Endry craves.

Iliona receives the Queen's blessing and hurries straight to her cage. "I thought you found me unworthy. But here you are, stooping to bestow such a favor upon me. Truly, I am grateful." It drones on and on, half praise, half poison, for what feels like an age. The Queen says nothing, pretending not to see it.

Badriyyah admires the Queen of Jinn's power and enjoys chatting with her, too. She tells the Queen about other beings summoned from other worlds. How badly they fared. How some were even eaten. The Queen, listening, seems to feel a little better.

Nabhani is absolutely captivated by the tiny Queen. He doesn't even care about the powerful blessing she gave him. He just wanted to know if she could reach full size. When he finds out she can, his face lights up. "Why not let her out of the cage?" he murmurs. "She's so elegant... simply perfect!"
You offer a grim description of the Queen's lethal grace on the battlefield.
"Oh. Oof... well then." Nabhani strokes his chin, returning his focus to the beautiful, if terrifying, Queen.

Lumera faces the tiny Queen. They gaze at each other in silence. For one moment, you glimpse something between them: a war that never was, a clash of wills, wishes colliding... Then Lumera leaves, bearing the Queen's blessing. Still, neither has spoken a word.

Maggie adores the tiny Queen for her beauty and delicacy. She visits often, bringing flowers each time. So when the Queen's blessing falls upon her, it surprises no one. But Maggie herself doesn't seem to notice.

Fatuna is genuinely surprised to receive the blessing. She brings the Queen fine fruits and expensive, delicate ribbons. "A proper thanks," she says.
The Queen reluctantly accepts these crude, material offerings.
Zaki is thrilled, over the moon, that the Queen blessed him. But you know what really gets him going? His teacher can command a Queen from another world! His teacher can do anything!

Jabal accepts the blessing. Then he finds you and asks, "Can you let the Queen of Jinn out? If she's this powerful locked up, trapped in our world, imagine what she could do free." He strokes his chin, eyeing the cage. "Let her out. Let her fight me." You have him escorted from your estate. And you tell the servants: this one is not to enter the Queen's room. Ever.

Arzuna gazes at the Queen for a long, long time. Just gazing. "You're like me," you hear her whisper. "Trapped. Aren't you?" The Queen, of course, offers no reply. Arzuna glances at you, guilt written plain across her face. You walk over and tell her, "Don't even think about letting the little prisoner go, or she might kill everyone." Arzuna leaves with the Queen's blessing, sulking.

Asal is beside himself with excitement over the blessing. Pen and paper in hand, he rushes to the Queen's cage. "What's your world called? Does it have directions? How many inhabitants? How do you reproduce? Do you mate? What are your naming conventions? Oh, sorry... too many questions. I just want to learn as much as I can..."
The Queen has had enough. In the end, she musters what power remains and conjures a shroud of darkness, veiling the entire cage. She may be starting to regret blessing a bookstore owner quite so curious.

Jawad is thrilled. A blessing for free didn't cost him a single coin! Now he's trying to convince the Queen to sell her powerful blessings. The Queen, naturally, wants none of it. But he won't let up. In the end, you have to call the guards to drag him out.

Inal is startled, genuinely terrified. How did she suddenly become so powerful? What just happened? The Queen's blessing? Who's the Queen? Does the blessing cost money? Why give it to me and not some noble lord? Is this really okay? Before she can drown the Queen in questions, you escort her from the room. The Queen, for her part, slumps against the silk cushion Inal sewed for her, a token of thanks, and sighs a long, deep sigh.
"I sense... something trying to strengthen my existence." That is all [xiaochou.name] has to say about the blessing. [xiaochou.gender] feels no need to visit the Queen.

Faraj documents everything. The feeling of receiving the blessing, its effects, its consequences, on and on. He visits the Queen, too. Circles her, noting every detail: her clothes, her features, her posture, her words. All of it. After he leaves, the Queen watches his retreating back, thoughtful. "So. He is your scribe?" she asks. She rarely speaks to you like this. "Be careful, then. All scribes are loyal only to the king they record, the king in their minds. That king is often very different from the one who sits before them." Now it's your turn to be thoughtful.

Nayla is overjoyed. You've gotten her such a rare blessing. She's going to show it off like crazy!
Too bad the Queen's blessing literally rewrites reality. However much she's improved, everyone else simply assumes she's always been this good. Which means it's like nothing changed at all, doesn't it? She complains to you about it for an entire week.

Shama strips, nervous and tense, and makes you examine every inch. She won't have anyone "adjusting" things behind her back. Fingers. Breasts. Chin. Eyelashes. Calves. And then, of course, her two... lower parts. She asks you again and again: any different from before?
Junah believes she does not deserve the blessing. She begs the Queen to stop choosing someone so lowly. The Queen offers no answer.

Jalila received the Queen's blessing. Of all people, who would have thought? But perhaps, to the Queen of Jinn's eyes, Jalila, who wields a whip and rules the desires of others, is worthy to serve at her side.
Faris is startled by the sudden blessing. He keeps asking you, "Can the blessing be given to a dog?" The Queen refuses, fumingly.

The Queen's blessing descends upon Adila, catching her by surprise. After you explain what happened, she insists on meeting the tiny Queen face-to-face. "Oh, a ruler from another world. And you're so small. So... cute." The Queen's gaze turns to ice. She speaks a vicious wish, and Adila's finger, the one reaching out to tease her, burns with a sudden, searing pain. "Tch—ow! Wow. She's strong. If we let her out... she could fight, couldn't she?" You push her out before she can say another word.
Raed loves the blessing. It makes her stronger, gives her more ways to protect what must be protected. She sends the Queen a gift: a long strand of pearls, perfect for adorning the cage.

Raed comes specially to see this "little thing that suddenly blessed me." She stares at the Queen. Stares until the Queen grows irritated. Then, suddenly, she smiles. "So beautiful," she says. "A queen from another world, and you're this beautiful. Are all jinns as lovely as you?" Clearly, she has pleased the Queen. The two of them chat happily for some time.
Hassan composes a line about the blessing: "Blessings are cages, locking us in loyalty." The Queen admires the verse.

Fardak startles at the blessing. It reminds him of something... "Back home, this happens sometimes. A young person, blessed by some unknown god..." He sighs, gazing at the Queen. "Those young ones usually die soon after. Tell me, lovely, beautiful, noble Queen, will I too?" The Queen smiles, gazing at him, looking elegant and serene. Across the cage, their noses nearly touch. You grab Fardak and pull him from the room.
Qais sends word: some Queen he's never heard of just blessed him, out of nowhere. And he doesn't like this "unjust, unpublic, untransparent business."

Alim loves this whole blessing business. "So even the poor can be blessed... Heh. Heh. Heh. Guess this Queen's better than the others... Heh." He brings a pack of street pups to see the Queen. The children are delighted.

[s2.name] feels it in a dream: that mysterious pull, that elevation. [s2.gender] rises from bed in haste and comes seeking the mysterious Queen.
The Queen, as always, says nothing. As if she already knows the outcome. Already knows the price.

As the blessing takes hold, the Queen's light dims, but you know she will recover before long.
(The Queen's blessing can be used once every five days.)

By the time you catch up to the Queen, she has already carried the victims too far. They stand at the crossroads now, that place of summoning, the one you could never find again.
Flowers erupt from the earth like an explosion. The air thickens with dust and petals, a fragrance so rich it drowns. And then, at last, the shadows of everyone fade into that floral sea... Only the Queen's cruel laughter remains.

You follow the trail of footprints and scattered petals, and corner the Queen of Jinn and the people she has beguiled. She means to perform the ritual again at the crossroads to return to her own world. Lucky for you, the enchanted ones have lost their wits. They fumble at simple tasks, clumsy and slow, obeying her frantic commands. You reach them before the ritual is complete.
The Queen hides her dominion deep within the blessing, a backdoor to their souls. Cracking this spell means finding the key to every door. One by one. Looks like you'll have to do this the hard way.

The Queen hides her dominion deep within the blessing, a backdoor to their souls. Cracking this spell means finding the key to every door. One by one.
In the end, she takes them all. Flees to her own world with everyone in tow. If only you hadn't been so greedy for her blessings. If only you'd brought more people.

The most powerful mind magic in the world is no match for a solid wooden club. You signal your people. Blows rain down, and the poor victims slump, unconscious. The Queen's cage is back in your hands. She curses your shamelessness, your ruthlessness to strike even your own people.

No time to explain. You summon a tornado, sweeping everyone into the sky. The jinn's glowing dust, the magic, the ritual... all of it.
You strain, stretch, catch the precious cage of the Queen as it falls, while the others are not so fortunate.

The Queen hides her dominion deep within the blessing, a backdoor to their souls. Cracking this spell means finding the key to every door. One by one. Lucky for you, you know your companions. You know the weak spots in their souls. With a magical shout from [s8.name], right on the head, everyone snaps awake and stops in their tracks. Now only the Queen of Jinn remains, still commanding and urging from her cage. What a naughty little jinn. You'll have to be more careful when you use her power from now on.

5006501.title: Crusade against the clan
strings: Crusade against the clan
You need to produce a Conquest Card to gain the right to level the territory where that clan resides.
You must use a Conquest Card no higher than Bronze.
Must use a Conquest Card no higher than Bronze.

The Sultan quickly grew impatient. You failed to produce the card that grants you Conquest rights, and you dared to fool him! Seeing the Sultan's sullen face, the Nobles showered you with insults. You... what can you say?
You present the Conquest Card before the Sultan.

He gladly agrees to your request, sending out a troop of elite soldiers. Under your leadership, this disrespecting clan is permanently erased from the world.

5006502.title: Forcefully Seizing the Withering Flower
strings: Forcefully Seizing the Withering Flower
You cannot marry Fatuna, but you covet her beautiful body. You decide to possess her, to forcefully take this nearly withered yet still fragrant flower. You know she cannot refuse you.
Fatuna is waiting for your response.
You have to handle this yourself.
You can use this to break a Carnality Card.
If you wish to break a Carnality Card, this matter will become public.
She originally thought you brought good news.

The room is filled with exquisite incense, a faint sweet scent hovering between you. You kiss her lips, silencing her troubling questions, wrapping your hands around her slim waist. As expected, she does not resist.
The delicate silk carpet and gold-embroidered cushions embrace you, feeling like a maiden's bare skin. You remove the veil from Fatuna's hair and kiss her gently under the lamp. Think about it, she shows no mercy to other nobles! But you... you are different.
 You saved her, you killed for her, you are her hero... She must love you, how could she not?
 You strip away her dress, feeling the burning heat on this mature and voluptuous body. Her hand on your chest loses its strength to resist, becoming a soft silk ribbon. See, how can she not love you? You harvest this ripe and succulent fruit, embracing her passionately, over and over, admiring her trembling back.
What an intoxicating night. When the candles go out, dawn light slowly spreads. Cold dark blue touches your weary brow. You don't notice that the visions of adoration that were once in Fatuna's tearful eyes have now faded. You are no different from other men.
You broke one Carnality Card
This event was done very secretly.

Publicly, you tell the story of you and Fatuna, in an indifferent, even slightly proud tone, describing how you seduced a widow to surrender her passionate love. The ministers are stunned, now everyone knows about your affair, even Fatuna's children have heard it... And you, the monster of lust growing within you is finally satisfied, you don't care at all.

You didn't mention that night to anyone, and if Fatuna is wise, neither will she. As expected, when you see her again, she remains dignified, reserved, and distant, as if that night's affair never happened.

5006503.title: The Poisonous Fruit
strings: The Poisonous Fruit

At dinner this evening, your wife sits beside you, takes your cup, sips it lightly, then whispers to you, 'Dear, I have something to say to you... but not here.'
You excitedly grasp her fingers. Oh, has the day finally come? Maggie is always so considerate, and Fatuna is so clever... How did Fatuna convince Maggie? She truly loves you... You feel a sense of intoxication, not from the many drinks tonight, but from the happiness that is now within reach... a happy life with Maggie and Fatuna!
Maggie wants to talk to you
You are the protagonist of this scene
Fatuna, who appeared out of nowhere
Zaki, who appeared out of nowhere

Maggie smiles as she leads you into the bathroom. The steam rising from the pool creates an intimate warmth on her face. The sweet scent of roses floats ambiguously, and Maggie helps you take off your outer robe, scrubs your back, and brings you a cup of tea brewed with cloves and a good bottle of wine.
In the steaming mist, you drink wine happily, sip tea, and caress her smooth skin. The steam seems to seep into your skin through your pores, and soon you feel a dreamy daze come over you...
A pair of slender hands gently stroke the top of your head, then those hands mercilessly push your head underwater! Wait, wait a minute...! Something's wrong! You struggle desperately, the will to survive nearly pulls you out of the tub, but another pair of hands climbs up like seaweed, tightly wrapping around your neck, and a younger pair of hands presses firmly on your back like a stone that won't budge. You can't breathe anymore, dizzy and weak. In the despair of near-death, you hear Fatuna's soft and vague voice, as if from the sky.
“I will share everything with you, Maggie, whether good or bad... this guy doesn't deserve you!”

What are they plotting? Are they shy about you overhearing? You suddenly recall Fatuna's earlier proposal, and your heart races. She must have been conquered by your charm. She still wants to marry you, doesn't she? She must have convinced Maggie.
You can't help but smile and let Maggie, who is also smiling, lead you to the bathhouse.

You prepared a string of honeyed words to make Maggie happy before revealing your true intention. However, Maggie remained cold-faced. Don't you know what you've done before? She's seen through you, this damned, disappointing man.
Seeing this, you quickly swallowed back the intention to marry Fatuna. Are you kidding? You don't want to lose Maggie over this trivial matter. You still rely on her for managing the estate, buying books, and negotiating with others... She is still of great use!

You prepared a string of honeyed words, finally making Maggie smile. Then, taking advantage of the situation, you revealed your true intention, telling Maggie about your desire to marry Fatuna.
Maggie was stunned. She widened her eyes, making sure you weren't joking, and then angrily stood up. She incredulously yelled for you not to even think about it and stormed into the room, locking the door behind her.
All right... even if you stubbornly marry Fatuna, no one will be willing to face Maggie’s reaction. You can only brace yourself and tell Fatuna the result. Fatuna silently nodded, showing no sign of regret or resentment, and returned to her usual composure. A peaceful life continuing like this isn't bad either. She keeps a clear line with you, but you notice that Fatuna still drinks tea with Maggie.

Maggie was persuaded by you. After a brief shock, she fell into deep thought: “She indeed is a pitiful person, and I do like her – of course, as a friend... Moreover, her family background is distinguished enough to match your lineage... But what do you think of it? You are the master of this house; you indeed have the right to marry another wife. But if you must ask for my opinion, I can only say she is not the worst choice, and I respect my man's decision.”
She looked straight at you, as if trying to see through your eyes into your heart and soul.
Reminds you of the absurd acts with Zaki and Fatuna.

As you were about to speak, you suddenly remembered the time at the bathhouse... that unexpected, unforgettable threesome with you, Fatuna, and her son... The rose-scented mist seemed to fill your nostrils once again. You began to wonder if you could really marry Fatuna and live under the same roof with Maggie, Fatuna, and Zaki...
The complex and immoral entanglement made you shiver as you couldn't decide whether you were yearning or dreading it. Nonetheless, this secret affair, not accepted by the world, made you lose the courage to openly propose to marry Fatuna to your wife.

strings: Two Ladies

You told Fatuna you would possess her completely, in every sense of the word.
Double Blessing

When bringing the second wife into the household, there was no need for an extravagant wedding. You held a simple parade, loudly announcing your union to everyone. After the necessary feasts and socializing, you took Fatuna away. That night, you fully relished the sweetness of this juicy and delightful fruit.
Afterwards, no matter how generous Maggie tried to be, she remained cold towards you two for several days, while Fatuna knelt earnestly before her every day, holding her legs and promising to serve her. Gradually, they started having tea together again.
This marriage earned you considerable support from the nobles, and of course, a lot of wealth. Zaki is now your son, and his prestige in the palace has also increased.
Marriage is truly a wonderful thing, you sigh inwardly, unable to stop wishing for more... But you can only imagine, now that there are two pairs of eyes watching you closely...

Although generally, the second wife’s entrance should not be so extravagant, you still organized an extremely lavish and opulent wedding that made all women envious and all men jealous.
You held a grand parade, taking Fatuna through every decorated street of the city before arriving at a huge open space to announce your union to everyone. You also spent a fortune on the best band, dancers, and singers, and all the guests at this grand event were laughing and blessing your marriage.
This unseemly wedding made Maggie very jealous and she ignored you for a long time, while Fatuna knelt before her every day, holding her legs and promising to serve her. Gradually, they started having tea together again.
This marriage brought you Fatuna's generous dowry, and the city nobles began to curry favor with you and Zaki – now recognized as your son. Some of them even brought their daughters... But you could only politely decline their advances. These twin pairs of scrutinizing eyes were now a constant reminder...

The Sultan never holds grand celebrations for concubines newly added to his harem. He only parades in triumph for conquests and victories – after all, how could a trophy deserve its own feast?

Now, watching you bask in the blessings of others, he reluctantly allows you to break an Extravagance Card.

Through the crowd, the gentlemen sing, the ladies dance, and the children scramble for candy. The servants wave colorful torches, clearing a path for the banquet's final dish.

Traditionally, this would be grand dish – a roasted camel, cow, or sheep. Each guest receives a piece of meat, symbolizing shared joy and blessings.

However, this time, the dish is covered with a massive, shiny copper pot – it seems smaller than expected. A strange odor fills the air, halting the singing and dancing as all eyes turn anxiously to the covered dish...

As the copper pot is lifted, silence shatters into screams. At the center of the plate lie the severed heads of Fatuna and Zaki, painted with festive makeup and draped in their finest jewelry. 

Blood pools beneath their heads, soaking the sliced cold cuts arranged like flowers – a jagged, beautiful yet mesmerizing scene.

Under your blade, the guests shudder helplessly. One by one, they gingerly lift the petals, forcing the blood-soaked flesh past their trembling lips – bearing in the wedding's twisted blessing. 

As the feast concludes and all have savored their fill, the Sultan himself breaks the Bloodshed Card card, highly praising your artistry.

Her entire family comes, each one of them. Of course this would happen – through her, the family has achieved an alliance with a powerful courtier! Finally, this woman has done something beneficial for the family... One by one, they step forward, offering congratulations more stale than halitosis... Ah, surrounded by these parasites, how could one breath free?

Fortunately, you have never intended to humble yourself – your love for Fatuna is going to be long-lasting. You won't let these dirty family ties rip your marriage and life apart like barbs... certainly not like her previous husband, whose life was threatened.

Thus, you personally fill each of their cups with a specially made fine liquor, even preparing preserves and candy for the children and infants...

After ensuring the liquor and delicaciesare consumed, you tightly embrace Fatuna and Zaki – your wife and son.

They stiffen in your arms, trembling like cornered prey, but they cannot escape your warm, strong arms. They watch as their relatives collapse one by one, foaming at the mouth, blood spurting from their ears and noses.

When the last body hits the ground, and silence blankets the room, you raise your hands, break the card in two, and declare to the stunned guests the extermination and conquest of a noble lineage.

From then on, everything that once belonged to this family now belongs to your wife and son – and they, in turn, belong to you.

At the peak of the celebration, tradition dictates that you take your bride on a luxurious carriage to tour your lands – fulfilling the ancient ritual of blessing the fertile soil through carnal union. 
The young men are in a frenzy; at this moment, even a powerful courtier like you and your wives aren't spared from their bawdy jokes. People shower you with spiced wheat and petals, shouting names of sexual positions, and you even hear some placing bets... 
But they'll all lose their wagers today – instead of only pulling the bride onto the carriage, you grab Maggie with your other hand. Why not? What's the point of having two wives if you can't enjoy them together? Perhaps in the future, there will be many annoying things, but today – at least today – no one can deny your desires. 
The carriage races through your domain; rich and lush fields spread on both sides, all yours now... They're worth your madness and tireless plowing, even if you might not live to see the harvest... 
This proves an exceptionally successful blessing ritual. The Sultan praises you as a model nobleman, not only allowing you to break a Carnality Card but also making an unprecedented decree – granting a year's tax exemption to all fields along your carriage route.
