strings: The Only Flower in the Garden
You couldn't bring up Fatuna's proposal, and Maggie seemed oblivious to it. Perhaps moved by your sweet words, she has been smiling more often lately.
Maggie Has Been Pacified
What Repulsion could she still harbor against you?

After telling Fatuna about this, she slightly lowered her head, hiding her face behind an expensive veil, saying nothing more. However, soon you noticed Fatuna still frequently appearing in your salon, having tea and chatting with Maggie, maintaining their usual friendship.
You observed for some time, sure that nothing had changed, and finally felt relieved. Moreover, you hadn’t actually done anything wrong to Maggie... Missing the chance to marry a noble widow might have cost you some wealth, but holding your wife in those nights made you sleep a little more soundly.

5006508.title: Silent Conversation
strings: Silent Conversation

Zaki sat there silently, like a drenched chick, looking somewhat despondent. He was in urgent need of someone to help and guide him, yet the mother he once trusted most was now mired in deep suspicion... Should you summon Fatuna to confront him, or let Maggie comfort Zaki, who always had a way...
Zaki doesn't know what to do
You can enlighten Zaki personally because you are his trusted mentor
Perhaps the meticulous-minded Maggie can help
Maybe calling Fatuna to have an open talk would be a good idea?
You can place any Character you deem necessary for this conversation.
No one plans to explain all this to the young man. He does not cry out, but what lies behind this silence?
Fatuna is already your wife
You called both Maggie and Fatuna here
You briefly explained the situation to Maggie, and Zaki presented the evidence to her.
You left matters to Maggie and Fatuna to resolve
You called Fatuna for a confrontation
You chose to comfort him alone
You left it to Maggie
You decide to leave the space for this mother and child

After seeing the old letter paper in her son's hands, Fatuna is silent for a moment, then looks up at you, as if asking what you mean.
She is now your wife, Zaki is her child and also your child, and of course you do not want to lose either. So you try to resolve the situation. You take the young man's cold hand and place it in Fatuna's pale palm. "Let bygones be bygones, there's no point, Zaki. She is your mother," you pause, emphasizing, "We are a family." 
The young man stares wide-eyed at you, incredulous. He wants to pull back his hand, wants to refute something, but ultimately does nothing, says nothing. 
He presses his lips tightly and lowers his head, abandoning the pursuit of that cruel answer, abandoning the question that torments you: what true justice is. However, the persistent doubts fester in his heart, turning into an unhealable sore that aches with every midnight recollection for the rest of his life.

After seeing the old letter paper in her son's hands, Fatuna had remained silent for a long time before sighing as if finally relieved.
"Yes, if you must ask, I gave him tea brewed from cloves, then gave him wine, and after that, my brother pressed his head into the bath." Fatuna said calmly, looking straight at you. 
"But why... why? Father indeed had a mistress... but... that's not a crime worthy of death!" The young noble cried hoarsely, tears welling from his eyes. 
"You didn't sentence him to death, my dear child, I know," Fatuna looked at Zaki gently, but her words were harsh, "But I did. I sentenced your father to death. That's how it is, I admit my crime." 
"Don't say that." Maggie squeezed her hand tightly, then looked at Zaki, "She did it for you, son. She—" 
"Don't, Maggie, don't." Fatuna tried to interrupt her several times, but Maggie continued to speak gently yet firmly, holding her cold and trembling hand, "Isn't it clear in the letter? Your father had a child with a mistress... A child would gradually empty your mother's property, take away your future little by little. Human nature is greed, Zaki... I can understand everything your mother did; she had to, because she must protect you. Who else could protect you, your father blinded by lust? Or the woman coveting your wealth?" 
Fatuna finally began to sweep, her shoulders slump helplessly. For the first time... even her brother did not understand why she was so determined... for the first time someone could really understand her. But this truth was not a burden that a child should bear. She collapsed, covering her face and cries bitterly, "This has nothing to do with him, why did you tell him? This is the sin I committed... This is my sin." 
Zaki was completely stunned. He looked blankly, unbelieving at his mother. Was his father's death because of him? This heavy sin falls upon his immature shoulders. But what wrong did he do? Maggie whispered to comfort Fatuna, telling her that children must know the truth while signaling to you. You understood her meaning, took Zaki, and walked out of the room. 
Zaki stood silently beside you. He had never seen his mother cry before. He recalled for a long time the once gentle and smiling mother who had not smiled since his father's death... She maneuvered strongly, putting forth a brave front, navigating among those wolves to protect their precarious and stable life... all but for him...!
"Yet even so..." he choked as he lowered his head, unsure of how to continue, "I really don't know what to do better... I have no right to blame my mother, but I also have no right to forgive her. What should I do? If you give me a knife, I will do it, if you tell me to forgive, I will do it. But... which is right, and which is wrong? I really don't know..." He leaned against you, slowly, his depressed confessions grew weaker and weaker, and you turn to look at him, this child... He fell asleep out of exhaustion. You pat his soft hair, wiped the tears from his face, and sighs softly. For a moment, you can feel that he almost regards you as his father.

The wife looked at the letters in astonishment for a long time before sighing, "... I understand her." Sympathy and compassion appeared in her eyes, "Maybe what she did was wrong, but... I understand her. She is a woman, a mother... what else could she do to protect herself and you?"
You knew, and you explained to the young man that if his mother hadn't acted, his father would have made the child outside the heir. The father would then slowly empty the mother's property and take away his future, bit by bit. None of this could be stopped unless one party died.
Zaki listened blankly, his clenched fists slowly unclenching. But how could this be... was this family broken because of him, what had he done wrong? The young man's eyes filled with tears, and he helplessly covered his face, "But what should I do? I... I can't blame her, nor can I forgive her... I... if you give me a knife, I will do it, if you ask me to forgive, I will listen to you. But which is right, which is wrong? I really don't know..."
Maggie gently patted his back, softly comforting him. The child's tearful confessions slowly exhausted themselves into quiet. Maggie wiped the tears from his sleeping face and sighed, "Poor child... let him sleep well for a while."

After seeing the old letter in her son's hand, Fatuna remained silent for a long time, then sighed as if she had finally released a burden. “Yes, if you must ask, I gave him tea brewed with clove buds, then gave him wine, and then my Brother pressed his head into the bathhouse.” Fatuna looked calmly at Maggie.
"But why... why? Father indeed had a mistress... but... that's not a crime worthy of death!" The young noble cried hoarsely, tears welling from his eyes. 
"You didn't sentence him to death, my dear child, I know," Fatuna looked at Zaki gently, but her words were harsh, "But I did. I sentenced your father to death. That's how it is, I admit my crime." 
"Don't say that." Maggie squeezed her hand tightly, then looked at Zaki, "She did it for you, son. She—" 
"Don't, Maggie, don't." Fatuna tried to interrupt her several times, but Maggie continued to speak gently yet firmly, holding her cold and trembling hand, "Isn't it clear in the letter? Your father had a child with a mistress... A child would gradually empty your mother's property, take away your future little by little. Human nature is greed, Zaki... I can understand everything your mother did; she had to, because she must protect you. Who else could protect you, your father blinded by lust? Or the woman coveting your wealth?" 
Fatuna finally began to sweep, her shoulders slump helplessly. For the first time... even her brother did not understand why she was so determined... for the first time someone could really understand her. But this truth was not a burden that a child should bear. She collapsed, covering her face and cries bitterly, "This has nothing to do with him, why did you tell him? This is the sin I committed... This is my sin."
The mother's tears awakened Zaki's lost soul. He remembered his once ever-smiling and gentle mother, who after the sudden change, risked everything to protect him, maintaining their precarious life, exhausting all her energy to deal with the wolves... it was to protect such a mother that he mustered the courage to seek a master to learn from, wasn't it?
He stepped forward and embraced his mother. It was also at this moment that he realized how thin and haggard she had become. “No, Mom, this is our crime.” He wiped away the tears from his mother’s face, and at that moment, it seemed he had finally grown up. He understood that justice and crime are not purely black and white; the helpless, the inevitable gray in between, that is the human world.

After seeing the old letter in her son's hand, Fatuna remained silent for a long time, then sighed as if she had finally released a burden. “Yes, if you must ask, I gave him tea brewed with clove buds, then gave him wine, and then my Brother pressed his head into the bath.” Fatuna looked calmly at you.
“But why... why? Father did have an affair – but – but that's not a death sentence!” The young nobleman roared hysterically, tears welling up in his eyes.
“You did not sentence him to death, my dear child, I know,” Fatuna looked at Zaki with soft eyes, but her words were firm, “but I did. I sentenced your father to death. That's how it is, I admit my guilt.”
Zaki could no longer listen, he glared fiercely at his mother and rushed out the door as if he had never really known her. You looked helplessly at Fatuna, this stubborn woman sitting in the shadow, like a sculpture that had lost its life.

How should you persuade this child? You opened your mouth, at a loss for words – true, the man had done wrong, but in your heart, you believed he didn’t deserve to die... It’s unfair to Zaki’s father, and even more so to Zaki, who has lost a stable life and his father's protection.
Zaki looked into your eyes, not needing you to speak, gradually calmed down. 'I know what to do, teacher.' He bowed to you, then resolutely left your sight.

Maggie read the letters seriously, and after a long silence, she looked up at the child who was nervously sitting aside waiting for an answer. He clutched the cloth on his knees tightly, bit his lip, and frequently looked out the window with eyes full of unease and anxiety.
Maggie sighed softly, knowing that the person the child was looking for was you – the person he trusted and admired, yet you were absent for some reason in this crucial conversation for him. Maggie knew that what she said to Zaki would not carry as much weight as your words, which made her feel heavy pressure, but she wouldn't back down. She put the letter down and gently asked Zaki, 'You think your mother was wrong, don't you? She killed a man who shouldn't have died.'
Her eyes seemed to see into the deepest parts of human hearts. Zaki was silent for a moment and then looked away. 'Father... Father indeed had an affair, but... if it were you, if my teacher made such a mistake... would you kill him?'
Maggie thought seriously for a moment, 'Maybe I would, maybe I wouldn't. But... if I were in Fatuna’s situation, I would certainly make the same choice. The biggest difference between me and her is that I do not have a child. Zaki, your mother had to do this because she had to protect you.'
'Protect me?!' Zaki looked up in surprise.
Maggie nodded, 'The letter makes it very clear, doesn't it? Your father had a child outside... it goes without saying that if this continued, he would slowly drain your mother's property, and bit by bit, take away your future. Human hearts are greedy, Zaki... when that day comes, who would protect you? Would you rely on your father blinded by lust? Or beg that woman who schemes for wealth?'
Zaki opened his mouth, 'You are saying, my mother killed for me... all because of me? But I, but I... but I didn't do anything! But I... sob...' He couldn't accept this result. He came to seek justice, but now, this heavy blame fell on his shoulders. Was he a mistake from birth? If he hadn't been born, neither his father would have died, nor his mother would carry this burden of life. What should he do to uphold the weighty word 'justice'?... He bent his back, nearly breaking down as he covered his face. At this moment, his reluctance and struggle against parricide faded. What he felt was a kind of unprecedented confusion and fear, as if the inner world he built cracked open a huge chasm in an instant, a gentle touch would shatter it into ashes.
Maggie didn't know that he had thought so much in an instant, she just softly patted the boy's back, 'I am not blaming you, Zaki. You're a good child, just young... Time will tell you the answer, give yourself some time, and give your mother some time, okay?' And Zaki, at a loss, could only nod haphazardly, then left in a daze.
After that, for a period of time, he seldom came to you. You could feel that he no longer admired or relied on you as he did before. Perhaps, some things in the boy’s heart were permanently rewritten. Perhaps, this is the path of growth...

In your perspective, the best way to resolve matters is to talk it out face-to-face. You call for Fatuna, and then leave the space for this mother and child.
However, things did not go as you expected. Before long, you hear sounds of argument from the room. The door is pushed open violently, and the boy runs out wiping tears haphazardly. When he sees you, he completely loses control. He cries loudly, 'It was really her... Teacher, it was really her!'
You hurriedly comfort the child and instinctively glance inside the door. The woman sits in the shadows, lips tightly pursed, not getting up, as stubborn as a lifeless statue.

5006509.title: What is Justice
strings: What is Justice
Zaki and Fatuna live their lives as usual, as if nothing had happened... but, is it really so?
Zaki doesn't seem to have changed much
Fatuna strives to maintain the status quo
If you intervene, maybe Zaki would get the courage to take the knife; if the wife intervenes, maybe she could move him with her gentleness.
You can choose to place yourself, your Wife, or a Bloodshed card to change the stalemate between Zaki and Fatuna, but the results will not be the same.
Please make a careful choice, and of course, ignoring it is also an option.

Arriving after hearing the disturbing news, you find only an intricate blood-drawn pattern covering the floor. Fatuna stands at its center, her belly slightly swollen, with clothing fragments scattered at her feet - unmistakably what Zaki wore yesterday.
"The Dark Lord blessed me with a miracle," her pale face, blood-red lips, and ink-dot eyes assemble into an unsettling smile, "allowing me to properly re-educate this child."

This mother and son continue their lives as if nothing had happened, but they will never be as close as before. This incident will forever be stuck in Zaki's heart, ensuring he will never trust anyone again.
I will bring you the dagger you need
It has come to this point, hasn't it...
I wonder how this mother and son have been? Let me go have a chat with them.
Do it, and I will absolve you of your crime.
This... could be considered redemption.
Thank you, Maggie... I really don't know how to thank you.
Is it right or wrong? I don't know...
You brought a dagger to Zaki.
Maggie brought some rare snacks to visit the mother and son.
You played the Bloodshed Card on Zaki

That night, Zaki finally made up his mind and used the dagger you gave him to kill his own mother. He then went to the palace and confessed his crime.
This case caused a huge commotion among the nobles; some said he was a matricidal monster deserving the ultimate punishment, while others said he was a filial son avenging his father and should be pardoned. Opinions varied, but Zaki no longer cared. He had fulfilled his own inner sense of justice.
The Sultan was pleased to see bloodshed. He first took a good look at Fatuna’s beautiful corpse, then happily said, 'You are all right, so let's sentence this child to death. It is the price for the deceased's life, and accompanying one's own mother, after all, is what a filial child should do.'
No one objected to the Sultan's decision. Zaki stood calmly amidst the accusations and praises, and as he faced the blade, he suddenly understood how his mother felt when she stood before him...

Zaki and Fatuna seemed to have forgotten how to interact with each other; the atmosphere was awkward and tense. Seeing this, Maggie nonchalantly mentioned that those unique snacks came from a distant land and were very precious and popular... and she had just recently learned how to make them.
Maggie winked and then gently but irresistibly pulled Fatuna and Zaki into the kitchen... Oh my, even young Zaki and Fatuna rarely cooked for themselves, but Maggie seemed enthusiastic, directing them on which ingredients to get, how to knead the dough, and how much sugar to add...
Very soon, thanks to her experience, the mother got the hang of it, while the child, who had never stepped into a kitchen before, was still clumsy. Fatuna was half-exasperated and half-sympathetic, wanting Zaki to sit outside, but the child refused to give up. He argued with his mother, determined to get it right. Maggie watched all this with a smile.
When the cookies were finally placed on the table, many cold things melted in the soft afterglow of the sunset. There was no ice to be held in the clenched hands of the mother and son who depended on each other.

You gave Zaki a dagger, telling him that you would absolve him of his crime, and besides... you happened to need to break that Bloodshed Card. So, that night, Zaki finally gritted his teeth and decided to kill his mother.
The next day, you publicly declared that you killed Fatuna, thereby breaking a Bloodshed Card. People half-heartedly condemned you for a moment, then greedily turned their eyes to the vast wealth inherited by the orphan after his mother’s death...
With no parents, Zaki could no longer accept your protection, for it was ethically untenable. Nor could he stay in the city, for it was full of wolves.
One morning he bid you farewell, leaving you with all of Fatuna’s inheritance, except a little travel money.
'Thank you, teacher. I have no regrets.' He bowed his head slightly, as if not daring to look into your eyes. 'I just want to go out and see... to see what justice really is...'

5006510.title: Easily obtained happiness
strings: Easily obtained happiness

Zaki comes to seek your teachings as usual, but this time, you sense a different air about him. After a few probing questions, he eagerly reveals that he's been frequenting the House of Delights lately. Hahaha, it seems he's finally become a 'man'! Should you have a deep conversation with him about techniques? Though, the women surely wouldn't think so.
Zaki's face is beaming with excitement
Wife or Protagonist
Choosing between your wife or yourself will lead to different branches.
Hahaha, what is this? Let me teach you a few more tricks!
Teacher, you really are the best!
What?! It can't go on like this!
Ah, please don't tell my mother...
This is a secret between men
Maggie harshly criticizes him

You share all your insights, teaching him various mischievous tricks that should be done discretely. You kindly tell him which places noble women might frequent and to go at night, and which places are more fun to visit during the day. You also detail the temperaments and preferences of the courtesans...
The young noble's eyes widen in awe, as if he's never admired you this much before.

Your wife, Fatuna, and you, the three of you surround Zaki and give him a stern lecture.
Maggie tells him how heartbroken his future wife would be over such behavior.
His mother warns him that courtesans can harm not only with weapons and diseases but also corrupt souls with their seductive words.
You quietly tell him that he has been seen at the House of Delights too many times, and that it's a matter of caution.
Whether he heeds your words or not, this incident teaches him several lessons.

5006511.title: Destroy the Corpse
strings: Destroy the Corpse

You quietly push open the door to Zaki's house in the drizzle. The dim light reveals ropes and whips, with the scent of essential oils in the air. A pale, emaciated woman lies twisted on the shiny silk carpet, lifeless. You must dispose of her before dawn.
Zaki in a Panic
You have to handle this yourself
Setting a fire isn't hard, but it's dangerous...
You attempt to escape from the fire
Your Physique and Survival determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to escape unscathed.

You must dispose of the woman before dawn. So, you quickly instruct Zaki to pour lamp oil on the thick silk carpet and set it ablaze.
The flames swiftly consume the courtesan's corpse but also threaten to engulf you...

You grab Zaki and pull him out of the fire. The rain contains the blaze within a moderate range. Only after the fire has subsided do you allow Zaki to call for his mother in shock. His mother quickly summons the guards, who manage to completely extinguish the fire.
As everyone collapses from exhaustion, people from the House of Delights come looking for the woman, prompting you to accuse them. If they hadn't sent this sneaky madwoman to knock over the lamp, the fire wouldn't have started, and your student wouldn't have suffered such losses?
With the corpse completely incinerated, the House of Delights has no choice but to accept this loss silently despite their displeasure.
Zaki finally breathes a sigh of relief and promises you he'll never bring a courtesan home again. But you know he will.

You barely crawled out of the fire, but you left Zaki behind, his face licked by flames, tears falling from the pain. You hurriedly woke the guards here, and the guards quickly woke the mistress. It wasn't until dawn that the fire was completely extinguished. Fortunately, it had rained earlier, or the consequences would have been unimaginable... 
Just as Zaki was recovering from the fright, people from the brothel came to claim him. You stepped forward and accused them in return, blaming them for sending the sneaky mad woman who toppled over the oil lamp, causing the fire, resulting in such a tragic loss for your student.
Seeing the burns on his face, and given that the corpse had been completely incinerated, the brothel could only bear this silent loss... this matter was thus dropped. 
Zaki finally breathed a sigh of relief, his taut nerves relaxed, and another fear surfaced. Out of sympathy, Fatuna called a doctor to treat him, but although the injury could heal, the scar remained forever. 
Since then, Zaki wore a fine mask, and he frequented the brothel even more often.

5006512.title: Negotiation
strings: Negotiation
Zaki accidentally killed a prostitute, and it's well known that a prostitute’s life is of little value. You can step in to negotiate with the people from the brothel, spend some money, or...
Zaki is very frightened
You have to handle this yourself
You may place a Bloodshed or an Extravagance card not exceeding Bronze tier
You need at least 5 Gold Coins to buy the life of the prostitute.
The brothel demands 5 Gold Coins, but if you are willing to spend 10 Gold Coins, you can break an Extravagance Card as well.
Of course, if you are not willing to pay even 5 Gold Coins, you can also handle this with a blade.

You changed your mind. With this money, you could have done something more beneficial for yourself. Zaki was severely beaten by the brothel's thugs, and after this incident, he never sought your help again.
You draw a Bloodshed Card
You gave him money

With a sudden move, you behead the unsuspecting thug. Then, you draw a Bloodshed Card and smile at the brothel owner so insistent on the 5 Gold Coins. "What was it you wanted again? I didn’t quite hear."
The terrified brothel owner hurriedly exclaims that everyone is friends here and it was all a misunderstanding. Zaki is always welcome, free of charge.
Thus, the matter is resolved. Zaki admires you immensely.

In this matter, you spend a lot of effort persuading the filthy brothel to give up the prostitute, and also convince some suspicious-looking men to 'reclaim' the corpse. Even more impressively, you persuade them to start a new service: offering beautiful yet fragile young girls for 'one-time use'.

The young noble is so thoroughly convinced by you that you steadfastly became what he aspires to be.
You thus break an Extravagance Card
The Sultan heard of this matter and announced that henceforth, killing prostitutes would be a legal activity at double the cost.

5006513.title: Ruin and Death
strings: Ruin and Death

Without your protection, the cowardly bully of the Dark Alley harassed this poor family endlessly. To resolve the matter, Fatuna and Zaki lost a large portion of their property and all their noble dignity.
Zaki is terrified
Fatuna is exhausted

Not long after, Fatuna's corpse was found at the bottom of a well, and people said she couldn't bear the humiliation and committed suicide. At the same time, Zaki disappeared from the city...
 But what of it? As Zaki's mentor, you inherited their estate, your purse bulging with wealth.
 Maggie, having lost a dear friend with whom she shared afternoon tea and bath time, was very repulsed. Using a woman's intuition, she believed you were involved in this matter, and you could only endure her anger, for she was your wife after all.

5006514.title: Ripples in the Bathhouse
strings: Ripples in the Bathhouse

You invited Zaki, and he did not refuse. What will happen in the ripples of the bathhouse? Zaki might know, or he might not. But you are fully aware of what you are doing, aren't you? You will hold his hand, using his curiosity, trust, and admiration to lure him onto a path full of temptation and danger...
You must attend the appointment in person.
Zaki is curious about what will happen
You can use this to break a Carnality card of no higher tier than Zaki
Choose to use the Carnality card at your discretion.
After much contemplation, you gave up. Fortunately, Zaki never mentioned it again.
Zaki would never refuse your invitation

The bathhouse has long been cleared, leaving only the two of you. Zaki is a bit shy but proud of the strength you've shown. He looks at you, repeatedly complimenting, admiring, and praising you. You know these words come from his heart.
'Sometimes I wish,' he says, his eyes sparkling, 'you were my father... Oh, if only you were my father!'
You move closer to his young and strong body, place your hand on his shoulder, and softly tell him that you can do better than a real father...
Zaki is not a foolish child; he understands what you mean.
Rose-scented water ripples endlessly, marking a very interesting and pleasant time.
You take out a Carnality card
Everything was done in secret

You make public what should have been a private affair, but the Sultan shows little interest and casually asks you for many details, seeming somewhat repulsed. To prove that your affair was enough to break this Carnality card, you have to emphasize the immoral aspects, how you used his naivety, how you tricked him into your trap...
By the end, the Sultan smiles meaningfully. You break the Carnality card in public as you wished, but when the cold wind chills your sweat, you realize that this was the Sultan's trap... and you will pay a price far beyond your imagination.

When Zaki says goodbye, there is a hint of reluctance and hope in his eyes. You smile and touch his wet curls, telling him it's time to go back and that... there will be many more opportunities. The young man's face reddens again. He tries to suppress the curve of his mouth, nodding vigorously, and then leaves without daring to look at you again.

5006515.title: Entangled in Scandal
strings: Entangled in Scandal
To break the Carnality card, you made public the affair between you and Zaki. He and his mother Fatuna became the targets of criticism overnight.
Zaki is entangled in scandal
Fatuna cannot bear the shame

Once stigmatized, there is no washing it away. People curse, blame, and mock Zaki and Fatuna. Those obscene words penetrate their ears no matter how tightly they shut their doors and windows. Those piercing stares make them feel naked in broad daylight no matter how tightly they wrap their clothes around themselves.
Finally, Fatuna could not bear it any longer. She took Zaki and left the city. However, before leaving, she sighed and had a servant give something to you. After that, you two had no further ties.

Once stigmatized, there is no washing it away. People curse, blame, and mock Zaki and Fatuna. Those obscene words penetrate their ears no matter how tightly they shut their doors and windows. Those piercing stares make them feel naked in broad daylight no matter how tightly they wrap their clothes around themselves.
Finally, Fatuna could not bear it any longer. She took Zaki and left the city. Naturally, she did not say goodbye to you, the perpetrator.

5006516.title: Perhaps We Shouldn't Have Done This
strings: Perhaps We Shouldn't Have Done This

Zaki didn't tell you explicitly what would happen next, so your boundless imagination took the lead and brought you into a realm of ultimate romance. You play with the perfectly warm ripples in the bath, smiling as you await the arrival of the young man and the unmentioned 'someone else'.
Zaki looks forward to meeting with you privately.
You must attend the appointment in person.
Who could be the 'someone else' Zaki mentioned? Feel free to speculate.
You can take the opportunity to break a Carnality Card not higher than Gold tier.
You can place a Carnality Card of Gold tier.
For some reason, someone is delayed by some affairs, preventing your wicked yet wonderful rendezvous from happening this time.

First to arrive is Zaki. You silently agree to avoid discussing what is about to occur.
The bath is very quiet, so quiet that the sound of flowing water covers a few ambiguous breaths. The young man’s beautiful face is soaked with the color of roses, and when he looks at you asking for a kiss, he appears like a clumsy but passionate puppy.
In the heat of the moment, none of you noticed when the bath's curtain was gently drawn aside. During a brief pause, you suddenly glimpse a pale figure wrapped in black gauze. A noble lady steps barefoot into the disturbed water. The rose-scented steam makes your faces appear blurry, hiding your expressions.
Fatuna slowly comes closer to you, you hear a soft sigh from her, then the black gauze slips off her body like a butterfly shedding its cocoon. She sheds something before coming to you, revealing her snow-white body, glowing faintly in the mist.
“We shouldn’t be doing this,' she says firmly but kisses you nonetheless, 'We really shouldn’t be doing this.”
What convinced her? Is it the protection your power can provide, the security from your life-saving act, or perhaps... no, her soft fingers wrapping around your desire now like a serpent.Strong and soft bodies cling to each inch of your skin, embracing the most instinctual part of your soul. There's no room left for thought or reason.
This is the first, the last, and the most marvelous time.

Zaki arrives first. You both tacitly remain silent about what will happen.
The bath is quiet, only flowing water sounds mask certain ambiguous, trivial gasps. The young man's beautiful face is suffused with rose color, his eyes moist, like a wet puppy seeking kisses, unable to conceal desire and enthusiasm.
In your passion, you don't notice the bathroom curtain gently lifted. During a kiss, you glimpse pale skin, a black-veiled noblewoman barefoot entering these turbulent waters, rose-scented steam making your faces shadowy, difficult to distinguish expressions.
Fatuna slowly approaches you, her cold skin against your heated back like a gentle knife. Strong bodies, soft bodies, honestly, hotly pressed against every inch of your skin, containing your soul's most instinctual parts, leaving no space for rational thought.
Is bathwater red? Do kisses leave wounds? Can pleasure make one so dizzy? You don't know. You cannot know.
You thus break a Carnality Card.

People were astonished by your audacity, yet envious of your fortune... Regardless, because of your power in the palace and your unbridled reputation among the populace, no one dared to openly say anything against you or the mother and son. It seemed as if the matter was forgotten. However, don't worry; the moment you fall from grace or even show a hint of instability, they'll immediately remember it all.

5006517.title: Ancient Language Lessons
strings: Ancient Language Lessons
You're ready to hire a noble with considerable expertise in ancient languages to be Lumera's tutor.
Lumera wants to learn ancient languages.
Your knowledge can provide some help.
An expense of 5 Gold Coins or 10 Gold Coins.
If you are willing to pay double the price, you can use this to break an Extravagance Card.
Something that clears the mind might come in handy.
If you pay 10 Gold Coins, you can use this opportunity to break a Extravagance Card of no higher than the Bronze tier.
Every evening, Lumera comes to report her learning progress to you, forcing you to recall the ancient language phrases you learned as a child. How much can you remember...
Your Wisdom determines your full dice count.
Requires 2 Successes.
Whether you forget or regret, you are Lumera's master, and Lumera has no right to say anything.
How can you lose?
How could you lose?
You spent a large sum of money and used an Extravagance Card.

Seeing that the student is just a Slave Girl, the noble felt rather repulsed, but begrudgingly agreed due to your power. He soon discovers that this lowly Slave Girl possesses an unusually sharp mind and quick insights. Holding some concealed jealousy and indignation, he makes Lumera’s lessons increasingly difficult and profound day by day.
You expertly converse with Lumera in the ancient language, recalling all the long-forgotten knowledge instantly, as if by instinct. Lumera looks at you with admiration, her eyes sparkling like stars.

You stumble through those obscure ancient words, as if returning to the age when teachers would hit your knuckles. After barely making it through another day of classes, Lumera leaves, and you curse the noble who taught her ancient language a hundred times in your mind.

The news of you spending money to teach a slave ancient languages spreads quickly. The nobles denounce you for your deviance, but the Sultan laughs and praises you lavishly – he didn't anticipate such a clever and absurd way of splurging! Amid the speechless silence of the ministers, your reputation rises again.

5006518.title: The Pain of Editing
strings: The Pain of Editing
As per your agreement with the ancient language teacher, Lumera heads to the library by carriage early in the morning to participate in the editing work.
Lumera is working hard.
Lumera completes today's work well. You can easily see from her sparkling eyes how much she enjoys this job, which most people find tedious.

Lumera completes today's work well. Her eyes sparkle, trying to restrain something, like a puppy circling around you but desperately trying not to overreact out of excitement. It seems she found some clues among the vast scrolls but hasn't finished deciphering them.
You smile and pretend not to notice anything.

5006519.title: Fragment of the Star-Souled Glyphs
strings: Fragment of the Star-Souled Glyphs
You and Lumera try to decipher these obscure spells.
Lumera looks forward to decoding the spell with you.
You must handle this yourself

The spell is written in the most arcane ancient language, full of metaphors and similes, making it very hard to interpret. You've managed a rough translation, to which Lumera adds more based on your work, and together you piece together the entire 'Starlight Spell'.
Contrary to what the nobles thought, this doesn't seem to be a curse against the Sultan's ancestors; its purpose is to 'open', but what exactly it opens isn't clear in the spell. Further interpretation will require much more time.
Lumera is utterly captivated by it. She looks at you almost obsessively, pleading for you to give her the fragment. She wants to decode it, decipher it, and uncover its hidden secrets. Her fervor overwhelms you, and you cannot refuse her.
Scholar Visits

Upon hearing this news, several young people knocked at your door, hoping to meet Lumera. Lumera recognized one among them and introduced her as someone who'd provided substantial assistance with compilation work.
They courteously bowed to you, identifying themselves as Scholar members - indeed, they all wore distinctive badges upon their cloaks.
As the girls conversed quietly, you sat in shade, gradually recollecting which "Scholar" this was. The empire maintained only one court-recognized society. In earlier years, the Sultan permitted an organization to gather various knowledge and curiosities from the populace - a common method for controlling masses and suppressing thought. Later, their work seemed unsuccessful, gradually fading from the Sultan's attention... What did they want?
Stroking your chin thoughtfully, the Scholar members had already departed the study. The leading lady approached, placing a badge in your hand: "You and Miss Lumera discovered extremely valuable knowledge. As gratitude... please accept this. With it, you can freely access our library. Don't worry, Miss Lumera possesses her own badge." She winked at you. "We welcome and willingly assist everyone who thirsts for knowledge and pursues truth."

5006520.title: Star-Souled Night
strings: Star-Souled Night
You burned the incomplete Star-Souled Spell, stopping the unknown passage from being opened. But Lumera, who bore the brunt of it, fainted. Will she wake up?
Lumera is in a coma
You need to wait patiently.
She wakes up.

You consulted the best doctors, but they all said she only needed time. After waiting patiently for several more days, finally, on a beautiful evening at twilight, Lumera reopened her eyes as if she had just had a good sleep. Though she didn't say a word, you could sense subtle, indescribable changes in her... It seems being touched by the unknown leaves traces.

5006521.title: Star-Souled Night
strings: Star-Souled Night
You loudly praise each name of the stars. The infinite paths recorded on the scrolls have been opened. The one who bears this great destiny is also destined to vanish.
Is she still Lumera?

A violent black whirlwind rushes into your residence, causing people to scream and hide. After the commotion, it’s found that nothing is missing, but Lumera has vanished. You look up at the stars, only you know where she has gone.

When you tell Lumera's new husband, he doesn't seem especially grieved. "She told me herself. In a dream, last night." He looks to the stars, long, searching. "I know where she is. And one day, we'll meet again. Up there."

5006522.title: Revenge
strings: Revenge
Lumera's father is clearly a scoundrel. Even without Lumera's plea, you wouldn't have let him live.
A scoundrel deserving of death
Lumera will witness it all
You must handle this yourself
You can break a Bloodshed Card no higher than Lumera's father's tier

When your hand rests on the scabbard, you suddenly hesitated... a noble, a minister, should they really kill for a Slave Girl... so many people watching...
Lumera understood your hesitation, but she had already made up her mind. She bows, asking you to leave. This is her revenge; she has to face it herself.
You killed the villain

You nod to Lumera and step forward. The man begs, cries, and repeatedly claims he is a free man, but you remain unmoved.
Lumera quietly watches from the side, the man's blood spreading across her bare feet. She stares at the blood flowing towards the filthy gutter. Then she kneels down in the pool of blood, solemnly bowing to you.
Your actions inevitably left traces.

When you broke this Bloodshed Card, the nobles were agitated, even protesting to the Sultan. They didn’t believe the scoundrel deserved to be killed for his crimes. You suspected that the crimes committed by these nobles clad in silk might be no less than those by the man you killed. It doesn’t matter; you silently calculated how many Bloodshed Cards you could still draw. There’s no need to rush.

5006523.title: The Orphan's Revenge
strings: The Orphan's Revenge
A story about revenge that suddenly became popular.
"The Orphan's Revenge"
The reader.

Lumera's young voice echoed in the study, her tone calm as when telling stories to the servants. In this book, it describes the story of a girl who depended on her mother. Her drunken, violent father repeatedly sold her mother for money, but her weak mother couldn't leave this man, constantly deceiving herself by saying, 'This is love'... After her mother’s tragic death, the girl gradually recovered with the help of a Noble master and planned her revenge against her father... 
After finishing the book, Lumera lowered her head, uneasily asking to leave. You watch her hurried back, unable to help but smile. 
Indeed, no matter how you read it, this book is all about you. And who the girl is, naturally becomes obvious.

The book describes a girl living with her mother, whose abusive alcoholic and gambling father repeatedly sells the mother for money. The cowardly mother can't leave such a man, constantly deceiving herself by saying 'this is love'... After her mother’s tragic death, the girl gradually regains her strength with the help of a noble master, planning her revenge on her father... Indeed, no matter how you read it, the book is all about you. The identity of the girl in the story is clearly revealed.

5006524.title: Acceptance of Reward
strings: Acceptance of Reward
You have the right to decide who will receive the reward from the palace. even though it is meant for Lumera.
Whom do you decide to receive this blessing?
If Maggie accepts this blessing, you can take the opportunity to resolve one Wife's Resentment.

You tell Lumera that these are items bestowed upon her by the palace and that she deserves them. The girl's eyes sparkle with bright light. After confirming you were not going to drive her away, she daringly draped the luxurious fabrics over herself, seemingly judging their worth. You watched her with a smile, estimating that in a few days, these rewards would all be turned into books, right?

You present these luxurious and beautiful treasures to Maggie and tell her they are for her. Maggie is overjoyed, not only because the beautiful and delicate silks are particularly appealing but also because she was the first person you thought of. She generously gives you a passionate kiss, and the former estrangement between you seems to have faded.

This book tells the life of a young girl, the happiness she once had, the care she lost, her decline, her hope, and most importantly, her revenge... In the end, her evil father died of starvation, and she finally broke free from the long-standing shadow that had bound her...

At the end, Lumera closed the book, 'I hope you won't want to hear this story anymore, Master...' She paused and lowered her head, 'And I hope there will never be such a story in this world again.'
The life of a girl – with happiness she once had, love she lost, her downfall, her hatred, and most importantly, her desperate revenge – all between these thin pages.

5006535.title: Justice Must...
strings: Justice Must...

During this time, Zaki returned home as usual, dining with his mother as if nothing had happened. He rarely talked about what he did or what he saw, only the occasional faint clink of tableware. When silence filled the luxurious mansion, it seemed so hollow and fake... It's time to fill it.
Zaki doesn't seem to have changed much
Fatuna strives to maintain the status quo
You don't know what will happen next, only wait for fate to arrive.

Arriving after hearing the disturbing news, you find only an intricate blood-drawn pattern covering the floor. Fatuna stands at its center, her belly slightly swollen, with clothing fragments scattered at her feet - unmistakably what Zaki wore yesterday.
"The Dark Lord blessed me with a miracle," her pale face, blood-red lips, and ink-dot eyes assemble into an unsettling smile, "allowing me to properly re-educate this child."

That night, after everyone had gone to sleep, Zaki, holding a dagger, quietly pushed open his mother's bedroom door.
His mother was asleep, her pale face expressionless. The new dagger was so sharp, it made no noise. Her blood gushed out, soaking Zaki's trembling hands like a warm embrace, splattering on his trembling lips like a comforting kiss.
“This is... For justice,” the boy muttered, clutching the weapon tightly, staring at his mother's face, tears uncontrollably streaming down, “Justice, yes... Justice,” he whispered, “I killed you, now I carry my own sin.”
When the tears dried, the cold dawn light spread over the two bodies lying close together, their blood mingling into one.

Before you finished, she leapt out of the window without hesitation, choosing death. Unfortunately, this cannot be counted as breaking a Sultan Card.

Bloodshed is like blood; when it drips, it soaks into your life, leaving indelible stains and traces. And you've stained yourself with too much blood. Now, at every corner, behind every footstep, outside every shadow in the window, you can see a complete murder. Those knives, those poisons, you can see them torturing your body in your mind... You urinate on the corpse of yourself stabbed to death by many knives; you spill wine over the vomit you spewed after being poisoned; in your sleep, you hear your own muffled sobs smothered by a pillow. If you don’t do something, one day, these will come true... These will come true!

At dinner that day, Maggie shares some rumors told to her by some noblewomen, all praising you: People say you are kind, capable, resolute, gentle, and even somewhat handsome. 
You chuckle, naturally holding her hand – a warm current spreading from your skin to your heart, and Maggie's gaze tells you she shares the same happy experience.
That night, you heard the High Constable's fort caught fire, and in their chaos, many dossiers were lost... perhaps yours among them.

The next day, you receive an identical replica, wrapped in pristine white linen, appearing on your bedroom windowsill with the sunrise.

Even the scratches are exactly the same...

The old woman takes out a bag of gold coins on the spot from her robe and gently places it in your hand, briefly caressing your cheek... 
When you wished to inquire further details, she vanishes into the shadows between the palaces, leaving only the pure white linen moneybag in your hand as evidence of what you've seen.
She tells you to bring your ear closer and whispers a secret you have never imagined... When you come back to your senses, she is already gone, leaving only that secret lingering in your heart.
You grab the woman's wrist: "I know who your master is." Then she reverses your grip, throwing you down. When you get up, the mud bears several crucial details you had previously ignored to.
The old woman comforts you as a puppy, assuring you that luck would soon favor you – you are patted on the head, and before you can react, she has already vanished.
You complain to the old woman, and the next day, find a note among the documents describing some shameful deeds...

It's not money or other resources you lack, but hope! After yelling at the old woman, you dream of a scene... In a place far away from the Sultan, resting under a tree, while your wife calls from afar...

No one can always win, not even the Sultan. The old woman chuckles: "But there are some tricks."
When the night comes, you dream yourself repeatedly delve into despairing battles, experiencing enough victory and death...

The next day, strange occurrences continue.
Jar of olive oils overflow endlessly, filling every jars in the house.
Unfamiliar long-tailed birds appeared in the garden, its chimes heavenly.
Finally, the hearth and chimney are renewed as if thoroughly cleaned... Everyone claim in earnest that your mansion is blessed.

This is a dangerous, frightening request, but asking does not necessarily mean evil. The old woman pondered for a long time... then her body crumbled like flowing sand... insects, mice, moths... all rushed out of the smoke and dust, pouncing on your face...
When you regained your senses, everything had disappeared, leaving only the surging magic within.
That night, you had a strange dream... The details are unclear, but it was a pleasant, even auspicious dream, and it was about you.

The world is inherently filthy. Your acts of goodness have separated the evil, but merely like a ship separating the water. The Immaculate Purity has been tirelessly worked to cleanse a world corrupted by darkness. Now, He has answered your prayers, channeling your virtuous deeds to make things right, returning the countdown of this cursed card to its pristine original state – as pure as when it first emerged from the magician's deck. 

This restoration is sacred and supernatural. All players – you, the Sultan, even the Magician herself – can feel the overwhelming power from this sacred reset.

Seeing the flames raging, the Sultan gives a satisfied smile.

You tell the Sultan, the books of the ten nations he once annihilated are all preserved here, they remember their languages, their cultures, their stories, their ideals... Now, for your Lord, you will cleanse them from this earth.

This is the real conquest. The Sultan nods, an exclaimation mark towards the agreement that, henceforth, this shall become routine after any city broken.

Why is this book-burning fire so wondrous, fragrant beyond burning costly spices, more splendid than the fire offered by an alchemist? The Sultan asks, and you reply: "It is a fire ignited using the future as fuel, thus it's extremely extravagance." – the Sultan feels this elegant act indeed deserves an Extravagance Card.

Voluntarily, Asal, the owner of The Angler Bookstore, begged to be burned with these books – and the Sultan graciously granted his request.

As flames engulfed him, he opened the book in his hand, chanted a curse towards you and the Sultan... using his life and soul to curse you to be sucked into this book after death, into a collection of terrifying, despairing, bizarre tales... to experience eternal fright and torment.

The Sultan sneered at this, as the monarch's demeanor and that powerful Signet Ring made ordinary curses ineffective against him. What about you? God, is there a more frightening game than the Sultan's Game? This is truly the most boring curse.

You have gently comforted her, even pleaded – but she had decided to die with the books, having gained the Sultan's permission and attention.
 Feigning madness has faked it into reality. And now, you've lost control of this tragedy by your own doing... Flames parted you, countless pages shattered, ashes flew – and she disappeared, into the swirling blaze with just a blink, as if she never came to this absurd world.

Wasn't it the girl you once ignored? She sat atop a mountain of mixed firewood and books, heedless of the soldiers' shouts, the malicious cacophony of the onlookers, ravenously reading the books in her hands – there were countless free books piled up for her to read right now.
Until the flames rose, in the unbearable fire and smoke, there always seemed to be a silhouette, calmly reading.
In the end, everything turned to ashes, leaving only the shadow and a sigh before it dissipated.
The gazes once fixed upon you are now completely severed by smoke and ash. Now the badge you hold is merely ordinary metal, devoid of other meaning.

You first went to the home of a friend that Maggie was visiting, and found that she had left in the early evening. Onto the trail you investigated, even calling on friends from the Dark Alley. Eventually, you found her in a locked, rundown warehouse.

Several unruly brutes lay drunk, sprawled out across the floor. Maggie was pale, holding a dagger and about to stab down when she turned her head. As her eyes met yours, an ocean flooded out, sniffles reverebrating the hopeless room.

You hurried forward, holding her tightly in comfort, then handed over those filthy reprobates to the High Constable, telling him to ensure a stern and severe punishment for them. Though you already had an inkling of the person behind them, you hope she'd stay away after this incident.

That night, Maggie returned very late. Her silk garment soaked in dark red blood, incongruous dissonance clouds her so much that it petrified her servants. You quickly clutched her cold hand, asking what happened. She shook her head, the silence of the answer so loud that you could still hear the frantic beatings of her heart. It was only after a while did she say, the thing you let her carry saved her life.

You waited for a long time, but she still didn’t return. Weariness pervade your eyes, until you finally give in to the unbearable fatigue. Come next day, you learnt from the servants; she returned at midnight, her garb bloodied, her eyes pale, her soul bleak. It was a horrifying sight.

It was not too far out of your consideration the perpetrator behind this... that damn Nayla, the lunatic, who dared to target Maggie for her own gain... Thankfully Maggie was unharmed. She's just seen through your indifference, not speaking to you for several days afterward.

You waited for a long time, but she still didn’t return. Weariness pervade your eyes, until you finally give in to the unbearable fatigue. The next day, High Constable Adil knocked on your door, speaking the words none wanted to hear: your dearest wife had been attacked by a group of bandits last night and tragically killed.

You could not blame Adil, your mind already filled with the baseless accusations by Nayla. Could it be her? You suggested this to Adil, but eventually, there was no evidence to prove this suspicion.

You did not satisfy Nayla, making her the laughingstock of the entire city! The exasperated Nayla rained down a tirade of various colorful curses on you all afternoon before leaving without turning back. This caused a stir among the city's nobles, and the next day, even the Sultan jokingly asked you if it was true.

Great, now you're an even bigger laughingstock than she is. But beware, she will not let you off so easily. She will repay this humiliation and pain a thousandfold.
Nayla's family won't let you succeed so easily.
The depth of your relations with Nayla has made it unconvincing for the Sultan to allow you to break this Carnality Card.

The wedding proceeds smoothly, after Nayla's ostentatious vow of love, everyone isn't surprised by your union, even finding you two are well-matched.

Nayla flits among guests like a butterfly, her teasing never ceasing, until during a break, she fixes her gaze on you, seemingly expecting something.
You don't let her down
You take out the Gold tier Extravagance Card
The tier of Extravagance Card you presented humiliated Nayla!
You fulfilled her wish in an unexpected way.
However, what replied to her was a cold dagger.

You clap your hands, then several slaves carry a massive jewel chest to the center. You take the specially prepared treasure out, raise it high for all to see, then hand it to Nayla. Amongst the envious stares, under the gold tier treasure’s glow, she beams a sincere smile.

"Oh, dear, there's more, isn't there?" she wrapps her arms around yours affectionately.

Until then, the wedding could not have reached true fruition. Nayla holds the Gold tier card, with a touch of fanatical devotion in her eyes.

She laughs heartily, breaking the card for you. What can surpass this moment? Golden fragments slip from her fingers, her chin raises in pride. Look! A golden wedding, golden treasure, golden card, golden bride!

She tosses the broken card on the ground, then jumps into your arms, embracing your neck with a blazing kiss. Oh at last, at last! She becomes the unimpeachable, the first-class noblewoman!

Nayla looks incredulously at the Extravagance Card you presented, this filthy, debased color!? This will be her lifelong blemish!! She did not marry you merely to become an ordinary woman, a one among thousands!! If she is not the most precious — if she is not the most cherished — then why need she have done so much? You can imagine, at this moment, she wishes she could slap you right there, but to avoid making the wedding even more embarrassing, she bottles up the anger. But just wait, ten years later, twenty years later, she will never forget the shame of this moment, and you'll face the consequences.

When Nayla glimpsed the gold on the card, the delight lighting up her face made her look so innocent, so pure, so beautiful. You smilingly flipped open the card, revealing its sacrificial engraving, and the dagger hidden in your sleeve. 
The woman's blood is red, is warm. Like Maggie's, like all others who’ve sacrificed for you. Before the blood cools, you broke the card, scanning the stunned guests, suddenly feeling a lightness. "Keep drinking, what are you staring at?" You smiles, raising your glass to the crowd, nonchalantly ordering melody to yet halt. 
The grand money-consuming wedding is not in vain, Nayla wished to be a woman worthy of Gold-tier, and you, left with ferocious bitter after a moment of precipitous emptiness: That box no longer had Gold-tier Bloodshed Card, what excuse would you find next to stain gold with blood?

Blood stained Nayla's lapels red, she stared incredulously at your hands, until she stopped breathing, her beautiful eyes wouldn't close in death, as if searching for an answer...

That answer bears no relation to love or warmth, those are things she long abandoned; nor to joy or happiness, for those are things she's already obtained.

Heartlessly, you pulled the dagger from her cooling body, unconcerned with blood splattered on your face. Publicly, you break the Bloodshed Card, pondering perhaps she wanted to see if this Bloodshed Card would be gold tier?

To hell with managing the estate, to hell with bookstores and bathhouses, to hell with the Grand Game, Nayla took all your money and left the city overnight, no one knew how, no one knew where she went.

Leaving you, a man unable to satisfy his wife in every way, a laughingstock at noble and commoner gatherings.

Your Herculean vigor has restored your dignity as a husband, and on this passionate night, Nayla forgave your previous neglect.

She waves for the dowry to be moved into your courtyard and then proudly looks around the crowd. Amid the sparse applause that grows warmer, you know, from this moment on, there's no turning back; Nayla would never allow you to have a change of heart.

You know better than anyone what this woman really is! Marrying her? You’d better value your life. You quickly ordered all the guards to secure the door tightly while hiding yourself in the study. Outside, various sounds could be heard from afar, but you pretended not to listen until everything quieted down by nightfall. 
Reportedly, Nayla shredded all her prepared dowry, letting jewels, pearls, and silks scatter like debris. They were snatched by onlookers after she left.
There’s no doubt; Nayla has become your relentless enemy.

You rarely see such seriousness in Nayla's eyes, as if she truly touched the end of life’s destruction. But how absurd was this earnestness mingled with ceaseless lust! It is even less scrutinized than love, collapsing yet once more into another deep, involuntary collision.

You are the Sultan Card's executor, second only to the Sultan. You hold the greatest power of life and death over all. But while many would stay away from you for fear of destruction, yet Nayla drew closer to you for the joy of manipulating it.

She shamelessly showed off the fun items she bought from Bharat's shop, repeatedly thanking you for this delightful discovery. 
But you're a bit mad that Bharat never sold these to you.

She tells you that despite her most seductive arts, Iman remained entirely unmoved, leading her to question his virility rather than doubt her own considerable charms! 
You hurridly praise her, and in the end, Nayla giggles, generously throwing a handful of Gold Coins into your lap, "Alright, let's not talk about that guy, really boring. Oh, you're much more fun, you're more fun now than in bed."

Under your deliberate arrangement, Nayla and Nabhani ended up in a room together, to each other's company they enjoyed... 

The day after, Nayla came to you. She commented with a smile: "I've always wondered, Nabhani has laid with almost every finely adorned woman of our empire, yet he only now has gotten into bed with me!" 

Nayla confides to you, then sweetly smiles, cupping your face, "Luckily I had dear [player.name] helping, I finally got to taste him, oh, he was delicious! Not just for that... um... but also very considerate, his tongue, that's truly an empire's treasure!"

You've never seen Nayla in such angry. 

She downs three cups of tea before endlessly complaining to you: "He's too rough! And he doesn't bathe! Oh my God! Luckily he met me, for the Empire’s most valiant man’s selection and for my self-esteem, I endured his foul stench and got the job done! If not for my strong will – he’d still be a virgin!”

5006617.title: Food Relief
strings: Food Relief
Again, the hungry poor squeeze outside the tent waiting for your alms. Following Aziz's advice, you entrust today's porridge to Inal.
It costs at least 5 Gold Coins.
You put Inal in charge of today's porridge.
You instruct Aziz to maintain order today.
