Aziz and Inal accurately find the source of the disorder.
This is getting out of hand. Something has to be done.

It is Inal's first time handling such an important task; she was so excited that her face turned red, getting up before dawn to cook the day's porridge, monitoring the heat and stirring non-stop, believing that only this way can draw out the natural sweetness of the wheat – it tastes much better even without expensive sugar.

She speaks truly. Sounds of appreciation arise from the crowd as they taste the porridge, praising it as the finest they've ever had. Hearing this, Inal lifts her head proudly before lowering it shyly…

It is a tall old man, who seemed to once be in the trade where ones often die young, his body foreboding in scars.

But Aziz came, pinning him to the ground with sheer strength before he can react.
No matter how he struggles or begges for mercy, the silent giant would not let go. Finally, he tearfully admits he has been sent by the original person in charge to make trouble, as he couldn't swallow the fact that he had been outclassed by an insignificant female slave.

But regardless, he probably won't dare cause any more mischief. No one else is hurt, and no one else dares to mess around here.

Aziz subdues the nearest boy. He is frail and fragile, as though a leaf, fallen in just a shove, yet his mouth still spry with curses against your family, spitting towards the porridge tent.

Aziz grabs his leg, lifting him upside down like fowl. The boy screams and struggles, but the higher Aziz lifts him, the further from the ground he gets, the more he turned from cursing to crying to begging for mercy, saying he will be grateful and stop causing trouble.

Aziz tosses him back to the ground, he vomitws all the delicious porridge he has just eaten.

The crowd was silent, then immediately exploded in anger. In the end, it is Inal who bravely steps in front of Aziz. Under the intimidating presence of his large frame and the allure of the fragrant food in Inal's hands, order is finally restored.

5006618.title: Reward
strings: Reward

Aziz offers you his Stone Lunchbox, though it's a trivial thing, his obedience pleases you. 

So, will you reward him with something?
1 Gold Coin is a sufficient blessing for a slave.
You generously reward Aziz 1 Gold Coin. He thanks you again and slowly retreated to the servant's quarter.

5006619.title: Let Me Have a Taste
strings: Let Me Have a Taste
What would berries with cream and honey taste like? You can buy some more berries and have Inal make more.
Inal is eager to try.
You decide to taste it yourself
You can indeed invite Maggie to share it.
You can also invite Aziz to taste the delicacy he once mentioned.
Crafting costs 2 Gold Coins
A Respite Most Rare
Inal serves the food, looking at you expectantly.
The sweet and sour berries dipped in a thin layer of shiny honey, with fine mint shreds adding extra refreshment to the cream – a rather clever combination. You admire and enjoy the rare treat.
Maggie leans against you, smiling, saying she once had similar snacks when visiting friends, but none tasted as good as Inal's. Inal's face flushes, her shy eyes shining brightly.

In high spirits, you invite Inal to share this rare refreshment. She is surprised and bows, then cautiously asks if she can take it back to eat. Of course, you have no objection. She bows again in thanks, then carefully takes a small bowl of cream and darts off. It's unclear whether she's not accustomed to sitting with you or eager to share it with someone.

You ask Inal to call Aziz too, to share this rare refreshment. She bows in surprise and then rushes to bring Aziz in, serving him a small bowl, watching him expectantly.

Aziz first thanks you, then sits beside Inal. His slow actions come with a peculiar elegance and composur, which is uncommon for a slave – as if he's used to such precious delicacies and is not in a rush.

But why? For the first time, you realize the slave you bought years ago is quite uncommon.

5006620.title: Betrayal and Escape
strings: Betrayal and Escape
You intend to lock Aziz up and deal with him after drawing a Bloodshed Card, but soon you heard that Aziz has escaped, and even took Inal with him…
Aziz has escaped.
He took Inal because following such a brutal master is unsafe.

It's the first time your slave has defied you so. In anger, you whipped the guard responsible, but it was all to no avail.

In your mind, Aziz posed no threat to you, and the entire city wouldn't offer him refuge, yet somehow, you find yourself restless for a long time...

5006621.title: A Huge Toy
strings: A Huge Toy
Aziz isn't entirely ignorant of what he will face, but like all slaves, he can't refuse such low-hanging fruit… Especially for a gift from such a beautiful lady.
Aziz
She will like this large toy.
Yourself
The Carnality Card up to Silver tier
Master and Slave
Fears and Gains
The courtiers and the Sultan are amused by your story.

This is Jalila's job, but that doesn't mean she is without passion and exploration about it.

Indeed, Aziz's crude yet firm soul will never yield to any whip...
But the Queen still has nimble and fierce hands, gentle yet stern feet, soft lips yet steely words...

In the end, she proudly displays to you the slave’s submission, like a trainer showing a tamed pet to the master.

You feel that some firm qualities have already vanished from the hunched giant frame... upon receiving the dog leash, you inexplicably understand the Sultan.

The heavy fruits require such sturdy branches. 
All day, Nayla stayed with Aziz, catering to him like a king – as long as he can satisfy Nayla's desires over and over again. 
Aziz did so. 
By the time the sun rose again, he was already covered in myrrh oil and honeydew, jeweled with precious gold and silver accessories, resting on a river-like soft bed while Nayla fed cheese, wines, and grapes from lips, all the while being attended to by slaves – one massaging him, one holding instruments of indulgence for any eventuality, and another kneeling at his feet for them together to humiliate and amuse... 
Finally, as the sun rose to its zenith, when Nayla once again requested satisfaction, Aziz gave a tired and irksome response. 
It ended his bliss. 
He was slapped, helplessly watching the three slaves strip him of each newly donned ornament before kicking him to the ground, to be insulted and trampled by Nayla again... in the end, you were left silently watching Nayla's game, feeling some of those firm qualities had already vanished within that prostrated massive frame... When Aziz cries for your help, you inexplicably understand the Sultan.
Even the court jester laughs along, as if you'd told a joke much better than the jester himself... really, although it is inexplicable, it is also a bit creepy.

5006622.title: Stone Lunchbox
strings: Stone Lunchbox
Bharat wants the Stone Lunchbox you are holding.
Only Aziz at your side has such craft.
After some time, you have Aziz grind a Lunchbox for Bharat. The merchant offers a fair price and looks forward to further cooperation.

5006623.title: Many Stone Lunchboxes
strings: Many Stone Lunchboxes
The lunchbox looks very practical, you want more. Aziz has no objection to his master’s decision, though this will take a lot of his time.
Only Aziz at your side has such craft.
Work like a Devil
After working day and night in a daze, Aziz presents you with three polished Stone Lunchboxes, hoping this will satisfy you.

5006624.title: Lunchbox Business
strings: Lunchbox Business
Bharat wants the Stone Lunchbox you are holding. He wants to buy it at proper and fair price.
The Stone Lunchbox Bharat wants to acquire.
Bring out as many as you have.
Keep some for your own use sounds good, too
You need to insert at least 1 Stone Lunchbox.
You've sold all the Lunchboxes.
You've sold 2 Lunchboxes.
You've sold 1 Lunchbox.
Bharat highly praises the quality of the Stone Lunchbox you presented, giving you 9 Gold Coins and promising to buy more when you have them!

You tell Bharat you don’t plan to make money from this because grinding these lunchboxes is too time-consuming. But in consideration of your friendship, you hand over two extra lunchboxes you had.
Though somewhat disappointed, he still offers a fair price.

You tell Bharat you don’t plan to make money from this because grinding these lunchboxes is too time-consuming. But in consideration of your friendship, you hand over one extra lunchbox you have.
He’s very disappointed; with only one, it’s impossible to market to caravans. Yet he buys it at a price where he won’t lose money.

5006625.title: The Sands of Time
strings: The Sands of Time
You harbor doubts about Aziz's origin, so you plan to call him over to make things clear.
These matters are only known to Aziz himself.
Perhaps he will accept some of your Convictions, perhaps not.
Insert the correct Conviction to unlock further plot

“Before becoming a slave, Aziz, what kind of person were you?” you ask.

Slowly, word by word, Aziz tells you his origins. He was raided by the Sultan's army from the western desert region when he was only ten, too young to understand; his height saved him from being chosen for the palace by the Sultan’s eunuchs, thus barely retaining his male dignity.
“I remember my father had five hundred camels, my mother was the most beautiful woman near the oasis, arms full of bracelets.”

He still speaks slowly, but his gaze shifts, seemingly looking at the moon, “When I wanted roast lamb, they let me choose from the flock. I knew which was the best meat, and I only ate the best. Sultan’s army would kill all sons of the leader, so when they came, my mother had me swap clothes with the maid’s son.”

What happened afterwards needs no further words. He ended up in the capital, and your steward chose him from the slave market. The vicissitudes of fate are truly moving. You sigh gently and look at Aziz again, feeling that this slave has somehow changed – the pride of old has seemingly returned to his body.

Silently, you suddenly ask him if he ever thought about redeeming his freedom.

Aziz still has no expression, appearing numb, calm, or perhaps hiding something. Slowly, he answers, saying if you permit, master, he would prefer to serve you.

5006626.title: The Master's Feast
strings: The Master's Feast
The banquet thrums with songs and banter, unaware of a guest never-seen-before about to arrive.
You decide to invite Aziz to join the feast.

Aziz washes his face at your courtyard's pond, reties his coarse cloth belt, then stands tall with princely confidence. “If you allow,” he says, “I am ready.” 
Aziz is seated, and it surprises everyone. But as you are the host and he stays beside you, no one dares question it. He calmly tastes each dish laid before him, slowly offering critiques now and then. 
Were it not for the coarse clothing and sunburned skin, he’d seem like a prince. Thus, people’s imagination paints this finically tasteful, nobly attired young slave in a rosy light. Rumors swiftly spread of [player.name] knowing a foreign prince. 
By the end of the feast, after all guests depart, he prostrates at your feet. “Please allow me to thank you; I feasted well, Master.”

5006627.title: The Feast for Everyone
strings: The Feast for Everyone
You have Aziz summon the servants; the feast for the guests has ended. A feast for everyone under this roof is about to begin.
You must attend yourself.
You have invited Aziz.
You can invite any follower.
You may invite anyone you wish to invite.

After sending off the last guest, Maggie half-jokingly asks what you’re planning. You bring her close and share your thoughts.

Maggie's cheeks have been lightly flushed with a hint of drunkenness – perhaps she drank earlier. You think she will scold you, for she has always been strict and unsmiling towards servants. But now, she smiles, whispering in your ear, “Sure, I'll go to the kitchen to cook a dish to reward everyone.”

You realize she has long been considered the servants as family. She understands everyone's concerns, knows the best place for each person, keeping the household running smoothly and worry-free. Each servant naturally gathers around her, often looking at her with admiration.

You have Aziz bring out the best wines from the cellar, toasting Maggie, naturally the servants toast Maggie too. Thus, the restraint and unease between you and the servants vanish completely.

After the last guest is sent off, the after-beast begins.

Unlike usual, the servants don’t gather in the kitchen but come to the candle-lit banquet hall, sitting on embroidered cushions. They feel somewhat uneasy, no one dares to speak, let alone touch the well-prepared delicacies on the plates.

But you have Aziz bring the best wine from the cellar and toast everyone.
“Tonight, I am no different from any of you, merely one among the masses, each of you possesses merits worthy beyond me. Let us toast this damned fate! At least tonight, we are all the masters here.”

Inal stands and cut the remaining meat for everyone. The enticing aroma of fruitwoods smoked lamb fills the room as the servants request larger slices from Miss Inal, then place the largest on Inal’s plate.

After a few more drinks, Zephyr find an Oud from somewhere, playing unfamiliar cheerful tunes. His off-key, tuneless songs provoke laughter from the crowd, yet he proudly claims he’s mastered the tavern poets’ art of entertaining!

Aziz sits beside you; before seating, he attentively cleaned his face and hands by the pond, tidying his clothes – judging by his demeanor, he could be a tribal chief. He calmly savors each dish before him, occasionally offering slow remarks.

Many, devastated by abrupt changes and fallen from grace, find only death as a release. Many slaves forget they were once lords of their lands. What about Aziz? Unfortunately, you ask again if he thought about buying his freedom.

Aziz looks at you; before answering, you signal him to wait with a hand gesture: “Come to me when you’re ready with your answer.”

He nods slowly, you are unsure if he's taken it to heart.

The moon climbs the palm tree cloud-like branches, under bright lights, the room seems free of any gloom. Class divisions, social barriers between companions all vanished, smiling, singing, drinking, relishing time eternal, fear forgotten at time's end.

5006628.title: Blow the Bone Flute
strings: Blow the Bone Flute
Blow it!
Bone Flute gifted by Aziz
Feeding more people inevitably costs more money. You need to contribute 8 Gold Coins.

That night, you tried it by the window; its sharp, trembling sound startled you. It seems designed for scouts to transmit orders, not for melodic pursuits. You blew it several times, ensuring its sound pierced through layers of smoke, reaching those it should. From that night, dark-skinned, tall men and women silently came under your roof... you fed them, showed them the Bone Flute, and they slowly nodded, swearing allegiance to you.

5006629.title: An Irresistible Comfort
strings: An Irresistible Comfort
For a moment, you have to admit, shadows deep within your soul stir restlessly. You notice Inal, the female slave Maggie brought with her, her cries suddenly spark your desires.
Inal trembles in fear, not daring to resist.
You decide to comfort Inal yourself
You can use this to break a Carnality Card of no higher than Inal tier.

You took Inal to your room, then leave. The young female slave, anxious, wished to escape but dared not. You return a day later, find her asleep on the carpet, tear stains dried on her face. As you awake her, she jolts, almost hitting her head. She greets you in a fluster, hurriedly saying it’s time to work, and you let her leave.
In any case, she should now know, the wolf in her dream wasn't as fearsome.
You embrace her.
This affair enraged Maggie greatly.

The young girl cried and begged you the whole time, her hands held obediently above her head, allowing you to ravage her without resisting her master. Blood dripped, flowed, forming a wound never to heal, a pain never to forget.

The girl is yours, but what have you lost?
Upon learning of the matter, Maggie slaps your face hard. You’ve never seen her so disappointed.
For several days afterward, you've slept poorly. You think you might have dreamt of Maggie, but cannot recall what she said or did.

When you break the card, some call you shameless for taking a girl against her will, others claim her lack of resistance means willingness. People argue about these in passion, however nobody concerns what did Inal think, nor anybody care about it.

5006630.title: Marriage
strings: Marriage

Maggie holds Inal's hand, her expression cold as she appraises you. At this moment, she seems less like Inal's master and more like a stern elder judging whether you're truly worthy of trust.
But Maggie, don't you know in your heart what's right?
You promise to marry Inal.
Preparing the wedding requires at least 5 Gold Coins.
You can use this opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of no higher than the Bronze tier
Marrying a slave doesn't need to be extravagant.

After the matter was settled, Inal knelt to the ground, crying and thanking both Maggie and you.
She should be grateful, after all, becoming a concubine means she's now a free person – a feat her family hasn't achieved in three generations.
However, her cries carry not only joy but also bitterness, sorrow, and endurance. She lost much more than freedom... though you neither know nor care what it is.
There are few who sincerely bless your marriage, many are accustomed to watching your performances and then wait for you to reveal a card.

5006631.title: Running Wildly All Night
strings: Running Wildly All Night
Your concubine Inal has eloped with a slave! If this disgraceful matter spreads, it would truly tarnish your reputation!
Escaped Inal
Escaped Aziz
You can do this yourself or send any follower to pursue them.
You can do this yourself or send any follower to assist.
Consumable
You can choose to send people to capture them, or you can let them go.
Furious, you send people to search everywhere for traces of their departure.
Not wanting to alert others, you carefully approach them.
With no other choice, you draw your scimitar against the wretched rogue who dared take your concubine.
Your Survival determines your full dice count.
Your Stealth determines your full dice count.
Your Combat dice count is affected by the Aziz attribute.
You need at least 3 Successes to find them.
You need at least 2 Successes to find them.
You need at least 1 Success to find them.

After deliberation, you eventually gave up on the pursuit.
You came to Maggie, asking if she heard Inal leave during the night. Maggie said no, she didn't seem angry about the slave's escape, just calmly poured some tea, and poured you a cup too.

Weary, you sit on the soft couch, now, you don't want to suspect your wife. Let Inal truly be free. At least Maggie hasn't left you, has she?
You discovered traces they left before leaving.
You failed to discern their whereabouts.
You aren't detected.
Inal spots you.
You kill Aziz.
You were injured by Aziz.
Following that direction, soon, you see a well-built figure in the distance, beside a petite one!
All is in vain. Aziz and Inal have disappeared! What can you do but curse them? You can only wish for them to be mercilessly destroyed by time. But don't forget, time marches on for everyone.
At last, in a deserted alley, you corner the elopers. Upon seeing you, Inal bursts into tears, while Aziz, expressionless, blocks Inal and slowly raises the sharp knife towards you.

She cries out, alerting nearby early-rising farmers. Thinking it is a thief, they lit lamps and come out with their knives. Upon seeing you, they whisper among themselves about why a courtier seated by the Sultan's side, a nobleman of unparalleled honor would come here for a woman gray in hair and pale in face? Overwhelmed, you lose sight of them, allowing Aziz and Inal to escape amidst the confusion. You return empty-handed.

Inal screamed, throwing herself on Aziz's corpse, desperately trying to cover his bleeding wound. But it was too late.
She stared with large tears dropping one after another. 
"Just kill me too, Master," she trembled, whispering, "I have wronged you, I am not a good slave, nor a good woman. I have caused the death of the man I loved... kill me!"
Yet, while you considered whether to forgive her, she had already seized the sharp knife Aziz had used and, without a second thought, slit her own throat. 
Perhaps it was the only decision she made for herself in her life. In the end, she was free.

You may have forgotten how fierce and strong a man can become to protect his loved one. If not for Inal's furious blocking, Aziz's sharp knife could have been in each of your throats. 

"We owe you nothing now," Inal courageously said to you before running off with Aziz. Suddenly, you lost the courage to send people after them, and you never heard from them again.

5006632.title: Never Leave Her Side.
strings: Never Leave Her Side.
That man has his eyes on Inal, so arranging for someone to protect her seemed natural. Hearing this, Aziz stands up and volunteers to do it. Whether to send him or not, it's your decision.
Startled Inal
You can send a non-noble follower to guard her.
Aziz gladly complies

You dispatch [s2.name] to temporarily protect Inal, so she can safely run errands. Just to see who dares to harass YOUR slave!

Aziz's massive body stays close to Inal, like a tempestuous yet tame big dog, giving her an unparalleled sense of security. With him by her side, she is no longer afraid of the wolves in her dreams!
You dispatch [s2.name] to temporarily protect Inal, so she can safely run errands. Just to see who dares to harass YOUR slave!

5006633.title: Make Peace
strings: Make Peace
Perhaps your manner of handing out money led him to misunderstand your stance, thinking you were weak and easy to deceive. He snorted and quoted an astronomical figure for compensation.
Troublemaking Noble
10 Gold Coins
You can choose not to send.
[s1.name] waited several days without seeing you bring the money, threatening to ruin you.

The noble's eyes darted around, searching for Inal behind you.
"I have a proposition, my lord," he smiles slyly, "if you sell me that slave, I could waive the compensation, perhaps even give you three – no, five Gold Coins. She's not worth that much, but I want what I desire. Consider carefully."
You coldly reject him, as she is your wife's dowry slave and will not be sold.
He starts to say more, but his companion pulls him aside, whispering a few words of caution against starting a conflict over a slave girl with a person in power... He reluctantly accepts your compensation, promising to drop the matter.
When Maggie heard, she was very pleased with your response, and you upheld the lady of the house's dignity to everyone.

5006634.title: Handle with the Slave
strings: Handle with the Slave
You agree to the troublemaking noble's proposal to send Inal to him.
Troublemaking Noble
You decide to send Inal to him.
You can choose not to send.
[s1.name] waited several days without seeing you bring the Inal, threatening to ruin you.
Never Provoke Witch

Inal remains composed when taken away, returning by evening. The nobleman's entire household had mysteriously perished. How could this frail slave girl possibly be responsible? You dismiss the investigating constable, though with no other leads, suspicion naturally falls upon you.

Inal cried heart-wrenchingly upon being taken away, but she's caused you enough trouble, and you don't lack an extra hand. 

The young noble was highly satisfied, not pursuing the matter of your servants hitting him, and even offering to support you as the "understanding" courtier in the court. 

Hearing of this, Maggie is very upset with your private decision regarding her dowry slave and become melancholic for days.

5006635.title: Private Investigation
strings: Private Investigation
Who dared to harass your slave girl, you're determined to root him out and make him pay for this.
You can investigate this yourself, or send a noble to handle the matter

You leverage some connections and finally learn about this person. His family's standing at court is far beneath yours, and he has a roguish look but considers himself as charming as Nabhani. What a joke! 

Since he dared make a move on your slave, you, the chosen one of the Sultan's game, will not let it go. What happens to him next is up to you.

5006636.title: How Dare You?
strings: How Dare You?
You knock on the presumptuous noble's door with the Sultan Card, demanding to know if he really wants to harass YOUR follower – even a slave girl.
Overestimated Noble.
You must show up yourself
You can intimidate him with a Silver Bloodshed, Carnality, or Conquest Card.
To use a Conquest Card, you must have an army, otherwise any helpful consumable can be placed here.
If planning to intimidate him with a Conquest card, bringing an army is more convincing.
Helplessly, you drew your sword. He wouldn't sit still waiting for death either.
Your Physique and Combat determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes.
Missing key card(s) to trigger the event
Your words made that noble tremble for a few days, but after that, without seeing any real action from you, he probably thought you were just bluffing and quickly resumed his activity in the court.
However, the Sultan finds out about it.
Your army mobilizes accordingly

You slaped the Sultan Card across his face, asking if he'd like to taste it. Briefly grimacing, he clenched his fists, but then bowed to you.
"Please forgive me," he apologized submissively, though deep down still unwilling, "But you can't blame me, it was your slave girl who seduced me. She's so beautiful, she looked at me among so many people, if not showing her willing..." 
Under your cold gaze, he swallowed the rest of his words.
Matters seemed to conclude in this way.

The Sultan curiously inquires what Sultan Card you brandished, then commands you to execute it.
He wants you to know he permits you to play this game, grants you these powers, but ultimately, he is the true master, and you're merely his entertainment.

He fell under your blade, ending his vile, pitiful life like a rat. Amidst the Sultan's laughter, you admitted you felt little pity for him – a man undeserving of sympathy.
You settled the matter with Inal honorably, and on returning, Maggie embraces you. She never finds you such dependable.
You died. Everyone laughs at you, dying for a lowly slave. Only your wife and followers loyal to you weep for you.

Though you were unwilling, you ultimately had no choice. The man jumped up terrified, dodging and fleeing across the court, captured only by the combined efforts of the guards, still desperately struggling and begging for mercy, his tears making that already unattractive face even more repulsive, and with that smelly, suspicious liquid dripping down between his legs.

Alas, was it worth it? Unlike you, he had not accustomed himself to accepting these things... Though, perhaps he should find it fortunate, at least, that he won't die. Such a man's flavor was hardly appealing... After a perfunctory ordeal, your grim face at last elicited a subtle smile from the Sultan. 

Even Maggie, upon hearing, couldn't criticize you harshly. What could be said... at least you resolved the affair with Inal. Rumor had it that the noble, having lost his face, left the capital overnight. 

You just wished whatever wind carried him away carry you with too.

His family, his lands, his dignity, all that he could boast of were ruthlessly crushed. The Sultan smiled, enjoying what he saw, moreover delighted by your army. Oh, what army! He watched as if a child rejuvinated in a toy he had long grown bored of. The Sultan's gaze pierced your back until you left the Court. He'll crush it all for amusement when you are most absorbed in it, just wait... ha ha. 

Though it brought much bloodshed, you sided with Inal to resolve the issue. Maggie doesn't blame you much... if anyone's to blame, blame the Sultan.

5006637.title: Deterministic Force
strings: Deterministic Force
The Sultan's guards accompany you to the doorstep. Poor Inal, she’s unaware of what awaits her.
Inal has been promised to the Sultan.
You can do nothing.

As she was taken away, Inal cried inconsolably, and your wife couldn't help but cry too. You embraced her and deeply regretted your powerlessness. 

The Sultan is very pleased with your compliance and rewards you like a beggar with some gold.

5006638.title: Melancholic and Disheartened.
strings: Melancholic and Disheartened.
After Inal entered the palace, Aziz was constantly sullen and even neglected his work...
Aziz is sullen.
At this moment, none might want to storm the palace and kill the Sultan more than him...
Any kind of Conviction of Rebellion is needed

You brought Aziz a pot of wine. "If you'll allow it." He unsealed it slowly, drinking deeply without reserve. Perhaps only wine offered solace to this disappointed man.
"I remember..." he sighed, his voice heavy as he recounted, "My father had five hundred camels and my mother was the most beautiful woman in the Western oases... We lost to the Sultan's army, they'd kill all the leader's children, so my mother exchanged my clothes with those of the maid's son..."
You were astonished; the usually silent, aloof giant had such a past. Unable to hold back, you asked if he ever considered buying back his own freedom.
Aziz looked at you, shook his head, then slowly replied, "In my eyes, the freedom of Inal bears more importance."

5006639.title: Tribulation
strings: Tribulation
You wish to offer the Sultan something else in place of Inal.
You have to handle this yourself.
Consumables to help convince the Sultan.
You choose to offer the Sultan 20 Gold Coins
You choose to offer the Sultan a gold tier equipment.
You choose to offer the Sultan another woman...
You can offer money, treasures, or more beautiful women to the Sultan.
Gold Coins are the simplest, yet also slapdash option. The Sultan will assess your sincerity; have you thought of an excuse?
You have 3 rounds to prepare this matter, or you will be executed by the Sultan.
For a mere slave, this is an unimaginable sum. The Sultan raised his eyebrows, seeming more intrigued by Inal.
Your Sociability and Wisdom determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes.
You have to make a choice

How dare you mock the great Sultan!
You were executed by the Sultan for not making timely tributes.
You convinced the Sultan.
The Sultan is not satisfied with your explanation.

Kneeling, you complained to the Sultan. Explaining your wife has a picky palate, only ever eating food made by Inal. If you give her to the Sultan – though everything in the world belongs to him – your wife might refuse to eat, wail, and take it all out on you... you're just someone afraid of his wife, hoping the Sultan would understand your uselessness...
The Sultan burst out laughing with his ministers, all mocking you thoroughly. He ultimately accepted the money. Thus, the Sultan's focus shifted away, and Inal was not mentioned again.
Maggie, upon hearing of such news, playfully slapped your hand, "Am I really that mean?" chuckled her with her hand covering hear mouth, "Many wives wishes from me to know how to control their husbands. Oh how I'd love to know that too!"
Regardless, through wisdom and willpower against the Sultan's anger, you kept her by your side, much to her delight.

Nothing you can say will stop the Sultan when he wants something; he waves his hand, ordering guards to take Inal from your home.
By the way, the money you offered earlier won't be returned.

The Sultan nods, accepts your gift. While he doesn't raise the issue again, you know he is displeased with your evasive attitude. It’s uncertain what might happen if someone fans the flames of it in secret...

You propose exchanging one woman for another; after all, offering a lowly, talentless female slave to the Sultan seems inappropriate... The Sultan glances at the [s5.name] you bring, pondering, then accepts your offer. 

However, it is expected that some will resent you for this decision.

You bring Maggie to court, telling the Sultan you are willing to exchange her for Inal. The Sultan seems momentarily stunned, then laughs heartily: "My clever, adorable [player.name], you’re finally fed up with your wife? I’ve heard so! Hahaha... Yes, yes, this makes sense." 
He motions for you to send Maggie to him. Maggie is furious, yet there is nothing to be said. The poignant silence severed all love and resentment between you, leaving you without ties that binds.
You'll never see each other again, but if there ever was a choice, you preferred to have been a stranger from the very beginning.

5006640.title: Deterministic Force
strings: Deterministic Force
The Sultan's guards accompany you to the doorstep. Poor Inal, she’s unaware of what awaits her.
The Sultan wants this slave named Inal. Perhaps she’s not beautiful or useful, but the Sultan desires her.
You have 3 rounds to hand over Inal, or face execution.
You were executed by the Sultan for disobedience, for not even willing to present a mere female slave.

As she was taken away, Inal cried inconsolably, and your wife couldn't help but cry too. You embraced her and deeply regretted your powerlessness. Courtiers that once held you in high regards now shudder to think what might happen to them in your hands – seeing your inability to save even a slave girl.

5006641.title: Confrontation at Court
strings: Confrontation at Court
You persuade the Sultan. He orders the guards to summon in the troublesome noble who disturbed your home. Allegedly, he is at home holding a large banquet; probably celebrating how he outwitted you.
Troublemaking Noble.
You have to handle this yourself.
Some items might help you win this verbal war.
You have 3 rounds to prepare this matter, or you will be executed by the Sultan.
The noble is clueless as he is brought to the court. Only at the sight of you does he finally realize what is happening. A heated verbal battle thus unfolds once more at court.
Your Sociability and Combat are influenced by the opponent's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 2 Successes
You enraged the Sultan by proposing a confrontation but fleeing at the last moment. He executed you without hesitation.

You harshly scold the scoundrel for flirting with anyone, especially favoring women of higher-ranking courtiers, displaying a despicable, distorted mindset – He won't even spare a slave girl! 
Though you could forgive him for flirting with your slave, using lies to cover his nature, exaggerating a mere common slave to mislead the radiantly divine Sultan – it's treason! As the Sultan’s most loyal servant, you wouldn't allow such an act! 
The man was struck speechless by your excoriation, his attempts to retort repeatedly cut short. Your words were forceful, confidently uttered and impactful. Finally, the Sultan was satisfied, waved his hand and said: "Death." 
The scoundrel was executed on the spot, blood soaking the floor. He had wrought it upon himself.
In your return, you recounts the event to Maggie, who nods and agrees he deserved it. You protect the girl she views as family, and in her eyes, you've never been more dependable on.

When Inal was mentioned, the scoundrel’s enthusiasm flared. He praised Inal to be incredibly enchanting, as beautiful as a fairy. No matter how you argued, the Sultan was unmoved. He waved his hand, commanding the guards to retrieve the intriguing slave from your home.

5006642.title: Free Will
strings: Free Will
Inal redeems her freedom, and from today, she is no longer a slave.
Inal is a free person now.
You may give Inal an Accessory
The gift you give Inal can enhance her ability.
You hand Inal the gift you prepared.

She receives her identification from you and Maggie, becoming a free citizen from now on. Tears well up in her eyes. Never before had she thought she could be free, something that hadn't thought of, much less done, for three generations before her.
Maggie embraces her, while you inquire about her future plans. She froze for a moment, as if suddenly realizing that she could now “plan” her life.
"May I... continue working for the Lady? I like this job!"
Why wouldn’t that be possible? You and Maggie exchange glances, smiling faces met in each other's eyes.

Inal is astonished, only accepting the small box after repeated confirmation. As a slave, she had no right to own anything. Aside from her identity papers, this is her first possession, a real possesion. Regardless of its value, it is filled with blessings and hopes... Inal is overwhelmed with gratitude. It is as if she was born into this world once again.

5006643.title: Lengthy Inquiry
strings: Lengthy Inquiry
Nawfal found the High Constable. It seems he wants to figure what the hell is going on with the pardon you've been given for the crime of murder.
You can handle this yourself, or send a follower.
Consumables that assist you in looking up books
You can decide whether to respond to this matter. After all, it is a privilege given by the Sultan, no one can take it away from you, except him.
You plan to find all the reasonable and legal evidence from this...
Your Wisdom and Sociability determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes.

The High Constable and several scribes go through all the imperial law codes and barely, but absolutely, manage to prove that it is indeed legal for you to play the murder game on behalf of the Sultan. 
Outwardly, no one say anything, but everyone knows that it is simply because no one dares to defy the Sultan's will in their hearts. Hearing this outcome, Nawfal clenches his fists in anger, but at this point, he can not change this established fact – just as he was unable to stop the Sultan’s many past absurdities.

You spend time in the extensive archives to find an ancient document, displaying it at court, eloquently explaining that playing the game and killing in the Sultan’s stead is legal. 

Hearing this outcome, Nawfal clenches his fists in anger, but at this point, he can not change this established fact – just as he was unable to stop the Sultan’s many past absurdities.

strings: Palace Gate Donation
Nawfal initiated a fundraiser at the palace gates, for the displaced people and for the war-torn lands.
3 Gold Coins, probably
You can decide to donate or not.

You gave him a cold look and walked away nonchalantly without giving a single coin. Nawfal had already anticipated this and snorted, continuing his speech on the busy street, hoping that his words might still bring him some useful gold.
Nawfal repeatedly cited your indifference and stinginess as a negative example, and naturally, your reputation among the people diminished.

As you pass by, you casually toss a few coins in, giving him a challenging look. Now, surely, Nawfal has nothing to say. He has no courage to throw the money back at you.

Although Nawfal doesn't believe in your kindness, the money has indeed helped many people. With a cold face, he expresses what seems to be a rather insincere thanks to you.

You gave him a cold look and walked away nonchalantly without giving a single coin. Nawfal had already anticipated this and snorts, continuing his speech on the busy street, hoping that his words would bring him truly useful gold.
Nawfal repeatedly cited your indifference and stinginess as a negative example, and naturally, your reputation among the people diminished.

You pose the question to [s4.name], wanting to hear [s4.gender(his, her)] perspective.
A busy day, you didn't take the time to discuss the matter with anyone.

At a banquet, you talk about it with your colleagues, eliciting a burst of laughter from them.

Charity is the nobles' way to flaunt their jewels, and the glimmer from those jewels can temporarily fill the poor's stomachs. But do the nobles truly wish to feed the poor? If they did, the next time they want to show off how generous they are, wouldn't there be fewer poor clamoring for that bowl of porridge?

That's what they think. This perspective ripples in your mind.

You condescent to mingle with the commoners and ask how to end their poverty once and for all?

The answers are varied: “Give me money, sir! I want... a hundred gold coins!”
“Marry me, though I have three kids... but they're well-behaved!”
“Make me a noble! I want to earn money without working like you do!”

...You can't tell them that nobles have their own troubles. Right now, your life is divided into [sudan_life_time] days, [sudan_life_time] days, and another [sudan_life_time] days...

You go to the temple to talk to the devout priests, as they most frequent commoners and always appear the most kind and gentle. They smile as they receive your offering and then tell you the best way to help the poor is to deepen their faith. In the eyes of the divine, humans are ranked not by status but by the strength of their faith.

That's what they think. This perspective ripples in your mind.

[s4.gender] pauses and tells you the best way to help the poor is to assist the mothers. A mother's poverty is transmitted to her children, and to give her children a better life, a mother will fight like a lioness and be cunning like a wolf.

So it is. This perspective ripples in your mind.

[s4.gender] pauses and tells you that to help the poor, the best solution is to elevate their status.
The poor are impoverished because what they deserve is taken by the rich. If the gap between statuses is closed, the poor will naturally reclaim what is theirs.

Perhaps so. This perspective ripples in your mind.

Your question elicits a burst of laughter from [s4.gender]. [s4.gender] suggests that instead of helping these useless poor people, one should utilize them, exploit them, treat them as fodder — to liberate them from their unfortunate lives is the real help.
Is that so? This perspective ripples in your mind.

[s4.gender] confidently tells you that the poor are poor because they lack skills and cannot teach their children, thus becoming dispensable parts.
Therefore, to help them, they should be taught crafts and skills, making them irreplaceable and necessary. Then they will always have their fill.

Perhaps [s4.gender] is right. This perspective ripples in your mind.

[s4.gender] shrugs and casually says that the way to help the poor is to lead them to rob, invade, and deceive. After all, the wealthy and the noble have accumulated their wealth through such means; what's wrong with taking it back?

This perspective ripples in your mind.
You ponder day and night, gradually organizing some vague thoughts in your mind...
This perspective offers nothing new; you find no valuable reference in it.
Although you and Nawfal are at odds, and though he probably no longer cares about your answer, reflecting on the question he posed has still benefited you greatly.
Although Nawfal is gone, and that he can no longer hear your answer, reflecting on the question he posed has still benefited you greatly.
How can we help the poor escape poverty? You seem to have a conclusion in mind, eager to share it with Nawfal.
How can we help the poor escape poverty? You don't seem to have an answer, but it doesn't stop you from seeking Nawfal to talk about it face to face.
How can we help the poor escape poverty? You don't seem to have an answer, but it doesn't stop you from seeking Nawfal again.

5006647.title: A Mother's Drop
strings: A Mother's Drop
You plan to implement the scheme you and Nawfal discussed in your territory, spending some money to help those mothers struggling in despair.
Nawfal covered half the cost, you still owe 6 Gold Coins
You need to provide enough Gold Coins

You spent some money to give each impoverished mother in your territory a pair of chickens and a pair of goats, promising that if they raise them well, they can receive another pair next year.

These mothers, with tattered clothes, often carrying infants on their backs and leading others by the hand, listened patiently and remembered carefully. They assigned tasks to their young children on who would care for the chicken coop and who would clean the goat pen. You also sent people to warn these women’s husbands that if they dared slaughter the livestock for meat or sell them for wine, they would be severely punished.

You share this with Nawfal, who nods and remarks, "I believe they can do it."
Perhaps. The droplets of water held in mothers' palm may someday gather into a river.

Soon after, you discover that Nawfal's porridge stall is open again, but this time, there seem to be far fewer people lining up. From a distance, you see Nawfal, who gives you a knowing, barely perceptible smile.

5006649.title: Changes Brought
strings: Changes Brought
Once again, you arrive at that secluded manor. You know Nawfal is waiting for you; regarding changes in the territory, he probably has something to tell you.
Nawfal is waiting for you
You must attend the appointment in person.

In private, Nawfal couldn't hide his excitement.
"As you can see, I've done as you said in my own territory. Now, the women have livestock to look after, milk and eggs to eat, and a future to contemplate – they stay, so their men and children stay, too."

This way, there are fewer wandering vagrants coming to his porridge stall for charity.

"I always knew!... I always knew you could do it." He grips your hand firmly, looking at you with solemn seriousness, "You can change this country."
And you give a slight smile, telling him he's wrong, it's "us" – perhaps many, many of "us" – who can truly make the change here.

He understands what you mean, you two need more comrades, more like-minded people, but it still requires time.

5006650.title: God's Grace
strings: God's Grace

You gather the poor together and then pay the temple priests to host a grand ceremony. They distribute food and read scriptures, preaching that suffering is a necessity and a divine test; only through this can sinners cleanse their souls’ filth, return with purity to the divine's presence and head to the eternal white distant shore... Many people sing hymns through tears, and in the endless sands, this place seems like the only haven.

You gathered the poor together, then showed them the miracle of the dark night. You concocted a elixir with animal blood, certain herbs, spices and invited everyone to drink, telling them that after daylight's arduous toil, the night would bring the sweetest and most joyful dreams. People were entranced by your enticing whispers, murmuring praised to an unknown, vague name.
Nawfal watched all night, tight-lipped, and only questioned you after everything ended. You smiled, using the prepared excuse: only secret faith can unite people, and besides, you did nothing to harm them – the every radiant gold leaf in the temple was extricated from the devotees' wallets by dubious means.
Nawfal sighed gently and left the scene without word.

5006652.title: Unchanged
strings: Unchanged
Once again, you arrive at that secluded manor. You know Nawfal is waiting for you; regarding changes in the territory, he probably has something to tell you.

Nawfal witness the cruelty and bloodshed beneath the veil of deception... Even though people fervently pray for the New World's arrival and no longer come to his porridge stall for charity, this isn't what he wants. After politely telling you these things, Nawfal asks you to leave the manor. You know he no longer trusts you.

In private meetings, Nawfal no longer hides his emotions. He sighs softly, and after this time, he truly sees the monks' meticulous haggling beneath their righteous facade. They preach kindness, salvation, purity, only to squeeze the last coin from their followers' already sparse purses...

This deeply disappoints Nawfal. This is not the true path of redemption, so, where should the path lead?

In private meetings, Nawfal doesn't hide his thoughts anymore. During this time, he has witnessed the cruelty and bloodshed, as well as the hypocrisy of kindness and salvation. "The divine's power cannot change this land," he shakes his head, "But if even the divine cannot do something, then why is He worshipped as a 'deity'?"

You remain silent and contemplate about it. Perhaps only time will provide the answers.

You quickly ensure no one is teaching the residents how to be tomb raiders since your ancestral graves are within the territory.

“They won't do anything to your family’s graves, my lord. They'll be grateful to you!” [s2.name] says with a smile on their face, "As the saying goes, a pair of skilled hands is a tool for gold, and you have granted them endless gold!"

strings: Bringing Hope
Once again, you arrive at that secluded manor. You know Nawfal is waiting for you; regarding changes in the territory, he probably has something to tell you.

In private, Nawfal couldn't hide his excitement.

“Fewer people are coming to beg for porridge. Those who were considered lazy and parasitic among the poor have begun to learn skills. I know many will give up... but if even one person can feed themselves with their craft, others will see hope – yes, what we give them is not just a skill, but... ‘hope.’” He quietly chews over this word, eyes fix on you.

“[player.name],” he lowers his voice, calling your name almost in a whisper, “we should persist in this matter, and beyond that... we can do something more, something bigger... something impactful.”

You clearly see in this secret ally’s eyes a glow of something shimmering. In spreading hope to the poor, are you not also passing hope to each other, no?

But you and Nawfal plan to create a legendary hero – it abhors evil, its rage as fierce as fire, its movements elusive as smoke, wielding a burning holy sword, avenging all the hopeless and oppressed people.

Red cloth strips riveted to the helmet depicting eyes of wrath, vermilion leather armor adorned with bright bronze trimmings... Weapons oiled, ready to ignite and frighten at critical moments, and five eloquent bards purse clanking with your coins... This is starting to get interesting.

This wealthy merchant, relying on relatives in the court and hired thugs, monopolizing the milling and oil-pressing business of thirty villages... His warehouse grows fuller, while the poor are driven to such desperation that they can't even eat the wheat they grow... It's time for the King of Flames to enact justice.

Standing upon the corpses of the merchant and soldiers, the King of Flames directed the hungry, urging them to distribute the overflowing wheat and olive oil... He handed bags of coins to those who still had courage in their eyes, instructing them to bring it back to their villages... 

This night onward, the legend of the King of Flames began...

The King of Flames aimed to play hero but was accidentally surrounded by a dozen soldiers... In the end, it blazed its way to a path of escape, barely evading capture by shedding its disguise under cover of night. 

The next day, the hero you and Nawfal meticulously crafted, well, the shell of that hero, was hung on a large tree alongside the five farmers who colluded with it, swaying together in the wind.

5006658.title: Vengeance in Justice
strings: Vengeance in Justice

There is a brutal and strong warrior whose hobby is hunting humans – especially young slave girls. In nearby forests and wilderness, corpses of people cut in two after being humiliated by him are often seen... It’s time for the role to change.

In the past, this was just nonsense comforting the humiliated... 

Now, the King of Flames is here, the messenger of wrath and revenge! As the ruthless warrior's bifurcated body was found at the city gate, every village sings the ballad of the King of Flames, countless mud walls are adorned with its terrifying visage – it's a mark of shelter to the kind, and a cursed, fearful emblem to the wicked...

The helmet of the King of Flames was split by the scoundrel's giant sword... Thankfully, there was enough cowhide padding inside... Eventually, it blazed its way to a path of escape, barely evading capture by shedding its disguise under cover of night.
The next day, the hero you and Nawfal meticulously crafted, well, the shell of that hero, was displayed by that scoundrel as a trophy, while more than one innocent body remained in the wilderness.

5006659.title: Terror Manor
strings: Terror Manor

This minor lord’s family has a long-standing renown for kindness – what but merely a facade. Evidence that Nawfal holds confirms they are the main sponsors of the local slave trade and possess a hereditary tradition of evil practices... They continuously 'consume' slaves to satisfy some twisted sadistic desires. When slaves are insufficient, ignorant commoners nearby disappear...Yet these crimes mean nothing before The Sultan, and the law is powerless against him – only the King of Flames can execute justice.
King of Flames
No check required
Cruelty Spreads
Exceeded My Expectations
Blood Gathered

The King of Flames had little trouble disarming the lord. His soldiers dared not confront the legendary bringer of justice... and under his guidance, the farmers armed themselves, finding the bone-laden cellar... Some even found their long-lost loved ones.
Quickly, things spiraled out of control. What should have been an executed ceremony personally overseen by the King of Flames turned into a massacre by the wrathful farmers – the already disarmed lord's soldiers, imprisoned servants, and housekeepers, including the entire lord’s family... his wife, three sons, five daughters, along with two toddlers and a infant, were all hacked by scythes, smashed with shovels, and hung with pitchforks... displayed in front of the burning manor.
Even the King of Flames couldn't, or dared not, stop the furious crowd; their anger pent up too long, their suffering deep as it is unleashed, their power shocking, their cruelty unspeakable.

After Nawfal heard about this, the silence hung in the air for time uncountable. Finally, he pleads with you not to let the King of Flames appear again for the time being... “Perhaps we're not ready, perhaps the people aren't ready either.” He seems a bit sorrowful, revealing a rare vulnerability, as if the events have worn away some of his sharp edges.

Amidst chaos, the manor burns fiercely, blood flows like rivers. Madness and death, anger and revenge, spiral into the sky along with ash and howls, rising high – until awakening something darker.
Under the guidance of mysterious powers, the King of Flames begins slaughtering the remaining residents, who only dance frenetically, desecrate corpses, and wail, showing no resistance.
When the last body is thrown into the fire, with no other living soul in the manor, all the blood – whether soaking in the soil, burning in the flames, or flowing through water – rise and gather onto the King of Flames’ sword, armor... then seep into the mask’s opening, filling the interior...
This is the scene you and Nawfal’s retinue see upon arrival: the birth of a monster.
Realizing how deep into darkness you’ve ventured, Nawfal silently distances himself from you.

5006660.title: Courage and Unity
strings: Courage and Unity

After some time of adventure and operation, the King of Flames has become a genuine myth in the mortal world – it has its followers, its cult, and even numerous imitators dressed similarly to rob the rich to help the poor... or simply to commit crimes. Of course, this is still far from being impactful enough to sway fates, but undoubtedly, it is a very valuable attempt.

On Nawfal's suggestion, you plan to let the King of Flames be silent for a while: on one hand, to continue observing how the people awakened to rebellion will develop, and on the other, to avoid the secret of the King of Flames being exposed – The Sultan's best High Constable has already begun investigating the matter. 

But regardless, you all know that one day, the King of Flames will return...

5006661.title: Call of the Flames
strings: Call of the Flames
The time has come. You know this armor, this form, this burning soul will not remain silent for long. The flames of rebellion are burning intensely, and the King of Flames is about to return.

When the armor of the King of Flames is filled by the brave's flesh once more, those angry people, those wronged souls, those voices of the poorest and hungriest – converge like a meteor shower.
The flames of revenge burn brightly. It is no longer just a normal armor, no longer merely a man-made idol. It is the soul of vengeance, the nightmare of those oppressors and deprivers.
Ignoring your words, the King of Flames walks straight out of the vault that holds it – leaving a fiery trail... By the time you catch up, hundreds of fervent people are fully armed, ready to set the world ablaze with the King of Flames.

strings: The Crossing of Clear Streams

Although Nawfal says there is nothing to hide, the atmosphere at the banquet clearly becomes more restrained and suppressed with your arrival, as if this really is just a normal, ordinary feast your family often has.
But Nawfal’s wine is really good! 
Half of your reason for pretending to be the Sultan’s jester, is to lull them into lowering their guard and muddling through today’s events, but the other half is for indulging in the wine. You drank cup after cup until, amid this bizarre atmosphere, the voices speaking loudly and passionately become less clear, until someone suddenly calls your name.

He loudly calls your name, resentfully, “[player.name], why did you agree to participate in that absurd game? If you refused, perhaps The Sultan would have given it up!” 
 – everyone here knows which game he means.

“Ha! Why refuse? Providing a mere morsel of entertainment to our supreme, unparalleled Sultan, isn’t that the duty of us subjects?”
Your smug, flattering response provokes loud jeers, evidencing that those gathered around Nawfal share similar political views.
“Shameless!” The young man turns red and white with anger. “You're—you’re usurping The Sultan’s authority, you...!” He bites his lip and halts his speech, as though you have exasperated him.
The young man’s outrage is genuine, but what can he do? The situation is already set in stone. 
Immediately, another man approaches you. A fat, middle-aged noble, whose name you can not recall. 
He looks at you with more flattery and eagerness, clearly also muddled by drink.

“I wish I could! But wouldn’t that mean my death? The Sultan will just find another unlucky fool... like you, you, or... ha, like Nawfal! Ha, you think the Sultan hasn’t toyed with you because he doesn’t want to? We’re all queued up, necks on the same line, waiting for the axe!” 

You laugh heartily, the young noble lowers his head in silence, while a fat noble clings to your shoulder, exuding the smell of liquor as he speaks, clearly quite drunk...

“I wish I could become you!” he slurs, “I heard you can request women from the Sultan’s harem under a pretense of carnality! There are so many, so many beauties in the Sultan’s harem! My God... I can only imagine such pinnacle...”
You laugh heartily at this...

But Nawfal, ha ha ha! You almost want to see Nawfal's expression right now – his group isn’t lacking for such libertines!
You skillfully pull an earnest, yet ambiguous, expression, and wav your hand, saying, “The merciful, great Sultan has pardoned your offenses, but you should never take pride in it! No one should covet the Sultan’s women; that’s the greatest disloyalty and defiance!”
Then you change the subject, saying any attempt to approach women touched by the Sultan's imperial power will find normal men can’t arise their interest at all, no matter how much effort you exhaust; you’d only be met with scornful chuckles.
The fat noble nods half-believingly, and people were somewhat silenced, seemingly weighing their strengths against the Sultan...
Until Nawfal makes an awkward cough awaking them from their trance. The fat middle-aged noble's face shows deep shame.
Nawfal casts you a cold glance, says nothing and orders all the wine removed. In fact, before this, they had never served wine at these gatherings; they had never seen each other’s drunken states before.

“No, no,” you drunkenly say, “is there really anything good about those women in the harem? The Sultan stuffed all the women of potentially opposing families in, even some dethroned princesses...What kind of life can these women lead, abused, dominated, monitored, manipulated daily...only our Sultan gets any joy from it!” 
You say while sighing deeply, “Ahhh! My current life’s no different from those women‘s...Enough said! Come! Brother, let’s have another drink!”
“Enough.” Nawfal spoke. He frowns at you two who hug and cry for each other, waving a hand to order the wine removed.
In actuality, earlier gatherings never served wine; no one had seen each other’s embarrassing drunken states before.

An elderly minister awkwardly clears his throat, forcibly ending the indecent topic, and, with a piece of cheese bread at hand, brings up the famine outbreak in many parts of the country recently. The more he speaks, the more enraged he becomes, almost hoarsely accusing the Sultan of refusing to aid the disaster-stricken citizens! 

People deeply sympathize with him because his territory is located in the most affected area, and he can only watch as his subjects starve to death... They vent their anger, criticize, and speak more and more outrageously, emotions spiraling out of control...

Does Nawfal care about nothing anymore? Isn’t he afraid someone will overhear?
You make a noise, raise the cup, and throw leftover wine in the face of that elderly noble, the drunkenness softening the fierceness in your eyes but still enough to sober a person. “Had enough?” You grab his collar, nearly lifting the frail elder before pushing him back. “How dare you question our fair and all-knowing Sultan? Huh, if everyone desires The Sultan’s attention for their territory’s affairs, wanting the treasury to be particularly generous, here would’ve been chaos a long while ago! Ha ha ha...if you don’t want to starve, then you, you, and you are the ones to starve...!”
You nearly press noses with them as you point, laughing heartily, returning to your seat with a drunken stagger, yelling for more wine!
“Bring a few more pitchers of fine wine! Let us toast the empire, toast The Sultan, toast...hic, toast the eternal sun!”
No one responds to your toast. The banquet ends in a not-so-joyful atmosphere. Nawfal orders the drunken you to be escorted out by servants and placed into your carriage.

You casually throw your arm around the elderly noble’s shoulders, squeezing his mournful face, laughing, “You’ll see, The Sultan won't even think of saving you, stop hoping! He saves his own territory first, then the nobles who willingly pay tribute, and at last, the very last of the last—it’s you lot with no grease and no insight, pests annoying the daylights out of him! Ha ha ha...if you don’t starve, who will?”
The elderly noble's face flushes, wanting to rebuke, but ultimately weakly nods, “You’re right. I’m doomed! We’re all doomed...”
Nawfal’s face darkens, ordering the raucously drunken you removed and placed into your carriage.

You’re unsure how you get home, and it’s past morning by the time you wake up... Oh, what a mess, you can only recall barging into Nawfal's banquet, but details after the third drink escapes your memory.
You pray nothing bad has happened...

A cold wind cuts across your sweaty back, bringing a chilling sting. The feeling of being scrutinized, like needles pricking your back, finally fades as you board the carriage...Only now do you have the clarity to review tonight's yield.
A gut feeling tells you there is a spy lurking at Nawfal's banquet. 
 – You're almost certain it's the young noble, despite his well-crafted disguise, what he didn't realize was, while he monitored you, you also watched him. Besides questioning and aping others’ perspectives, he never presented his own...
The only issue remaining is, should you tell Nawfal this?

You nod and agree.

After confirming the traitor's identity, Nawfal acts quickly and decisively. 
Later, Nawfal quietly finds you, looking somewhat weary. He tells you that the Young Noble was working for the Vizier, with whom he had long-standing discord. 
"Our young people shouldn't be like this. They were meant to be the clearest in judgment, the most ambitious, never extinguished hope," Nawfal shakes his head, sighs, and gifts you a jug of wine, perhaps noticing how you seemed to enjoy it at the banquet.
 "Anyway...thank you."

His eyes gleam coldly, but you only stare at his scarred hands hidden under his sleeves: "Do you think you can leave here?"
"Of course." A hint of a reassuring smile flashes across his face, quickly masked by a piercing pride, "Just wait and see, you dirty maggots!"
"We will." Internally relieved, you maintain an expressionless face, dropping a curt remark before leaving.

A few guards lead you through filthy, dark corridors and then open the cell door. 
You leisurely walk up to Nawfal, looking at his slender wrists and neck under the blood-soaked and filthy cloak. His health is so depleted by the prolonged torment that even the sound of you drawing the dagger does not awaken his tightly closed eyes. 
To the end, he did not struggle or make a sound of plea or pain, making your killing feel utterly flavorless. 
You wiped the dagger clean on his sleeve, clicked your tongue, and left the boring prison without looking back.

By then, people will just think he goes mad for a male prostitute anyway! After all, now this male prostitute's deep and complicated relationship with him has been retold in over a dozen versions.

"For a mere filthy prostitute, your reputation, your principles, your standing – all destroyed! Nawfal sighs deeply, shakes his head, and says, "Poor guy, you've been turned into the best servant by what you hate the most."
"Poor?! What qualifies you – " Abdul's face contorts with rage, but then he sees, the ropes binding Nawfal fall loose, and you remove the cloth over your head. At this signal, your people quickly rush into this courtyard, overpowering the few guards present.
Abdul looks at you and Nawfal, confused as to how you can stand together. But questioning is futile, the tide has turned, no amount of begging, howling, flattering, or promising will help. You and Nawfal kill him without hesitation.

Nawfal realizes you're once again linking this to the Sultan Cards. With a resigned sigh, he accepts the money: "At least the children will have better meals now..."

The next day, you stand before the court, announcing that you've spent a considerable sum renovating a building to feed the city's beggars. You believe this justifies discarding the Extravagance Card. Yet the Sultan appears to be in an unusually good mood. His simple 'Oh?' is followed by a barrage of questions. You struggle to keep Nawfal's involvement hidden while trying to discourage any royal visits... It is a very challenging day.

5006676.title: Nursery
strings: Nursery
Children gather in your garden, flourishing under your care and guidance. What future will these tender seedlings bloom into? No one knows.
Nawfal came to the nursery you built together
You teach them what love is
You tell them what true wisdom is
You guided them on what faith means
You lead them to know what strength to rely on
You lead them to seek what kind of happiness
Sheltered Orphans
First Lesson

"Only kindness, children – only kindness is true strength. Show kindness to your enemies, and no less to yourself... Never let your world grow small – let kindness guide your path. Don't let petty feelings hold you back. Love all people, and devote your heart to greater goals – that is where your strength lies."

Through the door, you hear Nawfal passionately spouting his nonsense again. You desperately bite your tongue, fighting every urge to burst in and embarrass him in front of the class.

Nawfal is unaware of what you're thinking. After class ends, he finds you. H He seems absorbed in some new idea, silent and contemplative until the last child leaves. In the empty mansion, only faint moonlight remains, gently swaying among the tree shadows.

Nawfal looks up, fixes his gaze upon you, and slowly says, "Do you know? Standing on the podium today, seeing so many innocent faces, I suddenly realize something." His voice is soft, yet his words carry profound weight, "What I hope for isn't – or rather, not just – to overthrow the Sultan's rule, not a mere change of dynasty, not letting our country cycle through one wise or wicked Sultan after another..."

"I want to completely transform these children's futures," his striking eyes burn with a clear flame, "exactly as we're doing right now."

5006677.title: Nursery
strings: Nursery
Compared to this humble shelter, all other treasures you built fade away – for what is stored here is the most precious and beautiful treasure of all: the future.
Shelter and Educate
5 Gold Coins, indispensable
