You will take them away, all for the world
With utmost humility and reverence, you invite the Sultan to offer his invaluable guidance

The children kneel trembling in front of the Sultan, then take turns performing on your cue.

Such tender voices! Their poems praise the Sultan's glorious achievements. Such supple waists! They dance with a charming youthful awkwardness. And then, one of them quietly sneaks up and steals the pouch of coins you carry, offering it to the Sultan. Your face, turning ashen with anger yet unable to utter a word, draws a hearty burst of laughter from the Sultan. Whether planned or not, the Sultan is thoroughly delighted. He even pats a few of the children on their heads, and then takes away the most outstanding one.
You led the children into the nursery.
You brought Little Moon to the Nursery; both delighted in one another's company.
Maggie doesn't say much to the children here; she simply visits regularly to gently care for them, bandage their wounds, and teach them how to share both food and kindness with friends.

"There's no trick in the world – treat a dog well, and the dog treats you well. Dogs are very smart! Smarter than most people! They understand everything... Learn from them!" Faris suddenly changes the subject, catching you off guard. "By the way, do you need some puppies here?" he asks, fixing his gaze on you.

You firmly refuse. No more mouths freeloading in this school.

Jalila teaches these children her secrets to finding footing in this city without reservation: "Always be loyal to yourself, my little darlings, don't give your love, your expectations, and your heart to anyone, not even the Sultan... Love has magnetism. The more you love yourself, the more others will love you."

"You don't need to believe in any tangible god, although it's fine to have one to believe in — the point is, you need a goal! You need something to chase, something to climb toward until you get closer to your ideal. Listen carefully now. Faith isn't for self-consolation; it's your destination, your purpose!" When Adila speaks, the light in her eyes intertwines with the children's longing.

Faraj spends nearly the entire lesson boasting about your deeds, only to conclude with this: "To live a good life, to do the right thing, to achieve greatness – none of this is possible without a great and wise leader! A wise leader can guide us toward the future, while a tyrant or a fool will lead us to ruin... Look around you – everything you see here is brought to you by [p layer.name]! Since you met him, think about how your lives have changed!"

Lumera teaches the children to read and write, often sharing stories and exploring books together.

"Why do you learn so quickly?" the children often ask Lumera. She simply smiles and replies, "It's because I believe in what's written in the books. Knowledge works like that – only when you truly believe in it can you use it effectively."

"I'm the smartest woman in town? Thank you for saying so, but I've just lived through more," Shama says, smiling gently as the children gather around her. "Life brings you all sorts of things – poverty, pain, danger, peace... and yes, physical and emotional pleasures too, though you're a bit young to hear about these..."

"Someday, you'll understand what I mean. But remember this: No matter what you experience, there will always be another deeper door opening before you; but you don't need to keep walking through one door after another... Don't experience just for the sake of experiencing! Your early life experiences are meant to help you find where to stop... Don't make the same mistakes I did."

"Well, well, look who's here! You poor boys got lucky today – Uncle Jawad is the only one who can teach you anything useful!" Jawad apparently enjoys the children's adoring gazes, "The most important thing for humans is to earn! Earn money! Buy low, sell high! It's not just about money; think about everything – how can you profit from it? Of course, once you earn money, you basically have everything!"

"Hey, kid, don't get distracted! Write it down! Every tiny detail I say next will make you earn big in this lifetime! What? How to write 'earn'? Damn… Coming here is a real loss."

"Oh, you're not here to learn cooking from me... But everything else is similar! Cooking is all about managing! Everything in life can be managed just like you manage food! Take roasting meat, for instance…" 
Habib goes on for a while, and soon, all the children's mouths are watering uncontrollably. Seeing this, he has no choice but to set up a pot, arrange the utensils, and start cooking with the children.

The essence of strength is to live like the characters in the poems... Once you choose this path, living this way comes naturally! This is how the most beautiful stories unfold – yes, this is the power of romance!
With gestures as theatrical as a performance and a cadence like reciting poetry, Nabhani declares: "When you meet a beauty, kiss her under the pomegranate tree. When you find luxurious silk, turn it into clothes and stride through the palace. And even if you become a Honor Guard, still live as free as the wind!"
"Kids... feel these hands. You see these calluses? Know what they mean? Practice hard, my friends, practice hard! But here's the thing – every royal guard has calluses just like these, yet none of them come close to my good looks! That's what sets us apart! My life, my sword – they dance along the path of poetry! Ah... if you could capture even a fraction of my flair, it would last you a lifetime."

"So you're the children raised by [player.name]? And now I have to waste my time teaching you life lessons? Pointless, absolutely pointless. Most of you will never amount to anything, not even with [player.name]'s sponsorship – because you lack desire!" Nayla tugs at the corners of her flamboyant coat, not hiding her dislike at all.

"Look at you, grinning like fools just because you've had a full meal and clothes without holes! This is as far as your lives will go. You should see what [player.name] and I eat, and the fine silks we wear... And in a few years, maybe even watch the men and women we play with... Haha!"

"When you finally develop the ambition to taste the finer things in life like we do... Ha, don't get any ideas – if you step even a little closer, I'll have the guards whip you. But maybe, just maybe, one in ten thousand of you might become beautiful, strong, and useful... And then, perhaps, I might grant you a taste of your desires."

You quickly pull her away before she can say more inappropriate things to children.

"The happiest thing in the world is to create! Hmm... there are five stages to the joy of creativity," Mahir counts to the children on her fingers. "First is the fleeting inspiration, then pondering over the design, next bleeding and sweating through the crafting... Then comes the most joyful part, which is using it! Seeing an idea become a tangible, valuable tool being used – that's indescribable! Finally, like I'm doing now, passing this idea to others – you only truly master your creativity when you complete this step!"

"The process is long, painful, yet joyful – just like a perfect climax! Sorry, you don't know what that is yet, but I sincerely hope you'll experience both in the future! Then, hopefully, you'll remember this: Creativity is even more exhilarating than a climax!"

Alim notices a child he knows and casually starts talking: "The happiest times in life are when you're lying on a dry, cozy bed, looking out the window with absolutely nothing on your mind – not troubles, not sadness, not anything disgusting – just nothing! That's when you and your mind are truly free!"

"Look, little pups, I really hope each of you finds that freedom and happiness someday... Study well, you hear me?"

The children perk up at his words, eagerly asking him to explain more about what freedom really means.

“The happiest thing in life is to win! To achieve victory, to suppress, to conquer! In this process, you will get everything that satisfies you."

"But... the most important thing is to conquer yourself; if you lose, then there is no happiness... How to conquer yourself? Oh, you will know when the time comes, child, you will know then."
For New Reality!

5006678.title: Last Wish
strings: Last Wish

In the orphanage, there is a well-loved child named Safaa. Little Safaa is a die-hard fan of the King of Flames and the most beloved happy spirit among the children. Sadly, she is afflicted with an illness that even the most excellent doctors cannot cure... Yesterday, you heard that Little Safaa wishes to become a "burning ghost" under the King of Flames when she dies. (You have no idea what this means – it wasn't part of your original writings. It seems to be a fan creation by subsequent bards).
Poor Little One, Gravely Ill
Find someone to play the King of Flames
It can also handle this heartwarming task
It would be great if there were a magical potion that could cure all ailments, don't you think?
Little Safaa soon passed away... for children born in the slums, this was not newsworthy.
You requested [s2.name] to dress as the King of Flames
You requested [s2.name] to educate the children well

The King of Flames enters the orphanage like a god, lays the sword on Little Safaa's forehead, calls her a true warrior, and promises her a place by his left burning side – her soul is granted the honor to follow the King of Flames in eternal conquest, executing justice! 
...Little Safaa left peacefully and serenely. You've never seen any monk guide the dying to such tranquility.

The King of Flames enters the orphanage like a deity, pouring the terribly bitter Water of Life into Safaa's mouth.

... After what seemed like only minutes, her breathing stabilizes. The King of Flames then summons all the children, scolding them for neglecting their studies and indulging in intellectually bankrupt literature and street tricks. It declares that only rationality and wealth can change one's fate.

After assigning shocking homework, the mysterious figure vanishes back into the flames.

5006679.title: Suspicious Coin
strings: Suspicious Coin
Something about this Gold Coin feels... wrong.
Whose eyes shall judge it?
Some characters skilled in craftsmanship might be able to help.
Do not break it. I may yet have use for it.
The Taste of Falsehood
You fear she remembers too much.
You still decide to find out the truth.
Enough to Fool Most

She taps it lightly with a small hammer and declares that the alloy is not in the same proportion as a true Gold Coin... You deny her request to cut open the Gold Coin, and likewise refuse to listen further to her discourse on the art of alloy casting.

Before you can stop her, Badriyyah slips the coin into her mouth... perhaps even swallows it!?
"Such greed, and for a counterfeit besides! The Cultic Gods have no use for trifles such as this!" She laughs, and with a sly flourish produces the coin from between her thighs, flicking it toward you with a ringing clink—and by instinct, you catch the tainted piece.
Lumera asks for a ruler, graphite, and a fine thread. She marks five tiny details that differ from real coins. Yet only when she points them out do you see them.
Bharat takes the coin, weighing it in his hand with a weary sigh. "I was just looking for a chance to explain this to you. If you don't mind, my lord, please come with me."

Together you study it for some time. Something about it feels off, but if mixed in with ordinary coins, you'd hardly notice anything wrong. If this really is a counterfeit, it's an exceptionally well-made one.

5006680.title: Revealing the Truth
strings: Revealing the Truth

The foreign merchant leads you to the residence you rented to him. At last, he admits it; he is the one who has been producing the counterfeit coins. Before you can respond, he adds hurriedly, "All of it was made in the cellar of the very house you lent me." The implication is clear, a thinly veiled threat. If his scheme gets exposed, people will think you're involved too—after all, you're the one who rented him the villa. Now, what will you do?
Bharat is waiting for your judgment.
Kill him
Making this much money without me?
Away with you!
Choose a way to deal with him.
How do you intend to deal with him?
He Must Die
Mint the Sultan's Damned Coins
Begone

To convince the Sultan that you are wholly innocent there are but two ways: slay the culprit outright, or render a substantial fine. If the first is accomplished, the second is seldom hard to find; the man's estate will furnish what is required.

Counterfeiting sounds like a venture that pays without fail.
You ease the foreign merchant's fears with but a few words. The crux is plain: you bear a deeper loathing for the Sultan, you have means to profit from his missteps, and you are better placed than he to turn his coin to your advantage. With all his energy and enthusiasm, he eagerly explains the secrets of the trade to you.
He counsels that you must bind both the lawful and the lawless to your cause, so that news of the fraud never reaches the Sultan's hounds.
When the hour is right, the minting press in the cellar will run again and a steady stream of wealth will follow.
(To undertake this perilous trade with any hope of safety, you require 15 Influence and 10 Notoriety.)
He knows you offer him the chance to flee, and he knows as well that should he drag you into this, no good will follow.

Fear takes hold; his legs quake, and at last he resolves to confess all.
No matter the threat [s2.name] shurls, the merchant remains unmoved. Clearly, he harbors secrets. Any ordinary man would have been trembling long ago.

[s3.name] seizes Bharat by the throat. Speak of the counterfeit coins, or cease to breathe.
At last, gasping, Bharat nods, agreeing to speak before suffocating.

[s3.name] seizes Bharat by the throat. Speak of the counterfeit coins, or cease to breathe.
Bharat struggles with all his might, yet utters not a single word. Fearing bloodshed, [s2.name] is forced to relent.

That wretch... You order your servants to sift through the remnants and set aside those pieces that most nearly pass for true coin.

The merchants still move the choicest valuables, but now they fall into your hands.
After a brief questioning, you establish that he truly was striking coin in your house. That wretch... You recover some of the pieces he failed to carry away.
Forgotten Realms and Tales
Forgotten Tales

Destroy Evidence

You discover two intriguing items: a modest statue, likely once belonging to a long-extinct faith... and a ring, woven from gold thread and soft hair. The hair whose hue recalls a certain comely figure at the Sultan's side... Inside the ring, words are etched: "Cruelty of fate tore us asunder."

You find another intriguing item: a ring, woven from gold thread and soft hair. The hair whose hue recalls a certain comely figure at the Sultan's side... Inside the ring, words are etched: "Cruelty of fate tore us asunder."

They have covertly tampered with your house, and in their final, hasty flight, the place lies in utter disarray... You sense that a thorough search might still reveal something, but there is no time now.

To sever any link between yourself and the counterfeit coins, you set the house ablaze... obliterating every trace, including the disappearance of your tenant. In the process, you even break an Extravagance Card! Everything now appears plausibly accidental.

To sever any link between yourself and the counterfeit coins, you set the house ablaze... obliterating every trace, including the disappearance of your tenant. Such unusual measures leave the city abuzz with speculation.

strings: The Sultan's Suspicion
You must account for all this to the Sultan—though perhaps offering a generous "tribute" will suffice to prove your loyalty.

These are all the counterfeit coins I could find.
Anyone But You
Have you pleased the Sultan?
Though you failed to catch the forger, you offer something far more tangible—real gold coins! The Sultan says nothing, yet at least your head remains firmly upon your shoulders.

You tell the Sultan that, by every means at your disposal, you have seized all these counterfeit coins... which now, of course, are the Sultan's trophies.
The Sultan examines the coins with utmost seriousness... and commands his eunuchs to gather them. You suspect he may well spend them as if they were genuine.
You trust the Sultan to see the truth within the ring. It's his own harem who are the real traitors and thieves, not you.

Today, you survive your audience with the Sultan. Still, you cannot shake the thought that one day he may recall some hidden detail... but every noble under the Sultan's throne lives thus each day, and today, like any other, passes as ordinary.

5006684.title: Please the Sultan
strings: Please the Sultan
As expected, the Sultan still suspects you of hiding something in the coin affair... Offer him a little more to sate his greed and cruel pleasures.
You must face the Sultan in person.

Your Majesty, forgive me, but hear my plea...

Your silver tongue amuses the Sultan.
Your final stance amuses the Sultan.
Does the Sultan even care about this? You cannot be certain... but your shame and submission amuse him, if only for the moment.
At last, he opens your belly—finally convinced that [player.name] has kept none of the Sultan's gold coins.
It matters not where the money came from.
This Is Truly the Last of It
Anyone But You
You present yourself once more before the Sultan, offering the gold seized from the remnants of some criminals' spoils... The great and merciful Sultan, of course, pardons your minor lapse.

Through [player.name]'s tireless efforts, even more counterfeit coins that would have tarnished the royal reputation are recovered... Such deeds, such wealth, are surely enough to earn the great Sultan's forgiveness for your previous suspicious conduct.
In the end, you surrender the ring. You trust the Sultan to see the truth within the ring. It's his own harem who are the real traitors and thieves, not you.

Royal authority shows itself as divine blessing in the heavens, as palaces and monuments on earth, and among men as the sovereign right to strike coin.
Artisan
Helper

Handler
Consumable

Shroud the smoke, conceal the comings and goings of goods, see to the disposal of the refuse...

Just to Cause Trouble for the Sultan
A Slip of the Hand

Turning lead into gold does not seem so impossible... You scoop a gold coin from the water; it is still warm, as if a newborn babe had just arrived. How endearing it is, each piece carved from the Sultan's very flesh!

It is said that humankind was once led by a lineage blessed with gold in their veins. Over time, greed and desire tainted that sacred blood, allowing the unworthy to claim the throne... Much like your own work now, blending lead and tin into gold, letting them wander the world.
Irregular shapes, gilding too thick, the Sultan's effigies grotesque... For all these reasons, you squander nearly as much real gold as you forge into counterfeits...
You create a lump of lead and gold, now requiring tenfold effort to separate them. A costly mistake, indeed—better leave this to someone more skilled.
That which is (not)
The union of long-practised forgery and peerless craft demands one final touch: with a small hammer you must "correct" these coins, lest they look better than the Sultan's own mint...
Stealthy as Shadows
Rumors Are Afoot
This is Lord [player.name]'s residence! What could possibly go wrong? Who would dare suspect him?

Perhaps it is a talkative servant, or maybe you've been too careless in dumping furnace slag, or even that noxious waste has tainted the nearby well... In any case, your actions have drawn the attention of the High Constable.

5006686.title: A Delicacy
strings: A Delicacy
The Sultan has prepared a courtly banquet... Share this weighty favor alongside Hassan.
A Poet's Tribute
The Wretched Hassan
The Wretched Witness
Consumable
You must offer at least one poem.
Rack your brains—or risk having them racked for you!
Hassan, oh Hassan
Your Wisdom and Survival determine your full dice count.
Your Physique and Survival determine your full dice count.
You need at least 5 Successes
You need at least 2 Successes
As the grand feast the Sultan prepared for you two began to spoil, flies started laying eggs in your headless corpses...
You are led into the palace.
A Poetic Feast
The main course arrives.
The Sultan's Understanding of Love
The Jester Suits the Tyrant Best
The Sultan's Delight
You subtly remind Hassan about the banquet.
Ah... Ah...
Not Yet Enough

The servants bow as they guide you and Hassan through the halls.
Beside you, the old poet staggers under the weight of it all, nearly collapsing from fright. You urge him forward, keeping a firm grip as you guide him along.
At last, you arrive at the place where the Sultan will dine today: a charming little garden, exotic and meticulously trimmed. A gentle stream winds through the center, over which a marble table is laid, the waters flowing gracefully beneath it.

He weaves the garden's splendor into verses on a consort who, reflected in the flowing waters, longs for her valiant sovereign... This fitting display of talent earns the Sultan's smile—a promising beginning.
He weaves the garden's splendor into verses on the fleeting seasons, praising only the ruler's virtue as everlasting... This fitting display of talent earns the Sultan's smile—a promising beginning.

He weaves the garden's splendor into verses on petty men coveting the king's reign, thereby highlighting the Sultan's wisdom and magnanimity... This fitting display of talent earns the Sultan's smile—a promising beginning.

He weaves the garden's splendor and channels his own dreams into the poetry, describing them with such vivid mystery that the Sultan's forthcoming wealth and glory seem magnified... This fitting display of talent earns the Sultan's smile—a promising beginning.

Exquisite dishes are presented in succession, until at last a cart laden with fruits and decorations is pushed forward—the "royal delicacy"—Concubine Zazie!
She lies supine, pomegranate seeds on her lips, caviar upon her chest, layers of savory meats arranged upon her abdomen... In the most intimate spots, pearls, diamonds, and golden beads glimmer. With each breath, the sumptuous feast and treasures quiver enticingly. Of course, beyond these adornments, she wears nothing.
"The poems just now were indeed moving," the Sultan remarks with pleasure, casually pointing at Zazie. "This is the banquet I have prepared for the two of you. Now, let the theme of those verses inspire another composition."
Beside you, Hassan kneels, trembling like a leaf. You must think quickly...

You pat Hassan on the shoulder, lending him a measure of courage, and subtly draw his attention to the radiant Zazie...
Hassan's eyes brighten. The old poet straightens slightly, still trembling, and recites in a shaky voice:
"Her eyes, like freshly plucked grapes,
Her lips, like newly ground rose paste;
Her body, sweet to taste,
Oh, the beating within her heart,
Is worthy of a king's finest wine!"
No sooner have his words fallen than the Sultan laughs aloud.
"Excellent. Wonderful! To savor a beauty is little different from savoring a feast... My beloved Zazie, you must taste divine indeed!"
Zazie smiles, yet her complexion has clearly paled... She understands all too well that the Sultan's reading of the poet's lines carries a far more dangerous, more terrible implication—and that her life may hang by a thread.
Her eyes flick briefly toward Hassan, filled with venomous resentment.
The Sultan, pleased, rewards you both with some coins. Carefully, you partake of the feast, warmed by Zazie's skin. Afterwards, you depart the palace with Hassan, the old poet forever grateful for your wit and guidance along the way.

You pat Hassan on the shoulder, lending him a measure of courage, and subtly draw his attention to the gold, silver, and jewels scattered beside the feast...
A spark lights in Hassan's eyes. He straightens slightly, still trembling, and recites in a shaky voice:
"Mortals, fools, you ignorant folk,
Hear me now:
Upon the king's table,
Hazelnuts hard as diamonds,
Caviar tasteless as pearls,
The table never settles,
The cloth warm and slick, hardly fine linen.
The highest delight is no more than this—
Why, then,
Envy it, you all!"
No sooner do his words fall than the Sultan and Zazie erupt in laughter; as Zazie laughs, pomegranate seeds, grapes, and diamonds tumble to the ground, some even slipping into the stream below.
Pleased with Hassan's clever, playful pretense, the Sultan allows you to partake of the feast alongside him—though only the food itself. Zazie, meanwhile, occasionally reacts with strange sounds to the Sultan's fingers plucking at the dishes, making the meal long and arduous.
Afterwards, you and Hassan kneel to offer thanks and then depart the palace.
The old poet clings to your arm, endlessly grateful for your cunning guidance.

You pat Hassan on the shoulder, lending him a measure of courage, and hint that he must not forget the most important audience—the Sultan himself.
Hassan's eyes brighten. The old poet straightens slightly, still trembling, and recites in a shaky voice:
What earthly delicacy can please a sovereign? What feast can match Your Majesty's greatness? None but victory and conquest! His spoon is named fear, and his fork commands dominion. Earthly delights—has time ripened them enough? Are they worthy of our mighty Sultan?
The Sultan listens, his lips curling in approval. Stirred by the verse, he seems eager for new conquests... Perhaps many will meet grisly ends because of this poem, yet today, you and Hassan remain unscathed, your bellies warmed by the exquisite flavors of Zazie.

You pat Hassan on the shoulder, lending him a measure of courage, and hint that he should praise the Sultan's clever design of the feast.
Hassan's eyes brighten. The old poet straightens slightly, still trembling, and recites in a shaky voice:
I once dreamed a goddess placed sweet cream between her breasts. Yet her slopes, so steep, I stumbled time and again, and the fragrance stayed ever just beyond my reach. I once dreamed a goddess set golden nectar between her legs. Yet her marble limbs, like endless mountain paths, I could never scale, and the scent remained ever just beyond my grasp... All of it belongs to the Sultan's feast, and only the supreme Sultan may savor the gifts of the gods.
The Sultan laughs heartily. Regardless of the poem's awkward turns, his appetite is thoroughly awakened—he lifts Zazie, letting fruits, jewels, and delicacies scatter, burying himself amidst her like a ravenous beast. Once their play grows truly fervent, you and Hassan quietly slip away from the garden...

Under the Sultan's impatient gaze, the old poet steels himself and praises the Sultan's greatness, entirely ignoring the dishes before him. "Truly tedious, a waste of my time," the Sultan yawns, and, with a casual motion, plucks a perfectly cut diamond from Zazie's breast. "Ah, I've thought of a fitting punishment for you, incompetent poet," he declares. "Since you have bored me to yawns, you must surely be punished." He hands the gem to a nearby guard, whose expression remains impassive. The guard strides to Hassan, raising the diamond high. "Eat. All of it—gold, jewels, every last piece. Survive, and I shall overlook your failings. Fail, and..." The Sultan shrugs. "The world could do with one less mediocre poet." The guard drives you away. Hassan stares after you, a mixture of terror, despair, and confusion etched across his face. Then he turns back, resigned, and begins to consume the deadly feast before him.

Zazie, expressionless, lays the jewels from her body onto a plate, strand after strand. The eunuchs take turns serving them before you. The old poet swallows every gem through tears, forcing himself not to linger, though his mouth is already filled with blood. Once the Sultan, finally sated, departs in indifference, you hasten to summon the finest physicians and urge Hassan with all your strength not to collapse within the palace walls. Such are the rules of this cruel game—and somehow, you seem to understand them.
The moment he is lifted into the litter prepared at the palace gate, Hassan swoons from pain, expelling a torrent of blood. Emetics, herbal pastes, resin... even a Priest of the Purist is called upon. At last, Hassan's life is spared. And thus comes the spoils of the game: throughout the following week, Hassan continues to tally the rewards of this ordeal—jewels recovered, whether from above or below. Thankfully, the Sultan proves not stingy enough to reclaim these treasures.

Zazie, expressionless, lays the jewels from her body onto a plate, strand after strand. The eunuchs take turns serving them before you. The old poet swallows every gem through tears, forcing himself not to linger, though his mouth is already filled with blood.
You quietly signal a familiar palace guard to prepare the finest physicians and even summon a Priest of the Purist. If only Hassan could stagger beyond the palace gates, the Sultan would spare him. Such are the rules of this cruel game—and somehow, you seem to understand them.
When swallowing a lengthy bracelet set with garnets, Hassan chokes violently. The gems he has already swallowed scrape against his throat, and he vomits a torrent of blood before collapsing.
The Sultan, now bored, commands his guards to cut open Hassan's body and retrieve each jewel. You remain kneeling at their side, forced to witness the entire, grisly harvest.

5006687.title: Calling the Dishes
strings: Calling the Dishes
Every dish is handpicked by Hassan, strung together in rhymes so smooth he rattles them off at lightning speed. It sounds absurdly funny.
Today's menu
You can go youselft, or invite followers to taste it
Someone should eat this, right?
You feast on a warm, hearty meal.
Everyone's bodies grow pleasantly warm...
Hassan was in high spirits.

Hassan rattles off the names of the dishes, rapid-fire, like beans spilling from a torn sack. The rhythm makes Inal burst into laughter. She even rehearses the chant in secret, eager to one day flaunt it as proof of her master's legendary feasts.
Hassan rattles off the names of the dishes, rapid-fire, like beans spilling from a torn sack. The rhythm has everyone laughing and clapping in delight.

5006688.title: When We Speak of Love
strings: When We Speak of Love
When we speak of love—what is it, truly, that we are speaking of? Hassan sits with the beauty you invite, conversing about love, and about a thousand other things besides.
Hassan
Introduce a woman you believe is captivating enough.
Hassan Only Wants to Talk to Women
Hassan longs to sit with different beauties, to exchange words and stories.
I'm looking for new inspiration. You know what I mean.
Maggie hosts him.
Nayla hosts him.
Adila hosts him.
Lumera hosts him.
Fatuna hosts him.
Mahir hosts him.
Jenna hosts him.
Malkina hosts him.
Arzuna hosts him.
Inal hosts him.
Raed hosts him.
Badriyyah hosts him.
[xiaochou.name] hosts him.

With tenderness and grace, she welcomes the old poet, recounting the tale of how you and she first meet, how you fall in love.
The shy, trembling feelings beneath the pomegranate blossoms... the harmony of a marriage well-matched, full of contentment and affection. Hassan is enraptured.
And later, the old poet writes:
"The other lovers who walk this world are wretched,
for the eyes of the goddess of love pass them by.
But Lady Maggie—
she gathers all love into her arms."

Naila clearly misunderstands what you mean by "a talk." She tries to... devour the old poet.
Whether she succeeds or not, you never truly know. All you have are the lines Hassan pens afterward:
"Her desire is deep as a dried-up well.
A passing boy,
unable to resist, tosses in a stone—
yet never hears it strike the bottom."

Adila tells the old poet she has no faith in love at all. To her, it is nothing but an excuse for the weak, an invention to trick themselves. Once you call it "love," every reckless folly gains the sheen of romance, and wasted time seems suddenly precious.
After their talk, Hassan writes:
"A warrior need not believe in love.
Yet lovers must still trust in steel."

Lumera offers her own answer to the question of love. To her, love is a force that shatters reason, tearing through the web of logic and hurling one headlong into chaos.
Hassan is startled by how bleakly the young woman speaks, but Lumera insists it is only honesty. Then she turns the question back to him: And you, old poet, how do you see love?
In reply, Hassan sets down this verse:
"What is love?
It is a burning hand cradling a heart,
offered to another,
as if that other had nothing at all."

Fatuna does not speak much of love, yet she shares her own story with Hassan. Whatever they discuss, you never hear. What survives are the words Hassan writes the next day:
"Love is remaking yourself into the shape another longs for.
Love is a blade.
Love is pain.
Love is what you wish your child to possess, and what you dread they might truly inherit.
Love is the beginning.
Love is the end."

Mahir scoffs at the very idea of love. Instead, she asks Hassan if he wishes to see her latest invention—a massive iron hammer that can smash ten pairs of lovers in a single blow.
Hassan bursts into laughter, though Mahir is not joking in the slightest. Later, he writes these lines:
"Love conquers all,
like the hammer in her hands.
Love shapes all,
like the hammer in her hands."

Jenna lounges lazily. She is, after all, an expert. Her finest clients either aim to become so beautiful that they stir a cold heart, or to charm someone they desire.
Hassan asks, "But isn't there a simpler reason? Don't some people just buy jewelry to please themselves?"
Jenna laughs. "Of course, many do. But those aren't my best clients—they haggle. Their minds are still clear; they haven't yet been swept away by love!"
Hassan enjoys their conversation immensely, and later pens this verse:
"To squander for another's love,
is only so,
because they have not yet learned to love themselves."

Malkina is skeptical of love. She has seen people dismiss one another entirely, but after a touch of her handiwork, the dismissed suddenly becomes charming, even kissable.
Her words inspire Hassan to write:
"The loved believe they are loved,
while the lover knows
they only love the shadow called Love."

Arzuna glides through her lines of flattery—noblewomen's usual odes to love, the "light of life," the "hero in dreams"... yet Hassan finds little satisfaction. Their conversation is awkward, strained, and ends on a slightly sour note.
Later, Hassan writes:
"If love exists,
it does not belong in silken boxes,
handed out fairly,
room by room,
to every decorated chamber."

Inal, of course, believes in love. She has countless stories to share! She clutches Hassan and talks endlessly, laughing and crying all at once. The old poet listens patiently, offering gentle encouragement. The two of them spend the entire afternoon in conversation.
Afterwards, Hassan pens:
"A lover's heart is like a spring,
never drying,
yet so full it cannot hold another drop."

Raed sneers: women's misfortune begins the moment they believe in love. Yet she admits she has seen things worthy of the name "love"—though she vows never to let it seize her. "Better it stays in storybooks," she says.
Hassan enjoys the discussion greatly, and later writes:
"Love, like a god,
can be believed in,
yet need not descend."

Badriyyah has an entire theory of love. She tells Hassan that love is a narcotic, a spell, a fleeting escape from mortal life. To die in love's intoxication—that would be bliss.
From their conversation, Hassan writes:
"If life is truly this harsh,
then you,
and all who read these lines,
living mortals,
are nothing short of saintly in your endurance."

[xiaochou.name] gives Hassan no chance to ask a single question. Instead, she pursues him relentlessly, volleying one query after another about love: What does first love feel like? Does a lover's embrace make the body quake? Can someone in love still touch another?
The old poet is driven to his limits. With no other recourse, he pens a little verse in reply:
"Even with [player.name]'s silver tongue,
and the Sultan's command,
no words can teach a beauty
what love truly is."
Perhaps this is not the "beauty" that can spark Hassan's passion...

5006689.title: Mischief
strings: Mischief
Hassan comes to you, his expression heavy, sighing repeatedly... an unusual force seems to press upon him, harsh and relentless.
Hassan
Which protagonist?
Consumable
Your Insight grants a bonus during checks.
Your gaze falls upon the lamb Hassan has brought along.
Your Wisdom, Magic, and Insight determine your full dice count.
You need at least 5 Successes
Unfeigned
He Plays the Part of a Good Friend Well
Not You Again
Sudden Weightlessness
You Think of a Plan
What the Hell Is This
An Idea is Shaken Out
Middle Age, This Is How It Feels

"My friend, I have run into a trouble unlike any before!" The moment he sees you, Hassan throws his arms around you in a desperate embrace. Behind him, the lamb chews lazily on some leaves, tilting its head as if observing the scene. "I have lost my inspiration—my fervor, my passion, my reckless impulses... all gone!"
You help him sit, finally grasping the weight of his plight. Ever since a strange dream, Hassan has realized he no longer cares for the beauties. Noblewomen's ankles fail to quicken his heart, and the waists of ladies of delights no longer spark a poem. He feels a hollow in his chest—once a channel through which inspiration flowed—now clogged, trapping his creativity inside.
"I could once compare flowers to women, women to jewels, jewels to power, and power back to a bouquet of flowers! But now... it is shattered, my friend. You must understand. There are only a few pure desires in this world: to eat, to drink, to live, and to love. And now I lack one... I can barely even love myself. What am I to do as a poet?"
You sigh with him... or perhaps, you might try something else...?

After he sees Hassan off, his face freezes for a flicker—an oddly vacant stare—then he reports back to you. He offers nothing of value about Hassan; only that the poet looks pitiable, bereft of inspiration. Can't love his muse, can't summon a rhyme—so what? You've been there. Eat, drink, live. You shrug and let it go.

Your gaze slides past Hassan to the lamb lingering by the doorway.
It stands perfectly still, chewing on a blade of grass, its calm eyes betraying nothing. It looks like a common, dim, oddly endearing lamb.
But you keep watching.
The lamb turns, and with a slow, deliberate step, it moves out the door... You know this for what it is: an invitation.
You tell Hassan to wait a moment and follow.

You stepped into a dreamlike haze.
From within the mist came the sheep's voice.
"Then what do you propose, baa? Otherwise he'll just keep writing and writing only love poems, always about love, baa! Of all the things humans do, love is the one I hate most!"
You smiled. Its anger only proved its regret; Hassan had been its favorite toy—perhaps more than just a toy, though it would never admit it—and now it truly didn't know what to do.

Why not keep his capacity for love, but punish the reckless scribbling of endless love poems? Send him to someone who knows nothing of love and let that person grind the habit out of him for a while...
The clouds still for a beat, then a vast lamb's eye opens within them—like a warped sun—fixing you with an unblinking stare.
"You are good at placating higher things, are you not, baa? You always find a way... ha, ha, ha, baa! Tell me—tell me how you will handle this!"
You turn over names in your head. Who among them understands love least of all?

It stands perfectly still, chewing on a blade of grass, its calm eyes betraying nothing. To any outsider, it appears only as a common, dim, oddly endearing lamb.
Yet you feel it—its influence seizes Hassan and spreads outward. Everything around you... bends and twists as if caught in a whirlpool, leaves and branches pulled by an unseen current.
The lamb turns, and with a slow, deliberate step, it moves out the door... you know this for what it is: an invitation.
Everything around you freezes. You leave Hassan, leave the mortal world behind, and follow it into the backstage realm.

You step into a cloudlike void. The living—or at least some fraction of them—seem suspended like puppets, strings descending from above. "Hassan is my toy! He just writes and writes—love poems on repeat—what can I say? Of all human affairs I loathe, love is the worst!" You realize it is at work, influencing Hassan, even affecting you.
Before you can resist, a force lifts you like a ragdoll, shaking your mind violently—spinning your thoughts faster than when the Sultan toys with it.

You tell Hassan that perhaps he has been overindulging lately—though, of course, you do not believe his excuses. You advise him to rest for a while; perhaps things will right themselves. Enough already—ease up a little. Such excess dulls that sort of power. And whatever you do, steer clear of the dog-whip! A total scam. Completely useless!

5006690.title: Hassan's Ordeal
strings: Hassan's Ordeal
You ponder: where could possibly inflict the greatest trial on a heart prone to passion?
Buthayna, Madam of the House of Delights. She's seen it all.
Nawfal, a man utterly clueless about romance... and those kids.
Abdul, um... a terribly greasy old man.
The Sultan. At least he can scare Hassan a little.
The Time Hasn't Come
Hassan
Only the true protagonist can make the choice.
Not choosing... is merely a matter of timing.
Choose one.
My reputation among commoners still isn't enough to make Buthayna help me.
Nawfal has no reason yet to accept someone I recommended.
The person was gone—what good is thinking of him now?
I have no influence to introduce anyone to him.
He was already dead.
I'm not that cruel.
Buthayna
Nawfal
Abdul
Sultan

"No one is more suited than Lady Buthayna," you tell it. "For someone in her line of work, the greatest taboo is falling for a client. Her heart is harder than diamond; there is no fear she will ever love anyone. If Hassan finds himself at her side, in three days at most, he may see love in a wholly new light!"
"So be it, baa! I'll set it up—just a few small adjustments, very simple! Baa baa baa baa—I'm thrilled! You have a remarkable talent for pleasing!" The lamb laughs so loud your ears ring. Its gaze never leaves you. "Next time I create a world, I must write a character like you... perhaps I will just whisk you away then, baa ha ha ha!"
The clouds dissipate. Hassan calls after you, asking why you have not returned. You pause a moment to admire the garden, then slowly walk back to the room.
His poetic talent, his passion, his desires—they are preserved. But his happiness in the days to come... well, that may not survive.

"No one is better than Nawfal to snuff out a poet's fire," you tell it seriously. "He has no sense of romance, no flights of fancy. His life exists only for the grand, tangible 'state.' Not a single moment is wasted on so-called love."
If he takes over Hassan's work, the old poet will see life in a whole new way—no more churning out cheesy love poems for a circle of beauties."
"So be it, baa! I'll set it up—just a few small adjustments, very simple! Baa baa baa baa—I'm thrilled! You have a remarkable talent for pleasing!" The lamb laughs so loud your ears ring. Its gaze never leaves you. "Next time I create a world, I must write a character like you... Perhaps I will just whisk you away then, baa ha ha ha!"
The clouds dissipate. Hassan calls after you, asking why you have not returned. You pause a moment to admire the garden, then slowly walk back to the room.
His poetic talent, his passion, his desires—they are preserved. But the next few days... well, he's in for a lot of hard work.

You tell it that the most suitable person you can think of is Abdul. Even if he had ever dabbled in love, he would have traded it all for power and gold. He trusts nothing that can't be bargained with. Everything Hassan owns is worthless in his eyes. If Hassan ends up at his side, Abdul will boss the old poet around in that slick, calculating way of his—and in no more than three days, Hassan's mind will be brimming with creative energy... probably all about murder plots and managing fiscal deficits. In any case, there won't be a single cheesy love poem left!
"So be it, baa! I'll set it up—just a few small adjustments, very simple! Baa baa baa baa—I'm thrilled! You have a remarkable talent for pleasing!" The lamb laughs so loud your ears ring. Its gaze never leaves you. "Next time I create a world, I must write a character like you... Perhaps I will just whisk you away then, baa ha ha ha!"
The clouds dissipate. Hassan calls after you, asking why you have not returned. You pause a moment to admire the garden, then slowly walk back to the room.
His poetic talent, his passion, his desires—they are preserved. As for the next few days... well, let's just wish him luck.

You speak only two words: "The Sultan."
That's all it takes. The lamb bursts into laughter—
"So be it, baa! I'll set it up—just a few small adjustments, very simple! Baa baa baa baa—I'm thrilled! You have a remarkable talent for pleasing!" The lamb laughs so loud your ears ring. Its gaze never leaves you. "Next time I create a world, I must write a character like you... perhaps I will just whisk you away then, baa ha ha ha!"
The clouds dissipate. Hassan calls after you, asking why you have not returned. You pause a moment to admire the garden, then slowly walk back to the room.
His poetic talent, his passion, his desires—they are preserved. Let's just hope he survives the days ahead.

Patience. Let me observe a bit longer. For now, Lamblet will accept your words.
The clouds dissipate. Hassan calls after you, asking why you have not returned. You pause a moment to admire the garden, then slowly walk back to the room.

5006691.title: Poem of Delights
strings: Poem of Delights
Send Hassan to the House of Delights to write! Let him compose odes to fleeting loves that last only an hour—write to his heart's content!
Busy Hassan
To Hell With the House of Delights

Hassan staggers back, utterly exhausted. He can barely walk, and the little lamb has to tug on his coat to keep him upright.
"Poet... of delights... it's impossible...", he pants. "I wanted to run on the first day... but she made me stay all three... so awful... doing such horrible things, and writing poetry, praising it... If it's not good enough, they make me do it all over again... I never want to write love poems again, my friend... to hell with poets of delights... to hell with love poems..."
You bite back a laugh. You know his vow will last only a few days—but his urge to churn out cheesy verse is clearly gone.
You lower your gaze. The little lamb puffs up its chest, tilts its head, and winks at you.

5006692.title: Nursery Lessons
strings: Nursery Lessons
Send Hassan to spend more time with the kids! Away from women, wine... and under a little moral guidance from Nawfal. Haha.
Happy Hassan
Educated at Last

Hassan returns—this time, not a whiff of alcohol on him. This is unusual.
"Those kids are angels," he laughs, pulling you into a hug. Then he holds up a thick stack of rough papers, all scribbled with wobbly handwriting. "Look! Isn't it wonderful? They've never learned poetry. I just asked them to write whatever was on their minds, showed them how to form each word—and look! They're poets already!"
You read one of the kids' poems:
"I saw a bee dive into a rose,
Pink houses, red walls,
It rolled around, happy as can be.
Adults say,
When the Sultan is in the palace,
He does the same."
You can't help laughing. Hassan pats your shoulder, laughing along.
"I'll never see poetry the same way again... I want to write poems children can understand. Poems that see the world through a child's eyes... pure, clear, transparent. Oh! Let the beauties wait—I have so much else to write!"
He leaves, excited, carrying the stack of papers. Behind him, the little lamb peeks out and tugs at a page from a cheesy love poem on Hassan's scroll.
It chews contentedly, eyes fixed on you. You nod in acknowledgment.

5006693.title: Art Advisor
strings: Art Advisor
Sending Hassan to attend to Abdul—this is guaranteed to ignite a poet's passion... the destructive kind.
Suffering Hassan
To Hell With Advisor

Hassan storms back, breathless, dragging a huge sack of scrolls. His little lamb is chewing on yellowed scraps of paper, and he's slinging two bundles stuffed with more sheets over his shoulders.
"That Abdul—the Vizier—is an enemy of art itself! He had me pull every line praising jewelry from love poems, compile them, and write them on tiny slips. I asked what for, and he said he'd hide them up his sleeves. Then, if he meets Concubine Zazie during court, no matter what she's wearing, he can recite them word for word. Can you believe it? To him, art is just a tool to flatter a concubine!"
Hassan rants like this for two full hours. Not only jewelry—Abdul also had him extract every line suitable for praising the Sultan, lauding the golden throne, insulting political rivals, or... coldly rebutting someone. By the end of three days, Hassan's hands were nearly falling off.
"My mind is bursting with inspiration, my friend!" he says, eyes blazing. "There is so much I want to write. I shall set the rotten world on fire! The beauties can wait; I have other matters to attend to!"
You exchange a knowing glance with the little lamb at his heels.

5006694.title: Court Poet
strings: Court Poet
Send Hassan somewhere truly unbearable—let him serve the Sultan for a few days. Only through suffering can a poet be forged!
Hassan
Farewell, Tyrant

Hassan returns.
He's a shadow of his former self—thinner, pockets jingling with a few coins, utterly drained.
He refuses to quote a single line of the poetry he wrote before the Sultan, and he won't set foot near the court again.
Yet this ordeal has clearly honed both his soul and his craft... His pen is once more sharp and cunning, just as it used to be.

5006695.title: The Poet's Renown
strings: The Poet's Renown
While Hassan hosts your guests, crowds gather, drawn by his latest works... Perhaps this is the perfect opportunity to host a grand banquet.
Great Poet
Present one of Hassan's poems to the guests.
Invite a noble to join Hassan in hosting the company.
Consumable
A poem by Hassan is required to hold the banquet.
The poem is for display only and will not be consumed.
[s3.name] speaks up loudly in Hassan's defense.
Your Influence and Sociability determine your full dice count.
You need at least 8 Successes.
Love is Fleeting, But Poetry Endures
Do Not Offend the Storyteller
Some Delight, Some Despair
Delirium and Wisdom Separated by a Thread
The Banquet Reaches Its Height
[s3.name] Looks Down on the Laughers
Nothing Can Shake a Poet
You Quietly Approach Hassan

The young nobles recite Hassan's latest love poems aloud, each one convinced that their beloved will hear the verses at the banquet and fully grasp the depth of their feelings.
However, those who hear these words are often thinking of someone else entirely... Yet these emotions travel with the poetry, circling around the poet, shaping the image of him in the minds of those who live in this world...

Hassan names twelve ancient wise kings, and mocks nine infamous tyrants. Any scholar familiar with history would know that these tales are hardly reliable, but no amount of diligent research can shape history quite like a single witty poem. The fool vents their dissatisfaction with the present through the past, while the wise savor the delicate dance between truth and fiction... Again, these sentiments travel with the poetry, circling the poet, carving his likeness in the hearts of all who witness it...

Hassan's latest work lampoons the petty and stingy ways of certain nobles... Even the servants carrying trays cannot help laughing.
All the guests laugh wildly, careful not to appear as if they take offense personally. These bursts of joy, envy, arrogance, and insecurity swirl with the poetry, circling the poet, carving his image in the minds of those who witness it...

Many fear the edges of their own sanity. Hassan has long since grown accustomed to it. Calmly, he strokes his little lamb, sharing with the guests his myriad mystical experiences—the visions conjured by alcohol, incense, sleepless nights, and daydreams, all the chaotic connections he perceives... As his words drift through the room, the barrier between reality and fantasy thins. Blind faith, desire, suspicion, and fear swirl with the poetry, circling the poet, carving his image in the minds of those who witness it...

A circle of dazzling women surrounds Hassan... As always, he appears half-drunk, his clothes disheveled, a grin plastered across his face. When someone speaks to him, he offers a few playful, witty replies; when the mood calls for it, he raises his glass and recites a beautiful verse. He likens these women to golden-winged birds, flawless jewels, bewitching spirits—always choosing the perfect words for the perfect moment, and the noble ladies cannot help but laugh with delight. The little lamb in his arms is as charming as ever, ever-chewing, and the women compete to feed it the juiciest fruits and vegetables.
But, as with any banquet where vanity and one-upmanship reign, there are other poets present... Their eyes on Hassan resemble the gaze one casts at a tiny insect drifting in a wine glass.
"Oh, Hassan, I've heard the most amusing tale about you," booms a greasy old poet, voice cutting across the laughter. "And of course, I may tell it here, my friend? It involves your little lamb."
Hassan freezes for a fraction of a heartbeat. From your knowledge of this old poet, bravery has never been among his virtues...
"Uh... dear friend, if you must... go ahead, then?" Hassan stammers.
"Everyone knows about you and that lamb... the one you carry everywhere. Everyone knows what you do together," the old poet continues, some others behind him nodding maliciously. "You treat the lamb as your wife—am I wrong? When the ladies pour your wine, they have no idea you prefer to sleep with a lamb!"
Laughter erupts. Even the noblewomen cover their mouths with amused smiles. Hassan's face first flushes crimson, then pales white. As with all true geniuses, the moment his talent is turned upon himself, it vanishes in an instant.

"Who here has ever heard a single line from that old poet, even one?" [s3.gender] asks disdainfully, then turns to the crowd: "And who among you has not been charmed by Hassan's verses? Who has never known his fame?"
"This is nothing but a shameful attack fueled by jealousy! Whatever beauties Hassan desires, all he needs to do is write them a poem. That lamb is his pet, his source of inspiration—a quirk every great genius possesses. Take Lord [player.name], for instance. You adore crocodiles. Aren't they rather delightful creatures?"
[s3.name] points directly at the old poet, arrogance in every gesture. "In [player.name]'s residence, such crude slander has no place..."
The words trail off, left unfinished—but in that poet's mind, the implications are terrifying... After all, this is [player.name]!
The banquet resumes its merry course. No one dares to trouble Hassan again. The old poet slinks away, humiliated.
Hassan, meanwhile, cradles his lamb with one arm and raises a glass in the other, tipping it toward [s3.name]. "To [player.name]'s wisdom and health!"

[s3.name] steps forward, attempting to defend Hassan, blaming the attack on the envy of lesser poets. But clearly, these wordsmiths are more cunning than your rhetoric alone... By the end, while the guests no longer believe any of Hassan's supposed scandal with the lamb, they still tease him playfully, and he doesn't mind in the slightest.
As the banquet draws to a close, Hassan cradles his lamb, raises a full cup, and returns the gesture to [s3.name].
"You are my friend, a true friend. Forget them—anger is bad for your health; quarrels harm Lord [player.name]'s reputation," he says, raising his glass. "As for me, I wish you everlasting health."
And so, they share several more hearty toasts.

Unable to endure the crude malice any longer, you step forward and lay a hand on Hassan's shoulder. You intend only to offer a few words of encouragement, but somehow, your support seeps into him, infused with a subtle, almost tangible force from your very soul...
It is an indescribable sensation, as if energy flows from your body, down your arm, and into Hassan's being. Even when you try to withdraw your hand, it will not budge, as if glued in place.
Suddenly, Hassan rises. The lamb slips from his grasp and scurries aside. The smile on his face shifts—it is no longer the cheerful, genial expression of the old friend, but something mocking, almost cruel...
He points a finger at the old poet, voice ringing through the hall. "Have you ever, in your entire life, written a single poem anyone would remember? You come to this feast because you are too poor to buy your own wine, is that it?" Then, almost casually, he recites a few of his own celebrated works—gesturing toward himself, laughing.
"Guess what I've won with my writing. Now, guess whether my pen alone could crush you?"
A hush falls over the room. Hassan's presence terrifies everyone, even you—it is the first time you have seen him like this...
The old poet scrambles away, humiliated and frightened. Hassan chuckles, sits back down, and scoops up his lamb once more.
He shakes his head, as if clearing a sudden dizziness.
"Oh, oh, my friend, thank you for giving me courage. This one's for you," he says, lifting his glass with an easy, radiant smile. "I'm always a little scatterbrained... but that doesn't stop me from enjoying a drink, does it?"
You keep your hand on his shoulder, a strange unease lingering—but for now, you let it be, and take a sip of wine.

5006696.title: The Poet's Lamb

strings: A Strange Story
The things that happened in the fog, the conflicting memories, that lamb... you can't help but want to tell someone.
Thoughts
Some people have a way of stirring your very mind...
Maybe consulting a few others will shed new light...
Only select companions can discuss it with you.

You try to tell Hassan about your earlier conversation with the beings in the fog, but the words that escape your lips are garbled nonsense: "&&%...%#)...)￥...%#." Hassan stares at you, certain you've gone mad.

You hint at the happenings in the clouds to Jenna. She fiddles with her bracelets, lost in thought, and after a long pause, she speaks.
"How strange... I've had this dream many times before... Surrounded by clouds, and there's this 'baa, baa' sound, and someone reciting a poem to me..."
She can't remember the whole poem, but a few lines linger in her mind:
"Men believe that gems and gold can adorn their souls,
But once adorned with jewels,
Who still cares for their souls?"
Shaking her head, she gazes at you with a distant, reflective look.
The words stir something in your heart...

You hint at the happenings in the clouds to Arzuna. She exclaims in excitement:
"The clouds! The sheep-like sounds in the clouds! I've dreamt of this, many times! And there was a poem in the dream... Would you like to hear it? But of course—I'm not exactly a dancer known for reciting poetry."
She clears her throat and recites in a clear, melodic voice:
"Remember, you must conceal.
With a supple waist and slender arms,
Conceal your heart of marble,
And the soul that gleams like steel."
She finishes with a smile, as if she had merely mentioned it in passing... yet you cannot help but feel deeply moved.

You can only vent your frustration and confusion to Lady Becky... but all it does is meow at you. Of course—it is, after all, just a little kitten.
Yet somehow, its meows sound different from usual... and that little difference stirs something in you.

You hint at the happenings in the clouds to Malkina, who had been tidying her makeup kit. She pauses briefly at your words.
"Oh—I just remembered something!"
She picks up a snow-white palette she usually uses to blend powders. Carefully, she spreads a layer of ultramarine eyeshadow, then sprinkles on heaps of crushed shells. With her fingers, she grinds, mixes, and shapes the pigments...
"Are you talking about that room made entirely of clouds, with sheep-like sounds coming from every direction?"
You watch her work, and cannot help but admit: she has recreated the scene in your memory almost perfectly.
"I've seen this... I don't know exactly where. Whenever I have some free time, I find myself drawing this... And there's also a poem, do you want to hear it?"
You nod, and Malkina recites from memory:
"On a filthy face,
Using white,
Red,
Blue,
Black,
Powder;
Depict the visage
It wears when clean."
Her words leave a quiet impression on you.

You hint at the happenings in the clouds to your twin brother.
"Huh... You'll probably think I'm crazy—though if I'm crazy, it probably means you are too—but I feel like I've been to the place you described."
He explains that sometimes he suddenly feels as if he isn't here at all, but floating in the clouds, inside a box made of clouds... And when he meditates, a few lines of poetry, whose origin he cannot recall, always come to mind:
"The waking envies the sleeper,
blaming him for devouring the sweetest dream.
Yet the sleeper cannot speak,
for the bitter one has sealed his throat."
It's a little unsettling... so the two of you exchange a knowing glance and, as usual, quietly steer the conversation elsewhere.
Yet the moment leaves its mark on you...

5006701.title: The Poet's Visit
strings: The Poet's Visit
Hassan comes to see you. He's heard things haven't been going well for you lately... yet there's something strange he must discuss with you right away.
Hassan
Madness, suspicion, wounds, and curses, all can be eased.
Perhaps this conversation will ease what has been tormenting you, or your followers.
Reality, memory, and life itself seem to settle once more into quiet order.

You talk about the little lamb in his arms. For a moment, you hesitate, afraid you'll be interrupted again or whisked off to some other place. But Hassan simply hugs the lamb close and begins to tell his story.
"That time I got drunk... I didn't even know you back then. I passed out in a filthy ditch and almost drowned. I could see my whole life flash by, and I thought, 'Well, this is it.' So I figured, before I die, I should write one last good poem... And then I heard one. A really good one. Shame it wasn't mine!"
You blink in confusion. "What do you mean?"
"Ha! I have no idea. Someone was reciting a poem inside my head. They asked if I thought it was good. I said, 'Of course, it's bloody brilliant!' Then the voice asked, 'If you survive, could you write something even better?' I said, 'I don't know, but I'd die to try.' And then... I woke up. I wasn't dead. Not even close. Strange, isn't it? I was sure I was done for."
You fall silent, thoughtful. Then he softly recites the final lines of that mysterious poem:
"Just listen, quietly,
like a river
listening to its own source..."
The two of you talk for a long while!

Gazing at this charming little creature, something stirs within you. You find yourself opening up, speaking aloud your troubles...
Lady Becky
Madness, suspicion, wounds, and curses, all can be eased.
Perhaps this conversation will ease what has been tormenting you, or your followers.
The World's Beloved Cat

Lady Becky rolls over.
Lady Becky falls asleep.

Lady Becky rolls over.
Lady Becky falls asleep.

5006705.title: The Makeup Artist's Visit
strings: The Makeup Artist's Visit
Malkina comes to see you. She's heard things haven't been going well for you lately... yet there's something strange she must discuss with you right away.
Malkina
Madness, suspicion, wounds, and curses, all can be eased.
Perhaps this conversation will ease what has been tormenting you, or your followers.
The Make-Up of the Soul

"Let me tell you something good," she says with a bright smile. "Perhaps it will lift some of your troubles as well. While practicing my makeup, I suddenly realized something: I can create the person I want to see. I don't need to care about the vanity table or anyone waiting for me. It was pure joy! I painted clouds, animals, stars, and the moon across the stage... I felt like, for the first time, I truly understood myself... Oh, I was so happy!"
Strangely enough, as you listen, a gentle warmth spreads through you, lifting the weight you didn't realize you were carrying...

5006706.title: The Kindred Bird
strings: The Kindred Bird

In the library, you encounter your twin. In theory, the two of you shouldn't appear in the same place at the same time... yet here he is, and you find yourself speaking openly of the troubles that weigh on you.
Twin
Madness, suspicion, wounds, and curses, all can be eased.
Perhaps this conversation will ease what has been tormenting you, or your followers.
Synchronization Rising

"Your troubles are my troubles. I can feel them completely," he sighs, then brightens with a spark of excitement. "But... remember the vision I told you about before, the one where it felt like we were in a room made of clouds? I had it again. This time, a two-headed bird burst from the clouds. It sang—oh, such a beautiful voice!—as it passed right through me. And then... I felt so light, so free. I wish you could feel it too. After all, you are me, and I am you. Together, aren't we just like that twin-headed kindred bird?"
Strangely enough, as you listen, a gentle warmth spreads through you, lifting the weight you didn't realize you were carrying...

5006710.title: The Bookstore Owner's Visit
strings: The Bookstore Owner's Visit
Asal has heard of your recent fascination with the mysterious, and he brings a few ancient volumes for you to peruse. Yet only one captures your attention...
Asal
Ancient Tome
Asal asks 5 Gold Coins for this precious volume.
A Rare Tome, Not to Be Missed
Asal did not take offense at your refusal. He wrapped the book carefully, bowed with calm courtesy, and left.
A Seemingly Ordinary Exchange?

You have your servant hand the money to Asal, and he wraps the book in silk before placing it in your hands. On the surface, it seems like any ordinary exchange. Yet, just before leaving, Asal speaks a few strange words: "Sometimes, you may feel like a small boat adrift on unfriendly waters... If that happens, come find me. I will gladly help."
Before you can ask what he means, he bows and departs.

5006711.title: Ambiguities
strings: Ambiguities
Reading can improve yourself, so develop a habit of reading.
Currently Reading
Only you can decipher this book.
So tired...

The words in this book cannot be read with ordinary eyes. Slowly, they draw you into a frenzied dream...
When you awaken, you find yourself in a remote, desolate corner, with no memory of how you arrived. The book is still clutched tightly in your hands, but the words have vanished—as if they slipped from your eyes straight into your soul.
You feel exhausted and strangely exhilarated, the uncanny experience reminding you of Asal's peculiar parting words...
You find Asal in the bookstore.

Asal receives you in the chamber, listening intently as you recount the entire ordeal. He nods, shakes his head, and even takes notes, as if confronting a complex academic problem rather than a mere personal matter.
Finally, he closes his notebook and promises he will find a way to help. The spark of curiosity and excitement in his eyes outweighs any concern for your well-being—but you are too weary to care.

5006712.title: Strange Rumors
strings: Strange Rumors

On the very day you read the peculiar tome, whispers reach your ears: someone in the slums spotted a certain high-ranking lord—you—wandering the streets alone late at night, trailed by three or four dark, shapeless figures. You remember nothing of it, and Asal is of little help. Perhaps it falls to you to investigate those shadows... or, rather, discover what they truly are.
You can send someone to investigate.
Consumables to assist the investigation
Better to send someone else to gather information.
[s1.name] hints at the truth.
[s1.gender] Wisdom and Sociability, and your own Notoriety determine your full dice count.
You need at least 5 Successes
Gold loosens many tongues.
[s1.name] succeeded.
Your Reflection in [s1.name]

Gold loosens many tongues. Under its influence, people begin to spill what they know. In their accounts, the shadows take on different forms—like mirrors, reflecting each person's deepest fear.
It brings to mind the otherworldly creatures from the book, who seem to play with human minds. Perhaps these two mysteries are somehow linked...

After speaking with the witnesses, [s1.gender] notices the same pattern: each shadow appears differently to each person, yet each mirrors their greatest fear.
It brings to mind the otherworldly creatures from the book, who seem to play with human minds. Perhaps these two mysteries are somehow linked...
At the mere sight of [s1.name], the witnesses scattered, retreating behind locked doors. Who here would dare speak ill of you to your face?

5006713.title: Midnight Banquet
strings: Midnight Banquet
Sleepwalking again?
Who am I? Where am I?
Where am I?
Who the hell is doing this?

You wake once more in an unfamiliar place. This time, you're in a crumbling, empty house. The night wind cuts through the walls like ice. You try to hold yourself for warmth, only to discover your hands are slick with blood.
Your heart lurches. You sit up fast, trying to see more clearly—then you do. On the half-collapsed brick wall before you, someone has scrawled a message in blood:
"How delightful. Let's meet again next time."

It has to be tied to that cursed book. You wipe the blood off in a hurry and kick open the door to the bookshop. Inside, Asal is buried in a stack of ancient tomes. He looks genuinely startled at your disheveled state.
He soothes you while deep in thought: "From what I've uncovered these past days... this is a ritual called the Midnight Banquet. It's a summoning enacted through reading, led by a reader of immense spiritual power. Their thoughts form the passage through which something not of our world squeezes into ours..."
He shakes his head, then lifts his hand in apology. "It's my failing. I should never have let you be dragged into this. My remorse is like frost on winter leaves—"
You cut off his poetic metaphors and demand the important part: how do you stop the ritual?
"According to the tome... Well, in short: the Banquet concludes on the third gathering. By then, the Lord of Revels is chosen, usually the strongest entity from beyond. And it takes the summoner's body as its vessel, crossing fully into our world."
You almost laugh from anger. Two gatherings already, all because of his cursed book! Now what are you supposed to do?
"I need time to research, if you'll permit me..."
Of course you do. "Skip to the point!"
"All right... the point is, I'll need help. Your next Banquet should be in a few days. If you can find a capable ally, I can prepare a weapon to face the Lord of Revels. And I'll be there in person to assist you."
His promise feels off somehow, but at this point, you have little choice but to accept.

5006714.title: Even Stranger Rumors
strings: Even Stranger Rumors
Stranger rumors are sure to spread through the Dark Alley. You've unknowingly done some terrifying deeds... It's best to send someone to investigate discreetly.
You can send someone to investigate.
Consumables to assist the investigation
Ignore it.
[s1.name] tries to figure out what's going on.
Your Charisma, Sociability, and Notoriety determine your full dice count.
You need at least 5 Successes

Sure enough, people in the Dark Alley now swear they saw you, late at night, gnawing on living flesh at a street corner... And for your inaction, soon you are the demon-king incarnate on everyone's lips, lord of monsters; your portrait on a door wards off fire and thieves; your name stops babes from crying! Ever more outlandish, indeed...
Gold loosens many tongues.
[s1.name] succeeded.
It's HIM!

Gold loosens many tongues. Under its influence, people began to spill what they know. Some claim they've seen a strange figure—perhaps not even human—prowling the streets at night, gnawing on the corpse of a starved beggar. Gigantic shadows loiter nearby, laughing, urging him on. Some of the eager witnesses even guide [s1.name] to the beggar's torn and bloodied body...
[s1.name] shells out a few more coins, and suddenly the alley's poor agree it was a pack of wild dogs after all. The rumors are swiftly tamed.

Rumors spread like wildfire through the Dark Alley. Some claim they've seen a strange figure—perhaps not even human—prowling the streets at night, gnawing on the corpse of a starved beggar. Gigantic shadows loiter nearby, laughing, urging him on.
[s1.name] questions several of the witnesses and even goes to inspect the beggar's mutilated body. In the end, with a shrug and a silver tongue, [s1.gender] manages to convince them that the story is nothing more than a wild rumor—that the desecration was actually the work of wild dogs.
Returning from the alley, [s1.name] even gives you a detailed lesson on how to disguise human bite marks as dog bites... for reasons you'd rather not ask about.

Rumors spread like wildfire through the Dark Alley. Some claim they've seen a strange figure—perhaps not even human—prowling the streets at night, gnawing on the corpse of a starved beggar. Gigantic shadows loiter nearby, laughing, urging him on.
By the time [s1.name] arrives, the rumors have already taken on a life of their own. All [s1.gender] can do is intimidate the witnesses, warning them not to link this so-called "powerful lord" to you... though you both know it's a hopeless effort.

5006715.title: Mortal's Research
strings: Mortal's Research
Asal has promised to help you survive the "Midnight Banquet" and prepare weapons against the otherworldly intruders, but he will need your assistance.
Cursed Asal
Asal needs an assistant who possesses both Wisdom and Magic.
Only those with Wisdom + Magic of 10 or higher are qualified to take part.
Weapons of Mortals

Asal arrives at your door early, bringing exciting news: with [s2.name]'s help, he has found the most effective way to fight these creatures.
"The real weapon is their true name," he says. "Every time they devour a human, they take that person's true name into themselves. Speak those names aloud, and you can awaken the victims—and weaken the monsters."
You ask, "Where do I find the names?"
His face flushes crimson. He grabs your hands—utterly improper, but he can't help himself. "Right here," he says, almost shouting. "All of it's in my mind! My brain is like a fragile, flesh-bound library. I read countless books, and I've pulled together a long list of names. And your assistant makes it possible. I never imagined in my life I'd connect every piece and finally see the Lord of Revels's true form. That's something no scholar has ever glimpsed."
You pry your hands free and frown. "Scholar?"
"Not important—at least, not now. Think of it like a fly buzzing over a feast. The meal is what matters, not the fly. After all this is done, I'll explain everything. I swear it."
He hands you a long list. When you face the being called the Lord of Revels, reading these names aloud will weaken it. He reminds you to bring a few friends skilled in dealing with the otherworldly creatures. They can help.

5006716.title: Midnight Banquet
strings: Midnight Banquet
The third—and final—feast begins now. Are you ready?
Asal insists on being present for everything.
The secret weapon against the Lord of Revels.
You are marked as the target of the Lord of Revels.
You may call any of your followers to fight alongside you.
You can take this opportunity to break a Conquest Card of Silver tier or lower.

Lose, and you die.
Confront the Lord of Revels.
