Ah! What a powerful, magnificent thing—I'll kill it!
Oh my, look at this big fellow; it is trying to squeeze over here!
No, no, no—There are already too many of "us" in this world... you are not allowed here!
...Tch, let me banish you.
Foul beyond measure—urgently in need of purification.
Oh! This isn't in the books!
Ha! What a battle it would be—sure to be utterly exhilarating!
C-could I hide at the back and write poetry... couldn't I...?
Darling, generally speaking, a courtier's wife doesn't need to personally go fight such a demon, does she?
Oh... heavens, me? I'm supposed to fight that?
I'll follow you into the charge!
How marvelous! You are saving the world!
Hah! This is way more exciting than boar hunting!
Honestly, if you look closely, that thing has a strangely graceful bearing...
I won't bring the dogs for this fight; I can't let them eat that filth.
...All right, I will fight.
I had heard of this thing... it has killed plenty of poor folk. Now it's time for it to pay.
Ah, splendid, I'll give it a proper dance!
I wonder if it is wearing any otherworldly precious gems...
Uh, you know, my family were all civil officials...
Meow—ah!
Could I take a share of the trophies? It ought to fetch a good price.
Oh, oh, this is truly rare to see... later I will design a new look based on it.
If I stuff this into an engine, I wonder what would happen...
We are really going to fight that...?
You took this opportunity to break a Conquest Card

You sit in the silent room, feeling the otherworld seeping in through every line of the book, through every spell etched into your blood. They come, hungering for innocent blood, delighted to find a vessel as perfect as you.
When the darkness finally takes shape, you rise. You refuse to be the lamb at the feast. No matter how many times this creature has presided over its midnight banquets, tonight it learns you are no easy prey.

The devoured souls knit themselves into a warped, living shape, their twisted mass breaking apart as each name is spoken. The more you call them, the weaker the form becomes—until at last it collapses and the malice dissolves. The room falls still. You catch your breath and lower your weapons—the blade of steel, and the blade of will.
Behind you, Asal is scribbling furiously into his notebook, pressing his face close to the space where the Lord of Revels lingered, sniffing, murmuring, his eyes alight. "At last... I've seen it. I can record it now..."
Even you can't help but think he looks like a lunatic.
Only when he scrawls his final line does he look up, bow deeply, and stammer: "My gratitude—and my shame—cannot be expressed enough, it's like—"
You're too exhausted to listen. With a weary flick of your hand, you dismiss him. Enough for tonight. You need sleep.

The devoured souls knit themselves into a warped, living shape, their wrath and despair striking you like a tide. You die—or maybe you don't. The Lord of Revels has claimed your flesh, and whatever comes next is no longer yours to know.

You're so sure of your own power that you refuse to rely on any other means to weaken your foe. You face the creature head-on, determined to show this arrogant outsider who truly rules here.
And you succeed. Malice dissolves into nothing. The world around you falls silent once more. You calmly sheathe your weapon. Behind you, Asal is scribbling furiously into his notebook, pressing his face close to the space where the Lord of Revels lingered, sniffing, murmuring, his eyes alight. "At last... I've seen it. I can record it now..."
Even you can't help but think he looks like a lunatic.
Only when he scrawls his final line does he look up, bow deeply, and stammer: "My gratitude—and my shame—cannot be expressed enough, it's like—"
...You're too tired to listen to more of his nonsense. You wave him off and let it go. At least you've had a fight worth remembering.

You're so sure of your own power that you refuse to rely on any other means to weaken your foe. But when the darkness closes around you, you realize too late just how reckless you've been. Regret is useless now. You die—or maybe you don't. The Lord of Revels has claimed your flesh, and whatever comes next is no longer yours to know.
The Sultan demands a full account of the battle. From the look in his eyes you catch a flicker of envy. He missed a fight like that. How unforgivable.

5006717.title: The Whole Story
strings: The Whole Story
Asal comes to offer his apology. From the courtyard gate he drops to his knees and shuffles forward. It's the highest etiquette of apology—or rather, the posture of the guilty.
Asal Comes to Apologize
You can take this opportunity to break a Bloodshed Card of Asal's tier or lower.
Ignore Him and Send Him Packing
You couldn't be bothered to see him—indeed, you never wished to see him again. So he knelt until sundown before leaving. He left you quite a few Gold Coins and a book—likely gifts in apology.

"I have come to lay everything bare. I used your kindness, your power, your courage." Kneeling before you, he began to confess.
He has known from the start that "Ambiguities" was a conduit used by an otherworldly thing to select vessels. He himself had read it, but was not chosen. Still, he needs to see what the Lord of Revels truly is, for only what is seen with one's own eyes may be written into the encyclopedia... so he used you.
"The Encyclopedia has been the life's work of my family," he continued, voice low. "It is meant to encompass all things—but only what the compiler has witnessed firsthand. Hearsay holds no place within it."
You pause, remembering the old reverence for knowledge that once ran through this land—though the Sultan's rule has long since eroded it. You've heard whispers of this Encyclopedia: a feat no one has yet achieved, the white jewel atop the tower of scholarship, the very limit of a seeker's reach.
"Now I have done what no one else could," he said. "I can write the entry for the Lord of Revels with pride. No one knows this being as I do. The creature I set down will become the creature the world knows."
His head bows lower, forehead touching the stone at your feet. "In my hunger, I drag you into this peril. This is a crime worthy of death. I accept whatever punishment you decree. Even if you choose to kill me, I will die fulfilled—for I have borne witness to knowledge no mortal has ever known."
Then, Die to Atonement
I Understand You

He faces death calmly, only regretting that he couldn't finish his encyclopedia. After he dies, you search his body and find a small bundle—apparently a gift, prepared as atonement for the debt he owes you.

The thirst for knowledge is not a sin, and battling otherworldly things... can hold its own grim pleasures.
Even as you speak, you warn him sharply: you hate being manipulated. He could have come straight to you, and you would have helped anyway, because you understand the compulsion to witness the truth.
Asal remains on his knees, shoulders trembling. "I... I never expected this. Lord [player.name], that you could understand..." His voice cracks, an almost subterranean sob. "I don't know what to say... I'm so grateful my folly didn't harm you... I'm so lucky."
He retrieves a book from his chest and offers it to you. Still kneeling, he retreats backward, never lifting his gaze, until he is outside the residence. His worn knees leave a streak of blood across your floor.

5006718.title: Encyclopedia
strings: Encyclopedia
All things in the world are chronicled here.
Acknowledgments
This entry chronicles a relic that does not belong to this world.
This entry records the embodiment of rules.
This entry preserves a curse of power.
This entry lifts the veil on all mysteries.
This entry recounts a treasure that has existed since ancient times.
This entry documents the pinnacle of human craftsmanship.
This entry preserves a vessel of unprecedented thought.
This entry was written under duress.
This entry recommends a compendium that masters the art of healing.
This entry preserves the legacy of a tribe.
Compiled by Asal
The items you believe merit a spot in the Encyclopedia.
Aim to fill its pages.
To glimpse even a single rare treasure in one's lifetime is already a blessing. Do not force yourself to possess them all.
It is already recorded in the Encyclopedia.
You forced Asal to include this in the Encyclopedia. He reluctantly agreed, but merely integrated it into other entries rather than giving it its own section.
Frontispiece
Next Time, Perhaps
Dragons Do Exist
A Game Fit for the Sultan
All Things Shall Pass
In a Dream
Tales of the Ancient Mirror
Not Quite a Cat
Playing Dumb
What Men Really Want

Nothing Different
Always a Cat Person

Too Common to Include
It's the One!

You insist that Asal paint portraits of you and Maggie on the Encyclopedia's cover. He refuses outright, and a heated debate ensues. In the end, you both yield a little. "Since you've truly helped me witness so many rare and fascinating things, I shall at least mention you and your beloved wife in the acknowledgments on the frontispiece."
You insist that Asal paint portraits of you and Maggie on the Encyclopedia's cover. He dodges, refuses, and eventually, the matter stalls. Hmph. You are not the type to surrender so easily.

Asal cradles the dragon's eye with trembling hands, yet quickly averts his gaze. "Oh... I've only read about it in a few fragmented records from ancient times... They say one must never stare into a dragon's eye, lest the soul be drawn in!"
Across a silk cloth, he measures its weight, feels its warmth, and quizzes you on every detail of its battle. He records everything meticulously, then sighs. "A pity the dragon escaped... But perhaps that is a blessing. Future witnesses may see it for themselves, and this entry retains its worth, right?"
He bows deeply, offering a long string of ornate metaphors to express his sincere gratitude.

You suddenly flash the Sultan Card, and Asal jumps in genuine surprise. You quickly assure him you mean no harm—you're not here to embarrass him or set his shop ablaze. You only want him to see whether this item deserves a place in the Encyclopedia.
He adjusts his glasses, studying the card carefully.
"I feel a peculiar magic in it, yet its power does not come from mere sorcery... The rules of this game are what merit recording." He ponders, sorts his thoughts, and finally shakes his head with a wry smile. "Whether the world should ever know this game... I cannot say. I am but a chronicler. And you, having lived it—what do you think?"
You answer only with a silence thick with meaning.

You carefully bolt every door and window, making sure no other living soul lurks nearby. Only then do you draw from your pocket the magical ring stolen from the Sultan. "I doubt you've ever seen anything like this," you remark.
Asal, of course, hasn't. He has never had the chance to meet the Sultan in person. He listens intently as you recount the ring's powers, its origin, and its history, studying its size and the intricate inscriptions inside. He records every detail—even your ambitions.

You describe to Asal the divine visage you once witnessed, speaking of the gods' grandeur and their terrifying presence. Your words ring so true that he can no longer dismiss you as a mere charlatan. Yet he steadfastly refuses to record the entry. Because the Encyclopedia tradition demands that only what is seen with one's own eyes may be written. Frustrated, you leave. That night, Asal appears in your dream garden...
By morning, he comes to you with the wet, inked pages. At the end, he writes: "Mortals cannot behold the true visage of the gods, for all live within the gods' slumbering dream."

Asal refuses to believe that the living form before him is indeed a mirror—until [xiaochou.name] melts into a shimmering pool of liquid, twisting and reshaping itself into countless dazzling faces and forms. Asal covers his eyes and shouts for [xiaochou.gender] to stop, and only then does [xiaochou.gender] relent, letting out a mischievous laugh at the chaos it has wrought. To witness such an ancient, primordial entity is a rare gift indeed. Asal soon recovers from his shock, bombarding [xiaochou.name] with questions, tracing the tangled mysteries of ages past. [xiaochou.name] answers them all, yet truth and falsehood blur together. Even as mere stories, they thrill and enthrall. The afternoon drifts away in the study. You can see [xiaochou.name] is enjoying himself as well—so much so that [xiaochou.gender] even offers to reveal his true form, granting Asal a rare, unguarded chance to observe.

Asal refuses to believe that the cat in front of him is the "mirror" you're talking about. The cat, seemingly amused, pretends not to understand a word you're saying. It keeps meowing and pawing at everything in sight—scratching this, knocking over that—completely making a fool out of you and Asal!
By the day's end, utterly exhausted, Asal clutches his manuscripts, wiping sweat from his brow, and implores you never to bring that cat into his study again. He peers at you with a touch of sympathy... The cat truly is a mirror in disguise! Why won't he believe it?

Asal refuses to believe the living person before him is actually a mirror. You try everything, every argument, every trick, but [xiaochou.name] won't shift back. In the end, all you can do is back off sheepishly under Asal's look of pure pity and the sly grin of [xiaochou.name].

You rehearse Mahir's sales pitch with fervor, demonstrating it to Asal once more. He fiddles with its connections, studies its inner mechanisms and the flow of Aether. Even though its design is far from elegant, he cannot help but marvel at its ingenuity and whimsical brilliance. Reluctantly, he admits it represents the pinnacle of human engineering.
Haha! Now that's more like it! You ask if he wants to try it out—after all, an entry in the Encyclopedia demands firsthand experience! He waves you off, insisting that mere observation suffices, and that dismantling the original parts is absolutely out of the question. Men... always so unwilling to dedicate themselves fully to science.

You present a piece of blue silk to Asal, but he shrugs. "I've seen many such fabrics."
"It's different," you insist, pulling him to the street. You show him the blue worn on the arms and waists of the poor, explaining its significance. This color is a symbol of defiance, a force unseen in history: one person alone may be weak, but thousands united can shake the world.
Asal furrows his brow and thinks for a long, long time, so long he almost seems to drift off. You can't help but wave a hand in front of his face, then give his cheek a firm slap, and only then does he snap back with a sharp "Ah!" Finally, he agrees to include that utterly unremarkable blue veil in the Encyclopedia. Huh... and here you thought you'd have to talk him into it.

You present a length of blue silk to Asal, but he barely raises an eyebrow. "I've seen many fabrics like this."
He flips through the Encyclopedia's entries on textiles, listing dozens of exquisite materials you've never seen or heard of... Well, convincing Asal that this blue silk is anything extraordinary seems hopeless for now.

Cats are common enough, but Lady Becky is exceptional! She carries a noble title, comes and goes freely in the court, attends meetings in your stead, swats at little crocodiles, kicks at grand lions. She has protected you and comforted you. She is, without question, the most remarkable and adorable kitten in the world!
Asal has had quite enough of you, yet faced with the little creature sharpening her claws on his manuscripts, he yields. Once he agrees to include Lady Becky in his writings, you leave the study, cradling the kitten with satisfaction.

"This is truly an extraordinary book, especially the final chapter... who could have imagined tending to a demon's wounds?" Asal exclaims. "Allow me to read it a bit longer. Later, I shall reserve a few pages in the Encyclopedia to offer it a proper commendation."
You nod your agreement.

"This is certainly an impressive book," Asal admits as he flips through it, spreading his hands in a faint shrug. "But it won't do... Many of the herbs and remedies in here are already cataloged in the Encyclopedia. And... do you not find it odd for one book's entry to include another book?"
Alright... you can only leave with a sigh of regret.

The instant you present the object, Asal's eyes brighten. He grabs the strange ornament, handling its feathers with a delicate reverence, murmuring to himself. Startled by his intensity, you watch until he finally calms down and explains: "When I was young, I once encountered a tribe that... well, they had a taste for human livers. I nearly became a meal for their chief!"
You can't tell what he finds impressive.
"The chief wore an ornament just like this. I told her that, should I die, my final wish would be to touch it... and then... well, I was knocked unconscious and left in the wilderness. I never found that tribe again. Such kind-hearted girls! They not only bandaged my wounds but left water and food for me."
You stay silent, withholding judgment on the story.
Even the rare white rhinoceros earns Asal's refusal—its rarity or any personal connection you might claim isn't enough to justify an entry in the Encyclopedia.

A servant greets you coldly, leads you to the parlor, and serves a few cups of bland wine.
After some time, Nawfal emerges, clutching a scroll. He frowns, scrutinizing you and Asal as he paces.
"I have little interest in meeting you outside the court, Lord [player.name]."
You're tempted to tell him you feel the same, but then you think of his legendary library and glance at Asal's wide, sparkling eyes... so you settle back onto the unyielding wooden chair, and with deliberate calm, introduce Asal and explain your purpose.
"I recognize the proprietor of the Angler, of course," Nawfal says, "but my collection... hmm. I see no obligation, or need, to show it to either of you."
Asal sends you frantic glances. It's time to reveal your sincerity.

Nawfal is trying very hard to keep his composure, but really, did he think he could fool you, his old rival? Asal's book is indeed a rare treasure, even you feel a twinge of envy. Still, the one you've brought is no less remarkable. Look at Nawfal's shining eyes and trembling hands—he's dying to dive into the study right now, yet still trying to keep that calm facade. Tsk.
You hear him clear his throat and call for a servant. "Take them to my library. They have one candle's time. When it burns out, they leave."
Asal nearly jumps with excitement, while you make a great show of adjusting your robes and pretending you couldn't care less. Time to see whether Nawfal's fabled "endless library" lives up to the stories.

You present the old wooden box and gesture for Nawfal to open it. He looks a little wary, a little puzzled. He turns a few pages, frowning deeper with each one.
"This isn't cheap," he mutters, setting the book down to look you squarely in the eye. "Why are you so eager to see my library?"
Ah, this man, always assuming you're up to no good, when in truth you're simply acting out of... pure altruism! You sigh inwardly. Guess it's time to flatter him like you would the Sultan himself.

You leap dramatically to your feet and shout out the answer: "Because your library, Lord Nawfal—how did Asal put it again?—is a Colossus of the Desert! A nectar of the Khan's golden tent! And in this Empire, it's long been said that he who gathers all wisdom is the one most fit to rule! Thus I say, knowledge is power, learning is dominion, and together they forge you, Nawfal, the steadfast, the just, the immovable idol untouched by worldly tide! Hail Nawfal! Holy be thy name!"
Asal's mouth twitches. Nawfal... he closes his eyes and takes a long, strained breath—three times—barely restraining himself from throwing you out on the spot. Through clenched teeth, he tells you to shut up, then waves for his servant.
"Take them to my library. One candle's time. No more." He marches off, gripping your gift tight—so tight, you can't help but smirk. Clearly, he's thrilled with your offering.
You clap him on the shoulder with a not-so-sincere "thank you," then cheerfully sling an arm around old Asal and head off toward the legendary library.

Convincing Nawfal, it turns out, is far harder than flattering the Sultan himself. You barely open your mouth—your finest rhetoric yet to come—when Nawfal's patience snaps. His gaze, sharp as it is in court, pierces you like a thorn, followed by a heavy sigh: "To think our Sultan finds joy in your... clumsy sophistry," he says, every word dipped in disdain. "It weighs heavily upon my heart."
But this is at home, and he can't be bothered to argue with you—he just waves his hand, signaling the guards to throw you both out.
Asal looks crushed, not only because he's been denied a glimpse of the legendary library, but because that self-righteous bastard didn't even return the gift! Fine. Tomorrow, you're absolutely filing a formal complaint against him. Let's see how high and mighty he feels then.

You were called away on short notice and lost a rare chance. Asal couldn't be bothered: he roamed Nawfal's library alone, practically glowing with joy, and only parted from the beloved tomes when the servants came to send him off.
So Many Books

The cellar has a few small windows at the top that let in shafts of light. Through them, you can just make out the titles of the surrounding books.
There are roughly dozens, perhaps even hundreds, of bookshelves here, each with three tiers, all packed with books. You drift through that ocean of knowledge. The scent of paper fills your nostrils, and your eyes gradually adjust to the dim light. Beside you, Asal moves in silence, scanning titles with feverish speed.
Poetry. Reason. History. Logic. Hymns. Elegies.
Nawfal's library is a wonder to behold, a hoard of wisdom gathered across ages. Even without time to read, simply standing among these relics feels like witnessing a miracle.

Time slips away unnoticed. A servant opens the door, lantern in hand, politely reminding you that your candle's hour has passed. He does not step inside, perhaps fearing a single spark might doom this treasury of words.
You turn to leave, calling for Asal. He hurries after you, sweat beading on his brow...
As he draws near, you notice a strange bulge beneath his robe. Your eyes linger for just a moment—enough to make him fidget, wiping his face in nervous haste...
You say nothing. He exhales in relief and follows you out into the corridor. The two of you leave without bidding Nawfal farewell, guided back toward the surface by the servant's dim light.

Asal arrives brimming with excitement.
Before you can speak, he launches into a stream of flattery—you're the sun, the drifting clouds, the white deer of the mountains. At last, he produces a hand-copied manuscript and offers it with both hands.
"I made an extra copy," he says. "The author's long gone, but his ideas shouldn't fade with him. I plan to see them reborn."
You skim through it and find that this book, titled "Errant Thoughts", a collection of the previous dynasty's philosophical writings, contains quite a few suggestions on how a ruler should govern... Hmm... You look up cautiously at Asal.
Asal laughs softly. "Ah, ever the silver jug—one gentle touch, and you start to rattle." It takes you a moment to catch the meaning before he waves a hand. "I know. Nawfal warned me too. But don't fret. A few careful revisions, and no one will ever notice what it really says."
He thanks you profusely again, comparing your help to all sorts of grand things—whales, dragons, silver light on the horizon... and so on—before finally bowing and taking his leave.

You steel yourself and step once more into Nawfal's residence. Outside, Asal is already in position, ready to slip in unnoticed.
That frigid servant leads you again into the parlor, where Nawfal greets you with open disdain. He doesn't even try to hide his impatience.
You must keep him talking... anything to buy Asal a few more minutes.

In a flash, you recall several unresolved court debates between you. What began as a shallow distraction soon turns into a genuine quarrel. Nawfal's sharp tongue cuts deep, and before you know it, tempers flare, voices rise, and an expensive-looking goblet shatters on the floor. By the time you're thrown out of the residence, Nawfal's lips are trembling with rage. Well, that's the power of playing away from home. You catch sight of Asal lurking around the corner, and only then remember why you came in the first place. Suppressing a prickling sense of guilt, you make a hasty retreat from the scene of the crime.

You and Nawfal know each other far too well. Your evasive chatter only deepens his suspicion. He narrows his eyes, then suddenly rises from his seat. You follow close behind, just in time to see Asal being restrained by a guard, hands twisted behind his back, the stolen book lying at his feet. Nawfal casts you a cold glance, lips curling into a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. Then, with a flick of his hand, he orders his servants to escort you out.

When you recite the charges, Asal bursts into laughter. All the printed pages and engraved plates are piled at his feet, feeding the fire. He curses you from within the flames until the sword falls, and his head tumbles forward, eyes still fixed on you. They will return in your dreams, again and again.

By the burning pyre, you raise your voice in praise of the Sultan's wisdom. The heat distorts your figure, twisting it into something almost demonic in its devotion. That image, the faithful servant wreathed in fire, burns itself into the minds of all who watch. If you ever raised a banner once, it now lies among the ashes, utterly consumed. And the cruelest irony of all: the Sultan says nothing.

You shook your head and told her this is the reward she had earned through her writing. She may use this wealth as she wishes.
"As I may use... I... may use the gold coins as I wish?" Lumera looked surprised. She lifted the coins, letting the light glint across them as if inspecting tiny creatures. "I never imagined such a thing... I will think carefully, thank you, Master."

You told her that this story was born of her heart, her fate, her very soul—things that cannot be taken from her. Thus, the money was rightfully hers.
She stared blankly at you, then lowered her head slightly, almost at a loss. "Can I truly... be this happy? My words, printed into a book, read by so many people... and now, you would also give me gold?"
"You are mistaken," you said, brushing your hand gently over her head. "These coins are not a gift from me. They are your own earnings."
"But they slipped into my palm by way of your kindness," she whispered, opening her hand to gaze again at the gleaming pieces. "I... I will think on it. I will find a way to share this happiness with others... Just as you do."

Its fragrance escapes the bottle even before the seal is broken. A gift most fitting for a friend or companion.
Rose Essence Oil
Who shall you gift it to?
A Lingering Scent
You presented the vial of rose essential oil to [s2.name]. Whether used in a bath, as a massage oil, or worn as perfume, its soothing aroma will surely become part of [s2.gender]'s very presence.

5006741.title: The Rope's Tempering
strings: The Rope's Tempering
Reading can improve yourself, so develop a habit of reading.
Currently Reading
The reader.
I love cords! They can remember time and remember what matters.
I know sixty-seven different knot-tying techniques!
When a line snaps—rumbling, tumbling...
I have many ways to draw us closer to the great Cultic God.
May our souls be strong—without fear and without dread.
For beings beyond this world, the souls of mortals serve as the fibres of a rope. Once woven, it may be used to climb into realms unseen...

5006742.title: The Makeup Artist's Visit
strings: The Makeup Artist's Visit

Malkina arrived at your residence, gliding through the halls as she chatted with your maids about the latest fashions in fabrics and hair. By the time she reached the parlour, nearly every maid in the house had gathered around her.
Malkina
Who shall receive her?
Express your gratitude.
I have an idea.

"That maple-red hair dye is hardly for everyone. Darker complexions should avoid it altogether. In fact, maple-red flatters only the fairest of skins! If you ask me, a scarlet headscarf tied high and finished with a few loops of copper chain at the hem is far more striking. Ah, but your master is waiting, I'll tell you more another time!"
With a bright laugh, and to the reluctant sighs of the maids, Malkina took a seat before you, smiling.

"About what happened at your door the other day... thank you for speaking on my behalf." She bowed deeply. "Your words touched on something I've long wrestled with. I've turned it over in my mind again and again. If you've time, I'd like to speak further—perhaps even ask for your help."
She paused, then fixes you with a steady gaze. It was only now you realised: you've never truly looked at Malkina herself. Each day she cloaks herself in a new impression—some adornment, a clever pairing, a carefully chosen face paint. But the woman herself? She hides in those eyes, staring directly into yours.

Lately, Malkina explained, she had wondered: if she can change the way people see a face, can she also shape greater truths?
"For instance, if I spent more time with the kind-hearted, perhaps I could distil the very visage of kindness, then paint it upon those who lack it. I could fashion virtue, and vice, and more besides! Imagine it—crafted by these hands, these pigments, these stitches!"
Her eyes shone with excitement, and you found yourself pondering the possibility.
Malkina yearned to meet the good, the scoundrel... the chivalrous... and nobles such as yourself. Once she has seen enough, her art of transformation will surely reach new heights.
You promised to aid her, and with a radiant smile she departed in high spirits.

5006743.title: The Look of Kindness
strings: The Look of Kindness
You invited a truly kind soul to let Malkina observe. Perhaps she can distill a connection between kindness and outward appearance, sharpening her craft. But who shall it be?
Malkina
Who is kind?
Malkina needs new inspiration.
You invited Qais.
You invited Maggie.
You invited Lumera.
You invited Alim.
Is [player.name] kind?

Qais accepted, though reluctantly. He sat stiff-backed on the carpet of your parlor, glaring at Malkina with mounting irritation.
Malkina, silent as a statue, stared back. The stand-off stretched on until Qais finally stormed out.
"I think I understand," Malkina murmured after him. "Kindness is an unshakable strength... the certainty that, no matter what happens, this person will never change."
She then launched into a flood of cosmetic notes—how to shadow the eyes, how to gray the sides of the nose—techniques she claimed will reproduce something of Qais's steadfast face.

Maggie arrived beaming, twice flattered. Once that you considered her kind, and again that you entrusted her with hosting a lady guest.
She laughed through the afternoon, trading stories with Malkina until the two parted warmly. As they said goodbye, Malkina suddenly whisked out a rouge box, dabbing Maggie's cheeks with quick, deft touches, then handed her a small mirror.
"Oh—how magical! I don't look tired at all," Maggie exclaimed, tilting her face this way and that. "Will you teach me this trick? Is it the shade of the blush, or some secret essential oil you've mixed in?"
The two falled into delighted chatter again, sharing secrets of beauty and laughter.

Lumera tilted her head, pondering. She spoke with Malkina about what "kindness" truly means, drawing examples from her many books: the kind wear white, the kind keep their lips pale, the kind are neither too rich nor too poor...
"So," she concluded, "what everyone desires can never be kind; and the one everyone wishes to be will never be kind."
Her words left Malkina quietly reflective.

Alim shrugged at the notion. "Kind? Hardly. I'm just... less wicked than most nobles."
He and Malkina talked at length. His face, quick to shift from sly to charming, sparked all manner of inspiration.
When it was time to leave, Malkina fussed briefly with his appearance—tidying his brows, pinning stray locks. The change was startling: the old Head Thief looks almost like someone new.
"Hee, hee... good! Now I can rob those who remember my face all over again,"
Alim chuckled, bounding away gleefully.
Malkina spended a long while in conversation with you, as you recounted deeds you believe to be "kind." She listens, nodding thoughtfully.
The person you invited may indeed be kind, yet they proved to be no source of inspiration for Malkina...
A Conclusion on Kindness

Through your efforts, Malkina gathered a trove of insights linking kindness and beauty. She filled pages upon pages of her notebook with observations.
"The key is modesty in exposure, balance in tone," she insisted, fussing over your appearance with practiced hands. "The outline mustn't pinch too narrow... ah, there! See? You look much kinder already."

5006744.title: The Look of Evil
strings: The Look of Evil

Malkina wished to study scoundrels firsthand, hoping to distill from them a way to look wicked. She's convinced she could devise a whole style of dress and makeup that makes one appear far more sinister. You've agreed to help her—though, truth be told, not everyone would be flattered by the words: "Because you're such an evil person..."
Malkina
Who is evil?
Malkina needs new inspiration.
You called Nayla over.
You called Jawad over.
You called Alim over.
You called Fatuna over.
Is [player.name] evil?
Eyes of the Guiltless
Innocent Violence

After a few gifts and flattering words from you, Nayla was all smiles. She eagerly shared with Malkina her secrets for making men helplessly devoted, giggling as she explained the delight of discarding them at their most besotted moment. Every gesture, every smile of hers made a deep impression on Malkina. By the end of their talk, Malkina gave Nayla a new look with her brushes, and both women were delighted.

Jawad boasted at length that he was not a bad man at all—on the contrary, he was the best, the noblest, the most righteous! Malkina played along with polite flattery, observing his expressions with care. Whatever the truth of his claims, by the end, both he and Malkina seemed satisfied with their exchange.

Alim declared he'd seen every kind of scoundrel imaginable and feared none of them—yet even he admitted the Sultan's Game surpassed his limits. "Who could imagine nobles inventing such horrors?" he said. Then he animatedly described to Malkina the faces of street rogues and how he himself judged which marks to steal from just by their appearance. His stories proved helpful to her.

At first, Fatuna was reluctant to join a "study of evil," but as the conversation unfolded, she softened. Malkina praised her smooth skin and elegant posture, and Fatuna laughed, saying it was the fruit of long discipline. She shared skincare secrets, traded eye-makeup tricks—and then, just when you thought their meeting would end on a light note, Fatuna suddenly clasped Malkina's hand. "I am not guilty. But that does not matter to you. Guilt is not eyeshadow, nor the powder on one's skin. Guilt cannot be seen. If you believe yourself guilty, then you are. If you believe you are without guilt, then you are blameless." Malkina returned her grasp. The two women gazed at each other in silence for a long time.
You lounged casually on the carpet, speaking with ease of your misdeeds and the benefits they had brought you. Malkina studied your face, your posture, your every movement with great intent...

Throughout the conversation, Amur fixes Malkina with a stare, cold, haughty, unyielding. What crime has he committed? He is Lord [player.name]'s loyal partner! And that look gives Malkina all the inspiration she needs. "Now I understand. The most wicked have no sense of guilt at all."

What a rare thing: a sweet girl actually talking to them! And she didn't cry, didn't shake, didn't scream! [s2.name] opens right up, rattling on and on about their robberies, their killings, their fires. To [s2.name], it's just something to brag about. Doesn't occur to him how it might sound to anyone else. Not that he would care.
Malkina wipes spit from her face as she sketches. That ignorant, primal brutality...
"I'm looking for a scoundrel, and you're just the—" ...But before you could finish, [s2.name] stomped away, face dark with anger.
A Conclusion on Evil

From these meetings, Malkina learned much about "evil." She sketched face after face onto sheets of mica, then held them up proudly.
"Villains should have narrower faces, deeper-set eyes, hollowed cheeks. Their colors lean toward blue, green, even violet."
With swift strokes, she altered a bland, forgettable visage until it radiated menace.
"See? Now they look crueler, wealthier, more powerful—less to be trifled with!" Malkina laughed softly. "Thanks to you, I've truly learned a great deal."
Then, with brushes and powders, she turned her attention to you. A touch here, a shadow there... Soon, you looked like a villain yourself. And really—what's so wrong with that?

5006745.title: The Look of Power
strings: The Look of Power

You shared stories with Malkina about the powerful figures in your mind. These people are of the highest rank and would never deign to meet with her personally, but as one of the closest to power in the entire Empire, your own words are more than enough to inspire her. Whose story will you tell?
Malkina
Let me tell you about the sole master of the Lapis Lazuli Palace...
Let me tell you about a woman who pleases Sultan...
Let me tell you about a sword-bearing Iron Guard...
Let me tell you about a minister in power...
Malkina needs new inspiration.
A Little Talk About the Sultan
A Woman Who Pleases Sultan...
A Sword-Bearing Iron Guard...
A Minister in Power...

Speaking of power, we have to talk about the man at the top—the Sultan.
You sigh, clear your head, and start telling Malkina what the Sultan is really like and how it feels to be in the shadow of his rule.
When someone holds that much power, it swallows up their personality. Is he good-looking? It doesn't matter. Is he brave or smart? Also doesn't matter.
The only real question is: who would be brave enough to say he isn't?
You describe his daily look for the court: that mandatory coronet, the heavy gold chains, and all those jewels... every single one from a "loyal" courtier. You mention the golden patterns on his face, his favorite fancy fabrics, those gold shoes, and his two famous weapons.
Malkina doesn't blink once, nodding while her fingers idly trace the carpet, like she's already visualizing what "power" looks like.
Before you finish, you tell her this little talk stays between you two. Everyone knows what he looks like, but having it come from you is a political nightmare waiting to happen.
She gives a serious bow and promises to keep her mouth shut.

Where there is power, there is desire. And a ruler's desire manifests in the women around him. You spoke of a few favored consorts, who, with a smile, a song, or a single enchanting night, can shape the lives of countless subjects.
You considered which consort to describe first. Any choice will delight Malkina, for every guest wanted to know how Sultan's women dress, adorn themselves, and present their beauty.

You recalled Sultan's Iron Guards.
These men are Sultan's most trusted warriors; they do not meddle in politics directly, yet they may enter the court bearing swords slick with the blood of ministers.
You explained to Malkina that these guards wield real power—every courtier warns their children or heirs never to cross them. For if one day Sultan's wrath falls, and an Iron Guard raises their blade, no one kneeling in the court will save you!
You also described their uniforms which are often modeled after the regiments they command, yet far more sumptuous, costly, and impractical than any common soldier's attire.
She asked for more, eager to know the details. Now, which guard shall you start with?
Within the court, beyond Sultan and those closest to him, there are courtiers whose decisions shape the Empire's destiny. You are one among them. Which powerful figure will you recount to Malkina?

5006746.title: The Look of the Chivalry
strings: The Look of the Chivalry

Malkina has long admired the daring figures of the Dark Alley, or rather, the bandits and rogues who haunt it. She wanted to know more about their lives. Perhaps she can distill a way to make someone appear stronger, fiercer, more untamed. You happened to know quite a bit about these people. Which one will you bring for her to observe?
Malkina
Who is the true hero?
Malkina needs new inspiration.
You called the Mercenary over.
You called Raed over.
Enter Princess Raedina
You called the actual outlaw over.
Is [player.name] truly heroic?

With meat and wine, convincing him isn't difficult.
This swordsman stomped onto your pristine, expensive carpet, mud on his boots, and plopped down carelessly, grabbing some jerky as he eyes Malkina.
She asked him careful questions about combat attire, weapon placement, muscle training, and even the posture one takes when striking an enemy. At first, the Roaming Swordsman answered halfheartedly, but soon his interest was piqued. Setting down the food, he began demonstrating for Malkina.
"Shoulders back when you present yourself—looks bigger... hands at the sides, only fools cross their arms, how else will you draw a blade? Chest armor is unnecessary; ribs protect the heart, but wrap the abdomen with a belt! Fish skin over beast skin. It's smooth, deflects blades. Watch this."
He pulled out his weapon and spent hours exploring techniques with Malkina, who tidied up his messy hair and outfit as they chat. They enjoyed themselves immensely.

The moment Raed entered, Malkina gasped with delight. The Leader of the Vagrants perfectly embodied the "heroic rogue" she imagined: fierce eyes, a massive spiked mace, teeth like a wild beast! She eagerly recorded every detail, hardly needing him to speak.

When Princess Raedina entered, Malkina was taken aback. She expected a street brawler, not a princess draped in pearls and silver.
The princess sat, smiled, and applied small white porcelain pieces to her teeth.
"See? Fiercer now?"
Malkina's eyes widened in astonishment.
The two women conversed eagerly for hours, exchanging admiration freely.

When [s2.name] entered, Malkina was thrilled. This was a real "hero," down to the letter.
She circled [s2.gender(him,her)], showering compliments like "so handsome" and "so manly," while meticulously noting his attire, movements, and expressions.
Before leaving, Malkina grabed [s2.name]'s hand and requested a demonstration of a sand-thief's classic opening line.
That day, every servant in your household witnessed a sand-thief bellowing outside a noble's study, "Hand over all your money!"

No need to seek anyone else. You are a figure well-known in the Dark Alley. Whatever Malkina wants to learn, she can learn from you.
You showed her scars from past brawls, reveal hidden weapons, and even called a retainer from the Guesthouse to explain, "[player.name]'s reputation outside."
She w as amazed, and insisted you include her next time you go out for a daring escapade. She can stab with a needle!
You silently vowed to avoid letting her anywhere near such chaos in the future.
This one might be heroic enough...but not the right choice to truly inspire Malkina.
A Conclusion on Heroism

Excited, Malkina draged you aside and began applying makeup on your face.
"I see. You can lift the outer corners of the eyes that makes you look fierce! Darken the complexion, arch the eyebrows, droop the corners of the mouth... all facial lines must be sharp and pronounced, no soft shadows allowed!"
Her techniques were likely effective that the servant delivering the hookah recoiled at your appearance.

5006747.title: Hidden Among the Many
strings: Hidden Among the Many
Reading can improve yourself, so develop a habit of reading.
Currently Reading
The reader.
But if a book isn't taken out to be read often, it dies.
Y-you—why did you hold back the gift I sent to Lord Nawfal?
To keep safe what one cherishes—truly enviable.
Then I could write a book on jewelry collecting too! I know where the biggest, brightest gems are!
Warfire can burn pages, but it cannot burn out ideas.
You have gained much from this lesson.

5006748.title: 神的侍从
strings: 神的侍从
Malkina insists: a god must have an attendant... So who's going to be talked into playing you, the attendant of a newly born god?
要谁来扮演这个侍从
只有特定带有命运羁绊的角色才能成为你的神侍
需要找到合适的人
最终你也没有按照马尔基娜那莫名其妙的想法去做，虽然她很失望，但也没有掩盖这段时间你对她的帮助。
Enough. You are no god—you are my husband.
What nonsense are you speaking? I must refuse.
Very well. Wait... whose divine servant did you say?
A God's Adornments
Serve A God Closer to Home
A Touch of the Divine
Eager to Please
Discourse on the Divine
Trust, Faith, or Belief?
A Worthy Challenge
No Mere Illusion
好奇心
No Fear of Failure
A Hair's Breadth Between Hero and God
Her Devotion Adds to Your Radiance
A Divine Granting of Wishes
Jenna takes the job without hesitation. She talks it over with you again and again about props, materials, and every last detail. Just imagining it, clearly, is inspiration enough.

When you tell Iman to worship you as a god, he gazes at you for a long, long time. Silent.
As your eyes meet, everything you glimpse and he longs for—truth, power, wisdom, salvation—dissolves into light and a mysterious fragrance, filling the room.
When the light has touched every corner, Iman lowers his head, and agrees.

Badriyyah bursts out laughing—you, playing at god, and demanding her worship? How absurd. She's refused the Cultic Gods, and even the demons couldn't command her. What makes you think you can?
You smile. Tell her it's a joke. Isn't a mortal playing god the finest mockery of divine authority? You need her expertise, her talent for trickery, to pull it off.
She laughs again. Then, reluctantly, agrees. Neither of you mentions what just filled the room. That strange presence. What her laughter stirred.
You haven't even finished explaining before Nayla says yes. Watching her throw herself into the preparations, you're almost scared.

You know Qais won't agree if you just ask. You have to start with philosophy.
The debate deepens. You speak of gods, their existence, and their countless ways of shaping the world. The great labor it would take to create one.
Blossoms drift out of the void, clinging to Qais from head to toe. Outside the window, the sinuous silhouettes of demons drift by, along with their lascivious laughter. One by one, the signs appear: you are approaching the truth of the world.
And so, as Qais stands stunned into submission, you dispel the visions and—as if nothing had happened—ask him to join you in a little experiment: playing the part of gods.

Lumera hears your request and gives a light "Ah."
"I've read about things like this. How gods appear before mortals. How easily they make themselves believed." She smiles, meeting your eyes. "I'd be happy to play the god's attendant. And you—you were always meant to play the god."
That clear, trusting gaze holds you. Long enough to make your back sweat. Even a god can fear disappointing their own children, perhaps?

阿迪莱觉得这件事很有趣，所以她答应了下来。
“我小时候想过一样的事，是谁规定那些神像必须长成这个样子的呢？那些一模一样的眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴、衣服，都是谁弄出来的？啊哈，原来是您和马尔基娜这样的人！”
她大笑一场，而后仔细询问了这个“玩笑”的时间地点，承诺自己一定按时赶到。

Fatuna grips your hand—tight. Then kneels. "Sometimes... I worry that my mind conjures too many fantasies. That they might bring ruin to me... or to you." She bows low, forehead to the dust at your feet. "Now I know. This was meant to be. I feel it, truly, I am blessed."

扎齐伊非常兴奋地答应了你的请求，他还高兴地说，构想出了好多让你显得更神圣的点子！
只不过，他千叮咛万嘱咐，这件事千万别跟他妈妈说……毕竟他妈每年都给纯净者捐不少钱，肯定不会喜欢这种有点，嗯……有点亵渎的事！
Fardak accepts your proposal without a second thought. The more he plays the fool—the wilder, the more absurd—the happier the Sultan will be. And the safer his people. And your plans.

Aziz doesn't flinch at your request. Playing god may sound arrogant, sure. But in the stories of his people, strong leaders are gods themselves. Even their servants ascend, in the end. He has no grand ambitions, but he doesn't mind giving it a try.

Inal obeys, of course. She even finds it amusing!
What surprises you, though, is the faint pulse of a mysterious power in her blood. It resonates, somehow, with the divinity buried deep within you.

When you explain the plan to Faraj, he falters and hesitates, stumbling over his words. He's afraid—afraid it won't match what he's imagined. Maybe he's not ready...
You soothe him, again and again. "It's just an experiment, a prank." You promise there will be even better chances later, something more real.

5006749.title: First Taste of Divine Power
strings: First Taste of Divine Power
You are not yet a god. To work a miracle, you need magic. And the strongest magic in this city flows from the Sultan Cards in your hand. From the game itself, decreed by that mortal king.
The one who would play—or become—a god.
The one fated to serve you.
Insert the Sultan Card as the catalyst.
Consumable
用不同的苏丹卡，来展现不同的神的威能
苏丹卡不会被消耗
The Sultan Card is just a catalyst. You don't need to harm the innocent in this event. Rest easy.
最终你也没有按照马尔基娜那莫名其妙的想法去做，虽然她很失望，但也没有掩盖这段时间你对她的帮助。
Drawing Power from the Sultan Card
All Life Is Suffering
Mortal Arts
A God Among Us
展示真正的非人力量
Valor and Miracles
The Great Desires

The god's attendant is chosen. Now you turn to the question: what kind of "divine power" will you show?
You've convinced Malkina to stage the revelation at dusk across the river, where boatmen and dockworkers gather on the banks. You and your attendant will appear together and perform a miracle. If Malkina can truly shape "what a god should look like," if the miracle is wondrous enough... they might just believe you're a new god.
Of course, it all comes down to one thing: finding the right power. The kind of magic that different Sultan Cards cast on the hearts of those who see them.

The Extravagance Card... but a god draped in gold? Too vulgar. This city is already crawling with nobles wrapped in the stuff. The slaves here have seen it all. They won't be fooled so easily.
Then it hits you. Extravagance isn't just glittering lords. It's the freezing, starving poor. People might be tired of gilded deity statues. But a god who suffers? That they would yearn for.
Malkina grasps it at once. She promises the finest ascetic's rags for you and your attendant. And she'll "try not to make it too painful."
You almost can't wait.

马尔基娜确实拿出了所有本领。
她用银粉把你身体的某些部分提亮，另一些部分则用沥青般的黑色化妆膏厚厚覆盖住。她尤其强调了你的颧骨，经过她的勾画，你的脸看起来简直就像是活骷髅一般。她给你准备的服装是囚犯般的破衣烂衫，都拖着长长的破布，那些布向外支棱着，就像是你自己带来了寒风；其实是因为这些布被泡在米汤里定了型。
这一切做完之后，她又准备了一大盆的红色颜料，嘱咐你的侍从何时、何样地把它们倾倒进你面前的河流。
天色昏暗，河水奔流，对岸的纤夫们正倚在船边闲聊天。这正是个适合神明显圣的好日子……
你深吸一口气，跨出了藏身的树林。

You appear, sudden as a thought. A girl prying shellfish from its shell looks up and spots you. She lifts her hand and points, and soon every eye is on you. Your attendant chooses that moment to tip the bucket.
Gasps rise from the crowd. Every eye fixed on the "blood" seeping from the ground at your feet, spreading until a wide stretch of the river runs red. You stand perfectly still, your gaze mournful, fixed on the people across the shore.
This silent play is exactly the god they've been waiting for. A god who suffers, because they suffer. A god who endures, because they endure. A god who rages, because they rage, though they dare not speak it. Until now, they see a gaunt, tormented divinity, raging for them.
You feel their grief. You raise your hand, pointing to the setting sun. Its crimson light drips down like blood, washing away the painted stains, dyeing the whole river red.
All of them fall to their knees. Some throw themselves into the water, struggling toward your feet. For weeks after, these people will show the crowds the bloodstains on their skin, marks that never wash away. And all will see them as a blessing from the divine.
Malkina shaped the god's appearance. But the god's soul? That was woven by those who witnessed.

You breathe deep. Close your eyes. Let everything collapse inward, into your awareness. There, the Conquest Card shapes itself into a crown. It tempts you, reminding you of all you could achieve.
Yes. You had the power all along.
Your foot already rests on that faint line between mortal and divine.
Is this moment truly just a whim of Malkina's? Or could it be that your own power—so rich it overflows—has seeped into her, stirring something deep, making her reach, without knowing why, to carve out a chance for you...?
In the darkness, you smile. Then you gather your will and shape a ball of brilliant light, storing it in the place where your heart beats.
You open your eyes and tell Malkina you're ready. "This miracle will be a new sun."
She startles, then steadies soon.
"I'll prepare the perfect look for you. Something fit for the sun."
Measuring tape, makeup box, cloth in hand, she throws herself at you.

马尔基娜确实拿出了所有本领。
她在你头上洒满了金粉，你的头发看起来和阳光一样金灿灿；她又用树胶涂在圆形玻璃背面，把它们贴在你的全身上下。而后，她仔细为你化了妆，让额头更高，鼻梁更高，双眼的眼角下垂，嘴唇十分的薄。
“人们都觉得这样的面孔最神圣，”她一边忙着一边说，“一定要厌世，一定要满不在乎，一定要轻蔑——人们就是喜欢被神明看不起的感觉！”
她用一块几乎没有重量的轻纱围在你腰间，轻纱上也贴了大量的玻璃片；接着，她在你的手臂和躯干上贴了一些黑色的布；布是粗糙的、不会反光的，这样一来，从远处看，你的身体像是在金灿灿的光芒中支离破碎一般。
“人是没办法断成好几截还继续活动的，对吧？所以大家一看您这样，就知道您不是人啦。”
……事已至此，你也只能相信她了。
于是，装扮好的你走出藏身之处，让你的侍从跟在你身后。天色昏暗，河水奔流，对岸的纤夫们正倚在船边闲聊天。
你深吸一口气，从自己的胸中取出了那轮太阳，将之托举到头顶之上……

The moment the blazing sun rises from your chest, every last one of them drops to their knees. The haulers, the boatwomen, the porters—all of them. People weep, pressing their foreheads to the ground.
The sun climbs higher, setting you ablaze with light. Your form, artfully fragmented, shimmers and sways within the golden glow. Countless shards of glass catch the rays, reflecting the sunlight, until you blaze like the sky itself. Beside you, your attendant, robed in equal glory, chants, sings, and praises. A sight like this... once seen, one will never forget.
Malkina has done it. Not a single soul among them thinks you are merely a mortal, finely dressed. She has shaped, with her own hands, what a god should look like.
She has proven she can sculpt divinity itself. Though she admits, quietly: if the one being sculpted were not you, it might not have gone so smoothly.
When the revelation ends, Malkina sweeps a black cloth through the air. You slip behind it in an instant. The light dims, and night falls. The crowd stands frozen, mouths agape.
In the days that follow, the tale spreads: a god descended at dusk. And they say that god looked a bit like [player.name].

The Bloodshed Card calls to you. This mortal world—saturated with violence, rage, death—calls to you. Yes, slaughtering mortals would be a kind of divine power. But in a city drowning in blood and brutality, that won't make you stand out.
"Let's stage a miracle," you tell Malkina. "A battle against a monster. People remember the valiant hero, yes, but they remember the formidable enemy more."
Malkina understands at once. She grabs her cosmetics, sends word: find the biggest stray dogs they can. She'll dress you up. And then, before the crowd, you'll give them a show, a fight worth remembering.

马尔基娜确实拿出了所有本领。
她扯掉了你身上的几乎所有衣服，只在腰部围了一圈绳子。她又用更多绳子装饰你有力的臂膀和宽阔的后背，给你涂了油，又在绳子上挂了一些小绳子，让它们看起来就像是蛇。至于你的脸，勇猛的神不用显得太英俊，她只是把你的头发向高处梳，让你的头显得更小，从而衬的肩膀更宽、更有力；她给你涂抹了更黑的化妆膏，在你腰间挂上了一卷硕大的长鞭。
至于那些狗，马尔基娜在它们身上涂了磷，又用银粉涂了它们的尖牙；现在，在昏暗的日光下，它们看起来有如从地狱中现身的魔兽一般！
她做好这些事之后，又举起一面镜子让你和你的侍从看看自己的样子。你几乎惊呆了——镜子中的人孔武有力，面目狰狞，身形健硕地不可思议；而且，这人浑身都挂着似乎正在蠕动的蛇，还佩着一柄看起来足有一百斤重的长鞭……那些狗儿则欢快地低吠着，丝毫不知道自己现在看起来有多骇人。
于是，装扮好的你和侍从还有狗儿一起走出藏身之处，让你的侍从跟在你身后。天色昏暗，河水奔流，对岸的纤夫们正倚在船边闲聊天。
你深吸一口气，让侍从放出狗群，然后做出了一副与其作战的姿态……

Between your menacing glare and the dogs going feral over their chicken treats, the act is incredibly convincing. Throw in your attendant's wild antics and Malkina's magic, and you've managed to make the absurd look authentic. That's the core of divinity: doing the ridiculous with total conviction.
The crowd is absolutely spellbound. At first, they're scared the "beast" will swallow you whole, but then they take one look at your snakes and your gear and realize you're the one in charge.
The show was supposed to end with the dogs retreating into Malkina's smoke, but the crowd's fear has taken on a life of its own. They aren't just watching a show anymore. They're waiting for a god to save them.
The long shadows of the sunset blend the dogs into a single, terrifying beast with heads to spare. It lets out a roar, clears the stage, and comes for you with a mouth as red as the evening sky.
In the local folklore, it's now a fact that a god like [player.name] saved the city and its river from a great evil. It took a lot of bandages to fix the "phantom" bruises you walked away with, but the dogs certainly didn't mind the act—they were paid handsomely in chicken.

You look at the Carnality Card in your hand, a tether to the restless sea of human desire. Lust, appetite, the need for attention, the drive to survive... how do you spark that one craving shared by everyone?
As you watch these tangled whims rise and fall, it suddenly makes sense. Everyone just wants to outshine their neighbor. But the millions left behind? All they want is a level playing field.
Malkina's hands are a blur while you're lost in thought. She's already dolling you up, making sure you look like the brilliant, kind god you are.

Malkina gives it everything she has.
She robes you in a white cope so pure it covers every inch of skin. Then drapes you in silver chains, like a sacred sinner. She sweeps your hair back, baring your face, and paints you pale as bone.
"You need to look like them," she says, working swiftly on your face. "The suffering ones. The poor. So they'll believe you've come to save them. But keep your eyes closed. Always closed. It makes you look more pained. More holy."
She traces silver and diamond patterns across your eyelids, then brushes more silver dust into the shape of tears. After that, she adorns your followers in the same way.
For the final touch, she gives you some herbs to make your voice raw and raspy.
Dusk settles. The river flows. On the far bank, haulers lean against their boats, chatting. A good day for a god to appear.
You breathe deep. Step from the trees.

You begin to speak, your voice low, raw, rasping. At first, they think you're just a madman, babbling. But soon your words carry farther, farther still, reaching even the far shore of the river. One by one, they set down their work and listen, drawn in by what you say.
You tell them: every soul is born in mercy of the divine. And you are living proof, for you have touched each one. Then you speak of the worst among them: those who steal the joy from other souls, hoarding it with dark magic, with lies and concealment. This you cannot bear. How you wish every being you ever touched could know equal happiness... and so the tears burn down your face. And so you have come. To tell them: do not give up. Do not despair. You were meant for joy. Look to the root of your sorrow. Do not fear, a god stands behind you. All of this is permitted.
The haulers, the boatwomen, the porters all stand frozen, staring. Your sacred robes. Your eyes, clenched in pain. That noble, solemn face Malkina painted. The attendant, kneeling in devotion behind you. But most of all: your words. Even Malkina admits: she can shape a god's appearance, but she cannot forge words that pierce the heart like this.
They fall to their knees on the riverbank. All of them. And they weep—with joy, with grief, with sudden understanding, with hatred long suppressed. Not a single soul among them thinks you are merely a mortal, finely dressed. Malkina has done it. She has shaped, with her own hands, what a god should look like.
In the days that follow, the tale spreads: a god descended at dusk. And people say: so that's what a god looks like... a bit like [player.name], they say.

Servants beat drums and gongs, shook bells and waved torches, shouting as they struck the thickets to flush out hidden prey. Falcons wheeled high above, their piercing cries guiding the hunters. Hounds ran eagerly, barking and bounding forward, waiting for their master's command.
You rode to the crest of a hill, leaving servants and friends behind. The open sky, the wind, the scent of grass—this is the taste of freedom.
Nabhani soon shattered the quiet, shameless as ever. He galloped past, hollering a challenge, waving his arm in mock provocation. "Come on! [player.name]! Let's see who spots the great beast first!"
Faris followed with his hounds, circling you, tails wagging, teeth bared, waiting for the chase to begin.
Jabal rode alongside, wiped his brow, and handed you a chilled cup of light wine. "What a fine day this is!" he said with a grin.
Adila appeared on another rise, pointing with her blade. "There! The trees are moving!" Without waiting, she spurred her horse down the slope.
"Wait for me!" cried Zaki, spear in hand, scrambling to catch up. You cannot help but laugh at his flustered haste—time to spur your own steed and let him chase for once.
And there, keeping to the flanks, was Seliman. Silent, deliberate, slipping along the ridge to cut the prey off. Curse him. You cannot let him take the glory!
[s8.name] arrived too, while [s8.gender] waved from another hilltop across the valley. No need for worry. Soon you will all meet again at the hunting grounds below.
Something is about to break through the undergrowth. By rights, you should hold your ground and let it come to you. But Gullis plunges headlong into the woods, and no hunter will be left behind.

You followed Gullis into the shadowed depths. "There's a place where bears roam," he said. "That is a prey worthy of this hunt." The canopy thickened, the air darkened, and his face hardened with focus. At a stream crossing, he suddenly halted. "Master, I have a request." His eyes burned with resolve. "Will you cross blades with me?"

Seizing his chance while the others were distracted, Nabhani caught up with Gullis and led him to the edge of the hunting grounds, where a cluster of noble ladies watches the hunt from afar.
Then, with a dramatic flourish, he dived into the water alongside the hunter-slave to wrestle a crocodile barehanded. The fight was mostly Gullis's doing. Nabhani, clad in pure white silk, let the water soak him until every muscle showed beneath the fabric. He rose and dived again like some swan, or perhaps a duck, while the noblewomen swoon with delight.
At last, they hauled the crocodile ashore—mostly thanks to Gullis's strength. The hunter slave rested on the bank, catching his breath. Watching Nabhani preen and pose, he suddenly spoke:
"I've heard you are the finest swordsman in the Capital. Will you not cross blades with me? With so many beauties watching, surely they would love to see a duel."
Nabhani turned toward him with the look of a man finding family at last. Of course, he had been waiting for such a stage.

Faris, with his pack at his heels, pressed on into the forest alongside Gullis. They tracked the heavy prints of a great beast, deeper and deeper into the wilds.
At last, they came upon a massive stone cavern at the edge of a cliff. Inside, piles of animal bones lay scattered, yet the master of the lair was nowhere to be found. Only a few particularly large animal bones remained, hinting at the creature that once dwelled there.
Gullis cursed their ill luck, convinced that the noise of the hunt had driven the creature off. But Faris was unbothered.
"Good," he said easily. "If it fled, it still lives. If it lives, it will sire cubs. And then we shall have more lions to hunt. A hunt is never spoiled simply because you do not strike the final blow."
On their way back, they caught plenty of other game. The hounds were wild with joy, long denied such sport.

Faris caught the Little Moon by its scruff and set it running with the rest of the pack. Together with Gullis, he followed the trail of the great beast, deeper and deeper into the hunt.
At last, they came upon a massive stone cavern at the edge of a cliff. Inside, piles of animal bones lay scattered, yet the master of the lair was nowhere to be found. Only a few particularly large animal bones remained, hinting at the creature that once dwelled there.
Gullis cursed their ill luck, convinced that the noise of the hunt had driven the creature off. But Faris was unbothered.
"Good," he said easily. "If it fled, it still lives. If it lives, it will sire cubs. And then we shall have more lions to hunt. A hunt is never spoiled simply because you do not strike the final blow."
On their way back, they caught plenty of other game. The hounds were wild with joy, long denied such sport.

Seliman labored through the mire with Gullis, pushing on into the far reaches of the hunting ground, where a pale swamp spread beneath a dying sky.
Together they waded through mud and stagnant pools, lying in wait among rotting logs.
At last they glimpsed it: a prize gleaming like a jewel in the filth, a giant marsh serpent with sapphire-striped scales as wide as a hand. It slid slowly, sinuously through the waters, searching for prey—or perhaps for the hunters themselves.

Jabal, brimming with enthusiasm, tracked the signs beside Gullis until the trail led them to a wall of stone cliffs. They climbed, inch by inch, until they reached the nesting ground of the wild Bharal. These beasts were wary and swift beyond measure. Could they mask their scent well enough, move quietly enough, to claim so rare and elusive a prize?

Adila could not wait. She and Gullis pursued their quarry all the way to the end of the hunting ground, into a shadowed gorge where the sun never reached. There, the songs of the dreaded harpies were said to ensnare the hearts of all who heard them. She stuffed her ears with wool and, blade in hand, set off at a reckless pace, dragging Gullis into the darkness with her.

Zaki followed Gullis into the woods without a second thought.
There, they stumbled upon a hunter's snare already sprung. Inside was a mother bear, fierce and snarling, with her cub cowering behind her.
As the two debated what to do, the trapper himself appeared. Without a word, he struck, mistaking them for thieves come to steal his prize.
At last, [s8.name] and Gullis reached the very heart of the hunting grounds. There, they brought down a magnificent stag, a trophy to crown the day's sport and a worthy prize for your Grand Hunt.

Gullis propped himself up with both hands, stubborn defiance burning in his eyes. Just as you drew breath to speak further, a sound from the thicket interrupted. A tiger, drawn by the fight, was closing in. Brace for battle!

When your blades sink deep into the tiger's flesh, you can no longer tell whose blood soaks you. The beast collapses, pinning you beneath its weight. Your vision blurs... The last thing you see: Gullis, pulling his blade from the tiger's back.

Gullis held back just enough, stopping the tip of his blade an inch from Nabhani's chest without so much as nicking the Capital's finest swordsman. Nabhani paused for a moment, then burst into laughter.
"Look, look!" he exclaimed, grabbing Gullis by the arm and parading the slave before all the noblewomen watching the fight. "Here is the fiercest, most skilled, and handsome warrior! Can you believe you didn't recognize him until now, my lovely ladies!"
The women laughed and bombarded Gullis with questions—how old was he, where had he learned to fight, had he served a mistress before? Flustered, Gullis hurriedly dragged the crocodile he had claimed as a trophy away, cheeks burning red. Nabhani followed leisurely, chatting with the ladies as they walked.
The Grand Hunt was a resounding success, and tales of it lingered long in noble circles.

Nabhani had captured the grandest prize of the entire Grand Hunt—all the hearts of the ladies.
Noblewomen crowded around, asking if he had been hurt. Gullis was pushed to the side, while Nabhani laughed, dragging the slave back beside him. He clasped Gullis's hand and announced to all the ladies,
"See here, another brave and handsome warrior worthy of your attention!"
Gullis, cheeks burning, trailed behind Nabhani through the swirl of powdered skirts and fluttering fans as they hauled the crocodile together, Gullis carrying the heavier share as usual.
It was, without a doubt, the most exhilarating hunt they had ever known.

Accidents weren't uncommon during the Grand Hunt, so no one minded much; however, Jabal insisted on giving Gullis a generous reward for saving his life.

It turned out that they had indeed ventured into the valley rumored to be haunted by monsters, only to find a slave hunter camp instead. The terrifying stories had been deliberately spread to keep people away.
These slave hunters often captured slaves who already had masters, and sometimes even forced commoners into bondage—something Adila and Gullis only learned after giving the slave hunters a good thrashing.
The Grand Hunt ended on a triumphant note, with everyone praising your sense of justice, wealth, and influence.

Afterward, he and Gullis filled the trap with soil and wood, then stepped aside to watch as the mother bear led her cubs out and disappeared into the forest.
When they returned to the hunting grounds' edge, they recounted the story to everyone. The onlookers praised their actions—though surely some secretly would have preferred a bloodied trophy, they at least congratulated Zaki and Gullis aloud.
Zaki was beaming with pride, and though Gullis said nothing, you could see he agreed with your student's approach.

Zaki and Gullis had failed to stop the hunters. They had only managed to save themselves. As they fled the hunters' ambush, the desperate roar of the mother bear echoed behind them.
They returned to the hunting grounds' edge dejectedly, where you were waiting... Still, they had at least tried, and that alone made it a fairly successful hunt.
