The Loss of Two Slaves

Zephyr led Gullis out to the hills beyond the city, his favorite place to run free. The valleys here were rich with grass, and wild game was plentiful. Together they delighted in the chase: Gullis loosed the arrows, while Zephyr gladly took the role of the hound, harrying the quarry until it faltered.
As the sun dipped low, a drifting shadow spoiled Gullis's shot. The deer bolted, wounded but not down. Zephyr shot forward like lightning, refusing to give up...

On any other day, Zephyr would never have risked running the cliff edge at sunset. But with the deer before his eyes, he saw nothing else.
At the last instant, Gullis caught Zephyr's arm and hauled him back from the brink. "Turns out Gullis can run as fast as me!" Zephyr never tired of boasting about it afterward.

Just as the deer sprang for the ravine's edge, Zephyr leapt and locked his arms around its neck. For a few breathless moments, he rode the beast between the cliffs, clinging on like a mad knight.
The tale had been told so often it wore the ear. And so, when Zephyr began again, you summoned Gullis to speak of the omitted part—the shameful moment when Zephyr retched upon the earth and lost the deer regardless.
Zephyr took Gullis to his second home—the Dog Track. Before long, the two were at each other's throats over which hound was best. Fortunately, here the results came quickly and decisively.

Luck favored Zephyr that day: he spread his bets wide and claimed win after win. Gullis, ever stubborn, placed his hopes on a single dog, and when the final race overturned every odd, his wager soared. Both men left richer than they came.
At Gullis's insistence, they shared their winnings with you, their patron. But from the wild gleam in his eyes, you could tell the nomad was already learning the city's bad habits.

Zephyr and Gullis slunk home empty-handed, trading blame at every step. "If we'd bet on my dog, we'd have won for sure!" "No, it was your foolish pick that sunk us!"
So ended their costly lesson. The city taught quickly, and never cheaply.
He had fled! The ungrateful wolf could not be tamed. Though you knew it was in vain, you sent riders through every street to hunt the runaway slave—if nothing else, so all might witness your wrath.
He would have tried... but his wife still lived. In your fury, you lashed Zephyr instead, for failing to keep Gullis in sight.
Zephyr, too, had vanished! Your heart bled, for these were your possessions, your wealth. One faithless slave corrupted another. Curse them both!

Inal delighted in roaming the fields. To her, hunting with Gullis was merely play. Gullis snared rabbits and a fox, while Inal gathered armfuls of flowers and herbs. Between them, scarcely a word was spoken, yet both felt a quiet ease.
Then a horse appeared—broad of chest, glossy of coat, clearly no wild beast but a stallion strayed from its herd. Was its master still searching?
Almost without thought, Gullis gave chase like a beast himself, matched the horse's stride, then leapt upon its back, and soon the proud animal was his.

When Inal tried to protest, Gullis pulled her up behind him. There was no saddle, yet his horsemanship was sure, and the steed strong. Like the wind, they flew across the meadow, smiling each their own hidden smile.
At last, Gullis set Inal gently down and, with a sharp slap to its flank, sent the horse racing toward the wilds beyond the city. Neither spoke, yet the unshared smile still lingered on their faces.

Inal scolded Gullis fiercely: this was not finding, but stealing! Together they tracked the hoofprints until they met a frantic herdsman. The rancher's thanks—and reward—were quick to follow, though Gullis's towering frame and dangerous bearing might have helped.
Still, he muttered in bitter protest, "Back on the steppe, I could mount any horse I pleased!"

With their rare reward in hand, Inal resolved to treat Gullis to a delicacy found only in the capital. She described the great iron cauldron of boiling syrup, the fragrance of nuts roasting within... never noticing that her purse had slipped away into a pickpocket's hand. It was a crushing loss for a slave girl.

Like lightning, Gullis struck. One kick bent the pickpocket's leg, and one fist hammered his face until he was unrecognizable beneath blood and swelling. By the time Inal caught up, it was already done.
Later, it seemed Gullis never did taste the sugared nut fritters, and you did not ask where the coin was spent—such money was trifling, after all.

Inal's cry rang through the market: "Thief!" At once, the workers of the market seized the boy before Gullis could even reach him. By Inal's counsel, the boy received only a few sharp slaps, and before long, their punishment ended in the sharing of sugared nut fritters.
Inal tried her best to explain how Gullis was swift as a leopard and cunning as a fox, and how the market was far too crowded for anyone to intervene. Anyway, punishing her would serve no purpose.
Inal too had vanished! Your heart bled, for these were your possessions, your wealth. One faithless slave corrupted another. Curse them both!

With Aziz at his side, Gullis carried in a single morning what would normally take three days' worth of firewood. Under the blazing sun, light gleamed across sweat and sinew alike.
Soon enough, other slaves gathered round, watching as the two giants locked arms and wrestled for dominance.
By the time you arrived, only two battered, bruised servants remained. The crowd had scattered, but you learned enough—Gullis had claimed the victory.

Aziz resorted to wrestling techniques—the kind born of the steppe.
Caught unprepared, Gullis was seized by the belt and hurled down like a sack of grain. It was a mighty throw, but the laughter of onlookers stoked Gullis's fury. A dagger suddenly appeared in his hand, and in the tongue of the tribes, he challenged Aziz to a duel to the death.

Before you could stop it, Aziz dropped to his knees, covering his head and surrendering wisely. Gullis spat curses you did not understand and flung the dagger to the earth. Seeing you nearby, he fell silent at once.
In the end, you chose not to intervene further.

Aziz seized a stout wooden stick to answer the challenge. They exchanged three blows: Gullis carved three bloodied lines into Aziz's flesh, while Aziz's stick struck hard against Gullis's brow. You stepped in before the fight could go further. Thankfully, when Gullis awoke, he showed some measure of respect for the outcome.

Aziz seized a stout wooden stick to answer the challenge. They exchanged three blows. On the last, the stick splintered against Gullis's shoulder, yet Gullis pressed in close, dagger drawn, and laid its point against Aziz's throat. Perhaps it was only because he knew your eyes were upon him.
In any case, both men had spent their rage, and you chose not to intervene further.

They sought out those even lower than themselves, buying what passed for a master's dignity, a man's pride. Aziz knew the path well. He and Gullis hired prostitutes of three different hues of skin and lost themselves until dawn, stumbling home on unsteady legs.

In the capital, every craving found its merchant. Aziz led Gullis to a tavern catering to slaves of the steppes. There they drank the fierce liquor brewed from souring milk in the stomach, showed off their knives, and devoured raw meat and cheese unfit for city dwellers. In a storm of curses and laughter, they sealed their bond as brothers.
Aziz came back meekly and confessed everything to you, yet punishment proved unavoidable. To make an example of him before the others, you had Aziz soundly flogged.
Aziz, too, had vanished! Your heart bled, for these were your possessions, your wealth. One faithless slave corrupted another. Curse them both!

Salwiyah never missed a chance to exchange glances with passersby. Though, of course, she never aimed such charms at Gullis! Those arts of seduction were never meant for a mere slave.
When they emerged from the spice shop, a young noble and his attendants blocked their path...

But Gullis struck with lightning speed, knocking them all aside. There was barely time to see whose master he served!
Even Salwiyah found herself momentarily enchanted by this Gullis, letting him lead her home while she giggled foolishly.

Gullis tried to resist, but a blow from behind sent him reeling—the situation spun out of control. When you arrived, he was drenched in blood, and three bodies lay sprawled on the ground... Ah, well, no matter. Lord [player.name] had bigger worries. Better head home.
Salwiyah did not hesitate to spend the coins herself, leaving none for Gullis. Naturally, he offered no objection.
Of course, Salwiyah did not flee; she still hoped to bask in Lord [player.name]'s favor.

As the pair walked through the market, a bricklayer suddenly hurled a jar at Arumina! Gullis intercepted it, flipping it back onto the attacker's face. The man drew a knife, shouting accusations at Jawad to the gathering crowd, claiming Jawad's usury had killed his parents. Blood ran down his forehead, staining his eyes red—today was the day of his vengeance.

The avenger's eyes met Gullis's once more, friction thick in the air.
"You have the wrong person," Gullis said, his voice capable of chewing nails. "Only one slave boy and one slave girl serving Lord [player.name] here. Those who destroyed your parents are long dead... Now, put down your weapon, or I shall kill you."
The matter ended thus, though sobs from both sides lingered through the day, leaving Gullis perturbed.

The avenger's eyes met Gullis's once more, friction thick in the air.
Gullis read the avenger's resolve and placed his dagger into the hands of the slave girl once known as Arumina.
He stepped aside, letting them settle their dispute themselves.

With a single strike, the fight was over. Arumina's dagger was buried deep in the avenger's abdomen—he had practically run into it himself!
Luckily, the avenger's knife only grazed Arumina's arm... The feud was thus ended.

With a single exchange of strikes, the fight was over. Arumina's dagger was buried deep in the avenger's abdomen—he had practically run into it himself!
Unluckily, the avenger's knife pierced Arumina's chest... The two glared in mutual resentment, twitching on the ground in agony for some time before the matter was finally concluded.

Arumina took Gullis to watch the city's acrobatic performance—somersaults, flying knives, magic, fire-breathing... It turned out Gullis favored the puppet play above all.
Amid these stories and laughter, they seemed to forget the sorrows of slavery... As Gullis cheered, Arumina habitually threw her coins onto the stage. She immediately regretted it—what a waste! That was a fortune! Gullis merely smiled and tossed his share as well, letting the puppets dance mockingly around them.
Arumina wept, begging you not to punish her, for Gullis was beyond her control... But you still struck her five times—no other reason than that you could.
Arumina, too, had vanished! Your heart bled, for these were your possessions, your wealth. One faithless slave corrupted another. Curse them both!

Habib was delighted with your arrangement and immediately set off with Gullis. They arrived at a bustling fishing port, where Habib told Gullis that he had long wished to catch fresh fish for cooking—especially the tiny, finger-length whitefish that would die almost instantly once removed from the water. Fried while still fresh, their flavor was said to be exquisite. Habib set up a large pot of hot oil by the riverbank, and Gullis waded into the water to catch the fish. The two of them labored together all afternoon... During the whole process, Habib had tied a very long rope to Gullis's ankle, with the other end secured to his own wrist. He claimed it was to prevent Gullis from drowning.
In any case, the dish turned out wonderfully.

Salt was the most precious seasoning on the steppe, and beef symbolized wealth—so salt-roasted ox hearts were considered a lavish feast for the nobility. Of course, in the capital, salt was far cheaper. After learning from Gullis, Habib cooked up a portion enough to satisfy any highborn nomad and share among everyone present.

Habib was delighted with your arrangement and immediately set off with Gullis. They arrived at a bustling fishing port, where Habib told Gullis that he had long wished to catch fresh fish for cooking—especially the tiny, finger-length whitefish that would die almost instantly once removed from the water. Fried while still fresh, their flavor was said to be exquisite. Habib set up a large pot of hot oil by the riverbank, and Gullis waded into the water to catch the fish. The two of them labored together all afternoon... During the whole process, Habib had tied a very long rope to Gullis's ankle, with the other end secured to his own wrist. He claimed it was to prevent Gullis from drowning.
In the end, Habib returned home with only half the rope...
Of course, you didn't scold Habib too harshly—after all, you still wanted to eat his cooking. It is basic wisdom that one does not anger a chef or a barber lightly.

Alim took Gullis through the Dark Alley, pointing out signs, tattoos, and building marks that required attention. This was also to ensure his gang recognized the face, lest anyone attempt to pilfer Gullis's purse and end up with broken fingers.

If nobles had bathhouses, naturally the poor had their own... though the smell left much to be desired.
When Gullis stripped off his clothes, revealing scars and tattoos, a small gap opened in the crowded water entrance. Alim peacefully enjoyed this rare calm, brought by the young man.
No matter how Gullis tried to flee, Alim could always find him somewhere in the city... In the end, the two returned as if nothing had happened.

Faraj enjoyed a smooth and pleasant day. Negotiators who were usually prickly treated him with courtesy. The petty officials who once delighted in giving trouble kept silent. No one demanded bribes...
As Lord [player.name] had said, one day, the capital's manners would improve! Faraj thought this until he noticed Gullis constantly making a monstrous face behind him.
Then, Gullis led Faraj to a tavern in the Dark Alley where only slaves would enter. Faraj heard and saw things he ought to know, yet this was the first time in his life he had encountered them.
Gullis got away, and Faraj failed to catch him—perhaps deliberately?

Gullis wasn't completely illiterate—he could at least read numbers! Shama liked students with a foundation; she could teach something a bit trickier, which everyone found interesting...
A few days later, you had to send all your servants to hunt down Gullis's scribbled curses—some you could pronounce but had never dared to write... Soon, even the Sultan learned about this wildly "cultured" slave of yours.

This used to be her everyday life, but now she could only relive it briefly through your grace. Shama didn't care for Gullis at first, yet this rugged man surprisingly knew his way around herbs and teas—he had once managed the steppe's most lucrative trade... Together, they refined a nourishing floral tea while quietly reminiscing about their former selves.
Did the city folk lure the steppe folk astray, or did the steppe folk lead the city folk into the wilderness? No one could say...

When you found Nawfal, he was already lying in a pool of blood, alongside the corpses of his two companions. His eyes were full of endless sorrow and a hint of relief.

In those final moments, you wondered if his eyes saw you, the victor. You couldn't know anyway. After all, the dead can't speak.

When you found Nawfal, he was already lying in a pool of blood... The instant you approached, he mustered all his strength to lunge at you.
Fortunately, even immense hatred couldn't overcome the loss of blood and fatigue; he slipped like a clown and was soon hacked to pieces by your men... Nawfal, you were never good at fighting, were you?

The ambush turned into a chaotic melee, everyone entangled in confusion. You swing your blade wildly in the dimly-lit room, surrounded by death, friend and foe indiscernable with each swings. Suddenly, behind a curtain, you spot Nawfal's silhouette...
When you pierced the curtain with all your might, you found Nawfal crawling disoriented from under the crushed drapery, loudly calling for retreat...
Afterwards, upon examining the body beneath the drapery, you discovered she was the nomadic woman who always followed Nawfal.
At least, this folly would severely decimate Nawfal’s morale, temporarily prevent him from hindering you.

You killed many, burned down this house, but amidst the archaic scene, Nawfal escaped.

Your twisted and prolonged struggle with Nawfal greatly pleased the Sultan, who ordered a troupe to create a special drama for repeated enjoyment... next festival.

As a powerful courtier, Nawfal's death inevitably triggered a shockwave; people gossiping, whether noble or commoner, both lost friends or family in the struggle, ensuring no shortage of trouble to follow!

5008001.title: Worries of the Wife
strings: Worries of the Wife
Now, everyone says the Sultan Card freed your nature – allowing you to do what you love most: rape, bloodshed… What others think doesn’t matter much, but what about Maggie's thoughts?

Maggie waited for you for several days. At bedtime together, at dinners together, when you attempted to kiss her lips... you remained silent, leaving her with only unfathomable disappointment.
It's impervious that you care about her attitude
She chooses to trust you.
So, this is the real you.

Of course, you understand Maggie's worries. At the dressing table, you embrace her from behind, soaking in the scent of her long hair, sharing your inner struggles.
Perhaps these flowery words were not entirely sincere, but Maggie felt what she needed most... Your need and respect for her.

She turns to rub her nose and cheeks against your face, telling you she will walk with you no matter what path you choose.

Does Maggie care about present sin because she is kind? Or does she worry about future punishment because she is afraid? You feel neither, but you know that this woman won't abandon you – at least, not before you manifested those imaginary crimes into reality.
Your attitude of admission instead reveals your mindlessness towards the crime... or rather, your mindlessness towards your wife. Deep ran Maggie's disappointment.

strings: Arming the Wife

With your Notoriety spreading throughout the capital, visitors to your home are no longer restricted to nobles – snake-summoning magicians, muscle-flexing barbarians, purpled face monks, thieves, smugglers... of course, none of them could win Maggie's affections. She always worried about home theft or felt these people eyed her with malice... Know this, Maggie isn't a timid woman. If you don't handle these matters, Maggie may have to handle them herself.

Maggie made a wooden dummy target – complete with correct vital points and joint structures, even two sandbags as eggs... she would practice swinging, hacking, and then use a roundhouse kick to send the dummy's eggs flying high.
Neighbors, visitors from all walks of life, and you, were all hugely frightened.
They respect me because of you.
You promise the carpet will be clean at home.
She continued on her own way.

You tell Maggie that these people, although suspicious, unhygienic, and poor in fashion, are each more kind-hearted than the well-dressed courtiers of the Sultan’s court.

More importantly, Maggie is the most beautiful, most benevolent, and most noble woman they have ever seen in their lives... these people, like adventurers in stories, respect the lord's wife and are willing to work for you.

Hearing this, Maggie laughed heartily, warning you not to think she hadn't read those romance novels which detailed affairs and relationships between lord's wife and other men, but you're not really worried, after all, you are the only man in this household who regularly bathes.
Soothing the wife indeed takes more effort than dealing with unruly toughs, but at least you still managed to do so...

strings: Special pillow
The wife prepared a special gift for you...
You can use this to break a Carnality Card

Wife

That night, as you lay down to sleep, Maggie gazed at you with a somewhat mischievous expression.

Just as you were about to ask her what was going on, you noticed a rare fragrance wafting from your bed, soothing you and reducing your stress significantly. "I added some herbs to your pillow, brought from my hometown, it can make people feel better and fall asleep more easily..." her face turned slightly red. "... and also make you, umm..." You understood her implications and wrapped your arms around her slender waist...

These herbs are indeed effective.

A servant tells you that today your wife quarreled with a noblewoman in the bathhouse – something you found ludicrous – Maggie is most elegant and dignified, as such, you have never seen her unfriendly to anyone in public.

"It was because that noblewoman said you would surely misuse the Carnality Card and fool around... and the madam got angry and stood up loudly saying – "my husband is not like that, rescind your words and apologize!"
The noblewoman did indeed apologize, perhaps forced by your power, or perhaps she hoped for the miracle of steadfast loyalty between you and Maggie.

5008005.title: Wife's Tea Party
strings: Wife's Tea Party
Ever since you got involved in the Sultan’s Game, Maggie began hosting tea parties for noblewomen at home...
The tea party needs to be hosted by your wife.
You must participate yourself to break the Sultan Card.

Using a Stone tier Extravagance Card costs 4 Gold Coins, a Bronze tier Extravagance Card costs 8 Gold Coins, and a Silve tier Extravagance Card costs 15 Gold Coins.

You must attend the tea party yourself to place the Sultan Card
Insert the correct number of Gold Coins to break the corresponding Extravagance Card
Need to insert proper numbers of Gold Coins to break an Extravagance Card
Pretentious play
You prepared some exotic fruits.
You prepared an expensive tea set.
You hired a theater troupe.
You raped a female slave at the tea party.
You had an affair with a noblewoman at the tea party.
You pinned Maggie in full view of everyone.
Most noblewomen have been trained into foolish, vulgar creatures who only know how to compare and pander to power – they are completely out of place with Maggie.

These fruits cannot be grown locally; only shipping traders who use secret techniques to harvest them before they are ripe manage to have some arrive intact across the oceans. Although they might not be that tasty, they are impressive enough – as all noblewomen care about is face anyway.

These exquisite porcelain pieces came from a distant land, each pieces of noble customs, meaning the designs and motifs on them aren’t of distant and foreign beasts, but of native legendary stories and floral patterns – this thoughtfulness and social connections earned great appraisal, and even Maggie lovingly placed them in a special display cabinet.

Everyone sipped tea and ate snacks, complimented and criticized the actors’ skills, even exchanged some not-so-outrageous jokes... all said your tea party was the most stylish in the capital, especially considering the Sultan never holds a tea party.

You didn’t bother being picky, just randomly called on a noblewoman’s servant girl – no one cared about their fate anyway.
Yet, not all noblewomen absconded your actions. Some were eager to find thrilling tales of the Sultan's game; they commented on your physique, size, and even the feedback from the female slave, as if this was all just an insignificant tea party show. Except for Maggie and that innocent victim, no one felt particularly embarrassed.

She kept seducing you with her eyes and gestures and mouth and tongue... you weren’t interested anyway, but there’s a Carnality Card that needed usage.
Maggie, serving guests snacks, saw your actions behind the room curtain. She knew tomorrow you would speak of this in court, everyone would know – but she said nothing, only turned and walked away.
As her distinct footsteps faded, the whore beneath you screamed even more indulgently...

"No time left, I must break this Carnality Card right now!"
You push the porcelain off the table, letting it shatter on the garden tiles... Maggie barely struggles beyond the initial surprise – she hears the exclamations, screams, and whispers of the noblewomen beside her, hesitates slightly, then embraces your backbone, responding to your passion with her strong legs and slender lips.
The lovemaking continues for quite some time, leaving every participant at the tea party, both nobles and servants, agape with surprise, fear, confusion, near faintings – yet no one avert their eyes.
Finally, a quick-witted maid brings a blanket between the kisses, which you use to wrap the exhausted Maggie, holding her close as you announce the end of the tea party.

Though it's called a tea party, it's really about exchanging intelligence, spreading rumors, plotting, and flattery – all of which tires Maggie out, as she ill-loved such scheming, but she never complains to you.

Fatuna casually mentions to noblewomen that she recently acquired a fascinating crystal ball revealing future visions through special techniques. Ladies eagerly request readings, bizarre questions flowing freely while Fatuna handles each gracefully. In this dimly lit chamber, none notice darkness itself peering into their souls, feasting on their boundless desires.

This subtle yet unsettling chill makes Maggie wrap her shawl tighter. She maintains a forced smile while conversing with guests, hearing their ceaseless complaints, schemes, and flattery - exhausting Maggie completely. She never enjoyed these political maneuverings but never complains to you.
From then on, Maggie never hosted tea parties again.
Of course, there will never be tea parties again, even though many people were quite looking forward to them.

5008006.title: Encouragement
strings: Encouragement

Recently, your renown in the capital has been increasing, requiring you to handle more matters and meet more people, naturally with more help from Faraj. Sometimes, after reporting on the day's affairs, he looks at you with anticipation...
Faraj awaits your praise
Praise his valor
Praise his alertness
Praise his grace

Faraj yearns for your affirmation – yours.
The three of you have lunch together.
I'll leave my back to you.
You are my eyes.
You are my spokesperson.
Obviously, such formal hospitality makes Faraj flattered... He even seems a bit nervous, yet it also makes him seem adorable – even Maggie rarely smiles several times.
Faraj is greatly encouraged. He excitedly invites you for a practice session with wooden swords, imagining a battle scenario where you two are surrounded by enemies back-to-back.

You praise him for three meticulous qualities surpassing your own, two of which are true, and one is an extra commendation. Faraj is greatly encouraged, and when he leaves your home, he squints at the surrounding streets as if trying to immediately spot something noteworthy.

Upon hearing you say this, he immediately stands up, straightens his clothes, and earnestly asks whether he needs a more stable accessory...
You smile and tell him the best accessory is already on him – confidence.

5008007.title: Encouragement
strings: Encouragement
Faraj is like a rapidly growing hound – wise and brave, longing for your praise.
Faraj expects your encouragement.
Praise his broad knowledge.
Praise his splendid appearance.
Praise his strong arms.
Faraj yearns for your affirmation.
You can choose to praise his various merits.
Faraj yearns for your affirmation – yours.
The three of you enjoy drinks and lively conversation, laughing and talking as the moonlit night unfolds.
You often inspire me.
I am only meant to stand by your side, blade in hand.
You communicate with actions, not words, like men do through strength.

You talk and talk, and by the end, it's clear that Faraj has had a bit too much to drink. His moist eyes fix themselves on you. In the haze of drunkenness and the illusions it brings, he feels for the first time that he is one of you – perhaps one of you and Maggie – the kind of person he once admired and looked up to.

This is the highest praise one person can give to another.

You can see him smiling, trying hard to suppress it, making every effort to keep himself from becoming too ecstatic. Yet the gleam in his eyes betrays him.

"Your wisdom lights the candle of my intellect, [player.name]," he says, gazing at you with adoration, though a hint of other, hidden emotions lingers in his expression.

You praised him as a true and just courtier, someone whose future is undoubtedly brighter than your own. He seemed shy and bashful, but you’re certain he allowed himself, for just a moment, to imagine you serving as his follower… Well, perhaps there were other thoughts too – who's to say?
He seizes the opportunity and throws you over his shoulder, slamming you to the ground – oil and sweat glisten on your bodies, like a symbol of pure brotherly camaraderie.

5008008.title: Desire and Happiness
strings: Desire and Happiness
Faraj eagerly awaits your sharing of information with him...
Invite Faraj for a forbidden sharing.
Such a bold attempt is sure to break a Carnality Card.
You can't leave it to others. You have to do it yourself.
Invite your wife for a forbidden sharing.
The tier of the Sultan Card cannot exceed Faraj's.
If your wife is somewhat unwilling, had better not to force her.
You missed the appointment, but he also seemed relieved... it was never mentioned again.
Having me join in this foolishness is one thing, but breaking a Sultan Card? It wouldn't look good if word got around..
The Awakening of Happiness
Forms of Desire
Entangled Dreams
Lost Desires

You and Maggie walk into his room hand in hand with the moonlight. His nervousness makes him rigid like a statue, but you can see his waist and legs trembling crazily.
So, you step forward to comfort him, soothing his back, trying to steady his breathing. Meanwhile, Maggie takes off her clothes, slightly shy but her eyes full of affection for this young man – not expressing desire, but rather appreciation, both physical and spiritual... Faraj has earned it all through his support and selfless help.
This emotion, along with Maggie's beautiful body, is projected into Faraj's eyes. At the moment he receives it all, he relaxes – you've seen all his expressions, joy, shyness, sadness, anger, longing... but for the first time, you see happiness in his eyes.
He stands up, kisses you like a true mature man, also kisses Maggie, then contentedly bows, opens the door, andleaves leisurely, leaving behind just you two and the bright moonlight.

The next day, he tells the Sultan the story with you in the Lapis Lazuli hall, and you see him talking with more ease than you, describing to the Sultan his spiritual awakening journey: "There was a time I felt unworthy, but now, I can calmly enjoy all the happiness, it should be considered a great act of carnality."
The Sultan frowns... but as Faraj speaks, the Carnality Card in his hand silently breaks itself. The female magician bursts into laughter, praising everyone's wisdom, of course, including the Sultan's – thus, this matter is recorded in the court for future philosophers and theologians to endlessly debate.

You and Maggie, hand in hand, walk into his room with the moonlight. His nervousness turns him almost to a statue, but you can see his waist and legs trembling furiously.
So, you step forward to comfort him, soothing his spine, trying to calm his breath. Maggie removes her clothes, slightly shy, but her gaze filled with affection for this young man – It's not desire, but approval, both physical and mental... Through support and selfless help to you, Faraj earns it all.
These emotions, together with Maggie's beautiful body, reflect in Faraj's eyes. At the moment of gaining all this, he relaxes – you've seen his various expressions: joy, shyness, sadness, anger, yearning... But for the first time, you see happiness in his eyes.
He stands up, kisses you with the stature of a man most matured, that kiss also towards Maggie, before saluting contentedly, leaving you and your spouse with the shimmering moonlight. 
The next day, he appeared at your door again, more at ease, more amicable. From then on, there was no more barrier between you.

Though Faraj is a very loyal and valuable friend, he is your friend, not Maggie's. She has yet to thoroughly interact with him.
Upon hearing you're going to such lengths to break the Carnality Card... she showed deep hesitation, disgust even.
"So, are you planning to give your wife to someone else today, and then share it in the court tomorrow?"
You couldn't answer, just comforted her, saying there was no other choice, and that Faraj was an excellent young man – as she would see once she interacted with him more intimately.
Maggie resigned herself like a deflated balloon, showing surprising enthusiasm and compliance... After frenetically changing body position, the three of you entangle in gasping exhaustion...
Then, Maggie took out tobacco and a drink, and everyone happily shared everything, just as naturally as sharing each other's bodies.
Soon after, you fell into a deep dream, in the realm between reality and illusion, feeling different bodies continue to entangle deeper and you drift into the abyss.

Though you promised Faraj, you dared not say the same to Maggie. After much persuasion, Maggie reluctantly agreed to this absurd requirement—if the Carnality Card let you get close to other women, her playing with another man wouldn't matter, would it?
For a mature lady like Maggie, Faraj was quite a handsome and endearing companion. So Maggie wasn't as resistant as you imagined in bed... It was Faraj who seemed downcast afterward, his dismay most apparent. Hey! Fellow! I shared my wife with you! Stay positive!
Afterward, it seemed like the three of you had forgotten it altogether, and no one brought it up again.

5008009.title: Betrayal
strings: Betrayal
Faraj has been very suspicious recently... He's not doing his job well and has been secretly following you. You noticed the malicious intent in his eyes.
Faraj intends to deal a deadly blow to you.
You have to be careful
There are things that can help you get through a crisis.
As come risk, so come reward. Perhaps you can take this chance to break a Sultan Card?
This is a personal matter between you and Faraj.
His blade comes unsheathed silently, but you hear his breath and heartbeat thunderously roar.
The number of dice provided by your Physique and Combat is affected by the enemy's Physique and Combat.
You need at least 2 Successes to win.

Perhaps this is a release of sorts He plunges the dagger into your back; your blood and his tears flow together. Your consciousness blurs, and you hear him cursing your betrayal – a betrayal of ideals, a betrayal of his expectations... It seems you also hear him speak of a betrayal of love, maybe it’s just an illusion before death.
He used the move you taught him.
This isn't practice.
Let's consider this practice.

And of course, you know the flaw in this move... Block, sidestep, swing your fist – you shatter his throat, a fatal blow.

The next day, the Sultan curiously inquires about every detail of the betrayal. Perhaps, in having a dagger on your back, you two can sympathize with each other.

And of course, you know the flaw in this move... Block, sidestep, kick – he falls heavily to the ground due to his own strength, the weapon slipping from his hand. You take a look at the Carnality Card in your hand, it’s time to teach him some new moves...

The next day, you and Faraj recount the scene of breaking the card to the Sultan. He stands silently in the center of the hall, lost in spirit, his body covered with the marks of your abuse – like a beautiful bird with broken wings exhibited for viewing.

He used the move you taught him – faster and more perfect than you could achieve. The dagger thrust into your backheart, blood, and tears spewing out.

Your vision blurs, as you hear him curse your betrayal – betrayal of ideals, betrayal of admiration... And perhaps you heard him speak of love's betrayal, or maybe it was just a dying illusion.

He used the move you taught him, and of course, you know how to counter it. He falls like a clown to the ground – you become genuinely angry.
Sighing, you pick up the dagger, playfully looking at the blood and tears all over Faraj... The two of you stared at each other for about a tenth of an hour, before that stalemate was shattered by your laugh. You pulled him up, pointed out the flaws in his moves as if this was but another training session, and called Maggie to help stop his bleeding.
Thus the matter was settled, and none of you mentioned it again.

5008010.title: Youth’s Curtain
strings: Youth’s Curtain

Under your roof, Faraj is humble as a servant. But in the Upper City's most luxurious, radical parties, he is the eagle chasing the storm, every word and gesture attracting attention and admiration... Unfortunately, such socializing might be too extravagant for the young, maybe you should provide him with some reasonable support.
Faraj
Radical crowd
You must participate yourself to break the Sultan Card.
You can place Gold Coins or Convictions, up to 15 Gold Coins.
You can take this to break a Bloodshed Card of Rock tier or lower
You can use the Sultan Card at the party but will also bear the corresponding consequences.
To break the Sultan Card, you must place both yourself and the Bloodshed Card at the same time.
You heard one day, when he needed to buy everyone a drink, he didn't have enough coins – a disappointing night for any young person.
Great, you want to join us?
Thank you for your generosity!
You must put yourself into it to break this Sultan Card.
The state is ruined by your parents.
Everyone adores heroes, ideals, but ultimately adores vanity.
While they were talking about swords and jade...
He is still embarrassed about money.
You gave him enough gold coins to make new friends.
You arranged for a servant to settle his bill.

Looking at these ignorant youths with their high-sounding talks, you can’t help but feel annoyed. You are running around trying not to get executed by the Sultan, while they drink the finest wine, flirt with the prettiest girls, and discuss reforms and policies for which they never have to pay... So, you give them a lesson about the Sultan, about politics.
You talk about the history of the Sultanate, the basic political and economic structure, and the noble class – that is, the behind-the-scenes division of their family’s interests, those dirty businesses supporting this velvet room... You write with blood all over a whole wall, and until the victim completely breathes his last, no student dares to leave the class.
Later, the Sultan personally comes to view this wall and orders that the host of the party preserve it forever with varnish and gold powder.
From that day on, Faraj seems lost in spirit... but he still habitually returns to your home.

At the party, you voiced words of treason – not out of agitation, but rationality, solid as a sledgehammer and stone sculpture, which easily shatters the flashy yet fragile minds of the noble youth. It's time to reshape them.
These gold coins are enough to cover his daily expenses, but that's about it – Faraj holds them, looking more anxious than holding a bowl of fire, but seeing this was worth it.
"Consider it for me", you comforted him... and he did fairly well.
Faraj happily told you he has made many new friends who spend time listening to him, and he conveys much of... your ideas. These concepts enlightened the spiritually empty noble youths.

strings: Dangerous Gathering

Among the young nobles, a concept circulates that you can challenge the Sultan in a game. This idea deeply attract radical youths, and Faraj is seen as your spokesperson... Perhaps this thought is worth investing in, worth utilizing? Or perhaps Faraj needs some assistance?

Radical Noble

Faraj was spotted wearing a worn silk shirt to a party, which led to him being mocked as your servant – he proudly declared it an honor, but no matter, it indeed hurt a young person's pride.
Great, you want to join us?
Thank you for your generosity!
You must put yourself into it to break this Sultan Card.
The state is ruined by your parents.
He returned home with red eyes.
You silently joined their card game.
You instructed him to procure a splendid outfit.
You bribe the hall's servant for him
You secretly invested in this tavern

Looking at these ignorant youths with their high-sounding talks, you can’t help but feel annoyed. You are running around trying not to get executed by the Sultan, while they drink the finest wine, flirt with the prettiest girls, and discuss reforms and policies for which they never have to pay... So, you give them a lesson about the Sultan, about politics.
You talk about the history of the Sultanate, the basic political and economic structure, and the noble class – that is, the behind-the-scenes division of their family’s interests, those dirty businesses supporting this velvet room... You write with blood all over a whole wall, and until the victim completely breathes his last, no student dares to leave the class.
Later, the Sultan personally comes to view this wall and orders that the host of the party preserve it forever with varnish and gold powder.
From that day on, Faraj seems lost in spirit... but he still habitually returns to your home.

Faraj won repeatedly with you that night, and people began whispering about your luck and courage... Someone bravely asked, "Would you dare to beat the Sultan too?"
Faraj glared at him, while you responded with a smile, causing the crowd to cheer.
At first, he refuses, but you remind him, it's representing you – he then cheerfully dresses himself up.
The topic of the party is dangerous enough... These young people are still not mindful of safety measures, but you are experienced in this.

The lady hosting the party is a noble and wealthy widow who doesn’t need your Gold Coins, but she respects you – or fears you, whichever is fine – but is Faraj too? It depends on how you view this issue.

You don't know if Faraj is truly as foolish as they are or if he fully understands the role you want him to play. But it doesn't matter; these people are now yours.

You let Faraj cut his own arm open, mixing his blood into the wine of the gathering – a fine wine only the wealthiest nobles can afford.
His loyal blood makes the wine extraordinarily red and tempting, filling golden goblets, which are drained by each attendee, pledge-drinking like brothers and sisters...
They believe they are swearing an oath to revolution and ideals, but in fact, they are pledging allegiance to the God of Darkness – and to you.

It costs 10 Gold Coins.
You can send someone or go personally to purchase the title
You've heard he intends to leave the city
Maybe there is something that can help you persuade them.

You succeeded
You failed

Without much effort, you find out that a minor noble can't bear the Sultan's madness and wants to just leave. Hearing your purpose, he, who has already gathered enough travel expenses, is rather indifferent.

You tell him that living an ideal life isn't as easy as leaving the capital. The title bestowed by the Sultan might not be useful in a foreign land, but the heavy gold is sure to help him find his footing.
The noble is persuaded by you, and on that same day, he and you handle the paperwork together, and like that, you successfully exchange the title with this one from Jawad for Qais's title.
The noble refuses to give up his surname and title, which, for a traditional noble, is even worse than vying for his life. It seems you'll have to wait for another opportunity.

5008014.title: Glorious Return
strings: Glorious Return
You've obtained the hereditary title of the Qais family, now it's time to return it to its rightful owner.
You invited Qais out
Things to give to Qais
This is...

At first, Qais doesn't know why you call him over until you present the title certificate. He almost can't believe the seal on it, opens his mouth, but doesn't know what to say.

Look at his flustered appearance! You laugh heartily, pat him on the shoulder and tell him, it’s his – now he can tell his mother that their family is once again hereditary nobility, their next generation will no longer live bereft of their forefathers' name!

Qais is extremely moved. In his eyes, filled with complex emotions, it seems he has never been treated so kindly, as if no one has ever helped him so unconditionally.
He has no friends in the court, those people once linked arms with him when the Qais family was at its peak, also kicked him mercilessly when he needed help. Qais doesn’t need such filthy and hypocritical friendship. But you are different, you are so upright, kind, and tolerant... You are the model courtier in his heart, and he has utilized your influence, your kindness... A sense of shame arises in his heart, then he solemnly looks at you, holding the thin parchment recording the hereditary status, pledging a promise that will be passed down in eternity: "I swear by the ancient honor of the Qais, as long as this surname exists; one day, you and I, your family and my family, will be friends eternal."

5008015.title: Purchase Title
strings: Purchase Title
The hereditary noble title of the Qais family has once again been lost due to the death of the noble who bought it, now anyone has the opportunity to get it.
You must provide 10 Gold Coins
You can personally go, or send any follower to buy it

Qais uses your money to buy this thin document. He lowers his head, hands it to you, slightly purses lips, saying nothing, only his eyes flicker slightly, revealing a bit of inner struggle.

He seems unaware that you bought it for him, you think for a moment, deciding not to tell him on the spot. Let's call it a small prank for when he once gave you just three Gold Coins and said "we're even," you'll wait for the right moment to give it to him.
Cash on delivery; even the title of a noble is just a commodity here, only more expensive.

5008016.title: Final Farewell
strings: Final Farewell
This day, Qais comes to you, seemingly with something to say.
Qais has something to say to you

This day you talk about many things. Qais tells you, his mother eventually passed away. After finishing his mother's funeral, he thinks repeatedly and finally comes to bid farewell to you.

"Perhaps, I should search for something truly meaningful... I should think clearly about what I truly live for... And clearly, the answer doesn't lie within this city." Before leaving, he gives you an Ancient Ring, thanking you for your care and help during this time – it might be the only treasure left in that impoverished home.

5008017.title: The Right Price
strings: The Right Price
You bid for all the family assets Qais sold, at ten Gold Coins – the same price it took to redeem his hereditary title.
You must provide 10 Gold Coins
You bought those things

Soon, the servants move the junk you bought back to your storeroom. You specifically instruct them to be careful not to damage anything. Though they were no valuables, they were still precious to Qais nonetheless...

5008018.title: No Second Chances
strings: No Second Chances
Qais is about to leave.
Qais

Qais couldn't gather the money. His family's glorious title fell into someone else's hands. It's said that his mother couldn't accept such a blow and soon passed away, leaving him deeply despondent...

After her funeral, he comes to your door to say goodbye. “Maybe, I should find something truly meaningful... long I have wondered the answer to my own life... now I know the answer is not in this city.” He gives you a ring, thanking you for your care and help during this time.

5008019.title: Glorious Return
strings: Glorious Return
Qais will reclaim his glory.
Qais
Noble's Hereditary Title

Although he sold everything from his home, Qais manages to reclaim his title, now he can tell his mother that their family is once again hereditary nobility, and that their next generation will no longer live bereft of their forefathers' name!

Before leaving, he suddenly grabs your hand and whispers close to your ear, "I will repay you. By then, will you return that ring to me? It's my mother's... You can keep everything else."

Without waiting for your response, he strides directly out, seeming too embarrassed to hear what you would say.
How does he recognize it is you? Maybe it’s because of the perfectly bid price you offered, or maybe because everyone in the Dark Alley knows you...

5008020.title: Eternal Legacy
strings: Eternal Legacy
Qais has gathered enough money. Now, he hopes to redeem his mother's ancestral engagement ring.
Qais family heirloom, an Ancient Ring
Qais

You did not give Qais a chance to redeem his family belongings. Qais was a bit disappointed, but he still smiled at you, “Well, maybe those things will serve some use with you rather than rotting in my family's warehouse.”
Thank you!

Without hesitation, you agree, allowing him to exhale a sigh of relief. You take him to your storeroom, where the old dressing table has been cleaned and repaired by the carpenter you hired, polished with sandpaper and wood wax, covered with varnish, renewed yet maintaining its old charm; the portrait also painstakingly restored, removing dull dust and old stains, the woman in the painting smiling softly, her features somewhat resembling Qais, and there’s the ring, now collected in a velvet-lined ornamental box...

"Take it, these are your things," you tell him.

Qais is too moved to speak. In his eyes, filled with complex emotions, it seems he has never been treated so kindly, as if no one has ever treated him with such thoughtfulness and kindness without expecting anything in return.

He has no friends in the court; those who were back-slapping when Qais's family was at its peak were the same ones ruthlessly stabbing him in the back when help was needed. Qais doesn't need such dirty and hypocritical friendships. But you are different; you are so upright, kind, and tolerant... As he gently touches these ancient yet new, familiar yet strange objects, a sharp pang fills his chest, and he solemnly looks at you, making an eternal promise: "I swear by the ancient honor of Qais, as long as this name endures, you and I, my family and your family, will be friends forever.

You ultimately did not have the resolve to carry out that cruel harvest ritual, yet the diagram for the ritual still turned to dust.

As you complete the ritual steps taught by Qais, at that moment, Qais' blood is drained. His eyes, gazing at the sky, lose their luster, turning into a black stone. You feel a warm breeze linger around you, then, with no reluctance, it drifts far away.

At the moment you completed this ritual as taught by Qais, his blood ran dry as well. Gazing towarded the sky, his eyes quickly faded, turning into a glossy black stone.

To break the Sultan Card, you omit many details while reporting the bloodshed to the court. The Sultan contemplates for a moment before recalling who this annoying subject was, then loses interest swiftly. He will never know Qais’s eyes before death – that hidden piety and fanaticism – even though it was conveyed through your to the Lord of Darkness, you still cherish them.

His mind flashed with confusion but soon vanished under the influence of the ritual. Suddenly, in his eyes, you became so charismatic, irresistible. As for the overwhelming guilt about your wife, it dissipated with your actions.
Everything ended in disarray; you didn’t feel any special change upon the ritual's completion. Qais weakly propped himself up, his voice hoarse: "I mentioned before, being watched by others is also a necessary condition for the ritual's success."
You finally came to your senses. Disappointment? Not necessarily. You looked towards Qais, into his eyes—this ritual may not have genuinely failed, that familiar longing shimmered in his eyes, although it quickly disappeared into the darkness.
When you publicly recounted the event, the Sultan took a moment to remember who Qais was. Then he looked at this minister, known for his stubbornness, integrity, and conservativeness, and appreciated his shamelessly calm expression, finally showing a meaningful smile. The Sultan permitted you to break the card.

People are reminded of the imperial days of glory – not only the glory of the land but also the glory that wasn’t so terrifying.

Some were injured, and some equipment was lost. But fortunately, none were fatal. You exhaled with relief as your army returned victorious!
You sent Qais to announce the success of this ritual in the streets. Crowds sang ancient songs to praise you, recalling the empire's golden days—the grandeur of its lands, alongside its milder touch.

Long-dead deceased return with slow steps, draped in gold and jewels, from distant lands!

Whispering fearfully, people finally burst into cheers when someone claimed it to be a symbol of ancestral protection, a harbinger of the old revival! You personally place the head of the high-valued Gladiator in Miss Arumina's hands, then used the blood on your fingers to add some rouge to her pale lips.
Jawad desperately presses her shoulder, urging her to kneel and beg for mercy, but you just praise Miss Arumina's earrings for matching her makeup and laugh off the matter.
You didn't even die in the Sultan's Game; you were merely beaten as a lecherous fool for teasing a girl. Was it worth it?
Every follower serving you holds a degree of resolve, ready to sacrifice their life for the Sultan's Game. But to be killed for teasing a girl? This is a severe blow to your authority...

You circle the pillar, dodging while hurling venomous words to distract the gladiator. Finally, you seize the moment when his guard drops and plunge your blade into his heart.

The gladiator falls.

No one cheers, except for the Sultan, whose laughter echoes through the court.

“What an interesting fight! It's the reward he deserves,” the Sultan chuckles. “Well, clean up the floor.”

You coat your weapon with poison. A small, shallow cut is all it takes. Then comes the wait for victory.
The gladiator falls.
No one cheers, except for the Sultan, whose laughter echoes through the court.
"He loved fighting so much, yet he couldn't even die like a warrior. What a perfect punishment," the Sultan says, clapping for you with a smile. Only then do the courtiers follow with weak applause, more like sighs of sorrow than celebration.

5008046.title: Again?
strings: Again?

Miss Arumina comes to find you.

She must have had a huge argument with her father, her face still carries anger. "I don't need my father to tell me which man I can or can't associate with!" she shouts at you, "I understand everything myself! Please don't get involved again; every time my father mentions something annoying, it's you!"

After dropping this heap of meaningless threats, she glares at you fiercely, as if waiting for a reply.
You carefully examine this pampered young lady, suddenly realizing that for her, her father's protection is her entire world, so a man like you whom even her father fears and avoids intrigues her... That's why she will take such a blatant risk to come, experiencing real storms in life, to her, danger just seems fun!
Arumina
Ask your wife to talk to her
You don't have time to lecture her, so you dismiss her.
Teach her how dangerous men truly are.
You need to handle this yourself, or send a follower to do it.
Good girl, don't be angry. Come home with me.
Troubled Father
No Time to Teach Her
Let the Wife Teach Her
Teach her how dangerous men can be

Jawad, evidently, has a different interpretation of your casual arrangements: He believes you are demonstrating to him as her Father, "Look, I can play with your daughter any time; for now, I'll generously return her to you!"

After he painstakingly persuades Arumina to leave, he humbly tries to befriend you for a long time, even leaving some Gold Coins as a friendly gesture.

You lead her to the outer courtyard, then lock the wooden door of the inner chamber.
She threw a fit, calling you a coward, completely unaware of the fate she narrowly avoids.

You sighed and ignored her noise until she sheepishly left.

Maggie whisked her away like a ragdoll, their voices disappearing down the corridor—especially Miss Arumina's screams.
Whatever Maggie did, the girl left well-fed, her hair adorned with flowers, her pockets full of books and trinkets Maggie had given her, subdued like a real doll.
The next day, her Father sent some recompense—with the only thing he knows, shiny Gold Coins.

Like a servant, you politely and humbly lead her to a guest room, then shout her alone inside... “I'll come find you, dear young lady, when there's a Carnality Card.”

Questions and anger seems lodged in her throat... In the suddenly quiet room, she helplessly leans against the window of the door, her body slumping, nails scraping the wood, her face once again turning deathly pale – that broken and fearful look makes you feel a pang of regret, but her bit-lip, so red and moist, seems to entice you, saying she came for something like this.

5008047.title: Feast
strings: Feast

Miss Arumina hosts a banquet for young nobles. You are her family's benefactor and a famous figure in court – young people are eager to see you, learn your manners, demeanor, and even lifestyle... It is best to prepare carefully and bring appropriate companions.
Arumina
You must go there yourself
Choose a female companion... Actually, a male would do too!
Bring along a servant
Choose a passionate partner or wife, you can break a Carnality Card of Silver tier or lower
You must choose a companion with Passion to break the Sultan Card.
An Example of Happiness
An Example of Passion
Super Boring Adult
An Example of Flirtation
An Example of Desire
Boring Adult

When you and your wife enter, whispers fill the banquet.
Young ladies glance enviously at your wife, married to a powerful man for many years, whose relationship appears very blissful – even attend such an event together – and she is strikingly beautiful, elegant, and noble.

Many young girls come to toast her, even kneeling before her, asking her to dip her finger into the wine and anoint their foreheads, a custom where married women do so to bless unmarried girls, praying they find similarly happy marriages.

Though she tries hard to conceal her pride and satisfaction, you can tell your wife is very happy.

When you and Maggie enter, there is much whispering at the banquet.
Young girls enviously look at her; she's been married to a powerful man for many years, and they seem to have a very good relationship – which is why they attend these occasions together – and she's so beautiful, graceful, and noble. 
Young men and women gather around, offering toasts... Soon they notice something is amiss, and under the influence of alcohol, you and Maggie unceremoniously reveal your elaborately adorned naked bodies beneath thin, luxurious robes... and those delightful portable toys that have brought you so much joy. The secret of happiness is keeping passion alive... 
Your words, images, and bold actions becomes the talk of the Court.

The easiest way to ruin a youthful banquet is to let a father join in. Jawad is overjoyed because Arumina normally wouldn't introduce these friends to him! He is busy giving small gifts to every girl, while verbally threatening any young man who seems too close to his daughter. 

All the young people are disappointed to find that the legendary dashing minister is just like Arumina's money-hoarding father. This world is hopeless.

You attend the banquet with [s3.name] as your lover. They are both surprised and curious, surrounding you with questions about love, marriage, and intimacy.
Few are so open about such private matters, but at least your honesty wins the trust of some.

You bring [s3.name] to the banquet as your lover. They are surprised and curious, asking about love, marriage, and intimacy... and you boldly reveal [s3.name]'s attire, showcasing exquisite jewelry and ornate toys that can bring continuous pleasure. 
This wanton scene frightens many young girls, but also becomes part of your legendary tale.

You and [s3.name] go to the banquet and merely stuff yourselves with food and drink – leaving the young men and women deeply disappointed. After all, the minister – rumored to play power games with the Sultan – turns out to be nothing more than an ordinary middle-aged man who chews noisily at the table....
You didn't bring servants
Brought Inal
Zephyr's Misstep
Hustle and Bustle

In others' imaginations, you might be commanding the court while seated on a slave – but their imaginations are not fulfilled.
In reality, power is nothing but imagination, something you should pay some attention to.

When leaving, Inal tells you Arumina gives her a gold bracelet – each of her maids has one. You think for a moment and allows Inal to keep the adornment.

Maybe with more worldly experience and becominghigher tier; he will be less incompetent. But because of this incident, you attended the banquet without any servants and were laughed at behind your back.

You were late because Zephyr insisted on taking a bath, then getting a shave and face cleanup, something unfamiliar since he’d never paid for such services before, which, when a razor was presented, led to a slip and a cut lip, requiring extra time to bandage it...

When you appeared at the banquet with him covering his wound, people glanced curiously, wondering why bring a slave?

Only one person, a maiden, blushed intensely.
You found an excuse to leave halfway through the banquet, but Zephyr stayed, saying it was a rare chance for him to visit a noble event. His face blushed a deep red, clutching flowers he'd plucked from the garden.
You left, silently wishing him luck in your heart.

He is very grateful to you, his demeanor humble, in stark contrast to his overbearing wife. Fardak needs to be received.
You ignored Fardak who came to visit, so he left alone.

You mention a steep path known only to mountain lions and gazelles. You remind the royal hostage that his escape depends not on a path, but on whether the Sultan still cares about him. Yet, he sees hope in your words. The royal hostage decides to make a request to the Sultan at the next court session.
You warn the cartographer to watch her words, as the Sultan's spies are everywhere... The royal hostage is very disappointed, but he knows you might be right.

5008056.title: The Promised Moment
strings: The Promised Moment

The Sultan ruthlessly rejected Fardak's request. Now everyone knows he can never return to his hometown.

Heartbroken, Fardak instinctively shows up at your door once more.
Fardak
You choose to embrace him, persuading acceptance of this cruel fate.
You choose to tell him that you can help him escape...
You choose to tell him he should act like a mouse...
Different choices will lead to different plots and Events.
You must receive Fardak yourself.
What should I do?
Embrace this cruel destiny, I can teach you the secret to happiness...
If you really want to leave, I can help you.
You must wait like a mouse...
Bittersweet Respite
I can help you escape
You need to act like a mouse...

At this point, what more can be done but to accept this cruel fate? You sit opposite each other, not speaking a word.

In his eyes, you see a familiar weariness and despair; perhaps he sees the same in yours. You are like two small boats facing the same storm at sea... He moves closer to you, or perhaps you to him; it no longer matters. You embrace each other.
This is no simple matter – you're not one to joke about such things. Fardak looks at you in surprise, waiting for you to continue.

You soothe the anxious and sorrowful young man, telling him that the steep path known to the lions and gazelles is unknown to the Sultan, and it is his only way out. But he cannot simply sneak away... He must hide like a mouse in the shadows of the Sultan's palace, then escape swiftly when the Sultan is unaware.

Fardak sighs deeply, clenches his fists, and says, "Of course, I can wait...! No need to rush."

He promises not to do anything drastic or impulsive. Before leaving, he places a sharp dagger in your hand.

"...At first...I was going to use it to end myself. Now I'd rather give it to you – whenever I see it, those thoughts just... they come right back."

You soothe the anxious and sorrowful young man, telling him that the only thing he can do is to hide like a mouse in the shadows of the Sultan's palace, then escape swiftly when the Sultan is unaware.

Unfortunately... you recall that narrow path again. It might have been a possible escape for Fardak if it had remained unknown to the Sultan. But it's all too late now.

5008057.title: The Same Storm
strings: The Same Storm
The shadow of the same storm looms over you, drawing you inexplicably closer to each other, seeking solace...
Fardak
You must personally...
You can take this opportunity to break a Carnality Card
Indecisive, you both returned home. The matter was concluded there.
A hug is not enough
Only joy can resist pain and despair
Let's forget about tomorrow
You show him a Carnality Card

Fardak's pale fingers clasp your garment tightly, trembling slightly.

He has always turned to you for solace without even realizing it... When did this become his refuge? Is it a habit? Since when?

Is it because he once laid his vulnerabilities bare before you, freeing him to confront his deepest heart and desires now? Or is it because you are a player of the Sultan Card, or simply... because you are special to him?

He lowers his eyes, asking for a kiss, and then, for more.

What happened that night is never mentioned again. But you both know, in the storm, you are not alone.

If cruel fate is inevitable, why not find joy amid misery?

You persuade Fardak, pushing him down onto the rough carpet.

The memory of that public humiliation resurfaces in his mind, and he struggles, sensing how different this moment is from the last time: there is no Sultan's gaze, no Sultan's intimidation... but, is it really different?

A tear forms on his trembling eyelashes; Fardak closes his despairing eyes, not looking at you, not resisting, simply clutching your garment tightly as he yields to your passionate advance.

You are sure of this truth. A moment of joy can help one temporarily forget the lingering despair. To accept it, to surrender to it, is all he can do.

You take him to your secret cellar. You have spent countless sleepless nights here; in that mesmerizing intoxication, where you can finally stop thinking about tomorrow. As if time exists only in this moment, as if the world contains no one but the two of you.

You clink your glasses, creating a loud sound. Like two wounded beasts who have wandered the dangerous wilderness separately, only to find each other by chance, you begin to tend to one another's pain. Together, you set aside thoughts of the Sultan, the Sultan Card, that cruel game, and that cold destiny. You pat the jug gently while he sings the songs of his homeland. You laugh heartily until tears stream from your eyes. Eventually, you both fall asleep drunk in this sheltered place. In this tiny respite from reality, you steal what little courage you can to face the uncertain tomorrow that awaits beyond these walls – even if it might ultimately lead to death.

He examines the card, feeling the cold seep from his fingertips into the depths of his soul.

"So this is what's been trapping you all this time?" A faint smile appears on his pale face. And then, he leans in to kiss you, gently guiding you back into the soft pillows and draping curtains.

In this luxurious yet impossibly cold mansion, in this world, the warmth of an embrace feels so fragile, so ephemeral. But what else can you ask from each other?

When morning light spills into the room, he sightly breaks the card for you: "I'm trapped now, [player.name], but you – are you one step closer to your freedom?"
You take the opportunity to break a carnality card

Fardak stands again in the center of the Lapis Lazuli Palace, head bowed, lips pressed tight, knees and elbows raw and red. Seeing this, the Sultan laughs heartily, allowing you to break this card.

This is exactly what he expected to see.

5008058.title: Let Me Be Your Shield
strings: Let Me Be Your Shield
You pledged to help Fardak leave here, but it won't be easy.
Fardak
You must mobilize a troop to escort Fardak out. Or do you have another plan?
After encouraging Fardak to escape, it seemed he was waiting for your next move, but you ignored him, and the matter was left behind.
I can escort you away
You can leave during the chaos

You tell Fardak you have a secret troop that can escort him discreetly onto the hazardous pathway to home. You can prepare enough food, water, and servants for him, allowing him to decide his future after returning home.

Fardak remains silent, contemplating, and finally looks at you, shaking his head: "No, I cannot leave."

"You've treated me so well; I cannot bring disaster to you, nor leave you to face the Sultan's fury alone... No matter how much I desire freedom, I won't sacrifice you for it." His eyes glow with unprecedented resolve. He chooses to stay.

You tell Fardak that you have resolved to rebel against the Sultan. When you launch your attack on that magnificent yet cruel throne, he can escape the city during the chaos and never return.

Fardak is stunned. He asks many, many questions, finally confirming you are not joking. He remains silent, contemplating, and finally looks at you, seriously shaking his head: "I will not leave."

"If I abandon you at this critical moment, I would despise myself for the rest of my life. Let me do something for you!" His eyes glow with unprecedented resolve. He chooses to stay.

5008059.title: An Escape Like a Mouse
strings: An Escape Like a Mouse

It is time. Your spies surrounding the Sultan report that he is in high spirits while hunting at his southern palace, without a trace of suspicion. Lately, Fardak has kept a low profile, and the Sultan has nearly forgotten about him. Now you only need to create a convincing story of his death, allowing him to escape secretly while still very much alive.
Pathway Home
Fardak
The escape will cost 10 Gold Coins, requiring your support.
A blindfold to cover Fardak's escape
Anything you find useful
Influence checks will be required in certain situations
Some items or hostages previously gifted to you might serve as distractions covering his escape.
The guards look at each other, uncertain whether to trust your explanation...
Your Influence determine your full dice count.
You need at least 3 Successes to win.
You didn't help Fardak escape, and gradually, he stopped communicating with you. Later, it was said Fardak died while on the run, but no one ever found his remains.
An Overthrow
A Carnival
A Closure

Arriving at Fardak's burning residence, the Sultan's guards found only a charred corpse, identifying him solely by the fragments of fabric and jewelry that remained.

Still shaken, you tell them Fardak had mentioned unrest in his hometown a few days ago. At the time, you didn't take it seriously. But how could anyone have imagined a traitor would infiltrate the capital so quickly, conspire to kill him, and even dare to set fire in public to destroy evidence!

You call [s4.name] and a group of Ladies of Delights, giving them enough money to entertain Fardak well, hoping he might forget his damned homesickness.

The following morning, the Sultan receives a peculiar report. According to it, Fardak suddenly "choked" during a carnival, then "shivered" before quickly passing away. The report also mentions that several prostitutes had witnessed him experiencing similar episodes before, suggesting some chronic condition.

The Sultan shows more interest in which prostitutes are involved than in Fardak's death. He dismisses you with a wave, instructing you to write a condolence letter to Fardak's father, demanding he send another son to serve as hostage promptly.

Little does anyone know that the messenger delivering this letter is Fardak himself, now under a new identity.

Fardak has taken his own life – or at least, that's what the person who found his body claims. According to him, Fardak slit his throat with a family heirloom dagger. It's said that this proud and solitary family uses this blade to protect something far more precious than their lives.

The Sultan furrows his brows, but the man quickly presents the Kaplan's End. The dagger is exquisite, instantly capturing the Sultan's attention. He examines it closely, gesturing with the blade for a moment, sending shivers through the women beside him and the trembling courtiers below.

"One less hostage, one more treasure. A fair trade." He smiles as he accepts the dagger, showing no interest in pursuing the matter further.

And so, that very night, a cloaked man bows to you repeatedly in gratitude before disappearing into the darkness on his way home.
You succeeded
You failed

Your display of heartfelt grief dispels most of the guards' suspicions. After some additional persuasion and a warning – that everyone will suffer if they disturb the Sultan's hunting pleasure – they accept your explanation and identify the body as that unfortunate hostage.

And so, Fardak seizes the opportunity to leave the city under a false identity, vanishing without a trace.

The guards do not trust your words; an experienced coroner discovers the corpse isn't actually Fardak through telltale details. After this revelation, they quickly launch a manhunt and find their target hiding at a remote farm.

As they report this to the Sultan, you stand below, drenched in sweat. Fortunately, your supporters defend you fiercely, and Fardak calmly states that you were not involved in his escape. He gazes directly at the man on the throne, and even as they take him away, he remains exceptionally calm and composed, as if he never held any hope from the start... just like that, he is ordered to be burned alive.

5008060.title: Matchmaker
strings: Matchmaker
Marriage can also bring happiness. With this in mind, you volunteered to help Fardak find a suitable wife and bring them together...
You can introduce a marriage partner that you consider suitable for Fardak
You pondered without finding a suitable person, and Fardak tacitly did not remind you of it. Implicitly, you sensed that he seemed more relaxed when facing you...
Lumera, what do you think of him?

How about Nayla?
How about Mahir?
How about Adila?
How about [s1.name]?

You call Lumera and tell her about Fardak, then ask about her opinion.

Lumera's clear eyes stare at you, without a hint of girlish shyness or hesitation: "If that's your wish, I'll marry him," she says, "but I'm just a beggar; how could I deserve a noble?"

Oh well, if Lumera agrees, then this is not a problem... You ponder that as long as your influence is high enough, persuading others that Lumera is your adopted daughter will naturally give her noble status.

As for Fardak, how dare he even be dissatisfied with Lumera?!
Before you finished speaking, Maggie slapped you.

She has a child, but undeniably, she's both beautiful and wealthy, coveted by many men.

However, upon hearing this, Fardak's face turns red, "How... how can this be? I've dined with the lady's son, sparred with him, hunted with him, this... this isn't appropriate."

You imagine that scene; it does seem a bit awkward...

Before you finish speaking, Fardak's face turns red. "But she... she's your wife!" he exclaims. Unable to continue, he hastily bids you farewell.

You think to yourself: this guy – if you don't mind, what's he so concerned about?
"But she has a husband! Please, don't make fun of me anymore!" Fardak replies loudly, his face reddening, rejecting your suggestion and leaving without finishing his tea.

Nayla's beauty is undeniable. With a face like that, who cares about anything else, right...?

Fardak jumps back like he's been stung, frantically waving his hands and spouting a string of lofty excuses – things like how he's not worthy of her or how such a delicate flower would only suffer if she were with him. But finally, after you press him hard enough, he cracks. He confesses, utterly defeated, that he can't handle the way this fine lady carries herself. "In the market, you can't even walk five minutes without bumping into ten guys who've slept with her! Ten guys – not ten times, ten different guys!"

Fardak is still hesitating, so you drag him along to see Mahir.

You explain your intentions extensively, and Mahir keeps her eyes fixed on the strange liquid-filled flask in her hand, responding quickly: "If he can beat me in a prime number challenge, it's fine."

"What's a prime number?" Fardak asks, looking confused.

Mahir shrugs, not bothering to explain. It seems this marriage won't work.

Fardak racks his brain, then cautiously asks: "You mean the woman who crushed that stone statue at the bathhouse? With just one hand?"

You scratch your head, falling into silence. Your survival instinct tells you it's better not to bring up this incident with Adila...
Whether it's appearance, identity, status, wealth, or character... in general, this person is not very suitable.

5008061.title: No Second Chances
strings: No Second Chances

Qais

5008062.title: First Sight
strings: First Sight
You resolved to organize a ceremony announcing to everyone that you have adopted Lumera as your daughter, purely because she is worth it.
You plan to invite Fardak to the ceremony so the two young people can meet
You are prepared to officially adopt Lumera as your foster daughter, not for breaking an Extravagance card, just because she deserves it

For a noble lady, not wearing jewelry is undignified
