The Sultan doesn't dislike religion - it often helps him rule the people - but he definitely dislikes religions that encourage subjects to throw away their lives, as that amounts to stealing from his tax coffers.
With your embellishments, he frowns but still doesn't speak. This is natural, after all - everyone knows these cultists are poor, so killing them all wouldn't cost much profit. So you grit your teeth...

What novel entertainment! The Sultan claps and laughs with interest. He commands his forces, and soon, before the summoning begins, all those cultists are captured. The Sultan personally forces the ritual's method from these terrified people.
However, since Badriyyah seems to have committed suicide - or supposedly dissolved in that black pool - the remaining cultists fail repeatedly to summon the legendary powerful, beautiful, wise creatures... No choice but to settle for these writhing chunks of rotten meat, and you can only proceed with tears in your eyes... The process defies recollection, but anyway, only you know you're the hero who saved this world, and heroes are always destined to be misunderstood... Sigh!

In the moment the card breaks, through the splattered stains, you glimpse a sublime vision - pure devotees kneeling before the true god. In ancient times, a god was judged evil and banished for unauthorized world-alteration - now, through game-created stains and your vision, Their name will be sanctified anew, returning once more.

You present a Bloodshed Card and outline your plan, finally arousing the Sultan's slight interest. He commands his forces, and soon, before the summoning begins, all those cultists are captured. You torture several to death, then force the ritual's method from the survivors.
Their leader - not Badriyyah, who reportedly dissolved in the black pool during the interrupted ritual - tremblingly summons several brutal but nearly mindless monsters. You and the Sultan sit safely, laughing as you watch these creatures tear the cultists apart and devour them. When the monsters are dragged back to their realm, you have the remaining survivors summon another...

In the moment the card breaks, through the corpse's gaping wound and spreading stains, you witness a sublime vision: a divine angel unfurling wings, heralding this world's master's birth. You convince yourself - no, you firmly believe: their death was necessary, sacred. Only through their blood could this stagnant world find change and liberation!

You present a Bloodshed Card with reverent persuasion, claiming that while the earthly realm bows entirely before the Sultan, darker underground territories... await conquest!
Your words spark the Sultan's interest. He mobilizes his forces, and soon all cultists are seized before their ritual begins. You execute several through torture, then extract the summoning method from survivors.
They tremblingly cooperate to open a portal, only to be kicked through by waiting soldiers... Malevolent vapors churn and swirl as screams echo from within. Unfortunately, just as the Sultan leans forward for a closer look, the otherworldly gateway snaps shut. He regards you with displeasure while you nervously wipe cold sweat, explaining this weakness must stem from Badriyyah's death - reportedly dissolved in that black pool during the interrupted ritual—leaving their portal too unstable... You repeatedly promise to arrange something more durable next time, and only then does he spare you.

As the card snaps, through the messy stains, you glimpse an exalted vision - a crown destined for the King of Kings, the world-ruling God. In ancient times, a god was judged evil and banished for unauthorized world-alteration - now, through game-created stains and your vision, Their name will be sanctified anew, returning once more.
Purist priests would never tolerate such blasphemy. Your intelligence fills them with zealous joy - they've long desired to stage a magnificent, costly crusade adorned in golden splendor.

When they storm this foul den, disrupt the evil ritual, and bind all cultists, you approach with a Carnality Card.
They exchange glances, then collectively withdraw, feigning blindness to what follows.
Yet many witnessed your debauchery through countless flickering candles in wall niches, through endless dark passages.

Everything becomes utterly sacred as this holy war's climax.
Through sweat and gasps, those shadowy watchers grow vivid, astonished, contemplating, disdaining, craving... This exemplifies what the Immaculate Purity most abhors - the purer one's abstinence, the more fiercely one judges others' desire.
Now, with this performance shocking, in this unjust game, you have atoned for God, absolving the sin of worldly lust.

When they storm this foul den, disrupt the evil ritual, and bind all cultists, you approach with a Bloodshed Card, demanding to personally behead them.
They exchange glances, then nod agreement. You chain these prisoners together, lead them to an open plaza where priests loudly proclaim their crimes - after each declaration, you execute one, continuing until sunset, until exhaustion prevents lifting your blade.

All slaughter becomes utterly sacred as this holy war's conclusion. The Sultan's Game witnessed this deed.
As the card broken, a matching wound opened across your throat. Blood flowed freely, painting your flesh. Priests rushed forward in alarm to heal you - but you felt no weakness or pain, casually wiping it clean before departing. You didn't realize this blood belonged to those you'd killed - in that moment, you'd embraced the sin of mass slaughter.

Your Conquest Card grants them absolute confidence - see how even priests grasp game mechanics!
Raiding the cultist stronghold, you march through streets shouting crusade slogans, rousing every citizen - through noble quarters, common districts, even the filthiest Dark Alley - ensuring all know this is war, sacred war! This absolutely merits a Conquest Card!
They don't merely strike cultists preparing divine summoning, but methodically comb every slum corner, dragging out anyone who participated in cultic rites or bears ritual scars. Naturally, some respectable "clients" who visited Badriyyah purely for attractive tattoos paid coins to prove Purist devotion - their peaceful lives remained undisturbed.
This massive purge slowly concluded after seven days, with countless souls whipped, judged, and executed.

Everything becomes utterly sacred - this holy war's inception, progress, and finale. The Sultan's Game witnessed this achievement.
As the card broken, a scar suddenly appeared on your chest... Bloodless, painless, even emanating waves of ecstasy - in this game, the sin of tearing reality is forgiven, even when committed by a god.

They fought desperately to prevent ritual disruption, but your power proved superior. Breaking into their cavern, you see Badriyyah's garments floating in that black pool, seething with endless malice, echoing infinite whispers... Overcoming revulsion, you destroy this altar, letting viscous liquid writhe and shriek across the ground before dissolving in sunlight...

This conquest stands unquestionably sacred, for you battle sin, evil, the divine enemy. The Sultan's Game witnessed this achievement.
As the card broken, a scar suddenly appeared on your chest... Bloodless, painless, even emanating waves of ecstasy - in this game, the sin of tearing reality is forgiven, even when committed by a god.
It undoubtedly deserves to be called a conquest, sacred and impeccable, for you fought against sin, evil, the enemy of The Immaculate Purity.

They fought desperately to prevent ritual disruption. By your third wave of kills, indescribable malice poured from the cavern, layered whispers filling everyone's ears. You watch cultists kneel tearfully, welcoming that deity's descent, this world's ending.

Before departing, an agonized scream pierces the air. [s5.name]'s flesh inexplicably erupts with blood blossoms, multiplying, intensifying... Badriyyah's tattoos writhe across [s5.gender(his,her)] skin, each pattern becoming wounds, claiming [s5.gender(his,her)] life.

Extreme unease grips all present - certainly victory, yet proving this creature wasn't the legendary omnipotent Cultic God. Will cultists cease activities, or grow more frenzied?

Cold needles bearing thick black herb essence pierce your skin like planted seeds, desperately rooting within your flesh, causing pain and maddening itch. You scratch frantically yet cannot remove them, dodge desperately yet cannot escape that pursuing needle...

Her visage has grown so alien. Did those black nipple stains always writhe so vividly? Does that navel pattern gradually expand? Cold hands embrace your shoulders from behind, restraining escape. Indescribable agony explodes through your soul - you nearly believe part of yourself has been devoured by dense darkness, as tribute, as sacrifice, never recoverable.
You struggle awake from this bizarre dream, finding barely fifteen minutes had passed. The palm stain grows ever darker, constantly stinging with unresolvable pain.

The summoned Cultic God savagely assaults your mind with endless suffering, piercing pain, despair, sorrow.
How predictable! You grit teeth in desperate resistance, fully grasping this deity's methods - They manipulate senses, rewrite skin-to-brain messages, making surroundings twisted yet real.
But that's all... just that! As long as you believe, remain unwavering, firmly commanding every nerve to obey your - not divine - will, you become an unyielding reef in the Cultic God's mental tide. They crash against you, flow around you, then overwhelm others.
Thus you hear Their unwilling shriek, feel Them burn a soul-deep scar, then silence. Badriyyah has fainted, surrounding cultists have fainted, so your departure meets no obstruction. Yet you know you'll never again be allies.

You barely feel your feet in the pool - cold breath coils around you, licking tattoo-covered skin, seeping toward blood, flesh, bone, every fiber. No, this ritual must cease. With final, desperate hope, you regard the woman holding you fast.

Living represents ultimate happiness - nothing surpasses possessing life.
You tell Badriyyah about Alim and his children struggling in Dark Alley. Though hungry and fearful, don't they share profound bonds? Don't those children laugh and play together? Even cultists awaiting sacrifice outside - sharing bread, don't their faces overflow with joy?
"Mere tricks prolonging daily endurance. Without these so-called pleasures, we could have found release ages ago... Only our master's joy remains pure - They directly stimulate senses, requiring no toil or humiliation for ultimate pleasure. Our master promises post-death enjoyment."
You smile - her rebuttal serves your purpose perfectly. You ask what joy the Cultic God provides. Does it match these pleasures you mentioned?
"Fine dining's joy, lovemaking's joy, cloud-reaching joy..." She regards you dismissively, "Retreat? Impossible. We shall all sacrifice ourselves here."
"Ah, these joys," you nod, "then does the Cultic God believe Their believers cannot obtain fine food, lovemaking, elevated status independently? Alim and his children earn everything through their own hands - aren't they as magnificent as the Cultic God?"
"Why attach your existence to something you know cruel? Without them, your life might hold less joy, but wouldn't it also contain far less suffering?"

Badriyyah's arm grip gradually loosens as she bows confusedly. Much requires consideration - even if final conclusions favor sacrificing life for the Cultic God - at least now, your words have carved small cracks in her heart's fortress. And opportunity, survival's chance, slips through that fissure.
Cultists outside grow anxious awaiting divine descent signals, knocking to query Badriyyah about progress. You seize this moment pounding stone walls, creating fierce struggle sounds - cultists open doors attempting joint subjugation, and you quickly grab the nearest person, dragging him down to block that doorway.
"If your god truly desires me, They wouldn't permit escape!" you shout, "Look at Badriyyah - she no longer restrains me!"
People gaze toward Badriyyah, standing dazed and bewildered. By her recovery and attempted prevention words, it's too late. You gasp while shoving through crowds, sprinting onto streets. Passersby stare oddly at this noble's disheveled, wounded appearance. Some summon guards while cultists lurk in shadows watching like nest-peering rats. You see no Badriyyah among them.
So be it - you're exhausted, not just from struggle but from that god... that voice still muttering unwillingly in your mind... Your servants arrive upon hearing news, guards too, and you collapse into their embrace, falling into deep slumber.
You failed to persuade her... if you wants to live, you have no choice but to resort to force.

This world holds as many ways of living as there are people in it.
You tell Badriyyah about that female warrior's story - how she challenged the most brutal battles in a woman's body, took pride in victory and conquest, needed no divine aid yet lived supremely happy.
"Those are mere tricks to make us endure another day. Without these so-called joys, we could have found release ages ago... Only our master's pleasure remains pure - They directly stimulate our senses, requiring no toil or humiliation for ultimate bliss. And this bliss, our master has promised, we'll feel even after death."
You smile - her rebuttal serves your purpose perfectly.
You tell her Adila's joy springs from constant transcendence - she transcended herself, her gender, all limits, while the Cultic God can only offer endless compromise. They make believers hunger while fantasizing about gluttony's pleasure, make them crawl with lice while imagining silk sheets' caress... They cannot change the world, only alter believers' thoughts - the Cultic God has never transcended anything, not even the Purist! In your view, Adila deserves far more respect
Badriyyah wants to argue, but you raise one finger.
You point out that when mortals endlessly hone their will, their souls shine brilliantly like divine radiance. The Cultic God loves such souls, yet They cannot even make a single believer become such a person - still needing Badriyyah to deceive you into coming here... Ha, this deity has truly never transcended anything, too lazy even to attempt it, wouldn't you say?

This inventor immerses herself daily in her creations, ignoring outside turmoil. For her, Cultic Gods, Purists, Sultans - as long as she has inventions, she's content. So the point isn't who provides joy, but finding what truly brings happiness, right?
"Those are tricks making us endure another day. Without these so-called pleasures, we could have found release long ago..." Badriyyah dismisses this, "Only our master's joy remains pure - They directly stimulate our senses, requiring no toil or humiliation for ultimate pleasure. Our master promises we'll feel this joy even after death."
You smile - her rebuttal serves your purpose perfectly.
You ask what pure pleasure leaves behind. Mahir's inventions might change the world, at least many people's fates. Yet a great deity, a master - what They accomplish is merely manipulating twitching, pleasure, and fluids triggered by your own body. The Cultic God understands nothing of this world - They can only manipulate believers. A century hence, people might remember Mahir but not Them!
Badriyyah wants to argue, but you raise one finger and shake it.
You ask her - if Mahir invented a machine producing bread and cheese, gave it some divine name like "Corruptor" or "Krenmasina," how many of Badriyyah's companions would convert to worship this deity? The key lies in changing the world that causes suffering, using this world's materials to create more materials - the key was never soul manipulation.

You used the joyful Nabhani as an example—his happiness certainly came from life! Dead, he couldn't enjoy roasted mutton, couldn't admire himself in heavy golden earrings, and couldn't embrace his beloved...
"But all this has a dark side, and all this fades with age." Badriyyah stared directly at you, no longer laughing madly but appearing somewhat weary. "When I'm old, I can't chew meat, my earlobes stretch thin by earrings, men and women no longer touch me... All my pleasures will be stolen by time. Better to let the Cultic Gods' grace preserve them while I can enjoy them. Our master promises we'll have these pleasures even after death."
You smiled. Her rebuttal served your purpose perfectly.
"So," you asked Badriyyah, "your faith exists only because you fear aging? You destroy everything present only because you don't want to watch others destroy it? You won't befriend a cat only because you know it lives only a dozen years? The Cultic Gods' believers are all too afraid to face life's weight. Your so-called noble sacrifice is merely a coward's escape. After all, there is only one true dedication—let life's thorns pierce your own body so those you embrace suffer no harm!"

You tell Badriyyah about Maggie, your wife - she strongly dislikes cults and cultists, yet she's gentle, wise, compassionate. She often gives servants extra half-days off, pretends not to notice when they keep fabric scraps for scarves. She can't bear seeing anyone around her hungry, spending her own money to help slum drainage projects. Even the water channels in cultist gathering areas were built with funds Maggie convinced familiar ladies to donate together - without her, this place would still be a stinking mosquito-breeding swamp.
"So if the Cultic God comes, what happens to people like Maggie? Killed? Hanged from trees? Buried underground? Is that truly what she deserves? How many who've harmed the poor... how many exploiters, how many parasites live high above - maybe the Cultic God would prefer them! Badriyyah, can you imagine? The master you summon with your life might cooperate with those you despise! When that time comes, those sitting on worldly thrones continuing to rule might not be the cultists beside you!"

You ask Badriyyah - didn't the Cultic God promise happiness? Doesn't death mean nothingness, meaning no more pleasure? This sounds like something the celibate Purists would demand she do!
She laughs contemptuously once, then says: "Our master certainly won't abandon Their children - They promise we can continue enjoying ourselves after death. Our souls will ascend among the stars, like those powerful beings we summon - we'll do whatever we want, we'll become demigods!"
You smile - her answer serves your purpose perfectly.
You tell Badriyyah that whether Iman's Purist, her Cultic God, even the Highland's Highlord and summoned monsters - all these things are identical. These beings are isolated from this world, can only manifest briefly through projections.
"If those monsters you summon are truly happy in their own world, why do they compete to be summoned? Why can just some living souls drive these great beings? Why can't they stay long before being dragged back? Finding pleasure is far harder for them than even the most humble living person! When we want to kill, we just go onto the street - the only concern is evading guards and enemies. But them? When they want to soak their hands in blood, they must wait and wait in nothingness for some filthy, mad cultists to perform summoning rituals!"
You conclude with vicious prophecy: "Such a sacrificial ritual abandoning all pleasures for a lying master might be better suited to Iman."

You seize this moment pounding stone walls, creating fierce struggle sounds - cultists open doors attempting joint subjugation, and you quickly grab the nearest person, dragging him down to block that doorway.
"If your god truly desires me, They wouldn't permit escape!" you shout, "Look at Badriyyah - she no longer restrains me!"
People gaze toward Badriyyah, standing dazed and bewildered. By her recovery and attempted prevention words, it's too late. You gasp while shoving through crowds, sprinting onto streets. Passersby stare oddly at this noble's disheveled, wounded appearance. Some summon guards while cultists lurk in shadows watching like nest-peering rats. You see no Badriyyah among them.
So be it - you're exhausted, not just from struggle but from that god... that voice still muttering unwillingly in your mind... Your servants arrive upon hearing news, guards too, and you collapse into their embrace, falling into deep slumber.

No matter how you pound the chamber door, it remains coldly immobile. Badriyyah giggles, waiting until you're exhausted from struggling, then slowly drags you back to the pool. She uses long needles dipped in the pool's black liquid to tattoo complex patterns on both your skin and hers. When no more space remains for needles, your consciousness slowly fades as your souls flow out through these tattoos, consumed eagerly by the waiting "god."
This power helps Them temporarily enter the mortal realm, though only briefly... after all, this isn't shadow or ethereal dream, but the massive divine being itself. They will burst from the cavern to feast on the cultists outside, then find more people. They'll keep eating and eating until They've accumulated enough power to remain in this world - until They devour the entire world.
None of that matters now. None of that matters now.

Mind Resistance
Elemental Purge
Eldritch Gods

The summoning-failed Cultic God savagely assaults you in dreams with endless suffering, piercing pain, despair and sorrow.
How predictable! You grit your teeth in desperate resistance, fully grasping this deity's methods - They can manipulate your senses, rewrite the messages your skin sends to your brain, making everything around you twisted yet real.
But that's all... just that! As long as you believe, remain unwavering, firmly commanding every nerve to obey your - not the divine - will, you become an unyielding reef in the Cultic God's mental tide. They crash against you but can do nothing to you.

You wear Mahir's creation - lightning captured in form - the perfect storm to either purify or devastate your mind.
Your brain sizzles from the electrical surge. Fortunately, that constant muttering Cultic God whisper falls silent forever.

You unleash the presence within your mind - impossibly dense ink spreads instantly, splashing across heaven and earth with unmatched terror and malice, reducing this greedy monster to a cowering insect, crushed by thunderous wrath until only withered remains persist.

You unleash the presence within your mind - impossibly pure radiance spreads like a second dawn, yet this light burns cold, majestic, merciless. The moment it touches this greedy Cultic God, They ignite, shrieking piteously, writhing in agony before inevitable annihilation...
As if burning Them still couldn't quell the remaining fury, you wake bearing many fire-scorched wounds, agonizingly painful.

Her needle, dipped in herb juice, worked while she murmured incantations... A cool breath spread along the gradually forming delicate petals, then the banished divine will began furious retaliation!
"How dare you? How dare you? How dare you make promises to a god and then break them? How dare you refuse to fulfill the divine will after receiving so many blessings?"
Pure white flames coalesced into a thick whip, lashing your body hard and nearly tearing your soul apart. Your heart split in two—half pure and devout, half sinful and vile, burning up in the fire!
When you slowly awakened from the vision, you had completely forgotten your purpose—why were you sitting on scorched earth, with ashes all around? Wind carried away those burned remnants like sand. You didn't know what you had lost.

"How laughable! How laughable! Foolish mortal, how could you think that once a Cultic God has taken root, you still have a chance to stuff Them back into the void? Who do you think you are?! Hahahaha!"
That malice-filled mockery pierced your ears and heart, leaving a small but unhealable hollow. The Cultic God's eye squeezed through the hollow, peering at this sweet world. They would descend... no, part of Them had already descended, through your body!
When you awakened from this nearly heart-rending agony, you had completely forgotten your purpose—why were you sitting on a land of brilliant flowers? Why did each flower sprout grotesque limbs? Why did blood seep beneath every leaf? In your daze, ink stains spread across your entire arm. You staggered toward the uncorrupted world, aware of none of this.

When Badriyyah's long needle approached your palm, a tremor ran through her.
A massive, indescribable black pillar hovered above you two, as if the entire earth had been inverted and forged into a shimmering obsidian. Should her needle drop a fraction further, divine punishment would follow immediately!
You focused every ounce of will, clutching her hand as you fought to repel the inner demons conjured by the dark gods. The moment you lowered your heads, the earth erupted amid flames from the sky! Blinding light consumed everything around you, as if you were standing above the very gates of hell!
The two gods warned: you, a mortal, shall never betray Them!
Ah... mortal.
Clarity struck your mind—you were no longer a mortal. You saw through Their avarice and cowardice... Were They now here to destroy you, even though you were just a hair's breadth from that ultimate fate? Carrying the unconscious Badriyyah in your arms, you rose undaunted and strode forward with eyes shut. Those thieves of destiny deserved your despise.
Counting to ten, you opened your eyes. The chaotic, free world of mortals came back into view.

The serpent spirits dwelling within stone sculptures were intimidated by this feline before them. Those stone-carved segments rolled, stirring underground quicksand... From deep stone steps came the sound of mechanisms activating - you opened the temple's seal... at least partially.

The first mechanism requires matching several special carved stone plates... The patterns upon that rock python sculpture seem mysteriously corresponding.
As [s1.name] drew nearer to examine it, the massive sculpture springs to life, ensnaring [s1.name] in its coils and eliciting a pained moan from [s1.name].
Quicksand flows through ancient gears as carved stone scales scrape against flesh, etching deliberate patterns into skin... The puzzle's solution becomes clear - [s1.name] must strip away their clothing so the stone serpent can brand complete markings... Just before [s1.name] would be crushed entirely, you decipher the full design and turn the tablet...
Stone coils unwind, releasing their sacrifice to the flowing sands below... Deep beneath the steps, grinding mechanisms echo - you've broken through part of the temple's ancient ward.

A sequence of carved tablets holds the key to the first mechanism, their symbols somehow linked to the great python's stone hide. But when you venture close enough to study the markings, the sculpture awakens with terrible purpose, crushing [s1.name] in its embrace. As the stone drinks [s1.gender(his,her)] life, crimson spreads across every carved scale - yet the riddle remains unsolved. This adventure was destined to end in devastating loss and empty return.

With the first lock turned, the cobra atop the second pillar stirs to life, sliding along hidden tracks to seal the great doors... Wind, sand, or sorcery strikes hollow chambers within, giving the statue human voice - ancient words offer a riddle: enter only when the sovereign takes pleasure - thankfully [s2.name] knows such lore!
You notice a ring of buttons atop the cobra's head, depicting the sun's trajectory - this appears to be where the second mechanism opens...
The answer, of course, was the noon button on top of the cobra's head. In the lost ancient empire, the monarch was considered an embodiment of the sun, and they would naturally engage in public debauchery under the midday sun to prove their power... at least that's what the blasphemous texts say.
Regardless, this answer satisfied the cobra statue. It slowly slid into the dark quicksand along the stone groove, clearing the way for you.

Convincing her to don this garment took considerable time, but in an instant, her body was suspended by writhing metal serpent chains. Those malevolent designs - even when the wearer tried to avoid such usage - fulfilled their original purpose under magical compulsion.
The venomous fangs, sharp forked tongues, and tail stingers pierced your wife's flesh, injecting curses that twisted human will... The ancient consciousness dwelling within the serpent chains tempted and threatened you, demanding you personally repeat their transgressions.
Did you anticipate this when you had your beloved wife wear this ancient garment? Was this born of ignorant curiosity, or deliberate intent?
Under magic's influence, her serpentine form coiled tightly around you. As your pleasure peaked, the vipers bit your lover more fiercely - and her ecstasy and agony blurred together in your vision.
Finally, when you lay exhausted, the serpents retracted their fangs and stingers with satisfaction, clattering to the floor like ordinary objects...
You quickly gathered the dazed Maggie... but your mind was already reweaving this tale, recalling her expressions, your sensations... hoping this depraved story would please the Sultan enough to break that damning card.

Convincing her to don this garment took considerable time, but in an instant, those malevolent designs - even when the wearer tried to avoid such usage - fulfilled their original purpose under magical compulsion.
The venomous fangs, sharp forked tongues, and tail stingers pierced your wife's flesh, injecting curses that twisted human will... The ancient consciousness dwelling within the serpent chains tempted and threatened you, demanding you personally repeat their transgressions.
Did you anticipate this when you had your beloved wife wear this ancient garment? Was this born of ignorance, or deliberate intent?

Later, you ordered servants to carefully clean the room's traces... but they reported in amazement that the chamber was spotless. All stains had transformed into black silk, woven into the serpent chains...
When light passed through it, the image of you and [s3.name] entwined flickered before people's eyes - dreamlike and ethereal, unclear whether it enticed or accused the world.

5008194.title: Serpent's Purification
strings: Serpent's Purification
People gossip about the new Religious Leader... and his scandalous black serpent silk. Someone suggests you hold a purification ritual to help everyone recognize the Purist's power.
Requires Lust Serpent's Veil

You didn't do this? Why not? People speculated about your true intentions, but stranger rumors made you a target for mockery, ridicule, and attack... The Lust Serpent's Veil absorbed this malice, thriving as your heart drew closer to darkness.
All Impurity Purified

You publicly demonstrated this miracle - divine light descended from heaven, transforming that impure and lascivious black silk into pure white. Now it would symbolize the Purist's great wisdom, compassion, and power... You improvised a speech about redemption for those who committed sins of lust, moving many listeners.
Amid praises to the divine, you lifted the white silk again - through the light, people could now only see devout praying figures. More came to confess and donate for redemption, growing more crowded - you quickly ordered the miracle hung high, lest they draw too close and see the meaningful smile in the silk's phantoms.

strings: A Mercenary's Journal
Reading can improve yourself, so develop a habit of reading.
Currently Reading
The reader.

There are no attribute requirements for girls who love to read.

5008196.title: The Vagrants' Demand
strings: The Vagrants' Demand

Raed brought a large group of vagrants to your doorstep. From now on, you can only enter the court through the back gate in your carriage. She claims that the vagrants are merely hungry and in need of assistance... If your game can help them, prove it!
Raed awaits your help or pressures you.
The vagrants have gathered.
8 Gold Coins or 1 Feast
You just happen to hold a Sultan Card.
You may provide 8 gold coins or any one Feast.
Breaking the Extravagance Card requires 16 gold coins or a Feast.
Aid them or take this opportunity to break a Sultan Card? You must choose.
As expected, you only talked and took no action... Raed left you, leading her vagrants to keep freezing and starving beyond the city walls... let her go, then!
Fickle Fate
A Meal
As luck would have it, it is this card.

The vagrants claimed they came to assist you... They were willing to do anything! Many of these stateless people survived by taking odd jobs—this could even be considered a form of dignified begging.
You noticed that many of them carried themselves with a certain poise; they were not used to begging, nor to wandering the streets. Their attempts to claim leftover food were tinged with shyness. You paused, and a thought crossed your mind... If Sultan stripped you of everything—as he so enjoys doing—would you too gather outside a noble's mansion, hoping for work to fill your stomach? The thought stirred your hand. You reached into your purse, gathering a large handful of gold coins. Your servants converted them into clothing, shoes, and food for the vagrants. Then you retreated into your residence, unable to watch further.

The vagrants claimed they came to assist you... They were willing to do anything! Many of these stateless people survived by taking odd jobs—this could even be considered a form of dignified begging.
You could not bear to see them stumbling, gaunt, and exhausted. You instructed your servants to fetch flatbreads, dried meat, tea, and dates. The vagrants sat and enjoyed a proper meal. They were thrilled—they had been waiting for this! Still, they avoided showing themselves as beggars. They first gathered to thank you, then helped move items and tidied things, before finally diving into the food. They may soon be hungry again, but for now, you've helped them survive another day.

Defeating the mobs besieging your home counts as a minor conquest. The vagrants gathered like ants—now is the time to pour boiling water over the bugs.
Many players enjoy this approach! When you revealed the Conquest Card, the nobles organized their private guards, blocking all escape routes. You dispatched the mob with little effort. Naturally, Sultan paid little attention cause the nobles are like his children, and how many parents truly mind cruel games of their little kids?
In the end, you didn't even find Raed among the bodies—she had likely become the spoils of some noble... a pity.

Though irritating, the crowd was numerous enough to count as a Bloodshed Card The crowd gathered like ants—now is the time to pour boiling water over the bugs.

In the end, you didn't even find Raed among the bodies—she had likely become the spoils of some noble... a pity.
[player.name] Performs Astonishing Feats

Now, Raed has come to believe you completely—this game can truly be used to do some good! This large sum of money is enough to see countless homeless souls through the winter... For now, they regard you as a living deity. Well... at least for the time being.

Now, Raed has come to believe you completely—this game can truly be used to do some good! Many of these people haven't tasted a clean, warm, properly seasoned meal in ages... You have, at least for a time, restored them from mere survival into something approaching humanity.

5008197.title: The Vagrants' Labor
strings: The Vagrants' Labor

These vagrants will do anything... and you realize they are not ordinary beggars, but displaced people of various backgrounds. Some are artisans, some can sing and dance, some can write or manage documents, and some are even of noble origin—simply lacking their identity papers.
This crowd never sits idle. If there is no work, they will find some, so long as it means a meal.
You may receive random rewards.
Should one too oft employ these rootless folk... they may become a lingering burden.
They truly can do anything.

Your crumbling walls and cracked teapot were mended; a strange smoke lent your garments an air of refined fragrance; six oxen and three horses were shod in a single breath; tales of your virtue—told from your third year onward—were spun anew and spread through the marketplace; your storerooms, ledgers, and shelves were brought into order... In the end, all was set in perfect order, and your household ran with newfound ease.

5008198.title: The Vagrants' Demand
strings: The Vagrants' Demand

Led by Raed, the vagrants surrounded your house again, banging rusted gongs and broken boards, shouting songs both wild and senseless. The stench of rain-soaked misery clung to them...
"Lord [player.name], our needs are few—just a roof against the rain, and walls against the wind. Help us, and we shall surely help you. We have our skills, don't we, brothers? We have the skills!" Their cries rose like a storm, shaking the rooftop of your residence. Whether it is praise or threat was hard to say.
Raed Awaits Your Help
Vagrants
The Vagrants' Labor
Their Demand: 20 Gold Coins or Any Vacant House
Maybe this is a chance to break the Sultan Card...
You need an empty house or 20 gold coins to satisfy their demand.
Of course, you can also use the Sultan Card...
Aid them or take this opportunity to break a Sultan Card? You must choose.

Through your indifference, you and Raed parted on bad term.s She had no choice but to lead that great troop of vagrants to seek another corner that was dry, clean, and fit for a night's sleep—places one must fight others to gain.
The Sultan will not allow you to remove the Extravagance Card repeatedly from the same group of vagrants.
A Mansion for All
As luck would have it, it is this card.

At the city's edge stood many manors of the old nobility, abandoned since their heads rolled beside their king's. Each manor had its claimants, yet few dared live within walls stained by blood, and fewer still could pay the price. You placed a weighty purse into the hands of a trusted servant, sending him to find the vagrants a dwelling broad and solid enough, one of those relics of the old dynasty: cheap, sound, and fit for many lives.
In time, Raed returned with her most capable followers to thank you. You saw it clearly then: these were not mere beggars, but people of talent, once educated, now displaced.

You sighed and thought a while. Was there not a vacant house of your own? Left idle, it would be taken by the desperate soon enough; better, perhaps, to give it freely, and grant them a few more seasons of shelter. You called for the keys and sent a steady hand to lead them there. With doubt and disbelief, they departed your gates.
In time, Raed returned with her most capable followers to thank you. You saw it clearly then: these were not mere beggars, but people of talent, once educated, now displaced.

In the end, you didn't even find Raed among the bodies—she had likely become the spoils of some noble... a pity.
[player.name] Performs Astonishing Feats
Show Me Something New

Now, Raed has come to believe you completely—this game can truly be used to do some good! The house is decent, and everyone has a bed of their own. It's a little cramped, but those with means will eventually move on. The house need only shelter those who cannot leave... A blessing no vagrant ever dared to hope for.

The Sultan laughed and waved you off. He reminded you that you'd already used these nameless wretches once before to resolve an Extravagance Card—and dragging their names through court again was dull, tasteless, and beneath the dignity of the crown. Reluctantly, you withdrew the Sultan Card, trembling a little, and hurried to dream up another use for it.

5008199.title: Squatting Tenants
strings: Squatting Tenants

While you were distracted, the vagrants had taken up residence in one of your vacant houses—you suspected Raed had a hand in it. Now they paraded your generosity across the city, singing of [player.name]'s supposed charity and plenty. You have spare houses for the poor!
Uninvited Vagrants
Occupied House
Adopt Peaceful Solution — 20 Gold Coins or Assign Raed to Manage Them
Evict with Troops
You can break a Conquest Card of Bronze tier or lower.
You could pay them to go away.
If you place Raed, you could formally hand the house to the vagrants.
Or you could call in army and drive these squatters out by force.
You must make your choice.
You did nothing—and the vagrants truly moved into that house. Now everyone calls it the vagrants' house! Some call you a fool; others call it a kind of chivalrous grace.
Financial Solution
Let us be frank.
You have seized the victory without battle.
As luck would have it, it is this card.

You handed the vagrants a large sum so they could buy a more suitable plot of land. Whatever resentments had lain between you and them, Raed thanked you openly for your generosity — and for your magnanimity. Under her direction, the vagrants would now be able to work for you when needed.
You told Raed, "If these people are to have a home, they must also bring benefit to Lord [player.name]'s household." She only grinned; she found the bargain fair.
At the sight of soldiers and weapons, the vagrants scattered — plainly they had understood your resolve...

Defeating the mobs besieging your residence counts as a minor conquest. The vagrants gathered like ants—now is the time to pour boiling water over the bugs.
Many players enjoy this approach! When you revealed the Conquest Card, the nobles organized their private guards, blocking all escape routes. You dispatched the mob with little effort. Naturally, Sultan paid little attention cause the nobles are like his children, and how many parents truly mind cruel games of their little kids?

5008200.title: The Vagrants' Labor
strings: The Vagrants' Labor

These vagrants will do anything... and you realize they are not ordinary beggars, but displaced people of various backgrounds. Some are artisans, some can sing and dance, some can write or manage documents, and some are even of noble origin—simply lacking their identity papers.
Their Tribute
Compared to before, they are now willing to do much more for you.
You have already discerned Raed's little game: the more you rely on the vagrants, the more they will come to demand in return.
One by one, they bring forth their treasures.

You granted them shelter, and in gratitude they offered what they carried through exile. Most of it was worthless trinkets and broken keepsakes. Yet every so often, amidst the scraps, lay something of true worth—books saved from burning, a soldier's blade, a noble's ring. Sifting through such gifts was a kind of treasure-hunting in itself.

5008201.title: [player.name]'s Fortress
strings: [player.name]'s Fortress

You set aside a dwelling for the vagrants. Should you wish, you could even let it bear your name... and if you were to appear in person at its dedication, they might feel safer, more content under your shadow. But is such favor truly worth granting? Or perhaps...
Raed Awaits Your Attendance at the Naming Ritual
The Vagrants' Labor
Will you attend... or not?
It is better simply to ignore them or to grant Raed this small courtesy.
Of course, you could also use this occasion to break a Sultan Card.

Raed brazenly trumpeted the deeds of [player.name] Fortress everywhere—now the whole city knows, and you truly cannot deny it with certainty... In any case, since it has happened, you might as well enjoy its benefits. After all, even in the Sultan's Game, that's exactly what you did—didn't you??
But all of this, you realized, was precisely the plot Raed had spun from the start.
In [player.name]'s Name

You sighed. Even if you were to cast them out now, the tale was already told. Too many eyes had seen Raed come alone to your halls—first to offer aid, then to secure a house, and now to claim a name for the place. At every step, whether you yielded or refused, she weaved the story to her advantage: "I am in the favor of the Sultan's trusted hand, [player.name]." With that claim, she and her vagrants could linger anywhere. And Raed was clever. Each time she asked, she first brought a gift, knowing full well that nobles feared nothing more than a debt of gratitude.
Still... You could not deny that under her hand, the place had grown orderly, even useful. Perhaps that too was part of her design.

You sighed. Even if you were to cast them out now, the tale is already told. Too many eyes had seen Raed come alone to your halls—first to offer aid, then to secure a house, and now to claim a name for the place. At every step, whether you yielded or refused, she weaved the story to her advantage: "I am in the favor of Sultan's trusted hand, [player.name]." With that claim, she and her vagrants could linger anywhere. And Raed was clever. Each time she asked, she first brought a gift, knowing full well that nobles fear nothing more than a debt of gratitude... yet she seemed unaware that you detest following someone else's script.
So, when all the vagrants had gathered inside the fortress that now bears your name, you announced the opening of a grand spectacle: all were free to hunt and slew these nameless, lawless vagrants at will! Like driving prey into a hunting enclosured in autumn, for the nobles to pursue as they please.
It quickly became clear that, when slaughter and pillage were without restriction, people embraced it with fervor... Even the Sultan himself later scolded you, grumbling that he was not invited to participate in such a magnificent event. To appease him, you and the participating nobles must present numerous trophies from the hunt, and only then did his anger subside.

5008202.title: [player.name]'s Fortress
strings: [player.name]'s Fortress
In the generous and merciful name of [player.name], all those wandering, nameless, and unclean may dwell here.
At last, the vagrants have a home.
What will you have vagrants do for you?
Among the vagrants are many capable individuals, able to accomplish countless tasks. Explore freely.
When they work for you, they also draw attention from the outside world, stirring new conflicts.
She originally sought only a spark of inspiration.
Among the vagrants are doctors.
This place was always a refuge for the cursed.
There's Always Something That Can Be Done
Some Bear the Burden of Your Crimes
[player.name] Laid an Egg
Tonight, you sleep among countless others.
You have truly helped many.
You ask the elder what the stars foretell.
You found a few professionals.
Vagrants excel at gathering whispers.
The wretched are fertile soil for Cultic God.
Your suffering is a blessing.
Sultan has taken everything from you.
You will reclaim the nation that was stolen.
Every sorrow will be cleansed.
You painted a picture of an ideal society for the vagrants.
A Vision of the New World
The day is close at hand.

The moment she stepped inside, the small bell on Mahir's belt jingled. Without hesitation, she turned [player.name]'s Fortress upside down—finally uncovering an ancient bird figurine. By striking the runes on its feathers in the correct sequence, the magic flowed from its beak.
Legend has it that many deities once commanded their followers to gather Aether, and when collected in abundance, the Immaculate Purity would seek them out...
Their tools are makeshift, and it's hard to say whether they rely on sorcery or medicine—but the results are undeniably immediate.
What curse is more terrifying than being a homeless, hungry, and exposed vagrants? When a Healer is willing to endure it all, most curses prove far easier to lift than they first appear.
Trade, hire assistants, gather intelligence... the vagrants are a treasure trove, always capable of revealing something interesting.
They may be dying, covered in sores; strange-smelling prostitutes; disoriented elders; or even a freshly departed corpse—each one leaving the High Constables utterly helpless.

After much debate, the vagrants staged a grand "Run of [player.name]" in the slums. A straw-stuffed effigy of Lord [player.name], taller than two men, went lumbering down the muddy streets, chasing after shrieking children and terrified livestock. Whoever was caught was dragged into its gaping, sheet-sewn mouth and devoured whole, only for torrents of blood to spray out afterward... well, probably animal blood.
At the climax, drums thundered and gongs resounded as alchemists showered the straw Lord [player.name] with bursts of glittering powder. And then—he laid an egg in the middle of the street! The crowd surged forward, beating at it with sticks.
Quick, smash it, or a little [player.name] will crawl out and steal your wife! Cheers erupted as the shell broke apart, spilling forth candy and coins.
The following day, eunuchs retold the spectacle in vivid detail. The Lapis Lazuli Hall rang with Sultan's laughter, and for once you seemed less threatening, less loathsome in his eyes. What a fine festival. From now on, it will be celebrated each year.

Mothers gathered around you, treating you as their lost son. Shaman and priests whose gods have long abandoned them stood vigil in the courtyard, commanding their forgotten deities to guard your rest.
Even those who have nothing—never blessed by any god—offered prayers tonight for [player.name]'s peace. Your suffering felt like a single drop falling into a vast ocean of pain, dissolved and carried away. This night was dreamless, and mercifully so.

Wherever Maggie walked today, she overheard tales of Lord [player.name]'s deeds—of shelter, food, safety, and, most importantly, dignity. She was not blind; she knew some of these stories had been carefully staged. But the truth remained undeniable, and for now, it was enough to soften her judgment, to let her forgive some of your past misdeeds...

Wizards, shamans, and priests of forsaken gods—they all spoke at once, their voices clashing as they interpreted the secrets of the stars, unraveling the mystery in your mind with their contradictory words...
Until, at last, a disheveled scholar overturned them all with a single scrap of paper, making you believe that everything can be calculated, and that it is purely objective.

They shared with you true knowledge—insights sharp enough to decide the rise or fall of great affairs. Had you not aided the vagrants so generously, such secrets might never have been passed to an outsider.
No matter the task, they always return with answers.
In their suffering, men cannot help but cry out to whatever presence they feel watching from beyond—whether for mercy, for ruin, or for curses. Those who sink deepest into misery welcome them all.

So the Purists Church preaches to the poor, that pain will one day transmute into miracles, into the path of eternal salvation. Many scoff at such words—yet they never fail to draw the desperate to your sermons.
They knew this already, of course. Yet none dared to speak it, or even think it. Now you whisper the truth aloud... and suddenly they see the beast that has long been gnawing at their hearts.
Many who once swore allegiance to the Highland Kingdom became vagrants, refusing to accept Sultan's papers of servitude. Now, they may sign instead upon the founding scrolls of a new realm.

You promised them a world without pain, without tyranny, without chains of name or title. Countless broken souls were moved by the radiance of your words—and their yearning began to feed your strength.

You spoke of changing fate, of freedom and equality—ideas that few among them could fully grasp. Some vagrants muttered that Lord [player.name] simply had too much time on his hands, others whispered of sorcery and hidden rites. Yet a few listened in silence, their eyes clouded with thought...

As you spoke, the clouds above twisted into shapes like children's drawings. "You will redraw this world," you declared, "as easily as you smear clay upon the ground." And in their despair, many vagrants joined your church—their wishes nourishing your power.
No need for words, no need for persuasion. They already understood the meaning of your march. And they will follow you—for vengeance, for hope, for a justice they have never seen.

5008203.title: The Besieged Keep
strings: The Besieged Keep

The refuge you and Raed had carved out was growing famous, which is a sanctuary for the homeless, the unprotected, and those without papers. Word spread, and what began as mercy soon looked like a prize to be taken. Gangs, nobles, and Cultist all began to sniff around, unhappy at losing the easy prey they once used at will. Trouble was coming from every quarter.
Raed
To solve this, you can place 40 gold coins or...
You could throw a great deal of coin at the problem.
You could present something that proved Raed's standing.
Or you could do nothing and let Raed spend months handling the fallout alone.

There is no perfect solution to solve such things, and Raed knows it. Tending vagrants is a bottomless pit, yet she keeps pouring her strength into it—just so someone else might have one night of sound sleep, one full meal.
In the end, it all still came down to money.
But you hadn't quite used the right approach.

Bribing the high constables, buying extra land, hiring mercenaries to maintain order, sending accountants, engaging negotiators to smooth relations... and finally paying a hefty tax—this place had practically become a noble estate under the Sultan's law.
Raed didn't know how to properly thank you. She understood that everything you'd done went far beyond what any one person could consider an act of charity—and no matter what motive you might have, she was willing to stand by your side.

You summoned Raed and told her: the vagrants didn't lack money—they lacked genuine, local support... and she had a way to solve that problem. She had simply forgotten one thing: that she was a princess.
Hearing this, Raed erupted in anger, but quickly calmed herself. What should I do? she wondered. If it's for the sake of the vagrants, I'll do anything!

5008204.title: The Busy Raed
strings: The Busy Raed
Coordinating disputes, sourcing medicine, begging for food, preventing crime, organizing crime... Raed does whatever it takes to keep the vagrants alive.
For now, Raed isn't available to help you.
Once she's done, she will return to serve you.
After the vagrant matters were settled, Raed came back to assist you.

5008205.title: The False Princess
strings: The False Princess

If it weren't for the coarse curses she muttered upon entering, and the dagger you glimpsed beneath her delicate, flowing veil, you might never believe that this beauty was really Raed. But to have the Capital truly accept a noblewoman, appearances alone weren't enough.
Raed must step forward.
Send a noble envoy with at least 5 in both Stealth and Sociability to forge the princess's title.
Who should you invite to build support for the princess?
You delayed too long. Raed gave up the mad idea—she would rather go back and spend her days among the stinking vagrants than wear perfume or skirts too tight to walk in!
The Title of Princess

On the fringes of the Empire, many barren, backward tribes exist, but they are at least recognized as nobles by Sultan. Your plan is to present Raed as the tenth daughter of a tribal leader, sent to the Capital to find a suitable husband. Naturally, this requires funding... but Raed surprisingly offered to pay it herself.
She twisted a silk handkerchief in her hands, a little awkwardly—by its craftsmanship, it seemed to be a relic from her homeland. But a foreign princess with a taste for vintage trinkets? Perfectly plausible. "My mother left me a small fortune... likely earned from selling off a princess in the past, which is why I've never touched it. But now I need to become Princess Raedina, gain standing in high society... then I can help your cause, and you can care for the vagrants. Perhaps together we can accomplish something truly remarkable, yes?" You talked for quite a while longer. Before leaving, she reminded you to secure influential nobles to spread the word: "A tribal princess is coming to the Capital." The more people who hear it, the less likely her true identity will be discovered.
Princess Raedina is supremely pure.
Princess Raedina is supremely valiant.
Princess Raedina is supremely beautiful.
Princess Raedina is supremely noble.
Princess Raedina is supremely graceful.
Princess Raedina is supremely wealthy.
Princess Raedina is supremely gentle.
Princess Raedina is supremely refined.

As the champion of the Purists, her reputation among the nobility was impeccable. Iman listened quietly to your request, then asked a few pointed questions: Does this princess follow the Purists? Of course—she is devoutly faithful! Will she be helpful to your cause? Absolutely—but, well... you'd rather this "help" remain discreet. "Understood," Iman replied. "I will tell the nobles who come seeking the Pure Word that Princess Raedina is soon to arrive. She hails from the most virtuous family, who once wandered the wastelands in austere devotion, and have only recently returned to the tainted world of men."

Jabal, of course, was willing to help, but he was puzzled over how. "Look, all that tea and gossip with noblewomen... I obviously won't attend. They never invite me anyway, right? So how am I supposed to spread word about this... Ra—Raedina Princess?" You explained that Princess Raedina—he must memorize her name carefully—comes from a fiercely warlike tribe. She wields a dagger with skill, and the husband she seeks must be the strongest warrior in the Capital! In other words, only the bravest may win her heart. Even Jabal understood the key points for praise—though, of course, you did not grant his request to duel Raed.

Nabhani could barely contain his excitement—this was a princess, after all! A never-before-seen beauty! He bombarded you with questions about her appearance, hobbies, attire, tastes, figure, choice of mate, birthday, hair color, eye color, favorite gemstones—until you were thoroughly exasperated. "Alright, alright, I get it! We simply must tell everyone interested in the Empire's beauties that the finest flower is about to join the garden. A pearl-crowned princess, how splendid... I can hardly wait to meet her! Shall I arrange an audience in the next couple of days? Come on, don't pretend—I can tell she's already here. It's just the identity she wants, right?" You swore you would regularly create opportunities for Nabhani to meet the princess alone, and only then did he reluctantly relent.

"I cannot help you; it's wrong. We must not deceive the world," Qais said, staring at you. "If she truly is a princess, I will declare it openly; if she is not, I cannot call her one." You stared, momentarily confused. He continued, frowning, "So... she really is a princess, yes? I see no reason for you to deceive me." Enlightened, you realized—yes, yes, of course! She is a princess; you are not deceiving the righteous Qais. Satisfied, he nodded. In the following days, you could hear him proudly proclaiming to anyone who would listen, "Princess Raedina is the most princely princess; no one embodies a princess more than she does"—words with little meaning, yet impossible to forget.

Fardak was delighted to be of assistance—it was a chance to show off before Lumera! That same day, he spread word that Princess Raedina's tribe and his own were closely connected. From childhood, he had known of her intelligence, her admiration for the superior culture of the Sultan, and her diligent study of etiquette... He emphasized that, overall, Princess Raedina was a jewel second only to his own concubine, Lumera.

Jawad began promoting the princess's riches in the Capital. To make the tale credible, he described her traveling expenses, the value of her veils, and her admirable skill in bookkeeping... In his account, the princess was nearly as impeccable as Arumina—wise, beautiful, kind, gentle, courteous, clever, and meticulous with accounts. It seemed that Jawad had a distinct fondness for anyone who could manage accounts properly.

[s3.name] shared stories among the nobility of the princess's gentle heart and keen insight—how even brief encounters with her brought a refreshing warmth, and how her presence exuded an effortless grace... These tales left many nobles dreaming of meeting her in person.

[s4.name] spread tales of the princess's refined tastes—her rare incense, her exotic carriage horses, and garments made with nearly forgotten techniques from her homeland... Half the noblewomen in the Capital were captivated, further boosting Princess Raedina's fame and the intrigue surrounding her.

5008206.title: Master of Intrigue
strings: Master of Intrigue

Princess Raedina is beginning to make her presence known in the Capital. Give her time, and she can skillfully steer public opinion and gather intelligence to address the vagrants' troubles. But she will still need your support.
The Princess must attend the ball in person.
Nobles Attending the Ball
The Challenge at the Ball
Supporters
The ball is held every three days; you can attend at any time.
Failing a challenge at the ball carries penalties.
You may send a noble to provide assistance.
Amid the undercurrents of the ball, can Raed successfully handle the skeptics?
Amid the undercurrents of the ball, can Raed successfully handle the rivals for attention?
Amid the undercurrents of the ball, can [s5.name] fend off admirers?
Amid the undercurrents of the ball, can Raed fend off admirers?
This is a contest of Sociability and Stealth.
This is a contest of Sociability and Charisma.
This is a contest of Combat and Charisma.
You need at least 5 Successes to overcome the challenge.
The Princess in the Mist
She was nearly conquering the city already.

She always arrived as night fell, just as the music and dance reached their peak, as if the entire world existed solely to welcome her.
Her voice carried effortlessly through the archways, through the haze of smoke, through the murmurs of servants, reaching the ears of everyone present.
Ah... the figure gliding into the ballroom draped in pearls and gossamer... her honeyed skin glowing, eyes sparkling like gemstones, fingers delicate, muscles sculpted to perfection... This—this is Princess Raedina!
She raised a finger to her lips in a delicate "shush." Even this simple gesture was breathtaking, her layered gold bracelets clinking softly with the movement. Every noble present felt as though she was looking directly at them, and as she twirled her silk scarves into the dance, she seemed to merge seamlessly with the celebration itself.

"Oh, forgive the trouble, I should have consulted you sooner...
You see, I've only just arrived in this city...
I do wish your master were as generous as my father, he would have made my stay comfortable, wouldn't he?"
Using words, glances, and subtle suggestions, she silently rearranged every pawn on the board, keeping rivals in check, preventing them from uniting against the vagrants, making them believe they were making way for the princess while actually clearing paths for the beggars. And when they thought they were shielding her, no one noticed the children hidden beneath her skirts.
She truly was a princess, more real than any pearl.
You hadn't managed all the details perfectly.
The ignorant became her stepping stones.
The princess became other's stepping stones.
A Duel
Twined in Grace

Of course, surprises could happen...
A fur trader whispered in the corner that he had visited that tribe, but had never heard of a noble Raedina.
Luckily, someone intervened before the rumor could spread, and Princess Raedina skillfully began discussing customs from her homeland, influential leaders, and even the archery skills of a few brothers. Who else could blend exotic culture and imperial etiquette so flawlessly? The young nobles were practically stripping off their attire to demonstrate their skills!

Of course, surprises can happen...
A fur trader whispered in the corner that he'd visited that tribe but had never heard of a noble Raedina. Besides, the style of her jewelry differed from what the locals wore. Most people didn't care—after all, a princess is meant to be admired for her looks! But those who truly held the power to decide paused, reconsidering their attitude toward Princess Raedina.

Of course, surprises can happen...
One prominent noble's daughter had come dressed to impress, hoping to outshine Princess Raedina at the ball... Yet, while they might have been evenly matched in beauty, our princess was well-versed in poetry and philosophy. She effortlessly steered the conversation into realms her rival could not follow... It was then that the truly talented and accomplished Princess Raedina finally made her name known throughout the Capital.

Of course, surprises can happen...
One prominent noble's daughter had come dressed to impress, hoping to outshine Princess Raedina at the ball... Unfortunately, although Raedina's beauty was nothing short of stunning, the rival had numerous admirers, forcing her to expend considerable effort dealing with their harassment and slander. These unsavory disputes disrupted the social engagements you had carefully planned.

Of course, surprises could happen...
A zealous young noble publicly proposed to Princess Raedina, putting her in an awkward position. At the banquet, he drew his sword and declared he would challenge any man bold enough to approach the princess...
Fortunately, the protector you arranged responded swiftly, disarming and humbling that noble without a drop of blood spilled.
This tale of skill and grace quickly spread throughout the city. Soon, invitations filled the guesthouse where Princess Raedina was staying, as everyone clamored for a glimpse of this legendary beauty.

Of course, surprises could happen...
A zealous young noble publicly proposed to Princess Raedina, putting her in an awkward position. At the banquet, he drew his sword and declared he would challenge any man bold enough to approach the princess...
Soon, a drunken brawl erupted, the hall was stained with blood, and the families demanded justice. Though many were likely intimidated by [player.name]'s reputation, most guests no longer dared invite Princess Raedina to their own gatherings.

Of course, surprises can happen...
A zealous young noble publicly proposed to Princess Raedina, putting her in an awkward position. He drew his sword at the ball, declaring he would challenge any man who dared approach the princess...
Fortunately, Princess Raedina calmed him with words as sweet and slow as honey. Only a few sharp-eyed onlookers noticed that, in a flash, she had already seized his weapon with lightning-quick hands. In the end, the sword was praised, everyone enjoyed the spectacle, no one lost face, and the noble's family later sent even greater gifts in return.

Of course, surprises can happen...
A zealous young noble publicly proposed to Princess Raedina, putting her in an awkward position. He drew his sword at the ball, declaring he would challenge any man who dared approach the princess...
Raedina was unable to prevent the farce, and the hall was stained with blood, and the noble's family vowed revenge—though many were likely intimidated by [player.name]'s reputation, most guests no longer dared invite Princess Raedina to their own gatherings.

5008207.title: Sparkling Presence
strings: Sparkling Presence

Princess Raedina quickly became the Capital's star! While many might still have reservations about the Lord [player.name], she was welcomed wherever she went—if handled with care, the benefits were practically endless. And of course, don't forget to quietly secure some advantages for the vagrants along the way.
The Princess must attend the ball in person.
Guests Attending the Ball
Those Who Came in Support
You can send someone to attent the ball.
The banquet is held every three days; you can attend at any time.
Certain characters may trigger special events during the banquet.
The rewards from attending vary depending on which guests are present.
The Moon Among Stars
Rising Reputation

People said Princess Raedina is the Capital's moonlight—only where she shines does the night feel gentle, filled with laughter and joy. She can even casually mention the difficulties faced by the vagrants, prompting others to compete in showing off their generosity and kindness on her behalf.

Is there anyone left in the Capital who doesn't know Princess Raedina? You have to admit, secretly pulling the strings behind the scenes while enjoying the benefits feels pretty satisfying... yet somehow, a tiny unease always lingers. Before you knew it, Raedina was already offering a toast to the most esteemed favorite, [player.name]. Better just enjoyed the moment.
Someone else has composed a poem in honor of the princess.
A Mountain of Gifts
Princess Raedina Sets the Trends
She is the symbol of the Purists' faith spreading far and wide.
This... turns out to be profitable.
An Obscure Disease
A Place Forgotten by the Gods
Capable Servants
So long as they are not test subjects.
Where Flowers Bloom

Moonlight, pearls, eagle feathers, the prairie wind, an agate hilt, silver scimitars... after hearing these extravagant metaphors and seeing Raedina casually picking at her toes or burping, it's all rather amusing.
Yet each gilded word only elevated the princess further.

You eye the beautifully wrapped boxes brought by admirers, eager for the banquet to end so you can inspect them one by one. Hopefully, this time they bring something useful for Lord [player.name] rather than gaudy powders and rouge!
Whatever she wears, women buy. Whatever she dons as jewelry, those who don't follow are ridiculed. Merchants now pay Princess Raedina to accept their gifts... and, naturally, you take your cut.

The monks never imagined that a barbarian princess would be so well-versed in the teachings of the Purists. They treat Raedina as a treasure, eager to bless her at every public occasion... Alas, even if you pay them, they are sometimes reluctant to do the same for you. Ah, these chanting monks, such feeble minds they have.

Princess Raedina happened to mention that she took in a starving vagrant who, as it turned out, had been a renowned merchant. Literate and skilled in mathematics, he quickly brought order to her accounts and interests... People praised it as a blessing from the divine, while many merchants clearly took note of this story—among them, Mr. Jawad.

Princess Raedina happened to mention that she saw a beggar in the streets who seemed stricken by a dreadful disease... Though unintended, this drew the attention of the Court Physician, Samir. He pressed her for details, so much so that at the banquet he was deemed out of place. Perhaps later you may seize the chance to have him actually treat the vagrants.

Princess Raedina happened to mention that she saw a cursed soul near the slums. Why should such a radiant and generous city still hide such pitiful wretches untouched by the gods' brilliance? Sadly, the nobles felt no sympathy. Yet others—those practiced in handling curses—found their interest piqued...

Princess Raedina happened to mention that she saw a cursed soul near the slums. Why should such a radiant and generous city still hide such pitiful wretches untouched by the gods' brilliance? This time, the guests turned their eyes to Iman, who promptly declared that he would bring purity to the afflicted—well, surely our generous Lord [player.name] will also lend a hand?

Princess Raedina happened to mention that she had hired several vagrants as servants—clever and proper, evidently once in service to great nobles! Many noble ladies grew curious, though doubts remained—what if the vagrants were swindlers, thieves... or perhaps this foreign princess was simply naïve? At that moment, Maggie chimed in at just the right time: the Lord [player.name]'s household, too, had hired many such servants—anyone curious may see them at her tea party.

At the banquet, a woman mocked that Mahir's experiments had frightened away her workers. Princess Raedina took note of this and later asked you—could Mahir employ vagrants instead? After all, they have nothing to fear.

Nabhani bought a flower from a vagrant peddler and wore it proudly to the ball. Princess Raedina seized the moment to praise its variety and beauty, while Naibhani, in turn, extolled the flower girl's charm and lively spirit... In the end, he offered the flower to the princess and won a dance with her. Soon after, the custom of gifting flowers to noble ladies had become the latest fashion.

5008208.title: Jawad's Smile
strings: Jawad's Smile
Helping vagrants find employment is indeed a good thing...
Jawad will not rest easy entrusting the work to others.
Intelligence of Silver and above.
Plant sufficient intelligence, and Jawad will drive the vagrants to conduct surveys and accounting.
So long as he is pleased.

Jawad led literate vagrants to study how to record market intelligence and inventory. He patiently taught them how to list entries, calculate, and even forge accounts... "My lord says he cannot sleep at night without at least two sets of ledgers."
In the end, those best at sums, and willing to help him falsify accounts, became Jawad's confidants. The rest, armed with new skills, easily found work at other trading houses. Rarely had one seen Jawad treat others so kindly—it turns out our own poor arithmetic was the true reason.

5008209.title: The Court Physician's Diagnosis
strings: The Court Physician's Diagnosis
Since Samir is intrigued by the diseases among vagrants, why not spend some coin to have him treat them all? It may even be remembered as one of the Sultan's benevolent deeds.
Samir must personally attend.
It costs 8 Gold Coins.
You may use this chance to break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower, though it will cost twice the usual Gold Coins.
You must spend 8 Gold Coins. Extravagance Card requires 16 Gold Coins to be played.
Remember to thank the Sultan for his boundless grace.

Samir arrived at [player.name] Fortress. Behind him trailed four eunuchs carrying medicine chests and instruments. His opulent robe swept the ground, though thankfully the vagrants had already cleared away the dung heaps.
His head held high, the rare spectacles upon his nose spoke of his station. One eunuch stepped forward to announce, "The Sultan's court physician, Lord Samir, has arrived." People fell to their knees in unison—so sudden that even you and Samir were startled. It was the first time they had been so close to the Sultan! A man who had once treated the Sultan himself was now here to heal them! Whatever Samir commanded in treatment and hygiene, they obeyed without question. You fell into thought: you, too, were a courtier at the Sultan's side, with influence greater than any court physician. Yet why did these people not revere you the same way? Perhaps... because they had seen how Raed treated you, and instinctively drew the comparison. To them, a "courtier" was distant and abstract, while a "court physician" was near and tangible.
After the treatment, Samir arranged that in the future, the vagrants would provide certain corpses in exchange for medicine to save more lives, which seemed perfectly sound for both the living and the dead.
Sultan's Sugar Pills

Beyond ordinary remedies, Samir brought a golden casket. It looked even more out of place than he did in the vagrant camp... Inside lay precious medicines—tiny pills, each sealed with wax and stamped with the royal sigil. These epidemic cures had been procured from other court physicians at great cost. Normally, only noble children ever tasted them, for each pill granted a lifetime immunity to many diseases. They were so rare that even you could scarcely resist the temptation—you still remembered their sweetness well! Yet Samir forbade it, giving only one pill each to children of suitable age. Their parents bowed their heads feverishly, praising the Sultan's supreme grace...
Later, the Sultan himself asked whether all the sugar pills had gone to the vagrants—he longed to have another! Samir rolled his eyes and cast you a look that said, "You're hardly the only fool." Then, bowing low, he gently warned the Sultan that such medicine might make adults ill...

5008210.title: The Cultic God's Blessing
strings: The Cultic God's Blessing
Those who are homeless, nameless, and abandoned are all children of the Cultic God—so declared Badriyyah.
Badriyyah must attend personally.
It costs 8 Gold Coins.
You may use this chance to break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower, though it will cost twice the usual Gold Coins.
You must spend 8 Gold Coins. Extravagance Card requires 16 Gold Coins to be played.
Connect

Badriyyah's visit was lively; many vagrants already knew her and greeted her warmly. As she distributed potions, they eagerly assisted. "When you feel unwell, drink a vial, eat a hearty meal, and sleep it off. Sweat it all out!" Badriyyah instructed. "I can also mark you with sigils bestowed by the Cultic God, to ward off sickness." Food, rest, tattoos... these were all the poor could trust. The people obeyed, and a gifted few even dreamed of new gods at night.
Supernatural Event

That very night, several strong bulls and rams, as if guided by unseen hands, wandered into the vagrants' quarter. Uttering strange words, they leapt into the fire, becoming mountains of fragrant meat... Many claimed it was the Cultic God's promised feast in their dreams. Of course, you knew better. It was you who had paid for the livestock. Had it not been for the Priests of the Purist' vehement opposition, the Sultan would have had you to stage such a spectacle for him as well.

5008211.title: The Blessing of the Truth
strings: The Blessing of the Truth
The Immaculate Purity makes no distinction among humans, but beholds all suffering—so declared Iman.
Iman must attend personally.
It costs 8 Gold Coins.
You may use this chance to break an Extravagance Card of Bronze tier or lower, though it will cost twice the usual Gold Coins.
This, too, counts as a merit in spreading the True Faith.
You must spend 8 Gold Coins. Extravagance Card requires 16 Gold Coins to be played.
Blessing Descends

The scent of jasmine perfume washed over the floors of [player.name] Manor, making you wince at how much of your offerings must have gone to this rather than healing... Yet when the priests emerged amid the fragrance, the vagrants were moved to tears. They fell to their knees, crying out the name of the Purist. Many wept aloud. Once abandoned, humiliated, and injured, they now found themselves again the children of God. This spiritual solace perhaps outweighed even the incense and medicine the priests dispensed.
Without Imagination

As vagrants lined up for ointments and sacraments... golden dust rained from the sky, glittering, with the laughter of a girl.
The crowd erupted, tears flowing as they snatched the drifting foil—some ate it at once, others clutched it to their hearts, carrying it home to bless the sick...
Of course, this was proclaimed as the Purists' miracle. So when you told the Sultan that the gold leaf came from your own purse, not from the Purists, he was bitterly disappointed—he found your way of breaking cards utterly devoid of wonder.

5008212.title: Shrewd Servants
strings: Shrewd Servants
