Maggie's tea parties are always popular. Not only thanks to your influence, but also for the hostess's grace, beauty, and elegance. Now she plans to use her reputation to find work for the vagrants.
Maggie must personally arrange it all.
Intelligence of Silver and above.
A Staged Accident

The ladies reclined upon Maggie's heirloom carpets, enjoying fine meals and occasionally a hookah puff. They gossiped endlessly, passing judgment on one another's lives, while secretly eyeing every jewel and fabric upon each other. In the midst of the banquet, Maggie spilled her pomegranate tea. Before anyone could gasp, a vagrant girl hurried forth, kneeling to blot the wet hem with a handkerchief. Another vagrant servant immediately brought three dresses for Maggie to choose from. As Maggie rose, yet another servant had already set up a curtain for her to change behind. The sequence was flawless, leaving the other ladies in awe. By the time Maggie reappeared, at least three ladies had already spoken privately with the vagrant girls. Soon, these girls entered respectable households as maids. One introduction led to another, and before long, many more quick-witted girls had jobs.

5008213.title: Reverse Engineering
strings: Reverse Engineering
Mahir discovered that some vagrants were skilled artisans who grasped her design thinking. She decided to give them a chance.
Mahir must supervise personally.
Let the vagrant artisans attempt a replica.
Spend 10 Gold Coins as funding.
Replicate one of Mahir's great inventions.
Only what can be repeated deserves the name of science

Though Mahir had explained every principle of [s2.name] as best she could, she watched the vagrant artisans with the nerves of a husband awaiting childbirth.
More than once she wanted to warn them—avoid an explosion here, a blast there—though she herself often caused them... In the end, the result was all but perfect. It looked a touch different from the original, but worked exactly the same!
Despite Mahir's poor reputation among nobles, she still convinced the city's artisans to begin taking in the vagrants.

5008214.title: Flowers and Swords
strings: Flowers and Swords
Nabhani volunteered to help the vagrants sell flowers... which mostly meant flirting with them in the streets—so that no one else would dare to truly harass them.
Nabhani must attend personally.
Have an ally with Charisma 5 or above help keep order.

Nabhani had become strangely industrious. He threw himself into "work", striding through the market in armor and trappings, eyeing the vendors one by one. In time, he marked out several prime patches of ground. Given his renown, charm, and place among the Honor Guard, no merchants dared complain, even though he took the best spots... "Let the girls sell flowers here!" He told you with a wide grin. "I'll make sure to visit often!"
...Well, so be it. At least some vagrants gained steady jobs. They sold not only flowers, but smiles, herbs, and lore of the wilds. After a while, even without Nabhani, both the young flower-sellers and the elder herbalists had found their place in the market.

5008215.title: The Sultan's Summons
strings: The Sultan's Summons
Princess Raedina was to face the Sultan. The city buzzed—everyone knew this might be the last time she was spoken of in public.
The Sultan Demands to See Her
Those Who Can Help Dress Raed
A noble companion whose Charisma surpasses Raed's.
You must go there yourself
A makeup artist can craft a convincing flaw for Princess Raedina.
The higher Raed's Stealth, the better she can conceal herself.
The higher Raed's Charisma, the more she stands out.
The higher her companions' Charisma, the better.
The higher your Charisma and Stealth, the less suspicion the Sultan will harbour.
The Sultan's gaze sweeps over Raed from head to toe...
Can you withstand the Sultan's questioning?
[s3.name] begins the performance...
Raed's Stealth minus Charisma determines your full dice count.
Your Charisma and Stealth determine your full dice count.
[s3.name]'s Charisma minus Raed's Charisma, plus Raed's Stealth, determines your full dice count.
3 Successes will keep the Sultan's eyes off her.
You need 5 Successes to get through.
You need at least 5 Successes to win.
Companions' Charisma must exceed Raed's.
Ignoring the Sultan's summons? Woman, you have truly caught his eye... The Sultan's soldiers seized Raed alive in your residence and carried her, and your head, into the palace.

When the Sultan's eunuchs arrived with a palanquin for Princess Raedina, your carriage burst from the corner... The title of minister still carried some weight; you declared you would personally escort the noble princess to the Supreme Sultan—on diplomatic grounds.
Good. You bought yourself some time.
Make Him Feel Defiled and Uncomfortable
No Exotic Allure
The Reverse Approach
A Calculated Comparison
No Time for Such Nonsense
A Hero's Gallantry
Perhaps a cat will do?
If the Sultan has any humanity...
Already Courageous Enough
First Sight
The Princess Smiled
Where is the Princess?
Barbarian Indeed
What Nonsense
So, [player.name], has this woman come under your wing?
What is your relation to Princess Raedina?
I'll Let Your Usual Tricks Slide...
Just Like Your Daughter...
He Saw Through Your Ploy
So Your Little Schemes Do Have Their Uses
A Fine Cat, Truly
Who, besides [player.name], is more amusing than the Princess?
[s3.gender] Successfully Misled the Sultan
She Stirred the Sultan's Cruel Desire

Raed's tale of porcelain veneers gave Malkina ideas... Using shells and soot, she crafted a more convincing set of false teeth, so that the story of Princess Raedina's rotten mouth, blamed on the crude customs of her homeland, would sound more believable.
Raed complained of the stench and the sour taste. "That's the point! Otherwise, something fouler, filthier will be coming!" said Malkina. The princess shut her mouth at once.

Maggie thought it over and advised Princess Raedina to dress like a model noblewoman of the capital, in full conformity with Purist etiquette. A Sultan longing for "exotic flavors" would surely be disappointed.
You set to work. Thankfully, Maggie had ample gowns and accessories to replace Raedina's flamboyant attire. A touch of dark foundation and lip color... now she looked like a lady bound for prayer—lost among the crowd.

After hearing the gist, Shama began to comb Raedina's hair. "What's in vogue is Zazie's wavy length with an enormous golden crown... so we'll go for something dull—a simple knot.
And the dress, too little fabric reads coy, too much reads wanton. We'll bare the least alluring parts, your arms—oh, so muscular! The Sultan won't like that. He prefers soft, delicate ones that look ready to snap. So, arms exposed. And a bit of waist—yes... much better." Raedina yielded meekly, letting Shama fuss over her without a word. You watched as the charming, radiant princess was, with just a few deft touches, transformed into someone most men would overlook... In the end, everyone was all quite pleased with the result.

Jenna prepared a full ensemble for Princess Raedina—basically a cheap imitation of the golden finery worn by Zazie. The effect was perfect: anyone who saw the saw Princess Raedina would instantly think of the peerless Zazie... and then wonder, why choose an inferior imitator when the true beauty is still alive? With luck, the trick would confound the Sultan.
If we keep the Sultan waiting, we might not even get a word in! Into the carriage—now!

On the way to the palace, Nabhani lavished Princess Raedina with praise, vowing that such a "flower of the mountain", so noble and pure, would never be left to wither in the court. Raedina wept right on cue, responded with perfect restraint, and let a soft, lingering affection slip through—until Nabhani was thoroughly besotted. "When the time comes, you mustn't be too enchanting. Say nothing, do nothing, just leave it to me. I... uh... with [player.name], will find a way to make the Sultan lose interest in you!"
Only then did you recall that Nabhani had never seen Raed's real face... Poor fool—let the play go on!

Lady Becky was placed in Princess Raedina's arms. You stepped back and watched: she purred, yawned, scratched her ear. Raedina looked like a piece of furniture that came with the cat. With such a kitten on her lap, who would still harbor lust? "Will this really work?" Raedina asked, stroking the cat. "Am I truly less alluring than a cat...?" You had no idea how to comfort her... In the end, you simply told her to hold the cat tight, and together you set off for the palace.

Maggie is your wife; surely, however "free-spirited" the Sultan may be, he would not seize a minister's lawful spouse... surely.
Maggie dressed with care, bathed in rose balm, and painted herself unlike her usual style; she emphasized those limpid eyes and parted her hair into several strands, each adorned with a different ornament. She went over with Raedina what to say, and what not to say, before the Sultan; then she took Raedina by the hand and came to you. "If the worst happens—what Raedina fears—my husband, you must protect us both." Your head throbbed, yet her plea was fair. You gritted your teeth and swore that if the strategy of having Maggie accompany Raedina failed and the Sultan still wanted Raedina, you would find a way.
And so, the three of you set out for the palace.
Though you and [s3.name] had yet to devise an effective plan, having someone willing to face the Sultan alongside her gave Raedina a measure of courage...

The Sultan awaited you.
By the harem fountain, he reclined on a couch of marble and ebony, two slave girls fanning him. He toyed idly with his dagger—you knew that bored look; it usually birthed cruelty... Raedina kept her gaze lowered as she walked between you, playing the rustic overawed by majesty—small, tremulous beneath a sovereign's gaze.
Perhaps it was luck, or perhaps her act truly worked; at the very least, the Sultan allowed you to approach without impropriety.

The Sultan awaited you.
By the harem fountain, he reclined on a couch of marble and ebony, two slave girls fanning him. He toyed idly with his dagger—you knew that bored look; it usually birthed cruelty... As he drew breath to speak, Princess Raedina forced a very nervous, very genuine smile—the ruined teeth shattered his prepared opening.

The Sultan awaited you.
By the harem fountain, he reclined on a couch of marble and ebony, two slave girls fanning him. He toyed idly with his dagger—you knew that bored look; it usually birthed cruelty... After staring for quite some time, he realized that the "ordinary local woman" among you was Princess Raedina... and his disappointment was plain to see.

The Sultan awaied you.
By the harem fountain, he reclined on a couch of marble and ebony, two slave girls fanning him. He toyed idly with his dagger—you knew that bored look; it usually birthed cruelty... Princess Raedina was hardly as beautiful as the rumors claimed—unless, unbeknownst to him, the capital had begun to prize women with chiseled abs?

The Sultan awaited you.
By the harem fountain, he reclined on a couch of marble and ebony, two slave girls fanning him. He toyed idly with his dagger—you knew that bored look; it usually birthed cruelty... In a blink he thought he saw a coarser, bulkier Zazie. Such clumsy pandering to his tastes only spoiled his mood.

You prostrated yourself, first apologizing for failing to report in time; then introducing Raedina's origins and background. Finally, you explained your caution: as the Sultan's minister, you were duty-bound to ward off every possible harm. What if she were an assassin? What if she carried disease? What could be more vital than the vigor and health of our radiant sun? Only recently had you confirmed the lady posed no danger. In the meantime, some irresponsible souls must have embroidered tales to the Sultan... They simply lacked your prudence—and your loyalty. Amused, the Sultan waved you up—enough groveling; it must be tiring.
Now, let Princess Raedina approach. The Sultan commanded.

You prostrated yourself, first apologizing for failing to report in time; then introducing Raedina's origins and background, but the Sultan cut you off coldly. He already knew you had pocketed every noble lady who came to the capital before he did. "You have chilled my heart..."
Enough. Stop groveling. Now, let Princess Raedina approach.

"Nabhani—what business have you here?" His gaze shifted to the Iron Guard. "I summoned a woman... why do two men appear before me?" Nabhani was struck dumb with nerves... The Sultan laughed. Whether Princess Raedina was plain or bewitching mattered little—he could wring amusement from you either way. The more you fretted, the greater his delight.
He snapped his fingers; eunuchs closed in, driving Raedina toward the depths of the harem garden. Laughing, he rose to sample his prey, while you remained kneeling, enduring the wild, feverish glances he cast back at you from time to time.

You gave the signal; Princess Raedina set Lady Becky on the Sultan's knee. "It seems Lady Becky likes Princess Raedina. She has an eye for people, doesn't she, [player.name]?"
The Sultan stroked the cat for a while, and just when you thought you'd muddled through... "Let Raedina enter the palace to serve. Few concubines win Lady Becky's favor. That way, she'll grace the court more often. Isn't that right, Lady Becky?"
He snapped his fingers; a cluster of eunuchs closed in, herding and forcing Raedina toward the depths of the harem garden. You remained kneeling, motionless, while Lady Becky mewed and even snagged the Sultan's robe—he did not care.

Maggie's poise, grace, and beauty were no secret in the capital, nor was the steadiness of your marriage. She set a hand on Raedina's shoulder and gently urged her, "Don't be nervous. Let our king see you." The scene was like a mother proudly presenting her daughter to the neighbors—hardly one to stir desire in any normal man. But our Sultan is no normal man. Malice kindled in his eyes. "Very well. Let me see what Lady Maggie has taught you." At his signal, a cluster of eunuchs closed in, herding and forcing Raedina toward the depths of the harem garden. Laughing, he rose to sample his prey, while you remained kneeling, enduring the wild, feverish glances he cast back at you from time to time.

[s3.name] tried to dress plainly as a court attendant, hoping to throw Princess Raedina's ordinariness into relief. Yet the more she tried to hide behind you, the more the Sultan's interest grew... "So, you would keep me from drawing near this princess." He sneered and snapped his fingers; at his signal, a cluster of eunuchs closed in, herding and forcing Raedina toward the depths of the harem garden. Laughing, he rose to sample his prey, while you remained kneeling, enduring the wild, feverish glances he cast back at you from time to time.

"Nabhani—what business have you here?" His gaze shifted to the Iron Guard. "I summoned a woman... why do two men appear before me?" "To guard you at your side, my king. Who knows what might happen?" Nabhani grinned, though you knew he was taut as a bowstring inside. "And the city has beauties aplenty of late—not just this one. I was hoping to tell you about a certain remarkably plump courtesan... Don't laugh! I wager you've never tasted the like."
That quick-witted rogue! The contrast piqued the Sultan at once; he and Nabhani spent a long while talking about courtesan, leaving you—and the foreign princess—set aside, brought up now and then for their jests and comparisons... Such humiliations, it seemed, pleased him.
At last, a eunuch hurried in to whisper in the Sultan's ear; with a wave, the farcical audience ended. Only then did you see Nabhani's back, drenched in cold sweat.

Lady Becky sprang onto the Sultan's knee. "You insolent puffball." He lifted her by the scruff; she windmilled her furry paws in protest. "You've raised her well, [player.name]. I doubt there is anyone in this realm she fears." You bowed, murmuring denials, while thinking: Come on, Lady Becky—purr, roll, do every cute trick—we're counting on you... Stroking Becky, the Sultan even spoke with you for a while about affairs of state—perhaps the first time in ages he had discussed governance with you. At last you felt like a true minister!
Then a eunuch rushed in to whisper; he waved, tossing Becky back into your arms, and the farce was over.

Maggie's poise, grace, and beauty were no secret in the capital, nor was the steadiness of your marriage—though of late that bond had been sorely challenged, much to the Sultan's amusement.
In full regalia, Maggie deliberately scolded Princess Raedina like a spiteful matron, telling her to "show yourself properly to the Sultan." The shrewd monarch caught the subtle note at once. What could make Maggie resent the princess? How interesting. Best let [player.name] untangle this himself... He gave the shrinking Raedina a perfunctory nod, then, feigning casualness, questioned you about the stories of the Carnality Card. Maggie's face went iron-dark, her nails digging into her palms, as you solemnly reported to the Sultan yet again...
At last, a eunuch hurried in to whisper; the Sultan waved, smiling as he dismissed Maggie and the princess, and the farce was over.

Princess Raedina deliberately tried to become the center of attention by sheer presence—yet under your careful staging she was instantly outshone by the resplendent [s3.name]. The Sultan took her for another rustic angling to crash the noble circle, tossed off a few perfunctory words, and left... When his figure vanished, both [s3.name] and Raedina slumped to the floor, as if all their energy had been drained.

The Sultan awaited you.
By the harem fountain, he reclined on a couch of marble and ebony, two slave girls fanning him. He toyed idly with his dagger—you knew that bored look; it usually birthed cruelty...
Before you could speak—or even pay homage—he strode over and seized Raedina's face, twisting her features with brute strength as he inspected her like livestock—teeth, lips, tongue. "[player.name], is this the new toy you've hidden in the city? Let me have her—you don't mind, do you?" Laughing, he hauled Raedina up and hurled her to a squad of brawny eunuchs. "Make her presentable... As for you, wait here."
You knelt there until deep into the night, when a eunuch finally ordered you home... with no word of Raedina.

5008216.title: Who Is She?
strings: Who Is She?
Polished speech, perfect makeup. Even a swindler would struggle to mimic nobility so convincingly... but what is her connection to Raed?
There must be an interesting story behind her.
Send a noble to probe the court archives. Requires Influence 15 or higher.
Send a commoner to the Dark Alley for clues. Requires Notoriety 8 or higher.
Send someone to the courtesans' quarter to gather information, or spend 5 Gold Coins to buy intelligence.
You must pursue three channels of inquiry at once.
Her Secret

When you first met Raed, the first thing you noticed was her ruined teeth; children from the slums often have poor dentition. But the courteous bow as she left, the appraising glance when she entered your residence, the calm way she trod the velvet carpet—most slaves and commoners balk at stepping on such expense their first time. Who is she, really? Why hide her origins? And this deliberately savage, coarse demeanor—could it be a disguise as well?
A Dispute of Inheritance
Dark Alley Inquiries
Squandering Beauty

A young lady of good birth who hides herself, alters her looks, and shuns the nobility—why? Prompted by a hint, you searched the files on noble inheritance disputes... and eventually turned your attention to the Sultan.
In a dust-caked tower of parchments, the conquests of the current Supreme Sultan's father were recorded in detail... You skimmed, wondering how it might connect to Raed, until a passage seized your attention. When the palace gate fell, the queen of the fallen kingdom fled through a hidden passage; but one noble lady-in-waiting betrayed her, revealing her escape route to the Sultan's army. Thus favored, the traitor became a consort in the new court—climbing to a golden bed over her mistress's corpse. More chilling still was her ultimate fate... When the present Sultan ascended the throne, he inherited all his father's women. Those too old to be of use were simply executed. "Afterwards, the Sultan struck off the heads of these women's children as well, tallying them by night. Some claim the count did not match the number of princes and princesses registered; though there is no evidence and the story is likely a rumor." You held the brittle, yellowed scrolls for a long time. Beyond a sigh, there was nothing you could do.

You sounded out a few familiar street toughs about the vagrants and Raed; they had plenty of tales to tell. The vagrants did not act violently on their own; they "helped" wherever nedded in exchange for payment. Some hardly looked like vagrants at all—literate, well-mannered, able to play instruments, with soft, uncalloused skin. Raed gathered them from the streets and sent them across the city. Their earnings were pooled; when wronged, they retaliated together. Each life was as fragile as a thin hemp strand—but Raed twisted these strands into a rope strong enough to fight fate.
They also mentioned something odd: the vagrants knew a truly elegant lady, noble as a princess, who had on more than one occasion appeared from nowhere to rescue them when cornered by nobles.

To inquire after a beauty, the best source was Nabhani. Of course he knew—a mysterious lady who had stood up for vagrants... He had even helped them thrash a bribery-demanding guard because of her! What? That woman might be Raed in disguise? Nabhani peered at Raed's face from the shadows...
"I see it! She smeared clay on the cheekbones to look sturdier and dirtier, and tousled her hair on purpose. And under the eyes... but the most crucial part—her teeth! She actually fitted herself with fake rotten teeth! How did she even do that? Gods—I spent days just trying to get her to smile once!"

To inquire after a lower-born woman, the best place is the House of Delights. Madam Buthayna knew Raed well enough. The girl seemed to come from nowhere. And at first, she had a noble air, with great beauty. Buthayna wanted her to work there. But the moment Buthayna asked, Raed flatly refused. After that, Raed made herself look ugly and drew close to the vagrants. "You know this: a beauty needs fine teeth to smile properly, to charm men for money properly... But she stuck things—thin ceramic slivers begged from potters—on her teeth, making them look like a natural set of dog fangs! Hah, she's wasting her looks. If she'd listened to me, she'd have been draped in gold by now, with money to burn!"
She cursed Raed viciously, while deftly sounding out whether [s4.name] might return to work... Profit guaranteed!

To inquire after a lower-born woman, the best place is the House of Delights. Madam Buthayna knew Raed well enough: the girl seemed to come from nowhere, and at first she had a noble air, with great beauty; Buthayna wanted her to work there. But the moment Buthayna asked, Raed flatly refused. After that, Raed made herself look ugly and drew close to the vagrants. "You know this: a beauty needs fine teeth to smile properly, to charm men for money properly... But she stuck things—thin ceramic slivers begged from potters—on her teeth, making them look like a natural set of dog fangs! Hah, she's wasting her looks. If she'd listened to me, she'd have been draped in gold by now, with money to burn!"
She cursed Raed viciously, while deftly lifting a sum of coins from your purse.

5008217.title: A Daughtet's Tale
strings: A Daughtet's Tale

This dagger bears the exclusive royal pattern—and the name of Gosama. It marks her as a woman of the Sultan, a token of her fidelity to him... Judging by the sigil, it belonged to the previous Sultan.
She was truly the former Consort's daughter? Then She's the Sultan's Sister?!
Perhaps you can show it to someone.
Some may be interested in this dagger.
You could also present it to the Sultan.
Perhaps Raed would be willing to share her story.
Be careful—this is not something to share lightly with anyone.
When you mentioned it, the Roaming Swordsman gave off a hint of killing intent... Do you want to show it to him?
Raed's Story
Her Tears
A Son's Power
A Betrayal Unproclaimed

What else would you ask? Why have I fallen this far? What do I plan to do next? Do you realize how condescending those questions sound? For those who roll in the dirt, the past moment hardly matters, and the next matters even less. What matters is the present—only the present. The past is a curse, the future a burden; all we can do is seize what little joy we can, here and now. Perhaps, when I have a moment to breathe, I'll think about the rest. Of course, this silver tongue of mine—these turns of phrase that pique your curiosity—also come from that old tale...
Yes. I am the daughter of Concubine Gosama. The favor she earned by betraying Concubine Mekana lasted only a few times. In our fallen kingdom, there had been but one consort; she never learned the intrigues needed to hold a king's love. The new Sultan's harem, however, was lavish—stocked from courtesans to princesses. Still, my mother had a bit of luck: by the time she conceived me, the Sultan already had several offspring. So this child, me, was spared the potion and the knife. And since I was a girl, he hardly took notice. To him, daughters were gifts yet to be given... My mother despaired over my future. She was forever reciting the rules of a proper lady: a lady must do this, must not do that. Scrub your teeth thrice a day with bark to keep them white; fix the hair at your temples with warm water and resin, and turn your head slowly so the strand's shadow falls just right upon your cheek; reveal just enough skin—the waist first, then the neck, then the breast—but never the ankles. Never. Strange, isn't it? She's been dead for years, and I can still recite every word. I forced myself to remember, because it made her happy. My mother was rarely happy... Truly, had she fled with Mekana and lived, she would have been far happier than she ever was beside the Sultan. Even if that meant I would never have been born—I would still... ahem.
When the Supreme Sultan began slaughtering his father's women and their children, some old eunuchs smuggled me out. They hated my mother, for they remembered how good Concubine Mekana had been. But they could not bear to watch me die. I had been raised in the fallen kingdom's rites—the last trace of a land they mourned. So they found a dead child beyond the walls, swapped her for me, and hid me in a rubbish cart out of the palace. They did it before my mother's eyes on purpose. They thought saving me while leaving her to die was a cruel sort of vengeance—but she wept thanks and praised them by the names of stars. In the end, everyone was crying. It was the day I shed more tears than at any moment in my life. I did have some property—a small residence and a few loyal relics of the former court who wished to care for me... but I refused to grow up alone in shadows. I abandoned it all to live among those who needed me. Imagining what it would be to be a prostitute's child... or a child born to no one, I made myself "Raed." I have been quite happy these years. Being a vagrant is freer than being a princess.
You know the rest—and I think you've heard enough street stories. That's all. I'm tired.

What else would you ask? Why I've fallen this far? What I plan to do next? Do you realize how condescending those questions sound? For those who roll in the dirt, the past moment hardly matters, and the next matters even less. What matters is the present—only the present. The past is a curse, the future a burden; all we can do is seize what little joy we can, here and now. Perhaps, when I have a moment to breathe, I'll think about the rest.
Here Raed wore a pitiable expression, tears glistening, lending extra weight to her words. Perhaps she had been trained once to gull men so. Yet behind the tears was a numb gaze that said: true or not, you will never reach her inner world.

You told Sirshana all of Raed's story. His mother was entangled in it; you felt he had the right to know. He remained silent for a long time, then bowed to you, deeply.
You said nothing more, and parted.

A Roaming Swordsman happened to hear you mention Consort Gosama, and the mercenary showed startling interest...
After he tried to steal the token by night, you resigned yourself to telling him Raed's tale. Perhaps that was a mistake. He seemed to grasp much at once—and left your residence without a word.

5008218.title: Death Match
strings: Death Match
In a hidden corner of the city, a silent death duel took place. All you know of it is what the survivor later told you.
The Traitor's Daughter Shall Face the Final Trial
He Came To Avenge His Mother
You can no longer stop the combat.
They will not rest until one lies dead.
Raed's dice count for Combat and Physique is affected by the Roaming Swordsman's corresponding attributes.
Raed needs at least 1 Success to defeat the Roaming Swordsman.
The Merest Revenge
A Revenge Unworthy of Trumpet
The End of It All
A Beast From The Past

Sirshana came to you with blood still fresh upon his blade... "I honored her. In the end she died as a warrior... not as a princess, not as a traitor's child, but as a warrior."He tucked the broken blade away. "That is a good thing. One day I wish to die as a warrior too, not as a prince—but not yet. For now, at least I have done a little for my mother... Such a tiny revenge, and yet so much warrior blood spilled for it! At least I no longer have to fear seeing her tears in my dreams." He bowed with a prince's courtesy and left without another word.

When the Roaming Swordsman returned, with blood still freash upon his blade... You pressed him, but he answered listlessly, dodging your questions. "I thought the taste of revenge would be sweeter. It was... dull."
He begged you not to ask further, saying only that Raed died as a warrior—in a fair and willing combat, and with honor.

Raed returned to you alive, soaked in blood, and—almost savoring it, recounted every detail of the fight... Everything between the traitor's daughter and the orphan of the consort ended here. She did not reproach you; on the contrary, she approved of what you did.
"We fought to the death as warriors—not as prince and princess, but warriors," she said, nodding. "We are both satisfied. Truly, I do not want to be a princess, and he did not wish to be a prince. So I suppose... dying in such a fight would have suited him." She had the vagrants lay Sirshana to rest, and the grave's location was revealed anonymously to the remnants of the fallen kingdom.

Raed came back alive, drenched in blood—mostly the blood of that maddened mercenary swordsman.
When she realized you knew nothing of what happened, she stopped giving details. "Let him die as a mercenary—a man without a name. As for me, do not worry. The past still lunges at me now and then... I've grown used to it."

5008219.title: Bloodshed and Passion
strings: Bloodshed and Passion
That night, deep and still, Raed came again... Blood clung unwashed in her hair, yet she gave off a scent more potent than blood, stronger than the tang of the vagrant camps...
Only tonight, she burns with passion.
Only tonight, you may return her passion.
Your calm and surprise quenched the fire in her eyes. Well—be grateful she is not yet used to such passions; she will not let them burn out of control like her brother would have.
Perfectly normal—your brother's the same

Her eyes burned red, as if lit by flame. She pressed you into a corner, hot breath on your face; one hand covered your eyes, the other seized your arms—she would take the lead in this.
You felt her body turn soft, yet iron-strong and fierce. You tasted blood on her lips—salty, warm... sensations that intoxicated and soothed, almost making you forget the bitter game you were in... For a heartbeat you wanted to go with her forever, no matter what road she walked.
Fortunately—or unfortunately—the frenzy that fueled this passion was not so strong in her veins. When at last you both collapsed on the carpet, spent, the madness and its temptations dissolved like a fading dream. Embarrassed, she slid away through the tangle of sweat, blood and limbs, putting distance between you. "I'm... not as I ought to be. Bloodshed stirs passion in me... It will not happen again!" Your next attempt at comfort only angered her completely, and from that day on she kept far more distance from you.

5008220.title: The Joy of Kinslaying
strings: The Joy of Kinslaying
Today the Sultan celebrates—for he may put another kinsman to the sword. Ah, if only we had found her when we were breaking that card!
Raed
Full Regalia

When Raedina's head fell, a golden crown was placed upon it, her face painted with a princess's radiance, and laid in the royal tomb—there to wait, to witness, with the blood of kings and queens, the history forged by the one true king...

5008221.title: Lost Lineage
strings: Lost Lineage
Arzuna, the stunning dancer, comes straight to your doorstep upon learning you are caught in this cruel game. She has something to say.
Arzuna
You must talk to her yourself.
You can handle this together with Maggie.
You ignored Arzuna, and she said nothing in response.
Meeting Arzuna in Private
A Very Formal Conversation

The servants, with curious eyes, led the beautiful lady into your parlor. She remained in her dancer's attire—bells jingling at her wrists and ankles, hair swept high, her delicate face finely made up.
Seated, she began at once to praise your servants' poise as proper to a courtier's name. When the servants retreated at your signal, she leaned closer and whispered with a soft smile, "You must have your doubts about me, Lord [player.name]. I am Arzuna, and I suppose I should call you 'brother'... As you might not know, I was born of your father's concubine."
She produced your father's letters, tokens, and proofs, along with documents signed by a local magistrate attesting to her lineage... Clearly, she had come prepared. After you examined them, she carefully tucked everything back into her arms and smiled. "Be at ease. I stand on your side."
"I know being a courtier's sister promises no certain wealth or glory, but being of use to you might grant me what I desire. So, when I learned you were caught in the Sultan's game, I came straight away."
You were at a loss for words. She edged a little closer, letting a heady scent drift toward you. One downward glance revealed her radiant, enchanting face. "Besides... I've long looked up to you, my brother."
Her gaze was steady, intimate, almost suffused with a hidden longing. Yet she pulled back, as if aware of propriety, and rose with a graceful curtsy. The breeze from outside carried away her subtle fragrance. Alone in the room, you felt a quiet, fleeting pang of regret.

Out of respect for the lady—and for the mistress of the house—you and Maggie went into the parlor together. The servants ushered in Arzuna, still dressed as a dancer—bells jingling at her wrists and ankles, hair swept high, her delicate face finely made up. A flicker of surprise crossed her face at the sight of Maggie, then vanished almost immediately. With a proper curtsy to both of you, she smiled and spoke, "You must have doubts about me, Lady Maggie, Lord [player.name]..." Her gaze alighted on you, light as a butterfly. "I am Arzuna, and I suppose I should call you 'brother'... As you might not know, I was born of your father's concubine."
She produced your father's letters, tokens, and proofs, along with documents signed by a local magistrate attesting to her lineage... Clearly, she had come prepared.
You cast a nervous glance at Maggie's slightly furrowed brow, thinking of how sensitive it always was for a concubine's daughter in aristocratic circles, and how this might stir gossip in a house with a childless mistress. Yet there was no trace of anger in Maggie's eyes, only a reassuring smile that made your spine straighten: it was not your fault—you were not your father.
Maggie read through the papers swiftly, set them aside, and sighed at Arzuna. "You must have had a hard life," she said, her tone not pitying but broadly accepting. "Take care of her, my dear—she is one of the few of your own blood."
You promised firmly, while Arzuna stared at Maggie for a long moment before forcing a small, vivid smile. "Rest assured, Lady Maggie—I am here to aid your husband."
"I know you are not short of followers, but I have my own strengths. So, when I learned you were caught in the Sultan's game, I came straight away."
You praised her efficiency—after all, she had helped you the day before when you were most short-handed—and Maggie nodded approvingly. Arzuna flushed and soon excused herself.
Once Arzuna left, Maggie sipped her pomegranate tea thoughtfully before turning to you. "Do men really need concubines so much, my dear? What do you think?"
Ah... you knew this wouldn't be so easily forgotten!

5008222.title: Twisted Branch
strings: Twisted Branch
A romantic night with Arzuna lets you break a Carnality Card. And sure enough, Maggie would catch wind of it in no time.
Maggie is outraged by what you've done.
You must soothe her yourself.
You might want to promise Maggie that you will keep your distance from someone.
Time to put your skills to the test.
The pool of dice determined by your Sociability and Charisma is affected by Maggie's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 5 Success to soothe Maggie a bit.

To lie with other women in your own home is a grave disrespect to Maggie, your rightful lady—it is a great sin. To feel no remorse afterward, nor even spare her a moment of explanation, is the worst sin of all.
Apologize Before the Storm
You failed

You beat Maggie to the punch with a sincere apology, explaining it was a desperate choice, a trick of that game, never your intent. You swore to the sky you'd never let it happen again. Maggie said nothing, only watched, then let out a long, weary sigh.
"I don't want to say much," she murmured, exhaustion heavy in her voice. You leaned in with care, massaging her temples as she continued, "I just need you to know... that girl, your sister Arzuna... she's not as simple as she seems."
Her words pulled memories to mind: Arzuna's flawless dancing, skillful charm, and the way she gazed at you—her "brother."
"I'm not speaking out of jealousy, my dear. Her eyes on you... It's more than desire, certainly not mere kinship! Truth be told..." She hesitated, then let it out. "It feels like she hates you!"
Maggie grabbed your arm, locking eyes with you. "Promise me, my husband. Promise me you'll have no more intimacy with her. Let me be blunt—don't sleep with her again. There's something dark in her heart! I can feel it!"

You rushed to apologize before Maggie could reproach you, but she stopped you. "Enough, my dear. I wasn't looking to hear that." Exhaustion was heavy in her voice. "I just need you to know... that girl, your sister Arzuna... she's not as simple as she seems."
Her words pulled memories to mind: Arzuna's flawless dancing, skillful charm, and the way she gazed at you—her "brother."
"I'm not speaking out of jealousy, my dear. Her eyes on you... It's more than desire, certainly not mere kinship! Truth be told..." She held your eyes without hesitation. "It feels like she hates you!"
"Promise me, my husband. Promise me you'll have no more intimacy with her. Let me be blunt—don't sleep with her again. There's something dark in her heart! I can feel it!"
You Are Overthinking
I Promise You

"Haha, what harm could she do? A dancer, an illiterate little commoner, an illegitimate child of the third woman—she ought to be grateful if I don't drain her dry!" Of course, you wouldn't do that... She could still be useful, and after all, she was family.
You tried to paint Arzuna in a scornful tone to ease Maggie's mind, but Maggie only fixed you with a quiet gaze.
At least, she didn't press you further for a promise; maybe that was for the best.

You nodded.
In all those years, you had never heard a word about that mother and daughter. Clearly, your father went out of his way to keep this secret. Arzuna's hatred of him was only natural. And such hatred could easily fall on his son, especially one who had inherited all of his titles, estate, wealth, and influence. In hindsight, Arzuna's arrival seemed almost too deliberate.
You promised to keep your distance, and relief softened Maggie's eyes as she turned to embrace you.

5008223.title: A More Fitting Job
strings: A More Fitting Job
Determined to stay away, you set Arzuna up with work far from the capital...
Arzuna
You assigned Arzuna to your territory for some minor chores, with the hope that she'd understand your intent to keep your distance.

5008224.title: Between Siblings
strings: Between Siblings
Arzuna desires you. In the madness of the night, that is the only thing you are certain of.
You have to face this.
Arzuna is gazing at you.
Is your mind still clear?
You could resist temptation with the right help... but do you even care to?
Should you really do this? You need to think it over.
Or maybe, just let yourself be swept away by desire?
Could you keep a hold on yourself?
The pool of dice determined by your Sociability and Wisdom is affected by Arzuna's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 5 Success for a chance to turn down her invitation.
The Point of No Return
Caught in the Web

Arzuna froze for a heartbeat. "You think this is wrong? After everything we've done, my dear brother?" A teasing curve lifted her lips. "If I weren't your sister in this moment... if I were simply someone who desired you, would you push me away?"
You shook your head with effort, explaining that last time's indulgence had been an accident of circumstance. But Arzuna stared at you, unwavering, as if she could strip your heart bare with her eyes. Finally, she stepped back. With a calm air, she lifted herself and brushed away the invisible dust from her clothes. "Ah, now you play the loyal, devoted husband. And the last time we... shared a bed? Heh..." Her eyes narrowed, a cold laugh curling her lips. "Men are all the same. Once you're off the bed, all the love and promises are gone. Reason creeps back into your head, and suddenly you're bright, upright, untarnished. How splendid, my dear brother. Let's see just how truly 'high-minded' you are in the end."

You struggled to convince Arzuna that last time's indulgence had been an accident of circumstance, a mistake meant to be corrected. Yet, she pressed closer. Her warm skin, shimmering eyes, supple waist and arms, and the tinkle of bells with every move pulled at you with irresistible temptation. Perhaps it began with a kiss, or just a gaze, and already you were caught in her web. Through her eyes, you saw yourself. In the heat of desire, she became a mirror reflecting how your face, your life, even your fate had all been shaped by the need to please.

In truth, you didn't catch a single word Arzuna said. The voices were too many—buzzing in your ears, cramming your skull, arguing virtue and vice, preaching restraint, and glorifying indulgence. You wanted only one thing: silence.
Your sudden roar startled Arzuna. She stepped back on instinct, but wasn't it too late? You seized her against the edge of the table, ripping apart her feeble guard and pressing forward relentlessly. Wasn't this what she wanted? Her fear flickered in your eyes, spilling into your palm. Why cry, Arzuna—your dear sister? Did she not know that cracking the dam of your heart would free a torrent that could only ruin her? You let out a cold laugh. Beneath the blood-red moon, only her trembling despair answered you.

5008225.title: Sudden Confession
strings: Sudden Confession
After breaking a Carnality Card, you arrive home and push open the door nervously. There sits Arzuna, beside Maggie, whispering something...
Arzuna
Maggie
You must handle this yourself.
Something that aids your check.
No time to explain! You need to find a way to quell Maggie's fury, and fast.
The pool of dice determined by your Sociability and Charisma is affected by Maggie's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 5 Success to calm her down a little.
You pretended you saw nothing. But can you pretend it never happened? You had best handle this properly, or else...

The moment Arzuna saw you, a flicker of guilt and embarrassment crossed her face. She curtsied, then slipped away in a hurry. Maggie's polite smile vanished, replaced by a sharp, unpleasant glare.
"So... she's your sister?" Maggie's eyes pinned you coldly. "A concubine's daughter, a Carnality Card... How touching is the bond between siblings, isn't it, my dear husband?"

You struggled to convince Maggie that you hadn't known Arzuna's identity beforehand, and that your last indulgence had been compelled, not chosen... Perhaps she believed you, perhaps not. She left without a word, only a shadow of disappointment in her gaze. Still, this needed proper handling. The question was, should you first try to cheer up Maggie or speak with Arzuna?

Your excuses fell flat... After all, no one could force you to put yourself where you had done.
Maggie was clearly displeased, but for the sake of dignity—mostly yours—she said nothing. Still, this needed proper handling. The question was, should you first try to cheer up Maggie or speak with Arzuna?

5008226.title: Guilt and Jewelry
strings: Guilt and Jewelry
Shouldn't you try to soothe Maggie? Perhaps... invest in some lovely, eye-catching jewelry?
Maggie
You have to handle this yourself.
You are ready to spend 20 Gold Coins for this. If you pay double, you can take the opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of Silver and below.
If you're willing to pay 40 Gold Coins, you can take the opportunity to break an Extravagance Card of Silver and below.
You can take the opportunity to resolve one Wife's Resentment.
Choosing to complete this event will end the Accusation ritual.
To Win Back Her Heart

You summoned several tailors and merchants close to Maggie, trying to find out what had drawn her interest lately. They exchanged uneasy glances and shook their heads. "Nothing works," they said. "Some mistakes cannot be fixed—like a cracked gem that never heals."
You set a box brimming with gold heavily on the table. Immediately, a familiar jeweler leaned in. "I know what Lady Maggie desires... A coronet like the one from her younger days, popular on her family's lands. I can craft an exact replica—if you pay."
Twenty gold coins, the jeweler said, as if she'd glanced inside the box and counted every piece.
Remedy Plan
I Want Something Better
Nothing Is Too Extravagant for Your Wife

You poured the gold coins onto the jeweler's carpet; they bounced and jingled, almost as if singing a cheerful song—"For Maggie's Joy".
"These should be enough," the jeweler said with a smile, counting the coins before nodding to you. "I'll deliver the finished coronet straight to your lady and make sure to highlight how much you paid... Don't worry, it's part of the service."
Exhausted, you said your goodbye.
A few days later, you entered the bedroom to find Maggie trying on a new coronet. It was truly a masterpiece: gemstones from her parents' lands glittered across its golden base, engraved with blessings. As she adjusted the coronet, the red-gold chains whispered a delicate tinkle, each link set with a tiny diamond.
"You're back," she said, glancing at you. Her face remained cool, but her voice betrayed a trace of happiness. "How did you know about this coronet? Since leaving home, I haven't seen one... Oh, look at these gold chains and diamonds—they're exquisite! Even my mother never had a coronet so beautiful!"
You stepped behind her and gently draped an arm over her shoulders. She made no move to shrug it off.
The gift spoke for your apology and affection. Heartfelt or not, Maggie chose to accept it.

Your gold coins spilled across the jeweler's counter, far too many to be contained. They sparkled with maddening brilliance even through the shop's windows, drawing every passerby's gaze.
"Look, everyone! A gift from Lord [player.name] to his lady!" Jenna called out, laughing. "Who in the world could be happier than she is?"
People nodded in agreement, their eyes full of admiration. You forced a smile, accepting their praise with weary grace. Finally, the jeweler relented. She promised to deliver the finished coronet straight to your wife, emphasizing your care and dedication in the process.
A few days later, you entered the bedroom to find Maggie trying on a new coronet.
Its base of pure gold was set with rare white gemstones that shimmered like moonlight. Above each gemstone was a tiny gold clasp, threaded with three impossibly fine gold chains. Even finer, smaller rings dangled from those chains, each cradling another moonlit gemstone. All the chains converged at the coronet's peak, coroneted by a cluster of large gilded gemstones, greedily drinking in every ray of light.
This was jewelry for the moon itself—a coronet any noblewoman would wear with pride.
"How did you know about this coronet? The jeweler told you, didn't she? Last time I mentioned it, but the price was outrageous... Oh, and yet you paid for it!" Maggie didn't look back—she knew it was only you in her bedroom. A faint tremor ran through her voice, revealing the hint of lost composure. "How laughable... how ironic! I tried to protect your wealth, and you... after silent betrayal... brought it back for me! My dear, is this love? Is this the gift of your heart?"
With the magnificent coronet on her head, she lowered her gaze and wept. You approached from behind, draping your arm over her shoulders. In that instant, joy, bitterness, guilt, relief, and anxiety—all the tangled emotions—flowed from her into you.
Afterward, you spoke little of betrayal, yet your marriage grew closer—not because of deeper love, but because you had both glimpsed the raw essence of "love."

The Sultan refused to let you break this card. So you knelt and explained why you had to—about breaking a Carnality Card with another woman, and Maggie's fury that followed...
"Now this is interesting," the Sultan exclaimed, delighted. He pressed you for every humiliating detail of your misfortune, then kindly offered his wisdom: always choose the largest and priciest jewel for a woman—so that, should fate ever demand her death, at least the treasure would soften the loss.
You nodded almost obediently as he dispensed his wisdom, and at last, the matter was laid to rest.

5008227.title: Accusation
strings: Accusation
You really want to know what Arzuna said to Maggie—or why she even went to Maggie at all?! Is she trying to cause trouble for you?
Arzuna
You must talk it over yourself.
Choosing to complete this event will end the Guilt and Jewelry event.
You Deserve Better

When you burst into Arzuna's residence, she was setting down a massive platter on the table.
"You're here, my brother." She brightened at the sight of you, innocent and yet touched with a flicker of worry. Her voice was soft, almost pleading. "I'm sorry... I ran into Lady Maggie and called her sister-in-law without thinking... I truly didn't mean to. Please forgive me. Look, I made soup for you. Have a taste!"
She shoved the spoon into your hand and nudged you into a chair. Fine. The accusations you had prepared dissolved in the first mouthful—rich, delicious, disarming. Arzuna settled beside you, chin propped on her hands. She reached out and gently rubbed the crease between your brows, a trace of perfume drifting in the air. "It's my fault you're troubled," she murmured. "Still... it feels unfair. My mother never once complained or grew jealous. The woman at your side hasn't managed that. My brother, you deserve someone better."
You shot her a look, and she sheepishly stuck out her tongue. Beyond coaxing you to enjoy your soup and care for your health, she said nothing more.
It was, undeniably, a bowl of comfort.

5008228.title: Dance of the Finale
strings: Dance of the Finale
At the end of the banquet, to everyone's surprise—even yours—Arzuna steps onto the stage with a smile, promising one last dance for all of you.
Arzuna
Arzuna's resolve.
You are the host of this banquet.
Consumables useful
Yet, your eyes catch it: brighter than her eyes, a dagger thrust in your direction!
The pool of dice determined by your Physique and Combat is affected by Arzuna's corresponding attributes.
You need at least 1 Success to win.
Last Dance

The bells on her wrists rang clear, perfectly in tune with the music. Every curve, every glance, and every gesture gleamed like a lethal jewel. People stared, almost hypnotized, at Arzuna's sinuous form, imagining the woman you had just unveiled and claimed. How many kisses and bites hid beneath her silks and makeup? How wild had it been last night? Had she been this passionate, supple, and yielding? And those eyes—oh—under the lights, behind the curtains, how they gleamed straight at you!
The Finale

Too bold, wasn't it? She was a dancer, not a fighter; a woman, not a man. She couldn't beat you—not yesterday, not today. You smiled as you snapped her dagger and pinned her to the wrecked table, the crowd roaring for another conquest. But then, without warning, she slit her own throat on a shard of broken porcelain. The blood gushed, then cooled; the hatred in her bright eyes froze, crystallizing into a trivial eternity.

Too late! The dagger plunged into your throat—then your palms, chin, eye sockets, chest... Her full, scorching hatred struck like a sudden storm, and in the last flicker of life, you saw only her icy eyes. Scarlet splashes across her face made her look twisted, mad, terrifying—but she was smiling softly.
"You're no different from your father, my dear brother." She leveled the dagger at your eye. "If Mom had done to him what I'm doing to you... none of this would have happened."
This was the last scene you saw. The last words you heard.

5008229.title: Final Conversation
strings: Final Conversation
You see Maggie at the doorstep, and she only gives you a cold glance.
Maggie
You Really Do Like Her

Dropping that sharp, loaded remark, Maggie gave you a cold glance and then walked off.
You waited endlessly, until it hit you: she wasn't coming back. Not ever. She had left you completely, carrying nothing but a heart shattered to its core.

5008230.title: Entertainment Banquet
strings: Entertainment Banquet
On this moonlit night, as music fills the banquet hall, perhaps you could have Arzuna grace your guests with a dance. She'd be happy to oblige.
Arzuna is glad to perform.
You are the banquet host.
Your invited guest.
You can now break an Extravagance Card or Carnality Card of Bronze or lower.
To break an Extravagance Card, you must spend 10 more Gold Coins.
You need to invite at least one guest.

Was it really necessary? Even if Arzuna did not dance for them, would your guests dare to be dissatisfied with your feast?
You brushed the thought aside...
Admire the Moon

The guests were seated in the courtyard, wine and food ready. Arzuna, veiled, emerged from the pomegranate trees into the midst.
She stood serene, bathed in silver moonlight, drawing every probing gaze to herself... Then she swept aside her veil and stretched her body, setting every bell and bangle jingling in unison.
She began to dance, eyes lifted to the moon, the treetops, the clouds—never meeting anyone present. Her arms were so long that when she reached for the moon, you almost believed she could cradle it in her hands. In the moonlight, she seemed to have four arms, each with a mind of its own, commanding every hand, every body, and every soul. She turned and stepped with deliberate grace; her body bent, collapsed, curled... then expanded again. In that instant, everyone there knew the same truth—Arzuna was the moon incarnate.
Strangely, this Arzuna was not seductive. Her dance was not meant to please you. If anything, the moon alone was her honored guest.
A Sultan Card Broken
Absolutely Irresistible

The dance ended. The old musician panted, spent, having strained every ounce to keep up with Arzuna's rhythm. And the dancer—she veiled herself again, standing silently among the crowd like a cold, distant new moon.
Applause erupted, led by you, wild and frenzied. None had ever seen a dance like this—none had imagined they ever could!
Arzuna, this unexpected "sister," was indeed a masterful dancer.
The moonlit banquet had left every heart stirred...
It was a flawless banquet: exquisite delicacies and a dancer who amazed everyone—everything left the guests praising in awe.

An incredible dance and an even more stunning beauty! You can't even wait for the performance to wrap up—you just have to have her. You jump onto the stage and pull her into your arms. Arzuna stumbles, completely shocked, and the music hits a jarring discord as the musician fumbles. The guests gape as you strip away her silks, their eyes immediately shifting to the hostess... Maggie looks on in total shock, her face turning white as she realizes the scene you've caused.
Talk about a public humiliation! You might be the one ravaging Arzuna, but Maggie is the one feeling every bit of the pain. Not that you care. You give in to your darker side, break the Carnality Card, and savor the chaos.

An incredible dance and an even more stunning beauty! You can't even wait for the performance to wrap up—you just have to have her. You jump onto the stage and pull her into your arms. Arzuna stumbles, completely shocked, and the music hits a jarring discord as the musician fumbles. The guests gape as you strip away her silks, giving them a front-row seat to your debauchery. You break the Card of Indulgence right then and there, making everyone in the room your witness. You're enjoying every bit of Arzuna, and honestly, you're loving it. What the guests think doesn't matter one bit to you.

5008231.title: Noble's Invitation
strings: Noble's Invitation
A noble asks to borrow your dancer Arzuna for his banquet, speaking as if she's nothing more than a slave girl in your house.
The nobles are eager to see Arzuna's dance.
How about having a noblewoman attend with her?
How about having a servant by her side?
How about taking care of her dressing?
You can stand up for Arzuna with your actions.
If you decide to concede her lower status, you can let her go alone.
Will you let her face it all alone, or arrange everything for her?
You forgot the matter entirely—and soon whispers spread across court and city: that you were too miserly to lend out even a single slave girl...
Not a Bad Misunderstanding
Arzuna's Opinion Matters

You had Arzuna summoned, arrogantly commanding her to perform at the noble's banquet—dazzle them and keep your honor intact. You even wrote to the noble, asking him to tolerate your "humble dancer".
Arzuna knelt and smiled, obediently replying, "Whatever you wish, my lord."
That day, Arzuna delivered a flawless dance at the noble's estate. Praise erupted like a tide. Everyone assumed it to be a bold show of your influence, and you were perfectly satisfied. As for whether Arzuna enjoyed it? What did that matter to you?

You relayed the noble's invitation to Arzuna word for word, asking if she would accept.
She raised an eyebrow. "I thought you'd accept for me. After all, everyone sees me as your dancer, your slave girl." She spoke as if it mattered little, toying with the bangles on her wrist. "I love dancing, but... hmm... I worry I might tarnish your reputation. What do you think—would I?"
Without hesitation, you told her that having a passion was a rare gift. If she liked to dance for others, why hold back? And your reputation? It should mean the least to her. Nothing should restrict her freedom to follow her heart.
Arzuna paused, stunned, before bowing deeply. "I will be there, my brother. And I will not bring you shame." She had never seemed so earnest.
The Mistress's Favor
Entrusting Arzuna to [s2.name]

Maggie, already invited to the banquet, couldn't suppress a smile as she watched you fumble through your hesitant request.
"Alright, I understand. I'll take care of Arzuna."
And so, Arzuna went, dazed, linked arm in arm with Maggie into the noble's estate. Under [s3.name]'s hands, she stiffly applied the newly bought rouge... Being waited on didn't suit her one bit! She had always prepared herself alone.
The noble was stunned, nervously probing her identity, too wary to show the slightest disdain. After all, what slave girl could have the company of a mistress?
It was a flawless performance. Beyond the applause, there was no disruptive noise, intrusive gazes, or malicious teasing—none of the petty cruelties she had assumed she'd endure forever. Arzuna had never known such pure admiration, and it was all because of Maggie and you. She held back tears as she took her bow, later raising a glass to Maggie with sincere gratitude.

At the noble's estate, Arzuna delivered a flawless dance. When the music ended, whispers rippled through the crowd, speculating about the beautiful dancer—look at her, in her expensive silks and vivid rouge, even attended by a servant. Heaven, how favored she must be! Was she your new slave girl? Or some woman you had taken a fancy to?
"That's enough." Amid the chatter, [s2.name] set down her glass with a cold, decisive weight. "If you wish to provoke Lord [player.name], go ahead. Let's guess how many more cards of Bloodshed or Conquest remain in the deck."
As if to memorize them all, she scanned every man present. They shrank under her gaze, none daring to meet her eyes. She snorted lightly, then stepped onto the stage and took Arzuna's hand. "Let's go."
Sheltered at her side, Arzuna lowered her head and nodded softly, concealing the tender flicker of surprise in her heart.

5008232.title: Rumors Everywhere
strings: Rumors Everywhere

Rumors about Arzuna spread like wildfire. For all that she is merely a lowly dancer, her dance dazzles, her beauty beguiles, and she is so soft and yielding before you... Everyone loves to discuss, to slander, to humiliate beautiful women, especially those with no one to back them up.
Enough. You decide to send someone to quell these rumors.
Intelligence and rumors used to divert attention.

You could not stop the rumors... or perhaps you simply would not. Let them talk! It would not harm you in the slightest. If anything, you might even secretly relish all those shocking, breathtaking tales.

[s1.name] raised her voice, warning every acquaintance who might speak a word: you were displeased with these rumors, and if they didn't want to provoke Lord [player.name], they'd best keep their mouths shut.
Whether out of fear or respect, the whispers about Arzuna quickly dwindled.

Maggie listened quietly to your worries, then shook her head with a soft smile. She didn't ask whether the rumors were true—she merely promised she could deal with whatever threatened your family's honor.
Sure enough, within days, the whispers about Arzuna died down.
You asked Maggie in the bedroom: did she use some kind of magic? How did she make the gossiping world suddenly stop?
"Oh..." Maggie said lightly, flipping through her book, "I just reminded them that everyone has a few juicy secrets. And if I hear another word about that dancer, I don't mind sharing some stories... Some had an affair with their daughters-in-law, some executed commoners in secret, and some greedily dipped into the Sultan's pockets..."
She turned a page, then glanced at you.
"They believed I really knew everything, so they shut their mouths. It's that simple, my dear husband."

You knew your wife would never tolerate rumors that tarnished your family's name, and she had silenced them. No matter how she did it, there was no doubt that these whispers—malicious, suggestive, improper, yet plausible guesses about you and Arzuna—once again hurt Maggie's already scarred heart.

5008233.title: Gutter's Invitation
strings: Gutter's Invitation

Buthayna has sent a letter, inviting Arzuna to perform at the House of Delights.
"My girls have long admired your dancing. If you wish, they would also be delighted to show their own skills."
Buthayna wants to invite Arzuna.
You can send someone to accompany her, but it's not a job nobles enjoy.
You can spend 2 Gold Coins to cover Arzuna's attire.
You can now break a Carnality Card of Bronze and below.
If you feel it's inappropriate, you may simply ignore the invitation.
Will you let her face it all alone, or arrange everything for her?
Arzuna is about to join the palace and cannot be present for this invitation.
Teaching prostitutes to dance hardly sounds respectable. Best not to.
Remember to Veil Your Face
Never a Disgrace

You instructed Arzuna to veil her face before going to the House of Delights—and to never, under any circumstances, mention her connection to you.
She smiled and obeyed without question.

You asked Arzuna for her opinion, and she seemed puzzled, tilting her head with a playful air. "My opinion? Does it matter to you?" Yet she quickly composed herself. "Madam Buthayna... I've heard of her. They say she was an extraordinary dancer in her younger days and even invented a dancing dress strung with coins! The girls at the House of Delights must be skilled—they earn their living that way. Dancing with them could be fun... though of course, I don't have to go. Performing at a brothel feels dishonorable. Even if I'm a concubine's daughter, I know that much."
You shook your head, not agreeing with her. Her dancing was exquisite; she never needed to feel shame, no matter the venue. Even in the "gutter," among the Ladies of Delights—the very same who could captivate the Sultan—the stage was no dishonor. They loved to refine their art and share it; masters had come to guide them and also learn from them. In that light, Arzuna had every reason to feel proud. Madam Buthayna's invitation was a recognition of her skill, a testament to her reputation as a true master of dance.
"Really? You won't be angry if I dance in a brothel?" Arzuna asked, her eyes searching yours. "Shouldn't a noble... I mean, a courtier like you care most about family honor? What if I told everyone I'm the daughter of your father's concubine—oh, of course I wouldn't... I just mean..."
You smiled and shook your head, then spoke earnestly: you had never once thought her shameful. On the contrary, having a sister with such extraordinary talent filled you with pride.
Arzuna turned her face away, hiding her expression.
Her farewell sounded a little hoarse at last.
As It Should Be at the House of Delights
More for Arzuna to Learn at the House of Delights

Back from the House of Delights, Arzuna went straight to her residence, offering no report to you. But soon after, Madam Buthayna sent you a token of thanks—a mark of full approval at Arzuna's dances.

At the night's end, you stepped among the girls. The Ladies of Delights instantly sensed it, and Arzuna yielded into your embrace. That was why you didn't see the faint, contemptuous curl at her lips—she had long known: men were nothing more than crude animals.

Still, for Arzuna's safety, you had [s2.name] and [s3.name] accompany her to the House of Delights.
That evening, Madam Buthayna cleared the entire front hall and greeted Arzuna with the respect due a master. Arzuna danced, sang, and laughed alongside the girls, delving into their skills and celebrating each other's elegance. She taught them much, and in turn, learned much. It was, without a doubt, a night to remember.

At the night's end, you stepped among the girls. The Ladies of Delights instantly sensed it, but poor Arzuna didn't notice a thing. She excitedly chattered with you about the evening's lessons, right up until you tipped her back onto the soft pile of pillows.
Tonight, Arzuna learned her most important lesson: never trust a man's words—the grander and sweeter they sound, the less believable they are.

5008234.title: A Free Day for the Ladies of Delights
strings: A Free Day for the Ladies of Delights
Maggie suggests bringing the Ladies of Delights to your estate, so Arzuna can exchange skills with them without any concern.
Arzuna
As the banquet host, you can naturally invite guests.
Maggie is also a host of the banquet.
Buthayna arrives with her girls.
You took no action, yet the ball went on as planned, arranged by Maggie. By all accounts, Arzuna danced joyfully with the Ladies of Delights.
Moons High in the Sky

You told Arzuna about your plan for the banquet, and her eyes widened at once.
"I never imagined it could be like this! Ah, this is wonderful! I can dance with everyone... for as long as I want! Oh, thank you—truly!"
A smile bloomed across her face, long-buried feelings rising to the surface; she looked, in that moment, like a little girl brimming with excitement.
When the hour arrived, your estate had never known such life—not when you entertained the Sultan's closest courtiers, not even when Maggie's kin crowded the courtyard. Laughter spilled everywhere, bright and breathless.
All Ladies of Delights stood flushed with joy, servants scrambling to set seats they barely noticed. To have stepped out of that perfumed cage was novelty enough, let alone dancing together in a courtier's house!
You stood with wine in hand, dazed.
They danced to a merry rhythm, smiles pure and radiant. Jewels chimed, braids swayed, and waists rippled like fish through water.
Every new dance was shouted into the night—Circle Dance, Fox Dance, Ale Dance, Apis Ring Dance, and countless others you had never heard. They gathered around Arzuna like stars about the moon—no, they were all moons, invited by you to fill the sky.
Your Moon Alone
Love at First Sight?
Arzuna's Visit Next Day

Maggie, unusually, had a couple more drinks. Her cheeks flushed, a soft smile playing on her lips—she was truly happy for these girls. Here, now, amid endless songs and dances, titles and status faded. The joy of life, at its purest, carried a warmth they all equally felt. When you pressed your lips to her moist eyes, that warmth rose into your heart, leaving you dizzy and weightless all at once. The sky held countless stars, yet she was your one and only moon.

Nabhani was the happiest soul at the ball! As the girls danced, this red-haired guy somehow slipped in, wriggling alongside them—an utterly unbearable sight.
You had the servants drag him out, yet he always found a way back in. Fine, let him be.
By the night's end, the beautiful girls left your estate, and Arzuna came to say goodbye. "I've never been this happy, Lord [player.name], my brother... Thank you for arranging all of this—"
Before you could speak, Nabhani seized her hand. "Truly! He's the best brother, the best man, and the best courtier in this world! And I am his best friend! I never knew he had such a radiant sister, but it's not too late now. Shall I see you home? It's late—I can't let you walk alone."
Arzuna tried to pull her hand free—and failed. Speechless, you gripped Nabhani's wrist, while he resisted with all his strength. The two of you nearly came to blows at the doorstep—until Arzuna chuckled.
In the end, you wore a forced grin and escorted Arzuna home together with Nabhani. After Arzuna secured the door, Nabhani lingered every few steps and finally headed back. Only then could you finally return.

Again, Arzuna thanked you for everything you had arranged last night. She said she had been dancing by herself at home, trying to memorize every step.
"And that swordsman... Despite you sending him away, he still managed to slip a note into my pocket." She handed the note to you, a smile hidden behind her hand. "I can't read, but I'm guessing it's just some 'love at first sight' message, right?"
Arzuna was right—the note read, "You have already captured my heart." Hah, that blasted Nabhani!
"Ahem, these young nobles... their hearts are easier to capture than fleas—two or three snags a day." She chuckled. "But honestly, the way you stopped him... it really felt like the 'brother' I used to imagine when I was little."
She let the subject drop, and the two of you chatted casually and happily for a while.
Just like any other siblings.

After all other girls left, Arzuna remained and gave a solemn curtsy.
"I have never known such joy, Lord [player.name], my dear brother. Thank you for all of this."
She curtsied again—then a third time—before withdrawing with quiet grace.

5008235.title: Sultan's Whim
strings: Sultan's Whim

Arzuna has become too famous of late—so much so that even the Sultan knows you shelter an extraordinary dancer. Now, eunuchs from his court deliver a summons bearing Arzuna's name. It could raise her to unrivaled favor... or cast her into a bottomless abyss.
Arzuna
Offer 30 Gold Coins, or try to persuade the Sultan.
You may offer Gold Coins, or try to persuade the Sultan to rescind his call, or simply watch as Arzuna is taken away.
Before the Sultan's patience runs dry, you make your attempt to sway him...
[s2.name]'s Sociability and Charisma determine the pool of dice.
You need at least 7 Success to dissuade the Sultan.
You acquiesced—naturally. How could you defy the Sultan's command? Arzuna did not complain—she was always understanding—and quietly prepared to enter the palace.
Dangerous Harem

You told Arzuna that the harem was a gilded cage—the Sultan cared not for skillful dance, only for the slave girls clustered at his side. As her brother... as her friend, you would never send her in for his pleasure.
"But... the Sultan is the ruler of us all. Could you truly defy him?" Arzuna tilted her head, curious. "I don't mind, brother, for I can outmatch those women... I've seen every nightmare they've survived. Neither bite nor betrayal can shake me."
She seemed almost indifferent to entering the Sultan's harem. But your mind was made up. With the servants' help, you freshened up and donned your court jewels and robes, then set out for the palace.
When you arrived, the Sultan was dining in his favorite concubine's chamber, surrounded by a dozen servants. Golden plates and glass goblets were strewn about like pebbles and mud. He cast you a sidelong glance, chewing fruit lifted to his lips by the concubine. The favor of a private audience had been granted—but it was clear he did not appreciate being interrupted mid-meal.
Gold Always Works

You told Arzuna that the harem was a gilded cage—the Sultan cared not for skillful dance, only for the slave girls clustered at his side. As her brother... as her friend, you would never send her in for his pleasure.
"But... the Sultan is the ruler of us all. Could you truly defy him?" Arzuna tilted her head, curious. "I don't mind, brother, for I can outmatch those women... I've seen every nightmare they've survived. Neither bite nor betrayal can shake me."
She seemed almost indifferent to entering the Sultan's harem. But your mind was made up. You knew exactly what he wanted—not a fresh-faced woman, not a dancer of genius. He wanted what you treasured... a test of your loyalty. And you knew a reliable way to prove it. It cost gold, but it always worked.
Sure enough, once the eunuchs had taken the coins you offered, no explanations or declarations were needed. The matter was settled.
Honor Guard's Help

You knelt respectfully, speaking before the Sultan's patience ran out: the dancer could not be admitted to the palace.
The Sultan's eyebrows rose just under his crown, and you continued—you wished you could present the dancer, but her background was still unclear and her approach toward the Sultan seemed too calculated...
Just then, Nabhani dropped to his knees nearby. "Yes, Your Majesty," he reported respectfully. "A few days ago, at Lord [player.name]'s request, I observed the dancer. Her movements were aggressive. I believe Lord [player.name] does not mean to deny her to you, but is concerned for your safety."
His eyes flicked to you, and you understood instantly. You bowed your head, explaining that you dared not speak earlier—afraid of the Sultan's reproach or of spoiling his mood. The matter also required caution; you still wished to investigate further, so you had delayed reporting...
The Sultan waved you off impatiently, dismissing you from the palace. Afterward, he never mentioned the dancer again. Nabhani, ever restless, soon appeared with a grin of triumph. "Well? Well? Did you feel my devotion to Arzuna?" Thrilled and puffed up with pride, Nabhani clearly saw the whole thing as an exhilarating hero-rescues-damsel story. "I lied to the Sultan just to keep my beloved free. Come on, call me your brother-in-law!"
You laughed inwardly—no chance—but thanked him cautiously. Nabhani, unconcerned, laughed and slapped your shoulder. But as he left, he leaned close, voice low. "Seriously... your sister's dance hides something fierce, something a fighter would have. As a swordsman, I can see it. Be careful."
Another tap on your shoulder, and he strode off with a jaunty, carefree air.

You knelt respectfully and got straight to the point: the dancer might not be fit to enter the palace.
The Sultan's eyebrows rose just under his crown, and you continued—you wished you could present the dancer, but her background was still unclear, and her approach toward the Sultan seemed too calculated. Besides... her recent practice seemed to hide a deadly edge. "Before everything is properly investigated..." You paused and stole a glance at the Sultan.
Just as you expected, the Sultan grew thoughtful. Of course he would be—his father had nearly been slain by an assassin posing as a concubine. The Honor Guards intervened in time; the wound was only a deep cut to the neck. Yet, the spray of blood and the indecent absurdity of a ruler poised to enjoy a new beauty, froze in that moment. It was all burned into the young prince's memory.
The Sultan clicked his tongue. A brief wave of his hand settled it—leave her out for now and look into it further. With that, he turned to a new slave girl, leaving Arzuna's matter aside for now.
You let out a quiet breath of relief, bowed low in gratitude, and returned home with your head still firmly in place.

You spun a dozen excuses to explain, but the Sultan remembered only one thing: [player.name] refused to offer him the flawless dancer.
"Is that so, you selfish, insolent, lowly, ungrateful subject? If you want your head to stay where it belongs and leave the palace standing, you know what to do, right?"

5008236.title: A Strange Dance
strings: A Strange Dance
Beneath a tall styrax tree, Arzuna is dancing.
Arzuna
Go see for yourself.

Hearing your footsteps, Arzuna turned with a smile. "Ah, my brother," she greeted, beckoning you over, "come and sit."
Beneath the tree, you settled beside her while an old servant brought snacks and hookahs. "What was that dance just now?" you asked—it was unlike anything you'd ever seen.
"Oh... that was my mother's dance."
She inhaled the smoke, then fell silent, switching topics. "I've been waiting for days, my brother, for you to take me to the palace. But you didn't... I suppose you convinced that mighty, unyielding Sultan?"
"Are you... trying to be nice to me?" She fiddled with her fingers, skeptical yet curious. "This is unusual; I'm used to pleasing others, not being pleased... My brother, is it because I'm still of some use to you?"
You assured her it wasn't about usefulness—she shouldn't be confined in a place like the harem.
