She revealed a bitter smile. "Then where should I be confined? I don't even know... what I live for."
She swayed the bells around her wrist, listening to their clear chime. Then, in the silence, she rose and walked to the flowering tree, dancing alone without music.
This dance was unlike any you'd seen from her before; it wasn't smooth, but punctuated. Each sudden stop or frozen pose pulsed with raw emotion pouring from her eyes, unrestrained and sharp like a flood directed at you. Then you understood—it was hatred.
"Do you hate me, Arzuna?" you found yourself asking.

Arzuna smiled. When the dance ended, she was once again the gentle girl you knew. She stepped lightly to your side, answering you with that familiar, practiced smile until the topic drifted elsewhere. You took the hint and asked no more.

"Do I hate you?" Arzuna smiled at your question. She came to sit beside you, but did not look your way. Instead, she lifted her face to the moon. "You've probably guessed," she said quietly, "my mother was a dancer. Our father noticed her at a banquet. But she wasn't a slave—she was free. He promised to love her, to cherish her, to make her his lawful wife. And she believed him. Then I was born. We lived in a small house that he provided. His occasional visits were like festivals, for my mother only smiled on those days. We lacked for nothing. No hunger, no cruelty. But..."
You waited quietly.
"At some point, he stopped coming. Four... maybe five years. Then suddenly he returned. My mother was overjoyed. She put on her old dress and painted her face, as beautiful as ever—at least to me. But he came to warn us. Never go to the capital. Never reveal who we are. We must not endanger my brother's future—the son who would inherit everything and walk into the Lapis Lazuli Palace!"
She looked at you, sharp and unflinching, before revealing the end of the story: "After that, my mother killed herself. She spent her life teaching me how to please him, how to please men, and how to please anyone who might love us... She always believed a man would love her! When she finally understood it was all in vain... living meant nothing either. That dance—the one you just watched—was her final lesson. It must be performed with hatred."
The old servant brought a plate of sliced peaches glazed with honey. Arzuna picked one up, turning it between her fingers without taking a bite.
"To be honest, I supported her death. Better that than watching her waste away or grow madder. After she died, I danced. I danced well. For a long time. I saved money—together with the small compensation our father left us, it was enough. So I came to the capital, the place he forbade. By then, he was already dead. And you, my brother, had inherited everything."
Before you could speak, she rose. She told the old servant to see you out. She was tired. She would rest now.
And so, you left her small house.

5008237.title: The Missing Dancer
strings: The Missing Dancer

Arzuna is gone. Her residence stands empty, as though she had never been there at all. In the courtyard, the tall styrax tree still sways in the night wind, its rustling almost echoing her dance... but she would likely never return.
Arzuna
Send someone to search.
If you intend to track her down, you'd better turn to someone who knows the ways of the streets.
Can [s2.name] dig up any word of Arzuna?
[s2.name]'s Sociability and Stealth determine the pool of dice.
You need at least 5 Successes to gain something.
Let her go, you thought. All may come and go as they please.

[s2.name] spent the day scouring the city and caught an important clue: Arzuna had been seen heading toward a hill beyond the city walls. If your memory served—you surely wouldn't forget—this was the way to your family cemetery.
Arzuna's caution was beyond imagination. [s2.name] couldn't dig up a single useful clue. And just like that, Arzuna vanished, like a grain of sand swallowed by the desert.
Telling Maggie About Arzuna's Sudden Departure

Maggie studied your worried eyes for a moment before saying, "Perhaps I know where she'll be."
"I've heard she bought a small plot in your family cemetery... using your family's name, with a few badges and letters to prove it. You know she has those. The gravekeeper reported it to me... I figure, if she's truly set on leaving, she'd likely visit it one last time."
Well, that was very possible.

Learning that Arzuna was gone, Nabhani blinked in brief surprise, then quickly regained his calm.
"Oh... maybe that's a good thing for her?" He scratched his head and lounged back among the soft pillows, the gems on his braids sparkling and tinkling.
Good thing? Furious, you dragged him into the streets to track Arzuna down, but came up empty-handed. Certainly the fault of this lazy, unreliable ally of yours!
[s2.name] put in every effort—or at least pretended to—tracking Arzuna. But the dancer, so used to handling nobles, had vanished completely. After that, you never saw her again.

5008238.title: Heart-to-Heart at the Cemetery
strings: Heart-to-Heart at the Cemetery

At your family cemetery, atop a hill on the outskirts, an elegant mausoleum adorned with mosaics and marble stands quietly. Though not tall—half-buried underground—it spreads wide, a testament to your family's flourishing lineage. And there, Arzuna waits for you.
Arzuna
You must attend the appointment in person.
You can bring Maggie along.
Let me break a card before you run.
You may resolve at most one Carnality Card of Silver or lower. But is that the right choice?
You did not disturb her meditation. Once her final business was done, Arzuna left the capital. She never appeared before you again.
Courtier and Dancer
Family Debt
Join This Family for Real

Candles flickered around Arzuna as she cradled a clay urn.
"My mother dreamed of being buried here. All it took was a bit of money and showing the old gravekeeper some proof... Easy as that." She shrugged, her sweet face twisted in the candlelight. "Women are strange, aren't they? She hated that man, and yet wanted to lie next to him."
You realized the urn likely held her mother's ashes.
"I have a question for you—here, in front of my mother's and your father's tombs. Oh, he's not here, but not far away, I suppose," Arzuna said, her gaze drifting away. "We're both children of the same man. In the end, you've become a powerful noble, and I... a dancer for others' pleasure. Why? My brother, what decides a person's fate?"
You fell silent, then sighed deeply. "I don't know. But what's the difference between a noble and a dancer? When you please guests, I'm trying to please the Sultan. When you earn your coins, I earn another day of life. Who truly lives better? Perhaps we both feel fate is unfair. But it doesn't matter, Arzuna, my sister. After we die, we'll equally lie beneath stones and dirt. So... instead of dwelling on 'why this cursed fate chose me,' what matters is living our days well and chasing the happiness that belongs only to us."
Arzuna froze, eyes wide. "Did you save me from the Sultan with an eloquent talk like that? Equally lie beneath stones and dirt? Live our days well? I... I..." She looked down at her hands, lost. "I'll grow old, my legs won't obey, and my ears won't catch the drum... So I should dance while I still can and enjoy myself now, right?"
Before you could answer, she shook her head sharply, eyes blazing. "That's just an excuse, isn't it? What if I leave you because of it? Would you still think this way?"
"I've never tried to bind you," you said. "I'm glad you came to help. If you decide to leave, I'll still wish you well."
She went quiet, staring at the urn in her hands, then at the candles burning around. Finally, she lowered her head. "Leave me here. I need some time to think it through. Until I do, I'll still be a useful piece in your game."
You nodded and stepped out of the dim mausoleum.

After a brief exchange with the gravekeeper, you and Maggie followed this old man into the dim mausoleum.
In the most forgotten corner, you found Arzuna. She was placing a clay urn into a hastily made coffin. Seeing you, she lifted it and revealed its engravings.
"I paid for this sliver of ground," Arzuna said. "This is my mother's ashes... She wanted to be buried here. Strange, isn't it? She hated that man, yet still wished to lie beside him."
A thin, mocking smile touched her lips as she glanced at Maggie. "Are you not angry? This glorious mausoleum will house a lowly dancer. A dishonored concubine."
Before you could rebuke Arzuna, Maggie stepped forward. Her tender gaze fell upon the small urn. "All I see is a woman consumed by love unto death," she said softly. "If there is shame here, it is not hers."
"You are always so kind, Lady Maggie!" Arzuna laughed. "I can't even hate you. I meant to hate you fiercely—to wound you deeply!"
Before your eyes, she set the urn in place and closed the coffin. From her sleeve, she took a strip of sandalwood, her mother's name written in heavy black ink: Tumkaba. She fit it into the hollow atop the lid, securing it with a firm click.
"Now I owe her nothing. For what she gave me, I've returned to her." Arzuna rose, her back to you. "She made me swear revenge on the man who deceived her and on his entire house. But I cannot harm the kind... If I did, I would be no different from him."
Together, you left the darkness of the mausoleum and stepped once more into the sun.

You found Arzuna deep in the mausoleum with little effort. She cradled a clay urn, likely holding her mother's ashes. But none of that mattered. The moment you revealed the sinister Sultan Card, shadows stirred as if the mausoleum itself had awakened. Long-buried secrets and ancestral scandals—every hidden sin of the noble family—rose from the darkness.
Ah, which ancient, noble house was without its share of disgrace? It was these very sins that kept their line alive. One by one, black specters emerged in the flickering candlelight, surrounding you to witness a new crime etched into the family legacy.
Arzuna's eyes were wide with terror. She trembled, stumbling backward. The urn slipped from her hands, shattering on the ground. Amid the ashes, you claimed her, carving the most searing humiliation into her soul...
Finally, laughing wildly, you let her flee. Wherever she ran, she was yours forever now—and the Sultan Card's magic would record every detail.

You and Maggie found Arzuna deep in the mausoleum with little effort. Arzuna cradled a clay urn, likely holding her mother's ashes. But none of that mattered. The moment you revealed the sinister Sultan Card, shadows stirred as if the mausoleum itself had awakened. Long-buried secrets and ancestral scandals—every hidden sin of the noble family—rose from the darkness.
Ah, which ancient, noble house was without its share of disgrace? It was these very sins that kept their line alive. One by one, black specters emerged in the flickering candlelight, surrounding you to witness a new crime etched into the family legacy.
Maggie screamed and struggled, trying to stop you, but the shadows compelled her to watch... Arzuna's eyes were wide with terror. She trembled, stumbling backward. The urn slipped from her hands, shattering on the ground. Amid the ashes, you claimed her, carving the most searing humiliation into her soul...
Finally, you ordered your servants to carry the two desperate women back home. Your mind already turned to how you would flaunt your marks—scratches, bites, and ecstasy—to the Sultan the next day.

5008239.title: The Wandering Seed
strings: The Wandering Seed
Arzuna decides to leave. She longs to wander the continent as a dancer, to see all dances and join all dancers. You cannot stop her—but you may give her one last gift.
Arzuna
You can fund her travel. 10 Gold Coins will do.
You can arrange for someone to follow or accompany her.
You can announce her identity, but only your word will give it weight.
The follower has to be non-noble.
You needed to do nothing. Arzuna left your residence, and departed the capital. What tied you together would never break; it only grew longer as Arzuna journeyed on...
Generous Pouch
[s3.name]'s Company
A Promise at Last
Arzuna's Departure

You called out to Arzuna and handed her a pouch brimming with gold and jewels.
"Well, thank you." She weighed the pouch in her hands, her smile radiant. "So this is what it's like to have a brother? Not bad at all—I almost want a few more brothers!"
She was even joking with you like this now.

Arzuna looked genuinely surprised. After all, it meant you'd be losing another helper. But you had already decided; you couldn't bear to let her wander alone.
Then she gazed at [s3.name], her eyes shining with joy.
"To think I'd have a companion... Childhood had left me with so few playmates... I believe we'll get along very well."

You told her that since she was your father's child, she was nobility by right—you would name her openly and accept her into your family. Life would trouble a noblewoman far less, and officials would be far more willing to help.
Arzuna stared at you in stunned silence, then answered with nothing but a bitter smile.
What tied you together would never break; it only grew longer as Arzuna journeyed on...

5008240.title: Dance of the Sun
strings: Dance of the Sun
A dancer from afar brings you Arzuna's message—and a dance of hers for you.
This dance is for you.
You can invite one more admirer.

Once the servants gathered, she drew herself up. As the drums struck, she danced for you—each step cut to the beat. It was Arzuna's choreography, taught by her own hand with one request: "Please dance this for my brother."
As the final beat faded, a bittersweet warmth rose in your heart.

Maggie was overjoyed; the delightful warmth of the dance radiated through her. The dancer spotted Maggie and asked, "Are you Lady Maggie?" Then she took Maggie's hand, leading her to the center of the carpet.
Sunlight and breeze from a thousand miles away settled on Maggie's brow and in her eyes—so breathtakingly beautiful! You couldn't help but rise and join in, and one by one the guests swayed and tapped along. Together, you cheered and sang—a moment so vivid it would return to your dreams again and again, leaving you awash in happiness.

5008241.title: Fine-Dried Fish
strings: Fine-Dried Fish
A sea fish personally caught and dried by Arzuna herself. She had it delivered to you from a thousand miles away. Call everyone and taste it!
Today's menu
You can go youselft, or invite followers to taste it
You can enjoy it with your followers
Someone should eat this, right?
A Hearty Meal

It was amazing—the fish seemed almost scaleless. Even air-dried, its flesh stayed springy and rich with fat. No fire, no seasoning—just tear the meat into strips with your hands and taste it as it is. That alone was enough.

5008242.title: Armed Beauty
strings: Armed Beauty
Beauty alone won't secure a place in the harem. The Sultan has never been short of pretty women. Before Arzuna enters the palace, you still have a chance to help her.
Arzuna
Use 10 Gold Coins either for palace affairs or to buy attire.
You can gift her another piece of jewelry with Charisma of 4 and above.
You can assign a noblewoman to guide her.
You can now break an Extravagance Card of Bronze and below, but it requires 10 more Gold Coins.
To break an Extravagance Card, you must spend 10 more Gold Coins.
You completely forgot about Arzuna entering the palace. She said nothing in response to your neglect—she had her own way of dealing with things.
Money Isn't Everything

But without money, Arzuna wouldn't last a day. You pressed a heavy bundle of gold coins into her hands, telling her to hide them well for whatever storms might come. She answered your generosity with a radiant smile. "Thank you, my dear brother."
Bring This Along
Extravagance Card Broken

Beauty might shield a woman in the harem, while jewels were what struck. You slipped [s3.name] into Arzuna's hand. As her smile slowly bloomed, you knew she would wield this weapon to its sharpest edge.

Before Arzuna's departure, you asked [s4.name] to walk her through the palace's rules, correcting gestures too casual for court. Then they whispered for what felt like hours. You didn't know what was said—only that Arzuna's eyes grew brighter with every word, and finally, she nodded, firm and resolute.

When the time came, you led Arzuna to the passage near the palace gate, where the most senior eunuchs were inspecting the "goods" brought by the slavers.
"Too old... too ugly... too... Oh, Lord [player.name]? And... the lady at your side—is she for the palace?" An old eunuch practically yelled, eyes lighting up as he appraised Arzuna. "What a beauty! Surely she's meant for the court—otherwise, we'll never justify this!"
Truly, Arzuna overshadowed all slave girls, especially when she spun through a few dance moves, her supple waist and nimble fingers captivating everyone. You told the eunuch she was a gift from you, a courtier blessed by the Sultan's favor.
"Excellent! His Majesty will be delighted!" Those eunuchs rubbed their hands eagerly, guiding Arzuna with careful respect—they knew this lady could one day be a mistress of the court. "Right this way... Arzuna, such a beautiful name..."
You watched her vanish into the shadowed passage, never looking back.

Your loyalty pleased the Sultan immensely. Not only had you offered a remarkable beauty, but you had spared no expense to enhance her—using even a Sultan Card for it. Triple loyalty, triple favor!
At least for today, you were the courtier most cherished by the throne.

5008243.title: The Fallen Fruit
strings: The Fallen Fruit
It isn't until this day that you finally see Arzuna at the palace gate—and realize how many days you have ignored her.
Arzuna

You saw Arzuna being led by a group of eunuchs through the side entrance toward the harem. You grabbed a familiar eunuch and asked what was going on.
"Do you mean the new beauty? She's a slave, but too lovely to pass up and skilled in dance. Perfect for His Majesty's side. So we purchased her at a fair price. Do you have any concerns, my lord?"
You stared in disbelief as Arzuna—willing to sell herself just to enter the palace—stepped into the gilded splendor... and there was nothing you could do. You couldn't very well ask the Sultan to refuse his newly bought treasure.
The eunuch, oblivious to the subtle atmosphere or simply indifferent, merely nodded politely and turned away. All around you lingered the faint perfume from her, yet she never looked back, not even once.

5008244.title: Struggle Among Slave Girls
strings: Struggle Among Slave Girls

The Sultan does sometimes take an interest in his slave girls, and once, passing by Arzuna, his gaze lingers on her slender waist. Everyone notices—eunuchs, slave girls, scribes, and nobles. It's a flicker of hope... and a tightening noose. For the other slave girls, watching a peer rise is agony beyond killing.
Arzuna
You may do it yourself, or have a palace-eligible noble to take care of it.
Bribe the eunuch for just 5 Gold Coins.
This event will last for three days.
You can choose to help Arzuna, or ignore her. After all, she has brought palace life upon herself.
If you have a Stone-tier acquaintance in the harem, you might not need to intervene personally...
You steel yourself to ignore Arzuna's plight—and she has never counted on you anyway.
Arzuna's Charisma and Survival determine her pool of dice.
She needs at least 3 Success to win.
Sending a noble into the palace is the only way to help Arzuna. If your influence is great enough, it won't cost a coin.
With your power and influence, a single word to the eunuchs should suffice. They would surely not dare to take your money.
First Trial
Clumsy Act

Slave girls were everywhere in the harem. Despite Arzuna's beauty, elegance, and skill in dance, she had no stage to shine. She slept in the crowded dormitory, ate bland meals morning and night, and spent her days scrubbing floors, sweeping dust, wiping away blood... Then came the Sultan's fleeting glance. Arzuna barely had time to feel a spark of hope before the other slave girls struck. They doused her bedding with dirty water, snickering at the shadow of confusion and fury on her face, and at her fists clenching and unclenching.

The second night, the torment escalated. Dead insects were hidden in Arzuna's meals, and her delicate bangs were hacked into a mess while she slept. The other slave girls had decided to drag her deeper into the abyss—after all, none of them had ever been lucky enough to catch the Sultan's glance, to leap out of this pit of misery.

Arzuna clashed with another slave girl in the Lapis Lazuli Palace, yanking her hair until a patch of bloodied scalp came away.
It all "just so happened" to fall within the Sultan's gaze. Amused, he called Arzuna forward, chest out and head high—and then he recognized this beautiful slave girl with a slender waist...
That very night, Arzuna moved out of the crowded dormitory.
She managed to survive the first act of this brutal war.
You never heard from Arzuna again. Perhaps she fought and struggled with all her might, but war was merciless... Even the war of flowers was no exception.
Because of Your Past Help

Slave girls were everywhere in the harem. Despite Arzuna's beauty, elegance, and skill in dance, she had no stage to shine. She slept in the crowded dormitory, ate bland meals morning and night, and spent her days scrubbing floors, sweeping dust, wiping away blood... Then came the Sultan's fleeting glance. Arzuna barely had time to feel a spark of hope before the other slave girls struck. They doused her bedding with dirty water, snickering at the shadow of confusion and fury on her face, and at her fists clenching and unclenching.
At that moment, Fadia came to Arzuna's side, pulled her close, and shared a faintly scented pillow with her.
No one had expected Fadia to intervene—she was the most favored among the slave girls, a woman who had lain with the Sultan and lived to tell it!
Before sleep, Fadia lightly silenced the childish cruelty, her gaze lingering on a few guilty faces. She said no more, for that was enough.
Arzuna stood behind Fadia, protected by her small frame. It was an unfamiliar feeling. Arzuna wanted to smile, but tears glimmered in her eyes.

Slave girls were everywhere in the harem. Despite Arzuna's beauty, elegance, and skill in dance, she had no stage to shine. She slept in the crowded dormitory, ate bland meals morning and night, and spent her days scrubbing floors, sweeping dust, wiping away blood... Then came the Sultan's fleeting glance. Arzuna barely had time to feel a spark of hope before the other slave girls struck. They doused her bedding with dirty water, snickering as they waited to see her dismay or tears.
But there was none. Instead, a voice rang out, "Who drenched my bed will see their blood spill on theirs." The girls laughed it off. But the next morning, one of them lay lifeless. Blood gushed from her mouth and nose, soaking her pillow and blanket. Yet, her body bore no other wounds. Arzuna brushed by with a sneer, then set off to answer the Sultan's summons. No one knew what she whispered to delight the Sultan—only that the dangerous beauty never returned to the slave quarters.

That day, you sent a servant to the harem passage, bearing a golden bracelet and exquisite sweets in your name for the fattest, most arrogant eunuch.
No words were needed... Everything slid into place silently.
From then on, the young eunuchs patrolling the harem at night scolded any slave girls who messed with Arzuna's bedding and made sure no tampering reached her food. When an old eunuch caught a girl cutting Arzuna's hair, he thundered, "You are destroying the Sultan's property!"
The slave girls quickly learned their lesson. They still hated Arzuna—but now, their hatred was buried beneath the surface.

5008245.title: Toxic Flowers
strings: Toxic Flowers
The bribed eunuch has soon brought news: a few vile slave girls had spiked Arzuna's skincare cream, forcing her to stay veiled all day.
Arzuna
A potion is needed; she cannot face the Sultan with a face so swollen and red.
This event will last for three days.
You can choose to help Arzuna, or ignore her.
If you have a Bronze-tier acquaintance or a healer you know in the harem, you might not need to intervene personally...
You steel yourself to ignore Arzuna's plight, and she, in turn, resolves not to count on you.
Arzuna's Stealth and Physique determine her pool of dice.
She needs at least 3 Success to win.
Storm Under Her Control

Arzuna's face was swollen and red, making it impossible for her to show herself. In desperation, she begged a eunuch to deliver a message to you, hoping for your help—unaware that you had long known everything.
The rash on Arzuna's face flared worse, and another day drew her closer to serving the Sultan.

Arzuna had real skill.
She discovered what the other slave girls had mixed into her skincare cream. Then, quietly, she smeared it onto the beds of the schemers—and all those who had turned a blind eye.
The result was a spectacle: every low-ranking slave girl in the palace was scratching their skin raw, faces red and swollen.
The Sultan, astonished, asked the eunuchs what had happened. Before they could answer, Arzuna crawled forward on her knees.
"It was me, Your Majesty," she said. "They tried to ruin me, so I ruined them first."
The Sultan liked that answer. He laughed and told Arzuna to lift her head, curious to see her face. Arzuna wouldn't, revealing the rash on her arm instead. Normally, such defiance might have angered the Sultan, but a furious slave girl nearby suddenly lunged at Arzuna, trying to strangle her. The two women rolled across the floor before the Sultan. When others tried to intervene, he waved them off, watching with fascination as Arzuna slammed her rival's head into the floor until the girl foamed at the mouth.
"Send the physician to tend her face," the Sultan said before leaving.
With that, Arzuna gained the right to the court physician's care. She had officially become Concubine Arzuna.
Arzuna's face was ruined, and the Sultan would never waste his time on such a woman. She vanished without a trace, like a withered flower rotting in the mud.
Because of Your Past Help
No Big Deal

There were no secrets in this gilded cage, and the news soon reached Ansuya. She summoned Arzuna to her chamber, spoke at length, and handed her a healing salve—cruel mischief was no stranger in the harem.
Before long, rumors spread that Arzuna had earned Ansuya's favor. This concubine always lived quietly, under the radar, yet recently she had inexplicably won the Sultan's attention. No one dared provoke Ansuya, and naturally, they stayed away from Arzuna as well—any schemes now required greater finesse and craft.
That evening, as Arzuna clutched the salve in stunned awe, Ansuya smiled faintly and said, "If you want to thank anyone, thank your brother. He's helped me plenty."

As soon as you received the news, you wrote Samir a letter, asking him to look after your sister. By rights, a woman not yet titled shouldn't have access to the court physician—but Samir agreed. Soon, after a court session, you glimpsed your sister in the corridor. In that brief moment, she mouthed a silent "thank you", then hurried away. Samir later told you she was now Concubine Arzuna. She had moved out of her tiny corner in the harem and now lived along the stream that ran through the entire palace. Every night, the court physician and the eunuchs came to check on her needs.

The next day, the Sultan summoned his newly acquired woman. Arzuna, veiled in sheer red silk, nestled at his feet. With a smile, she recounted the clumsy trick played on her. "So?" Intrigued, the Sultan lifted her chin and squinted, as if to see through the veil the scar left by poisonous herbs. Arzuna smiled sweetly, letting him brush the veil aside. Beneath it lay a face decorated with blood—yes, blood—fresh and warm from the hearts of the vile slave girls plotting against her. Scarlet flowers bloomed on her skin, vivid enough to captivate the Sultan.
By the night's end, she had truly become Concubine Arzuna.
Remedies for Her
Stalling for Time

You filled a chest with remedies for everything—rashes, wounds, stomachaches, and colds—and sent it into the palace. Arzuna's face healed quickly; her restored beauty and alluring dances unsurprisingly won the Sultan's favor. Soon, she moved out of her tiny corner in the harem and lived along the stream that ran through the entire palace, with the court physician and eunuchs checking on her needs every night. Everyone addressed her as Concubine Arzuna. She never thanked you in person—it wouldn't do—but whenever you caught her distant figure in the corridor, she would give a quiet nod, her eyes soft and warm.

The moment Arzuna got the perfume, she understood your intention. She sprayed herself liberally, then sought out the eunuch arranging the Sultan's intimacies. Ten paces away, his face changed dramatically—torn between rushing forward and recoiling from the overwhelming scent. She strained to hold back a smile, and with a delicate, innocent air, told him that a few slave girls had caused her trouble. With a few coins pressed into his palm, she whispered tearful entreaties, all the while certain he wouldn't dare bring a stinking woman to the Sultan's bed. Heads would roll for that!
The result? Arzuna missed her chance to serve the Sultan that day. But it didn't matter. As long as she remained in the harem, as long as she was cautious—or bold—she would have a second or third chance to appear before him, to captivate his eyes with her most radiant face and dances, even if only for an instant.
Soon, she moved out of her tiny corner in the harem and lived along the stream that ran through the entire palace, with the court physician and eunuchs checking on her needs every night. Everyone addressed her respectfully as Concubine Arzuna.
She never thanked you in person—it wouldn't do—but whenever you caught her distant figure in the corridor, she would give a quiet nod, her smile a secret shared between you.

5008246.title: War of the Flowers
strings: War of the Flowers
The rumors about Arzuna spread like wildfire. Without a doubt, this newly favored consort finds herself caught in a fresh war, where birth and influence matter far more than beauty.
Concubine Arzuna
Any Gold intelligence.
Or, any love poem?
This event will last for three days.
You can choose to help Arzuna, or ignore her.
If you have a Silver-tier acquaintance in the harem, you might not need to intervene personally...
This is Arzuna's battle.
Arzuna's Stealth and Combat determine her pool of dice.
She needs at least 3 Success to win.
You need to place 3 pieces of Gold intelligence or any love poem.
Bloodied Hands

The stream that ran through the heart of the harem was flanked by lavish chambers, each with a bed exquisitely crafted. Every bed held a graceful beauty, waiting in desperate silence.
And then there was Arzuna, who had already received the Sultan's favor twice in her new chamber.
Why her?
Hadn't she just arrived?
Why not me?
Curse it...
If only she were dead!
Noblewomen who had once earned the Sultan's favor began to target Arzuna. They wouldn't let her share a single patch of shade with them. They mocked, humiliated, and spread rumors from their lips. Arzuna endured it all alone, silently, without a word.
No one in the entire harem spoke to Arzuna. She spent the whole day locked in her chamber, sitting silently... like the dead shadow of the once lively woman.

Something disgraceful had happened in the palace...
One of the noble concubines who had led Arzuna's ostracism was dead. Her body floated in the harem stream, petals and leaves scattered across her face, lending the scene an eerie beauty.
The eunuchs discovered she had been strangled. Someone had waited for her by the stream at midnight—nobody knew why she was there at that hour—and looped a rope around her neck from behind. After a desperate struggle, her last breath escaped.
Her maids wailed for the harem official to investigate, certain that Arzuna was responsible—surely it was! Weren't her nimble hands covered in blood from ropes? Wasn't her face pale? Hadn't she stormed past the victim the night before, whispering threats?
However, Arzuna bit her lip and said nothing.
The Sultan, stirred by the news, came himself to the stream and gazed at the corpse.
"Let it be, then. Give her parents some money and one audience." He grinned, leaning close to the corpse's grayish face. "At least this is a little entertainment. They should be proud of their daughter's sacrifice."
Everyone lowered their heads, not daring to speak a word. The Sultan stepped over the dead body and came to Arzuna, pinching her chin affectionately. His meaning was unmistakable—she was his favored woman now, and could do as she pleased.
Arzuna let her hands—the same hands that had killed—drop to her sides and knelt trembling in gratitude. Tears soaked the grass beside the corpse.
As the rumors slowly died down, you never heard a word of Arzuna again, as if she had never existed.
Because of Your Past Help
Ah... What an Annoying Noise

The stream that ran through the heart of the harem was flanked by lavish chambers, each with a bed exquisitely crafted. Every bed held a graceful beauty, waiting in desperate silence.
And then there was Arzuna, who had already received the Sultan's favor twice in her new chamber.
Why her?
Hadn't she just arrived?
Why not me?
Curse it...
If only she were dead!
Noblewomen who had once earned the Sultan's favor began to target Arzuna. They wouldn't let her share a single patch of shade with them. They mocked, humiliated, and spread rumors from their lips.
So when Sadani approached Arzuna, all those jealous, hostile, or indifferent women looked on with malicious delight. In this palace, what woman with any beauty hadn't felt the sting of Sadani's slap? How many vibrant corpses had been carried out by her eunuchs? She was the queen of competition, the mastermind behind the most ruthless tactics to ruin favored newcomers. And there she was, proud and haughty, stepping into the battlefield of flowers!
But to everyone's shock, Sadani did nothing. She simply sat with Arzuna, sipped her tea with an icy demeanor, nibbled on some pastries, and left without saying a word. The next day, Sadani ordered the eunuchs to toss all of Arzuna's plain pastries into the stream and, with a raised chin, demanded her own be brought. She then shared them with Arzuna. Soon, another bold concubine sent her treats, then another, then another. One by one, the women began to gather in that small patch of shade, as if nothing had ever happened.
Arzuna knew well: Sadani had cleared away all those biting daggers, which forced Arzuna to smile despite the pain. Later, Arzuna visited the feared concubine, offering gifts in thanks. With an unreadable face, Sadani only told Arzuna that the gratitude was meant for someone else. Who? She didn't say. Let this infuriatingly beautiful woman figure it out herself.

The stream that ran through the heart of the harem was flanked by lavish chambers, each with a bed exquisitely crafted. Every bed held a graceful beauty, waiting in desperate silence.
And then there was Arzuna, who had already received the Sultan's favor twice in her new chamber.
Why her?
Hadn't she just arrived?
Why not me?
Curse it...
If only she were dead!
Noblewomen who had once earned the Sultan's favor began to target Arzuna. They wouldn't let her share a single patch of shade with them. They mocked, humiliated, and spread rumors from their lips. But Arzuna merely smiled, unfazed. She curtsied to the smug concubines and returned to her chamber. The women laughed, boasting as if victorious.
Go ahead, laugh, talk—by tomorrow, all this noise would vanish.
Soon, one by one, they fell to a mysterious sickness. Madness overtook them; they clawed at their skin, tore at their flesh, and howled until they could breathe no more. The most arrogant among them lasted longest, but the terror of death led her first into the river. She was rescued, but already insane.
What a pity. Arzuna sat in her small patch of shade, watching with a cold smile as the eunuchs dragged her rival away. No one shared her shade now—but neither did anyone dare to whisper another word. How sweet the silence.
Master of Tricks
Touching Poem

Heh, the games of the harem were nothing but child's play to you. And really, who in there even cared about Arzuna's status? No need for explanations at all. You simply let a few rumors slip: about the shocking, half-true family scandals of the few concubines leading Arzuna's ostracism. They scrambled for days, desperate to figure out whom they had offended, but all their investigations led nowhere—of course. Your manipulations were far cleaner than theirs, and you never gloated over such trivialities. In the end, these nobles paid for their loose tongues. Mountains of gold flowed into the Sultan's hands. In high spirits, he favored the most agreeable concubine, the gold transforming into the embroidery on her veil and rubies around her wrists. She performed a dazzling dance for the Sultan, and the favor she earned soared even higher.

You had Hassan craft a stirring poem and spin a tearful backstory for Arzuna. With your subtle push, the tale spread like wildfire, even reaching the harem. How could Arzuna not seize such a perfect opportunity? She composed herself, playing helpless, fragile, and tender as she poured her heart out to the Sultan...
That very night, she received a lavish pair of gem-encrusted bracelets.

5008247.title: Fine Tea
strings: Fine Tea
Petals sent by Arzuna, perfect for brewing tea.
Royal Night-Blend Tea
Taste the tea yourself.
Invite any consort to tea.
This can resolve one Wife's Resentment.
You can enjoy them with your consort.
To soothe your wife, you need to invite her to join.
With petals this sweet and tea this fragrant, it was a shame to enjoy them alone.
Petals Delivered to Maggie
Petals Delivered to [s3.name]

Maggie beamed, proud as ever of her tea expertise.
She blended the petals with exotic leaves, brewed them just right, and sweetened the pot with a touch of honey. Soon, a fragrant pot of flowering tea was ready.
Under the pomegranate tree, you sipped, chatted, and relaxed together. What a rare, lovely moment.

Fatuna brewed the petals into a bitter tea—not to most young tastes, yet you found it strangely enjoyable.
You shared tea and lingered in light conversation together.
What a rare moment of ease.

Nayla didn't know the first thing about brewing tea, but she had a full set of gem-encrusted gilded teaware.
Excitedly, she brought it out, had a maid brew the tea, and watched as the amber liquid poured into the cups.
"Ah, isn't it beautiful?"
She handed you the cup, and together you breathed in the scent of gold and petals...
What a delightful tea.

Shama was skilled at brewing tea—a necessary art for any noblewoman.
She blended it with a touch of strong liquor, then added milk and honey, creating a drink rich beyond words.
You sipped and chatted in the bedroom, and before you knew it, your bodies had intertwined.
What a delightful moment.

Junah brewed tea using only these petals—nothing more. It was little more than warm water, with a faint, elusive aroma lingering on the surface.
Then she dipped silk into the tea and gently wiped your skin, bit by bit: starting from your face, down to your neck, chest, abdomen, and beyond...
The fragrance of the petals bloomed on both of you, making it an unforgettable moment.

Jalila had never learned to make tea properly, but she put her own, well... clever mind to it, adding something she thought you would enjoy. Well...
You had an absolutely wonderful time that night.

Inal put the petals into the teapot, followed by some fresh, red berries... She knew exactly how to brew it to achieve the perfect balance of sweet and sour, having once studied diligently by borrowing another's discerning palate to please her mistress. The resulting tea was a vivid red, and she fought hard not to cry in front of you and ruin the moment.
Any rift between you temporarily vanished in the sweet, rising steam.

5008248.title: Nightly Privileges
strings: Nightly Privileges

The war between Concubine Arzuna and Zazie has begun, their battlefield being the Sultan's limited attention each night. On many nights that should have been Arzuna's turn, the Sultan would approach her chamber door—only to see the naked Zazie suddenly appear beside him, adorned with gold chains, covered in petals, and glistening with essential oil. On those nights, Concubine Arzuna could only watch as the Sultan turned to caress Zazie, before being pulled into her room...
Concubine Arzuna
A noble with influence in the court, with both Magic and Charisma of 5 and above.
Deceive with astrology.
This event will last for three days.
You can choose to help Arzuna, or ignore her.
Arzuna attempts to launch a counterattack.
Arzuna's Physique and Survival determine her pool of dice.
She needs at least 4 Success to win.
The Sultan's favor was quietly slipping through Arzuna's powerless fingers. Listening to the sounds of merriment—real or imagined—she lay awake night after night.
Arzuna could bear it no longer. She had to take action. But... but what could she do? What should she do?

You heard that Concubine Arzuna had bided her time. Waiting until the Sultan left Zazie's chambers—in the early hours of the next morning—she stepped out from the rosebushes, her robe open, revealing her bare body... with only three roses placed strategically. These roses had even been plucked from the rose tree outside Zazie's door.
Zazie stared at her, her face dark with fury, following closely behind the Sultan. But Arzuna acted as if she did not see her at all. She began to dance, laughing as she asked the Sultan: My ruler, the mightiest of men, the tireless eagle, the Sultan, do you content yourself with only one woman in a single night?
The Sultan arrived late to the audience that morning.
After waiting in the flower bushes all night, Arzuna caught a cold. But of course, it was all worth it.

You heard that some foolish harem woman hid naked in the flower bushes, trying to seduce the Sultan... She waited the entire night, soaked by the morning dew. Yet as the sun rose, the Sultan never came. Instead, she was struck by a severe cold.
She died. Her chambers were immediately cleared to make way for the next favored concubine.

Then, on another night when Zazie prepared to welcome the Sultan's favor, Concubine Arzuna danced in their courtyard. Several slave girls stood at each corner of the garden, each holding a golden basin. With her dance, her arms, and her long, powerful, graceful silk sleeves, Arzuna dipped into the rich juice, painting streaks of deep red across the night sky, the garden, and the faces of every slave trying hard to suppress their fear. The Sultan watched intently for a moment. At that moment, Arzuna's slender waist naturally leaned into the sovereign's palm as she twirled and took delicate steps. That night, it was Concubine Zazie who stood pale with rage down the garden corridor until dawn.

In the Sultan's court, there were several astrologers so old that no one knew their exact ages. Your family had once helped recommend a few of them, and they still remembered your kindness. You sought out the oldest among them, hoping he would slip a little favor into his astrological readings... You told him Arzuna's date of birth—and he caught your drift at once and nodded.
A few days later, the eunuchs suddenly went around asking every woman in the harem for her date of birth. The women answered, confused yet curious. Then the Chief Harem Official announced that the Sultan would spend the next few nights exclusively with Arzuna.
Everyone was astonished, but no one dared to ask further. And just like that, Arzuna had won another round.
Afterward, Concubine Arzuna sent you a flower basket from the palace, filled with fresh blooms from the imperial garden, still damp with morning dew.
Hidden at the bottom of the basket was a letter.
"Thanks to your help, I have even begun to enjoy these struggles. I am starting to understand why Zaziei is Zazie, and why the Sultan is the Sultan. They are alike, and I am different from them. Without you, I could never see this through to the end."
The letter was written in delicate, elegant script—certainly dictated to an educated eunuch. This meant Concubine Arzuna was beginning to build her own power in the harem.

5008249.title: More Expensive Beauty
strings: More Expensive Beauty

Zazie flaunted a ruby as large as an egg. Everyone at court knew: the bigger the jewel, the higher her status in the harem—not only for the difficulty of obtaining it, but also for the courage to wear it openly.
If Arzuna was to win this battle, she needed to be more expensively beautiful.
Arzuna
Any accessory inlaid with large, high-grade gems.
This event will last for three days.
You can choose to help Arzuna, or ignore her.
Arzuna attempts to launch a counterattack.
Arzuna's Physique and Charisma determine the pool of dice.
You need at least 5 Success to win.
Needs 2 accessories that meet the requirement.
A Ridiculous Farce
A Foolish Farce
Faced with Zazie's arrogant display, Arzuna's silence only made her seem weaker and paler.
Arzuna could bear it no longer. She had to take action. But... but what could she do? What should she do?

You heard that Arzuna had managed to steal some of Zazie's jewels, then altered them slightly and pinned them to her chest.
Zazie flew into a rage. She immediately stormed into Arzuna's chambers with her eunuchs and slave girls, dragged Arzuna by the hair, threw her to the ground, then seized Arzuna's jewelry box and left. Arzuna managed to hide her most precious pieces and struck one of Zazie's slave girls, but that was the end of her resistance. Having stolen first, she knew she was in the wrong.
Zazie won this fight completely. Yet Arzuna did not truly lose—she kept her life, and because the silly farce amused the Sultan, she was even given a proper ruby as a reward.

You heard that a theft had been caught red-handed in the harem: one favored concubine had tried to steal another's jewels...
By the Sultan's law, a thief caught in the act could even be beaten to death by the victim without punishment. So how could the clever Zazie let such an opportunity slip?

No one knew where Arzuna had gotten it, but the day after Zazie flaunted her gem, Arzuna produced an even larger, deeper, more brilliant ruby. She wore it on her wrist, and when she moved, it looked like flowing blood.
It was said that several of her slave girls had vanished. But such things happened often in the court and drew no attention.

You had someone send the [s2.name] and [s3.name]—inlaid with large, dazzling gems—into the royal palace. Their breathtaking beauty befits the title of a favored concubine. Wearing these jewels paired with a pure gold waist chain, Arzuna only needed to sway her hips and waist while dancing to capture the Sultan's gaze.
Just as you and she had planned, Concubine Arzuna stole the show at the harem banquet.
She removed all other jewelry, wearing only the gem-studded waist chain, and chose deliberately plain, solid-colored garments. She twisted and turned in the moonlight, dancing right before the Sultan, her waist glittering brilliantly—it was a sight almost too beautiful for this world...
At the banquet, the Sultan had already begun fondling Arzuna's slim waist and breasts. To all the other women, including Zazie, their own lavish jewels suddenly seemed worthless.

5008250.title: A Contest of Bedchamber Skills
strings: A Contest of Bedchamber Skills

This was Zazie's ultimate weapon: she respected her opponent, so she held nothing back. On the nights the Sultan visited her, she doubled down on her already legendary skills that kept him spellbound. For several nights, they stayed together until dawn, leaving the Sultan yawning repeatedly at court the next day.
After days like this, Arzuna received far fewer summons... After all, a well-fed lion loses interest in antelope. Arzuna was only a dancer after all; when it came to pleasuring the Sultan... she might need further instruction.
Concubine Arzuna
You may ask the Lady of Delights to teach her skills and experience.
Madam Buthayna can be hired for just 20 gold coins.
This event will last for three days.
You can choose to help Arzuna, or ignore her.
Arzuna attempts to launch a counterattack.
Arzuna's Physique and Charisma determine her pool of dice.
She needs at least 6 Success to win.
You must summon Lady of Delights, or pay to have Buthayna enter the palace to assist.
Once again, Arzuna waited in vain for the Sultan's summons that day.

Arzuna could not just sit and wait! Frantic, she rummaged wildly through her chambers, hurling her dance gowns and jewelry to the floor in a rage. This one won't do, neither will this—none of it is any use!

It was said that during one night with the Sultan, Concubine Arzuna had performed a "union" in a "dance-like pose," which made the Sultan roar with laughter.
It may not have been the most pleasurable position for a ruler, but it was new, something he had never seen before. And the mix of desperation and flattery on Arzuna's face as she performed such an indecent act thrilled a man—at least a man like the Sultan.
From that day on, the Sultan stayed with Arzuna for nights on end. He forced the former dancer to twist her soft body into all kinds of positions... moves that had once been her pride, but now took on a lewd meaning.
For now, let us set aside dignity and pride—at the very least, she had turned the tide, and won back his favor, if only temporarily.

Uh... the strangest news has arrived.
It was said that Arzuna tried to contort herself into new positions to please the Sultan in bed, but accidentally injured his royal manhood... Good heavens, her death was beyond brutal! The only mercy was that the Sultan did not take revenge on you, the one who had brought her to the palace.
A Stimulating Aid

Just as the Sultan was about to draw aside Zazie's bed curtains, he caught an intriguing, alluring scent. It was hazy, tempting, like a veiled woman on a moonless night, waiting for her layers of mist to be peeled away. The Sultan smiled thoughtfully. After being with Zazie once, he turned without hesitation and strode into Arzuna's chambers. The dancer sat gently in the dark, smiling, ready to receive him.

That day, your concubine accidentally got lost in the palace and met the kind Concubine Arzuna. They talked happily in the garden, and before parting, the noble concubine even sent servants to guide her back.
Well, after that, you heard the Sultan spent more and more nights in Arzuna's chambers. She really was a dancer. Skillfully controlling her beautiful body was a skill the Lady of Delights had to train hard for, but for Arzuna, it came easily—she understood at once... she learned very quickly.

You knew the perfect person for this task: Madam Buthayna, the owner of the House of Delights.
You sent a servant to fetch her to your manor. The madam thought you'd suddenly developed some strange taste or refined lust, so she dressed herself up to be both coquettish and ridiculous.
After hearing your request, the elderly madam froze for a moment, then tore off her expensive silk headscarf and burst out laughing: "Live long enough, and you really will see everything! A high official of the Sultan asking a madam to teach a favored concubine how to move her hips seductively in bed!"
She laughed so hard she choked on her own saliva... After a violent coughing fit, she tied the scarf around her waist like an ordinary old woman on the street, then loudly ordered your servants to bring paper and a brush.
You asked cautiously, "You... can read and write?"
"Read and write? Why would I need to? I'm not some poor poet-prostitute. The things that go on in bed—I can explain them without a single word!"
You watched her grip the brush as she would a piece of food and scribble roughly on the paper... Soon you realized she was drawing nothing but, well... men and women in those acts.
"Here—most men never get this part stimulated... I know some brothels teach their girls this. When a client lasts too long and delays her next customer, she hits this spot suddenly, and no matter how tough he is, he'll finish at once... And this—lie flat like this, then lift your legs up—did I draw that right? At this angle, his manhood is wrapped in something soft and warm, and she can push with her stomach. I drew it like this; she'll understand..."
You stared dumbfounded as she finished the crude but practical scroll of erotic art. After it was secretly delivered to Arzuna, you heard the Sultan spent more and more nights in her chambers. For a former dancer, skillfully moving her beautiful body was the easiest thing of all... she learned very quickly.

5008251.title: The Crowded Throne
strings: The Crowded Throne

On this day, the Sultan brought both Arzuna and Zazie to the Lapis Lazuli Palace.
The two concubines sat on either side of the throne, both heavily made-up, exuding exotic fragrances, and posing alluringly. Neither so much as glanced at the other.
"My lords and ladies, you may raise your heads and look," the Sultan said, in high spirits. "Come, tell me—who is more beautiful: Zazie or Arzuna?" When no one dared to answer, he casually pointed at you. "[player.name], you may speak first."
Concubine Arzuna
Concubine Zazie
You believe Zazie is more beautiful.
You believe Arzuna is more beautiful.
Your Magic can aid the one you choose to support.
The trumpet for the final battle between Zazie and Arzuna has sounded.
Your Magic and all the Attributes of the one you support determine the pool of dice.
You need at least 2 Success to win.
Will you support Zazie or Arzuna? You must choose.

Sometimes silence is a choice, especially given the tangled ties between you and Arzuna.
Zazie laughed wildly, while Arzuna's face turned ashen, and fell speechless for a long moment... In that brief moment of weakness, Zazie struck and exploited it. In the harem, countless bloodless battles unfolded silently. Even a small retreat could spell eternal doom. Arzuna vanished from the harem. You never knew if she fell from favor or died. You heard nothing more of her.
Concubine Zazie Is More Beautiful
I Believe Concubine Arzuna Is More Beautiful

You respectfully replied that Concubine Zazie was undoubtedly the more beautiful.
She had been with the Sultan the longest, knew best how to please him, and had granted him so many wondrous pleasures... You firmly declared that there was only one measure of a woman's beauty: whether she was favored by the Sultan.
Your answer greatly pleased the Sultan. Knowing you were the one who had recommended Concubine Arzuna, he had tested you to see if you would favor the girl you had brought to court...
"Ah, no—I won't accept this!" Concubine Arzuna suddenly let out a sharp cry. She threw herself onto the Sultan, rubbing her soft skin against his hair. "I won't lose—Your Majesty, tell them! Just as Lord [player.name] said—tell me, who do you think is more beautiful: Zazie or me?"

At once, Arzuna feigned surprise and delight.
"Oh, you flatter me. I think Lady Zazie is more beautiful..." She deliberately emphasized the word "Lady." "After all, she is more experienced, having served Your Majesty for so long. Surely you find her more comforting?"
Zazie's face turned as dark as thunder. She toyed gently with the Sultan's hair, then pressed herself against him, caressing him intimately...
"Your Majesty, what do you say? I care not what others think—only your judgment. Between that girl and me, who do you prefer?"

The Sultan squeezed Zazie's hip with one hand and tilted Arzuna's chin up with the other.
His gaze drifted between the two women, as if judging and weighing... while reveling in the power to decide their fates as he pleased...
The hall fell deathly silent. Everyone held their breath, awaiting the outcome of the struggle.

"You both please me greatly, but..." The Sultan smiled, pinching Zazie hard enough to draw a soft cry. "I do prefer you, my beloved Zazie."
Zazie lit up, radiant, nearly floating with joy. And Arzuna? She was crushed, defeated, her breath coming short and fast.
"Your Majesty, you will grant your dearest one a small wish, won't you?" Zazie purred, kissing his cheek. "There is something I desire!"
"Speak." 
She leaned close to the Sultan's ear and whispered sweetly. He roared with laughter. He slapped Zazie's bottom playfully, lifted her light frame, and strode toward the inner chambers. No one dared follow—not you, not the courtiers, not the despairing Arzuna.

"I am not a man of sentiment," the Sultan said, pulling Arzuna tighter against him. "You please me most now, Concubine Arzuna." 
Arzuna blossomed! One look at her face and anyone would think she loved him madly—yet you knew the truth: she loved only power, and this victory.
"Your Majesty, I am overjoyed—I love you so! As a woman loved by you, may I ask for one small favor?" Blushing shyly, she whispered into his ear. And the ruler, in high spirits, was happy to grant her anything.

5008252.title: I want her beautiful head
strings: I want her beautiful head
Soon, all of you learned what wish Concubine Zazie had asked of the Sultan.
Arzuna

"I want Arzuna's head! She is so beautiful—does she not think herself prettier than me? I want her lovely head!"
And so, Arzuna was executed. Her head was placed in Zazie's chambers, eyes wide open, watching every moment of the Sultan and Zazie that night.

5008253.title: Dance of the Headless
strings: Dance of the Headless
Soon, all of you learned what wish Concubine Zazie had asked of the Sultan.
Arzuna

"I want Arzuna's head! She is so beautiful—does she not think herself prettier than me? I want her lovely head!"
And so, Arzuna was executed, even before your eyes. Her beautiful head was severed by the guards. Yet strangely, her headless body did not fall. Instead, her limbs twitched, twisted, and—as if controlled by some unseen force—performed the most exquisite dance you had ever seen... Yours, Zazie's, more and more headless bodies joined the surreal performance. Before the Priest of the Purist could burn you all with magic, as your frantic consciousness faded, you heard nothing but the Sultan's mad laughter.

5008254.title: The Favorite's Wish
strings: The Favorite's Wish
Arzuna had won the war. Now she was entitled to voice her wish to the Sultan.
Arzuna
I Want the Head of Lord [player.name]
All Is Forgiven

You looked up in shock, meeting her cold, hateful gaze—no more pretense, no more hiding.
"[player.name], I hate you," she said, twirling the golden ring on her wrist—a habit you once found charming, but now... it sent chills down your spine. "Not only because your father deceived, betrayed, and hurt my mother. Not only because your family ignored us all these years. Not only because you used and humiliated me... but because after I entered the palace, when I needed you most—even when I was useful to you—you still stood by and did nothing. How does that saying go? More harmful than our enemies are the friends who refuse to help us."
She smiled, confident of victory, and leaned against the Sultan's shoulder. But to her surprise, the Sultan refused her. "Absolutely not! He still has to play games with me!" With that, he plucked the golden crown from Zazie's head and placed it on Arzuna's... He looked at you with an amused smile—perfect, perfect. With Arzuna's murderous gaze, he had another tool to torment you.

"I want Lady Zazie's golden crown! I've loved it for so long! Please, I just have to have it! After all, everything she has is yours, and everything in the empire is yours. Just reassign what's yours and give it to me, please? Your Majesty! Your Majesty!" 
The Sultan laughed at her tease. Then he turned, reached over, and casually took the golden crown from Zazie's head, placing it on Arzuna.
Zazie's hair fell loose... her face ashen. She slid off the throne and said not a word.
Everything continued as before. Audiences proceeded; the Sultan ruled. The only difference was that the Golden Throne was no longer crowded.

After Arzuna won the Sultan's deep favor, you spent days on edge, terrified she might mention your past conflicts and turn the Sultan against you. During court, you avoided looking toward the Sultan's side. But nothing happened.
Then you began to hope that Arzuna might remember your help and speak well of you to the Sultan... But Concubine Arzuna acted as if her world revolved only around the Sultan, completely ignoring your hints. Well, perhaps this was already a good outcome for you. You tried to convince yourself, feeling both disappointed and relieved.

5008255.title: The Thorn of the Rose
strings: The Thorn of the Rose
Humiliated, Zazie would never let Arzuna go—just as Arzuna would never forgive Zazie. So... whom will you help?
Arzuna is in the full flush of triumph.
Zazie is itching for action.
You side with Arzuna.
You side with Zazie.
This event will last for two days.
A conspiracy against Arzuna is brewing.
Will you and your chosen ally win?
Arzuna's Survival and Wisdom determine her pool of dice.
Your and your ally's Survival and Wisdom determine the pool of dice.
Arzuna needs at least 2 Success to survive.
You need at least 2 Success for a favorable outcome.
Choose to help Arzuna or Zazie.
Hesitation
Arzuna Did Not Grow Careless
To Victory, Eternal as Gold
You have little time left to think and choose.

That day, she noticed an unfamiliar eunuch preparing her meal. Suspicious, she forced him to taste the pastries he had made... and discovered he had been bribed by Zazie, along with a packet of poison.
She went to the Sultan, overjoyed—yet appearing terrified on the surface—claiming that Zazie had intended to assassinate him. The meal was meant for him, she said; if she had not uncovered the plot, his life would have been in danger. Such a thing was unforgivable—everyone ought to serve the Sultan with all their heart!
The Sultan agreed.
Zazie was executed. Her body was taken to a remote graveyard outside the city. Before the jewels could be removed, beggars, vagrants, and thieves dug her up and stripped her naked. Birds and beasts feasted on the soft skin once touched only by the emperor, and worms made their home in her once-beautiful eyes.
This was the end of one of the Sultan's favorite concubines.

Arzuna was overjoyed. She even held a lavish feast to celebrate her triumph. During the banquet, she drank heavily and tasted rare delicacies... then died in agony.
The Sultan was furious. A woman's death meant little, but he had only just declared her his favorite. This murder felt like an insult to his authority.
All eunuchs and maids present at the feast who had helped prepare the food were forced to take the same poison and buried with Concubine Arzuna.
It took nearly three days to fill the empty positions for the grand palace. Three days later, the silence was broken. For another woman—golden and brilliant, yet temporarily overshadowed by Arzuna—had soothed the enraged Sultan.
The empire carried on as usual. The Sultan sought fresh diversions once more.
You Warned Arzuna Not to Get Carried Away
As You Wish
One Move Short

Nevertheless, Arzuna knew you were right. That day, she noticed an unfamiliar eunuch preparing her meal. Suspicious, she forced him to taste the pastries he had made... and discovered he had been bribed by Zazie, along with a packet of poison.
She went to the Sultan, overjoyed—yet appearing terrified on the surface—claiming that Zazie had intended to assassinate him. The meal was meant for him, she said; if she had not uncovered the plot, his life would have been in danger. Such a thing was unforgivable—everyone ought to serve the Sultan with all their heart!
The Sultan agreed.
Zazie was executed. Her body was taken to a remote graveyard outside the city. Before the jewels could be removed, beggars, vagrants, and thieves dug her up and stripped her naked. Birds and beasts feasted on the soft skin once touched only by the emperor, and worms made their home in her once-beautiful eyes.
This was the end of one of the Sultan's favorite concubines.

Nevertheless, Arzuna knew you were right. But despite her vigilance, a poisoned cup... or a poisoned pastry... still took her life.
The Sultan was furious. A woman's death meant little, but he had only just declared her his favorite. This murder felt like an insult to his authority.
All eunuchs and maids present at the feast who had helped prepare the food were forced to take the same poison and buried with Concubine Arzuna.
It took nearly three days to fill the empty positions for the grand palace. Three days later, the silence was broken. For another woman—golden and brilliant, yet temporarily overshadowed by Arzuna—had soothed the enraged Sultan.
The empire carried on as usual. The Sultan sought fresh diversions once more.

Arzuna was more cautious than you expected—or perhaps the gods favored her. She sharply noticed an unfamiliar eunuch preparing her meal and grew suspicious. She forced him to taste the pastries he had made... and discovered he had been bribed by Zazie, along with a packet of poison.
She went to the Sultan, overjoyed—yet appearing terrified—claiming that Zazie had intended to assassinate him. The meal was meant for him; if she had not uncovered the plot, his life would have been in danger. Such a thing was unforgivable—everyone ought to serve the Sultan with all their heart!
The Sultan thought she was right.
Zazie was executed. Her body was taken to a remote graveyard outside the city. Before the jewels could be removed, beggars, vagrants, and thieves dug her up and stripped her naked. Birds and beasts feasted on the soft skin once touched only by the emperor, and worms made their home in her once-beautiful eyes.
Fortunately, you stayed completely out of sight. No one knew you had once turned a blade of malice against your favored sister.

5008256.title: The Only Favorite
strings: The Only Favorite
You heard that Arzuna's favor had risen even higher.
Concubine Arzuna

At last, Concubine Arzuna moved into the chambers once occupied by Zazie. The rooms lay at the source of the stream running through the harem, closest to the Lapis Lazuli Court, with fragrant roses blooming outside.
She had expected a brutal fight with the empire's most skilled seductress... but now her greatest rival was gone.
Concubine Arzuna spent days savoring her victory... and of course, the Sultan stayed with her every night.

5008257.title: Submission
strings: Submission
You actually intend to consider questions of this magnitude? What use are you to the great Creator? How will you serve this new master—err, sheep?
In What Manner Will You Serve Them?
Like The Servants
Like The Books
Like The Jewelry Pieces
Like This Weapon
Like a Wife...
Like a Path...
You Are Completely Clueless

You bowed humbly and declared you would serve it as a slave, as a servant.
Your words pleased the great sheep. "Baa-baa-baa-baa-baa!" It laughed loudly, and the clouds roiled with its voice. "Back when I still walked the earth, I heard such words often... Baa-baa-baa! How nostalgic! When I create a world of my own using the power I stole from you—sorry about that, baa, ha-ha-ha-baa!—I'll do it all again!"
The sheep then fixed you with its enormous eyes, gazing meaningfully. "And so, as my slave... how do you wish me to treat you?"
The judgment was not over. Behind you, the sea of clouds still waited to devour you into the hell of regurgitation. You had to think of an answer—desperately, quickly, immediately.

You promised you would record and spread its fame, making it the greatest god in history!
Your words seemed to stir memories the sheep preferred to forget.
"Baa-baa-baa... There were many books and poems about me once, but... but those two erased everything when they fought! Nothing remained! I don't have the time to waste guarding this boring world like those foolish stars... But things will be different now! I've stolen such great power from you. You've worked so hard for me, baa-ha-ha-ha! From now on, I will have my own world!"
It paused, its enormous eyes fixed on you. "If... very well... if I let you follow me... then how do you wish me to treat you?"
The judgment was not over. Behind you, the sea of clouds still waited to devour you into the hell of regurgitation. You had to think of an answer—desperately, quickly, immediately.

You told it that a god naturally needed followers, just as a noble lady needed jewels on her wrist. You were a powerful noble caught in the Sultan's games, one who could seize the power of two gods with the Dragon's Eye. Were you not the most dazzling jewel to show off?
"Baa—baa-ha-ha-ha-ha!" the sheep roared with laughter. "Well said, baa! They do love grand retinues—the more humans there are, the lower their total intelligence, and the easier they are to control! Since I will use your Dragon's Eye to build my own new world—sorry, baa, you've worked so hard, baa—then it is only fitting that you come along."
It laughed again, gloating, before continuing. "Very well. I ask you: if I accept your loyalty, how do you wish me to treat you?"
The judgment was not over. Behind you, the sea of clouds still waited to devour you into the hell of regurgitation. You had to think of an answer—desperately, quickly, immediately.

You told it you could be its weapon, its tool and its instrument. With you, it can achieve all it wants without getting its hands dirty. You will sacrifice everything to safeguard its world.
Your words made the sea of clouds pause for a moment. The sheep's golden eyes scanned you up and down—only then did you realize the sea held far more than one pair of golden eyes. The sheep was watching you from every angle, every direction.
"Some other things would indeed be more convenient, but maintaining a 'weapon' like you would require extra effort. Baa, I possess such immense power now—thanks to you, baa-ha-ha! I intercepted it, sorry about that, baa! What kind of weapon could I not obtain? Baa..."
It opened several more eyes, staring intently at you. "If I mercifully allow you to follow me and be my weapon, how do you wish me to treat you?"
The judgment was not over. Behind you, the sea of clouds still waited to devour you into the hell of regurgitation. You had to think of an answer—desperately, quickly, immediately.

You spoke softly, telling it you could keep it company, ease its boredom, amuse it, handle its affairs, and manage its possessions. You would be its most loyal companion.
The sheep widened all its eyes—perhaps a thousand of them—staring at you. "You think a sheep needs a wife? A sheep? A wife? Even if I really were a sheep—oh, even if I were truly a sheep, I suppose I would need one... baa... I've never thought of it this way! Oh! I'm still too inexperienced as a Creator. I never even considered this!"
It seemed thrilled. The clouds twisted violently, nearly swallowing you at once. Seeing you scramble to dodge, the culprit burst out laughing: "Now that I've stolen such great power from you—oh baa, sorry about that. It took you so much effort to gather it all, didn't it? Baa-ha-ha-ha—I can create a whole world for myself. Having a wife sounds nice, baa! Or a husband? Or a spouse? Ah-ha—anyway, it sounds good!"
It paused, seeming to seriously consider the idea. "So... if I allow you to follow me as my companion, how do you wish me to treat you?"
The judgment was not over. Behind you, the sea of clouds still waited to devour you into the hell of regurgitation. You had to think of an answer—desperately, quickly, immediately.

You used the old world's magic as an example—many miracles in the world relied on Aether, and even gods needed it to interfere with the mortal realm!
Seen this way, the old gods letting this precious substance scatter naturally was an incredibly crude design. But you could now assign a humble servant to fix this oversight.
The clouds fell silent at your words. Lamblet thought for a long time, even summoning Aether that drifted between the clouds like droplets of water!
"Truly, this would be more convenient... safer. But why would I entrust such an important duty to you? I used you to gain the power to create a world. Why would I give any of it back, even a small part, for you to manage? What do you want? How do you wish me to treat you, baa?"

While you were absorbed in thought, Lamblet suddenly attacked and knocked you from the clouds. Amid a long string of shrill "baa-ha-ha" laughter, it soared higher, leaving you to watch helplessly, powerless to stop it.

5008258.title: Expectation
strings: Expectation

You have chosen to follow the great Creator—one that claimed its throne by stealing your strength and harvesting your fruits—and now, in its mercy, allows you to follow. Tell me, how do you expect it to treat you? Or more precisely, how far do you think its tolerance extends?
How do you expect the Creator to treat you?
Like a Meal
Like a Pet
Like a Child
You Are Completely Clueless

You gritted your teeth and told it to treat you like food. You could nourish it; after all, you possessed strength and ideas, did you not? You even had the Dragon's Eye! Your tiny power could surely serve it... You want it to just think of you as a dessert!
"Dessert! Baa-ha! Dessert! A hero with the Dragon's Eye says they're just a little dessert!" The sheep roared with laughter again, and the small cloud-creatures around it joined in. But when they laughed too hard, their shapes came undone, the clouds unconsciously reforming into generals, priests, kings, dictators—all kinds of murderers. "Very well, I will treat you as a tasty snack. I will make good use of your power... you're right, this will be useful to me, baa-baa-baa-baa —"
The louder its laughter, the weaker the pressure on you became. You could stand a little straighter.
"Ah, but baa... since you seem so interested and full of ideas about creating a world—ah baa, sorry, I forgot again. After all, you're the one who gathered all this power. You were supposed to be the Creator, baa-ha-ha—so what do you think? Who should be my enemy, baa? After all, enemies create friends, and hatred gives rise to love, doesn't it?"
Its enemy? The enemy of the new world? Before you could even breathe easy, you had to think once more...

You told it to treat you just as humans treat cute animals and pets—you wanted nothing more.
"I know exactly how that works, baa-ha-ha-ha —" The sheep laughed again, and the little cloud creatures around it joined in. But when they laughed too hard, their shapes came undone, the clouds unconsciously reforming into generals, priests, kings, dictators—all kinds of murderers. "Very well, I'll treat you like a little creature, just as cute as me, baa. Or rather, no human can be as cute as me, for humans are not very cute by nature, baa-baa-baa-baa—fine, I'll leash you, feed you grass, and teach you a few tricks now and then!"
The louder its laughter, the weaker the pressure on you became. You could stand a little straighter.
"Ah, but baa... since you seem so interested and full of ideas about creating a world—ah baa, sorry, I forgot again. After all, you're the one who gathered all this power. You were supposed to be the Creator, baa-ha-ha—so what do you think? Who should be my enemy, baa? After all, enemies create friends, and hatred gives rise to love, doesn't it?"
Its enemy? The enemy of the new world? Before you could even breathe easy, you had to think once more...

You wondered what a sheep that created the world would want to hear. Since it led a legion of strange creatures... you tentatively spoke the word "child."
You told it that compared to its ancient, immense power, you were merely a child who had existed for mere decades—not even a child, at most a precocious infant! So you hoped it would guide you, teach you, treat you like its own child...
Your words made the sheep and the clouds around it pause. Then they slowly gathered, as if thinking and discussing.
"I am not yet a god. Only those who have created a world—and those two shameless castaways—can call themselves gods, baa. But... since you gave me your power, I can create my own world. I will be a god, baa. And a god... should probably have divine offspring."
They surged toward you, pressing in from all sides.
"You helped me become a god, baa, so it would only be fitting for you to be my divine offspring, my child, my heir! And then... if I grow bored and go off to play in other worlds, you will take the role of those two castaways—staying in this world forever, waiting for my return! Ah-ha-baa, perfect!"
Castaways? What did it mean...? But there was no time to think. The sheep nodded in satisfaction and immediately asked the next question.
"Ah, but baa... since you seem so interested and full of ideas about creating a world—ah baa, sorry, I forgot again. After all, you're the one who gathered all this power. You were supposed to be the Creator, baa-ha-ha—so what do you think? Who should be my enemy, baa? After all, enemies create friends, and hatred gives rise to love, doesn't it?"
Its enemy? The enemy of the new world? You had to gather your thoughts once more...

While you were absorbed in thought, Lamblet suddenly attacked and knocked you from the clouds. Amid a long string of shrill "baa-ha-ha" laughter, it soared higher, leaving you to watch helplessly, powerless to stop it.

5008259.title: Enemies
strings: Enemies

Can the Creator of a world still have enemies? Or rather, who should they take as enemies to pass the long, boring days after the world was made? (or would they be boring? You had no idea—you'd never been a Creator)
Something for Lamblet
Whoever Opposes You Is Your Enemy
Only Gods Are Fit to Be Gods' Enemies
Pleasure Is the Enemy of Piety
You Are Completely Clueless

You told the future creator god that all who refused its command were enemies: whether a nation, a silent rock, or an ocean that refused to split in two for it.
Any enemy must be made to yield. Those who defy, disbelieve, or disobey shall never be permitted to leave unharmed. Fear is the Sultan's most favored tool of dominion—and the divine is the greatest king of all, the supreme Sultan upon earth.
It listened to your words, looking thoughtful... "Baa... One last question, baa..." As the sheep pondered, its body gradually faded into transparency, much like when the sun broke through the clouds and evaporated them along the way. In the end, They vanished almost completely, leaving only a voice still questioning you...
"The world should have a theme, right, baa? Baa... any interesting themes, baa? Ah, I am a god now... I suppose I can't baa anymore, baa... a little lonely, but... you may kneel before your god and answer."
A rough stone slab appeared beneath your feet, with just enough space for you to kneel.

You point out that many worthy foes surround you both. Any existing god—or spirit foolishly called a god—could fill the role of enemy. One god needs no reason to oppose another, especially a supreme creator whose power partly comes from old gods!
You describe a brutal war between new and old gods, where angel feathers and demon flesh flew, the land scorched, human spines used to build towers...
It listens to your words, deep in thought...
