"Baa... true. They will soon learn I took the power you stole. Baa-baa-baa, I can blame you—baa-ha! But it won't matter. I'll soon be a god. I know other gods! We love war! So... one last question, baa..."
As the sheep ponders, its body gradually grows transparent, just as the sun breaks through the clouds and evaporates them along the way. In time, it fades almost completely, leaving only a voice that still questions you.
"The world should have a theme, right, baa? Baa... any interesting themes, baa? Ah, I am a god now... I suppose I can't baa anymore, baa... a little lonely, but... you may kneel before your god and answer." 
A rough stone slab appears beneath your feet, with just enough space for you to kneel.

You told the future creator god that humans were contradictory beings. They craved pleasure yet believed only toil led to virtue; they desired love yet pitied those ruled by it; they drank fine wine yet despised drunkards; they worshipped wealth yet denied it; they exhausted themselves to live longer yet gladly died for trivial reasons.
So the creator's enemy should be all joy. Keep its creations unhappy, and they would unconsciously seek pleasure while patiently enduring life's suffering—that was how the world you once lived in was made.
It listened to your words, deep in thought...
"Baa... makes sense, baa. The last one said something similar, but where did They hear it? Hmm... never having lived as a creature, never suffering under a world... I never thought of this..."
As it thought, its body slowly turned transparent, like the sun burning through clouds until they vanished. Soon They were almost gone, only a voice remaining...
"One last question, baa... the world should have a theme, right, baa? Baa... any interesting themes, baa? Ah, I am a god now... I suppose I can't baa anymore, baa... a little lonely, but... you may kneel before your god and answer."
A rough stone slab appeared beneath your feet, with just enough space to kneel.

While you were deep in concentration, Lamblet suddenly ambushed you and knocked you from the clouds. Amid a long, piercing chorus of "Baa-ha-ha-ha", its form ascended to perfection, shrouded in overwhelming divine radiance. You could only watch helplessly, powerless to stop it any longer.

5008260.title: Blueprint
strings: Blueprint

You kneel on that rough stone slab—this accursed sheep, no, this noble deity's very first creation was meant to make you bow! You ponder and recall, offering a blueprint of an entire world to this newborn Creator... Wait, you have to come up with that too?
Reference for creation
You Mentioned [s1.name]
So Close, Yet So Far

There was no need to elaborate on the contents of this book. In an instant, They had comprehended all.
No longer in need of mortal language, They nodded to you—Their form had vanished entirely. A brilliant explosion surged within your heart. You futilely covered your face, yet the light pierced through you, reducing your body, your thoughts, all your mortal self into flame, light, particles... And so you merged with the great Creator, and from now on, you shall follow Them for all eternity.

While you were lost in deep thought, Lamblet's form completely dissolved into overwhelming divine radiance, shedding all mortal shape and image. It had finished seizing the divine authority. As for this ridiculous question—ha, did it really need you to answer? Did it truly intend to create the world based on your ideas? Did it really need you to point out its enemies? Did it have to consider your will? Did it even need you as its servant? Just think! A brand new world had already bowed at their feet! What else could you possibly do?

5010000.title: Escape Countdown
strings: Escape Countdown
One way to win the game.
Each round consumes one cover
If necessary, let a follower cover for you
Pack 10 Gold Coins
Escape together, requires the Bond of Fate
When the cover reaches 0, the Sultan will find you and execute you.
When all covers disappear, you can use followers to cover for you
Each follower can only cover for you 1 time and cannot flee with you
You still have some time
You ordered someone to create a diversion
The Sultan knows your plan
The bureaucrats are still following protocol, thinking they are stalling, but they're actually drawing others' attention away from you.
Plenty of folks are still quietly pitching in for you – some out of gratitude, others just because they treasure your kindness.
All kinds of illegal channels and group resources can still help you prepare for this.
Your steps are ahead of fate, the omens of your betrayal have not yet reached the Sultan's ears.

[s5.name] makes conspicuous appearances at important events, places expensive orders in your name, and even engages in duels – all to create the illusion that you are still vying for power in the capital.

What a great honor it is to play this game, yet you fail to appreciate the Sultan's grace. The Sultan is disappointed in you, and he can only end your life with banal bloodshed – along with all who planned to escape with you...
Indispensable items
Let's run away together
Most of the Gold Coins have been exchanged for gems… the rest became cloth, rope, wheels, oxen and horses, weapons, jars of water, dried meat… anything that can help you survive in the wilderness.
You informed [s7.name] of your plan, and [s7.gender] joined without hesitation. In the days to come, [s7.gender] will keep a low profile and prepare everything – waiting to depart with you.

5010001.title: Let's go!
strings: Let's go!
With a goal and the means, you are free to leave anytime. But here's the real question: do you grab all the key stuff, or is there something worth sticking around a little longer for?
Protagonist
Destination
Packed Valuables
People escaping together
Sultan Cards that are impossible to break in time
Just place yourself in there, and the escape event can start immediately.
The Sultan Card will attract you. If you hold multiple Sultan Cards, the ending of the escape will be very tragic.
You must take at least one person to leave with you
You set out together
Let it all end now. You will leave here, escape the Sultan, and escape his damn game! [s2.name], here I come!
Let it all end now. You will fulfill your promise and leave with Maggie, escaping the Sultan and his damn game! [s2.name], here we come!

5010002.title: Night of Soul Shattering
strings: Night of Soul Shattering

At the moment, you have decided to give up Sultan's Game and leave the city walls... You realize you made a huge mistake – too many Sultan Cards are left behind; the cards are drawn recklessly, unfinished. Even leaving them behind won't help, they have already targeted you... the magician's depraved laughter echoes in your ears; you know you're doomed...
Protagonist
This is also an ending
Your soul is devoured by wronged spirits in the Sultan Cards

You stop by yourself, sitting on the ground in the wild... the magician's laughter draws closer, and your body grows colder... 

Until midnight, when dark clouds suddenly appear, covering the starry sky and moon.

When the stars and moon shine upon the earth again, you have vanished, leaving only shattered remnants。 (Holding more than one Sultan Card leads to death when escaping.)

5010003.title: Final Carnality Card
strings: Final Carnality Card

At that moment, you have decided to give up Sultan's Game and leave the city walls... You realize that an abandoned card didn't let you go... it is a hook, a rope, a cage, a curse... Now, the magician blocks your path. She chuckles, toying with that little card. 

She tells you to complete this card… one of you must engage in carnality with her – have you been looking forward to this so-called good fortune?
Choose someone to indulge with the sorceress
Carnality Card
It would take divine power, a miracle, to intervene in your current predicament...
What will you lose if you engage in carnality with the magician?
You decide to personally indulge in carnal pleasures with the magician
You let [s1.name] engage in carnality with the magician instead of you
She wasn't joking

If this is temptation, then you must taste her yourself. If this is punishment, then you must endure her yourself.

Before everyone, you approach the magician – the mysterious being who toys with you and even the Sultan, reaching for her enigmatic face...

It feels like wandering the world. As if you, in your youth, longingly stretch out to the stars, and now the starry sky suddenly responds to you with her lips...

You forget where you are, forget your friends behind you – you only want to roam in this starry sky.

Finally, when you are exhausted, you fall back to the mortal world... the starry sky retreats to the distant heavens; the magician and her cards leave only faint laughter lingering at your ear.

She does not take your life, but you can feel that something very, very important has been taken from you... What could it be?

Those who have reached here have boundless trust in you. [s1.name] hears your choice and, without hesitation, goes forward – [s1.gender] trusts you, perhaps because you think [s1.gender] is the most likely to pass the magician's test?

But regardless, after a long kiss as cold as dawn, [s1.name] falls to [s1.gender(his, her)] knees – losing [s1.genderr(his, her)] soul, letting the magician send mist and mysterious liquid into [s1.gender(his, her)] mouth with her tongue... 

When [s1.name] stands up again, you all realize that [s1.gender] is no longer [s1.gender(himself, herself)], but the opposite version of [s1.gender(his, her)], or perhaps an even worse existence... [s1.gender] will be the magician's new toy to play with this country, your substitute... 

In the magician's mad laughter, your party once again gets lost in the sands. When all calms down, there is no trace of her or [s1.name]...

You decide to ignore her and start desperately fleeing across the wilderness... the magician's laughter draws nearer, and your body grows colder...

Until midnight, when dark clouds suddenly appear, covering the starry sky and moon.

When the stars and moon shine upon the earth again, you have vanished, leaving only shattered remnants.
This is a miracle, this is divine intervention

Just when you are about to make a difficult choice... the stars gather.

Starlight envelops you and the magician – this cold light burns her skin like flames, making her screech angrily.

In a daze, you see Lumera descending from the sky, commanding the stars to pierce the magician's body like nails, and then the stars release light, tearing her apart from within... assembling her fragments – the writhing darkness and bones – into a terrifying arch.

Lumera orders you to pass through this gate: her most powerful spell cannot destroy the magician, only temporarily tear her apart. Once you cross this gate, you'll forever say goodbye to the magician, to the Sultan's Game...

You wish to ask her more questions, but as the magician struggles, darkness sways, starlight flickers, and you must hurry through this dreadful portal...

Beyond the arch is a dim road not belonging to this world, sky and earth are one color, with only the lines woven by starlight and flames guiding your path.

With each step, the parts of you belonging to the Sultan's Game slowly burn and fade away... Finally, when you clear your mind again, the road dissipates like mist in the wind, and you return to the real world—from the nearby peaks and markers, you have traveled at least 250 kilometers. Unable to look back at what happened, but now nothing can stop you from running towards freedom...

5010007.title: Before Dawn
strings: Before Dawn
Your mind is made up. It's time to share your resolve with your closest comrades. Once you do, the countdown to battle begins.
Protagonist
Conviction of Rebellion
Follower
You can place up to 8 followers
Completing this ritual will start the battle countdown
Other followers can still participate in subsequent combat
At least 3 followers are required
Where is everyone?
I, [player.name], have something to say here.
Lady Becky, this isn't a game...forget it.
[s3.name], I am glad you came.
[s4.name], Are we all here?
The Sultan will fall to his own game
Don't keep everyone waiting too long
This is not rebellion; this is revolution
Writer of History

You all drink through the night in the courtyard, your allies trading hushed secrets that ripple the air, sizing up your next move...
In your hand, you fiddle with the golden Conquest Card – others see your face catch the gold glow, blending into that image of the crowned one. 
But all you see is blood and fire, all you hear are the wails of dead kings – and it hits you: taking this last step means those who crashed and burned gave up way more lives than the ones trusting you to lead the fight.
Still, these folks won't even show up on the Conquest Card to take the hit. 
"I will use this Conquest Card on the Sultan!" you declare, jumping up and bellowing to the crowd – you're set to face it all.

You all drink through the night in the courtyard, your allies trading hushed secrets that ripple the air, sizing up your next move...
Everyone knows, except the Sultan.
Isn't that what everyone here's thinking – the court, the markets, the alleys, even the wilds? You just weave it all together, loop by loop, into a noose tight enough to choke the Sultan and yank him off his throne.
Sometimes you wonder, kneeling under him, weaving day and night – doesn't he know it's coming? This power feast – soldiers' flesh, heroes' blood – sits ready on the table. Host and guests wait for you to claim your spot. They all stare, and in your mind's eye, their hunger’s already dripping...
So you fill the cups yourself, loudly proclaiming the toast they’ve all been itching for.

You all drink through the night in the courtyard, your allies trading hushed secrets that ripple the air, sizing up your next move... 
And you only speak of the future – at least half of them cannot grasp your words, and half care nothing for what you say. 
As long as the Sultan can fall, they follow you – or perhaps they blindly follow you anyway. 
But you know that these words of the future, these blueprints, matter more than all the lives in this courtyard. Perhaps everyone dies in the end, even you, but this vision you describe is already written in the stars – it will come true, it must come true.

You all drink through the night in the courtyard, your allies trading hushed secrets that ripple the air, sizing up your next move...
You turn the pages of a golden tome marked with handprints – some faded with age, others fresh from yesterday. 
It is not the noble blood of the old land that rebuilds the empire – those who revive their homeland rise as its new nobility. This is the ancient oath's promise – it holds out power, glory, dominion, and the chance to write history as rewards to lure the victors.
So now, it's time to become the victor.
When the bell tolls, his fist rises

After announcing all the plans, the nameless swordsman raises his fist alongside you – he has waited for this for too long. With his blood boiling, the ancient oath is finally fulfilled... you both hear the thunderous call, some long silent thing awakening in the distance...

5010008.title: Assemble the Troops
strings: Assemble the Troops

After you give the order, countless people move. As with all major decisions, it has already become unstoppable – yet nothing has yet begun. However, one good thing is: you no longer need to care about the countdown of the Sultan's Game. Now the countdown of life and death is in your own hands.
Countdown
Conviction of Rebellion
After the countdown ends, all normal rituals will be closed
Comet Strikes the Moon
Gathering of Crows
Prelude to Chaos
Lightning and Thunder
Only One Sun in the Sky

Messengers rush through the wilderness to relay signals to their allies in the wild – the night roads are eerily clear, but they don't dare look up at the ominous flickering stars and a hauntingly twisted moon.

In these final moments of respite, you walk the streets with your centurions, silently indicating terrain features and planning routes for the army's advance – wherever you go, hundreds of ravens quietly follow from rooftops, high towers, and the skies above, watching with unwavering focus.

Nine murders occurred in a single night, shepherds reported fourteen miscarriages at dawn, visitors to the House of Delights multiplied sevenfold, and the Sultan executed three innocent court performers in one fell swoop.

The storm lasts the whole night. Huge lightning tears through the sky like a beast, casting monstrous shadows over the city. You worry that your troops will be affected by the weather – but the next day is cloudless, with the blazing sun scorching the earth.

After your banner appeared on the horizon, news of war finally reached the Lapis Lazuli Hall.

It is said the setting sun was like blood, soaking the court... the Sultan laughed with madness, while you ordered the soldiers to launch an attack with the morning sun the next day.

5010009.title: The Dawn Rally
strings: The Dawn Rally

This is a hilltop overlooking the capital, surrounded by your troops... They wear no uniform, their appearances diverse and disheveled, with nearly half wielding nothing more than farm tools or crude improvised weapons... Yet they stand in silence, watching as the sun slowly rises over the hill where you stand – waiting for you to speak.
Protagonist
The Legitimacy You Choose
Troop
10 Gold Coins Pre-battle Reward
Appoint Messenger, his Stealth and Survival will aid future battles
Appoint Standard-bearer, his Charisma will aid future battles
Everything is ready, you must decide immediately
Supplies and rewards will enhance your troop
Other troops can still participate in subsequent combat
The appointed Messenger and Standard-bearer won't directly engage in combat with the various forces but will provide bonuses for the battles
You need at least one troop to participate in the Dawn Rally
You fail to muster your forces; the Sultan spots flaws riddling your ranks and sends cavalry charging straight for your tent while you dawdle, lost in thought... Thus, the rebellion ends.
Light of Conquest
The Sultan Must Die
We fight alongside the sun
The Time Has Come

You lift the golden Conquest card, letting its reflected light merge with the rising sun. The troops become restless, seeing the pinpoint reflection grow from the mountain peak... until it turns into a God's spear aimed at the Sultan's capital walls still shrouded in darkness.

The Sultan's troops see this gleam, more dazzling than dawn, causing dizziness and madness – the signal to begin the assault.

[s15.name] urgently blows the horn as they ride furiously down the slope, while you toss the glowing card in your hand towards the flag [s16.name] holds high.

The moment the card meets the flag, it transforms into burning gold, dancing in the wind, emitting a terrifying radiance as your main force begins to march towards the Sultan's walls.

You proclaim the Sultan's guilt with a voice that shakes the air. [s15.name], mounted on a horse, weaves through the infantry, loudly repeating every charge you recite to ensure no one will miss a word. You declare that the throne is no longer his, and only through his death will things improve for everyone – peasant, slave, criminal, or once-loyal noble; everyone bears the duty and the right to strike him down! At last, you swear a solemn oath: you will face the Sultan yourself. Only then do the soldiers erupt into thunderous cheers.

With [s16.name] raising your banner to the sky, your troops surge toward the Sultan's walls, their blades carving a crimson road to the duel that fate demands.

Some say the Sultan is the only sun on this Earth! This is completely wrong! The sun shines upon all equally... neither owned by any single soul, nor confined to illuminate only the privileged few! Rise up! We fight for everyone! We shall scale the Sultan's walls alongside the breaking dawn! And illuminate our entire nation!

With these words, [s16.name] raises the banner high, accompanied by ten thousand rays of morning light – as if the banner itself holds up the sun. In this golden blessing, [s15.name] gallops through the formations of soldiers, touching his blade against their weapons – steel swords or rusty pitchforks alike – as if to share his strength with them.

All those who once signed the Testament of Bygone Oaths – decades ago or yesterday – gather at the top of the mountain. Together with them, you raise the golden tome, gleaming in the morning sun.

All the loyal people of this land are here. You loudly announce, "We shall use this loyalty to restore a better era."

[s16.name] lifts your banner, an abstract representation of the Testament of Bygone Oaths: depicting God's tome and fingerprints that symbolize both oaths and stars.

5010010.title: Honor Guards
strings: Honor Guards
As you prepare to overthrow the Sultan, keep in mind that some of your followers vowed to protect the Sultan with their lives – and they are warriors who keep their word.
Nabhani
Faris
Jabal
Captain Seliman
This is their decision, you cannot interfere
No Honor Guards remain loyal

When Seliman walks into the room and pours himself a drink, Nabhani whistles. 
Faris curses, and Jabal wears that "I expected this" smile.
"So, for the first time, it seems, all of us gathered after our monarch no longer personally wages war?" The honor guards' duty is to protect the Sultan's safety, usually on the battlefield alongside him... They are among the few fully aware of the Sultan's capabilities. You sip your drink, hoping they'll share a brilliant strategy to defeat the Sultan. 
They stare at each other for quite a while, exchanging glances and using secret hand signals only Iron Guard members would understand. Finally, Jabal stands up and speaks on behalf of his brothers: 
"To conclude, you may defeat the Sultan's army, but don't expect to kill the Sultan with sheer numbers. Never underestimate that dejected tyrant on the throne... At least three times, he carved a path through impossible situations, turning certain defeat into victory when we were hopelessly outnumbered." Jabal pauses, deep in thought. "And I don't believe anyone can kill him in a fair fight – at least I can't. What do you think, Nabhani?" Nabhani shakes his head, while Seliman and Faris remain silent, refusing to even engage in the discussion. 
You're somewhat frustrated by Jabal's intimidation... but he soon gives you a conclusion: "However, the fact that we're all sitting at this table shows our monarch has lost every quality worth serving... so we've decided to make a bet with you: We will return to Sultan's side, as long as you complete the first half of the rebellion, break through the walls and streets, enter the palace, and stand before our monarch – then we will sacrifice our Iron Guard's honor to help you finish the latter half of the rebellion from behind... We will help you kill the Sultan." After saying this, Jabal looks utterly exhausted. He gulps down his entire drink in one go, pats Seliman on the shoulder, and walks out of your house without another word. 
Nabhani and Faris fill their glasses too. After drinking, they ignore all your questions and attempts to make them stay. With knowing smiles, they simply claim it's a sacred secret among the Iron Guard brothers, then leave. Only Seliman stays, sighing continuously and finishing all the remaining drinks with you.
He's your friend but also a Honor Guard
He truly is the Sultan's loyal hound
Our Shape
Nabhani Regained Vitality
A dog with its tail between its legs
Jabal is Worried
It's Okay if You Die

Nabhani, relaxed as if attending a ball, fills both your glasses to the brim and jokingly wishes your rebellious endeavor success, hoping to see you in front of the Sultan – "my dear brother, we'll then be able to duel with swords, how romantic." 
You don't stop his departure.

Faris didn't say anything as he left, only leaving behind a whistle and a note: If you succeed – blow this whistle and all my dogs will follow you... Please take care of them. I sincerely hope you triumph.

Jabal seemed to age ten years overnight. He appeared to be the only one tormented—"You may not understand, a warrior is sustained by oaths... If I can't abide by them, I am no longer myself... If you cease resisting... you are no longer yourself... There's no way to resolve this—let combat replace all debates."

After saying all this, he felt much better and expressed the hope that you would pardon his family if you emerged victorious. You naturally understood what this warrior meant: if you failed, he would protect your remaining family with his life.

Of course, Nabhani chooses you – he has already despaired of the Sultan, and even of the system of oaths and honor that produced the Honor Guard.

However, he is now as happy as a child; even while talking to you, his mind wanders as he gestures through fighting moves and imagines battle... He has been this joyful ever since realizing he might have a chance to cross swords with the Sultan. Though he tells you, in his current imaginings, he hasn't defeated the Sultan even once... but he'll keep trying.

Faris fears the Sultan, this is evident. He suddenly asks whether his dogs can be sent outside the city before battle, but then quickly denies himself...

You can only reassure him that he only needs to help you defeat the Sultan's troops... you will personally confront the Sultan. Clearly, this relieves him, but his gaze towards you becomes rather nuanced.

Among the Sultan's honor guards, Jabal has fought at his master's side more often than any other, and you eagerly hope he might reveal some of the Sultan's weaknesses... But he only warns you never to underestimate that dejected tyrant on the throne... He says that if you plan to wear the Sultan down with sheer numbers, he will almost certainly carve a bloody path through the chaos and escape. Even if you take the capital, the Sultan will rally more troops and drag you into a long and grueling civil war.

In his opinion, only a fair duel can take advantage of the Sultan's arrogance... But is there anyone who can truly defeat the Sultan in a fair duel? Anyway, he doesn't nominate himself.

Seliman tells you bluntly that he thinks about it, and you can't defeat the Sultan.
In the best-case scenario, you'll be able to rush in front of the Sultan and have your head cut off by his very hands - but that's enough, he'll do his best to help you get there, and he'll do his best to leave a wound on the Sultan's face.

They claim to know a unique route... this smuggler's passage, a dog hole, leads directly to the interior of the walls through an abandoned sewer. Without guidance from these former rogues, no one could find their way from the sewage-filled underground pits.

Your troops appear behind the guards, easily securing this battle. Out of friendship with Alim, you order these young fighters to halt their advance and honorably hold this position... to survive this war.

When you raise the consort's token, you still feel a bit nervous – to let the garrison see it clearly, you step within range of their bows and arrows. Sadani doesn't deceive you. The general at the gate opens it – the bloodstains on his body suggest it has taken some effort.

He takes the unremarkable silk scarf from your hand, presses it tightly against his chest, and then fixes you with a predatory gaze. You immediately recite the secret words taught by the consort: "The debt from that night is repaid."

So, he kneels on the ground, weeping bitterly, allowing your troops to pass by him.

You barely show your face at the city gate when chaos breaks out on the wall. An officer spots you, frantically aiming a ballista at you – but instantly, he is hurled down. The soldiers chant your name, lifting you through the gates... But then you spot [s10.name] charging toward you on horseback. [s10.gender(his, her)] hair is caked with dust, and [s10.gender(his, her)] eyes blaze like wildfire. "They're pouring boiling oil on the eastern breach!" [s10.name] shouts. "And maybe excrement brew, too! We need two hundred men – now!"

The war is not over yet. No time for celebration. Keep sending those who adore and trust you straight into the inferno of fire and ash!

Some say that directly assaulting city walls is the lowest strategy a commander can employ – but you've just invented an even lower approach... Mahir's massive drilling machine has finally delivered value worthy of its wasteful budget and aether essence, penetrating the hard bedrock beneath the walls like tearing through the silk scarf of a lady of pleasure.
According to the original plan, you would have sneaked into the city through this tunnel without anyone noticing, but the entire gate collapsed after the bedrock was compromised, creating a tremendous commotion – nevertheless, you immediately leads troops through the breach, and before the Sultan's garrison can respond, you'll gain a significant strategic advantage.

No matter how much Mahir brags about this thing while tricking you into the budget, its actual power is thirty times more terrifying than her most exaggerated adjective.

[s2.name] reports that half the soldiers are now deaf but still able to fight... They maneuver to flank two key positions through the gate ruins, securing a significant strategic advantage...

You suddenly think warfare will soon employ such devastating weapons in every battle, simply because you initiated today's events... Can destroying the Sultan ever make up for this sin?

The walls are designed to stop humans, so naturally, they can't stop the wind—or those who fly upon it. By the time your soldiers leap onto the walls, few can maintain their discipline—they easily capture this position.

This is clearly not the first time the Sultan's army has faced an enemy wielding magic – your assumption proved naive. Someone atop the city wall cast a defensive spell, sending the storm hurling back toward your position... at least partially.

Soldiers from both sides rained down from the sky, their screams cutting through the chaos as bodies added to the mounting casualties...With the storm now turned against you, your offensive ground to a halt.

The soldiers begin climbing the Sultan's walls – at least half of them must sacrifice their lives under the countless arrows, rolling logs, boiling water, and flames hurled from above before you can truly begin the fight...
[s2.name] isn't the first to climb the walls, but [s2.gender] is the first not to be pushed back down. Corpses pile up on the walls, even blocking the enemy's path for reinforcements... Finally, more soldiers make it up, and the scales of victory slowly tip toward the rebel army...

The soldiers begin climbing the Sultan's walls – at least half of them must sacrifice their lives under the countless arrows, rolling logs, boiling water, and flames hurled from above before you can truly begin the fight...
[s2.name] isn't the first to climb the walls, but [s2.gender] is the first not to be pushed back down. Corpses pile up on the walls, even blocking the enemy's path for reinforcements... At last, the battlefield falls silent, with no one left standing, neither enemy nor ally... At least, everyone on the other battle lines witnesses [s2.name]'s flag rising above the battlements.

The soldiers begin climbing the Sultan's walls – at least half of them must sacrifice their lives under the countless arrows, rolling logs, boiling water, and flames hurled from above before you can truly begin the fight...
[s2.name] isn't the first to climb the walls, but [s2.gender] is the first not to be pushed back down. As [s2.gender] faces enemies on all sides, more soldiers follow [s2.gender] up the wall, fighting together... Bodies pile up as enemies stumble over corpses trying to reach [s2.gender]...
Suddenly, when [s2.gender(his,her)] last companion collapses, no new allies emerge from below the battlements... All soldiers, all blood and flesh, are smeared and spent across the walls... [s2.name] fights until [s2.gender(his,her)] final moment.

Usually, people don't undertake such a mission, but [s2.name] indeed scales the wall single-handedly by your command – [s1.name]'s commander becomes distracted by battles elsewhere... it is a highly risky assassination, but [s2.gender] succeeds. Deprived of leadership, the troops crumble as they see [s11.name] approaching with the banner. You seize this wall at no cost except for exhausted [s2.name].

[s1.name]'s commander holds his neck, directing the ensuing battle, uncovering your strategic intention – now [s10.name] must quickly warn the other two fronts about the pincer attack.
You refuse even a holding force, leaving this enemy's unit an unpredictable mobile threat in other battles... not wise.

Some say that directly assaulting city walls is the lowest strategy a commander can employ – but you've just invented an even lower approach... Mahir's massive drilling machine has finally delivered value worthy of its wasteful budget and aether essence, penetrating the hard bedrock beneath the walls like tearing through the silk scarf of a lady of pleasure.

According to the original plan, you would have sneaked into the city through this tunnel without anyone noticing, but the entire gate collapsed after the bedrock was compromised, creating a tremendous commotion – nevertheless, [s5.name] immediately leads troops through the breach, and before the Sultan's garrison can respond, you'll gain a significant strategic advantage.

No matter how much Mahir brags about this thing while tricking you into the budget, its actual power is thirty times more terrifying than her most exaggerated adjective.

[s5.name] reports that half the soldiers are now deaf but still able to fight... They maneuver to flank two key positions through the gate ruins, securing a significant strategic advantage...

You suddenly think warfare will soon employ such devastating weapons in every battle, simply because you initiated today's events... Can destroying the Sultan ever make up for this sin?

The moat has long since dried up this season, but it is still a massive trench filled with sludge, garbage, and makeshift spike barriers arranged by the garrison. [s5.name] has to order the soldiers to brave the arrows and use sandbags and logs to build a path...
Initially, their biggest challenge is a lack of materials, and later, it is a lack of soldiers daring to charge forward – the corpses serve as enough filler.
So [s5.name] personally stands at the front, shielding the soldiers transporting corpses from arrows and stones with shields and blades. [s5.gender] jumps to the other side as soon as the makeshift bridge is set up; at this moment, the enemy troops regard [s5.gender] as a god – they can't believe [s5.gender] has stood firm under a rain of arrows for so long!
After crossing the river, the combat turns into a one-sided massacre.

[s5.name], along with a small band of brave warriors, quietly crawls across the moats – Coated in sludge, they circle around to the rear and remain undetected. Taking advantage of the fight elsewhere drawing the enemy's attention, [s5.gender] conducts a desperate raid – severing the ropes controlling the drawbridge... The enemy scatters before [s11.name]'s banner approaches and you capture this entrance bridge with little cost – Unfortunately, during this process, [s5.name] has several bones broken by the drawbridge mechanism and can no longer fight.

[s5.name], along with a small band of brave warriors, quietly crawls across the moats – at least, that was your plan. But the enemy has already poured oil into the waterway... [s10.name] doesn't even see clearly why they suddenly decide to set the moat ablaze – perhaps [s5.name] is discovered, or perhaps the fighting in the distance simply causes the defenders to overreact... In any case, your plan fails.

Of course, the Sultan's troops know this, too. [s7.name] does not intend to wait behind the city walls; they charge out against the trebuchet position while [s8.name] fights desperately behind the rudimentary defenses...

Time and again, the enemy reaches right up to the trebuchets, and the launching mechanisms hurl not stones but the corpses of fallen gunners... yet [s8.name] still holds onto the trebuchets, and starts hurling burning stones, corpses, and and anything else at hand over the city walls...

With the guidance of this group of former rogues, you navigate the slums with ease. They know every alley and every hidden passage like the back of their hands.

Your troops appear behind the guards, easily securing this battle. Out of friendship with Alim, you order these young fighters to halt their advance and honorably hold this position... to survive this war.

[s1.name] first occupies the lighthouse and port, but they clearly underestimate your influence in the capital: the chaotic waterways around the port are the world of the poor, and at least half of the population stands ready to guide you... As your soldiers cross the gloomy canals shrouded by shacks, they easily flank the enemy's rear, setting up an inevitable ambush.

You swear never to use such weapons in a city again, especially in the slums... The massive explosion destroys all defensive structures built by the enemy and even stirs up the sediment of sludge and garbage beneath the slums... The large crater keeps belching foul gas – as if burping... [s1.name]'s soldiers surrender thoroughly, willing to do anything as long as you do not throw them into that hell's asshole.

Nabhani, with his blue ribbon, joined the ranks of farmers. By all accounts, he should stand out among them, yet in his wake, more people wearing blue ribbons joined the group—craftsmen, merchants, young nobles, monks, scholars, washerwomen, prostitutes... They differed in dress, age, gender, and race, coming from every corner of the city. Indeed, if that thing was truly so beautiful and worth sacrificing everything to pursue, then it should belong to everyone.

And so, within these blue-adorned ranks, the varied skin tones and garments blended into a harmonious and striking sight destined to live on in countless paintings...
The tornado leveled the entire port and half of the slum... There's no time for sorrow, at least we won't have to worry about the Sultan's fleet for a long, long time.

A tornado's destructive power in a city is hundreds of times greater than in the wilderness. Everything is swallowed by chaos – garbage, houses, sewage, innocent people... The wind spirals completely out of control, rushing all the way to the sea... Many warriors vanish just like that.

[s1.name] are the Sultan's pride, his elite troops, but they are not skilled at fighting in the narrow streets and canals of the slum – [s2.name] orders the troops to split up flexibly and engage the enemy at close quarters from all directions, quickly gaining the upper hand. Unfortunately, the relentless fighting also sets the slum ablaze. The fire spreads rapidly until it illuminates the sky and the palace high above... In the end, it is your army that makes it out alive. Can this really be called a victory?

[s1.name] are the Sultan's pride, his elite troops, but they are not skilled at fighting in the narrow streets and canals of the slum – [s2.name] orders the troops to split up flexibly and engage the enemy at close quarters from all directions, quickly gaining the upper hand. Unfortunately, the relentless fighting also sets the slum ablaze. The fire spreads rapidly until it illuminates the sky and the palace high above... At last, [s10.name] sends someone to rescue [s2.name], but only [s2.gender] is saved...

[s1.name] are the Sultan's pride, his elite troops, but they are not skilled at fighting in the narrow streets and canals of the slum – [s2.name] orders the troops to split up flexibly and engage the enemy at close quarters from all directions... Soon, the enemy forces are also split apart, hacking at your troops in the darkness... 

The battle is merciless – for everyone, enemies could appear anywhere, until finally someone sets the flames alight... The fire spreads rapidly, until it illuminates the sky and the palace high above... Through discipline, or perhaps through ruthless efficiency with callous disregard for human life, the Sultan's army withdraws. Besides them, no one escapes alive.

To spare the slum from the ravages of war, [s2.name] challenges the Commander of [s1.name] to a duel. Naturally, the opponent has no intention of honoring the agreement, but the narrow alleyways hinder their forces, allowing only a few to engage [s2.name] at a time.

In the end, both sides fall into the foul-smelling mud of the canals – these ancient gutters have drunk in centuries of the capital's refuse and sewage, as well as the blood of heroes and villains.

When [s2.name] rises from the dark sludge, holding the Commander's severed head, the remaining soldiers drop their weapons and surrender.

In the end, both sides fall into the foul-smelling mud of the canals – these ancient gutters have drunk in centuries of the capital's refuse and sewage, as well as the blood of heroes and villains.

In the end, no one can escape from the dark mud...

Letting the Sultan blockade the harbor is a grave mistake. With sea routes open for support and supplies, you might not be able to capture the inner city even after a month, and the nobles will simply shift their allegiance with the changing winds.

These former rogues easily evade the guards' sight, leading you through alleyways, windows, and rooftops, launching ambushes from all directions... In the end, the opponent think they are surrounded by more than ten times their number and surrender without fighting. Out of friendship with Alim, you order these young fighters to halt their advance and honorably hold this position... to survive this war.

[s4.name] sets up an ambush. They plan to overwhelm you on the main road with a massive assault, like meat being stuffed into a sausage.

But their scheme unravels fast as locals thwart them at every step. The moment they charge into a street, a warning gong rings out from above. Stones, chamber pots, knives, hammers, and pots rain down as furious citizens bombard them, giving you the chance to wipe out their forces with ease.

As your troops march along the avenue, women toss homemade flatbreads from above, some skewering the soldiers' spears, some into the chariots – each cavalryman's saddle soon brims with more than one jug of wine, and the weapons – every soldier still fighting with farm tools receives a fine blade… some snatched from Sultan's army, others treasured heirlooms from the townsfolk.

For a long time, you've provided the capital's residents with ample entertainment – just like the Sultan, they enjoy watching your struggles in the game. Rumors are exaggerated hundreds of times over. Even as your troops arrive at the city gates, some still think it's just another of your theatrical stunts... 

A powerful explosion is the best response to these thoughts. Sweeping through broken walls and limbs, your troops barricade warehouses and streets, and the citizens finally believe: this time you are serious.

The tornado sweeps away everything not anchored down – the Sultan's army and the neighbors' rooftops, all gone. Many foolish citizens already turn to new idols in prayer – or at least start by taking down the Sultan's portraits from their homes.

You're not the only one who knows the secret of magic... When [s5.name] guides the storm to destroy the enemy troops' defenses, a flash of terrifying lightning suddenly descends and engulfs him. In such stormy weather, summoning lightning becomes much easier; perhaps this is the most successful casting ever by the war mages within the Sultan's troops.

[s4.name] and [s5.name] lead their troops in fierce combat in the residential area. Surprisingly, the capital citizens prove to have rich war experience: most valuable houses and streets are barricaded with obstacles and roadblocks they built themselves... Is this the lesson they learned from the last war? Or has this ancient city relied on a self-preservation mechanism for centuries? At least this time, your troop is winning the slaughter – if you finally succeed, you may have the opportunity to explore all this.

Is this the lesson they learned from the last war? Or has this ancient city relied on a self-preservation mechanism for centuries? Again and again, armies meet their doom here, and this time is no exception... Kind citizens help you find [s5.name] in the pile of bodies. [s5.gender] took a blow to the head, but is only unconscious and can still continue fighting – can still continue this performance of dynastic succession that everyone never tires of watching.

Your army is crushed... but the kind citizens help you find [s5.name]'s body from the pile of corpses – they rub their hands together, shedding crocodile tears, knowing this will earn them some reward money.

[s5.name] publicly requests a one-on-one duel with the Commander of [s4.name]... Generally, no one accepts such a challenge when holding an advantage with superior forces, but the entire city populace gathers at their windows, shouting and cheering... Thus, the duel takes place in the square, complete with a roaring crowd, thunderous applause, and eager spectators, until [s5.name] pierces through the opponent's chest... [s11.name] quickly takes over the area, and the people welcome your banner as if greeting heroes, marking it a glorious battle, though [s5.name] requires bandaging and treatment, unable to continue fighting.

Generally, no one accepts such a challenge when holding an advantage with superior forces, but the entire city populace gathers at their windows, shouting and cheering... Thus, the duel takes place in the square, complete with a roaring crowd, thunderous applause, and eager spectators, until the opponent's blade pierces through [s5.name]'s chest... Flying your banner, [s11.name] claims [s5.name]'s body from the battlefield. At the very least, it is an honorable end to a warrior's fight.
The Sultan's troops controlled most parts of the city and organized a defense relying on sturdy buildings – if you act rashly, they can easily launch attacks from behind your back.

These former rogues know the back doors of the noble fortress well – they even know where to leap from one balcony to another rooftop. As a result, all defenses prove useless against you. The enemy doesn't even grasp how they're ambushed before the fight ends. Out of friendship with Alim, you order these young fighters to halt their advance and honorably hold this position... to survive this war.

The houses of the Nobles are their fortresses... And their doors are open to you.

While [s7.name] is still deploying defenses outside the Upper City, your banner is already flying inside the inner city, enjoying all the supplies and praise.

But deep down, you know that half of them are already quietly fleeing this city, and you can't stop them – regardless of who ultimately wins, the Nobles will always return.
You once worried you couldn't get recognition from all the Nobles, now that problem is solved – as long as you keep bluffing and tell them you have many more such things, everyone will smile at you.

The Upper City is sturdy enough to withstand a tornado – but it's also a trap, troops sheltered by buildings lose their fighting spirit.

So you direct the storm, letting your troops occupy the strategic points of the Upper City as if they are part of a parade, while the cowering nobles continue to witness your final victory.

As you guide the storm over the Upper City, a mysterious sorcerer –perhaps offered to the Sultan by a great noble, or one of the Sultan's own hidden powers – counterattacks against your magical astronomy. The tornado loses control, quickly charges out of the city, taking many of your own innocent soldiers with it.

[s7.name] and [s8.name]'s troops are embroiled in a melee between the nobles' mansions. With astonishing valor, [s8.name] opens a path for your troops. The nobles watch uneasily from their closed doors as your men march forward. Soldiers trample the blood and flesh of enemies and allies, leaving chaotic red footprints on the white stone steps that lead to the Sultan. Tomorrow, servants will clean everything up to welcome the final victor.

[s7.name] and [s8.name]'s troops are embroiled in a melee between the nobles' mansions. There are too many fortified strongholds here, grinding soldiers' flesh and blood like millstones, letting it flow into the streets.

In the end, it is [s10.name] who arrives first with reinforcements, opening a path to the Sultan's palace for you. Tomorrow, servants will clean everything up to welcome the final victor.

Finally, [s10.name] arrives first with reinforcements. Your troops are exhausted – and silence still reigns between the nobles' mansions, just like this country, awaiting more bloody raw materials.

[s8.name] infiltrates the enemy lines alone, choosing a narrow yet defensible slope to intercept [s7.name]'s troops. [s8.gender] loudly challenges their courage – and so the enemies come one by one to duel [s8.gender] on the stone steps, only to be thrown off the cliff one after another.

Seizing this opportunity, [s11.name] plants your banner at the top of the highest tower nearby, a move that breaks the will to resist among most nobles and defenders.

Yet, despite it all, the Sultan isn’t foolish enough to charge out from that golden gate – one so heavy it takes twelve oxen to pull it open – and face your rain of arrows. So, you begin to calculate how many warriors must be sacrificed to force it open.

Now, you find yourself surrounded by a throng of eunuchs, tax collectors, and clerks, all eagerly detailing the damage you've inflicted on the Sultan: your precise and clandestine betrayal caught the entire empire off guard! So many industries, so much wealth, so many soldiers – all rendered useless by your thunderous strike at the core... Especially with their timely surrender, they claim you will seize the entire empire as easily as plucking a flower.
You know they opened the gates to you because they believed you would be a better ruler... Before entering, you look back – the mountain path is littered with corpses and blood, while cities burn in the distance.

Everything goes perfectly according to plan – if only [s2.name] hadn't fallen before [s11.name]'s reinforcements could arrive...
If the palace gates remain closed, sneaking in through other places will prove far less effective...

If you plan your war with the sole aim of killing the Sultan, everything you do will eventually backfire – you need to fight with the goal of controlling this country. The newly surrendered officials and eunuchs are trying to briefly introduce you to the real core of this country – the tax archives, legal documents, the Scribe's archive, and the national treasury, which you cannot open yet.

They praise your wisdom and mercy, though they don't have many choices... You listen with half attention, issuing orders one after another until someone suddenly reminds you of something important. So here you are, tearing away another piece of the Sultan's authority, stripping away his power bit by bit... Yet wasn't killing the Sultan the very reason you started this rebellion in the first place?

You draw your weapon, loudly challenging the Sultan as you step into his hall. If you didn't, no one would dare to enter the Lapis Lazuli Hall as a rebel... The combat stretches from dawn till dusk, the setting sun casting blood-red light between you. With each step closer to the Sultan, you feel the shadows dance, flames flicker, and even the columns around you seem to spin wildly in the tension... The honor guards remain motionless, while the Sultan applauds you – his shadow expanding...

The Sultan stands as if matching the speed of your approach step by step. He reaches for his battle sword, beckons a guard to help him don his armor, then pauses briefly between weapons before choosing another blade – a light, serpentine scimitar. 

During these preparations, your team remains still and silent, neither speaking nor charging, as if bound by some unspoken pact, simply maintaining the pilgrimage's pace, slowly arriving at the hall's center.

"I accept your challenge, rebel," says the Sultan, leaving his long-held throne and descending the stairs toward you, step by step... With each step, his reflected light becomes more radiant. His form seems to grow even larger.
Behind you, someone loses control—you hear stumbling retreats and weapons clattering to the ground, but there's no time to scold or inspire your companions now. You need to gather all your courage and strength so you can confront him. You realize: the beast, once chained, corrupted, and tormented, has finally been unleashed by you.

When Seliman enters behind you, even the Sultan looks surprised. 
"My faithful Seliman? You conceal your identity, all to plot rebellion with [player.name]? For so long?" 
The former Captain of the Royal Guard, a man who has lost both his name and face, finally draws his weapon against his sovereign – "Long before that, you monster! Ever since you seized everything, since you scorned me… You deserve no loyalty!"

You suspect there might be a sacred agreement among the four honor guards – Jabal's eyes show evident sadness as he realizes Seliman did not enter the Lapis Lazuli Hall with you. Unable to find words to break this silence, you momentarily lose awareness of the Sultan's watchful eyes.

The Sultan will not tolerate such disrespect, but you are not the first fools to try insulting him in this hall. He toys with his Signet Ring, pondering how to best amuse himself with you rebels... The Honor Guard draw their weapons, naturally – like dogs first barking, intimidating, biting on behalf of their master... this feeling fills him – 

Three weapons stab him from behind. Not only does this cause fatal wounds, but it also pins this legendary invincible warrior to the throne.

Each honor guard pledges unbreakable oaths to the ring, symbolizing the monarch's power – to protect their sovereign with their lives, unwavering till death.

This is why the Sultan's Signet Ring does not alarm in their presence, allowing them to wield weapons next to the Sultan on the battlefield. Now, the honor guards break their life-bound oaths, and the penalty for this sin shall be death.

As their master's life hangs by a thread, the ring bursts forth nearly limitless power – a terrifying magic surge blocks you from approaching, and each Iron Guard weathers this red light, crumbling, burning. Their tears turn into golden flames instantly – not shed for this sacrifice, but for lost glory, and their dearly respected sovereign.

The Sultan is not dead yet; even the ring's power is healing his wounds, giving him more strength to struggle, to extract the Iron Guard's weapons, pinning him down...
Nabhani smiles, kneeling before the ugly, enraged monarch, gently holding the hand wearing the ring... he is slowly being dissolved by magic, thus, his movements are gentle and slow... slowly removing Sultan's Signet Ring:

As he turns into golden sand, the invincible Signet Ring falls to the ground, and all light, power, oath, magic, and monarchy come to an end.

This sudden betrayal, massive wounds, and suddenly vanished magic from the ring exhaust his body and mind. Now, the unfinished healing spells twist all his wounds: his hands and legs impaled by the Iron Guard's weapons, almost fused with the throne – every struggle accompanied by quivering flesh; his heart and lungs twist into a cluster, open mouth uttering nothing but a dying beast's gasp – Finally, the once-invincible monarch lies at your mercy.

5010016.title: Do Whatever You Want
strings: Do Whatever You Want

No matter how powerful he once was, his brutal deeds that turned everyone against him have led him to this pitiable corner – pinned to the throne by blades, barely breathing... now, your command shall become his destiny.

"Oh, wait, we all know what's coming, but wait - we, at least I don't want to witness this firsthand," Nabhani declares, hastily exiting the palace. The others exchange knowing glances before unanimously leaving this victory spoil for you to savor alone. 
Perfect. You approach the fallen Sultan with deliberate steps, your eyes taking in every detail of his defeated form. For the first time, you look down upon those once-commanding eyes, now dimmed by defeat. 
"At last, this moment is mine, Your Majesty." A smile plays across your lips as you casually hook a finger around the golden chain adorning his chest. 
His breathing quickens - is it rage or something baser? It hardly matters now. 
With calculated cruelty, you smear his blood across his flesh, methodical as those nights you studied battle maps by candlelight. You toy with his broken dignity, like raising your standard over each conquered territory. This city, this kingdom now bows before you, and its embodiment lies bound to this golden throne by traitors' blades, awaiting your final conquering act. 
When pained sounds escape his throat, you crush his feeble resistance without mercy - just as he once trampled countless others beneath his boot. You force his gaze to meet yours, a perfect mirror of how he once delighted in others' suffering. 
A satisfaction beyond description surges through your chest, more potent than any carnal pleasure. For one crystalline moment, you understand perfectly how the Sultan transformed from the vibrant ruler he once was into this hollow shell. 
Yet you will not relent, not today. You'll return his cruelties a thousandfold. Once could never suffice. "Death shouldn't claim you too quickly, Your Majesty," you whisper against his ear, with the intimacy of a lover and the coldness of a mortal enemy. "Where would be the satisfaction in that?"

"None remain, Your Majesty." You approach the fallen Sultan with deliberate steps, your eyes taking in every detail of his defeated form. For the first time, you look down upon those once-commanding eyes, now dimmed by defeat. 
"Your guards, your courtiers, your soldiers, your subjects..." Your voice barely carries to his ear. "Your dynasty perishes today." 
A strange sound rises from the Sultan's throat - perhaps laughter. It hardly matters now. 
With calculated cruelty, you smear his blood across his flesh, methodical as those nights you studied battle maps by candlelight. You handle his vulnerable form with clinical detachment, as though raising your standard over each conquered territory. You crush his feeble resistance without mercy - just as he once trampled countless others beneath his boot. You force his gaze to meet yours, a perfect mirror of how he once delighted in others' suffering. 
The taste of victory should be sweet. Yet as this long-dreamed triumph finally comes to pass, why do tears mark your face? 
Your companions, your allies, the righteous souls who rallied to your cause, even the common folk who joined your banner - countless lives extinguished in this fiery night. Their collective grief courses through you, more potent than any carnal pleasure. 
You search the Sultan's hollow gaze - did this mighty ruler beg for mercy? Did he plead for a shred of dignity? The words never reached you. You know only that his debt must be repaid a thousandfold. Once could never suffice. 
"Death shouldn't claim you too quickly, Your Majesty," you whisper against his ear, with the intimacy of a lover and the coldness of a mortal enemy. "Where would be the satisfaction in that?"

You whisper at the Sultan's ear, a soft hiss that declares this to be the punishment – or perhaps the reward – for all he has wrought in his fleeting life. His face twists for the first time, a mask of flesh buckling, but whatever words he means to spit, you silence them. Before his lips part, you pierce his body with your flawless creation – a thing of ruinous perfection. 
Aether surges between you, crackling with lightning and thunder – yet its clamor pales beside the merest fraction of his screams, his wails of anguish. 
Wielding this seemingly boundless power, you transport him between ecstasy and agony, countless times unleashing years of suppressed humiliation... 
Throughout this communion, you experience pleasure transcending imagination. Did the mighty ruler beg for mercy? Did he moan from depths of shameful desire? Did his proud spirit finally break? The words never reached you... At last, even the Rod of Life reaches its end, shuddering to a halt in a keening wail of metal. 
Only then do you see it: the thing once called Sultan lies shattered, a broken relic of flesh and bone. Rising, you turn. Lightning flares, and your loins – ablaze with the sacred flame of aether – stand proud before the cowering court. They kneel, one by one, trembling as they greet the new monstrosity that claims their throne.

Sword in hand, you approach the fallen Sultan with deliberate steps. Blood loss has drained most of his strength; his arms hang limply at his sides, each breath a laborious struggle. 
When has the mighty ruler, perched upon his golden throne, ever known such defeat, such vulnerability? 
Without a flicker of mercy, you examine every detail of his defeated form, looking down upon those once-commanding eyes, now dimmed by defeat, as you speak: "At last, this moment is mine, Your Majesty." 
You recite his crimes, your blade dancing across his skin, opening precise, shallow cuts with each transgression named. 
In days past, he would have mocked your impudence, ordering guards to drag you away, or demanding tribute to soothe his wounded pride. Now he can only tremble in silence, unable even to voice his terror. 
Will the Sultan repent as death approaches? Perhaps - yet what solace would this bring to those who suffered beneath his cruelty? 
Blood weeps from countless wounds, forming crimson rivulets across his skin. In the solemn silence of final reckoning, the tyrant's chest falls still - so quiet, so insignificant in death. 
You regard the broken vessel expressionlessly before severing his head with a clean stroke. 
In death's frozen moment, his eyes hold the same fear any commoner might show. This is the Sultan you served faithfully for years, the despot who trampled countless others beneath his boot. Now, his reign ends! 
With your own hands, you mount his head at the palace's highest point - amidst gasps of shock, cries of fear, and swelling cheers, the news spreads like wildfire through the city streets: The Sultan is dead!

The Sword of the Sun trembles and sings in your hand, rejoicing – you once feared possessing the finest phallus in the country, knowing deep down that only the Supreme Sultan was worthy of such thing...but now, you have conquered your fear with your own hands!

Such chaotic thoughts flash through your mind, and so you swing down your blade without hesitation, sending the Sultan's head soaring high. From now on, you will fear possessing nothing.

You approach the fallen Sultan with deliberate steps, your eyes taking in every detail of his defeated form. 
Blood loss has drained most of his strength; his arms hang limply at his sides, each breath a laborious struggle, yet somehow - he smiles! 
How magnificently theatrical this final act of defiance! The proud king refuses to acknowledge defeat, treating this conquest as mere performance! What finale will you compose for this drama? Death? Humiliation? Or something more fitting? A chuckle escapes his throat. You merely regard him with icy detachment. 
You know the perfect punishment. 
You'll confine him in the quietest cell, buried in the deepest dungeon beneath the palace. 
There he will see no face, hear no voice. Endless darkness will consume his sanity, yet no matter how he screams, pleads, or repents, only silence will answer. 
You'll visit periodically - indeed, you've already composed the monologue for your next visit, your tenth visit, your thousandth visit - until eventually, you forget his existence, until the last soul alive forgets he ever ruled. 
He will perish from madness, from isolation, and ultimately from the mundane humiliation of starvation... Let this be his atonement! Perhaps in his next life, he'll discover how not to trample countless others beneath his boot.

You summon all the nobles, ministers, and generals worthy of heed – those already sworn to your cause and those dragged reluctantly into your shadow. 

Before them all, you speak. This wretched failure, this once-Sultan, shall not meet death's embrace. Whatever atrocities the tyrant has wrought, half the sin stains our own hands... His punishment – the loss of all he held dear – suffices. You spare him the noose, and in doing so, you absolve the multitude's guilt. No longer must blood scour the throne clean. The fallen one lives. His kin, those willing to exile, live too. This mercy flows from you, destined to bind all rulers yet to come.

Some kneel in dread of your might. Others bow to your mercy and wisdom. All hail this hallowed pardon with trembling voices.

The starry sky glimmers for the sacrifices of the multitude; the aurora, like tears, moistens the firmament. Lumera – she represents the stars – returns to the mortal realm once more for your battle. The radiant starlight cloaks the blood-red hues of the setting sun; whether the Sultan's roars or others' cries, all fade after Lumera's gentle reassurance to you…God reaches out from the sky, through the burning city and smoke, plucking the ring from your hand like a flower. The symbol of power is thus shattered, the ancient Magic is abolished…and now, let the slaughter among mortals begin – the stars shall witness this.

You provocatively pull the Sultan's Signet Ring out of your pocket. You loudly share the story of how you acquired it, telling everyone that because the Sultan is tyrannical, even those closest to him are willing to risk everything to betray him. 
Clearly, the Sultan expects this, but instead of anger, his smile is one of anticipation – he seems to thank you, and only by becoming the next Sultan would you understand what you helped him accomplish… Now, let blades and swords decide everything!

The Sultan has high expectations of you, but that doesn't mean he will compromise his standards: the rebellious traitor must face the piercing light of death from the Signet Ring. As its magical power surges, the sunset light and shadows in the hall twist and writhe, morphing into crimson beasts poised to devour you whole.

Just as you brace yourself to resist, a greater, holier force descends from above.

The starry sky glimmers for the sacrifices of the multitude; the aurora, like tears, moistens the firmament. Lumera – she represents the stars – returns to the mortal realm once more for your battle.

The radiant starlight cloaks the blood-red hues of the setting sun; the deadly tides fade into nothingness. Lumera holds you close, shielding you with her back from all calamity, until she finishes speaking those words of gratitude and comfort that can never be said enough。

The Sultan feels such shock and rage that he pushes the ring's power to its limit – until it cracks. At last, even the embodiment of kingship and power reaches its breaking point – the ring no longer glows and leaves a charred scar on the Sultan's hand, hissing with heat. The starlight fades in turn – the meddling of gods and magic ends here. Let the slaughter among mortals begin!

You drew a ring from within, raising it high - it looked almost like that Signet Ring's replica! Only the Sultan knew it wasn’t - you had neutralized its magic and covered its troublesome curse through means unknown to him. How amusing! He laughed loudly and wildly, delighting in this gift you brought! Dear minister, only you could always surprise him!
At that moment, a more powerful, more sacred, more transcendent will cast its gaze upon the mortal realm.
Stars flickered for everyone's sacrifice, aurora tears moistened the sky. Lumera - representing stellar will - witnessed your oath to all people, witnessed this great moment that would utterly overturn ancient monarchy...

You drew a ring from within, raising it high - it looked almost like that Signet Ring's replica! Only the Sultan knew it wasn’t - you had neutralized its magic and covered its troublesome curse through means unknown to him. How amusing! He laughed loudly and wildly, delighting in this gift you brought! Dear minister, only you could always surprise him!
If you won't obediently present the ring, then let blades decide everything!

You drew a ring from within, raising it high - sunset's radiance ignited it, making it shine like an earthbound star! Even the Sultan's face showed momentary surprise, then he laughed wildly: the exiled Star still had descendants offering worship; and corrupt oaths still had foolish believers maintaining faith! But dear minister, how much could its feeble power help you?
Let those damned stars bear witness! Witness how he would tear you apart, thoroughly purging the already-overturned faith and dynasty once more!

Kingship, fear, time—you had transcended them all—and you returned to prove it to the Sultan. At the sight of your figure standing taller amid the radiance, the Sultan laughed aloud—Excellent! My loyal subject! Let us see what other surprises you have in store for me!

The Sultan's Signet Ring blazed to life, and a tide of destruction surged toward you. But you raised the divine weapon in your hand without fear.
Light and flame alike were split and subdued by this higher creation... Yet the Sultan felt no anger, only delight—his greatest joy was a foe wielding a divine armament! You are truly a master at pleasing your emperor, Lord [player.name]!

Subsequently, your resistance, hope, friends, everything...turns to ashes. 

The Sultan is also very disappointed in you.

The Sultan grinned viciously, waiting to see what you would do. If the Ring on his finger had truly been swapped, then you should have the real one... right? What's going on?
You had lost the chance to pull out the ring publicly and humiliate the Sultan, but you had indeed succeeded in drawing a look of utter bewilderment from your sovereign, a sight no one had ever beheld.

You tell the Sultan, it's merely for breaking this Conquest Card – you're just fulfilling the obligations of the game. 
"How interesting!" The Sultan laughs: "my loyal [player.name], you truly amuse me the most!" – then his sword comes at you in the most graceful way.

You don't tell the Sultan this, but your sword, your body, are pouring all their power into delivering this message to the Sultan's heart – and he laughs wildly as he understands your true intent: "Wonderful! My loyal [player.name], I've always dreamed of this day!"

You tell the Sultan that you will educate the people with a new system of governance where history advances without a tyrant's whip! Of course, the Sultan cannot comprehend such things. To him, he hears only that you will use some incomprehensibly mad force, some great calamity to destroy him – this delusion brings him nothing but supreme joy, as his sword techniques become wild and ferocious as a beast.

The Sultan is slightly disappointed, he doesn't think an opponent once defeated by him could surprise him again: "However, I will slightly elevate my evaluation of that old man – he spent decades nurturing a gift like you." After speaking, his sword comes at you in the most graceful way.

No one can intervene in the battle between you and the Sultan. It is a solitary clash between those burdened with the mandate of kings.
The brave stand hesitant and unsure, the wise quake with dread, the compassionate turn their eyes away... and the righteous waver in their resolve. As if decreed by the heavens, the fate of the many rests in the hands of the few. Must those untouched by destiny merely look on in silence?
While all can only endure and wait, Gulis slowly draws his longbow—the poisoned arrow, a gift from Nawfal, now taut against its string.
Does the dormant noble blood in his veins grant him the right to this fight? Or has his fractured fate, broken time and again, carved out this moment of vengeance? We know only this: he murmurs the names etched into the arrow’s shaft—names of mortals insulted, wounded, and slaughtered by the Sultan.
At first, the recitation flows gently, like a sacred prayer, then surges into a frenzied incantation: there are far too many names.
The chanting stretches on, as though spanning a century, yet it might last only a fleeting moment. Gulis' eyes roll back, and blood trickles from his mouth and nose—he has reached his limit as a vessel and conduit of power.
In the moment when the Sultan's sword overwhelms you, nothing remains between him and the arrowhead. In that instant, Gulis releases his hold, allowing the mighty bow to snap forward, his own skin tearing as the arrow—laden with the names of mortals—vanishes from sight. No eye witnesses its path, yet it finds its mark in the Sultan's mouth, piercing through his cruel smile and wicked soul—it slays the invincible Sultan.

At first, the Sultan's furious assault overwhelms you – if one of the monarch's virtues is madness, then he indeed possesses much more power than you.

Just when you are about to falter, [s6.name] launches Nawfal's arrow – [s6.gender] chants every name on it repeatedly, gaining the courage to intervene in the monarch's combat.

The Sultan blocks this arrow, but he is clearly taken aback by this – and you take the opportunity to launch a counterattack…

Just as you expose an opening, the Sultan shifts his blade to deflect another weapon aimed at him... It is the Blade of Lament, the legendary weapon of the previous dynasty. Though the nation has long perished, its legacy endures unbroken. Wielding it is a swordsman, stripped of name, homeland, and kin by the Sultan, who now seeks his revenge.

Facing this challenge, the Sultan calmly traces a graceful arc with his twin blades and declares, "Come at me, both of you, together."

You have no idea how long this battle has lasted, but your body and mind are near their limit—and your weapons are the first to give in.

With a magnificent slash, the Sultan shatters your blade and right hand, then turns and, with a flurry of intricate swordplay, clangs relentlessly to pin down the Blade of Lament, leaving it unable to move, as though he were hammering an unruly nail into place. 

Just at the moment of impending defeat, [s5.name] suddenly abandons his blade, seemingly overwhelmed by the Sultan's power, allowing the precious artifact to fall to the ground, where it turns immediately to ashes.

The Sultan's blade stabs into his flesh, but he seems prepared for this, using every muscle and bone to trap the fatal weapon – for just a moment, but enough for you to pierce the Sultan's back with the Sword of Lament.

This weapon is forever bound to return to the hands of the ruler willing to wield it! This is the true secret of its unbroken heritage. Finally, [s5.name]'s wish comes true, and you, exhausted, no longer have any monarch to wield it... so the divine weapon fades into the air along with the life of the Warrior King once more...

Failure is imminent, and both you and [s5.name] know it well. Thus, as if by agreement, you both launch the final charge from opposite sides – betting your lives as weapons.
…………
Everything ends. You are pierced by the Sultan's dual blades, lifted high as if in an embrace. He grants you his final praise, whispering it at your ear.

The Sultan crushes your resistance repeatedly, savoring the game. "Come on! Show your tricks!" he taunts, etching new scars. In despairing defense, you see the Magician pulling fate's strings–soul fragments in cards, victims, and perpetrators alike. Tears flow as you plead for closure, for redemption, but faces remain unmoved, victims, the Sultan, or your abandoned self. In the end, hope manifests, as cards empower you, overcoming his strikes, choosing you over the Sultan for your perseverance or his detestability. As you win, pressing his edge upon him, his likeness vanishes from each card, signifying release. Only you know the victors.

Failure is imminent, you know it well. Thus, you desperately launch your last charge—betting your life as the weapon.
…………
Everything ends. You are pierced by the Sultan's dual blades, lifted high as if in embrace. He grants you his final praise at your ear.

When you accomplish all this, you look back... Beneath the steps of the throne, hardly anyone remains standing – neither victors nor vanquished, all exhausted by the battle. At this moment, a child suddenly dashes out from behind the throne – he is the one taken by the Sultan from the orphanage! He had always been by the Sultan's side...

"Go, tell everyone, shout with your loudest voice as you run," you command. "Tell them everything you just saw!"

The youth nods; he runs down from the throne, down the steps... across the remains, and into the Lapis Lazuli Hall...

Thus, in the clear voice of this youth, in a place unknown to all, a great monarch and his dynasty meet their end.

When you accomplish all this, you look back… Beneath the steps of the throne, hardly anyone remains standing – neither victors nor vanquished, all exhausted by the battle… Not a single soul witnesses the fight that just took place! Beyond the Lapis Lazuli Hall, chaos still rages… Amid this mountain of corpses and sea of blood, in a place unknown to all, a great monarch and his dynasty meet their end.
