5010022.title: Behind the Veil
strings: Behind the Veil
The moment the Sultan failed, you felt a bond dissolve—a game binding, manipulating, forcing you was broken by your hand. Now, you desperately pursue the severed thread, trying to grasp its master...
Legitimacy
Possible Means to Eliminate the Sorceress
Protagonist
What can you do to her?
Inked
Erased
Data Deletion
Data Poisoning
Celestial Intervention
The Game is Over, For Now

The Magician stood at the very top of the royal palace. When you found her, the moon had just risen, and she was gazing at the city below.
You suddenly realized that the Sultan's Game was over, and she was no longer protected by those laws... Perhaps now was the moment she could be destroyed...
At the sight of the divine blade in your hand, the Magician leaped and fled swiftly—yet you had already hurled the spear forged by the Creator Themselves. Navudo, Inscriber of Worlds, pierced the Magician's chest effortlessly beneath the moonlight. Through this puppet body, it siphoned the power of the mastermind behind it, just as a nib draws in ink.
Even her scream was devoured. The mysterious woman who had toyed with all living things turned into a tattered rag. Everything that it and its master had amassed by tormenting humanity over millennia reverted to ink and returned to Navudo's nib. So long as you resisted the temptation to wield it again, you could seal this evil away forever...

The Magician stood at the very top of the royal palace. When you found her, the moon had just risen, and she was gazing at the city below.
You suddenly realized that the Sultan's Game was over, and she was no longer protected by those laws... Perhaps now was the moment she could be destroyed...
At the sight of the divine blade in your hand, the Magician leaped and fled swiftly toward the sky—yet you had already hurled the edge forged by the Creator Themselves. Shunia, Purifier of Worlds, pierced the Magician's chest effortlessly beneath the moonlight, bringing purification upon the distant mastermind.
Even her scream was erased. The mysterious woman who had toyed with all living things contracted upon the blade and faded into nothingness... Everything that it and its master had amassed by tormenting humanity over millennia was utterly wiped out. Even the sacred blade was worn down by a full hand's length in the process.

The Magician stood at the very top of the royal palace. When you found her, the moon had just risen, and she was admiring the city below.
You suddenly realized that the Sultan's Game was over, and she was no longer protected by those laws... Perhaps now was the time she could be destroyed...
So you raised the glowing Dragon's Eye; it trembled slightly, and you decided to stall the Magician with words until the next blast finished charging.
"This is pointless—at your level, you should understand, shouldn't you?" The Magician stretched beneath the moonlight, offering an alluring smile. "I am merely a terminal, a vessel walking the world... Rather than waste your precious firepower on me... why not choose a special experience from me instead?"
She then unfolded her form, and countless cards and scenes spread out before you, shifting with your thoughts... There was the long homeward voyage of a hero, who tricked the gods for blessings by breaking cards; a loyal minister who played this game with her in the dark to preserve the dynasty's last embers; a revolutionary who used this forbidden power to forge a divine blade to slay the Thunder Emperor... All were new games and upgraded rules you had never known. These were the tools with which it toyed with humanity, seeking to archive the entire world.
You pretended to be entranced, leaning forward, your hand drifting through the countless scenes as if lost in the stories—until the Dragon's Eye chimed, signifying full charge.
A blazing white pupil emerged from the crystal sphere, taking in everything: not the Magician, but the countless stories and cards, all the data They had gathered since humanity's birth—using a thousand forms and games to tempt heroes, manipulate souls, and sort all living things through suffering. All of it now fell within the Dragon Eye's gaze.
The Magician fled, screaming as she turned into billowing smoke and soared upward to escape destruction, but it was too late... As the Dragon's Eye closed and its light faded, everything it had stared upon and recorded vanished into the void.
You waited a moment, wondering if any great reward would appear after the Magician disappeared into the sky... Sadly, just like the illusory game, nothing changed in the real world save for the stir in your heart. It was time to return and finish your work.

The Magician stood at the very top of the royal palace. When you found her, the moon had just risen, and she was admiring the city below.
You suddenly realized that the Sultan's Game was over, and she was no longer protected by those laws... Perhaps now was the time she could be destroyed...
So you raised the Dragon's Eye that exuded a dark aura; it trembled slightly, and you decided to stall the Magician with words until the next blast finished charging.
"This is pointless—at your level, you should understand, shouldn't you?" The Magician stretched beneath the moonlight, offering an alluring smile. "I am merely a terminal, a vessel walking the world... Rather than waste your precious firepower on me... why not choose a special experience from me instead?"
She then unfolded her form, and countless cards and scenes spread out before you, shifting with your thoughts... There was the long homeward voyage of a hero, who tricked the gods for blessings by breaking cards; a loyal minister who played this game with her in the dark to preserve the dynasty's last embers; a revolutionary who used this forbidden power to forge a divine blade to slay the Thunder Emperor... All were new games and upgraded rules you had never known. These were the tools with which it toyed with humanity, seeking to archive the entire world.
You pretended to be entranced, leaning forward, your hand drifting through the countless scenes as if lost in the stories—until the Dragon's Eye chimed, signifying full charge.
A pitch-black pupil emerged from the crystal sphere, like a blade in the void. It did not target the Magician, but the countless stories and cards, all the data it had gathered since humanity's birth—using a thousand forms and games to tempt heroes, manipulate souls, and sort all living things through suffering.
At first, only a tiny wound appeared, then it widened and gushed black venom... The Magician fled, screaming as she turned into billowing smoke and soared upward. She tried to escape, but it was too late...
What you infused into it was not the poison of destruction, but the creation of all life—all that They disdained, loathed, and rejected: the ordinary days of mortals, repetitive labor and meals, mundane love that was neither romantic nor decadent, meaningless effort and endurance, the daydreams of fools and cowards... Now these stories flooded her collection a trillion times over, corrupting and erasing the meaning of all Their future work.
You waited a moment, wondering if any great reward would appear after the Magician disappeared into the sky... Sadly, just like the illusory game, nothing changed in the real world save for the stir in your heart. It was time to return and finish your work.

You discovered the Magician atop the palace's highest tower, silhouetted against the rising moon as she gazed upon the sprawling city.
A realization struck you - with the Sultan's Game concluded, the arcane protections that once shrouded her had dissolved. For perhaps the first time, she stood vulnerable.
Your finger traced the celestial sigil in the air - a beacon to the watching cosmos. "Here!" you called to the void above. "Bear witness, the Star-Souleds! If your Highlord's covenant holds true, strike down this deceiver!"
Even as you made your desperate plea, the Magician's lips curled into that knowing smile. She leapt gracefully toward the silver moonbeams, ready to vanish into their embrace.
A heartbeat later, she hung suspended in the night air. A luminous lance, thin as gossamer yet unyielding as fate itself, had descended from the heavens to impale her.
The firmament trembled. The stars - those ancient arbiters - had answered. Justice arrived not swiftly but with terrible certainty as countless shafts of stellar light transfixed the Magician's form. Held aloft like a divine puppet, her first true cry of anguish reached your ears.
The celestial tapestry rotated as it had since time immemorial, following its ordained path. Methodically, mercilessly, it tore her essence asunder, consigning each fragment to cosmic oblivion. Not until eleven millennia had passed would the stars align again to permit her return.
The Highlord's will was done. As the North Star blazed triumphant, outshining even the moon's pale glow. Your covenant with the divine had been fulfilled at last.

The sorceress was at the highest point of the palace. When you found her, the moon had just risen, and she was admiring the city below.
You suddenly realized, now that the Sultan's Game had ended, she was no longer protected by those rules... perhaps now, she could be eliminated.
But the opportunity was fleeting; what was it that caused your hesitation at that moment? Physical exhaustion, the endless magical power contained in that card box, or her ambiguous smile?
When you came to your senses, she had already leapt, disappearing into the moonlit ripples, as if she never existed...
No matter how dramatic the experiences of the past while were, your duties and rights as both actor and audience had all ended—you could clearly feel this. Only those cards you hadn't yet broken remained in your collection as mementos and tokens, evidence of your experiences.

Many are asking you about your views on the future—you tell them we can do better.
You have begun dividing the trophies, using them to bribe those powerful enough allies to cement your position.
As a Noble, you have governed this country for many years, and everyone should trust you that everything will be as it was before.
An impulsive and sentimental person rarely climbs to such heights as you—perhaps you will bring some change!
In tales passed down by word of mouth, the courts of the mythic age held jinns, demonic servants, and faerie concubines... Now, at long last, you had brought one of them into reality.

You quietly told Ziad that the accounts of the previous Sultan would simply be wiped clean—no need to calculate them. Just tell you how much remained in the treasury... He fell to his knees and wept bitterly, as if he had just returned from the depths of hell.

You had barely spoken Abdul’s name—let alone named the reward for your former superior—when he began to protest, showering you with honeyed words. Amidst the false warmth, you both smiled thinly and let the matter lie.
You appointed Alim as the court's master spy—his pickpockets will steal things far more valuable than gold coins... and he accepted this commission with a complex expression.
You bestowed a new title upon Adila [Dragon Slayer], a title more honorable than Lion Hunter, belonging to warriors. In the future, countless warriors might embark on adventures for this title...
You conferred a noble title to Arumina right there—much more noble than her father's. Her surprised expression was utterly charming.
You granted Murad Tus a new surname and title, now also called 'Zephyr,' but this time 'Lord' can be added to it—this name was not bought by a father-in-law.
Amur was made the Royal Judge by you, now even nobles must submit to his arbitration.
You granted Junah noble status, along with twelve servants, an estate, and tax privileges in textiles, encouraging courtly women to practice the act of saluting a former commoner in secret.
You instructed Jawad to oversee the capital's commerce—ideally gathering enough funds for the new government swiftly.
Previously, the Sultan always controlled the nation's troops, but now Jabal has been given this honorable mission by you—his family is overjoyed and has become powerful supporters of yours.
You have ordered Zaki, as the Court Honor Guard commander, to restore order in the capital—both nobles and commoners need to fear his rod and chains.
You bid Iman kneel, patting his shoulder and head as a priest blesses the humble – then you grant him alone the right to raise a new temple.
You command Emane to build a school, spreading Rationality—and your command to all commoners.
You ennoble Inal—she will become one of the court administrators in the future.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys – they must be impatient to know what happened here. 
She embraced this opportunity with enthusiasm.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys – they must be impatient to know what happened here. 
For this purpose, you bestowed upon her an ancient, tongue-twisting noble surname - to which she raised no objection, as long as it wasn't her original one - along with several trunks filled with exquisite garments, both men's and women's attire.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys—they must be impatient to know what happened here.
Wait, come back, put on a few more clothes, men's or women's clothes are fine.
In short, you declare that the Dancer has regained a noble status, becoming a member of a great family again—your family.

You tell [xiaochou.name] that this realm is vast beyond measure, and all you know is but a speck near the capital. You hand it secret documents and proofs, along with a new charge: to roam, to uncover all that lies upon this land! And to tell you of it through mirrors and verse. [xiaochou.name] finds this most intriguing.

You command [xiaochou.name] to take up the mantle of the new headsman—henceforth, it shall be [xiaochou.name] who severs every noble head. And in that fleeting moment, it may glimpse the tales of the condemned—etched in the glint of the blade, mirrored in the spill of blood... and share them with you in the hushed hours of the night.

You command [xiaochou.name] to join the scholars of human in devising intricate experiments—of magic, of light, of gods and realms beyond. No matter the cost, the essence of the world's workings must be uncovered. It will sate [xiaochou.name]'s every curiosity and grant you power unending, perhaps.

You command [xiaochou.name] to raise a city in the desert—one meant solely for those who are unhuman. In time, spirits and fiends alike shall kneel as your subjects... though most dismiss it as the fevered dream of a mad ruler.
You gift the closest and most fertile grassland to the capital to Aziz, and the grasslands originally belonging to his Father are also returned to him... He is now a nomadic prince again.
You grant her a license to operate a brothel—tax-free for ten years. Salwiyah cries with joy and desperately kisses your toes.
You declare that all of Zazie's Property and status within the Sultan's court are protected by you—that's enough; she already has too much.
You allow Seliman to continue managing the court guards – his expression is extremely complex.
You informed Samir that he was free to choose between staying on as court physician or leaving the court with a great fortune. He chose the former without hesitation.
You declare that you will protect Sadani's wealth and safety—including the child she carries within her. As these words leave your lips, a cascade of whispers ripples through the court.
You gift the three hills near the capital to Riel, which are now the habitat of her people, and she can now go to the slave market and break the chains of all the slaves on the spot.
You command Jenna to manage all the artisans in the capital and all the licenses for processing precious metals. This privilege is enough to reward any loyal friend...
Nawfal certainly doesn't want any privilege or reward... So you announce a pardon in advance for anything Nawfal says in this hall in the future—no matter who she curses, no matter how harsh.
You command Nabhani to set up a swordsman academy in the capital, of course, he evades countless times, so you easily title him as Sword Saint, now he's satisfied.
You quietly tell Nayla that soon you'll be making love to her, not just once... Nothing could please her more than this promise.

Maggie... for everything she's done, it's almost impossible to repay her with material things, so you reward her family and announce a three-year tax exemption for the residents of the capital in her name.
You give Manar enough investment and privilege, ordering her to explore unknown territories – and this time, you're bringing peace.
You announce the establishment of the Miracle Society, a research organization led by Mahir—this time she will have practically infinite budget and resources.
No matter what, you think the new era needs new attire and flags—the creation and design of these will be entrusted to Malkina.
You give the Royal Library to Lumera, she can barely hold back her desire to go take a look immediately.
You announce the true identity of the Nameless Swordsman to everyone, and restore all his privileges as a member of the royal family—to which he merely shrugged.
The Chamberlain grovels before you, expressing loyalty with lavish words—you merely offer him some comfort: from now on, fewer people will die in the court.
You appoint Raed as Tribune—restoring the position... more people will join her in the future.
You restore Arumina's status—the title and Property her Father lost are now back in her hands, but she still seems unable to feel happy.
You give him an official court position: to manage a team of couriers, ensuring that information and orders are transmitted quickly and accurately in the chaotic capital.
The former thief... now people call him the High Constable—you tell him to catch whomever you want.
You command Jalila to quickly go to the Sultan's Harem—to rein in the chaotic concubines, servants, and looting pickpockets. From now on, she is your chief steward of the court.

You declare the King of Flames to be a national saint. Every year on this day is the flame festival, people will wear the King of Flames' attire and parade in the streets, celebrating the tyrant's demise... All handicrafts must be sold with national authorization.
Few decisions you genuinely feel sorry to the ancestors for—but as long as Hassan is happy: now you can call him a court poet.
You gift Habunah a royal spinning factory and command her to pass on her craft, making it a national specialty.
Habib is now a cour de chef, and you assure him that no matter who becomes the Sultan later, his troublemaking root won't be cut off~
After Gullis gained the status of a Free Person, nothing changed; it seems he believes he has not repaid the debt of gratitude he owes you...
You grant Qais a lot of wealth and a mansion, and land... He is so stunned by such splendor and wealth—this is exactly why you came to watch.
You give Fatuna the privilege to procure supplies for the court, a job that is both wealthy and prestigious, soon people will forget that she was a widow.

You don't reward Faris directly. Instead, you tell him that since there is already a Lady Cat in the court, it's only fitting for a dog to hold a noble title as well. He can handle the details himself, but overall, it's a title that will echo through the ages

You've never seen Faris smile so brightly.
You announce that Faraj has become the new court scribe—from today on, what he writes will become history.
You prepare a generous gift for Fardak—and promise to send him back to his hometown: to tell everyone afar that the Sultan's Rule is over!
You announce that Fadia is no longer a Slave, she will become a free person and receive enough reward—then you secretly tell her to be ready to become your spy.
You permit Buthayna to write [Location where the Sultan fought] and [Location where [player.name] fought] anywhere in her shop, in golden letters.
You request craftsmen to erect a statue for Lady Becky, build a temple—telling people about the great achievements they can obtain once blessed by the cat.
You announce that Badriyyah's church no longer needs covert dissemination, this ancient belief is now legal—and her laughter makes everyone genuinely doubt whether that might be a good idea...

You order the construction of an academy, specifically to collect and study the nations and cultures destroyed by the Sultan, and gather their former survivors. Perhaps one day, we could gain something valuable from this lost Rationality.
You restore Ansuya's royal status and treatment—furnishing her with enough wealth and slaves: from now on she can do whatever she wishes to.
You command Asal to organize through a century of royal archives – perhaps the few tomes he hasn't yet cracked open. You hope he crafts a history for the ages, ensuring the Sultan's tale lives on.

You retire Adil and grant him land far from the capital, preventing those he once hunted from coming for revenge. Stubborn and headstrong, Adil knows only very few catchers have such good fortune, and accepts everything respectfully.
You told Anita that you had always admired her gift for medicine, and that you would fund her continued study, practice, and research—until she became a truly exceptional physician.
You sealed this creature that did not belong to the mortal world. Perhaps one day, another desperate minister would shatter its prison...

You told Ziad that you wanted to see the Sultan's old accounts by sunset tomorrow—fully balanced, not a single coin out of place! Good grief, why had the fool wet himself? You hadn't even said you would kill him!
Perhaps by some foxy instinct, when your men stormed Abdul's manor to seize him for execution, the former Vizier had already vanished into the night with his kin... the halls left hollow.
You strip Adila of the privilege of swordplay and confine her to her home until she bears a son. Adila would rather die.
You distribute images of Alim and anti-theft manuals to every commoner, and he seems to see this as a new challenge.

You publicly announce that in the coming months, even half a year, you need Zephyr to deliver the news of the Sultan's death throughout the empire and announce the name of the new king. After he agrees, there is another heavy, tearful bite mark on his arm.

You arrange for Arumina the strictest court etiquette teacher, one on whom no amount of wheedling or tantrum will work, and assure everyone she will transform into the most polite lady in the capital.

You deprive Zephyr of his surname and tell him that a real Man must earn his name himself, not rely on his father-in-law's handouts. He seemed optimistic and held Arumina's little hand tightly, making many promises.
You list Amur's every crime and smile genuinely as you ruthlessly behead him.

You publicly hold Junah's soft hands and announce your love for her, as her eyes sparkled with tears of emotion, only to laugh and say it was just a joke. The next day, you receive news of her death and the mockery toward this lowly woman, who could not bear a simple jest.

You tell Jawad, that you have always known about when he dispatched an Assassin against you for a few Gold Coins. Now, you want to play a game with him—your Assassin will set out within seven days.
He's almost on his knees in fright, sobbing, offering his entire estate for his life... hehe, this is exactly the result you wanted. You smile while confiscating his home in front of him.

You strip Jabal of his Honor Guard and General title, reclaiming control over all the Troop under his command.
When he hands over the token to you, he even smiles: "Great, now I can finally go off on an adventure free"

You announce that Zaki is no longer your student, the boy's eyes immediately redden. He looks at you in disbelief, trembling, saying after a long time, he will strive... strive to earn back the qualification to learn from you.
You command him to receive the Queen of the Whip's whip for seven consecutive days, then display those beautiful scars to all the guests in the House of Delights.
You deprive this proud old lady of her title. From now on, no one will have the patience to listen to anything she says anymore.

Given all the trouble Inal stirs up for you, you gift her a vial of poison. She drinks it in tears, and nothing happens – until the next day, when her first bite reveals she tastes nothing, no matter what she eats.
You give Shama an exceptionally sharp dagger, she smiles slightly, and without hesitation makes a choice.
You deny her bloodline and expel her from your home. Anyway, now she's of no use to you.
Who would pay special attention to the Sultan's harem at such a turbulent time? The disappearance of a concubine or slave girl went unnoticed by all—except you, who had arranged everything.
You no longer have anything important for Aziz to do. You order Aziz to polish ten stone lunch boxes a day and hand them to you, no work, no sleep.

You loudly praise Salwiyah's beautiful eyes, and when she shyly approaches you, you order to have them gouged out, then personally inlaid costly amethyst into her bleeding eye sockets as compensation.

You order Zazie to remove all her gold ornaments, silk, and satin, then send her off on a sealed godly palanquin. Your people will carry her to the highland snow mountains and offer her to her worshiped deity.

Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Seliman has long anticipated this moment, kneeling on the ground, eyes lowered, restraining himself, without looking at anyone.
You order the Court Physician to bring out a bowl of poison that will kill a person within an hour, then pour it into his mouth. He struggles painfully but ultimately couldn't detoxify himself.
The concubine Sadani takes the dagger you grant her, her pale face showing unexpected calm – her final plea is to glimpse the Sultan one last time.

When you intended to kill an Ally who once fought alongside you, this Beast escaped the city with astonishing intuition. It's imaginable she'll wander around this land, lurking in the shadows, waiting for you to show a flaw, looking forward to the day she can eat the traitor's liver.

You give Jenna a bag of gold, urging her to leave the capital. It is foreseeable that the storm will not calm with the Sultan's death, but become increasingly tumultuous, with endless biting and fighting, until this country welcomes a new Sultan recognized by the majority.
When you pronounce his death sentence, Nawfal says nothing, merely accepting everything calmly, accepting that you will be another Sultan.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. No matter what grievances you once had with Nabhani, everything ends here.
You use Nabhani's head to prove to the world that you are more ruthless and suspicious than the Sultan.
You have him placed under house arrest, soon he died of illness.
Just this once, you cruelly tell her, she has no right to refuse.

In this world, only the dead will always keep secrets, only the dead will never change their original intentions.
Seliman takes the dagger, smiles slightly, neither hatred nor regret.

The cruel game has ended, but the harm towards each other is forever etched in your hearts.
Upon divorce, you gave her a lot of money, but when leaving, besides her dowry, she didn't take a single extra dime. You tell her, if in the next life, don't become your wife. She just purses her lips and smiles, not agreeing with you.
You decide to imprison Manar, forbidding her from further drafting more detailed maps, in case of leaking secrets to your enemies. Soon, her guards send you the news of her demise.

You let her personally try the Confused Learning Machine she created herself. After about five tries, she will just lie in the yard basking in the sun. Perhaps the sun can give her some inspiration? Who knows.

Malkina had never heard of such an absurd reason for execution, and because of this absurdity, she knew your decision was irrevocable. Soon after, you hear that her mother burned down the tailor shop in remorse, but unfortunately, there is no medicine for regret in the world.

You not only burned Lumera's books but also ordered that commoners are not allowed to read or learn, because this girl made you realize how terrifying this force was. You used it to overthrow the Sultan, and one day, someone will use it to overthrow you.
Ironically, until Lumera jumped into the burning study, desperately trying to save them, and was eventually swallowed by the flames, she did not use her power to resist your decision.
You did not believe that he had no ambition for the throne that was within his reach, so you executed him, completely burying those departed names in the blood and dust of history.

Whether they left their handprints on the Testaments to Bygone Oaths or not, whether they were loyal to you or doubted you—all were stunned by your shameless betrayal. Chaos engulfed the court. The stars glinted above, and a streak of murderous light pierced through the war-ravaged window lattice, casting itself upon your neck...
You killed Lazag for the same reason that those who usurped the throne before you killed the chamberlain of the previous dynasty.
As long as she dies, those promises you made to bend her to your will need no honoring – what a joke, a mere vagrant daring to barter with you?

At the victory banquet, you ordered her to pour wine for all the nobles and noblewomen who recognized her. Tears welled up in her eyes, but she gritted her teeth and endured it.
It's okay; life will slowly teach her that the more she endures, the more torment there is.
You handed a large box of documents to Zephyr, ordering him to deliver them to every station in the empire. He won't be back for three to five years.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Jemor without hesitation.

You publicly announced a long list of Jalila's 'Fat Sheep', sweeping your fierce gaze over those men who desperately ducked their heads like ostriches. Of course, they wouldn't dare retaliate against you, but they certainly wouldn't spare the woman who leaked this secret, nor would they trust a safe house riddled with cracks.

You held up the cloak of the King of Flames high and then threw it into the fire. The sparks and ashes stained the desperate faces of the onlookers and children. You scorn those trembling people. Did you see? The redemption they longed for is nothing but a useless joke.
Without waiting for you to drive him away, he left you a farewell note with wet edges, not sure if it was just pulled out from a lamb stew.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Hamar without hesitation.
You executed Habunah because you dreamed of the blue waves no longer lifting you but drowning you on that night.
You executed Habib, without giving anyone any reason.
So, you didn't dare to bet on whether he would point the fearsome bow and arrow at you. You executed him.

Qais once defied you and even pointed at your nose and scolded you... These things you had almost forgotten suddenly emerged from the corners of your memory, leaving you tossing and turning, with a lump in your throat.
Forget it, let him die.
Fatuna confessed to her crimes without objection, and the simple truth of the world is that murder must be atoned for by death.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Besides, shouldn't a loyal person accompany his beloved master underground?
Loyalty is meaningless. A dog that betrays its master once will do it again. You don’t trust him, so you execute him.

You drive him out of the capital and tell him the truth: the Sultan's realm would take twenty years to cross by camel, the continent beneath would require one hundred and fifty years, and beyond the sea, there is another one hundred and fifty years, and another after that... The world is so vast, he should not waste his life merely staring at you.

He has no choice but to swear to you with tears in his eyes that he will record everything during his journey and send it to you.

By your order, Fardak is stripped of his surname and inheritance rights, but still keep him under house arrest in the most expensive mansion in the city. Now he should know that you and the Sultan are cut from the same cloth.

In despair, he draws Kaplan's End, the blade he couldn't decide to use before, ending his own life.
You expelled her from your court, knowing well what harsh fate awaited a defenseless former Sultan's Slave.

You had your eye on that tender piece of Property from the House of Delights for a long time! And Buthayna had the good sense to offer the majority of profits to you, and from now on, free of charge.
Only then did you give a satisfied nod.

Lady Becky is a clever little cat. He knows who is good and who is bad to him. When you wanted to order him caught and spanked, he had long disappeared to someplace unknown. Perhaps it's somewhere nobody knows him as Lady Becky. People might call him Little White, Pearl, or Rice, but it doesn't matter to him.

You bound her with a chain imbued with magic to the stake, announcing to all the disaster brought by the Other she worshipped. She laughed insanely. The fire burned for three days and nights before it was extinguished, but her laughter seemed to linger above the execution ground for a month.

The Sultan is dead, what reason does Bharat have to linger in your city? You threw him out and confiscated all his merchandise as revenge compensation. It must be said, some of the items inside were quite useful... Hmm, why not take them out sooner?
You give Ansuya travel expenses. Her homeland has turned into scorched earth, but you believe she still wants to go back for a look.
Just those few books, who could possibly read enough? You order Asal to immediately collect books from all over the world for you, and not to return until he has gathered at least a hundred.

Until the seas run dry, until every mirror in the world is shattered... pledge your loyalty forever to the humans you despise and scorn!
Facing your greedy visage, [xiaochou.name] laughs aloud—the words you speak as a sovereign lend this pact such potent magic! [xiaochou.name] kneels to kiss your hand, like the humblest of servants—"Very well, my master. With this decree, humans shall never be free of the Mirror!"
So long as charges are fabricated, no one in this world remains innocent. Your men quickly uncover solid evidence to accuse him, and, in accordance with law and reason, they put him to death.
You killed the girl—simply because you needed to kill one of the exiles from the fallen kingdom, to prove that you had not forgotten the traditions of this land.

At long last, you exhale softly, step before the crowd with a faint smile, and – with a weight lifted – declare that you confess your sins. In this Sultan's Game, you kill the innocent, you violate the unwilling, you exhaust every means to amass wealth beyond your needs, and you bring chaos and war to this land… The game ends, but the sins endure. You proclaim to your friends, ministers, and people that you set forth today on a path of atonement – a bitter journey until the nightmares that haunt you night and day and the restless spirits that linger find their final peace.
The tumultuous day finally comes to an end. May everyone find peaceful sleep tonight.

strings: Fruit
Go on, everyone is waiting for you to make the final division... Right now, you have the power to taste the sweetest fruits of victory, and cast aside the seeds of the past.

To take this book as one's faith is to take knowledge as one's faith.
But knowledge, once made a belief, is powerful enough to wash away every other turning of fate...
and drive all things toward one solitary end.

You proclaim the usurper has fallen, the homeland restored, all promises fulfilled. People cheer jubilantly, though they've long forgotten what the homeland once was.
And you will rule with kindness and justice over everyone - otherwise, be careful, because you have completely taught too many people how to revolt.

You enumerate the previous Sultan's atrocities - drinking the people's blood, consuming their flesh, seizing their children, violating their parents - all maintained through the people's own resources! Now the tyrant falls, a new nation rises, the oppressor's good days end! You'll be a monarch who stands with the people, creating a nation belonging to its citizens!
Doubtful, hesitant gazes fill the hall. A non-oppressive ruler? What even is that? Is it possible? This empire has suffered brutal rule by Sultans and kings for hundreds of years. Can your new era truly gain support from the people you cherish?

You end the Sultan's Game with a Sultan Card.
You smile as you break this Conquest Card and declare there will be absolutely no more after this. Only then do the ministers breathe a sigh of relief and begin to swear allegiance to you one by one.
Humans admire strength, and you are the world's mightiest hero. Your rule stands upon the fire-dragon head dripping magma-thick blood.

You announced the abolition of royal power and slavery, organized the national assembly... During this part, even though all the nobles were full of doubts, Nawfal still began clapping first... Then you called his name and told everyone that Mr. Nawfal will discuss how to create the future as the chief speaker - oh, judging by his expression, ruining a country was worth it.

You announce that the Sultan's blood-heir will continue ruling under your loyal guardianship. Nothing has changed, yet everything improves.
Sadani sits upon the throne's thick fur cushions, her unborn child the legitimate ruler, the future Sultan.

You informed everyone that the Sultan's bloodline heir would continue ruling under your loyal guardianship.
Before finishing, Zazie leapt onto the throne like a cat finding comfort.
"The Sultan is here," she caressingly touched her still-flat belly, "He's coming soon."—her gaze was fixated on you.
Before all witnesses, you declare Prince Sirshana's restoration complete - he reclaims his country, his authority, and his true name. All hail him by Sirshana's name!

Sirshana struggles desperately against ascending the throne, fearing he'll become like the Sultan you overthrew. To quell his resistance, you become his vizier, promising to personally monitor his conduct.

You demonstrate kingly generosity and magnanimity: as victor, you spare the defeated dynasty's bloodline.
Your actions appear noble, but unfortunately, many believe you spared the royal children because you're intimately involved with the former Sultan's princess...
You orchestrated a revolution and personally led it to success, which offered the ancient empire new hope but also showed the ease of toppling a nation...
"Nawfal as vizier"—an imperial saying meaning "the right person for the right task".

Amidst the revolutionary fervor and excitement, you pull Nawfal onto the platform, announcing to all that he shall be the nation's vizier.
"Now, address the people, Mr. Nawfal."
You know, Nawfal truly cares about this country, more than you, more than anyone else... This should be the best arrangement.
Nawfal won't worship you just because you killed a winged, fire-breathing reptile - that's precisely why he should be vizier.
Thank you for your trust! I will serve you until death.
It has to be Abdul – named heir to the vizier's seat, he bows at once in the Fallen Dynasty's style - his movements so fluid and natural, as if he'd practiced daily for decades.

It has to be Abdul – named heir to the vizier's seat, he swiftly condemns the Sultan's past crimes, deftly lifting everyone, himself included, out of the mire. Now, only one villain remains, and he is dead - perfect!

Abdul delivers a passionate, brief speech – he clearly knows Nawfal's theories inside out, and through his lips, those rough, noble-rattling words turn to honey and gleam with gold... The crowd sheds their fears for the future at once!

It has to be Abdul – named heir to the vizier's seat, he swiftly condemns the Sultan's past crimes, deftly lifting everyone, himself included, out of the mire. Now, only one villain remains, and he is dead - so let us living ones enjoy ourselves!
Upon accepting the vizier position, Abdul immediately presents your imperial title and honorifics, the latter stretching to... let me count... one hundred seventy-four words.
Iman humbly accepts the vizier position. The Purist becomes increasingly entrenched in the empire, with the clean fragrance of purity permeating the court.
Badriyyah accepts the vizier position with a smile. The cultists regain their confidence - that very night, they smear the Purist temple with foul mud.
When Mahir took what you offered her on instinct, she thought it was some new toy worth studying. But once she held the seal of the vizier, letting go would not be so easy.
With a smile, you bestowed upon Qais the seal of highest authority beneath the Sultan alone.
In your eyes, Raed—with his deep ties to both palace and street—was the only fitting choice for vizier.

Amid the uproar of the crowd, you publicly revealed your relationship with Arzuna. They still murmured and doubted the ability of the woman you had just appointed as vizier. But in this moment, none dared lead against your will.
[s3.name] was dumbfounded, it was truly an astonishing decision—[s3.gender] was obviously unprepared

You declare the country will no longer have a state religion; people may freely choose which god to worship. Many devout believers disapprove of your decision. Previously they hated each other; now they unite in hating you.

You loudly announced the contributions of the Church of the Immaculate Purity in this coup, praising them as educators, healers, and guides! Keeping this stable reassured many people. At least, you didn't intend to overthrow everything that was.

Many people heard of this God for the first time, and people whispered, you even heard 'they eat children' and 'they can enhance virility'... and other unwise murmurs. Supporting a new God is a good symbol, telling everyone you will change everything - even things in the sky.

You tell everyone that gods show no mercy and humans shouldn't place hope in god hands. Therefore, you ban all religious activities, promoting atheism nationwide. People whisper among themselves - some think you're insane, while others anger you more by claiming you're a new god.
Once, the stars blessed this land, and they never left! Now those who feel kindness and wisdom in their light need fear no longer—speak your faith aloud! Praise the stars!

You gestured to the Encyclopedia in your hand. This was only the table of contents. Many did not truly grasp what you meant by "knowledge," yet they knelt anyway. The pages stirred, and as all living beings bowed, they began to record everything.

Monarchs are born to battle each other, like lion pack leaders who lose only once - when killed by the new leader. Standing beside the Sultan's corpse, you finish speaking. Everyone bows their heads, the herd accepting its new master.
People stare in horror at the cage containing the Sultan beside you - no longer a ruler, just a pitiful lump of flesh. You ask your supporters to stand on the left, so no one stands on the right.

You have finished speaking, and it is clear that nothing you could say would satisfy everyone. But you made a gesture to the soldiers—signaling them to start pulling the chain of the Sultan to embark on his exile...
The former monarch slowly passed through the ministers who once revered, praised, and catered to him, leading to his downfall. They simply watched in silence, with no one following him.

You have finished speaking, and it is clear that nothing you could say would satisfy everyone. But beside you is the Sultan's corpse... or rather, what remains defiled. People always argue with the wise, mock the intelligent, question the faithful—but they always show submission and praise to every puff of the monstrous.
Thus, beside this unbearable filth, your cause is completed.

You finished speaking. Clearly, whatever you said couldn't please everyone. But beside you was a human bound in chains and shackles - weak and exhausted, covered in blood and filth, yet watching everything with keen interest.
He didn't speak, and others dared not voice any opposition, only exchanging strange glances below - what new game were you playing?

You boldly produce this ring, wearing it on your finger... Nobles glance briefly before prostrating. They don't know this ring lost its menacing power, nor do they care about following your ideals and oaths - they simply submit from habit...
This moment brings sudden understanding of the Sultan - this is indeed tedious. Though undeniably effective.

People noticed you did not arrange a seat for yourself but instead distributed the fruits to everyone—and you did not bother to explain, but simply floated away... No one dared to stop you.

You explained to everyone—and demonstrated the power of this artifact. They all knelt down sincerely, though most of them wondered how many you could slay with it... You had meant to show that this thing would make war unnecessary and spare countless lives for goodness' sake.

You arrange the empire's political structure with intricate complexity, ensuring every class and faith receives some satisfaction from the new empire. But can a nation pleasing everyone truly achieve lasting stability?
You've designed an era filled with unrest and change. Risk and opportunity coexist - will you be the one to seize destiny?

You thrash wildly, too fierce for the five soldiers to hold, but then more join in – your colleagues, those who've feared you, shunned you, or used you in the Sultan's twisted game. They claw at your neck and your ankles, jabbing with knives, hairpins, and rings, tearing into you like butchers at a slaughter. These are the countless souls ranked by this game, then mercilessly slaughtered. Now, you join their ranks, twisted into a record of the world alongside those you once harmed.

So, with a final surge, you clutch the Sultan's chest – dragging his soul with you, trapping this moment in eternity... Thus, your suffering will be endless, and neither of your souls will ever find release.

You embraced [s3.name], then extended more arms to embrace everyone. Your dark power entranced them... Then you peeled away their skins like removing clothing. Your kiss wandered within their bodies, drinking their life essence one by one. All love and desire you ever shared, might have shared, or could have experienced across countless realities were harvested alongside their organs, becoming a feast for the abyss. 
The Old Ones gathered as ancient entities sampled the newcomer's offerings, nodding in approval... The Carnality Card, along with all sacrifices, crumbled to ash, opening the gateway to eternal darkness. 
From afar, the Magician uttered impotent curses, but you no longer needed to heed them - like a heartless wanderer, you tidied your lovers' forms and garments, ignoring the dark stains and the chaos left behind... You entered the abyss without hesitation.

Before everyone's eyes, you cut open your throat, extracting the first dagger from within. You then opened many old wounds, recounting their stories—some were physical scars, others wounds of the heart. 
From each wound emerged a weapon, and with each weapon created, another pair of crimson hands grew to wield them. Soon, you blossomed into something vigorous and terrible, like the hundred-armed monsters that battled gods in ancient myths. 
Yet you remained gentle, caressing the bodies of the witnesses with your powerful arms, demanding a final parting gift... 
Darkness surged as demons gathered, the Old Ones urging the newly-brave warrior to join the eternal game of violence... With the final Bloodshed Card, you sliced open their chests, extracting all blood, love, and joyful memories—henceforth, only hatred for you would remain, their suffering forever forging your blades... 
From afar, the Magician's impotent curses held no power over you. Four bloody blades pierced the wound in your neck, sprinkled with the Bloodshed Card's ashes... your massive form contracted inward, falling through this wound directly into the abyss, leaving behind only your solitary human head.

You gathered all valuables in your home - not enough, still not enough... Amid [s3.name]'s questioning, you begged from them... They painfully vomited gold and jewels - once their trust and love for you. Others heard this strange commotion, but at your demand, they too collapsed... 
Finally, everyone's despairing tears transformed into pearls, providing sufficient travel expenses as you used the final Extravagance Card to unlock the abyss. 
As cards and wealth vanished into dark flames. 
Demons gathered, the Old Ones accepting the newcomer's offerings with approving nods... The Magician's distant curses meant nothing now. Fangs, claws, and fur grew wildly, revealing your bestial nature... Gold gradually replaced your flesh, your dwelling, even those beside you, weaving a gate magnificent enough to match your greed. 
At last, you departed what you once called home, leaving nothing but empty golden shells.

Today, your home is unusually crowded. All those you killed have gathered. The dead line your hall and courtyard in neat rows, rotting mouths murmuring loyalty. 
This scene terrified [s3.name], but when they found you, they discovered only a corpse - playing with the final Conquest Card, crumbling it to pieces, you opened a dark passage... The army of corpses began their march, with [s3.name] soon to be captured and join their ranks. 
You rose, challenging the approaching demons - ignoring the Magician's furious curses, ignoring your companions' struggles and laments, you eagerly marched toward a darker world.

You understood you would no longer be [player.name], but something remade. Few mortals ever reached such a state - perhaps this could be considered its own form of happiness.

You toss the card, broken in two, back into the magician's box with a crisp sound. "You've really completed all the games, well done, my dear courtier," the Sultan says languidly. He waves his hand, and the magician knowingly presents the box to him. "As a reward, I will grant you a grand favor." The Sultan grabs the bottom of the box and pours its contents onto the floor... You are startled to find all the cards are restored to their original state – every single one! The Sultan Cards that you broke with such agonizing effort, the ones that cost you harm to others and cruelty to yourself, now stand completely untouched... intact... perfect. Every. Single. Card! "You can choose someone to continue this game; this is my gift. Judging by your expression, my dear, are you shocked? Do you really think the game was over? Come on!" You freeze in place. Choose someone? WHO exactly? Someone you've insulted? They'll draw the Bloodshed Card and slit your throat without hesitation. Someone you love? Watch them suffer the same torments you did, then fail – just like you did. Someone you don't care about? Haven't you already fed enough strangers to this meat grinder of a game? Remember when you plucked that leaf to shield yourself from the rain? That bird underneath – its feathers soaked through. It died. That was your doing, too. A familiar impulse rises in your chest – the same righteous fire that once made you stand against the Sultan's Game. But then reality crashes down. Playing again means repeating everything. And look around you: your allies are gone. Like a harvested cornfield with only a few forgotten cobs remaining. The lonely survivors after your game. Can you truly go through with this again? Is any of this right? Dejection washes over you. Maybe just point at someone – anyone – and be done with it. Why did you even play by the rules from the beginning? You had your chance to change fate and you squandered it! If only you could start over... "Wait! Did you just mentionstart over?" "Like a trigger word has been spoken, a voice emanates from within you... It feels like a hook scratching the inside of your navel. "Want to start over? It's just a formality, you want thisevery time, hurry up! Just as you've done countless times before, you grab the hook. It yanks you – hard...

You remain the Sultan's most loyal, beloved subject! What could be more fascinating, more inconceivable than challenging a god? And you, [player.name], have delivered your master before a deranged god! The Sultan laughs uproariously - a game beyond imagination...
The Highlord raises Their javelin - They never conceived that a contemptible mortal could truly honor the sacred pact and alter the world's fate...

Their divine form should have proven unassailable. Yet as Their herald, you learned Their transgressions, Their secrets, Their vulnerabilities...
The Highland Highlord strikes first! They drive a starlight spear through the Destroyer's right eye... representing their mutual arrogance.
Next, the Sultan's graceful blade-work carves countless wounds across Their back... embodying their equally mad desires.
And you, seizing this opportunity, thrust deep into the Destroyer's chest! Your shared obsession, that willingness to shatter the world for victory, guides this nearly fatal blow...
Victory lies within reach - a deity bleeds golden ichor, approaching death... though not without cost.
The Highlord loses both eyes, punishment for Their presumption to rule mortals; the Sultan's body erupts in countless wounds, blood spattering in response to each malicious joy taken in harming others...
And you, poor [p layer.name], your chest slowly splits open, mirroring how you've repeatedly torn your own spirit throughout this game...
The Destroyer's face cracks with maniacal laughter. Now, who will deliver the killing stroke? Who will sever Their throat while cutting their own? Who will bear the sin of slaying the innocent? Will you selfish maggots surrender your lives to preserve this world?
Against Their expectations, the three despicable masters quickly choose their sacrifice - the Highlord who commands heaven's stars grasps your left hand, while the Sultan who rules earth's multitudes seizes your right arm. Your heart lies exposed, your lungs seep blood... lacking any strength to resist these monarchs' dominion, you let them guide your hand, the blade pressed between... Like a puppet, you slice open the Destroyer's throat - committing an unprecedented crime since creation's dawn, you murder a being who helped forge the world...

Their divine form should have proven unassailable. Yet as Their herald, you learned Their transgressions, Their secrets, Their vulnerabilities... First, the Sultan's graceful blade-work carves countless wounds across Their body... you know this can harm Them, for this mirrors the very desire They revealed when seeking to enter the world.
Seizing this chance, you pierce Their right eye with your spear - you know this can wound Them, for this represents Their covetous gaze upon mortal realms...
Unfortunately, this triumph demands its price. The Sultan's body erupts in countless wounds, blood spattering in response to each malicious joy taken in harming others... while you suffer blood-tears corroding your eyes, punishment for gazing directly upon divine truth.
The Destroyer's mockery rings out: Two guilty maggots dare judge a deity's sins! Each arrogant attempt will return upon you tenfold, hundredfold, millionfold! For you already wallow in sin! Like all mortals!
Without words, without sight, hearing the Sultan's mad war-cry, you instinctively hurl your weapon at the Destroyer: guided not by muscle and skill, but by your shared obsession - that madness willing to destroy the world for victory... This sinful connection drives your attack through the divine chest - while simultaneously, the Sultan's twin blades sever Their throat... You and your sovereign jointly commit an unprecedented crime since creation's dawn, conspiring to murder a being who helped forge the world...

Their divine form should have proven unassailable. Yet as Their herald, you learned Their transgressions, Their secrets, Their vulnerabilities... After you reveal everything to the Highlord, that master of stars unleashes frenzied vengeance.
Starlight spears first pierce the Destroyer's pale eyes, then methodically create countless wounds large and small across Their entire form, finally severing Their neck and letting golden blood flow.
The Highland Highlord wins again and again, this Star laughing wildly as if washing away ancient shame... Yet with the Destroyer's rending, mocking smile, retribution arrives - the Highlord's eyes explode from Their arrogance in ruling mortals! The Highlord's body tears apart, each wound marking a mortal They seduced... Finally, They bleed dry for every excessive demand for blood sacrifice.
A guilty Star-Souled dares judge true divinity's sins! Each arrogant attempt returns upon you tenfold, hundredfold, millionfold! For you already wallow in sin!
The Star weeps tears of regret - mourning Their mistakes? Or raging at failure? As Their blood nourishes the Destroyer's revival, as They rise to consume this sustenance and savor the crushed spirit... Seizing this final chance, you summon all remaining strength to hurl the Star's fallen javelin from behind: guided not by magic or skill, but by your shared obsession - that madness willing to destroy the world for victory... This sinful connection drives your attack through the divine chest - you commit an unprecedented crime since creation's dawn, murdering a being who helped forge the world...

Your body splits and bleeds, mirroring the torment you inflicted on lovers and those you never loved through lustful excess!
You begin bleeding, yet even draining every drop pales beside what you've made others shed!
The Destroyer's mockery rings out: Guilty maggot, you dare judge divine sins! Each arrogant attempt returns upon you tenfold, hundredfold, millionfold! For you already wallow in sin!
In dying despair, you hurl your weapon at the triumphant Destroyer... guided not by magic or skill, but by your shared obsession - that madness willing to destroy the world for victory... Infinite light, infinite sin. Retribution approaches - the Destroyer's final punishment. You will die for all you've done... yet without regret.
.......
Finally, after waiting centuries or perhaps mere moments: the sound of countless things breaking, like innumerable Sultan Cards snapping simultaneously... Something bound to your soul has shattered, your accumulated achievements exceeding its capacity to measure or contain...
You watch the sorceress disintegrate in the brilliant storm, see the Sultan's spirit face judgment as the game's instigator... while you become the final remnant of this runaway game.

Theoretically, you know Their weaknesses through shared sins... but They know yours as well. This is a hopeless battle - Their divine form deflects all attacks while you cannot perceive those hidden vulnerabilities... Feel no sorrow, no guilt. As a mortal, you've reached unparalleled heights... Accept glorious purification, accept the world's destiny.

Under [s3.name]’s guidance, [s4.name] undressed everyone, [s5.name] distributed the honey-flavored nectar, and [s6.name] lit the candles.
In the flickering light, shadows began to dance, woven by the ritual’s power... merging with your blood and flesh, anchoring you between reality and illusion. Praising this exceptionally elegant posture, the devotees drank the nectar, moistened themselves, and exuded the dark, holy liquid.
One by one, they filled you—through every orifice of your body and the fissures ripped open by the shadows—until you were blackened inside and out, utterly profane, drawn ever closer to the Supreme Lord…
In that abyssal darkness, the perilous seed in your heart materialized and took root in your belly. [s3.name] raised a blade and, before the dark egg could devour your flesh, swiftly extracted it and placed it into an etheric solution—not out of mercy, but because the god's egg required a vaster, more abundant vessel; one mortal alone could neither sate its hunger nor reflect its majesty!
As the followers examined your blood and Body, pulling at the tendons on the egg sac, you dreamed amidst extreme pain. 
The Abyss called to you, the evil forces once friendly to you were agitated by The Creator’s breath: For countless times, we longed for it to play with us, but it kept refusing the Abyss's invitation.
Now, it has found you, bring it to play with us! We'll reward you with legions! Let’s have endless games on the lower realm! Don’t let this arrogant guy ruin the material world, or no new players will join us!
Before you can reply, they eagerly deliver their summons—your flesh, blessed by the Abyss's power, churns and contorts... extruding a mass of uncanny flesh suspended between life and death. It radiates unbelievable magic... a gift any god would covet, yet also a trap the Abyss has set for it.

Every soul harbors fractures, and through these flaws, you allow shadow to seep into Maggie's heart. This proves necessary - no other could better carry the dark seed nestled within your spirit.
The ceremony commences... In wavering light, shadows begin their dance. You weave them with practiced care, binding them to Maggie's flesh, anchoring her between the world of substance and the realm of dreams.
All voices rise in hymns as you draw near, embracing her as every living thing must to spark creation, depositing the seed within your wife's form... allowing this vessel, already stained to perfect blackness, to complete the divine quickening.
Within mere heartbeats, Maggie's belly distends beyond mortal limits - this celestial egg cannot mature within such frail human confines... Believers swiftly produce ready blades, slicing open your wife's abdomen to transfer the dark egg into an aether-enriched solution.
The scene descends into bloody chaos, while Maggie's eyes turn obsidian - leaving only the pure tenderness the god has bestowed upon her.

Drenched in gore, her wounds still gaping, she struggles to prostrate herself before her master's incarnate flesh...

The ritual begins. She weaves darkness skillfully, manipulating the rhythm of all things, channeling the dark lord's will here... The seed in your heart transforms from phantom to reality. The divine beacon enters the world - becoming something that can be destroyed.
Seizing this opportunity, Lumera converts all remaining ritual power into a destructive command: the spell to shatter stars, knowledge etched in her soul's depths through countless cycles since birth - allowing star-spirits to sacrifice themselves for higher purpose when the world has need.
Starting from her heart, everything in the ritual becomes stardust: beautiful, ethereal, fading into dreams, distant from the material world. A deity coveting the physical realm loses Their key, and you find liberation...
Hereafter, you will exist only within stellar songs, which will speak only of the care and joy you brought Lumera - the tenderness that saved the world.

A black hand punctures the crimson membrane. Blood oceans surge as the humanoid form staggers and fights to stand upright... After unknowable eons, the Creator witnesses sunlight and earth again - the world They personally authored... And They behold Themselves anew.
How repulsive, how warped... The god begins sobbing.

Dark tendrils embrace Their designated sacrifice - yet Inal harbors no fear, only compassion.
She has eternally served as the Creator's priestess. Since the master god's exile, this bloodline has wandered lost through countless ages... yet still comprehends all the god's anguish.
My god, my god, You have endured excessive suffering! Misunderstood, forsaken, cursed, imprisoned... until You surrendered ideals and achieved this corrupted form!
Within this ocean of endless distortion and agony, one pure tear falls into Inal's palm - pristine as agate, beautiful, reflecting no light in absolute black... This represents the Creator's ink, the final remnant within the Corrupter.
"Dance, my cherished people." The teardrop's voice resonates in Inal's mind: "Offer prayer-dances for the new Creator! Through your desires, your god shall reshape this world!"
Such tremendous power - infinite possibilities explode in Inal's consciousness, nearly causing her to faint: She could possess wealth, nobility, beauty, accomplish anything... Should she make any wish, for the new world's birth, the old world shall naturally face destruction - then the Corrupter shall overflow within it, completing Their long-desired eternal dominion.
Thus, amid expectations from god and world, the girl voices her wish: "Knowledge, power, magic... these prove wonderful things. Under Your blessing, with [player.name]'s assistance, I already possess these, though merely a little, though gradually... I can already transform the world around me! Great god, share this world-transforming power with everyone who needs it! Especially children as helpless as I once was! Let all girls transform the world around them!"
The Creator's remaining ink transforms into sacred script with these words. Throughout heaven and earth, the sound of shattering glass continues endlessly - the world's laws undergo rewriting, the girl's wish materializing.

My god, You desire to dominate this world, willing to embrace such falsehood? My god, You've lost Your dreams, hence You've become so corrupt?
Before dark tendrils devour her, you witness her bewildered expression: Is destroying the world for such a god truly worthwhile? [player.name], is this genuinely your heartfelt desire?

Originally, that final sacrifice bore a sacred mission: within the Corrupter's body, using their soul and life to voice the ultimate wish. Through this hope for a new world, the Corrupter could annihilate the old world and eternally permeate, pollute, and shroud it... Yet Lumera has long perceived everything... She erupts in flames - even while being devoured by the god, she shines starlight upon you.
[player.name], is this truly your heartfelt desire? Do You so desperately wish to destroy this world? If You still harbor any regret, any hope, any mercy... then I can also grant You this final opportunity.

So that's the truth - that final sacrifice bore a sacred mission: within the Corrupter's body, using their soul and life to voice the ultimate wish. Through this hope for a new world, the Corrupter could annihilate the old world and eternally permeate, pollute, and shroud it...
Before being devoured by the Corrupter, you finally comprehend all Their schemes... So, will you simply be exploited by Them, deceived by Them, as long as this world can be destroyed?

The Corrupter devours the sacrifice you prepared. Sun, moon, and stars vanish as darkness enshrouds the earth... This world's laws were originally written with Their body. Now, foolish mortal worship and wishes grant Them true divine authority, so naturally, They shall erase the previous Creator's design. Yet you also perceive that the Creator's ink has corrupted... They no longer possess that creative ingenuity - merely a mass of unsolidified stench... They can only pollute the world, cover the old world's remains, yet absolutely cannot create a new world... If you had foreseen this outcome, would you still permit things to unfold this way? Would you possess a chance to alter everything? Or does destroying everything indeed offer you some form of release?

Just as you anticipated, the Corrupter is born. You've long harbored this secret... and prepared accordingly. This world's laws were originally written with Their body. Now, mortal worship and wishes grant Them true divine authority, so naturally, They desire to erase the previous Creator's design.
Perhaps the Corrupter speaks truth - the Creator's work, especially humanity, truly represents disgusting design... Yet everything also returns to humans. Their destructive authority now also stems from human grants. As humanity's representative in dialogue with Them, you, [player.name], possess the power to decide this world's fate... and only you can oppose Their decision.

The sky darkens as if someone pours ink into clouds. The sun fights helplessly like a dim lantern chased by giant beasts.
Black puddles manifest on the ground, swallowing livestock, panicked people, even tilting houses.
Some people suddenly sprout black spots that spread throughout their bodies - if not killed immediately, monsters emerge from melting skin...
Almost all unprotected flames extinguish, becoming disgusting phosphorescent slime that spreads like fire... While every ink-written text not stored in sealed metal boxes worldwide automatically transforms into stories praising the Creator.
You failed - everyone believes this marks the world's end... The fear in their hearts provides the Corrupter with materials to weave doomsday. Hope supporting the world's continuation vanishes...

You command everyone still willing to obey, rapidly spouting dozens of lies about this doomsday scene - just moments ago you personally summoned Them!
Under your orders, magicians scatter meaningless yet inspiring light effects in the air while officials carry your false commands to rally anyone accustomed to following superiors...
Gather around Lord [player.name]! This is the final test - warriors following [player.name] through doomsday shall gain everything they desire in the new world!
You attempt several times, yet any light that rises gets swallowed by black clouds above - just like the sun. Soon, the entire city loses direction, everything consumed uselessly in chaos...

A massive light pillar rises, even piercing black clouds to shine alongside the sun... All living things - people, horses, camels, rats, birds - desperately gather around it, followed by even more terrible dark waves.

Mutated abominations and living darkness assault your newly established fragile position. The scene grows chaotic with heavy casualties, yet having no retreat, people fight desperately...
Just as battle reaches fever pitch, tremendous cheering erupts from one direction. Many heads - mutated and normal - tumble down like an overturned fruit stand... The Sultan arrives! The human monster follows your lit beacon!
Crowds gather, yet this only provides darkness with a more abundant feast... Your defenses don't last long - whenever light rises, it attracts a hundredfold darkness...

With no time for complete defensive arrays, parts of the magical circuit use living people as conductors holding hands. Corpses, stones, carts... everything useful gets piled up. People construct not walls that truly block monsters, yet hope that can withstand overhead darkness... This ugly, unplanned, panic-stricken work stands firm amid the former Creator's destruction, mocking Their taste.

The time has come. The Highlord raises Their spear - then more starlight shoots earthward like spears.
One after another, like streetlights piercing darkness, driving away evil... A path toward the Corrupter opens.
You organize several breakout attempts, all repelled by dark abominations and tendrils... As time passes, darkness grows denser... while your beacon of hope dims and finally dies.

You carve a bloody path through darkness with blade and flame. A crimson route slowly extends toward the Corrupter - in this dark tide, it creates stunning contrast that even mesmerizes the former Creator.

Now, that rule-writing ink moves independently, executing final commands... Layer by layer, seals unlock - earthquakes, poison rain, storms, flames... All elements prepare to destroy this world.
Furious winds tear you apart... along with everything else.

[s1.name] releases all their magic, piercing merciless storms with brilliant lightning. [s1.name] vanishes, becoming formless ash in the wind, yet wind accepts [s1.gender(his,her)] courage. Doomsday is successfully delayed - as long as people still remember [s1.name]'s deeds with the wind... As long as stories about [s1.name] continue spreading on the breeze, the final blade-wind won't arrive.

With inner thunder, [s1.name] successfully pleases storm spirits. They remember human hair and banners flowing in wind, white sails playing with waves on seas, people breathing lovely sounds into wind through small tubes... For this, they're willing to pause before doomsday, awaiting humanity's miracle challenge to god.
Flames consume you... then everything else. This marks doomsday's beginning.

This proves intense negotiation. [s2.name] ignites their own body, bargaining with fire elemental princes amid flames for humanity's final time.
Finally, [s2.gender(his,her)] body becomes charcoal while their soul continues arguing... This determination successfully moves fire elements - before [s2.gender(his,her)] soul extinguishes, flames won't burn this world! Of course, [s2.gender(his,her)] agony won't lessen even slightly each second.

[s2.name] ignites their soul, making fire elements see them as family. Everyone recalls humanity's long history of feeding flames with wood, ore, flesh. They remember crackling wood sounds, sizzling meat aromas, countless colors from burning and explosions. Humans prove such interesting creatures!... For this, they're willing to pause before doomsday, awaiting humanity's miracle challenge to god.

Earth rages - you can still endure, yet true extinction comes from sky... A massive meteorite answers extinction's call, returning to earth. This represents the doomsday mechanism the god arranged for the world.

Earth hides true doomsday in the sky - [s3.name] knows this secret. So [s3.name] begs earth to transform them into stone... As long as [s3.name] still watches the sky, as long as foolish humans don't demolish it, the doomsday star won't fall.

[s3.name] prays to distant mountains. [s3.name] asks earth to remember human decorations on the land, their joy climbing peaks, generations nurtured by earth and returning to dust... What can we do with you? Humans are also earth's children... We'll give you more time! Earth Mother and Mountain Father are willing to pause before doomsday, awaiting humanity's miracle challenge to god.
Life begins in water, finally dissolving back into it... Your flesh melts first, then all living things - everything returns to corrupted chaos.

[s4.name] dances in poison rain until completely dissolved... Bloody foam scatters in rain, moving water elements... Go quickly, humans - dirty humans - before this foam completely disperses, world's end won't arrive!

[s4.name] dances, mimicking various creatures - all life needs water. Humans, galloping horses, mice, birds, fish... Finally, water elements remember their ancient memories of gifting life to earth... For this, they're willing to pause before doomsday, awaiting humanity's miracle challenge to god.

First, hatred's thorns that hunger for flesh; behind them looms a sealed door painted with countless fools' entanglements... blocked by a massive boulder - a cowardly giant clutching its head. Beyond, darkness churns like fog, awaiting your arrival...
Maggie produces golden shears from nowhere - no matter how fierce the thorns, all are severed cleanly and wither away... As effortless as tending her garden at home, you pass this first trial.

Faris studies briefly, testing with his staff, quickly grasping these living thorns' nature.
He shows you how to free entangled bodies by moving with the thorns' growth pattern, or offering them soft leather strips to play with... "Simple as handling dogs," he explains: "Never snatch from a dog's mouth - feed it gently and they'll release willingly."
When the first thorn bundle ensnares Jalila... you discover her skin gleams like diamond. Ignoring the sharp barbs, she becomes your vanguard, clearing every obstacle - what indomitable spirit!

Like hatred itself, these thorns burrow deep and spawn more thorns, eventually piercing your bodies completely. You swing blades, kindle fires, battle desperately... yet become hatred's fertile ground... The corrupted nightmare imprisons you eternally... Even as the world dies, you remain trapped in this suffering dream.

[s1.name] turns inward, stepping deliberately into the thorn maze. These barbs may wound [s1.gender(his,her)] flesh and tear [s1.gender(his,her)] garments, yet cannot halt [s1.gender(his,her)] advance... As if losing their purpose, the thorns curl weakly... opening a path through this dreamscape.

Nabhani doesn't even touch that door-blocking boulder... he wouldn't stoop to such manual labor! Simply whispering in the stone giant's ear makes it leap up excitedly, laugh three times, and bound toward the horizon... Perhaps it too has found its own tale to pursue.

Nayla sweet-talks the rock giant at length... even baring one breast, finally convincing it she burns with desire to admire its mighty form below! Naturally, once the stone giant falls for her ruse, standing and spreading its legs, Nayla strikes with her whip... Now the doorway stands clear - time for clever hands to work the lock!

Like confronting fate itself, the harder you struggle, the heavier and more immovable that rock giant becomes... The corrupted nightmare imprisons you eternally... Even as the world dies, you remain trapped in this suffering dream.

Brute force cannot budge this boulder... yet this certainly isn't [s2.name]'s first triumph over failure! Each time [s2.name] rallies, reconsidering how to apply force, the stone giant shrinks slightly.
Eventually, it poses no obstacle at all, though [s2.name] carries it along as a traveling companion.

Before you stands a mirror-door bearing countless uneven, spinning wheels that reflect one's entire existence... its mystery as unfathomable as life itself... Who truly understands their own journey?
Shama hesitates momentarily, then suddenly produces a large key from her crotch, fitting it perfectly to unlock this portal... Unfortunately, though she tries to leave the key behind, a chain yanks it back into her trousers.
