In this filth-choked, tangled nest, you share your followers' eyes. They slaughter each other in darkness and chaos, bleeding, dying in the muck alongside enemies as foul and frenzied as themselves.
Someone lights the first fire. Soon, flames drag more insects into the fight, believer and non-believer alike. This magnificent vista of a city in flames, this solemn symphony woven from countless screams and cries, at last shapes the scattered fragments into a vision even a god can savor. Mortals, you have pleased your god with everything you are!
In this ecstasy, your divine power surges. All corpses, faithful and faithless, start to call your name in the flames, declaring your sovereignty over this pile of ruin.

In this filth-choked, tangled nest, you share your followers' eyes. They slaughter each other in darkness and chaos, bleeding, dying in the muck alongside enemies as foul and frenzied as themselves.
Someone lights the first fire. Soon, flames drag more insects into the fight, believer and non-believer alike. This magnificent vista of a city in flames, this solemn symphony woven from countless screams and cries, at last shapes the scattered fragments into a vision even a god can savor.
Yet a strange weariness rises within you. Casually, you turn your gaze elsewhere. Below, blackened corpses cry your name, all in vain.
Have your insects dwindled? Or have you spared them out of a lingering sense of humanity? Nevertheless, you will settle everything with your divine might.

Your faithful clash with non-believers, but your attention drifts from the bloody field. You notice them now: the silent insects hidden in this nest. They lurk in countless cracks and burrows, lurking, watching... Their minds are grey, untouched by a single ripple.
Only now do you see how many there are: no faith, no loyalty, mere background and footnotes, alive only to fill the world with their flesh. You win. The grey swarm does not stir. They simply let your faithful pass through.
For the first time as a god, you feel disgust for the world, and the ache of failure.

Your faithful clash with non-believers, but your attention drifts from the bloody field. You notice them now: the silent insects hidden in this nest. They lurk in countless cracks and burrows, lurking, watching... Their minds are grey, untouched by a single ripple.
Only now do you see how many there are: no faith, no loyalty, mere background and footnotes, alive only to fill the world with their flesh. After the bitter victory, the bodies of your faithful merge into the gray swarm, without stirring a single ripple.
For the first time as a god, you feel disgust for the world, and the ache of failure.

Your faithful clash with non-believers, but your attention drifts from the bloody field. You notice them now: the silent insects hidden in this nest. They lurk in countless cracks and burrows, lurking, watching... Their minds are grey, untouched by a single ripple.
Only now do you see how many there are: no faith, no loyalty, mere background and footnotes, alive only to fill the world with their flesh. The battle ends. The bodies of your faithful merge into the gray swarm, without stirring a single ripple. As if mocking your defeat.
For the first time as a god, you feel disgust for the world, and the ache of failure.

In those nests, you can see certain insects of unusual size, commanders of many, yet they never join the war. They simply watch your swarm slaughter and be slaughtered. Then open their gates to the victor. You see it. You know it. Their souls shift color even faster than the banners over their mounds.
Still, you accept this cheap faith.

In those nests, you can see certain insects of unusual size, commanders of many, yet they never join the war. They simply watch your swarm slaughter and be slaughtered, until your divine power crashes directly into their minds. You see it. You know it. Their souls shift color even faster than the banners over their mounds.
Still, you accept this cheap faith.

In those nests, you can see certain insects of unusual size, commanders of many, yet they never join the war. They simply watch your swarm slaughter and be slaughtered. One moment, they wear the color of non-believers. The next, their souls gleam with loyalty. In the end, as your forces fade, so too does that fawning hue. But really, is this worth despairing over?

When your faithful seize this nest, you finally draw close, close enough to savor this delicate trophy.
The sky over the capital darkens. They cannot see, but they feel it: something vast, blotting out sun and sky, pressing down upon the city. The earth trembles. No living thing dares remain outdoors. They cower behind walls, shaking. Sometimes, they sense a great eye at the window, peering into their very souls. That is your curious gaze. Sometimes, a person or a beast bursts into flame, or twists into a writhing monster. And that is your mischievous touch.

Your insects fail. They could not take this nest. No matter, you meant to pry it open anyway. This is just... a bit rougher.
Amid the capital's screams, heavenly fire splits the sky. Then comes the rain of flame, descending like restless ghosts. The strange blaze devours the Sultan's army, as if in vengeance. Then, as if at play, it suddenly plunges into some noble's mansion.
Witnessing this divine power, your faithful regather. Your army rises again. Following the flames' guidance, they begin to climb the palace mountain.

Your insects fail. They could not take this nest. No matter, you meant to pry it open anyway. This is just... a bit rougher.
Amid the capital's terrified screams, all the fallen gather together, twisting into a surging tide of flesh, wrapped in blades and armor. Like a flood, you race through the streets in this makeshift body, tasting the shape of the city. Driven by the horrified screams and the roar, your surviving faithful press onward, toward the highest point, with you.

Your insects fail. They could not take this nest. No matter, you meant to pry it open anyway. This is just... a bit rougher.
Amid the capital's screams, a giant hand descends from the sky, translucent and glowing, vast as a castle. With this manifestation of your will, you rummage through the city, tossing houses and armies aside.
At last, you glimpse the city's highest point, the palace still beyond your reach. But your hand points. As the giant hand points the way, your faithful surge forth once more, renewed, beginning their merciless advance.

With all accomplished, the time has come to return to the realm of the divine to reign over this land! However, before that, you need to use the remnants of your humanity to cast this great emperor down to the mortal world...

Clutching the Sultan's shattered face, [player.name] venomous words into his ear. "Taste the suffering you once inflicted upon me! Endure what you forced me to witness!"
Despite the torment inflicted by the venomous tendrils and thorns, all the Sultan feels is a fractured soul steeped in emptiness, Amid wounds scarred by innumerable agonies, what fresh torment could you impose? Out of disappointment, surprise, or perhaps mercy, you violently retract the tendrils, casting his corpse—almost as a mockery of your own fate—down to the mortal world...

Whether out of sarcasm or genuine benevolence, [player.name] offers the Sultan a sip of the purest, sweetest nectar—a treasure long forsaken and forgotten by the tyrant in the mortal realm. As this elixir trickles down his throat, his soul would begin to heal, recalling those blissful moments and finding eternal solace beneath the tree's shade.
However, the Sultan rejects your mercy, spitting back the nectar along with his blood and life at your face. With a derisive laugh, falling into the mortal realm as a soulless husk.

[player.name] instills the essence of darkness into the tyrant's soul before casting his hollow vessel down to the mortal world. In time, a new demon is destined to rise... Even though you have obliterated his empire from history, his terror and sins will endure in myths and legends...

[player.name] strives to eradicate all traces of this tyrant, driven by desires for vengeance and precaution.
Alas, as the purifying flames ignite, the Sultan erupts into maniacal laughter, propelling himself into the mortal realm with his final breath... His lifeless body and his malevolent lore will linger as a blemish upon the world for generations to come.

Proficient in the ways of power in the mortal realm, [player.name] effortlessly traces the Sultan's lineage, exterminating his bloodline, ensuring that his scions will never ascend to rule. With a burst of laughter, the Sultan accepts his fate, falling to the mortal realm without regret—letting his own remains mark the end of his dynasty.

[player.name] offers the Sultan's soul to the stars, convinced that the tyrant, who once massacred numerous followers of the Star-Souled, will endure eternal torments!
Unexpectedly, the stars accept the Sultan, compelling him to witness perpetually your domination over the world, the dawn of a new era under [player.name]... "Those stupid stars," you ponder, casting the Sultan's hollow husk back to the mortal realm...

Harnessing the purest ideals crystallized within humanity, [player.name] wields the authority once held by the late Sultan to shake the very foundation of authority itself.
Henceforth, the blind obedience, the overwhelming fear—those ingrained curses of humanity are permanently weakened, if only slightly. Perhaps the words of the sage may enlighten a few more among the myriad lost souls, and a handful more may dare to rise against injustice...
Upon witnessing this seemingly futile endeavor, the Sultan erupts into laughter as his life ebbs away. Even as his lifeless form falls back to the mortal realm, a hint of smile remains frozen on his face.

In an anticipated one-sided battle, the Sultan, against all odds, repeatedly prevails over your warriors and beasts, his guards sacrificing themselves to shield him from your devastating spells... until only ashes and flesh fragments lie beside him.
"What? Running out of your tricks, [player.name]?" He jeers, calling out to you. Although he is keenly aware of his inevitable end, he remains determined to show you that no mortal means can subdue him!

Eventually, the emotion called "fury" floods back to you, as if you were once more a humble courtier facing a tyrant... With power beyond reality, you obliterate this vermin and shatter his throne. This arbitrary and brutal act marks the initial sin you have committed as a deity...

You appointed Alim as the court's master spy—his pickpockets will steal things far more valuable than gold coins... and he accepted this commission with a complex expression.
You bestowed a new title upon Adila [Dragon Slayer], a title more honorable than Lion Hunter, belonging to warriors. In the future, countless warriors might embark on adventures for this title...
You conferred a noble title to Arumina right there—much more noble than her father's. Her surprised expression was utterly charming.
You granted Murad Tus a new surname and title, now also called 'Zephyr,' but this time 'Lord' can be added to it—this name was not bought by a father-in-law.
Amur was made the Royal Judge by you, now even nobles must submit to his arbitration.
You granted Junah noble status, along with twelve servants, an estate, and tax privileges in textiles, encouraging courtly women to practice the act of saluting a former commoner in secret.
You instructed Jawad to oversee the capital's commerce—ideally gathering enough funds for the new government swiftly.
Previously, the Sultan always controlled the nation's troops, but now Jabal has been given this honorable mission by you—his family is overjoyed and has become powerful supporters of yours.
You have ordered Zaki, as the Court Honor Guard commander, to restore order in the capital—both nobles and commoners need to fear his rod and chains.
You bid Iman kneel, patting his shoulder and head as a priest blesses the humble – then you grant him alone the right to raise a new temple.
You command Emane to build a school, spreading Rationality—and your command to all commoners.
You ennoble Inal—she will become one of the court administrators in the future.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys – they must be impatient to know what happened here. 
She embraced this opportunity with enthusiasm.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys – they must be impatient to know what happened here. 
For this purpose, you bestowed upon her an ancient, tongue-twisting noble surname - to which she raised no objection, as long as it wasn't her original one - along with several trunks filled with exquisite garments, both men's and women's attire.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys—they must be impatient to know what happened here.
Wait, come back, put on a few more clothes, men's or women's clothes are fine.
In short, you declare that the Dancer has regained a noble status, becoming a member of a great family again—your family.

You tell [xiaochou.name] that this realm is vast beyond measure, and all you know is but a speck near the capital. You hand it secret documents and proofs, along with a new charge: to roam, to uncover all that lies upon this land! And to tell you of it through mirrors and verse. [xiaochou.name] finds this most intriguing.

You command [xiaochou.name] to take up the mantle of the new headsman—henceforth, it shall be [xiaochou.name] who severs every noble head. And in that fleeting moment, it may glimpse the tales of the condemned—etched in the glint of the blade, mirrored in the spill of blood... and share them with you in the hushed hours of the night.

You command [xiaochou.name] to join the scholars of human in devising intricate experiments—of magic, of light, of gods and realms beyond. No matter the cost, the essence of the world's workings must be uncovered. It will sate [xiaochou.name]'s every curiosity and grant you power unending, perhaps.

You command [xiaochou.name] to raise a city in the desert—one meant solely for those who are unhuman. In time, spirits and fiends alike shall kneel as your subjects... though most dismiss it as the fevered dream of a mad ruler.
You gift the closest and most fertile grassland to the capital to Aziz, and the grasslands originally belonging to his Father are also returned to him... He is now a nomadic prince again.
You grant her a license to operate a brothel—tax-free for ten years. Salwiyah cries with joy and desperately kisses your toes.
You declare that all of Zazie's Property and status within the Sultan's court are protected by you—that's enough; she already has too much.
You allow Seliman to continue managing the court guards – his expression is extremely complex.
You tell Samir that he can leave the court with a wealth and assure him there will be no assassination. He seems a bit disbelieving about the latter part...
You declare that you will protect Sadani's wealth and safety—including the child she carries within her. As these words leave your lips, a cascade of whispers ripples through the court.
You gift the three hills near the capital to Riel, which are now the habitat of her people, and she can now go to the slave market and break the chains of all the slaves on the spot.
You command Jenna to manage all the artisans in the capital and all the licenses for processing precious metals. This privilege is enough to reward any loyal friend...
Nawfal certainly doesn't want any privilege or reward... So you announce a pardon in advance for anything Nawfal says in this hall in the future—no matter who she curses, no matter how harsh.
You command Nabhani to set up a swordsman academy in the capital, of course, he evades countless times, so you easily title him as Sword Saint, now he's satisfied.
You quietly tell Nayla that soon you'll be making love to her, not just once... Nothing could please her more than this promise.

Maggie... for everything she's done, it's almost impossible to repay her with material things, so you reward her family and announce a three-year tax exemption for the residents of the capital in her name.
You give Manar enough investment and privilege, ordering her to explore unknown territories – and this time, you're bringing peace.
You announce the establishment of the Miracle Society, a research organization led by Mahir—this time she will have practically infinite budget and resources.
No matter what, you think the new era needs new attire and flags—the creation and design of these will be entrusted to Malkina.
You give the Royal Library to Lumera, she can barely hold back her desire to go take a look immediately.
You announce the true identity of the Nameless Swordsman to everyone, and restore all his privileges as a member of the royal family—to which he merely shrugged.
The Chamberlain grovels before you, expressing loyalty with lavish words—you merely offer him some comfort: from now on, fewer people will die in the court.
You appoint Raed as Tribune—restoring the position... more people will join her in the future.
You restore Arumina's status—the title and Property her Father lost are now back in her hands, but she still seems unable to feel happy.
You give him an official court position: to manage a team of couriers, ensuring that information and orders are transmitted quickly and accurately in the chaotic capital.
The former thief... now people call him the High Constable—you tell him to catch whomever you want.
You command Jalila to quickly go to the Sultan's Harem—to rein in the chaotic concubines, servants, and looting pickpockets. From now on, she is your chief steward of the court.

You declare the King of Flames to be a national saint. Every year on this day is the flame festival, people will wear the King of Flames' attire and parade in the streets, celebrating the tyrant's demise... All handicrafts must be sold with national authorization.
Few decisions you genuinely feel sorry to the ancestors for—but as long as Hassan is happy: now you can call him a court poet.
You gift Habunah a royal spinning factory and command her to pass on her craft, making it a national specialty.
Habib is now a cour de chef, and you assure him that no matter who becomes the Sultan later, his troublemaking root won't be cut off~
After Gullis gained the status of a Free Person, nothing changed; it seems he believes he has not repaid the debt of gratitude he owes you...
You grant Qais a lot of wealth and a mansion, and land... He is so stunned by such splendor and wealth—this is exactly why you came to watch.
You give Fatuna the privilege to procure supplies for the court, a job that is both wealthy and prestigious, soon people will forget that she was a widow.

You don't reward Faris directly. Instead, you tell him that since there is already a Lady Cat in the court, it's only fitting for a dog to hold a noble title as well. He can handle the details himself, but overall, it's a title that will echo through the ages

You've never seen Faris smile so brightly.
You announce that Faraj has become the new court scribe—from today on, what he writes will become history.
You prepare a generous gift for Fardak—and promise to send him back to his hometown: to tell everyone afar that the Sultan's Rule is over!
You announce that Fadia is no longer a Slave, she will become a free person and receive enough reward—then you secretly tell her to be ready to become your spy.
You permit Buthayna to write [Location where the Sultan fought] and [Location where [player.name] fought] anywhere in her shop, in golden letters.
You request craftsmen to erect a statue for Lady Becky, build a temple—telling people about the great achievements they can obtain once blessed by the cat.
You announce that Badriyyah's church no longer needs covert dissemination, this ancient belief is now legal—and her laughter makes everyone genuinely doubt whether that might be a good idea...

You order the construction of an academy, specifically to collect and study the nations and cultures destroyed by the Sultan, and gather their former survivors. Perhaps one day, we could gain something valuable from this lost Rationality.
You restore Ansuya's royal status and treatment—furnishing her with enough wealth and slaves: from now on she can do whatever she wishes to.
You command Asal to organize through a century of royal archives – perhaps the few tomes he hasn't yet cracked open. You hope he crafts a history for the ages, ensuring the Sultan's tale lives on.

You retire Adil and grant him land far from the capital, preventing those he once hunted from coming for revenge. Stubborn and headstrong, Adil knows only very few catchers have such good fortune, and accepts everything respectfully.
You told Anita that you had always admired her gift for medicine, and that you would fund her continued study, practice, and research—until she became a truly exceptional physician.
Perhaps by some foxy instinct, when your men stormed Abdul's manor to seize him for execution, the former Vizier had already vanished into the night with his kin... the halls left hollow.
You strip Adila of the privilege of swordplay and confine her to her home until she bears a son. Adila would rather die.
You distribute images of Alim and anti-theft manuals to every commoner, and he seems to see this as a new challenge.

You publicly announce that in the coming months, even half a year, you need Zephyr to deliver the news of the Sultan's death throughout the empire and announce the name of the new king. After he agrees, there is another heavy, tearful bite mark on his arm.

You arrange for Arumina the strictest court etiquette teacher, one on whom no amount of wheedling or tantrum will work, and assure everyone she will transform into the most polite lady in the capital.

You deprive Zephyr of his surname and tell him that a real Man must earn his name himself, not rely on his father-in-law's handouts. He seemed optimistic and held Arumina's little hand tightly, making many promises.
You list Amur's every crime and smile genuinely as you ruthlessly behead him.

You publicly hold Junah's soft hands and announce your love for her, as her eyes sparkled with tears of emotion, only to laugh and say it was just a joke. The next day, you receive news of her death and the mockery toward this lowly woman, who could not bear a simple jest.

You tell Jawad, that you have always known about when he dispatched an Assassin against you for a few Gold Coins. Now, you want to play a game with him—your Assassin will set out within seven days.
He's almost on his knees in fright, sobbing, offering his entire estate for his life... hehe, this is exactly the result you wanted. You smile while confiscating his home in front of him.

You strip Jabal of his Honor Guard and General title, reclaiming control over all the Troop under his command.
When he hands over the token to you, he even smiles: "Great, now I can finally go off on an adventure free"

You announce that Zaki is no longer your student, the boy's eyes immediately redden. He looks at you in disbelief, trembling, saying after a long time, he will strive... strive to earn back the qualification to learn from you.
You command him to receive the Queen of the Whip's whip for seven consecutive days, then display those beautiful scars to all the guests in the House of Delights.
You deprive this proud old lady of her title. From now on, no one will have the patience to listen to anything she says anymore.

Given all the trouble Inal stirs up for you, you gift her a vial of poison. She drinks it in tears, and nothing happens – until the next day, when her first bite reveals she tastes nothing, no matter what she eats.
You give Shama an exceptionally sharp dagger, she smiles slightly, and without hesitation makes a choice.
You deny her bloodline and expel her from your home. Anyway, now she's of no use to you.
You no longer have anything important for Aziz to do. You order Aziz to polish ten stone lunch boxes a day and hand them to you, no work, no sleep.

You loudly praise Salwiyah's beautiful eyes, and when she shyly approaches you, you order to have them gouged out, then personally inlaid costly amethyst into her bleeding eye sockets as compensation.

You order Zazie to remove all her gold ornaments, silk, and satin, then send her off on a sealed godly palanquin. Your people will carry her to the highland snow mountains and offer her to her worshiped deity.

Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Seliman has long anticipated this moment, kneeling on the ground, eyes lowered, restraining himself, without looking at anyone.
You order the Court Physician to bring out a bowl of poison that will kill a person within an hour, then pour it into his mouth. He struggles painfully but ultimately couldn't detoxify himself.
The concubine Sadani takes the dagger you grant her, her pale face showing unexpected calm – her final plea is to glimpse the Sultan one last time.

When you intended to kill an Ally who once fought alongside you, this Beast escaped the city with astonishing intuition. It's imaginable she'll wander around this land, lurking in the shadows, waiting for you to show a flaw, looking forward to the day she can eat the traitor's liver.

You give Jenna a bag of gold, urging her to leave the capital. It is foreseeable that the storm will not calm with the Sultan's death, but become increasingly tumultuous, with endless biting and fighting, until this country welcomes a new Sultan recognized by the majority.
When you pronounce his death sentence, Nawfal says nothing, merely accepting everything calmly, accepting that you will be another Sultan.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. No matter what grievances you once had with Nabhani, everything ends here.
You use Nabhani's head to prove to the world that you are more ruthless and suspicious than the Sultan.
You have him placed under house arrest, soon he died of illness.
Just this once, you cruelly tell her, she has no right to refuse.

In this world, only the dead will always keep secrets, only the dead will never change their original intentions.
Seliman takes the dagger, smiles slightly, neither hatred nor regret.

The cruel game has ended, but the harm towards each other is forever etched in your hearts.
Upon divorce, you gave her a lot of money, but when leaving, besides her dowry, she didn't take a single extra dime. You tell her, if in the next life, don't become your wife. She just purses her lips and smiles, not agreeing with you.
You decide to imprison Manar, forbidding her from further drafting more detailed maps, in case of leaking secrets to your enemies. Soon, her guards send you the news of her demise.

You let her personally try the Confused Learning Machine she created herself. After about five tries, she will just lie in the yard basking in the sun. Perhaps the sun can give her some inspiration? Who knows.

Malkina has never heard of such an absurd reason for execution, and because of this absurdity, she realizes that your decision is irrevocable. Soon after, you hear that her mother burns down the tailor shop in remorse, but unfortunately, there is no remedy for regret in the world.

You not only burned Lumera's books but also ordered that commoners are not allowed to read or learn, because this girl made you realize how terrifying this force was. You used it to overthrow the Sultan, and one day, someone will use it to overthrow you.
Ironically, until Lumera jumped into the burning study, desperately trying to save them, and was eventually swallowed by the flames, she did not use her power to resist your decision.
You did not believe that he had no ambition for the throne that was within his reach, so you executed him, completely burying those departed names in the blood and dust of history.
You killed Lazag for the same reason that those who usurped the throne before you killed the chamberlain of the previous dynasty.
As long as she dies, those promises you made to bend her to your will need no honoring – what a joke, a mere vagrant daring to barter with you?

At the victory banquet, you ordered her to pour wine for all the nobles and noblewomen who recognized her. Tears welled up in her eyes, but she gritted her teeth and endured it.
It's okay; life will slowly teach her that the more she endures, the more torment there is.
You handed a large box of documents to Zephyr, ordering him to deliver them to every station in the empire. He won't be back for three to five years.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Jemor without hesitation.

You publicly announced a long list of Jalila's 'Fat Sheep', sweeping your fierce gaze over those men who desperately ducked their heads like ostriches. Of course, they wouldn't dare retaliate against you, but they certainly wouldn't spare the woman who leaked this secret, nor would they trust a safe house riddled with cracks.

You held up the cloak of the King of Flames high and then threw it into the fire. The sparks and ashes stained the desperate faces of the onlookers and children. You scorn those trembling people. Did you see? The redemption they longed for is nothing but a useless joke.
Without waiting for you to drive him away, he left you a farewell note with wet edges, not sure if it was just pulled out from a lamb stew.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Hamar without hesitation.
You executed Habunah because you dreamed of the blue waves no longer lifting you but drowning you on that night.
You executed Habib, without giving anyone any reason.
So, you didn't dare to bet on whether he would point the fearsome bow and arrow at you. You executed him.

Qais once defied you and even pointed at your nose and scolded you... These things you had almost forgotten suddenly emerged from the corners of your memory, leaving you tossing and turning, with a lump in your throat.
Forget it, let him die.
Fatuna confessed to her crimes without objection, and the simple truth of the world is that murder must be atoned for by death.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Besides, shouldn't a loyal person accompany his beloved master underground?
Loyalty is meaningless. A dog that betrays its master once will do it again. You don’t trust him, so you execute him.

You drive him out of the capital and tell him the truth: the Sultan's realm would take twenty years to cross by camel, the continent beneath would require one hundred and fifty years, and beyond the sea, there is another one hundred and fifty years, and another after that... The world is so vast, he should not waste his life merely staring at you.

He has no choice but to swear to you with tears in his eyes that he will record everything during his journey and send it to you.

By your order, Fardak is stripped of his surname and inheritance rights, but still keep him under house arrest in the most expensive mansion in the city. Now he should know that you and the Sultan are cut from the same cloth.

In despair, he draws Kaplan's End, the blade he couldn't decide to use before, ending his own life.
You expelled her from your court, knowing well what harsh fate awaited a defenseless former Sultan's Slave.

You had your eye on that tender piece of Property from the House of Delights for a long time! And Buthayna had the good sense to offer the majority of profits to you, and from now on, free of charge.
Only then did you give a satisfied nod.

Lady Becky is a clever little cat. He knows who is good and who is bad to him. When you wanted to order him caught and spanked, he had long disappeared to someplace unknown. Perhaps it's somewhere nobody knows him as Lady Becky. People might call him Little White, Pearl, or Rice, but it doesn't matter to him.

You bound her with a chain imbued with magic to the stake, announcing to all the disaster brought by the Other she worshipped. She laughed insanely. The fire burned for three days and nights before it was extinguished, but her laughter seemed to linger above the execution ground for a month.

The Sultan is dead, what reason does Bharat have to linger in your city? You threw him out and confiscated all his merchandise as revenge compensation. It must be said, some of the items inside were quite useful... Hmm, why not take them out sooner?
You give Ansuya travel expenses. Her homeland has turned into scorched earth, but you believe she still wants to go back for a look.
Just those few books, who could possibly read enough? You order Asal to immediately collect books from all over the world for you, and not to return until he has gathered at least a hundred.

Until the seas run dry, until every mirror in the world is shattered... pledge your loyalty forever to the humans you despise and scorn!
Facing your greedy visage, [xiaochou.name] laughs aloud—the words you speak as a sovereign lend this pact such potent magic! [xiaochou.name] kneels to kiss your hand, like the humblest of servants—"Very well, my master. With this decree, humans shall never be free of the Mirror!"
So long as charges are fabricated, no one in this world remains innocent. Your men quickly uncover solid evidence to accuse him, and, in accordance with law and reason, they put him to death.
You killed the girl—simply because you needed to kill one of the exiles from the fallen kingdom, to prove that you had not forgotten the traditions of this land.
The tumultuous day finally comes to an end. May everyone find peaceful sleep tonight.

The former thief... now people call him the High Constable—you tell him to catch whomever you want.
You command Jalila to quickly go to the Sultan's Harem—to rein in the chaotic concubines, servants, and looting pickpockets. From now on, she is your chief steward of the court.

You declare the King of Flames to be a national saint. Every year on this day is the flame festival, people will wear the King of Flames' attire and parade in the streets, celebrating the tyrant's demise... All handicrafts must be sold with national authorization.
Few decisions you genuinely feel sorry to the ancestors for—but as long as Hassan is happy: now you can call him a court poet.
You gift Habunah a royal spinning factory and command her to pass on her craft, making it a national specialty.
Habib is now a cour de chef, and you assure him that no matter who becomes the Sultan later, his troublemaking root won't be cut off~
After Gullis gained the status of a Free Person, nothing changed; it seems he believes he has not repaid the debt of gratitude he owes you...
You grant Qais a lot of wealth and a mansion, and land... He is so stunned by such splendor and wealth—this is exactly why you came to watch.
You give Fatuna the privilege to procure supplies for the court, a job that is both wealthy and prestigious, soon people will forget that she was a widow.

You don't reward Faris directly. Instead, you tell him that since there is already a Lady Cat in the court, it's only fitting for a dog to hold a noble title as well. He can handle the details himself, but overall, it's a title that will echo through the ages

You've never seen Faris smile so brightly.
You announce that Faraj has become the new court scribe—from today on, what he writes will become history.
You prepare a generous gift for Fardak—and promise to send him back to his hometown: to tell everyone afar that the Sultan's Rule is over!
You announce that Fadia is no longer a Slave, she will become a free person and receive enough reward—then you secretly tell her to be ready to become your spy.
You permit Buthayna to write [Location where the Sultan fought] and [Location where [player.name] fought] anywhere in her shop, in golden letters.
You request craftsmen to erect a statue for Lady Becky, build a temple—telling people about the great achievements they can obtain once blessed by the cat.
You announce that Badriyyah's church no longer needs covert dissemination, this ancient belief is now legal—and her laughter makes everyone genuinely doubt whether that might be a good idea...

You order the construction of an academy, specifically to collect and study the nations and cultures destroyed by the Sultan, and gather their former survivors. Perhaps one day, we could gain something valuable from this lost Rationality.
You restore Ansuya's royal status and treatment—furnishing her with enough wealth and slaves: from now on she can do whatever she wishes to.
You command Asal to organize through a century of royal archives – perhaps the few tomes he hasn't yet cracked open. You hope he crafts a history for the ages, ensuring the Sultan's tale lives on.

You retire Adil and grant him land far from the capital, preventing those he once hunted from coming for revenge. Stubborn and headstrong, Adil knows only very few catchers have such good fortune, and accepts everything respectfully.
You told Anita that you had always admired her gift for medicine, and that you would fund her continued study, practice, and research—until she became a truly exceptional physician.
Perhaps by some foxy instinct, when your men stormed Abdul's manor to seize him for execution, the former Vizier had already vanished into the night with his kin... the halls left hollow.
You strip Adila of the privilege of swordplay and confine her to her home until she bears a son. Adila would rather die.
You distribute images of Alim and anti-theft manuals to every commoner, and he seems to see this as a new challenge.

You publicly announce that in the coming months, even half a year, you need Zephyr to deliver the news of the Sultan's death throughout the empire and announce the name of the new king. After he agrees, there is another heavy, tearful bite mark on his arm.

You arrange for Arumina the strictest court etiquette teacher, one on whom no amount of wheedling or tantrum will work, and assure everyone she will transform into the most polite lady in the capital.

You deprive Zephyr of his surname and tell him that a real Man must earn his name himself, not rely on his father-in-law's handouts. He seemed optimistic and held Arumina's little hand tightly, making many promises.
You list Amur's every crime and smile genuinely as you ruthlessly behead him.

You publicly hold Junah's soft hands and announce your love for her, as her eyes sparkled with tears of emotion, only to laugh and say it was just a joke. The next day, you receive news of her death and the mockery toward this lowly woman, who could not bear a simple jest.

You tell Jawad, that you have always known about when he dispatched an Assassin against you for a few Gold Coins. Now, you want to play a game with him—your Assassin will set out within seven days.
He's almost on his knees in fright, sobbing, offering his entire estate for his life... hehe, this is exactly the result you wanted. You smile while confiscating his home in front of him.

You strip Jabal of his Honor Guard and General title, reclaiming control over all the Troop under his command.
When he hands over the token to you, he even smiles: "Great, now I can finally go off on an adventure free"

You announce that Zaki is no longer your student, the boy's eyes immediately redden. He looks at you in disbelief, trembling, saying after a long time, he will strive... strive to earn back the qualification to learn from you.
You command him to receive the Queen of the Whip's whip for seven consecutive days, then display those beautiful scars to all the guests in the House of Delights.
You deprive this proud old lady of her title. From now on, no one will have the patience to listen to anything she says anymore.

Given all the trouble Inal stirs up for you, you gift her a vial of poison. She drinks it in tears, and nothing happens – until the next day, when her first bite reveals she tastes nothing, no matter what she eats.
You give Shama an exceptionally sharp dagger, she smiles slightly, and without hesitation makes a choice.
You deny her bloodline and expel her from your home. Anyway, now she's of no use to you.
You no longer have anything important for Aziz to do. You order Aziz to polish ten stone lunch boxes a day and hand them to you, no work, no sleep.

You loudly praise Salwiyah's beautiful eyes, and when she shyly approaches you, you order to have them gouged out, then personally inlaid costly amethyst into her bleeding eye sockets as compensation.

You order Zazie to remove all her gold ornaments, silk, and satin, then send her off on a sealed godly palanquin. Your people will carry her to the highland snow mountains and offer her to her worshiped deity.

Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Seliman has long anticipated this moment, kneeling on the ground, eyes lowered, restraining himself, without looking at anyone.
You order the Court Physician to bring out a bowl of poison that will kill a person within an hour, then pour it into his mouth. He struggles painfully but ultimately couldn't detoxify himself.
The concubine Sadani takes the dagger you grant her, her pale face showing unexpected calm – her final plea is to glimpse the Sultan one last time.

When you intended to kill an Ally who once fought alongside you, this Beast escaped the city with astonishing intuition. It's imaginable she'll wander around this land, lurking in the shadows, waiting for you to show a flaw, looking forward to the day she can eat the traitor's liver.

You give Jenna a bag of gold, urging her to leave the capital. It is foreseeable that the storm will not calm with the Sultan's death, but become increasingly tumultuous, with endless biting and fighting, until this country welcomes a new Sultan recognized by the majority.
When you pronounce his death sentence, Nawfal says nothing, merely accepting everything calmly, accepting that you will be another Sultan.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. No matter what grievances you once had with Nabhani, everything ends here.
You use Nabhani's head to prove to the world that you are more ruthless and suspicious than the Sultan.
You have him placed under house arrest, soon he died of illness.
Just this once, you cruelly tell her, she has no right to refuse.

In this world, only the dead will always keep secrets, only the dead will never change their original intentions.
Seliman takes the dagger, smiles slightly, neither hatred nor regret.

The cruel game has ended, but the harm towards each other is forever etched in your hearts.
Upon divorce, you gave her a lot of money, but when leaving, besides her dowry, she didn't take a single extra dime. You tell her, if in the next life, don't become your wife. She just purses her lips and smiles, not agreeing with you.
You decide to imprison Manar, forbidding her from further drafting more detailed maps, in case of leaking secrets to your enemies. Soon, her guards send you the news of her demise.

You let her personally try the Confused Learning Machine she created herself. After about five tries, she will just lie in the yard basking in the sun. Perhaps the sun can give her some inspiration? Who knows.

Malkina has never heard of such an absurd reason for execution, and because of this absurdity, she realizes that your decision is irrevocable. Soon after, you hear that her mother burns down the tailor shop in remorse, but unfortunately, there is no remedy for regret in the world.

You not only burned Lumera's books but also ordered that commoners are not allowed to read or learn, because this girl made you realize how terrifying this force was. You used it to overthrow the Sultan, and one day, someone will use it to overthrow you.
Ironically, until Lumera jumped into the burning study, desperately trying to save them, and was eventually swallowed by the flames, she did not use her power to resist your decision.
You did not believe that he had no ambition for the throne that was within his reach, so you executed him, completely burying those departed names in the blood and dust of history.
You killed Lazag for the same reason that those who usurped the throne before you killed the chamberlain of the previous dynasty.
As long as she dies, those promises you made to bend her to your will need no honoring – what a joke, a mere vagrant daring to barter with you?

At the victory banquet, you ordered her to pour wine for all the nobles and noblewomen who recognized her. Tears welled up in her eyes, but she gritted her teeth and endured it.
It's okay; life will slowly teach her that the more she endures, the more torment there is.
You handed a large box of documents to Zephyr, ordering him to deliver them to every station in the empire. He won't be back for three to five years.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Jemor without hesitation.

You publicly announced a long list of Jalila's 'Fat Sheep', sweeping your fierce gaze over those men who desperately ducked their heads like ostriches. Of course, they wouldn't dare retaliate against you, but they certainly wouldn't spare the woman who leaked this secret, nor would they trust a safe house riddled with cracks.

You held up the cloak of the King of Flames high and then threw it into the fire. The sparks and ashes stained the desperate faces of the onlookers and children. You scorn those trembling people. Did you see? The redemption they longed for is nothing but a useless joke.
Without waiting for you to drive him away, he left you a farewell note with wet edges, not sure if it was just pulled out from a lamb stew.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Hamar without hesitation.
You executed Habunah because you dreamed of the blue waves no longer lifting you but drowning you on that night.
You executed Habib, without giving anyone any reason.
So, you didn't dare to bet on whether he would point the fearsome bow and arrow at you. You executed him.

Qais once defied you and even pointed at your nose and scolded you... These things you had almost forgotten suddenly emerged from the corners of your memory, leaving you tossing and turning, with a lump in your throat.
Forget it, let him die.
Fatuna confessed to her crimes without objection, and the simple truth of the world is that murder must be atoned for by death.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Besides, shouldn't a loyal person accompany his beloved master underground?
Loyalty is meaningless. A dog that betrays its master once will do it again. You don’t trust him, so you execute him.

You drive him out of the capital and tell him the truth: the Sultan's realm would take twenty years to cross by camel, the continent beneath would require one hundred and fifty years, and beyond the sea, there is another one hundred and fifty years, and another after that... The world is so vast, he should not waste his life merely staring at you.

He has no choice but to swear to you with tears in his eyes that he will record everything during his journey and send it to you.

By your order, Fardak is stripped of his surname and inheritance rights, but still keep him under house arrest in the most expensive mansion in the city. Now he should know that you and the Sultan are cut from the same cloth.

In despair, he draws Kaplan's End, the blade he couldn't decide to use before, ending his own life.
You expelled her from your court, knowing well what harsh fate awaited a defenseless former Sultan's Slave.

You had your eye on that tender piece of Property from the House of Delights for a long time! And Buthayna had the good sense to offer the majority of profits to you, and from now on, free of charge.
Only then did you give a satisfied nod.

Lady Becky is a clever little cat. He knows who is good and who is bad to him. When you wanted to order him caught and spanked, he had long disappeared to someplace unknown. Perhaps it's somewhere nobody knows him as Lady Becky. People might call him Little White, Pearl, or Rice, but it doesn't matter to him.

You bound her with a chain imbued with magic to the stake, announcing to all the disaster brought by the Other she worshipped. She laughed insanely. The fire burned for three days and nights before it was extinguished, but her laughter seemed to linger above the execution ground for a month.

The Sultan is dead, what reason does Bharat have to linger in your city? You threw him out and confiscated all his merchandise as revenge compensation. It must be said, some of the items inside were quite useful... Hmm, why not take them out sooner?
You give Ansuya travel expenses. Her homeland has turned into scorched earth, but you believe she still wants to go back for a look.
Just those few books, who could possibly read enough? You order Asal to immediately collect books from all over the world for you, and not to return until he has gathered at least a hundred.

Until the seas run dry, until every mirror in the world is shattered... pledge your loyalty forever to the humans you despise and scorn!
Facing your greedy visage, [xiaochou.name] laughs aloud—the words you speak as a sovereign lend this pact such potent magic! [xiaochou.name] kneels to kiss your hand, like the humblest of servants—"Very well, my master. With this decree, humans shall never be free of the Mirror!"
So long as charges are fabricated, no one in this world remains innocent. Your men quickly uncover solid evidence to accuse him, and, in accordance with law and reason, they put him to death.
You killed the girl—simply because you needed to kill one of the exiles from the fallen kingdom, to prove that you had not forgotten the traditions of this land.
The tumultuous day finally comes to an end. May everyone find peaceful sleep tonight.

You had barely spoken Abdul’s name—let alone named the reward for your former superior—when he began to protest, showering you with honeyed words. Amidst the false warmth, you both smiled thinly and let the matter lie.
You appointed Alim as the court's master spy—his pickpockets will steal things far more valuable than gold coins... and he accepted this commission with a complex expression.
You bestowed a new title upon Adila [Dragon Slayer], a title more honorable than Lion Hunter, belonging to warriors. In the future, countless warriors might embark on adventures for this title...
You conferred a noble title to Arumina right there—much more noble than her father's. Her surprised expression was utterly charming.
You granted Murad Tus a new surname and title, now also called 'Zephyr,' but this time 'Lord' can be added to it—this name was not bought by a father-in-law.
Amur was made the Royal Judge by you, now even nobles must submit to his arbitration.
You granted Junah noble status, along with twelve servants, an estate, and tax privileges in textiles, encouraging courtly women to practice the act of saluting a former commoner in secret.
You instructed Jawad to oversee the capital's commerce—ideally gathering enough funds for the new government swiftly.
Previously, the Sultan always controlled the nation's troops, but now Jabal has been given this honorable mission by you—his family is overjoyed and has become powerful supporters of yours.
You have ordered Zaki, as the Court Honor Guard commander, to restore order in the capital—both nobles and commoners need to fear his rod and chains.
You bid Iman kneel, patting his shoulder and head as a priest blesses the humble – then you grant him alone the right to raise a new temple.
You command Emane to build a school, spreading Rationality—and your command to all commoners.
You ennoble Inal—she will become one of the court administrators in the future.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys – they must be impatient to know what happened here. 
She embraced this opportunity with enthusiasm.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys – they must be impatient to know what happened here. 
For this purpose, you bestowed upon her an ancient, tongue-twisting noble surname - to which she raised no objection, as long as it wasn't her original one - along with several trunks filled with exquisite garments, both men's and women's attire.

You ask Shama to help you meet all the foreign envoys—they must be impatient to know what happened here.
Wait, come back, put on a few more clothes, men's or women's clothes are fine.
In short, you declare that the Dancer has regained a noble status, becoming a member of a great family again—your family.

You tell [xiaochou.name] that this realm is vast beyond measure, and all you know is but a speck near the capital. You hand it secret documents and proofs, along with a new charge: to roam, to uncover all that lies upon this land! And to tell you of it through mirrors and verse. [xiaochou.name] finds this most intriguing.

You command [xiaochou.name] to take up the mantle of the new headsman—henceforth, it shall be [xiaochou.name] who severs every noble head. And in that fleeting moment, it may glimpse the tales of the condemned—etched in the glint of the blade, mirrored in the spill of blood... and share them with you in the hushed hours of the night.

You command [xiaochou.name] to join the scholars of human in devising intricate experiments—of magic, of light, of gods and realms beyond. No matter the cost, the essence of the world's workings must be uncovered. It will sate [xiaochou.name]'s every curiosity and grant you power unending, perhaps.

You command [xiaochou.name] to raise a city in the desert—one meant solely for those who are unhuman. In time, spirits and fiends alike shall kneel as your subjects... though most dismiss it as the fevered dream of a mad ruler.
You gift the closest and most fertile grassland to the capital to Aziz, and the grasslands originally belonging to his Father are also returned to him... He is now a nomadic prince again.
You grant her a license to operate a brothel—tax-free for ten years. Salwiyah cries with joy and desperately kisses your toes.
You declare that all of Zazie's Property and status within the Sultan's court are protected by you—that's enough; she already has too much.
You allow Seliman to continue managing the court guards – his expression is extremely complex.
You tell Samir that he can leave the court with a wealth and assure him there will be no assassination. He seems a bit disbelieving about the latter part...
You declare that you will protect Sadani's wealth and safety—including the child she carries within her. As these words leave your lips, a cascade of whispers ripples through the court.
You gift the three hills near the capital to Riel, which are now the habitat of her people, and she can now go to the slave market and break the chains of all the slaves on the spot.
You command Jenna to manage all the artisans in the capital and all the licenses for processing precious metals. This privilege is enough to reward any loyal friend...
Nawfal certainly doesn't want any privilege or reward... So you announce a pardon in advance for anything Nawfal says in this hall in the future—no matter who she curses, no matter how harsh.
You command Nabhani to set up a swordsman academy in the capital, of course, he evades countless times, so you easily title him as Sword Saint, now he's satisfied.
You quietly tell Nayla that soon you'll be making love to her, not just once... Nothing could please her more than this promise.

Maggie... for everything she's done, it's almost impossible to repay her with material things, so you reward her family and announce a three-year tax exemption for the residents of the capital in her name.
You give Manar enough investment and privilege, ordering her to explore unknown territories – and this time, you're bringing peace.
You announce the establishment of the Miracle Society, a research organization led by Mahir—this time she will have practically infinite budget and resources.
No matter what, you think the new era needs new attire and flags—the creation and design of these will be entrusted to Malkina.
You give the Royal Library to Lumera, she can barely hold back her desire to go take a look immediately.
You announce the true identity of the Nameless Swordsman to everyone, and restore all his privileges as a member of the royal family—to which he merely shrugged.

You no longer have anything important for Aziz to do. You order Aziz to polish ten stone lunch boxes a day and hand them to you, no work, no sleep.

You loudly praise Salwiyah's beautiful eyes, and when she shyly approaches you, you order to have them gouged out, then personally inlaid costly amethyst into her bleeding eye sockets as compensation.

You order Zazie to remove all her gold ornaments, silk, and satin, then send her off on a sealed godly palanquin. Your people will carry her to the highland snow mountains and offer her to her worshiped deity.

Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Seliman has long anticipated this moment, kneeling on the ground, eyes lowered, restraining himself, without looking at anyone.
You order the Court Physician to bring out a bowl of poison that will kill a person within an hour, then pour it into his mouth. He struggles painfully but ultimately couldn't detoxify himself.
The concubine Sadani takes the dagger you grant her, her pale face showing unexpected calm – her final plea is to glimpse the Sultan one last time.

When you intended to kill an Ally who once fought alongside you, this Beast escaped the city with astonishing intuition. It's imaginable she'll wander around this land, lurking in the shadows, waiting for you to show a flaw, looking forward to the day she can eat the traitor's liver.

You give Jenna a bag of gold, urging her to leave the capital. It is foreseeable that the storm will not calm with the Sultan's death, but become increasingly tumultuous, with endless biting and fighting, until this country welcomes a new Sultan recognized by the majority.
When you pronounce his death sentence, Nawfal says nothing, merely accepting everything calmly, accepting that you will be another Sultan.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. No matter what grievances you once had with Nabhani, everything ends here.
You use Nabhani's head to prove to the world that you are more ruthless and suspicious than the Sultan.
You have him placed under house arrest, soon he died of illness.
Just this once, you cruelly tell her, she has no right to refuse.

In this world, only the dead will always keep secrets, only the dead will never change their original intentions.
Seliman takes the dagger, smiles slightly, neither hatred nor regret.

The cruel game has ended, but the harm towards each other is forever etched in your hearts.
Upon divorce, you gave her a lot of money, but when leaving, besides her dowry, she didn't take a single extra dime. You tell her, if in the next life, don't become your wife. She just purses her lips and smiles, not agreeing with you.
You decide to imprison Manar, forbidding her from further drafting more detailed maps, in case of leaking secrets to your enemies. Soon, her guards send you the news of her demise.

You let her personally try the Confused Learning Machine she created herself. After about five tries, she will just lie in the yard basking in the sun. Perhaps the sun can give her some inspiration? Who knows.

Malkina has never heard of such an absurd reason for execution, and because of this absurdity, she realizes that your decision is irrevocable. Soon after, you hear that her mother burns down the tailor shop in remorse, but unfortunately, there is no remedy for regret in the world.

You not only burned Lumera's books but also ordered that commoners are not allowed to read or learn, because this girl made you realize how terrifying this force was. You used it to overthrow the Sultan, and one day, someone will use it to overthrow you.
Ironically, until Lumera jumped into the burning study, desperately trying to save them, and was eventually swallowed by the flames, she did not use her power to resist your decision.
You did not believe that he had no ambition for the throne that was within his reach, so you executed him, completely burying those departed names in the blood and dust of history.
You killed Lazag for the same reason that those who usurped the throne before you killed the chamberlain of the previous dynasty.
As long as she dies, those promises you made to bend her to your will need no honoring – what a joke, a mere vagrant daring to barter with you?

At the victory banquet, you ordered her to pour wine for all the nobles and noblewomen who recognized her. Tears welled up in her eyes, but she gritted her teeth and endured it.
It's okay; life will slowly teach her that the more she endures, the more torment there is.
You handed a large box of documents to Zephyr, ordering him to deliver them to every station in the empire. He won't be back for three to five years.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Jemor without hesitation.

You publicly announced a long list of Jalila's 'Fat Sheep', sweeping your fierce gaze over those men who desperately ducked their heads like ostriches. Of course, they wouldn't dare retaliate against you, but they certainly wouldn't spare the woman who leaked this secret, nor would they trust a safe house riddled with cracks.

You held up the cloak of the King of Flames high and then threw it into the fire. The sparks and ashes stained the desperate faces of the onlookers and children. You scorn those trembling people. Did you see? The redemption they longed for is nothing but a useless joke.
Without waiting for you to drive him away, he left you a farewell note with wet edges, not sure if it was just pulled out from a lamb stew.
To show your fairness and benevolence, and to prevent people from knowing you were involved with such a thief, you ordered the execution of Hamar without hesitation.
You executed Habunah because you dreamed of the blue waves no longer lifting you but drowning you on that night.
You executed Habib, without giving anyone any reason.
So, you didn't dare to bet on whether he would point the fearsome bow and arrow at you. You executed him.

Qais once defied you and even pointed at your nose and scolded you... These things you had almost forgotten suddenly emerged from the corners of your memory, leaving you tossing and turning, with a lump in your throat.
Forget it, let him die.
Fatuna confessed to her crimes without objection, and the simple truth of the world is that murder must be atoned for by death.
Executing the former Honor Guard, executing a defeated foe, is such a natural thing. Besides, shouldn't a loyal person accompany his beloved master underground?
Loyalty is meaningless. A dog that betrays its master once will do it again. You don’t trust him, so you execute him.

You drive him out of the capital and tell him the truth: the Sultan's realm would take twenty years to cross by camel, the continent beneath would require one hundred and fifty years, and beyond the sea, there is another one hundred and fifty years, and another after that... The world is so vast, he should not waste his life merely staring at you.

He has no choice but to swear to you with tears in his eyes that he will record everything during his journey and send it to you.

By your order, Fardak is stripped of his surname and inheritance rights, but still keep him under house arrest in the most expensive mansion in the city. Now he should know that you and the Sultan are cut from the same cloth.

In despair, he draws Kaplan's End, the blade he couldn't decide to use before, ending his own life.
You expelled her from your court, knowing well what harsh fate awaited a defenseless former Sultan's Slave.

You had your eye on that tender piece of Property from the House of Delights for a long time! And Buthayna had the good sense to offer the majority of profits to you, and from now on, free of charge.
Only then did you give a satisfied nod.

Lady Becky is a clever little cat. He knows who is good and who is bad to him. When you wanted to order him caught and spanked, he had long disappeared to someplace unknown. Perhaps it's somewhere nobody knows him as Lady Becky. People might call him Little White, Pearl, or Rice, but it doesn't matter to him.

You bound her with a chain imbued with magic to the stake, announcing to all the disaster brought by the Other she worshipped. She laughed insanely. The fire burned for three days and nights before it was extinguished, but her laughter seemed to linger above the execution ground for a month.

The Sultan is dead, what reason does Bharat have to linger in your city? You threw him out and confiscated all his merchandise as revenge compensation. It must be said, some of the items inside were quite useful... Hmm, why not take them out sooner?
You give Ansuya travel expenses. Her homeland has turned into scorched earth, but you believe she still wants to go back for a look.
Just those few books, who could possibly read enough? You order Asal to immediately collect books from all over the world for you, and not to return until he has gathered at least a hundred.

Until the seas run dry, until every mirror in the world is shattered... pledge your loyalty forever to the humans you despise and scorn!
Facing your greedy visage, [xiaochou.name] laughs aloud—the words you speak as a sovereign lend this pact such potent magic! [xiaochou.name] kneels to kiss your hand, like the humblest of servants—"Very well, my master. With this decree, humans shall never be free of the Mirror!"
So long as charges are fabricated, no one in this world remains innocent. Your men quickly uncover solid evidence to accuse him, and, in accordance with law and reason, they put him to death.
You killed the girl—simply because you needed to kill one of the exiles from the fallen kingdom, to prove that you had not forgotten the traditions of this land.
The tumultuous day finally comes to an end. May everyone find peaceful sleep tonight.
