strings: You hear a strange story: When executioners routinely cut out the tongues of the Sultan's eunuchs, one deliberately threw himself onto the blade seeking death... Everything is predestined, and hope truly is a corrosive poison for the human heart.

5320273.title: 宫廷-索要妃子-报复来临
strings: The Highlord won't simply leave... They return, thirsting for human souls - especially your soul, having offended Him.

5320274.title: 宫廷-索要妃子-销毁圣像
strings:
When you destroyed the Highlord's statue, Their final strong anchor to this world snapped. Contaminated by human desires, unable to return to the stars, yet losing connection to the present world, where will this declining deity fall? 
Regardless, They likely can no longer torment Zazie... She should feel this good news when she dreams tonight.

5320276.title: 宫廷-索要妃子-莎姬拜访
strings:
You dutifully hand over the small bottle you worked so hard to obtain. Zazie is overjoyed: "I got it... I can use this to stuff that damned Highlord's mouth! But... I can't help wondering, what will he demand next? What if next time he wants the Sultan's - eyeballs or something, what then?" She clutches the bottle tightly, staring into your eyes... 
"Let me be honest with you, you might think I'm crazy - but my wish was... power, power greater than the Sultan's! I don't want to be just a vessel for the next Sultan... God, I want to manipulate others' fates too!" She stares at you, seemingly waiting for you to contradict her. But you remain silent... 
"The Highlord promised to help me, but now I realize relying solely on him isn't the solution. I must give him whatever he demands, which is unacceptable... and I doubt he can truly fulfill my wish anyway. So... I'd like your advise..."
You should fulfill the contract
I can handle this better

While walking in your garden... a woman in dirty wrappings suddenly jumps from the bushes, colliding with you.
As you are about to scold her, she raises her head and gestures "shh"... It's Zazie! This favored concubine has stripped off all her jewelry and gold. She dresses like a slave girl, smears with something foul-smelling, and her hair is made deliberately dirty and messy... If not for those leopard-like eyes, you wouldn't recognize her!
"I don't trust eunuchs to fetch something this important, so I disguised myself... But I can only be away briefly... the Sultan wants me constantly these days." She glances back nervously. "Come on, let's talk inside."
She takes your hand, but her eyes question you about that item...
"You're impressive! I never imagined anyone could complete such a complex plan under the Sultan's nose!" You can't help but feel nervous: Zazie already knew you had succeeded! Hardly anyone knew about it at all!

You advise Zazie to fulfill the Highlord's contract. god beings aren't easily managed - though satisfying Their contracts doesn't guarantee a good outcome either. Let our ambitious Lady Zazie learn this lesson herself.

You tell Zazie you can eliminate this Highlord. Anything hey desires, like what's in this bottle, can serve as excellent bait... 
Zazie stares at you silently for a long time, then places the bottle back in your hand... "This is the first time in my life I've trusted a man so completely. Don't disappoint me!"

5320277.title: 宫廷-索要妃子-苏丹的奴隶事后感谢
strings:
A hooded figure knocks at your door, bringing a book - a gift in gratitude for giving him physical freedom, reading freedom, and even the freedom to express thanks.
After saying this, he quickly disappears into the night.

5320278.title: 宫廷-索要妃子-苏丹的奴隶事后感谢
strings: The eunuch who was pretend-killed never reappears... Could sewer alligators really eat people? Who cares, you've achieved your purpose.

5320282.title: 可疑的房租
strings: This foreign merchant's expression seemed a little off as he handed you the coins. Was it the Gold Coins? Careful as ever, you noticed one looks a little different—was it only a trick of the eye?

5320283.title: 跑路的巴拉特
strings: Bharat vanished without a word. In the room he rented, in a crack in the cellar floor, you find a "Gold Coin"... From the traces, it was clear his counterfeiting work was done here. To avoid trouble, you ceased your investigation and even helped erase all remaining evidence.

5320284.title: 被捕的异国商人
strings:
Following the money's trail, you seized a foreign forger—his identity papers and travel pass both forged, clearly a seasoned forger...
When the Sultan's headsman took his head, you received his remaining "Gold Coins." They spend just like the real ones—call it a reward from the Sultan, perhaps?

5320285.title: 不安的访客
strings: It is no easy task to uncover clues on the counterfeit coins by the deadline the Sultan demands, and days of raids by soldiers and High Constables have left the capital on edge. Today, just as you finished questioning some unfortunate innocent, the foreign merchant Bharat—your tenant—came to your door. He was tense, flustered, afraid... and suspiciously eager to ask how the counterfeit case was progressing.
If the criminal would only stop.
I can't help you if you don't tell the truth.

You gave him a knowing look. "At present there are no leads... If no more counterfeit appears in the market, the Sultan will not dig any deeper, will he?" Clever as he is, he should realize that this is the last moment for him to stop.
He hesitated, then sighed. "You're right, my lord. Please—come with me."

5320286.title: 苏丹的问询
strings: While you chased the forgers' trail, the Sultan watched you in turn... and now suspicion stirs in his heart.

5320287.title: 苏丹的追问
strings: What you reported and presented before failed to satisfy the Sultan... he summoned you again.

5320288.title: 安的噩耗
strings: Consort Ansuya has not appeared of late... some say she is already dead within the Sultan's harem. As with all women who vanish into that shadow, no explanation will ever be given.

5320289.title: 诺言
strings: You have made every preparation; Bharat is brimming with excitement, ready to strike hard at the Sultan's mint with counterfeits.

5320290.title: 诺言
strings: You have made every preparation; Bharat is brimming with excitement, ready to strike hard at the Sultan's mint with counterfeits.

5320291.title: 阔别已久
strings: Bharat knocked at your back door by night once again—this time with a new name and a new identity... none of which matter to you now. What matters is that you are the closest minister to the Sultan... and he still has obsessions with the Sultan—or with things around him—burns like a moth drawn to flame... and offers himself to your service.
Nameless Peddler

5320292.title: 可疑的收入
strings: Eh? Wait. How did it end up back in my hands?

5320293.title: 诗人与美食
strings:
It was just at noon when your servants ushered Hassan into your receiving room.
"My friend—my powerful, handsome, pleasure-wise friend, dear [player.name]! The scent of your kitchen drew me here!"
His voice set the servants laughing, and even you smiled.
"What's for lunch?" Hassan glanced about your dining hall. "Oh! Fig custard! Stuffed roast pigeons! What did I say—no one knows fine eating like you!"
You had a low couch brought for him and seated him by your side; together you enjoyed the meal. After a few cups from your cellar, Hasan half closed his eyes and drifted to another topic.
"You know me. My creed is that life is for gratifying oneself. And I, old Hassan, I have done rather well at that! But lately I've begun to feel..." He shook his head and popped a fried cheese dumpling into his mouth. "I feel these homely dishes are... not thrilling enough—not giving me inspiration. My noble friend... if you should come upon some a truly rare feast, do call me to taste it. I swear I'll write fine verse that your table will be famed across the city!"
You promise that if there is a feast worth the name, you will invite him.
Hassan left well content, belly in his hands; the little ram trotted after, munching the green radish a servant had slipped it.

5320294.title: 诗人与美食
strings: This day, Hassan came pale-faced; you had never seen him look so stricken. Trembling, he handed you a thick sheet of vellum. It was the Sultan's decree: "Your poems in praise of [player.name]'s table have reached even Us. Come taste the royal cook's work—let Us hear what you can write." Sweat crawls down your spine. You never thought such poems would reach the Sultan's ears... A minister's household feast with such renown—the sovereign will not be pleased... "Please—go with me. You know me—I'm hopeless when I'm nervous—and what could be more terrifying than standing before the Sultan himself? [player.name], I beg you!" Hassan pleaded again and again, and you too felt you must go; if he performed poorly before the Sultan, the consequences could be far worse... You made an appointment with the eunuch who brought the decree: 3 days from now you will enter the palace. Remember: prepare the poetry well, and do not miss the time. To keep the Sultan waiting is a crime punishable by death!

5320296.title: 诗人与美食
strings: Because Hassan died, the Sultan canceled the banquet.

5320297.title: 诗人与美食
strings: Zazie's death seems to have spoiled the Sultan's appetite for a banquet.

5320298.title: 倒胃口
strings:
Hassan comes to see you. After only a few days apart, he looks noticeably thinner.
"My old friend... my dear [player.name], last time was nearly scared me to death..." He takes your hands the moment he sees you. "So this is what it feels like to serve the Sultan... and this is what you face every day... By the heavens, if I were you, I couldn't endure a single day!"
He tells you that since that "royal delicacy," the mere sight of pomegranate seeds, caviar, tuna and other delights turn his stomach. As a result, he has grown thinner and even drank less than before.
"Now I think... home-cooked food is the best! Nothing beats home cooking!" Hassan says sincerely. "I wrote a little poem—for you—about home-cooked fare. Oh, my friend, thank you. Without you, I would likely be a headless corpse today!"
He seems to be in fine spirits. It looks like his accidental diet has done him some good.

5320299.title: 诗人与美人
strings:
Hassan came running.
He had heard every rumor of your amorous escapades; people said that in the Empire, save for the Sultan himself, you were the most battle-tested of all. So he had a request...
"All pleasures are my inspiration... and every thrill, every exploit, every stirring of the heart! Could you, ah... help me find some beauties to talk with? Perhaps I might find inspiration... and write more of my very best!"
You looked him over, wondering which beauties would agree to converse with this old poet...

5320301.title: 够了！够了！
strings: Of late Hassan's love poems were everywhere. Not only ladies who collect such lines adored them, but even those who seldom read poetry were quoting his lines. All thanked to your arranging beauties for him to talk with; each meeting yielded at least fifty love poems!
This seems like another ordinary tale, and yet...

At noon, as you are dozing over Hassan's poetry scroll, you have a dream...
In the dream, you and Hassan sit back to back, surrounded by cloud-like little animals—squirrels, frogs, birds... They chatter at you:
"Stop writing! Love, love, love—don't you know anything else! Sour! Cloying! Boring! Write something else! We're sick of this! I might as well take this stuff out of your brain—humans are such trouble, always obsessed with this kind of thing! Baa!"
You wake up, yet the dream still lingers, vivid as ever.

5320302.title: 爱的教育
strings: Hassan came to you, dejected.

5320303.title: 羊的抱怨
strings:
You stepped into a dreamlike haze.
From within the mist came the sheep's voice.
"Then what do you propose, baa? Otherwise he'll just keep writing and writing only love poems, always about love, baa! Of all the things humans do, love is the one I hate most!"
You smiled. Its anger only proved its regret; Hassan had been its favorite toy—perhaps more than just a toy, though it would never admit it—and now it truly didn't know what to do.
I have an idea.
None of my business.

So you make a suggestion: let him keep the capacity for love, but punish him a little for his overproduction of love verse. For instance, send him to someone who understands love the least, and let that person grind him down for a while...
The rolling clouds pause; then a huge ovine eye opens within them—like a malformed sun—staring straight at you.
"You're very good at pleasing those above you, aren't you, baa? You always have a way... ha, ha, ha, baa! Tell me, how will you do this!"
You ponder: who could be the one who understands love the least?
You can feel it is angry, and before you can make amends, you are expelled from that void... back into the flat, impotent, passionless, and hazard-filled real world.

5320304.title: 青楼诗人
strings:
Hassan bursts in, elated, waving a sweet-scented card.
"Look—look, my friend! I've finally made it! Look!"
It is an invitation from Madame Buthayna, mistress of the city's greatest House of Delights. She wishes the old poet to serve as her house's Poet of Delight, composing love verses for the Lady of Delights.
"I'll deliver—I swear it! My verses will leave every man in the city burning with desire, rushing to taste the beauties I've praise!"
He claps you on the shoulder and thanks you—for it was you who once arranged so many conversations on love, the very source of his countless verses.
He leaves in high spirits. You trade a glance with the little sheep at his heels.

5320305.title: 教学的工作
strings:
Hassan arrives in high spirits, saying that Nawfal has suddenly sent for him with a teaching post.
"He said there's a place called the Nursery, full of children who can't yet read... He asked if I could teach them what poetry is—what the art of letters is—oh, I'd love to!"
Cautiously, you suggest it might be best not to teach the children love poems...
"Eh, we'll see when the time comes!" Hassan is as breezy as ever. "And I suppose that court official you're acquainted with won't keep me on a tight leash, will he?"
You watch him sway away. Behind him, the little lamb pauses a moment and meets your gaze.

5320306.title: 诗歌审查员
strings:
Hassan comes to you, frowning with suspicious.
He says Vizier Abdul has summoned him to be a reviewer of poetry in the royal library, mainly for love poems—classifying, grading, and excerpting them...
"True, all I want to write lately is love poetry... but I don't think this job will be that simple." He scratches his head. "Anyway—see you in three days, my friend. I'll share what I learn then."
You and the little sheep exchange a look.

5320307.title: 宫廷诗人
strings:
Hassan is nearly in tears when he rushes to your house. He clutches your arm and says he has been appointed court poet.
The Sultan read his love poems and was delighted. Now the Sultan wants him to compose for his women as well—
"I won't be able to write—I won't be able to eat or drink—I won't even be able to... to go! In front of the Sultan I can't do anything—I can't even breathe! What do I do—what do I do!"
You and the little sheep try to comfort him, one with words, the other with a gentle nudge of the head. But in your hearts...
Hassan leaves still sniffling. The next three days will not be kind to him.

5320309.title: 选择布缇娜
strings: On Hassan's questions, you have an idea—perhaps Madam Buthayna could help.
Choose her.
I'll think on it.

You found another chance to meet Lamblet. No one could suit the task better than Madame Buthayna, you told It: in the trade of the Lady of Delights, the greatest taboo was falling in love with a client; her heart was harder than diamond—there was no fear she might fall for anyone. If Hassan were placed at her side, he would likely revise his views on love within three days!
"So be it, baa, so be it! I will arrange it—just a few tiny adjustments, nothing difficult! Baa-baa-baa-baa—I look forward to it, baa; you really are very good at this game of pleasure!" The sheep laughed thunderously, its eye never leaving you. "If I ever go to find another world to play in, I will write a character like you, baa... perhaps I will simply snatch you over, baa-ha-ha!"
Hassan's gift for poetry, his passion and desire, should remain intact. But his happiness for the next few days—well... that may not survive.
It seems that lamb is running out of patience.

5320310.title: 选择奈费勒
strings: On Hassan's questions, you have an idea—perhaps Nawfal could help.
Choose him.
I'll think on it.

You found another chance to meet Lamblet. No one is better than Nawfal to snuff out a poet's fire," you told it seriously. "He has no sense of romance, no flights of fancy. His life exists only for the grand, tangible 'state.' Not a single moment is wasted on so-called love.
If he takes over Hassan's work, the old poet will see life in a whole new way—no more churning out cheesy love poems for a circle of beauties."
"So be it, baa, so be it! I will arrange it—just a few tiny adjustments, nothing difficult! Baa-baa-baa-baa—I look forward to it, baa; you really are very good at this game of pleasure!" The sheep laughed thunderously, its eye never leaving you. "If I ever go to find another world to play in, I will write a character like you, baa... perhaps I will simply snatch you over, baa-ha-ha!"
Hassan's gift for poetry, his passion and desire, should remain intat. But his happiness for the next few days—well... that may not survive.
It seems that lamb is running out of patience.

5320311.title: 选择阿卜德
strings: On Hassan's questions, you have an idea—perhaps Abdul could help.
Choose him.
I'll think on it.

You find another chance to meet Lamblet. You tell them that the most suitable person you could think of is Abdul. Even if love had once lingered in his life, he would have traded it all for power and gold. He trusts nothing that can't be bartered. Everything Hassan owns is worthless in his eyes. If Hassan were placed at his side, Abdul would surely put the old poet to work in his own slick, calculating way. In no more than three days, Hassan's mind would be brimming with creative urges... probably all about murder plots or managing budget deficits—anything but second-rate love poems!
"So be it. Baa. So be it! I will arrange it—just a few tiny adjustments, nothing difficult! Baa-baa-baa-baa—I'm looking forward to it. Baa. You really are quite skilled at pleasing others!" The lamb laughs thunderously, their eyes still fixed on you. "Next time I go looking for another world to play in, I will write a character like you. Baa... Perhaps I will simply snatch you over, baa-ha-ha!"
Hassan's gift for poetry, his passion and desire, probably remain intact. But as for the next few days awaiting him—well... best of luck to him.
It seems that lamb is running out of patience.

5320312.title: 选择苏丹
strings: On Hassan's questions, you have an idea—perhaps Sultan could help.
Choose him.
I'll think on it.

You found another chance to meet Lamblet. You spoke only two words: "The Sultan."
That alone was enough. The lamb bursted into laughter—
"So be it, baa, so be it! I will arrange it—just a few tiny adjustments, nothing difficult! Baa-baa-baa-baa—I look forward to it, baa; you really are very good at this game of pleasure!" The sheep laughed thunderously, its eye never leaving you. "If I ever go to find another world to play in, I will write a character like you, baa... perhaps I will simply snatch you over, baa-ha-ha!"
Hassan's gift for poetry, his passion and desire, should remain intact. But his happiness for the next few days—well... that may not survive.
It seems that lamb is running out of patience.

5320313.title: 生气的羊肉炉
strings:
Baa! You had dawdled far too long! I had lost interest now! Tiresome humans! Lying humans! Suffer!
As the words droned in your ears, a greasy, dark, ill-omened force clung to your body... like a gob of spittle spat by a god.

5320314.title: 诗人登门
strings:
Your servants came laughing to announce that Master Hassan had come to drink with you. Hassan was welcome in every noble house: the servants liked him because he put on no airs and slipped them tidbits from the banquet; the nobles liked him because any feast shone more elegantly with him present.
Bleating and laughter drifted up the hall; you stood in the doorway to welcome the poet. He embraced you warmly and again thanked you for helping him at the last banquet.
"I would have built a wall of ten thousand poems to keep all those conflicts out... but ten thousand seemed still not enough!" he said with a laugh, settling easily on the carpet in your receiving room and grabbing a handful of the pastries your servants had set out. "Your sweets were excellent... Believe me, I seldom said so. Trust old Hassan—I knew whose wine is best and whose pastries smell the finest!"
You chatted lightly for a while; then, idly teasing his little sheep, you asked how old it was. In your memory it had always been about this size...
"Ah, you mean Lamblet? Yes, that's its name—how old? Hm... let me think, I came by it when..."
Hassan's eyes went a touch glassy... You felt something was off—something seemed to be spilling out of the sheep and boring straight into your and Hassan's minds...

5320315.title: 奇怪的攻击
strings: You seemed to arrive within a mass of cloud, woolly as fleece, cut off from the real world... This appeared to be a realm you ought not to tread, and ahead some odd guardians appeared...

5320316.title: 和咩咩对谈
strings: At last, everything fell quiet. You raised your head—this space, wrapped in cloud, should have been your courtyard.
Is—any—one—there—? Where—am—I—?

"Baa—ah! What are you doing, baa! Why is it that every time we meet, there's chaos, deviation, wrong turns everywhere! Baa! Can't you not make trouble for once?"
Deafening bleats pressed in from all sides, as if to crush you. You fought back with your own strength, striving to keep calm.
You asked the voice—what was it? What was its connection to Hassan? What did it want?
"Who am I? Baa, baa, baa... I am something you could not truly comprehend—I merely like poetry, like stories, like to find a little fun! Compared to those so-called gods you worshiped, you will have found I am the most merciful, baa! As for Hassan, baa... since you have mangaged to reach here, it means you can bear a little of the truth's weight... I will tell you this: the world you see has two parts—one part existed before Hassan, including you; the other appeared only after Hassan."
You were startled and pressed it on what the latter part meant—
"Baa—you are abusing my patience and my kindness toward lower beings—baa! Begone. I will spare you this time; but remember, baa-baa-baa—you are not to provoke Hassan to question my existence again. Do not even think about it. Do it again, and everyone will only think you are a fool!"
The clouds peeled away. You still stood in the courtyard; birds sang, servants' footstepsechoed as before. They told you Hassan had dashed off to chase his sheep and had already taken his leave.
What had happened still lingered in your mind—but who would believe it?

5320317.title: 命运的诗集
strings: Realizing these words might bear extraordinary meaning, you copied them all down... (The more phrases you gathered, the greater the value of this transcript might become.)

5320318.title: 你怎么敢咩
strings: You seemed to arrive in a bank of cloud; Hassan beside you appeared frozen in time, and the sheep was nowhere to be seen.

5320319.title: 攻击间隙
strings:
You held out against the onrushing spirits, barely.
Before the next assault you found a gap and shouted toward the thing behind the clouds.
You must ask what will interest it...

"Haah, baa-baa-baa... how hilarious, baa!" Thunder rolled. "Why would I need the offerings of a lesser being, baa? It's precisely because I'm sick of such 'offerings' that I came to this world for some fun!"
The ground vanished under your feet—and you fell.
I wish to serve you, O God who can rewrite reality!
We are the same—you don't have to be my foe.
Awaken

What had happened?
You looked around; Hassan regarded you with a patient smile.
You remembered nothing, yet your body felt as though it had just survived a fight to the death; you sensed that you had grown stronger...

"Like me? Baa? Like me?" The voice took on a hint of puzzlement—which meant you had struck a chord, and it was growing more interested in you!
You steadied your breath and spoke as smoothly as you could: It had come here, meddled in Hassan's life, joined this game because it longed for excitement, for curious, for fun, didn't it? It loved poetry, loved probing the unknown, loved indulging its curiosity—was that wrong? In that case, you and It were alike: you wished to peer at It precisely because you could not hold back your own curiosity—that curiosity was like a beast devouring you from within; you had to feed it, had to sate it!
"Ha-ha-ha-ha, baa—baa-ha! You truly were amusing! The Sultan's Game... how delightful, baa!"
Thunderous laughter erupted, and then the clouds pressing upon you eased a little...
"I like you; unlike those weaklings who worship—baa-baa—other gods.I despise them, and I despise their gods alike. Come then, come, baa-baa-baa, I will reward you! I will give you a single chance to choose, amusing lower being—just once—you could pick one poem from my bookshelf, read it, even alter it, baa—just once!"
A blaze of gold flashed before your eyes.

5320320.title: 羊肉炉的恶意
strings: At the very last instant before leaving that place, you feel yourself overwhelmed by a crushing, tidal force—as if a wad of flimsy grass-paper were being chewed and churned within some unseen maw. Only after they have vented enough displeasure and malice, do they spit you back into reality.

5320321.title: 命运变动
strings: The colors of dreams, the shapes of clouds, reflections in puddles, the patterns traced by drifting tea leaves—whenever reality was altered, the excess pigments and inks spilled into such places, the ones mortals rarely noticed... and even if you sensed it, there was nothing you could do but let it shift as it would.

5320322.title: 我也来一首
strings:
After so many talks on poetry with Hassan, you felt you wanted to try writing a poem yourself...
So that night you strained in your study for quite a while and finally produced these lines:
"If fate were steered by no hand,
as when fine wine gose untasted,
its sharpness sipped by worms."
You did not know whence the lines had come, but all in all, they were rather good, weren't they? You left the poem on your desk and put it out of mind.

5320323.title: 可爱的蹄子
strings:
You suddenly noticed extra ink on that sheet with your few lines...
"It did not mind Its hooves are stained,
a little poem, a little pawn,
a tiny twist,
the emporium of fate.
To join the game,
madness, joy, and poetry!
Yet he still sighs and wonders,
whether fate lies in human's hands!
Baa—ha—ha!"
You held the paper, feeling a pang of bewilderment. It wasn't only the verses that troubled you—the dainty trail of ink-stained hoofprints across your study carpet gave you quite the headache as well...

5320324.title: 可疑的钱币
strings:
A special gold coin had begun to circulate in the Dark Alley lately. To the eye it was no different from those minted by order of the Sultan, but its gold was thin, and when cut open, one could see the trace of lead within.
A petty official at the market had confiscated such a coin; he dared not report it directly to the Sultan's Tax Collector, fearing he would be punished by association, so he brought the coin to you instead.
You studied the Sultan's profile on the coin's reverse and pondered: who could be behind this...?

5320327.title: 午夜欢宴
strings: You woke again in an unfamiliar place.

5320332.title: 百科全书
strings:
Asal visits with some leaves of the manuscript. He spreads the sheets of minuscule script before you. You pick one up and find it filled with entries—each term followed by its pronunciation, its appearance, its use. Just these few pages alone explain hundreds of things in the world.
"I never imagined I would show these to anyone outside my family." He lifts his chin, plainly proud. "The Angler's is a livelihood to me, and I do it well—but the Encyclopedia, that is my life."
Then he points to the very last entry on the last sheet: "Lord of Revels: a powerful being from another world, who lures humans into their feast through 'Ambiguities.' After three times, they devour their shells..." The entry even described the Lord's appearance and how to defeat them.
"You are qualified to join my work—to leave your name in the greatest enterprise in the world." He looks you in the eyes. "In the future, if you encounter anything remarkable... call me to take a look, and I will record it in the Encyclopedia."
He gathers the pages, bows with measured grace, and takes his leave.
Perhaps you can try contributing entries to him—who will know what secret future that may lead toward...

5320345.title: 另一位爱书的权臣
strings:
Asal, the proprietor of the Angler, came to pay you a visit.
Courteous as ever, he presented a book as a gift before plunging straight into his request.
"There is a certain grand vizier of the Empire, renowned for his love of books..." Noticing you start to adjust your robes, he adds, somewhat tactlessly, "Oh, I do not mean you, of course—you, sir, are beyond comparison. I speak of Lord Nawfal. I hear his collection is vast beyond imagining, filled with volumes so rare they can't be found in any market. To borrow a metaphor from the poetry of the fallen kingdom, his library is like a giant in the desert, like nectar stored in the Khan's golden pavilion."
You exchanged a wordless look with him, waiting for him to continue, yet he seemed to expect you to understand his meaning without further prompting. After a long pause, the Bookstore Owner furrowed his brow and sighed, forced at last to speak plainly:
"...I take it you are a man of influence, and a bookworm as well... Might you introduce me to Lord Nawfal? I wish merely to behold his collection, nothing more."
"Nothing more", is it?!

What did he mean by that—did he think it an easy request? Anyone with half a wit knew Nawfal guarded his books like glass goblets ready to shatter at the slightest touch. Never mind you, his sworn rival—there likely was not a single noble in the court who had ever set foot in his library!!
You were about to curse Asal when he at once produced a fine sandalwood casket: "I also brought a gift-book that lord might fancy—do you think he would like it?"
Swallowing your anger, you opened the box: inside a rare old volume lay swaddled in silk. You could not help glancing again at the "calling gift" he had given you earlier—the gap was... considerable.
"I truly wish to visit Lord Nawfal's library... and I believe you won't want to miss this rare opportunity either." Asal spoke earnestly, expectantly; after waiting a beat and seeing you had not taken the hint, he added: "I mean—perhaps you could also furnish a gift of your own? After all, he is a courtier and so were you; surely you knew best what tickled a lord's fancy?"
What—did you want so badly to stroll Nawfal's stacks? Had you time for such leisure? And you were to curry favor with gifts for that man? On what grounds? Slamming the casket shut, fuming, you nevertheless found your mind straying to whether your own collection held aught more precious than this book...

5320346.title: 要阻止他吗
strings: Asal seems to have a book hidden on his person... a book of Nawfal's.
Stop him.
Pretend you saw nothing.

Asal recoiled as if stung by a bee, while you reached to see just what he had hidden.
What a joke—Nawfal had been generous in opening his vault to you; if he then discovered your companion stealing a book, where would your face be? Next time he flayed you in court, you would not be able to hold your head up again!
Your tussle drew Nawfal; he came past the servants and stepped between you.
Flushed with shame, Asal finally slumped and pulled the book from his breast, then fell to his knees with a thunk.
"Your library is magnificent, like trapping the stars in a birdcage—of all those books, this was the only one I had not read! I simply could not bear to let knowledge slip past me... I knew you would never permit me to return, so I meant to copy it and put it back! I swear it! I swear by the Encyclopedia!"
His voice echoed in the vaults. You said nothing, only turned to Nawfal.
"The Encyclopedia, you say? I recall there once was a family who vowed to record all things under heaven..." Nawfal mused. "And you say you have read all the rest of my collection? There are thousands of volumes here."
Asal nodded hard. Nawfal randomly chose a few and quizzed him. To your surprise, Asal could recite each from the first page...
"Impressive indeed... I admire your memory and your hunger for knowledge. But I cannot condone theft. Fortunately, my Lord [player.name] here forestalled you in time." Nawfal glanced at you, then said to Asal, "I can permit you to make a copy—yet my books cannot leave my vault. So you must take up residence here for the next few days. How about that?"
The thought crossed your mind: this was like setting a cat loose in the cream—or Nabhani loose in a House of Delights.
Asal thanked Nawfal in rapture, and then turned to thank you as well.

If Nawfal was displeased, then you were very pleased. You cast Asal a subtle smile and looked coolly away.
The two of you left Nawfal's vault one after another.
Before you each went home, Asal, half-hiding his face, murmured his thanks.

5320347.title: 归于木林
strings:
Asal came with a roll of manuscript. Bowing deeply at once, he presented the volume, then confessed he had stolen a book from Nawfal's vault.
"It was the only book in his vault that I had not read... I simply could not accept watching it slip past me, and in a moment of... alas, I am deeply ashamed—I stole it. Now I have finished reading it and copied it out."
You reached for the book, but Asal did not let go. The two of you hung there in an odd stalemate—wait. You suddenly grasped his meaning: he expected you to help him return the book...?
"Ah—so you did catch my meaning! That was exactly it! You would help, would you not? Otherwise, wouldn't you become my accomplice? After all, we entered Lord Nawfal's vault together..."
...
You had an overwhelming urge to shake his head and see what it contained.
"All you need do is delay Lord Nawfal and his personal servants for a moment. I have studied the path to pry open the vault and put the book back... I remembered exactly where it sat, and I guaranteed no one would find out!"
And to bribe you, as it were, he laid the cursed manuscript in your hands: "This one is for you."

5320348.title: 不合时宜的思想
strings:
Not long after, you notice that "Untimely Thoughts" has reappeared in the Angler, its title changed, its contents subtly altered.
The fresh pages still carry the scent of ink. As you turn them, you become aware of the eyes of passersby, their gazes flicking between the book and you. The whispers of those around, intertwined with the text itself, stir a quiet unease within you...

5320349.title: 书窖里的窃贼
strings: Soon after, you heard Asal had been jailed for breaking into a noble residence and committing theft.

5320350.title: 提醒
strings:
At day's end, as you left the palace after audience, Nawfal remarked, half in passing, that a collection of thought from the former dynasty had appeared on the Angler's counter. How strange—he had thought he alone possessed that book in the whole realm.
It was beyond doubt he had seen through the whole affairs; his face was calm—tinged with displeasure, but not anger. In that habitual needling tone of his, he blandly warned you not to bring trouble down on your head, as though you lacked the cultivation to read, to understand how sharp those ideas were. Hmph! You tossed him a "mind your own business" look; and in full view at the palace gate you nearly fell out brawling again. Though you parted on bad terms, you had to admit his warning carried weight. Back home, you had Asal read the text carefully that very night to see what passages might need trimming...

5320351.title: 可怜的阿萨尔
strings: After much weighing, you decided that the safest way to satisfy the Sultan is to execute Asal.

5320353.title: 一本书的诞生-2
strings:
Your thoughts had barely torn free of Lumera's revenge when Asal, owner of the Angler, arrived.
As always, he bowed with exquisite deference, moving like a noble of the fallen kingdom.
"My thanks for allowing me to set foot in your splendid residence—it is so beautiful, like silk spun by the goddess from the thinnest threads..."
After a flurry of florid praise, he politely brought up Lumera's book. The acclaim on the streets smelled like an opportunity to him; thus he wished for your permission to publish it. If you consented, he would see to plates and printing—more formal, more accurate, and far wider in reach than the handful of hand-copied manuscripts now in circulation.
Agree
Reject
I need to ask the author.

You agreed to Asal's request; he happily promised the venture would turn a profit and that he would report revenues to you at any time.
Offhand, he also mentioned the book would go to market "with a recommendation by [player.name]"— a way to shelter the edition under your name and dodge trouble. You know that could cause you headaches, but you let it slide: after all, the book was Lumera's—and you truly wished to recommend it.
For various reasons you did not think a mass publication would benefit you or Lumera. Though Asal implored you again and again, you refused in the strongest terms.

Since the book was Lumera's, the author must consent.
You had her invited to your receiving room. The moment she entered, Asal launched into a string of extravagant metaphors—she was the moon, the nightingale, a pagan muse, the moon of the plateau—only then repeating his request.
"Oh... you mean—that what I wrote would be carved on blocks and printed, is that it?"
Lumera's cheeks flushed slightly; it was rare to see her so excited. She widened her eyes and looked at you, many feelings passing through them, though her lips were still pressed tight.
"I think—if you would allow it—I think I would like to publish..."
Dear Lumera—what words were those? Of course youagreed! You would even fund the printing yourself!

5320354.title: 大麦
strings:
At first light, Asal comes to you, looking extremely excited, and a fat bag of money is clutched in his hands.
"Madame Lumera's book sold well... incredibly well! I already ordered a reprint! This is the share from the first edition—I will of course give you a share, just as a mirror naturally returns light to the sun!"
Leaving aside that metaphor... you weigh the bag. It is indeed satisfying.
"But there is a small problem now, for which I hope you can help... Just as a pomegranate tree needs a gardener to prune away the excess branches if it is to flourish."
After saying this, he holds your gaze for a moment. Seeing that you haven't quite understood, he has to explain: "I mean... there are quite a few shoddy pirated copies appearing on the market now. All reprinted from my... no, our edition! If you can resolve this... our sales will do far better."

5320355.title: 第一次版税
strings: Asal brought you the royalties. Holding the small bag of gold, you wondered whether you should hand the money to the book's author, Lumera.

5320356.title: 盗版横行
strings: Piracy ran rampant; any hope of further royalties evaporated.

5320357.title: 不受欢迎的小书
strings: A little chapbook suddenly went viral, describing how you had brutally killed over thirty booksellers and committing every imaginable atrocity against them. You could not clear your name; you even wanted to seize the author and have him killed, but such writers hid better than rats. The scandal not only hurt your reputation, it damaged the name and sales of Lumera's book—the source of the whole affair: people claimed this slave girl had soared to fame only because she had such a cruel patron and sponsor like you. Worse, quite a few hopped up to claim that they were her ghostwriters... Asal sought you out and let out a helpless sigh. In short, you could no longer expect this book to earn anything further.

5320359.title: 思考之后
strings:
Lumera came to you.
Head respectfully bowed, she made a request you had not expected.
"Master [player.name], if you would allow it... I would like to use the gold you gave me—the one you called 'royalties'—to do one thing. I wish to sponsor more stories to be published." Lifting her eyes slightly, she seemed to watch for your reaction.
Those eyes shone like a scatter of stars—who could harden his heart before such a gaze? You told her the money was hers to spend as she liked, and that if she wants to print more books, she should go ahead.
Lumera's cheeks flushed again; she thanked you lightly.
Thereafter you could keep sharing royalties with her... and those coins, in turn, gave birth to even more books.

5320360.title: 后续版税
strings: Asal brought you the royalties from Lumera's chapbook.

5320362.title: 命运的书店不处理的诅咒
strings:
You missed the chance...
Hassan looks at you with worry. You glance around and can not remember what just happened... You only feel as if life has gotten a little worse...

5320363.title: 一桩纠纷
strings:
A servant tells you Malkina is arguing with a strange man outside your residence, so you go to look.
The man seems a low noble, one hand gripping a shy-eyed young woman; the other jabbing angrily at Malkina, who wears a face of lofty indifference.
After listening a while, you untangle it: the girl had long pined for the man but could not win his affection, so she went to Malkina, asking to be remade in the image of his ideal woman... and it worked. But later, he discovered the hair, the skin, the figure had all been "enhanced" by Malkina... He felt deceived; Malkina, of course, felt she had done nothing wrong.
The two glare at each other, neither yielding an inch... perhaps you should say something?
You are to blame.
The woman behind you is to blame.
Malkina, honestly?
None of my business.

You sighed and stepped between the man and Malkina.
You first asked Malkina how she had dressed the girl.
"She said the man liked curves, maple-colored long hair, skin like ebony, and bright red lips," Malkina replied, indifferent. "That is nothing a little costuming sleight-of-hand, a few straps in the right places, a dab of skin oil and hair oil, and a smear of honey on the lips could not solve."
"And what I got was a fake—!" the man shouted angrily. "Her hair was not even maple—it was dyed! It even ran—look!"
You blocked his hand as it reached toward Malkina. You told him the fault is his own:
he built an idol in his mind, a perfect image no one could ever be. So of course someone could reach his heart by copying that illusion. He was the one who refused to love a soul—so how could he blame the mask that fooled him?
Leaning close, you spoke more softly. "Look at her. She changed herself completely for you. She painted her skin, tied her body, sweetened her lips—all to become what you desired. Isn't that proof enough of her love? And doesn't it show that what you call 'beauty' is no more than a clever trick of oils and threads?"
The man frozen, glancing between you, Malkina, and the girl behind him — only now realizing he's still clutching her hand.
They exchanged a quick, flustered look, cheeks burning.
Then they left. The man muttered a hasty apology to Malkina; the girl, teary-eyed, thanked you.
Your eloquence left a deep impression on everyone who witnessed the scene.

You sighed and stepped between the man and Malkina.
You first asked Malkina how she had dressed the girl.
"She said the man liked curves, maple-colored long hair, skin like ebony, and bright red lips," Malkina replied, indifferent. "That is nothing a little costuming sleight-of-hand, a few straps in the right places, a dab of skin oil and hair oil, and a smear of honey on the lips could not solve."
"And what I got was a fake—!" the man shouted angrily. "Her hair was not even maple—it was dyed! It even ran—look!"
You blocked his hand as it reached toward Malkina. Then you seized the girl behind him and pulled her forward.
You told the man that the real deceiver isn't Malkina—it's this girl. She learned all his preferences first, then had Malkina disguise herself to fit them. Malkina was only the knife; the one holding it is the real culprit.
You went on to say that being deceived wasn't always such a terrible thing. After all, not everyone was worth deceiving. Coming from the Sultan's own minister, your words sounded all the more convincing. If a woman was willing to change her appearance just to win his favor, wasn't that something for a man to feel proud of? Think about it—what exactly was he angry about? No one's been hurt here.
The man's face turned red as he mumbled something about "feeling humiliated when people saw she wasn’t really dark-skinned." Yet his grip on the girl's hand only tightens. Her face, too, flushed crimson. She stole a glance at you, then quickly lowered her eyes.
And just like that, the quarrel ended. The man mumbled a vague thanks, the girl winked at Malkina, and the two of them left together.
The onlookers, meanwhile, seemed utterly convinced by your eloquence.

You sighed and stepped between the man and Malkina.
You first asked Malkina how she had dressed the girl.
"She said the man liked curves, maple-colored long hair, skin like ebony, and bright red lips," Malkina replied, indifferent. "That is nothing a little costuming sleight-of-hand, a few straps in the right places, a dab of skin oil and hair oil, and a smear of honey on the lips could not solve."
"And what I got was a fake—!" the man shouted angrily. "Her hair was not even maple—it was dyed! It even ran—look!"
You blocked his hand as it reached toward Malkina, and then waved Malkina to your side.
You told the man that Malkina indeed had made a mistake—her only fault lay in dragging the woman he imagined out of his dreams and into the real world. He wanted a full-figured, maple-haired, dark-skinned, dazzling beauty, and hopelessly in love with him. Malkina's craft was the only way to fulfill his wish. But yes, she meddled where she shouldn't have. What harm would there have been in letting him go on dreaming?
Malkina bowed sincerely to the man and promised to restore the girl to her former look; snickers ran through the bystanders, and the man, realizing you were right, only grew angrier.
He ranted for a long while as you and Malkina watched him like one might watch a clown perform. In the end he dared nothing, and slunk off home with the girl in tow.
The crowd came away impressed by yoursharp tongue and eloquence.
You said nothing at all, simply watched. After a brief quarrel, the man stormed off tugging the girl behind him; the girl cast Malkina a complicated look and said nothing.

5320364.title: 街边的风
strings:
Your servant spotted that loud man again at market and rushed back to gossip with you.
He runs a small caravan, only four horses, and peddles foreign spices. The girl who loved him, the one who changed herself for him, was a slave girl at the spice shop next door... With that disguise and a few "necessary" tricks, she first made him fall in love, then persuaded him to buy her freedom and marry her as a free woman.
Yet she had been a slave girl, and he was a noble. True, she was skilled. She could distill perfumes; but he was the most insignificant sort of noble, with only two old servants at home... Still, he felt he ought not to have married a slave, especially one who didn't match the beauty he'd imagined. Even if he loved the girl and knew she was the best gift fate would grant him, he was furious at himself.
So, the night after their wedding, he raised that quarrel—his tonic for a wounded pride.
Now they run a business together. He paid her master, tore up her slave papers; she is free. She sits smiling before their own shop, blending perfumes—deft hands, a keen nose, and a sweet smile. Their trade grows better by the day.
Something is off.

You asked a servant—what of the oil the girl had used to fake ebony skin? Her maple-colored hair? Her lips plumped with honey...?
"Oh my lord, you were measuring ordinary folk by the standards of great nobles! What husband and wife could keep that up every day, unless they were the Sultan and his consort!" The servant's eyes went round. "Of course she looked just the same as before now! Pale skin, yellow hair, and hardly any flesh up front!"
You could not help a laugh.
The servant also gave you a bottle of perfume, a gift from the newlywed who had reverted to her original look; when she had stopped by earlier, she had remembered the servant's face.

5320365.title: 马尔基娜来找你
strings: Malkina awaited you at home; she seemed to have something to discuss.

5320367.title: 更深的塑造
strings: You already have an idea, so you call for Malkina.
Show her the face of Kindness.
Show her the face of Scoundrel.
Show her the face of Noble.
Show her the face of Chivalrous.

5320368.title: 善良的样子-不满足
strings: Your renown is too low to find a kind person.
Think again.

5320369.title: 恶名的样子-不满足
strings: Your infamy is too low to find a scoundrel.
Think again.

5320370.title: 权势的样子-不满足
strings: Your influence is too low to find a person with enough influence.
Think again.

5320371.title: 侠名的样子-不满足
strings: Your notoriety is too low to find a heroic person.
Think again.

5320372.title: 善良的样子-已完成
strings: The face of kindness has been shown enough—for now.
Think again.

5320373.title: 恶人的样子-已完成
strings: The face of a scoundrel has been shown enough—for now.
Think again.

5320374.title: 权势的样子-已完成
strings: The face of influence has been shown enough—for now.
Think again.

5320375.title: 强侠的样子-已完成
strings: The face of heroism has been shown enough—for now.
Think again.

5320376.title: 额外的问题
strings: As the talk drew to a close, she suddenly tossed you a question. "Do you think someone not quite kind can still be beautiful?" You consider how to answer...
Yes
No

You found her reasoning sound.
Beauty and ugliness were not objective standards; each person's "supreme beauty" differed. Perhaps an evil man would see beauty in wickedness, or a kind soul might be drawn to the grace of a sinner—what harm was there in that? Shouldn't people be free to praise what they found beautiful?
Hearing you, Malkina clapped with delight. She treated you to a full set of facial massage and essential oils; now you looked younger—and handsomer.

You judged that the allure of the wicked could not be called "beauty," for beauty calmed and called people toward goodness, while wicked charm leads the other way.
Malkina mulled your words and nodded repeatedly.
The conversation had taught her much.

5320377.title: 额外的问题
strings: After a while, she asked softly: "Was it this game that made you this way, [player.name]... or were you born so?"
It is my nature.
It is all for the game.

You smiled.
The game could not change you—or rather, you changed the game.
In Malkina's gaze flickered admiration, fear, and a hint of doubt.
You did not continue the topic.

You sighed, meeting Malkina's eyes with your weariness.
When the world around you had gone mad, what good was reason? All you could do was try to shield a small patch with your hands... and even that was very hard. You could not manage the rest—if malice flooded it, all you can do was pretend not to see.
Malkina nodded thoughtfully.

5320378.title: 某位取悦君主的女性……
strings: You ponder which consort to speak of in detail.
Zazie
Sadani
Ansuya
Fadia and Slave Girls

Zazie was the most favored beauty of the moment. That was, of course, chiefly because of her dazzling looks, but you had always felt another key reason for her favor was... she was, at bottom, somewhat like the Sultan himself.
She would sacrifice anyone to seize advantage; she knew exactly how to inflict pain and how to give pleasure; she had a rare instinct for power... If there was any difference between her and the Sultan, it lay perhaps in this: Zazie cared more about satisfying herself, and had far less interest in tormenting others.
You described in detail the outfits Zazie usually wore. Though she had new jewels and new robes every day, she always wore the gold crown that the Sultan had commissioned especially for her—a crown that flagrantly exceeded all bounds. Never in imperial history had any woman of the harem borne so much gold upon her head... yet Zazie said her neck never tired—"It's light as air! I could wear more!"
Malkina asked many questions about Zazie's makeup. Since you did not, in court, make a habit of staring at the Sultan's women's faces, you could only answer by feel. Even so, your answers pleased Malkina greatly.

Sadani—once the most favored, the sovereign's choicest fruit—had then plunged into the hell of rivalry.
You told Malkina that from Sadani you had learned what power looked like: when she was favored, she wore red and purple, setting off her most beautiful wine-violet hair; she wore rubies bigger than an ox's eye; the gold dust on her face ran down her neck. But once she fell from favor, her image shattered: the splendid jewels somehow no longer suited her; the heavy brocades always slipped from her shoulders... So what were these women of the harem truly fighting for? The sovereign's true heart—or that instant's whim that could be traded for power?
Malkina nodded again and again; she said many of her clients were much the same.
"When a man loved and doted on them, they dazzled; the moment that so-called love vanished, they withered like blades of grass robbed of sunlight!"
She wrote everything down, then thanked you solemnly, saying she had learned a great deal.

Ah, Ansuya—the Princess of a Fallen Kingdom, a pallid lotus. She had once roused the Sultan's pride and desire—just as her now-ruined homeland had. But what had the Sultan truly enjoyed? Was it the country and the princess, or the moment he let her father and brothers believe they were safe, only to crush them utterly? Surely what he savored was the despair and madness in men's eyes.
You told Malkina that, though you had never seen it yourself, the elders said Ansuya had entered the harem as a bride in a red robe studded with gems; as she stepped from the palanquin she found only a few maidservants to greet her, not her "husband". Then she was informed that every woman in this harem was the Sultan's slave; there was no mistress here, none above another, and the Sultan might sleep with whomever he pleased. Moreover, she was not allowed to conceive. It was said the proud princess laughed through her tears and tore her robe to shreds. Her dowry maids wept and tried to cover her body; their sobbing echoed long through the harem...
Malkina recorded the tale in detail and said she would look into the exact style of the princess's magnificent robe—once a symbol of power and later a byword for humiliation.

You spoke of the enormous number of slave girls in the Sultan's harem, among them Fadia, one of the few the sovereign occasionally brought before the royal court.
These slaves did not live in luxury: they emptied chamber pots, scrubbed floors, fetched and carried in the kitchens. Yet they seized every chance to cross the Sultan's path, baring their lovely bodies in hope of a moment's favor. Even those who were favored lived scarcely better lives, though they were allowed to own property, for the Sultan often tossed them rewards. Thus some plotted to save enough to buy their own freedom before they were too old to marry...
"When they redeemed themselves," Malkina asked, "did the Sultan's women cost more?"
You nodded. A slave who had been favored by the Sultan often had to pay one extra gold coin. Yes—she had been touched by the Sultan; perhaps he might wish to enjoy her again; therefore she must pay for such a phantom loss!
The matter left Malkina speechless with a bitter little laugh. Afterward she asked many more questions about the slaves' dress, grooming, and makeup, then thanked you gravely.

5320379.title: 某位持剑的铁卫……
strings: A Sword-Bearing Iron Guard...
Nabhani
Faris
Jabal
Seliman

Nabhani—the first swordsman of the royal city.
You had ever seen him truly apply himself only once: to earn the title "First of the City," which did his wandering among flowers a world of good.
Nabhani's pursuit of women verged on the absurd; with a studied nonchalance he fought down many thoughts in his heart... As for those thoughts, you did not care to say more before Malkina. Still, she must have heard how he cared for his hair and skin and how he trained that proud carriage. You dwelt particularly on his hair: whenever a new noble appeared in the Lapis Lazuli Palace, they could not help staring at Nabhani's hair for a long while—the intricate structure, the ingenious ornaments, truly a work of art.
Malkina giggled and nodded; she said meeting Nabhani was not too hard—she had many clients in high-class brothels; next time she would be sure to find a chance to study that famous mane closely.

Few knew much about Faris, for the Captain of the Cavalry almost never joined in any court affairs and would bolt the moment the sovereign vanished.
You described for Malkina how Faris dressed; like all cavalrymen, he carried the scent of beasts—mostly dogs. You described how that scatterbrained, careless Faris cut a splendid figure before his squadrons; when he hoisted the standard of the commander-general, he seemed to blaze.
You added that, to your eye, Faris kept his radiance and splendor banked most of the time; thus when he needed them, the contrast was stark. That too might be a way to wield power...
The thought inspired Malkina.

Jabal was the realm's most exalted warrior; across coup after coup his clan had always chosen the winning side.
You laughed as you described his usual dress and his unkempt look; yet even so, Jabal possessed immense power—a power not housed in his appearance, and yet somehow tied to them.
"I see what you mean..." Malkina murmured.
"Precisely because he had enough power, he dared present himself in such a slovenly state, isn't it?"
You nodded. Jabal cared not a whit what others thought of him; he stood outside the system. What others fought a lifetime—or generations—to earn was what he had at birth. He had mastered the finest way to treat power from the cradle: to ignore it.
Malkina pressed you about Jabal's exploits and his family's weapons and armor; she still seemed quite disapproving of the general's disregard for appearance.

Seliman was the most taciturn of the Iron Guard. He had once been Nabhani's strongest rival for "First Swordsman of the City."
This silent guard enjoyed the court's trust: he was upright, incorruptible, and never one to join the throng of courtiers at day's end to flirt with the ladies waiting in their carriages. It was said he scarcely cared for women; even if someone tried to gift him a beautiful slave, he would smile and decline.
Malkina found this "silent power" fascinating. She asked many questions about Sairiman's attire: could he project such pressure without a word because of his clothes? Did his coronet differ from others' due to the Sultan's taste?
Some questions you could answer; most, you could not. Yet that was enough: Malkina said, bright with interest, that she would find her own ways to learn more.

5320380.title: 某位掌权的老爷……
strings: A Minister in Power...
Nawfal
Abdul
Myself

Nawfal—your chief political opposition, the pale critic of the Lapis Lazuli Palace.
The very mention of him made your blood rise.
But Malkina would not let you off; she was intensely curious: how could a thin, foreign, pallid man come to radiate such power? She pestered you with questions!
What did Nawfal wear?
What jewels did he put on?
Did he use a staff? Ivory?
How big were his rings—bigger than yours?
What shoes did he wear?
How high was his collar?
...
On and on she went until your patience finally snapped—and you ended the conversation outright.

Abdul—the shrewdest manipulator of power in the Empire—the Vizier of this country; the Vasir of the Lapis Lazuli Palace.
You enumerated the "games" Abdul had played with power: the coin he cradled to himself, the tricks with which he hoodwinked the ministers, his boundless appetite for more...
Malkina listened intently, nodding. Her focus, however, was on Abde's hat. Only a Vasir might wear such an extravagant one, and each Vasir's differed. She asked whether such a hat made one appear more powerful.
Probably, you said. Strange, isn't it—how a man's power should be measured by the size of his hat?

Malkina looked at you, hoping you would speak of your own power—and you found youself at a loss.
Where could you begin? With your family? With your marriage to Maggie? With your standing forth to stop the Sultan's Game? With how you had been swept into madness—how you had become a wretch forever rushing to put out fires?
And yet you had gained something, hadn't you? These cards were both scepter and curse. Could you honestly say they'd brought you no joy at all?
After you had thought long and at last were about to speak, you found Malkina writing quickly.
"You don't need to say a word," she said. "You already look the part—crushed almost to breaking under power's weight, yet ready at any moment to seize it and strike your enemies down!"
She thanked you formally.

5320381.title: 内与外，人与神
strings:
马尔基娜来找你了，她心情似乎极好，嘴里哼着歌，手中抱着一大捆布料。
穿过庭院来到你面前之后，她行了一个漂亮的礼，而后，就把那些布都摊在了你的面前。
“我觉得这些比较适合神明！”
……哈？你听的一头雾水，而她则一拍脑门，大笑了起来。
“我忘了说前因后果了——您一定要原谅我，因为我太兴奋了！总之啊，托您的福，我觉得自己现在已经学会如何从里而外地塑造一个人了——所以，现在我想塑造更大的东西！”
你沉吟着，她的意思该不会是说……
“您就不好奇吗？不好奇神明是什么样子的吗？为什么祭司们要这么穿，为什么神的形象要是那样？说不定我也能把凡人打扮得跟神一样……说不定人们崇拜的说到底只是一副神圣的外壳！”
你小心地问她，这个“凡人”是……？
“当然是您啦！只要您点头，我就试试看怎么把您打扮成大家心目中的神！试试看吧——哦，您一定要点头，这一定超级好玩！”
你重重叹了口气……
要点头吗？
点头
摇头

You give a slight nod—and in that instant, Malkina lets out a cheer and throws herself at you!
"I knew you'd agree! I knew you were like me! That's why I followed you... why I showed up in this game! I've thought of so, so many ways—what should a god look like? I've studied how those temple styles—oh, I've done so much research!"
She pulls a few scrolls from the cloth and spreads them before you. The scrolls are covered with embroidery patterns of every kind, all in the traditional styles considered "sacred."
"Leave the clothes to me—but there are two things only you can do!"
You ask what they are.
"First, an attendant—no god can wander about alone; there has to be an entourage. You must find an attendant. I'll dress that person too, and then you two will appear together!"
...Fine, and the second thing?
"Power! A god must have might, right? You can't rely on appearances alone!"
The moment you begin to seriously consider this, Malkina sees the light hidden deep within your heart...
She is startled for only a second—then she lights up like a blazing torch with excitement.
"No seamstress or cosmetician has ever done this—they only ever shape a mortal body. But I—oh heavens—I am going to shape a god! Isn't that the pinnacle of craft? I can't imagine anything happier... Thank you, thank you!"
She kisses your cheek and prostrates herself.
As for you... now you have to consider how to become a god.

You shake your head and refuse the absurd proposal. You have already walked too far down the path toward godhood, and you fear this will be the final step...
Malkina is clearly devastated. In her eyes, you lack courage, ability, ambition!
In the midst of your struggle with her, she accidentally catches a glimpse of the divinity buried deep within your gaze! It frightens her badly. When you try to explain that mortals are exactly as timid, incapable, and unremarkable as yourself, she leaves the room on her knees.

5320382.title: 访圣
strings:
That night, Malkina comes to visit.
After dismissing the servants, she suddenly falls to her knees before you.
"You have allowed me to accomplish an unimaginable feat. I will never forget how men bowed to the image I shaped."
No matter how you try to persuade her, she refuses to rise. Later, you realize she is weeping for sheer joy...
After a long while, she wipes away her tears, stands up, and embraces you. She solemnly pledges that you can regard her as your most reliable friend.

5320383.title: 百科全书--阿萨尔
strings: Asal died. There was no one left who could compile that great Encyclopedia.

5320384.title: 百科全书--全收集
strings:
Asal was overjoyed when he found you, clutching a thick volume—but it turned out to be nothing more than the table of contents for the entire set.
"Done—done! I had seen every book, every marvel in the world! With my own eyes—thanks to you!"
He suddenly flung his arms about you and sobbed, barely able to get a sentence out. You awkwardly comforted him for a long time; at last, sated with tears, he gave you the deepest bow in embarrassment and presented the contents as thanks... Yes—divorced from the Encyclopedia itself it meant nothing, but it was proof of the world's wisdom and knowledge, a treasure that could prove useful in extraordinary moments.

5320385.title: 权的总结
strings:
You asked Malkina whether she had distilled anything of the face of power.
Smiling, Malkina brought out paints and fabrics and dabbed here and there on you as she spoke.
"Power is confidence, isn't it? The more confident you are, the more power you hold—and only the confident can truly maintain it. Otherwise, even if you get it, you cannot keep it. I learned that from your stories. So—flatten the brows, relax the expression, a touch of boredom and a touch of alertness... Make the back hem longer than the front, since you don't bow often but must stand tall... Ah, and not too many jewels, but each one must be precious; and makeup light, tones gentle..."
When she finished, you looked in the mirror and found the person there truly looked like someone who had spent too long in the Lapis Lazuli Hall...

5320386.title: 内与外，人与神
strings: You had perfectly completed Malkina's commission; her face glowed and she seemed on the verge of bursting with things to say—clearly, more awaited you.

5320390.title: 游猎会
strings:
Gullis likes to tilt his head back and gaze at the sky. When flocks of birds pass overhead, joy brightens his expression.
One of your servants tells you that Gullis often shared hunting tales with them. He seems quite an accomplished hunter... Perhaps you could host a Grand Hunt—Gullis might bring you a pleasant surprise.

5320392.title: 用来关闭游猎会
strings: He stands there, as if he won't move on without an answer.
Very well. Come on.
What are you thinking?
"I knew there was more to you than meets the eye." You draw your weapon with a smile, and tell Gullis to ready himself. His eyes light up.

After that incident, I spare your lowly life not so you can provoke your own master. Do your work, slave. Otherwise, I will show no more mercy than your former master.
Gullis bows slightly and no longer insists. In silence, he turns and continues scouting ahead. You fail to find the bear, but you unexpectedly bring down a large stag instead... This catch adds considerable prestige to your Grand Hunt.

5320393.title: 游猎之后
strings:
When you wake again, you are in your bedchamber. The servants anxiously keep watch at your side, and finally breathe in relief when they see your eyes open.
They tell you that it is Gullis who carried you out. He even returned with men to retrieve the tiger's carcass—because "it is my master's catch."
You look toward the proud slave; he turns his face away, refusing to meet your gaze.
You seem to have won his genuine respect—not the respect given to a master, but the respect one man gives to another.

5320394.title: 古利斯-虎皮献给苏丹后
strings: The Sultan is well pleased with the tiger skin you offer. Yet the very next day, his pride drives him to the hunt in person. He returns with his own prize and sends you what, in his judgment, you most require—carefully packed within a bloodied casket. Hmm... that is the tiger's potency, freshly taken, and cures your pretended impotence that same evening. Offer your gratitude for the Sultan's generosity!

5320395.title: 游猎之后
strings:
When you wake again, you are in your bedchamber. The servants anxiously keep watch at your side, and finally breathe in relief when they see your eyes open.
They tell you that it is Gullis who carried you out. He even returned with men to retrieve the tiger's carcass—because "it is my master's catch."
You look toward the proud slave. He is smiling at you now—a smile that looks nothing like one belonging to a slave.

5320396.title: 借一步说话
strings:
Seliman draws you aside.
"That plate of scales on the Serpent-King's neck—the largest, the fairest—you won't mind if I skin it off, will you?"
By rights, all trophies of The Grand Hunt are yours—and your slave worked for it too—but...
Do you mind?
As you wish—you took the kill.
No.

He is overjoyed, almost about to embrace you and kiss you. You hurriedly drag him back to the crowd and have the servants remove that scale for the esteemed Honor Guard. Cradling the scale in his hands, he offers profuse thanks before taking his leave.
You shoot Gullis a displeased glance, then refuse Seliman. He seems downcast, but quickly hides it again.

5320397.title: 宫中的传闻
strings: Word spreads through the palace that Concubine Sadani has obtained a rare jewel—a vast and beautiful serpent scale... She flaunts it everywhere, leaving the other concubines seething with envy.

5320398.title: 奴隶阿本分
strings: You saw Jabal hand the Gold Coins to Gullis with your own eyes; Gullis then brought them to you, and, as his master, it is yours to decide what becomes of them.
They're yours.
Hand them over.
You tell Gullis this is earned by his own bravery, and he has the right to decide what to do with the money. He seems a little surprised, but quickly regains his composure. Then he bows to you.
Gullis obediently hands over the gold coins, his face blank.

5320399.title: 古利斯地兴趣
strings: Since you have filled Gullis's purse with gold coins and left him idle, he decides to go find some amusement... and not to stop until every coin is spent.

5320400.title: 古利斯地兴趣-夜酒
strings: Gullis is a great favorite at a low tavern. He even takes part in a fierce brawl—and comes out the winner.

5320401.title: 古利斯地兴趣-赌狗
strings: Gullis went to the Dog Track...
You wretch.
He returns in high spirits and even shares a gold coin with you.

5320402.title: 古利斯地兴趣-赌狗
strings: Gullis went to the Dog Track...
You wretch.

And he comes back dejected.
One look at his face is enough—you do not even need to ask whether he won.

5320403.title: 古利斯地兴趣-欢愉
strings:
Well, Gullis certainly won't miss the House of Delights...
He enjoys himself, but remains cautious. Even in bed, he keeps a tight watch on his money pouch.

5320404.title: 古利斯地兴趣-浴场
strings:
Gullis enjoys the bathhouse services like a true noble. Even he cannot deny that this urban leisure of soaking in steaming water... is rather intriguing.
By the time he returns, he is polished to a radiant shine.

5320405.title: 古利斯地兴趣-闲逛
strings:
Gullis went wandering. It costs nothing to stroll around. But with empty pockets, it's hardly enjoyable.
He was having a fine time until a child bumped into him...
—A thief!

Gullis reacts at once. Without checking his purse, he twists back and seizes the little pickpocket's wrist.
Amid the commotion, a raspy-voiced old thief chuckles and presses Gullis's shoulder...
"All right, all right, I'll pay you back... heh... Aren't you from Lord [player.name]'s house? We're friends—friends... Let go, my friend."
The old thief treats Gullis with a generous round of drinks as an apology, and both sides leave satisfied.

5320406.title: 古利斯地兴趣-闲逛
strings:
Gullis went wandering. It costs nothing to stroll around. But with empty pockets, it's hardly enjoyable.
He was having a fine time until a child bumped into him...
—A thief!

Gullis reacts at once. Without checking his purse, he twists back and seizes the little pickpocket's wrist.
The pickpocket screams and struggles, but it is useless. Gullis breaks his hand—this is the customary punishment the highlanders give to thieves.

5320407.title: 古利斯地兴趣-闲逛
strings:
Gullis went wandering. It costs nothing to stroll around. But with empty pockets, it's hardly enjoyable.
He was having a fine time until a child bumped into him...

....It is over. Gullis reaches into his pocket and finds the purse gone.
He slinks home in low spirits, having lost the funds to continue his "interests."

5320408.title: 教育扎齐伊
strings: Zaki stares wide-eyed, as if waiting for your praise.
Well done
Shake head

You praise Zaki generously and tell him he will make a remarkable noble—a remarkable man.
He stares at you wide-eyed, pride and joy surging within him, almost enough to lift him off the ground.

You coldly tell Zaki that once they leave, those hunters will surely catch up with the bear and slaughter both it and its cub. All they have done is give the beast a futile hope and prolong its suffering a little longer.
Zaki stands frozen, nearly in tears...
You pat his shoulder again and murmur softly: next time, if he truly wishes to protect the bear, he should push the hunters into the trap and bury them. Is that not so?
Kindness demands a price—paid by you, or by another.
He stares at you wide-eyed... and it is clear he understands.

5320409.title: 母熊的谢礼
strings:
You receive a parcel together with a letter from Fatuna.
"My thanks to you on behalf of the mother bear—and for the lesson you have given my son."
Inside the package lies a beautiful bracelet, engraved with a mother bear playing with her cub. The piece appears quite old. Perhaps, the reason Zaki made that decision is that, as a child, he once saw this very image resting on his mother's wrist.

5320410.title: 古利斯的工作
strings:
You realize that Gullis is an "untrained" slave. He doesn't know how to deal with city dwellers, can offend passing nobles with a glance, and constantly gives off a feral air. When you ask him to keep a lower profile, he instead looks like an assassin.
Perhaps you should send him out often with other servants and learn how to handle the ways of this urban world.

5320412.title: 可疑的钱币
strings:
Another strange gold coin finds its way into your pocket.
You study the Sultan's profile stamped upon the reverse, wondering... who could have made this?

5320414.title: 小圆声望事件--梦中之狼
strings:
Inal comes home in a panic, telling you she saw the wolf of her dream.
 
It happened while she was at the market buying ingredients – while picking a fat duck. "A duck must have plump wings to be tasty, then I opened the wings to inspect... oh, sorry master, I digress... then he appeared! He looked like a wolf... his eyes were glowing green! He stared at me, asked whose family I belonged to! I was terrified, I... I dropped the duck and ran home! Thankfully I hadn't paid for it yet... I brought back all the money – oh, master, what should I do, things from dreams are coming out!" She gesticulates frantically, tears on her face, visibly panicked. 

Just as you consider how to comfort her, you notice the large slave, Aziz, seems to be quietly eavesdropping from outside the courtyard.
Aziz seems to have something to say?
Call Maggie to comfort her
Distract her

You call Aziz over. Without needing to say a word, Aziz seems to naturally understand what needs to be done. His massive figure follows behind Inal, matching her pace, like a gentle giant dog. You can't hear their whispered conversation, but from afar, you notice Inal's expression relaxes significantly.

Handing over the authority of handling household affairs to the mistress is a sign of respect towards her. Maggie listens to you and nods. She supports Inal by the shoulder and accompany her as they walk out slowly. Once they've finished their talk, you can find out what actually happened.

To relieve tension, the best way is to distract yourself, do something else. You pat Inal on the head and tell her she can freely buy something she likes with the money originally set aside for groceries. Once she's feeling better, she can tell you what really happened.

Her sobbing stops, and she shows a hesitant expression. A slave probably rarely has the chance to receive such a reward... She kneels to thank you and suddenly dashes out, having thought of something.

5320420.title: 移除誓言之证的情况
strings:
The final rightful heir to the Highland Realm—the star-blessed prince—has passed from this world. The sacred contracts once inscribed with binding vows are now nothing but waste paper, smeared by the lines of a hand.
You no longer possess the rightful cause to move against the Sultan in an old country's name.

5320421.title: 移除誓言之证的情况
strings: Sirshana has fallen! The Star-Souled failed to protect their prince! Though you may yet possess the strength to continue the struggle, those who rallied under the banner of their homeland have completely lost the courage to rebel...

5320501.title: 再利用
strings: Mahir recently had a brilliant idea She is just short of some investment to put it into practice. She waits eagerly outside your study, wanting to talk to you about her idea. What concerns you slightly is her insistence that the discussion must take place without any others except you... and she also carries a large box with her... which seems to be vibrating slightly.
There's no one else, come in
Let's talk about it next time...
You don't want to be alone with this somewhat madness person and her mysterious giant box, so you politely declined her request.

5320502.title: 没别人，进来吧
strings:
Mahir hurriedly dragged the box into your room, and something that made you even more worried happened – the box emitted a foul smell and strange goo was dripping from it...
She closed the door and turned to you with a bright smile.
“I have discovered a technology for reusing humans!”
Before you could ponder what "reusing humans" meant, she abruptly opened the box and inside appeared... a human corpse. The corpse was already half decomposed, with plump maggots crawling in and out of the tendons and skin.
She grabbed your hand, trying to make you touch the corpse, you –
Desperately resist
Just touch it

Asking you to reach into such a thing might as well be asking you to die — you push Mahir away, standing up, and instinctively look for a weapon to defend yourself.
However, she ignores you and inserts her hand into the hole in the corpse's skin, muttering things like “Why can't you touch this,” “He was a dignified person not long ago,” and so on, all while rummaging in the corpse's chest cavity. You feel so disgusted that you are almost about to throw up...
Finally, she pulls out her hand and shows you a strange brass device, pulsing rhythmically like a heart.
“I used an aether bottle, borrowed from the Righteous Path's church, and mounted it in my exclusive bi-directional semi-fluid tube, simulating the motion of a heart, but it's metal and won't rot!” She becomes more and more excited as she speaks, pulling your hand around the chest cavity, “Should I can connect the other blood vessels and muscles, then alive, it shall be alive!”
Then, she eagerly grabs your shoulder with her slimy hand.
“I need more corpses to complete the invention, you will help me, right? Wealth unimaginable awaits us both!”
You just can't bring yourself to pry her dirty hands off, so you twist your body to avoid the dirtiest part while trying hard to think...

Gritting your teeth, closing your eyes, you harden your resolve! Following her force, you reach down. After the initial slimy, disgusting sensation, she pulls your hand further in, and you suddenly touch something warm... In the heart area of this decayed corpse, the originally putrid flesh is gone, replaced by a beating metal device.
