She laughed coldly and opened her hands. "Or did you hear some tragic tale and want to give us more coins? I won't refuse that." You told her you mean no harm—at least not in your asking—only curiosity. "Then I must ask a favor in return." Arms folded, Raed stared at you. "Never speak of this to anyone."
I will keep the secret.
We'll see.

You nodded and told her you would never tell anyone, because you knew it might cost Raed her life. You also warned her that though she had concealed her noble schooling from childhood very well, her movements and posture still bore traces—about velvet carpets, about the curtsies of the nobility.
Raed was silent. After a while, she drew a dagger, touched its blade to her own brow, and then handed it to you. "This is a token that we now share this secret... that I have entrusted it to you."

You told Raed you could not do that—because you needed her to serve you in return for your silence. If one day you judged her service wanting, you would hand her and her vagrants to the Sultan; you guessed he would take quite an interest in his half-sister—perhaps an interest not limited to taking off her head. Raed stared at you for a long time, then let out a soft laugh. "Fine. That's as it should be—people should use one another; whatever you say." She gave you a dagger as a token—symbol that you now knew her secret... and from then on she was in your hand.

5321224.title: 令人不愉快的刺探-拉伊德入队
strings: Some trust had grown between you and Raed—on that basis you could direct her, but do not forget: what she cared about most was still the vagrants.

5321225.title: 消除一个苏丹的猜忌
strings: In light of your merit in presenting the Gold Dagger, some of the Sultan's suspicion of you ebbed.

5321226.title: 拉伊德离队
strings: You never found Raed again... Had she been killed along with the vagrants? Or had she fled with the survivors—leaving you and this game behind? Either way, it no longer mattered.

5321227.title: 无赖租客-拉伊德入队
strings: Since you were still willing to help the vagrants, Raed was also willing to serve you... a fair trade.

5321228.title: 拉伊德查无此人
strings: You had told the Sultan of a tempting toy, and he could not have it! Without Raed, he could only vent his disappointment and anger on you—consider yourself lucky; it could have been worse.

5321230.title: 稀疏的禁忌
strings:
Arzuna comes to see you.
"I heard you drew a Sultan Card—a Carnality Card that perfectly matches my rank." Your sister sits on the sofa, back straight, her ten slender fingers interlaced with deliberate precision, her posture as if carefully arranged. "I am here to tell you this—the Card is why I came. Remember? I am here to help you, my only brother, my blood. I won't blame you. After all, this is all for survival. How could I bear to watch you be beheaded?"
Her gaze is warm, gentle and open. Its intensity makes you look away.
Between siblings, between blood relatives... You know the taboo, yet she has said it is all for survival...

5321232.title: 阿图娜尔纵欲卡后续
strings:
Rumors quietly find their way to the Sultan's ears, suggesting that when you obtained a dancer of rare beauty, you failed to present her to the Sultan, but instead kept her for your own enjoyment...
In the days that follow, the Sultan's expression toward you remains noticeably dark.

5321233.title: 你我之间
strings:
That night, as you snuff out the lamp in your study and prepare to rest, a slender hand presses against your chest, forcing you gently back toward the desk. "Dear brother," Arzuna murmurs, her eyes kindled by the moonlight, flickering with some dark flame. "My dearest brother, don't you think we have been apart for too long?"
Her fingers circle idly over your chest, her gaze lingering upon your face... Is it love, or a twisted desire? In the moonlight all things appear painfully clear—yet you cannot truly see it.

5321236.title: 深沉的失望
strings: You truly believe what you and Arzuna have done could remain hidden from Maggie? She's deeply disappointed with you!

5321237.title: 无言的失望
strings: You truly believe what you and Arzuna have done could remain hidden from Maggie? She now has nothing left to say to you.

5321242.title: 树顶的月亮
strings:
Arzuna is a remarkable dancer—something you recognize from the very first time she visits you. She once said she would gladly dance for you on an appropriate occasion.
And on this night, before the feast begins, a bright moon rests gently above the tree, and a cool breeze drifts through the courtyard. It occurs to you that perhaps now is precisely an "appropriate" occasion.

5321243.title: 贵族的邀请
strings:
Arzuna's enchanting performance at the moonlit banquet quickly earns her widespread fame. Not long afterward, a nobleman sends you a polite and respectful letter, requesting to "borrow your dancer for a performance."
His politeness is clearly directed toward you. The nobles seem to assume quite naturally that the dancer is your household slave. Thus the request is made to you alone, without sparing a thought for Arzuna's content.

5321244.title: 梅姬的主意
strings:
Finding you entirely unmoved, Buthayna shifted her efforts toward Maggie. Somehow, they succeed in convincing her, and before long Maggie comes to speak with you.
If it is unsuitable for Arzuna to appear in the House of Delights, then why not invite the girls to your own residence instead? In that way, no one could blame Arzuna. And for nobles, inviting entertainers to a banquet is perfectly customary.
...To be honest, summoning Ladies of Delights to your own estate is something you would never have dared to imagine—had Maggie not proposed it herself.

5321245.title: 求求你
strings: Nothing that happens in the House of Delights ever escapes Nabhani! He appears at your gate, begging in exaggerated humility and throwing a tantrum, determined to attend this most unusual ball at your residence, no matter what it takes...

5321248.title: 一个奇怪的请求
strings:
Arzuna comes to you, her familiar, well-practiced smile still upon her lips, though her expression is touched with gravity.
She offers you a solemn bow, and then asks whether you might accompany her to a certain place.
"This place may bring you discomfort—perhaps even anger. I would rather not visit... Will you come with me?"

5321249.title: 一封信
strings:
An unfamiliar lady arrives at your door, bringing with her a letter. While traveling from the frontier with her husband on their way to the capital for an audience, they encountered a dancer along the road. Upon hearing of their destination, the dancer asked them to deliver this letter to you, offering an unforgettable dance in gratitude.
You host a banquet to receive the lady and question her carefully about the dancer. At last, you open the letter. Its message is brief:
"The world is beautiful. Thank you. —Arzuna"

5321251.title: 旅行的妹妹2
strings:
A fur trader comes to visit you, bringing a short message written at Arzuna's request:
"I am well and happy. I have learned a dance performed upon the decks of ships. The merchant delivering this message still owes me the payment for a dance—remember to claim it from him."
You inform this messenger about the payment. He lets out an awkward laugh. While repeatedly praising Arzuna's dancing, he offers you a finely crafted pair of fur boots as payment.

5321252.title: 旅行的妹妹2
strings:
A fur trader comes to visit you, bringing a short message written at Arzuna's request:
"I am well and happy. I have learned a dance performed upon the decks of ships. The merchant delivering this message still owes me the payment for a dance—remember to claim it from him."
You give the merchant a small reward, and he departs in high spirits.

5321253.title: 旅行的妹妹3
strings:
To your surprise, the fellow you previously sent to accompany Arzuna on her travels returns alone.
It is said that Arzuna employed a small trick and left him behind at an official post station, together with a message: "That lord has already shown me more kindness than I deserve, but you need not choose the same path as I have. Perhaps he has a greater need of you. So do not complain—go back."
You cannot help but feel both amused and speechless... yet perhaps this is for the best. And during the time spent traveling with Arzuna, the man's abilities have improved considerably.

5321254.title: 旅行的妹妹3
strings:
A frontier soldier comes to visit you. Having just completed his rotation and returned to the capital, he encountered Arzuna along the way, who entrusted him with a message for you.
"I am far away from you now, yet I feel closer to you than ever before, for I have never sent so many messages to another, nor have I ever wished for anyone else to know where I am."
The soldier offers you a salute and refuses your reward, saying that Miss Arzuna's dance is already the greatest payment.

5321255.title: 旅行的妹妹4
strings:
Arzuna makes a public visit to your land under the title of "Lord [player.name]'s sister," and everywhere along her route she is greeted with enthusiasm. Stages rise in the town squares, and dancers from among the people come forward one by one to join her in dance.
The shared dancing soon becomes popular in every place she visits. Dancing, singing, and laughter—the people delight in it, and your land grows somewhat more prosperous as a result.
"At last, this place will no longer return to me only with memories of pain and tears." She sends these words to you in a letter, accompanied by a bouquet of dried flowers, perhaps wishing to share with you this joyful and fragrant passage of time.

5321256.title: 旅行的妹妹4
strings:
Arzuna returns to your land, the place where she was born. Stages rise in the town squares, and dancers from among the people gather to dance. Among them is Arzuna herself, dancing, singing, and laughing. Who would not cherish such joyful days?
"At last, this place will no longer return to me only with memories of pain and tears." She sends these words to you in a letter.

5321257.title: 旅行的妹妹5
strings:
A spice caravan visits your guesthouse, leaving behind a large parcel of dried, richly cured fish along with a letter written at Arzuna's request:
"I'm staying for a time on an island. The people here dance in skirts woven from grass, their hair mingling with the hems like the tide in motion. I am truly happy here. The fish I send is a local delicacy and is very delicious. Here, every child must catch such a fish by hand upon reaching adulthood. This one I caught myself, and I sent it to you as a gift. —Arzuna"

5321258.title: 旅行的妹妹5
strings:
A messenger brings you a letter from Arzuna, wherein she describes a marvelous dish: simply vegetables, strips of dried meat, and beans stir-fried over a great flame. Wandering dancers and actors of traveling companies are said to enjoy this humble food while journeying from place to place. Amid the songs of poets, beneath the glow of firelight, and after one exhilarating dance after another, even such ordinary foods taste wondrously good.
"Perhaps happiness is its richest seasoning," she writes.

5321259.title: 旅行的妹妹6
strings:
A veiled dancer, wearing anklets adorned with small bells, comes to you.
She offers you a graceful bow before delivering Arzuna's message:
"I am healthy and happy now. Today, I dance under the sun with many other dancers, unable to fall asleep even at night, for I feel simply overjoyed. Thank you, [player.name], my brother."
"There is one more message she wishes me to pass along," the dancer continues. "Might there be someone in your household who knows how to play the drum?"
Judging by her manner, she seems eager to perform a dance for you!

5321260.title: 旅行的妹妹6
strings:
A veiled dancer, wearing anklets adorned with small bells, comes to you.
She offers you a graceful bow before delivering Arzuna's message:
"I am healthy and happy now. Today, I dance under the sun with many other dancers, unable to fall asleep even at night, for I feel simply overjoyed. Thank you, [player.name], my brother."

5321268.title: 野心的果实
strings:
When you returned home from the palace that day, Arzuna was waiting for you in the reception hall.
She was dressed in full regalia, her hair elaborately braided, her face painted more gorgeously than usual. She looked up at you with a mysteriously knowing smile...
"I've realized something, my dear Lord [player.name]. I know how you should use me... Send me to the Sultan. You will have an ally, a supporter, a follower, a servant in the sovereign's harem—trust me, I can capture his heart. Oh, I've always been good at this!"
You were startled by her ambition, but after calming down, you studied her and realized her charm was indeed irresistible. Perhaps she really could satisfy the Sultan...
What do you say?
Agree
Oppose

Think of it this way: if one of the Sultan's concubines stands with you, those who oppose you will find it difficult to voice their objections. Besides, ever since Arzuna came, your household has rarely been at ease. Perhaps sending her away is not a bad solution...
You agree to her request, though you caution her that powerful courtiers often offer beauties to their ruler. Yet once the beauty enters the harem, she must depend upon her own wit and capability.
She lowers her head obediently, saying she knows this well. Still... "If you might smooth the way for me a little, it would be better. After all, who knows the Sultan's tastes more thoroughly than you, my lord?"
Indeed, the woman you present must neither seem shabby nor prove herself lacking in propriety...

After much consideration, you refuse her.
The harem is a place of tangled alliances and rivalries. She is only a dancer, untrained in such intrigues, and she cannot even read. Sending her there would likely bring you greater trouble.
There is also another concern you do not speak aloud—you still worry whether this suddenly appeared sister harbors resentment toward you. If she does, placing her at the Sultan's side would be far too dangerous...
Arzuna says nothing. She simply smiles, bids you farewell, and then takes her leave. The smile leaves you deeply uneasy.

5321270.title: 石宫斗触发
strings: You know that the Sultan's harem is far from a safe haven. You know even better what awaits your sister, who has sold herself into slavery: her striking beauty and figure would bring her coldness, jealousy, and quiet cruelty. Perhaps you should help her—whether out of the last trace of compassion bound by blood, or perhaps for the sake of benefits that may arise in the future. After all, what use might a slave girl placed within the harem hold for a powerful courtier such as yourself?

5321271.title: 铜宫斗触发
strings: Now Arzuna formally enters the Sultan's harem. Though she receives no title and no one addresses her as a concubine, her circumstances are already better than those of the countless unnamed slave girls who spend their days in endless drudgery. Yet flowers have always struggled eagerly for the light of the sun, and those within the harem are no different. Perhaps you should pay closer attention to her circumstances. After all, at this stage, even without the ties of kinship, a woman who gains even a measure of the Sultan's favor may still serve your interests.

5321272.title: 银宫斗触发
strings: Rumors about Concubine Arzuna spread with sudden intensity. People mockingly call her a prostitute, an illiterate woman, a vulgar beauty who pleases men with the sway of her hips. Some even boast that a handful of gold coins would be enough to purchase her charms, as though they had truly laid hands upon a woman of the Sultan. The talk unsettles you greatly. After all, you are the one who sent her into the harem—or at least she once lived beneath your roof before entering it. Damaging her reputation likewise damages your own. Perhaps you should not remain indifferent to this matter.

5321273.title: 妃子的礼物
strings:
Concubine Arzuna sends a gift from the harem—an honor granted only to those women who are especially favored by the Sultan.
When you open the exquisite silk wrapping, a generous cascade of fragrant petals pours out. The eunuch messenger explains that Concubine Arzuna gathers them each morning outside her chambers and dries them by her own hand.
"She says the petals may be steeped as tea. Such tea brings cheer and restrains impulses toward killing, violence, and wrongdoing," the eunuch recites stiffly, seeming not in the least aware of the peculiarity of his words. "She says all this is owed to your assistance. These are the words the honored Concubine Arzuna instructs me to deliver."

5321274.title: 金宫斗触发
strings:
At last, Concubine Arzuna can hold her head high before Zazie.
Their chambers stand together, for each evening the Sultan visits either one or the other. Roses flourish before Zazie's chamber, while on Arzuna's side, eunuchs and servants work through the night to plant graceful pomegranate trees, adorning the small garden of this newly favored concubine.
What lies ahead is a fierce contest between Arzuna and the woman most skilled in pleasing the Sultan throughout the empire. Zazie honors her rival and prepares to meet her with all her strength. From this day forward, she will remember that you once stood behind her enemy.
Between these two favored women, you can clearly choose only one side.

5321279.title: 贬斥
strings:
A eunuch brings a bound slave girl to your house and lifts her veil. Before you stands the former favored woman, her once-beautiful face now cruelly branded with the marks of slavery. She struggles violently, but the moment your eyes meet hers, she freezes, and glares at you with fierce hatred, like a mother beast at bay.
The eunuch speaks: "She was meant to die, but for your sake, she is returned to you. This is what Zazie commands me to tell you."
Well, in any case, at least her life is spared.

5321283.title: 流浪的果实
strings:
Arzuna comes to you with unusual solemnity. Since you first met her, this is the first time her face shows such resolve and seriousness.
"I must confess something, [player.name]," she begins. She no longer uses her sweet voice to call you "brother," nor does she sway her body deliberately as she sits before you. "At first, I came to you for revenge. I sought to use you to reach those in power—even the Sultan himself—and then wield that power against you. The only way I knew to take revenge was through flattery, pleasing, using, and servility... My mother taught me nothing else."
She looks straight into your eyes and continues: "But now, I no longer want to do this. I will not explain why—you will understand. If you do not, it means you are one of those who do good without knowing it, like a figure from a fairy tale—and I cannot harm someone like you. Anyway, I may still harbor hatred for you, for I have spent many years immersed in hatred toward you and your family, and my mother made me swear on her deathbed to continue hating you. But I will not take revenge. You may rest assured, you will not have an enemy who dances well and shares half your blood."
She bows. The jingling of her ornaments rings around her, and you notice she seems dressed for travel.
"Now, I intend to depart. Having abandoned revenge, I must find a new purpose, one to live for myself." She smiles, delighted with her idea. "I want to be a traveling dancer, like those I saw as a child—dancing while wandering, experiencing every dance on this continent, dancing with every dancer I meet... Perhaps I will return, or perhaps my journey will never end, but I will remain free, always immersed in what I love, always happy."
She pauses, smiling at you with a pure, heartfelt expression. "Farewell, brother."

5321285.title: 玫瑰的刺
strings: Arzuna's victory left Zazie utterly humiliated. She will not withdraw so easily and accept this unmistakable defeat. If she lacked the courage to stake everything on a final gamble, how could she have long occupied the king's favor?

5321286.title: 玫瑰的提示
strings: Arzuna's victory left Zazie utterly humiliated. You are certain she would not withdraw so easily and accept this uncommon defeat, and you even fear she might strike at Arzuna—but she does not. The woman who has lost her favor takes no more drastic action. She merely sends you a brief note: "For your sake."

5321287.title: 宫中支持者
strings:
Arzuna earns the king's praise and favor, and that same day she sets an exquisite banquet in the garden, summoning a number of courtiers. The act is improper—but when the Sultan favors a woman, her whims become the court's new order.
Your name is also on the list, and you have no choice but to go.
You arrive earlier than most. By the stream in the garden, you encounter Arzuna. Surrounded by her maidservants and eunuchs, she looks every inch the noble beauty. She stares you for a long while, then suddenly says, "I hate you, [player.name]."
"I had meant to take fierce revenge on you... I meant to become the most powerful woman alive and spend that power on vengeance. Those who wounded and shamed my mother were to answer for it. Only then would I be released from the oath she forced me to swear." She idly turns the bracelets at her wrists, her voice growing low. "But you... Why do you always help me? Each time... cruel fate befalls me in the harem—you are there. It makes no sense. Even if my rise as a favored woman might benefit you, you did not have to..."
You remain silent, and she does the same for a long while.
"I have never thought of you as a brother, yet you truly seem to treat me as a sister. I am just a lowly dancer, an illegitimate daughter who should never have been born..." She exhales softly, as if she might laugh or weep. But in the end, she only shakes her head and accepts the gold hookah a eunuch offers. "Perhaps you simply require a supporter in the palace. Very well—I will aid you. But only once."
You are about to object when the other courtiers arrive. The banquet begins, and the matter is left where it stands. Arzuna smiles and speaks lightly with everyone—including you. It is a banquet in celebration of victory, and no one raises a word that might spoil the mood.

5321288.title: 舞姬的帮助——谋反阶段
strings:
At the moment you make up your mind, you quietly pass your intention to your most formidable friend in the harem. Not long after, at the very height of your tension, Arzuna's attendant delivers you a modest cloth packet. "Please open it in private," the eunuch says, offering a bow before withdrawing.
Within lies a slender ring. You have seen it on the Sultan's hand. With the slightest lift of that hand, the Sultan can erase countless enemy generals, assassins, lurking threats, and anyone who displeases him. And now, though you have no idea of Arzuna's thoughts and purpose, nor of the means by which she accomplishes it, the ring lies silently in your open palm.

5321289.title: 舞姬的帮助——信物
strings:
At the moment you make up your mind, you quietly pass your intention to your most formidable friend in the harem. Not long after, at the very height of your tension, Arzuna's attendant delivers you a modest cloth packet. "Please open it in private," the eunuch says, offering a bow before withdrawing.
Within lies a thin slip of paper. It is not written by Arzuna. Instead, it shows a concealed mechanism set into the palace walls—likely used by certain eunuchs to smuggle forbidden goods into the harem. It could serve your army just as effectively.

5321294.title: 发放孩子们
strings: Images of the children you once helped surface in your thoughts. Perhaps... they might serve as suitable examples?

5321295.title: 发放所有书
strings: The books you have studied and the knowledge you have gathered surface in your thoughts, each becoming a reference for the act of creation.

5321297.title: 羊肉炉臣服线结局—百科全书

ending_0.title: Ending Title
strings: Ending Title
All Sultan Cards have been resolved. The game has ended.

ending_1.title: Walking with the Tiger
strings: Walking with the Tiger
You died from provoking the Sultan
Not funny. The Sultan executes you like the jester you are.

ending_2.title: Eternal Slumber
strings: Eternal Slumber
The one who loved you most slew you
In Maggie's embrace, you were granted eternal rest.

ending_3.title: Overconfidence
strings: Overconfidence
Next time, refrain from provoking those beyond your station
You died in a duel. a death befitting a warrior, at least.

ending_4.title: Retribution
strings: Retribution
As the blade opened up your heart, was there a sliver of remorse to be found?
You died from an assassination.

ending_5.title: Ultimate Pleasure
strings: Ultimate Pleasure
Junah’s bed became your velvet coffin.
You were joyous as if ascending to the heavens, but never returned.

ending_6.title: Ultimate Pleasure
strings: Ultimate Pleasure
Junah’s bed became your velvet coffin.
You were joyous as if ascending to the heavens, but never returned.

ending_7.title: YOU DIED
strings: YOU DIED
Next time for sure
The Sultan is dead, you won.

ending_8.title: Walking with the Tiger
strings: Walking with the Tiger
The Sultan's will cannot be defied
You died from provoking the Sultan.

ending_9.title: Love's Embrace
strings: Love's Embrace
You died from some expectation that should not have arisen
You could not even discern the identity of your killer. It hardly mattered, though.

ending_10.title: Follow the Trend
strings: Follow the Trend
You met your demise for plotting against the Prince

No one was willing to listen to your defense, no one dared provoke the Sultan at the critical moment of his loss. Soon, you were on the rack, the executioner sharpening his cold blade beside you. As you squinted against the bright sunlight for one last glimpse of the world, you saw that the Sultan's face lacked even the pretense of grief.

ending_11.title: A Momentary Careless
strings: A Momentary Careless
You were assassinated

A dagger silently slips into your unprotected chest. Pain shatters your mind. Scorching blood floods the icy blade. You look into the cold eyes of the masked assassin. Did the Sultan send him? Just because through your guile, you managed to avoid death by an inch? No... no. Those eyes are full of hatred, a hatred that will not die even if you died. Who is he...? You do not know, and you can no longer think.

ending_12.title: Deadline Reached
strings: Deadline Reached
Is this your way of pleasing the Sultan?
You were executed for failing to break the Sultan Card in time.

ending_13.title: The Death of Nobody
strings: The Death of Nobody
Your death brings a new cycle for the game, at least.
Because of your death, the game has come to an end.

ending_14.title: A Life of Wickedness
strings: A Life of Wickedness
Perhaps virtue awaits in another lifetime.
You were hacked to death by rebellious people due to lack of preparation for the enemy's assault.

ending_15.title: WIN!
strings: WIN!
Really?

Congratulations, you have conquered the test version of this game! The game is still under development and there are many more endings.

Thank you for playing, please continue to follow us!

ending_16.title: Farewell, Tyrant
strings: Farewell, Tyrant
At times, people cling to this most laughable of delusions, as if they might say "no" to fate itself.
You refuse to perpetuate this game, and choose to die.

ending_17.title: No Escape
strings: No Escape
Where are you going, my loyal minister?
You and Arzuna didn't escape the city and were captured and executed by the Sultan.

ending_18.title: Tomorrow and Tomorrow
strings: Tomorrow and Tomorrow
Oh, the mighty Sultan yield to a trifling game?
You need to break this Sultan Card to continue the game.

ending_19.title: Betrayal’s Edge
strings: Betrayal’s Edge
Who truly betrayed whom?
Your allies’ steel silenced your questions. You met a tragic end.

ending_20.title: Grievances Abound
strings: Grievances Abound
The monarch's wary eye is the keenest executioner's blade.
You lost the Sultan's trust and favor entirely, executed without a decent reason.

ending_21.title: The Dragon Folly
strings: The Dragon Folly
Many cursed your recklessness… yet they wept for you through the night.
You and your companions were consumed entirely by the dragon's flames, turned to ashes.

ending_22.title: YOU DIED
strings: YOU DIED
Next time for sure
Faraj plunges the dagger into your body. His strike is clean, decisively. You do not feel much pain. A sigh brushes past your ears like a breeze, and you close your eyes...

ending_23.title: The Fall
strings: The Fall
Only in your final moments did you see it: the world hungered for your ruin.
You have gone bankrupt. Having sullied the Sultan's precious game with your failure, a fate worse than death awaits you.

ending_24.title: Coward’s End
strings: Coward’s End
He would not suffer a warrior’s honor to be defiled.
You disgracefully evaded the duel, and were executed by the Sultan.

ending_25.title: Flames of Vengeance
strings: Flames of Vengeance
Now you learn what a man will endure for his beloved.
You perished in flames.

ending_26.title: Can't Even Protect Yourself
strings: Can't Even Protect Yourself
You died from futile mercy.
Executed for sparing the innocent youth, disobeying the Sultan’s decree to shatter his card by dawn.

ending_27.title: Star's Decline
strings: Star's Decline
You bore the madness of the gods

The Highlord of the Highlands was trapped in this game with you, yet He was the first to lose wits? A fragile and useless deity indeed... Fortunately, you, too, were driven to madness by Him, and together, you escaped this game.

ending_28.title: Reduced to Ash
strings: Reduced to Ash
You perished by the gods' unease
Like all wretched masters, the gods never consider the suffering of those below...

ending_29.title: The Pool of Desire
strings: The Pool of Desire
To share desire is to share life
Slain by the maddened mother and son.

ending_30.title: Last Embrace
strings: Last Embrace
You gave Maggie her final comfort.
Your blood filled the tub, strewn with rose petals.

ending_31.title: Star's Redemption
strings: Star's Redemption
Was it deliberate, or an accident?
Whatever your intent, Lumera always believed you were good...

ending_32.title: The Elixir of Regret
strings: The Elixir of Regret
A lethal dose
At least you earned Iman's respect...

ending_33.title: So Close to Glory
strings: So Close to Glory
Mortals could scarcely comprehend your design
Most things that change the world, for better or worse, fail just like this. Grieve not overmuch.

ending_34.title: Taking Root
strings: Taking Root
Your death was but another contingency.
Succeed, and you'd be the messenger of a god's descent. Fail, and you'd be mere compost.

ending_35.title: The Shattered Mirror
strings: The Shattered Mirror
A marvelous journey

The journey lasted many years, until you grew old—your face lined with wrinkles, your joints aching, your muscles withered... Yet through it all, your dearest companion remained by your side. Never once did you doubt that this was the life meant for you. But now, you are old. Too feeble to walk, too weak to join your best friend in seeking out new wonders. Strange... after all these years, has [xiaochou.gender] not aged a day?

The moment the thought crosses your mind, a sound like shattering glass echoes in your skull—the Mirror Spirit! Its magic unravels in an instant. The twisted perceptions, the buried memories—they flood back. God, what have you been doing all these years? So many people, so many duties, so much love... all left behind! The pain you must have caused when you abandoned the capital! These decades, you lived the life the Mirror wanted—wandering, feeding its hunger for spectacle!

Frantic and lost, you stare at your aged reflection—a stranger, as if the Mirror Spirit still watches through those eyes, savoring your final moments of amusement.

Fury drives you to smash the mirror, to tear the room apart—but age has weakened you. Breathless, you falter. And then, slowly, the memories of your long journey return: the wonders you beheld, the tales you lived, the fame, the riches, the magical treasures you amassed. Even now, two lovers who adore you wait below. All of it—left for the real you, [player.name]. A paltry reward for entertaining the Mirror's whims. Now, think and act. Perform one final act to please it: How will you spend what little remains of your own life?

ending_36.title: Death in the Mirror
strings: Death in the Mirror
Dream, delusion, or real?
For [xiaochou.name], it was merely an experiment, a fleeting curiosity. For you—it was death and end.

ending_37.title: Reckless
strings: Reckless
None dare break an appointment with the Sultan
Not funny. The Sultan executes you like the jester you are.

ending_38.title: Soul Usurpation
strings: Soul Usurpation
You died—or perhaps you did not
The Lord of Revels has claimed your flesh, and whatever comes next is no longer yours to know.

ending_39.title: Sin of Usurpation
strings: Sin of Usurpation
The gods shall not tolerate such a feat.

You have drawn the divine closer to this world, and the Dragon's Eye has brought you nearer to their realm... They shattered you and took away the power that did not belong to this world. How will later generations record this? Was it that [player.name] met retribution for coveting divine power, or that the gods sowed the seeds of corruption out of envy for humanity? These future matters shall remain unknown to you forever.

ending_40.title: Spontaneous Combustion
strings: Spontaneous Combustion
You chose to leap into the flames.
Hoping for a sacred end, you found only silence and stillness.

ending_41.title: Echoing Cycle
strings: Echoing Cycle
Lamblet stole everything.

You were utterly defeated and abandoned in the void, with nothing but darkness before you... Suddenly, you seized something. Was it flesh and blood shed when Lamblet transformed? Charred remains from the burning void? Or merely a lump of sheep dung? It no longer matters. With this last power, you called upon yourself and restarted the game.

ending_42.title: Fading Star
strings: Fading Star
You have lost the legitimacy to reclaim your homeland.
With the news of Sirshana's death, your army quickly fell into hesitation and chaos. Just as you prepared to rally your forces, Legions of the Sultan seized the opportunity and surrounded you...

ending_43.title: Star of Doom
strings: Star of Doom
Karma comes swiftly.

In the chaos, no one could tell if it was a miracle or a murder. A flash of light slit your throat—in your dying vision, the stars in the sky mocked you, a treacherous human. You shall never know the story that follows, but they will laugh at your folly for generations to come.

ending_100.title: Escape to China
strings: Escape to China
Cast everything aside and flee eastward, the ancient wisdom shall erase your presence, and none shall catch you!
Through endless hardships, crossing deserts, mountains, and wilderness... you reached this foreign land. Such prosperity! Such marvels!

What a vast nation – you continued traveling, but the road would stretch on and on to new discoveries and stranger wonders. As a foreigner, you drew attention. But you had learned to navigate the shifting tides of hostility, curiosity, and kindness… Compared to the life of an influential courtier, perhaps this – this endless wandering – was what you had been born for.

Upon your funds' depletion, a general guarding the borderlands took you in. One of his subordinates spoke your tongue, and soon you earned their respect through your wisdom and legendary adventures. In the following days, you served the general as an adviser and friend... Your words and deeds – unknown to chronicles and historians though they may be – played their role in shaping another country's history.

You ventured deep inland, all the way, until you saw the sea gain. You even found some familiar faces! Merchants that traded with the Sultanate – the world is truly connected! So you invested in your own fleet... not an entirely legal endeavor, but nothing that could not be solved with ingenuity and wealth. After the Sultan's Game, few things are ever considered challenging to you. Eventually, your fleet returned to the Sultan's port... yet time and distance had left their marks on you, transformed you, remade you, ensuring that you would not be recognized. In the end, you did not set foot ashore.

Arriving at the empire's capital, you presented the supreme monarch (yes, another one) with exotic treasures, legends, and knowledge as offerings. He is no kinder than the Sultan, but he is much calmer, and possessed a subtle patience that matched his allusive style... Long story short, you rose to be one of his most favored courtiers.

Having lost your eyes, it was challenging to find a place in this foreign realm – until one day, an esteemed monk sought you out for the translation of some ancient texts. This was your turn of fate. Your legendary adventures and well-tested wisdom attracted people from far and wide. They regarded you as a sage from a distant land. Through theology and philosophy your soul found solace... as the days of your life passed, some things started to take shape in the darkness of your sights. Fate. Divinity. Plans yet unfolding around you... One day, some day, you shall uncover them all.

Wandering, endless wandering. This is a magnificent land, and yet her beauty shall forever lie beyond your sight. Bound by Darkness, your soul, the landscape of your heart, remains forever imprisoned in the Sultan's realm...

Let's talk about those who love you... Very few were so fortunate as to possess the love of many at once. But you had proven your worth through sacrifice. Soft whispers described to you the exotic scenery all around. Tender caresses guided your path. In the darkness, you could not see the face of this foreign realm. Perhaps, it was the domain of love that you had arrived in.

You escaped with as many lovers as possible – the least you could do for love. Perhaps you underestimated the difficulty of maintaining this much love and passion. This might be even more challenging than the Sultan's Game. But at least, when things were going well, you have found enviable happiness aplenty...

After leaving the Sultan's Game, you met plenty of women and men, many of whom fell in love with you, some of whom received your affection... But you could no longer find happiness in passion. They have not shared the Sultan's Game with you. Such shallow exchanges of bodies and moods... how could they console your soul?

It was hard to say whether the Magician had given or taken more from you. From then on, love became an impossibility –you could no longer find meaningful care or passion in your life. Anyone who came close to you sensed that your attention and thoughts had long been captivated by something strange and ominous. Everything you did might have only been a distraction while you waited for her reappearance…

During moments of intimacy, you would have occasional flashbacks of the the scene of [table.被献祭.name]'s sacrifice. Such visions were not themselves frightful. They did not fill you with guilt. You committed plenty of acts that weigh you down with guilt, but it was a burden you could bear to live with. What truly terrified you was the envy you felt towards [table.被献祭.gender]. You kept imagining, if it were you... perhaps therein lied redemption... or truth. Again and again, you doused your body with ice-cold water to rid yourself of such absurd thoughts.

[table.被牺牲.name]'s face haunted you. Sometimes, it was reflected in a blade. Sometimes, it was on the body of another one of your victims... Someday, this fear will grip you, and death will catch up to you... Perhaps then, you will finally know peace.

Occasionally, you thought of [table.被驱逐.name]. Was [table.被驱逐.gender] still roaming the wilderness? Or perhaps [table.被驱逐.name]'s ghost would one day cross the wilderness in search of vengeance? Such dreams kept you up at night...

As time passed, even nightmares faded. But you still felt the occasional fear when you looked into the distance, dreading that you would see a familiar figure, that some day, a magician would come, carrying with her a game befitting a Sultan.

Some of the children you once taught have traced your footsteps here. They built a humble academy in the local streets, in imitation of your old Nursery. Here, beggars, cutpurses, and strays alike were given equal education; their stomachs filled, their minds sharpened, their voices heard, their paths free to choose. And so, generation after generation, your Nursery never lacked for blooming flowers; your desk was always tidied by eager hands. When night fell, you and your beloved would tell them stories of the Sultan's realm – mere stories, now, nothing more... And each time you remembered this, peace settled over you like the hush of dusk.

Not long after you secured your footing in this land, something wholly unexpected happened – some of your former pupils traced your steps here. Passionate and romantic by nature, schooled in the Way of the Warrior’s Victory under Jebal’s tutelage, they soon found their calling in China. They raised a stage, draped it in brilliant fabrics, and wielded wooden blades and golden-painted swords. Their troupe became famous, for they performed stories never before seen: tales of a distant land, where a tyrant bound his subjects to cruel games, where loyal ministers were forced to play or perish... Sometimes, you would sit among the audience, watching as the actors reenact your past. You would watch as the stage-you embraced a lover in sorrow, gathered belongings against time, and fled into the night, away from the Sultan's insidious temptations. The crowd applauded the performances. You would applaud, too – for your past, for where you are now.

ending_101.title: Escape to a Distant Oasis
strings: Escape to a Distant Oasis
Above you, the sky stretches impossibly high; beneath you, the grass grows impossibly green. You live with impossible freedom, and all of it is your rightful due.

Following the secret map, you crossed the desert, traversed mounds that moved and labyrinths of razor sharp stones, and hid from deadly sandstorms by crawling across an ancient riverbed... At last, you reached this paradise yet unknown to and untouched by tyranny. Such beauty and tranquility, it felt less like a real place, but a dream come true... You plunged into the lake at its heart and tasted sweetness: the purity of molten snow from the highest mountain peaks. You also tasted bitterness: the saltiness of tears streaming down your cheeks...

You became a hermit. In this secluded corner of the world, you had time to cleanse your soul. Wealth held no value there – you crafted your tools and grew your own food. The climate, spring-like all year, spared you the need for much clothing. A revelation unfolded within you – in this blessed sanctuary of nature, you were both protected and imprisoned by your solitude. But if you were to leave, all the evil that had once tormented you would find you once more...

With your own hands, you and your companion built a home. In this secluded place, you cleansed your soul. Wealth had no value here – you hunted with your hands. A pair of priceless swords or two simple sticks made no difference in your afternoon spars. But such peace was not without cost. A revelation unfolded in your hearts – in this blessed sanctuary of nature, you were both protected and imprisoned by your solitude. And if you ever left, all the evil that had once tormented you would find you again...

You could no longer see the world around you. Yet the beauty your companion spoke of – the mist-laden air, the scent of damp earth – all of it nourished your soul. In time, the land took shape within you. You knew the shifting patterns of every leaf, the dips and rises of the earth beneath your feet. Deer did not startle at your approach, and migrating birds passed your voice down to their young. You abandoned cloth and weave, for such things only dulled your closeness to the earth. Your companion followed suit – there was no one watching anymore. Now and then, some lost traveler stumbled into your oasis. When they departed, they swore they had glimpsed the sanctuary of gods. But alas, none ever found their way back to that paradise...

With your own hands, you and your companion built a home for yourselves. The past was behind you. Here, you renewed your bond as partners in love and in life, birthing the next generation as the only humans in this paradise. Wealth lost all meaning. You grew and gathered your food. No finery was needed to adorn your forms – when placed between your lover's breasts, a colorful pebble was as lovely as a ruby. You raised many children and gave them all that you could, and nature, too, bestowed its gifts upon them – extraordinary intelligence, strength, and purity of mind. Finally, the day came when a realization dawned on you: your children should not remain confined to this hidden world forever. Though evil awaited beyond, they had to choose their own paths. And you – you, too, had your demons to face. So you wove clothes, crafted weapons, dried fruit and meat. You set out for the journey... That's another legend waiting to be told.

You could no longer see the world around you. Yet the beauty your companion spoke of – the mist-laden air, the scent of damp earth – all of it nourished your soul. In time, the land took shape within you. You knew the shifting patterns of every leaf, the dips and rises of the earth beneath your feet. Deer did not startle at your approach, and migrating birds passed your voice down to their young. You abandoned cloth and weave, for such things only dulled your closeness to the earth. Your companion followed suit. You became accustomed to her scent, and more and more familiar with the ridges and crevices of her body. Now and then, some lost traveler stumbled into your oasis. When they departed, they swore they had glimpsed the sanctuary of gods. But alas, none ever found their way back to that paradise...

With your own hands, you and your companions built a home for yourselves. The past was behind you, your old identities and vows gone. Here, you became family – the only family that existed in this paradise. Wealth lost all meaning. You grew, gathered, and hunted for your food. Swords of steel or wood, crowns of gold or flowers, jewels of stone or gems... they mattered little to you. Without the veil of power and vanity, you can finally indulge fully in each other's emotions and pleasures. You raised many children and gave them all that you could, and nature, too, bestowed its gifts upon them – extraordinary intelligence, strength, and purity of mind. Finally, the day came when a realization dawned on you: your children should not remain confined to this hidden world forever. Though evil awaited beyond, they had to choose their own paths. And you – you, too, had your demons to face. So you wove clothes, crafted weapons, dried fruit and meat. You set out for the journey... That's another legend waiting to be told.

You could no longer see the world around you. Yet the beauty your companion spoke of – the mist-laden air, the scent of damp earth – all of it nourished your soul. In time, the land took shape within you. You knew the shifting patterns of every leaf, the dips and rises of the earth beneath your feet. Deer did not startle at your approach, and migrating birds passed your voice down to their young. You abandoned cloth and weave, for such things only dulled your closeness to the earth. Your companion followed suit – there was no one watching anymore. Your companions accepted you for who you are. In the day, they would leave you to your solitary wanderings, to the warm sunlight in the clearings, to the nuzzling of beasts and birds. At night, they embraced you with their own warmth, a landscape of rolling hills and beautiful fields you were most familiar with. Now and then, some lost traveler stumbled into your oasis. When they departed, they swore they had glimpsed the sanctuary of gods. But alas, none ever found their way back to that paradise...

She was always there, the Magician, tempting you. Her laughter rode the wind through the trees. Her reflection wavered on the water's surface. The fire's flickering light sometimes twisted into obscene pantomimes of your union... And yet, as long as you withstood the test – as long as you did not reach out – this sanctuary remained safe. You repeated this to yourself, again and again.

When the night was still and quiet, you would hear [table.被献祭.name]'s moans in the woods – whether they were moans of pleasure or pain you could not tell. What truly terrified you was the envy you felt towards [table.被献祭.gender]. You kept imagining, if it were you... perhaps therein lied redemption... or truth. Again and again, you doused your body with ice-cold water to rid yourself of such absurd thoughts.

[table.被牺牲.name]'s face haunted you. When you shot a bird, or bled a deer, you would see it, looking back at you in the pool of blood. Such sights kept you away from your food, each time for longer periods of time...

Occasionally, you thought of [table.被驱逐.name]. Was [table.被驱逐.gender] still roaming the wilderness? Or perhaps [table.被驱逐.name]'s ghost would one day cross the wilderness in search of vengeance? Such dreams kept you up at night...

As time passed, even nightmares faded. But you still felt the occasional fear when you looked into the distance, dreading that you would see a familiar figure, that some day, a magician would come, carrying with her a game befitting a Sultan.

ending_102.title: Servant of God
strings: Servant of God
You had to hand over the sweetest and fullest fruits.
You followed the being once known as Lamblet to the New World they had created.
They dwelled in their cloud palace suspended above the zenith, and you became the brightest star above it. On clear winter days, people could even see your radiance in daylight.
As the servant of god, you were affectionately called God's Servant [player.name]. When the Creator circled the heavens to inspect their creation, you were the Morning Star that upheld them.

As the scribe of god, you were warmly named the Morning Star [player.name]. The people of this world believed that creative inspiration was personally bestowed by you, and poets worshipped you almost fanatically.

As the symbol of god's authority, you were endearingly titled the Crown of the Morning Star. Indeed, they often shaped you into a great star crown, worn proudly upon their forehead. The most exquisite jewels in this world were engraved with "In the name of [player.name]."

As the guardian of god, you were lovingly known as the Shield of the Morning Star [player.name]. Your faithful protection earned the worship of the people, and warriors prayed to you before going to battle.
As the companion of god, you were tenderly called the Gentle and Loyal Morning Star [player.name]. Lovers in this world prayed to you late at night, hoping their love would come true.

As a path of magical power, [player.name] lost his own name entirely. Some said you were a web, carrying the power of god. Others claimed you were a cloud, showering miracles upon the mortal world. A few heretic dark mages whispered that they had dreamed of a rapidly spinning brass scepter, and that with certain gestures, they could unleash magic from it...

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are more primitive and wild. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

Though they do not understand love—they hate it most of all!—they have broken down the barriers between living beings, allowing them to freely mate with those they love, whether of the same kind or another, and bear offspring. And humans, unbound by mating seasons, have spread their seed to every corner of the world... On the grasslands, in the jungles, the skies, and even the deep seas, humans have freely mingled with fish, birds, horses, cats, rhinoceroses... Well, with all kinds of creatures to produce countless hybrids. They fight for mates, for habitats, for better paths of evolution, and for dominion over the world... The Creator is having an absolute blast!

Oh, and of course, there are sheep in this world. But sheep do not mingle with any other species—not even humans. Sheep are just sheep.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are lonelier and more wandering, just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

They designed it to be vast and boundless, so vast that one might spend an entire lifetime without ever seeing another soul. Living beings no longer gather in groups, and communication has become unnecessary. Aside from the gods, they have only themselves to rely on. Each wanders and survives in the wilderness, trapped in their own cocoon. Only on extremely rare occasions are their prayers heard by the gods, allowing them to briefly meet another of their kind, bear children, then soon part and continue their solitary journeys and solitary cultivation... just like some animals in the wastelands and forests you once knew, just like all the stars in the sky, and all the deities.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are crueler, ruled by the law of the jungle. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

Just as birds and beasts feel no guilt for snatching food from others, the people here oppress one another, live by plunder, and take pride in theft. Instinct needs no restraint, and morality is utterly meaningless. For a time, humans even crowned an extraordinarily strong and wise chimpanzee as their king, for in this world, all living beings worship only the strong. And of course, as the Creator and Maker, the one and greatest god of this realm has won the unreserved worship of all living things.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are colder and more mysterious. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

This is a world shrouded in damp mist. Most creatures are born blind, for that is the price they must pay to touch the truth. By day, they live as normal. At night, behind locked doors, their bodies are infiltrated, twisted, and controlled by hordes of demons—beings exiled and driven away by gods in countless other worlds, forced to lurk in shadows, unknown to all... All living things of the day are offerings and playthings of the night. When the sun rises again, they wake from those absurd dreams, and with their newly formed strange limbs, they recite in prayer the desires and weaknesses of the demons, and all knowledge that should never be known to mortals, to their only deity...

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are more thrilling, exciting, and tense. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

And so this world is filled with treasures of old eras—no easy feat, for the Creator, it meant they had to create everything twice!—And so, whether kings or thieves, all people share one sole purpose: to dig downward. The present is too thin, too brittle, too dim; the past was better, greater, more radiant! In this world, the new is inferior to the old, the living are less than the dead, and there are far more guardians in the tombs than in the Sultan's Harem.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are more lucid and more focused on spiritual cultivation. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

And so, everyone in this world embarks on a path of cultivation from birth. They sustain their physical lives with minimal resources, even believing that they are closest to the divine when weak and dizzy. They pour all their energy into the inner world; all their thoughts, meditations, communications, and conflicts take place within the spiritual realm. Little do they know, every time the garden of their souls blooms in splendor, the Creator who made them plucks its petals and reaps its fruit—this is their consistent method, yet the people believe it to be ascension!

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are more elegant, orderly, and sharply stratified. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

And so, this world is carefully divided into sixty-eight levels. And as recorded in that book, "The sole duty of everyone in court is to serve Sultan, our only master." In this world, there is only one deity above the first rank, a handful of first-rank beings, several in the middle ranks, and billions upon billions of ruled sixty-eighth-rank beings. Those of lower ranks must support those above. The first-rank beings enjoy the offerings of all sixty-seven lower ranks. Yet this comes at a cost: every rank's code of conduct is regulated in meticulous detail. First-rank beings may not let their feet touch the ground, may not bend their heads to drink, and may not look at their food while eating. Those who break the rules are flogged. The sixty-eighth-rank may do as they please—they may even defecate on the heads of the first-rank, and the penalty is likewise only a flogging.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, only they are quieter yet noisier—sounds contradictory, doesn't it? But just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator thought little of this book and had their own understanding of social interaction...

And so, in this world they created, people can know each other's thoughts just by looking into each other's eyes. All intentions are conveyed without distortion. To the Creator, this must be the most perfect form of communication: no secrets, no lies, no pretense. Humans no longer even need the cumbersome burden of "language"!

Yet a small group of people is deeply dissatisfied with their design. To avoid the gaze of others, these fools would rather blind themselves. The Creator is furious at their ingratitude! Fortunately, they are few and easily spotted in crowds. The Ruler of All, on the surface, can capture and execute them without difficulty. But why can these people never be fully wiped out?

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are more interesting, with the spirit of a poet or a hero. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

They wove incredibly bizarre, thrilling, and twisted threads of fate for the creatures here—curly, soft, and easy to knead, just like sheep's wool! They prepared countless difficult challenges, desperate traps, and miraculous turnarounds. They toy with them as effortlessly as grooming themselves. When thoroughly amused by their creations, they may even permit themselves a rare few bleats! Naturally, you would do best to pretend you heard nothing.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are bloodier and more brutal. Just like the book you recommended – [all.创世书.name] – remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

They deliberately made this world's resources extremely scarce. When people realize the fruits of the land cannot feed their infants, they naturally turn to plunder and killing. Conflicts between individuals quickly escalate into wars between tribes, towns, and races. When everything finally settles and a single greatest warlord on land emerges, the Creator will gladly flip the entire board with a natural disaster and gleefully watch the next round of bloodshed.

The basic elements of this world are similar to the one you once knew and have long left behind, yet they are stranger and more absurd. Just like the book you recommended—[all.创世书.name]—remember? The Creator shaped this world based on it, fused with their own understanding...

At first, they implanted carefully selected knowledge or falsehoods into some people at birth, making them believe they were born wise. Then they watched them be toyed with and tormented by this incomprehensible knowledge and talent, swelling with pride or falling into despair. Later, they even took to revealing a cruel truth in some people's dreams—that they live in a game, a story, trapped in futile cycles. They make them think they have awakened! But this is merely one of god's ways to mock them. You feel deep sympathy and pity for all this...

As for you, the Creator has kept their promise to you: They dote on you like a fine hound or a temperamental cat. To be specific, you may eat whatever you like and play with whatever you wish, but you must not leave their palace. You must also endure their occasional outbursts of poetic inspiration—a habit they picked up from their last servant—and applaud and praise them at the right moments.

However, when they fight their enemies, you are not allowed to take part at all, for the battlefield is no place for a pet.

As for you, the Creator has kept their promise to you: They regard you as a source of power. Whenever they want something new, they ask for your opinion. The word "ask" here means forcing you to grow what they desire in the Halcyon Days, then cutting off a piece of your soul to give it to them... Through exploiting you, they grow ever stronger. Yet in a way, this also grants you some power: you have managed to weave many stories and legends about yourself into the fragments of power and spread them across the world.

And when they battle their foes, you are exploited and used in the most painful, cruelest ways... Sometimes you think: the Creator and Sultan are so alike. Both exploit to ensure their victims can never resist.

As for you, the Creator has kept their promise to you: They have shown you all the skills of world-making, even though you will likely never need them. That is the fun of teaching a child: "You may not use this later, but let me show you how great I am—and praise me loudly!" In this little game between parent and child, half in play and half in earnest, they shaped the world ever more fully, until in the end you began to admire them with genuine sincerity. It is like a reversed childhood: first doubt, then belief.

When they fight their enemies, you are always placed at a safe distance to watch. Later, they decide you ought to grow up—for growth is the most important and amusing trait of a "child"—and so you are given chances to personally snap an enemy's neck.

Their strife with those who oppose them never ceases for a moment. This world is filled with people who defy the gods. And the reason, of course, is that the Creator Themselves regard their own creations as enemies: every so often they send down disasters, destroy a batch of living beings, and start over.
Yet as time passes, you find it becomes harder and harder for them to end the world... and more and more intelligent creatures survive each cataclysm. You do not know if the Creator has noticed this, but you choose not to remind them.

It is truly a brave new world.

...

Even now, the gods still feud with one another across the worlds. They have even carved out a desolate, abandoned realm solely for their wars. They hurl mountains and seas at each other, wipe out each other's armies with their power again and again, and fill the emptiness of this world with hatred and curses.
They have fought for so long that even you have grown tired of it. Perhaps... even the gods are thinking of abandoning their strife and seeking other amusements. You have come to see the pattern of these so-called gods: they create, they destroy, then they wander away in boredom.

It is truly a brave new world.

...

In this world, the people's enemy is all joy. Except for religious sites and rituals, fine clothing and ornaments are forbidden—at least on the surface. Wine, delicious food, singing and dancing must not even be mentioned. The Creator demands that everyone devote themselves entirely to the cultivation of their souls. They want creations brimming with power, not billions of short-lived but happy ants. And so, some who have truly opened the gates of their souls turn to pray to you—and you always find a chance to answer them in secret... Perhaps you are the Creator's real enemy.

In any case, until They discover the truth, this is a brave new world.

...

Hmm?

You want to start all over again?

Well, baah... I can understand that. Baah, very well... Let me see... Ah... Here's a timeline, much like the ones before—off you go.

Have fun, baah. Say hello to me in that world, baah-baah-baah ha ha ha—!

ending_200.title: Blood of the Rebel
strings: Blood of the Rebel
Sultan has sensed your intent to rebel
You must understand—once you set foot on this path, there can be no more hesitation!

ending_201.title: Blood of the Vanquished
strings: Blood of the Vanquished
You failed to overthrow the Sultan.
You failed to breach the city in time and were annihilated by the Sultan's troops.

ending_202.title: The Long Night approaches its end
strings: The Long Night approaches its end
You forsook vast and glorious power, but in turn, gained small and hidden happiness.

You forged this new realm with blood and steel, yet chose to retreat from its seething heart of power, withdrawing to a quiet corner where jagged cliffs meet weeping willows.

No longer do you startle awake to the Sultan Card gnawing at your thoughts. Dawn now breaks not with court messengers' clamor, but your wife's whispers and the rasping cries of carrion crows beyond the glass.

You've taken up writing, from tales and fables to chronicles of the past. Maggie tends gardens that bloom unnaturally vibrant - your countryside manor boasts the most enchanting and meticulously crafted gardens, a twisted Eden that makes even the local baron's hedge-mazes pale with envy.

Time drips like thick honey, sweet and cloying. You've made it through the long night together — perhaps this is the best ending the Sultan's Game could offer...

Maggie's voice cuts through the stillness. A rare songbird has alighted among her blood-red roses. Nothing in this world takes precedence now. Go - the garden awaits.

ending_203.title: The Weight of Guilt
strings: The Weight of Guilt
I declare I am guilty

In those early days, filth was ever poured before your door, and the air was thick with curses and wailing. You bore the lash and the spittle of the people, so long as they claimed you had wronged them. You severed ties with all your lovers. You scattered the wealth you had gathered, giving it to those who truly needed it. You turned your gaze from the shifting tides of power and did not reach for the spoils of victory, not even once. Slowly, the voices of pity grew a little louder. Slowly, the people returned to their own lives, forgetting the lingering pain from the aftermath of that mad game. Slowly, you, too, ceased to wake in terror from nightmares, no longer sitting hollow-eyed until dawn.

And so, on a quiet morning, you slipped away from the capital without farewells, refusing even the company of friends. You sentenced yourself to an exile that would last a lifetime, for guilt, no matter how faded, never truly lessens. You would wander to many places, do many good deeds. Strangers would welcome you, would love you, but none could keep you. Only in taverns would you sometimes catch word of homeland, a familiar name or two slipping into the talk. Then you would feed your camel and ride on, ever further into the unknown.

ending_204.title: A Nascent Nation
strings: A Nascent Nation

Unbelievable!
You actually did it!
A new country (still under construction)
King of Light (still under construction)
Solomon (still under construction)
There will be nothing new under the sun (still under construction)

ending_205.title: Endless Night
strings: Endless Night
You cast aside power and returned to the place where your journey began, yet the night did not end...

You have withdrawn from the political fray, surrendered the kingdom you built with your own hands to worthier souls. Exhaustion clings to your bones—so profound you'd trade it all for a single hour of dreamless sleep, were the world's gold piled at your feet.

Your hermitage lies remote, twelve days ride for any royal messenger. Servants haunt your halls like shadows, tending only to bare necessities. No hands nurture the gardens; weeds twist skyward, choking the sunlight. Coin flows freely, yet purpose eludes you. The soul wears thin after years of clawing for survival, after wounds that never truly sealed. In twilight hours, you wander half-alive—still flinching at phantom knives, still crying for mothers and wives in fevered dreams.

Maggie is gone. The throne is another's. The game is done.

ending_206.title: Book of the New Sun
strings: Book of the New Sun
Hail! Hail! A new sun rises! The new Sultan is the greatest Sultan!

Lapis floors gleam under scrubbed-away bloodstains. Tapestries bear witness to meticulous cleansing. The golden throne's spine reshapes itself to your frame.

A crown crafted anew from every gem wrested from the empire's soil catches fractured light. The old chapter lies buried where new sun ascends. Seated upon sovereignty's radiance, you who once endured scrutiny now pass judgment upon supplicants. Scribes etch your every breath into vellum - this age shall be named the Book of the New Sun.

You govern through the Sultan's shadow, where political quakes were muffled. Vital organs of state now pulse with creatures of your own making. To still the murmurs, your chosen ones bow to tradition's corpse, court petty functionaries' favor, indulge their coin-laden schemes. Let worms gorge while the harvest lasts. Let them dream of endless feasting.

Thus does the slumbering beast of empire shift its bulk without waking. They name you the New Sun. Let them pray you hang eternal in heaven's vault.

ending_207.title: The Descent of the New Sun
strings: The Descent of the New Sun
A child is best when it's one's own, a spouse is best when it's another's, and a Sultan is always better when new.

The old sun sank into oblivion while the new one ascended the horizon. The creatures of earth never discerned this celestial substitution - they cared only that a sovereign eternally occupied the golden throne... 

And you, successor to the Sultanate, saw your reign immortalized in chronicles as "The Descent of the New Sun." An ill-omened title, for your rule lasted but seventy-seven days. Your reforms cut too deep, too swift, severing the sinews of entrenched powers. You spurned their honeyed flatteries, refused to indulge their plundering ways or partake in their excesses as your predecessor had. The new nobles you raised, though fanatically loyal and straining to enact your vision, stood as saplings easily uprooted in this ancient empire's soil.

The chroniclers praised your "virtues of enlightened rule" through gritted teeth, while condemning your "lack of regal ruthlessness" with poisoned quills.

Your end came by dagger's kiss in the velvet darkness of your bedchambers. 

Those who followed - whether styling themselves Sultan, Emperor, or King - found the throne crumbling beneath them. The empire fractured into perpetual twilight, its broken crown rolling through bloodstained hands until the last ember of order died.

ending_208.title: Cage of the Sun
strings: Cage of the Sun
The realm needs a Sultan as all things need the sun, even if it be a sun in chains.

After overthrowing the Sultan to claim the gilded throne, you realize with cruel clarity: this land didn't serve the Sultan - it made him. 

His power flowed from noble houses, whose own authority stemmed from crown and territory. These gears interlock, forming the nation's true nature:

a machine of oppression, a system built on exploitation.

Each noble child demands five or ten peasant infants raised to sustain it. Yet peasant babes rarely see ten winters. So nobles tighten their grip. So peasants starve. So the Sultan needs more enforcers. So power becomes currency. In this smooth, self-perpetuating cycle, sacrifices like your former self (who played the Sultan's games) get consumed - while other nobles bask in unchecked privileges. Recall the maxim? "Gold flows to those who needn't labor."

You vowed to reform it all: reshaping the bureaucracy, reclaiming power from masters, overturning privileges. But the land resists. Your decrees twist like poisoned vines. Rewards become traps. Your eyes see only theater. Lies buzz in your ears like corpse-flies.

Each dawn brings fresh venom from court vipers. You clench jeweled fists, restraining the crimson urge (gods, how it swells daily!) to let blades speak. You repeat the bitter truth: slaughter them, and chaos follows. Rebellions bloom. The gilded throne, however heavy, will fall when ten thousand hands push.

Did you overthrow a Sultan merely to become the next fallen tyrant?

Silence consumes you. It's a cage of the sun - your radiance imprisoned by eternal night.

ending_209.title: The Conqueror's End
strings: The Conqueror's End
Common folk chase happiness. But for a Sultan, there is only one worthy pursuit: a good death.

The foundation of your claim was but a golden Conquest Card.

You told the people the Sultan granted you the right to conquer, yet set no bounds upon its use. Thus, your usurpation, your victory, your seizure of his throne, all could be framed as his tacit blessing. This sophistry swayed few... but your armies and the blood on your hands sufficed. The crowd parted in silence, letting you ascend the throne upon a path of crimson. 

The scribes named you usurper. You slew a few, yet their successors came to court with coffins at the ready, refusing to rewrite history as you wished.

The nobles conspired to thwart you will.If you ruled as the old Sultan did, they scorned you. If you dared change, they praised the past. 

The masses obeyed half-heartedly, for a rootless Sultan seemed doomed to fall. To heed your reforms was to waste breath...

It wearied you, or worse, made you wonder if you differed at all from the Sultan you'd overthrown.

So when the dagger found your heart in your second year, you felt but relief. As your vision dimmed, you saw them: friends rushing forward, enemies standing cold, lovers weeping in terror...

This was conqueror's end. You had achieved greatness, and greatness demands a fall.

ending_210.title: The Realm of Game
strings: The Realm of Game
Come, revel, indulge in wickedness - for this is the Sultan's game!

Your justification for overthrowing the last Sultan was... flimsy. You merely showed the courtiers the Sultan Card, declaring that the Sultan himself had granted you the right of conquest with no restrictions on whom you might conquer.

Amidst the whispers, you strode toward the golden throne. The courtiers saw your claim as hollow. Many called you usurper in hushed tones. Stupid peasants and cunning merchants defied your first decrees, certain you would soon be toppled by the next contender...

But they underestimated one truth: What is the greatest legitimacy of power? Not royal blood, not brute strength, nor even the people's support - but evil! The wicked imagination festering in your heart, the will to act upon it, the fervent desire to watch the world drown in depravity!

Since forging your pact with the will of ultimate malice, none have understood the power of evil as you do.

Soon, you introduced the Joyous Ticket, a game mimicking the Sultan's Card. People bought these tickets to commit the acts inscribed upon them without legal consequence: Carnality, of course, but also Bloodshed. You ranked every citizen by tier though, naturally, one could rise in tier by paying you enough. Why fear a mere Stone Bloodshed Card when three gold coins could spare you? The Golden ones, however, cost a hundred and twenty! You rewarded and punished officials with these tickets. At first bewildered, they soon groveled desperately, who would gamble their entire fortune to satisfy the whim of a card?

Alas, this time, no hero rose to stop you like you used to do. The realm descended into a game, and in your eyes, everyone reveled in delight.

And of course... you were the happiest one.

ending_211.title: The Conqueror's Cage
strings: The Conqueror's Cage
A Sultan can be killed. A Sultan can be caged.

You brandished a single Conquest Card as proof of your legitimacy. When you held it aloft, their faces twisted with doubt and scorn.

Even if it was the last Sultan's own writ of supreme authority, but how could you use his power to justify overthrowing him? You remained a usurper, a monkey upon the throne, a traitor without rightful claim!

The crowd before you seethed with outrage. The blood at their feet had not yet dried, yet in their hearts, the last Sultan had already transformed from tyrant to sacred sovereign of pure lineage. Such is the nature of these fools: the moment the yoke lifts from their shoulders, the first they turn against is the one who removed it. "By what right do you take what I've borne for centuries?"

You couldn't help but laugh. They took it as mockery, perhaps it was, and their fury burned hotter. The alleys buzzed with crude rumors of your treachery. The nobles withheld their oaths, waiting to see if another would topple you. Peasants and peddlers knew only that a new face sat the throne, and every Sultan exists to oppress, so why not stick with the old devil they'd already fed? Thus, they too opposed you.

To keep your crown, you spent each day setting one man against another, diverting hatred here, dodging sycophants there, scrambling to soothe tempers you hadn't even sparked. You achieved a precarious balance. By the standards of history's usurpers, your reign lasted long. But only you and a handful of confidants knew the true cost of that equilibrium...

In the Sultan's Game, you once fought daily to survive. Now, as a Conqueror, you are trapped in a cage called "Ruler".

ending_212.title: The Conqueror's Reward
strings: The Conqueror's Reward
This is the Sultan's Game, and so it must end with a Sultan Card.

The last Sultan's warmth had not yet faded from the golden throne when you took your seat. The courtiers filed into the chaotic hall, trembling, their eyes fixed upon you, waiting for your words.

There must be some justification, must there not? Did you claim the throne by blood? By justice? By what right? How would the messengers announce your name to the vast empire's bureaucracies? How would you explain your usurpation...?

You tossed something before them: a Golden Conquest Card.

You told them the last Sultan himself had placed this authority in your hands. He commanded you to conquer, and he, of course, was worthy of the Golden Conquest Card. Thus, you had only done what he permitted. When he began this game, he should have known he might become its target.
