A ruler's word is law, his decrees are unbreakable - and so none could deny the legitimacy of a throne won through conquest.

The crowd stirred. A thousand thoughts, a thousand arguments rose, but you raised a hand for silence. Then you beckoned your supporters forward. Familiar faces stepped from the ranks without a word, then turned to face the doubters.

Among them stood reformers who had fought beside you to reshape the realm. Their very presence heralded a new dawn. Yet there too were heirs of ancient houses, staunch traditionalists, voices of spiritual authority. Their defiant stance struck the old nobility mute.

And so, the court began to move. Some rushed eagerly, others wept as they embraced you, while a few dragged their feet, each step grinding away the loyalty they'd spent years building for the last Sultan... Yet by day's end, they all knelt before you.

You had birthed a new age. The old empire's era-name was discarded. The new realm would be called "[player.name]'s Mamlaka", meaning the "Land of [player.name]".

ending_213.title: The Standing Sultan
strings: The Standing Sultan
The true Sultan who stands beside the throne. A Regent. A man who understands power's true nature.

When the last Sultan fell, the people gathered in silence around the Golden Throne, waiting to see the new ruler before deciding whether to cheer or spit.

You came forward with a veiled woman. Bowing, you offered your hand and guided her onto the throne with practiced reverence.

Two highborn ladies, mothers of many, stepped forth without a word. They knelt at the veiled woman's feet, drew aside her silks, and revealed her face: Sadani.

"I carry the Sultan's bloodline," she said, her jeweled head held high, her gaze cutting through the crowd like a scimitar. "This child shall wear the crown. Its father is dust. You will kneel to your new, rightful, and supreme Sultan."

The noblewomen pressed their foreheads to the marble and proclaimed their findings: the timing of her pregnancy perfectly aligned with the late Sultan's last visit to her chambers, the robust health of her unborn child, and their eternal loyalty to the legitimate bloodline.

Of course, after this performance, their houses would find favor when the new order came. As for when Sadani truly conceived, or by whom - that mattered less than the flies buzzing about the throne.

The crowd stood frozen, exchanging uneasy glances. None had heard of late Sultan leaving any heir. Yet here was a child with claim beyond dispute, and more telling, not a soul seemed inclined to weep for its dead father. The final truth hung heavier than palace tapestries: You had placed Sadani on the throne. You had pulled down the last Sultan.

One by one, the nobles bent their knees. You remained standing, watching the sea of bowed heads which on lapis lazuli floors, in courtyards, through bazaars and alleys, as the realm submitted to its new power.

And you? You were its beating heart. You were the Regent of the realm. You were the true Sultan who stands beside the throne.

ending_214.title: The Blade of Loyalty
strings: The Blade of Loyalty
A sharp blade, a long-awaited devotion.

Once the prior Sultan's rule crumbled entirely, two noble women of high birth accompany a veiled lady before the crowd; they silently transcend towards the golden throne with you stationed beside.

Revealed is Sadani, pregnant—and to underscore, the noblewomen stuffed fabric under her attire. She proclaims herself with imperial lineage; regardless of the Sultan's former cruelty, the nation's exalted lineage should reign. Thus, this child is born a Sultan.

Perplexity stirs among the populace, surprised by the news of Sadani's pregnancy... but in binding oaths, the esteemed ladies attest the fitting timeline. Then, you publicly kneel before Sadani, expressing fealty to her unborn child. The undeniable clarity unfolds: this nation is your control, and Sadani is your necessary governance tool. Gatherings arise, authoritative bending occurs.

Thereafter, you pursued reform policies, replacing prior Sultan loyalists, bolstering your dominion. Sadani birthed a male infant safely.

During this infant Sultan's inaugural birthday celebration, Sadani subtly pries about relinquishing power to her and the heir... you dismissively suggest ages, eliciting suspicion distinguishable in her gaze; verifiable as unfeigned displeasure.

Nonetheless, distractions abound, resistant noble factions persistently stir; your inability to supplant bureaucratic roles pleasing elite agenda hindered you, discontent continually surfaces. Sadani's mistrust grew known; aged nobles lament your throne usurpation. Unknowing, one most loyal blade awaits disposal: in her and her child's defense.

During the youthful Sultan's third celebration, a hunting festivity convened; within royal forestry, Seliman pierces your heart with a blade astute.

ending_215.title: The Realm of Game
strings: The Realm of Game
Come, revel, indulge in wickedness - for this is the Sultan's game!

You sought out Sadani and told her you believed the child in her womb was the Sultan's blood, and so you would place her and the babe upon the throne.

The former concubine, still reeling from the upheaval, stared at you wide-eyed. "But..." she said, "You could claim the throne yourself. What... what do you want from this?"

You smiled. She was a clever woman, wasn't she?

You told her you wanted a realm to play with as you pleased. You spoke of your plan to introduce "Joyous Ticket", a game mimicking the Sultan's Card. People bought these tickets to commit the acts inscribed upon them without legal consequence: Carnality, of course, but also Bloodshed. You ranked every citizen by tier though, naturally, one could rise in tier by paying you enough. Why fear a mere Stone Bloodshed Card when three gold coins could spare you? The Golden ones, however, cost a hundred and twenty! You rewarded and punished officials with these tickets. At first bewildered, they soon groveled desperately, who would gamble their entire fortune to satisfy the whim of a card?

Sadani grew increasingly horrified, repeatedly trying to interrupt before you silence her. The more you spoke, the more delighted you grew, gesturing wildly, making one thing clear: you were ready to slaughter every dissenter, even including her and the child in her belly.

"You wish to do evil, yet leave no tyrant's name for history to curse," she murmured, hen laughs bitterly, "You want me and my child to issue these mad decrees in your stead. And even if I begged your oath to spare us... even if you gave it... I suppose you would break it all the same. Fine... just do as you will."

Yes, she was a clever woman indeed.

ending_216.title: Ruler in Hell
strings: Ruler in Hell
Laugh while you can, foolish murderers! I shall see you all in hell!

After the preceding Sultan's realm subsequently collapses, two noble birthright females accompany a veiled woman amongst the populace advancing the golden throne, where you linger beside.

Amidst the populace, a pregnant Sadani stands unveiled—enhancing the façade with clothing stuffed. Announcing imperial blood—despite erstwhile despots' treachery, noblest inception aligns sovereignty.

In disbelief, the populace comprehends that Sadani's state matched prospectively with Sultan pursuits despite previously undisclosed. You knelt in homage to Sadani's unborn destiny, which solidifies your grasp of the nation.

Thereafter, enforcement of reforms denoted erstwhile appointments' displacement, bolstering dominion, proceeding with Sadani birthing safely.

In navigating ostensibly simplistic power contention, entrapping Sadani seclusion among innumerable inter-palatial grounds, audiences demand rigorous protocol.

Each intermediary eunuch has tongues shorn; former aides are replaced with veneration-worthy personnel. Discontent protests flux amongst traditional factions, incessantly petitioning limited vestment in infant Sultan executive authority or proposition for a Principal Nobility Council fosterment.

Exhortations to counter pressure rest deficient, intricate oversight prevalence engenders nescience; reformatory implementation ricochets confirm surface nomaly. Fortuitously, the prolonged reformative initial decade fails from fault oversight, ignorant bastion oversight staring hallmark present.

In unrest anxiety compiling, ultimatums close proximity surfacing—the evoked firebrand rebellion culminates palace encirclement.

Exhausted combat, immortality departs steadily. With parting exclamations of subjugation yet grandeur, assassin accusations multiply among your transgressors. Agitation's resolution might prelude eternal meet, your mark endured beneath—a warning mastering death herald.Vengeful perpetuation lends weight to your legacy—shadow cast lingering solace within rival spirits post-vital threshold.

Even post-departure, rumors of "[player.name]'s awaiting netherworld presence" endure among the trepid rank.

ending_217.title: The Cage of Bloodline
strings: The Cage of Bloodline
Power, once spun from deceit, demands ever more deception to hold its shape. Were you skilled at lying?

After casting down the previous Sultan, you came to Sadani with a proposal.

You proposed that you could place the child in her womb upon the throne as the next Sultan.She had a child of pure blood, whose very existence would be the foundation of the new regime. And you would serve as Regent, ruling in the child's name until they came of age.

Sadani lowered her beautiful eyes, considering carefully. Then she raised them, studying you.

"But what if others do not believe?" she asked. "The timing of the Sultan's visits and the conception may not align... If we are exposed, you and I will both die."

You conceded she spoke true, but you also pointed out that this was the only path left to you both. You needed a claim to rule, and she needed to bear this child. The realm needed a Sultan. The Golden Throne had to have a master to sit on.

She bit her lip and agreed.

In the days that followed, you scoured the court for noblewomen willing to bear false witness to the timing of Sadanis conception. The royal physicians were men, and Sadani could refuse their examination by claiming modesty before strangers. But still, you had to find witnesses. A noblewoman of high birth, one who had borne children herself, had to pretend to have examined Sadani and publicly swear that "the timing was beyond doubt."

Yet, to your dismay, you failed to sway most of the traditionalist nobles to your cause. They still saw you as a usurper and regarded Sardarni with suspicion. If you chose your own followers as witnesses, the nobles would cry fraud. And if you sought those with no ties to you... none would perjure themselves for your sake.

The farce of testimony was held regardless. Sadani, flanked by her handmaidens, took her seat upon the Golden Throne. With all the dignity and solemnity she could muster, she declared that the child in her womb was the Sultan's trueborn heir. And thus, she claimed the right to swear fealty in its name.

The courtiers laughed. They saw through the ruse but welcomed it, for they believed you and Sadani would be pliable rulers, and the unborn Sultan a chain to bind you both to the court.

This moment marked the beginning of your reign... and the shape of every single day to come...

Every. Single. Day.

ending_218.title: A Realm with Two Rulers
strings: A Realm with Two Rulers
Perhaps the title of Sultan was never meant to be borne by one alone.

No sooner had you defeated the last Sultan than Zazie came to you without delay.

She had likely stuffed her robes with cotton, her belly swollen far beyond what her months should show. With exaggerated care, she cradled her false pregnancy as two eunuchs supported her, parading through the court until she stood before you.

You understood at once. The child in her womb, real or not, could be the next Sultan. And you? You needed a reason to steady the restless nobles...

"We've spoken enough of what I want, and what you want," Zazie said plainly, her eyes locked on yours. "You shall be Regent. Rule as you please. But do not interfere in my affairs. I am the Queen Mother. My child is the Sultan. You and I... we may share everything. Share the throne, share the people. What say you? I promise you this - the child I bear will be a good Sultan...for you."

She extended a hand to you, slender fingers heavy with rings, nails lacquered deep as blood. That was A hand that had once pleasured a Sultan, A hand that now reached for his throne.

You took it. Your grip sealed the pact...

And so began the era of a realm, with two rulers.

ending_219.title: The End of Golden Blood
strings: The End of Golden Blood
A wise Sultan always begins his reign by slaughtering those who crowned him, that’s it.

Zazie claimed the child in her womb was the rightful heir. The traditionalist nobles, though disgusted by your regicide, especially when you'd done it with the Sultan Card! But they grudgingly accepted the unborn heir... and you as Regent.

A new order rose around you and Zazie. After a brief dance of cautious probing, she withdrew to her chambers, citing the needs of her pregnancy, while you worked tirelessly to plant loyal men in every corner of power. For months, the arrangement held.

Then Zazie's child was born. Swaddled in white silk, the babe wore gold warmed against a slave's skin before ever tasting breast milk. He was Sultan now, divine and untouchable. The babe and his mother were the perfect apex of empire. His birth meant the realm no longer needed a Regent.

In those quiet months, Zazie had whispered in every dissenting noble's ear. She promised, lied, flattered and threatened. She made them believe her son would be gentler than his father and more generous to the old blood.

And she planted darker seeds. "When [player.name] usurps the throne..." she would begin. The great nobles would be beggared by his reforms. Corrupt officials would hang. Noble-born officers would compete with baseborn brutes for rank...

She struck at their deepest fear: the loss of privilege, the privilege they knew full well was poison to the realm. But men will drink poison to quench today's thirst.

Fear was Zazie's trade. She had learned much at the side of the child's father.

So when you came bearing gifts for the newborn Sultan, she smiled and bade you hold the babe, even asked you to choose his nickname. You reached for the sacred bundle... bur eunuchs behind you moved faster. Leather cords bit into your throat.

The first great act of the little Sultan's reign was the death of his Regent.

ending_220.title: The Realm of Game
strings: The Realm of Game
Come, revel, indulge in wickedness - for this is the Sultan's game!

Since forging your pact with the will of ultimate malice, none had understood the power of evil as you did.

This power had trampled all legitimacy beneath its heel. It could elevate slaves to Sultans and vice versa. To demonstrate this, you chose the child in Zazie's womb as the next Sultan. The boy would be steeped in your cruelty from birth. He would be pliant, agreeable and terrified. As for his mother, the golden lioness of a slave, you had known how to silence her.

So you seated Zazie upon the Golden Throne and declared to the court that she was but the vessel for the next Sultan. Then you crowned yourself Regent with a diadem larger than the last Sultan's own. As the nobles gaped at this breach of decorum, you unveiled your masterpiece:

Joyous Ticket, a game mimicking the Sultan Card. People bought these tickets to commit the acts inscribed upon them without legal consequence: Carnality, of course, but also Bloodshed. You ranked every citizen by tier though, naturally, one could rise in tier by paying you enough. Why fear a mere Stone Bloodshed Card when three gold coins could spare you? The Golden ones, however, cost a hundred and twenty! You rewarded and punished officials with these tickets. At first bewildered, they soon groveled desperately, who would gamble their entire fortune to satisfy the whim of a card?

The court fell silent. You had overthrown one Sultan already, the power was yours. You could order any noble to fulfill a Bloodshed Card...or another to become a beggar with Extravagance Card that could consume all of his property...

This time, no hero rose to stop you like you used to do. The realm descended into a game, and in your eyes, everyone reveled in delight.

ending_221.title: The Cage of Golden Blood
strings: The Cage of Golden Blood
What trapped you was not what you despised, but the future you had once longed for...

You overthrew the last Sultan, making you a hero to those who hated him, and a vile usurper to those who loved him, or loved the privileges his rule bestowed.

So you needed to gild your actions with plausible excuses, needed a "Sultan" more palatable to traditionalist nobles than yourself appeared... and thus you thought of Zazie.

The favored concubine seemed to have expected your visit. Adorned in the lavish attire of a noblewoman with child, she deliberately concealed her still-flat belly, likely padding her robes with cotton to feign pregnancy.

"The child I carry is the next Sultan. This is beyond dispute," she said lazily. "And you may certainly serve as Regent. After all, look how diligently you've cleared my child's path to the throne... But alas, we are not ungrateful. We merely require... assurances."

She suddenly grew fascinated with her long, gold-dripped nails.

After a weighted silence, you pledged to return power when the boy came of age. Promised the Queen Mother luxuries and diversions, the young Sultan an education fit for rulers.

Zazie smiled, satisfied, and dismissively bade you leave. But you knew obedience now would make reclaiming authority harder later. So you straightened, clasped your hands behind your back, and smirked back with equal arrogance.

Another silence. Zazie weighed your capabilities, influence, allies, methods, deeds... placed them on one scale, against her own skills, her child, her supporters on the other. Finally, reluctantly, she rose and curtsied, thanking you for your visit.

The exchange left you both weary, a fatigue that would persist through the coming years of rule. Your faction lacked strength to openly challenge the old-blood nobility, so Zazie would keep testing you, again and again and again...

Your soul, your flesh, your dreams, all imprisoned. You couldn't flee the palace, for abandoning power meant death at Zazie's leisure. Nor could you crush the opposition that constrained your reach, denying you full authority...

In this struggle, you even forgot why you'd fought initially, forgotten overthrowing a Sultan was meant to build a better realm. Sometimes you missed the old tyrant. Perhaps his madness and cruelty had been attempts to break this same cage? Perhaps he too had chafed as you did now. Perhaps you should take after him, should fill a few more baskets with heads...

The damned court life endured. Weary, you dragged yourself toward the throne room once more.

ending_222.title: The Realm of Remembrance
strings: The Realm of Remembrance
No more Sultans, only the Great King who restored the ancient kingdom! Long live the King!

You and Sirshana ascended the steps of the Lapis Lazuli Court together.

The blood beneath your boots had not yet dried. The banners in the hall still bore the colors of the last Sultan's reign. Yet the courtiers crowding around you had already scrambled into the long robes of the old kingdom, though beneath the hems, the telltale edges of the previous regime's garments still peeked out, hastily concealed. They whispered among themselves, rehearsing new phrases: No Sultan rules here now, the King has returned!

You rebuilt your realm in the image of the past, from the architecture of the palaces, to the cut of women's skirts, to the meter of court poetry. Everything was made to evoke nostalgia. You redistributed power among the most favored nobles as it had once been, reuniting the territories fragmented by the Sultans, weaving the old web of checks and balances between the great houses. You restored the title of "Queen." Now your harem had a single mistress, not a flock of equal concubines for the Sultan's pleasure.

Overnight, noblewomen changed their hairstyles. Children's rhymes in the streets shifted melody. The altars of the Purist quietly gave way to the shrines of the Star-Souled. The reigns of the two Sultans seemed to have left no mark...

But the marks remained in people's hearts—just as the Sultan's games had carved grooves into your very soul.

At least that game was over now.

ending_223.title: The Starrenegade with Crimson Robe
strings: The Starrenegade with Crimson Robe
Power is a splendid crimson robe that dyed in the blood.

You restored Sirshana's ancient kingdom, revived the title of "King," and consigned "Sultan" to the dust of history.

Yet as king, you could not mold the kingdom to your will. Every move was watched by a council of nobles from old world. Behind your throne, they built a small chamber with walls of pure gold. You addressed the court while they whispered commands at your back.

Naturally, you resented this meddling. But your loyalists, those willing to truly change the realm, were too few. Without these relics of the past, you'd never hold the kingdom. And for a king who had overthrown a Sultan, losing control meant death.

Your reforms stalled. Your appointments leaked before announcement. Your military investments were vetoed... You realized these aristocrats meant to make you a puppet in truth...

So you struck first. Royal guards stormed the golden chamber. Six nobles of the old blood were stabbed to death before the court. The hem of your magnificent kingly robes grew heavy with their blood.

It won you control of the court and a host of new enemies. The people, who had cheered the restoration, now turned against you. Lords who had sworn fealty denounced you as a tyrant. They named you "the Crimson Robe King" and "Starrenegade" in scorn.

The rest of your days were spent crushing dissent. The stars bore witness to your weary, numb existence.

ending_224.title: The Starblade's Last Words
strings: The Starblade's Last Words
What was the most important sentence you ever spoke in your life?

You ascended the throne with Sirshana. You seated upon the golden throne, the sword of kingship in hand, while he stood at your side bearing a massive golden star crafted in the image of the ancient kingdom's treasure. This star symbolized the celestial bodies over the highlands, the very source of the old monarchy's legitimacy.

Then you began reshaping the realm. You reunited territories fragmented by the Sultans, weaving a delicate balance of power among the nobility. You restored the title of "Queen", your harem had a single mistress, not a flock of equal concubines for a Sultan's pleasure. All these reforms seemed righteous, inevitable... yet you forgot one thing.

What had doomed the old kingdom that ruled this way? When dissenters gathered in secret, were you as unprepared as Sirshana's father had been?

On the first anniversary of your new regime, the military struck. You were celebrating in the old kingdom's tradition, riding a majestic stallion with four guards, clad in plain white robes, while subjects knelt along the road. You scattered honeyed wine brewed by your queen; those touched by its drops were said to be blessed for a year.

Then some old crones among the prostrate women seized your horse's legs. Your guards reacted, but too late. The "crones" were swordsmen in disguise. They severed the stallion's tendons and stabbed downward as you fell.

Some hands reached to save you, others to strangle you. Though your guards had been stationed throughout the streets, noble retinues and street thugs poured from alleys, hurling flaming oil to panic the horses. Chaos erupted. Those wishing you alive and those craving your death clashed like hounds over a hare. One moment you were cradled gently, the next battered by shields.

When Sirshana arrived with the royal guard, the rebels were subdued. Your guards carried you before him, still breathing. You spoke one last phrase, but what it was became history's great debate.

Some claimed you said "Avenge me", so Sirshana purged the bureaucracy thoroughly for three years, even couldn't muster enough officials to collect taxes.

Others insisted it was "Show mercy." Many commoners believed this, fearing bloodshed, slaughter, a mad king's wrath.

Still others swore it was "This is your fault" or "No regrets" or "Protect my queen"...

People shaped your last words to their desires where the truth no longer mattered.

ending_225.title: The Realm of Jungle
strings: The Realm of Jungle
Civilization, nothing more than wrapping "the Law of the Jungle" in fancy rules.

Sirshana was a prince raised in the filth of back alleys, and you were the courtier who survived the Sultan's Game. What drove you both to seize this realm wasn't homeland restoration, but to create a jungle where only the strongest survive.

Your realm became a jungle, not in trees, but in spirit. Here, soldiers earned rank through mortal combat. Officials clawed their way up over the bodies of rivals. Merchants poisoned competitors' goods with the crown's blessing. Murder became just another trade, revenge a sacred right.

You answered violence with greater violence. As king, you were the mightiest predator of all. Every week, hundreds fought to the death in your arenas. The survivors would kneel before you, receiving appointments to fill the endless vacancies in your armies and enforcer squads where vacancies you deliberately created by constantly driving your kingdom to war, to conflict, to bloodshed. The jungle demanded its "apes" tear at each other's throats. The Arena became the capital's beating heart. Even children were brought by their parents to witness the slaughter. Let the moralists wail while you and Sirshana reveled in the carnage.

But even the king atop the jungle's canopy must face challenges from the beasts below. When the arena's champion, having slain thirty-four men, knelt before you and begged for the honor to fight his king.

The crowd roared like a raging sea. Sirshana watched you, torn between the crude urgings of a back-alley swordsman and the measured counsel of a prince.

You accepted the challenge.

The gladiator's steel found your heart... and Sirshana's blade found his too after that.

At last, the kingdom had become the jungle it was always meant to be.

ending_226.title: The Realm of Starblade
strings: The Realm of Starblade
Could a prince raised in dark alleys truly rule a kingdom? Even Sirshana had never imagined it.

You and Sirshana ascended the steps of the Lapis Lazuli Court together. Sirshana strided ahead as the restored king while you followed half a step behind as his great supporter.

The blood beneath your boots had not yet dried. The banners in the hall still bore the colors of the last Sultan's reign. Yet the courtiers crowding around you had already scrambled into the long robes of the old kingdom, though beneath the hems, the telltale edges of the previous regime's garments still peeked out, hastily concealed. They whispered among themselves, rehearsing new phrases: No Sultan rules here now, the King has returned!

At your counsel, Shirshina rebuilt the realm in the his memory of the lost kingdom, from the architecture of the palaces, to the cut of women's skirts, to the meter of court poetry. Everything was made to evoke nostalgia. He shared power with you and other high lords, reuniting the territories fragmented by the Sultans, weaving the old web of checks and balances between the great houses.

Overnight, noblewomen changed their hairstyles. Children's rhymes in the streets shifted melody. The altars of the Purist quietly gave way to the shrines of the Star-Souled. The reigns of the two Sultans seemed to have left no mark...

Or perhaps no king should expect to carve his name into history, like even the finest sculptor cannot chisel the wind...

And that, at least, was fair.

ending_227.title: Prisoners of Oath
strings: Prisoners of Oath
To cut away the rot is to wound the healthy flesh. To slay one's enemies is to harm those who were once friends.

With your aid, Sirshana restored the old kingdom. The title of "King" returned; "Sultan" was buried in dust.

Yet no sooner had you stepped into the Lapis Lazuli Hall than a council of the old nobility assembled, who had once risked their lives to shelter the exiled prince. Now, they believed, was the time to trade loyalty for power. Behind the throne, they built a small chamber with walls of pure gold. While Sirshana addressed the court and you stood by the throne, they whispered their commands from the shadows.

They opposed every counsel you gave. Your reforms stalled. Your appointments leaked before announcement. Your military investments were vetoed... You realized these aristocrats meant to make Sirshana a puppet in truth.... Had you not been there, they might have succeeded. But they had not accounted for you.

On a day when Sirshana rode out to hunt, leaving no king in the court, you struck. The royal guard stormed the golden chamber. Six nobles of the old blood died on the blades of their own king's men.

The poets of the old kingdom once sang of the Lapis Lazuli Palace: "Its floors drink noble blood, yet never stain." True enough. When Sirshana returned, the stones still gleamed blue as midnight.

The king was silent. These slain lords had been his staunchest defenders. They had cradled him as a babe, given him refuge, spilled their strength to keep him alive.

And yet he knew, without you, there would be no restoration. What you had given him outweighed them all

After that day, you and Sirshana scarcely spoke again. The kingdom stumbled forward along the old paths. Enemies multiplied, rebels and avengers rose like weeds. But in the Lapis Lazuli Palace, two rulers dared not meet each other's gaze.

ending_228.title: The Falling Star Rises Again
strings: The Falling Star Rises Again
What ending could be more fitting for Sirshana? He would have agreed that too.

Together, you pushed open the heavy doors of the Lapis Lazuli Palace, restoring the fallen kingdom.

Soon enough, King Sirshana began ruling in his own fashion: He dreamed of ruling through sheer might alone. Soldiers earned rank through mortal combat. The kingdom thrived on constant war. Only the bloodthirsty could rise high in this realm.

You protested these... if they could even be called policies. But he would not listen. "I lived for revenge all these years," he scoffed. "Now that I've taken what's mine, even my father would be satisfied. But can't I rule as I please? Besides, had the Sultan's father not interfered, I'd have been king years ago! I might have made things even more interesting!"

So he built the grandest arena the world had ever seen, where gladiators came to die. He promised the first gladiator to survive all matches would be granted one wish...

"This is madness!" you warned. "Who knows what they might demand? A king cannot make such promises!"

But Sirshana reveled in it, lounging in his embroidered cloak high above the bloodshed.

Two years later, a champion emerged, the one who had slaughtered all opponents. Kneeling before the king, he claimed his prize: "I beg the honor to cross blades with Your Majesty. They say before becoming king, you were the greatest Roaming Swordsman of our age."

You rose to rebuke the man, but Sirshana only laughed. Tossing his cloak to you, he grabbed a sword and leapt into the pit!

What followed was the cruelest duel - two men fighting not for crown or cause, but simply because they wanted to prove who was the better fighter!.

At the end, both blades found their marks, piercing deep as fountains of blood arced before the roaring crowd. You could bear no more, vaulting into the arena, screaming for the imperial physician.

Dying in your arms, Sirshana smiled as he whispered his last words:

"Told you... I was never meant to be king... should have let you rule from the start..."

He died.

Twenty days later, as High Lord and named heir, you took the throne for yourself.

ending_229.title: The Realm of Jungle
strings: The Realm of Jungle
Civilization, nothing more than wrapping "the Law of the Jungle" in fancy rules.

Sirshana was a prince raised in the filth of back alleys, and you were the courtier who survived the Sultan's Game. What drove you both to seize this realm wasn't homeland restoration, but to create a jungle where only the strongest survive.

Yes, the realm you built where Sirshana as king, you as high lord, was a jungle. The jungle not in trees, but in spirit. Here, soldiers earned rank through mortal combat. Officials clawed their way up over the bodies of rivals. Merchants poisoned competitors' goods with the crown's blessing. Murder became just another trade, revenge a sacred right.

You answered violence with greater violence, and Sirshana were the mightiest predator of all. Every week, hundreds fought to the death in your arenas. The survivors would kneel before you, receiving appointments to fill the endless vacancies in your armies and enforcer squads where vacancies you deliberately created by constantly driving your kingdom to war, to conflict, to bloodshed. The jungle demanded its "apes" tear at each other's throats. The arena became the capital's beating heart. Even children were brought by their parents to witness the slaughter. Let the moralists wail while you and Sirshana reveled in the carnage.

But even the rulers atop the jungle's canopy must face challenges from the beasts below. When the arena's champion, having slain thirty-four men, knelt before Sirshana and begged for the honor to fight his king.

The crowd roared like a raging sea. You almost moved to stop him, but then caught yourself. Even if Sirshana refused, the jungle would hunt you both down. This was the law you had made. The world you had built.

He accepted the challenge.The gladiator's steel found his heart, then you leapt into the pit and cut the gladiator down.

The crowd screamed in ecstasy. Your ears rang. Your pulse hammered like war drums. Your vision blurred. Your thoughts shattered into pieces.

Sirshana's body lay at your feet, yet you could only wonder: should you regret the kingdom you had made together?

ending_230.title: The Realm of Great Cause
strings: The Realm of Great Cause
This is a great cause, accomplished by a great man.

At last you ended the Sultan's Game.The people who supported you gazed up, waiting to see what rule would begin under your hand.

Your first act was to wipe fear from their faces.

You commanded all messengers to proclaim that your realm would no longer be ruled through terror. You wished for all to stretch their body and mind without fear for their life. You wanted your people to create, to labor, to revel, to love, to rejoice. The suffering of others would stir only your compassion and remorse. Never would you poke people's bleeding wounds with a stick as the last Sultan had done.

Then you summoned your Vizier, Nawfal. You told him you would abolish slavery throughout the empire. These former slaves would toil as free men, for their own happiness. Next, you announced the formation of a Noble Council, where each noble's voice would be weighted by the number of freemen in his domain. Those who emancipated their slaves soonest would hold greater sway.

You crushed the nobles' resistance while showering them with favors. You lifted up the oppressed while quietly pruning away the rotten among them. You killed many, indeed, but with these deaths you bought a new world. You did not know if the price was fair. Or perhaps... all necessary deeds were fair.

The work was hard, exhausting. Yet you knew you were loved and supported.

Nawfal toiled sleeplessly by your side, barely pausing to eat, yet his eyes remained sharp, his spirit unbroken. In rare moments of respite, he would silently offer you the water pipe. Outside the palace windows, flowers and dates from your people piled high. Children shrieked "Long live the Sultan!" when you appeared. Young men and women crowded recruitment stations, eager to serve the new empire. Ragged elders beat nobles who spoke ill of you with their canes. Nobles' sons brought their household guards to swear fealty, their eyes burning like live coals.

To be a Sultan beloved, this too is a great cause.

ending_231.title: Laughter at the End
strings: Laughter at the End
How many would remember your laughter, the joyful, self-mocking, or desperate laughter?

You became the new Sultan of this land, raised upon the golden throne by countless hands stained with mud and blood. A Sultan from the people, bound to serve the people. You ruled all, yet belonged to all.

After your coronation, your Vizier, Nawfal and you enacted reforms that shook the empire to its core. The most radical: the total abolition of slavery, and a decree that noble's power would be measured by the number of free subjects in their domains.

These policies were right, striking at tyranny's root where some were stripped of all power while others hoarded too much.

Yet what is right is not always welcome.

Disgruntled officials (of course they were displeased, they gained nothing!) twisted your words. To slaves, they said: "You are free, so take from the freemen! What is freedom otherwise?" To freemen, they whispered: "The Sultan rode to power on slaves' backs, so what sits the throne now but a baseborn usurper?"

Chaos spread. Some slaves didn't know the meaning of freedom and how to survive without their masters, slain by other slaves. Some slaves turned on freemen and nobles, who retaliated with private armies. Cities starved as supply lines frayed. Petty nobles and urban freemen who had never owned slaves found their children crying with hunger. The great nobles, already resentful of your reforms, stood aside. They withheld their soldiers and let slander flourish.

The crisis escalated. You exhausted yourself explaining your true intent...but none listened. The poor cursed you for denying them vengeance, idleness, or the thrill of crushing their betters. The rich said nothing, knowing you meant to take their privileges.

Then the mob came, bearing the last Sultan's banners. They dragged you from your palace, beat you down, and strung you up on a scaffold built just for you.

As death approached, you felt no pain. Only laughter.

ending_232.title: The Shears of Fate
strings: The Shears of Fate
Hear me, Great Sultan: fate was truly a pair of shears.

Some called fate a goddess. Others believed it to be cruel dice. But you knew better: fate was a pair of shears

After your coronation, your Vizier, Nawfal and you enacted reforms that shook the empire to its core. The most radical: the total abolition of slavery, and a decree that noble's power would be measured by the number of free subjects in their domains.

These policies were right, striking at tyranny's root where some were stripped of all power while others hoarded too much.

Yet what is right is not always welcome. 

Chaos spread. Some slaves didn't know the meaning of freedom and how to survive without their masters, slain by other slaves. Some slaves turned on freemen and nobles, who retaliated with private armies. Fields lay fallow. Workshops stood empty. All took to plundering!

Cities starved as supply lines collapsed. Petty nobles and urban freemen who had never owned slaves found their children crying with hunger. So they threw open the gates to rioters, blaming you for everything.

Then they came, bearing the last Sultan's banners. They dragged you from your palace, beat you down, and strung you up on a scaffold built just for you.You didn't resist, not from guilt, but from bitter irony... and crushing disappointment.

The rope bit your wrists. The rabble poked your legs with spearpoints, laughing as you twisted in agony. Your death was made slow, you were thirst, hunger and in pain.

But Fate was a pair of shears.

When moonrise scattered the mob to taverns, shadowy figures overwhelmed your guards. They climbed the scaffold and cut you down with shears.

Half-dead, you were smuggled to the countryside, another corpse dangling in your clothes. Gentle hands stitched your wounds. They parted your cracked lips, pouring in milk and honey. A hundred souls had risked their lives silently...

All whom you'd ever helped. All who knew your true worth.

This was fate. Fate that severed ropes. Fate that cut the thread between malice and its prey. Fate that sheared misfortune. Fate was truly a pair of shears.

ending_233.title: The Hanging Fruit
strings: The Hanging Fruit
Was fighting the only way to make dreams come true? Splendid! You happened to be the finest warrior!

You led your people into the Lapis Lazuli Palace. That was your victory, but more so theirs.

After coronation, you immediately began drafting reforms with Nawfal. The most crucial: abolishing the empire's slavery. In your vision, the future empire wouldn't even have "nobles". Every soul should rise by merit alone. As the ancient sage said, "Are rulers and nobles ordained by birth?"

Naturally, your reforms met resistance. But that your gathered strength couldn't overcome it, which was out of your expectation. Nawfal and you had believed that so many hands, so many fervent eyes, so many souls craving freedom and justice would suffice. Yet a vast empire has its inertia... You pushed hard in the right direction, but not enough to derail ancient wheels.

Nobles slandered you. They ignored your decrees, or obeyed with hollow gestures. Slaves never heard your voice where their masters confined them, exploiting them more brutally lest they realize the law now called them men. You clashed endlessly with bureaucrats and nobles. Friction became conflict. Conflict became civil war. War eventually sputtered out through compromises, leaving only scars upon mutual trust.

It seemed endless. The realm you longed for seemed forever out of reach... You'd toppled a Sultan, yet couldn't savor victory's fruit, the jewel-bright prize still hanging above the realm...

How many more challenges must you face? How much of your spine must wear away to taste its sweetness? A hundred? A thousand? Ten thousand? Would your lifetime suffice?

Ha... No matter! You'd try again and again, a hundred-and-first time, a thousand-and-first, ten-thousand-and-first!

ending_234.title: The Realm of Thousand Colonnades
strings: The Realm of Thousand Colonnades
What thoughts occupy the nobles' minds as they traverse the endless colonnades leading to the royal court...?

Amidst the cheering masses, you strode into the Lapis Lazuli Palace and took your throne as Sultan.

You appointed Maggie - your wife, your partner, your beloved - as Vizier of the realm. This unprecedented appointment sparked outrage, for never in the empire's history had a woman held such high title. To your detractors, you posed a simple question: "Does the empire's past dictate its future? Has its history not brought enough suffering?"

Change came swiftly. You granted regional autonomy to the nobles while reclaiming all military authority for the crown. Maggie spearheaded even more radical reforms, rewriting succession laws to grant women equal inheritance rights, and creating bureaucratic advancement paths open to both sexes.

These twin reforms combined like saltpeter mixing with charcoal and sulfur, igniting fury across the realm. Nobles without armies became more dependent on the Sultan's favor. Female heirs threatened established power structures. Yet... while stripped of military might, the nobles paid fewer taxes to the treasury and bore no burden of maintaining troops. Moreover, you granted them interpretive authority over certain laws, a tantalizing privilege that set their minds racing with possibilities. As for female succession: what noble house lacked at least one capable, ambitious daughter, sister, or aunt?

Your palace changed too. The Lapis Lazuli Palace now stood surrounded by countless colonnades, through which nobles emerged to kneel before you. They spoke for their domains where fine clothes, gold ornaments, even entertainment were forbidden.

Women too began emerging from these colonnades. Shortly after Maggie's reforms, several "natural deaths" and rather violent successions occurred. As result, proud, steel-spined noblewomen appearing at court, whose people fiercely loyal to Maggie. Commoners followed suit where merchants' daughters, landowners' heirs, even tenant farmers' girls began demanding equal treatment, invoking Maggie's name: "This is what Lady Maggie decreed!"

Posterity would name your new world the Realm of Thousand Colonnades. The political structure you crafted would reshape the continent's history. And you would be remembered as one of its greatest Sultans.

ending_235.title: Under Lamplight
strings: Under Lamplight
You cast a shadow upon this realm's history that no hand could erase.

You took the throne as the new Sultan.

Ruling beside you in the Lapis Lazuli Palace stood your wife, your partner in battle, your Vizier - Maggie.

Together you brought winds of change: you reclaimed the nobles' military powers while granting commoners freedom of migration. Maggie devoted herself to rewriting inheritance laws, demanding daughters inherit titles equal to sons.

Your reforms won supporters, yet they hungered for more. The people who raised you to Sultan demanded richer rewards! The nobles hated you, convinced you sought to strip them of gold, tradition, dignity, honor and all.

Soon discontented masses converged on the capital, goaded by anxious nobles and bureaucrats who whispered that petitions could reshape the realm. Their demands were legion: some wanted three hundred sheep, others six wives, or women barred from work, or the old Sultan's games revived...The swelling crowds overwhelmed you. The capital's order crumbled. Vagrants everywhere, brawls in every square, food shortages and filth piling high. Noble conspirators moved through the throngs, whispering, cursing, lining pockets with silver...

At last they charged, screaming incoherent slogans. They stormed the barracks, dragging and killing royal guards, hanging countless charred corpses on the trees. They breached the palace gates. Your guards fought desperately as you commanded them from the golden throne, until rebels hauled a massive log to batter the Lapis Lazuli Palace's side gate! The timber slid across polished floors with terrible force, toppling the throne itself and pinning you beneath its weight.

Lamps overturned, flames licking at gilded arches. Windows shattered, glass glittering like crystal. Your fading reflection danced across broken mirrors as the light left your eyes...

ending_236.title: Recompense of Fate
strings: Recompense of Fate
You may have forgotten what kind of man you were, but they never did.

You ascended the throne as the new Sultan.

You brought winds of change: you reclaimed the nobles' military powers while granting commoners freedom of migration. Maggie devoted herself to rewriting inheritance laws, demanding daughters inherit titles equal to sons.

But your reforms wounded noble interests and they hated you for it. Yet your supporters still cried for more, always more!

Soon discontented masses converged on the capital, goaded by whispers that petitions could reshape the realm. Deliberate agitation fanned this assembly into terrible riot. Noble conspirators moved through the throngs, whispering, cursing, lining pockets with silve...

At last they charged, screaming incoherent slogans. They stormed the barracks, dragging and killing royal guards, hanging countless charred corpses on the trees. They breached the palace gates. Your guards fought desperately as you commanded them from the golden throne, until rebels hauled a massive log to batter the Lapis Lazuli Palace's side gate! The timber slid across polished floors with terrible force, toppling the throne itself and pinning you beneath its weight.

Darkness swallowed your vision. Agony stole your voice, leaving you couldn't even scream. Then a palace slavegirl spotted you, shrieking: "The Sultan! Save the Sultan! Save [player.name]!"

For one frozen moment, the chaos stilled. The mob didn't understand, but all who knew you: all nobles and commoners, handmaids and eunuchs, masters and beggars, they remembered what manner of man you were. They rushed the golden throne.

They twisted garments into ropes, lashing the heavy throne. Men pulled while women lifted, all shouting in unison, until the throne shifted just enough for countless hands to drag you free. Then came Maggie, wild-haired and shrieking curses at the culprits. None had ever seen her so fierce! Physicians bound your broken ribs. Opium smoke filled your lungs, carrying the pain away...

When you woke, the palace's shattered floors remained unrepaired, but the fever had left your people's eyes.

ending_237.title: The Fruit Overhead
strings: The Fruit Overhead
One day, you would pluck that fruit overhead.

You led your people into the Lapis Lazuli Palace. That was your victory, but more so theirs.

After coronation, you immediately began drafting reforms with Maggie. The most crucial: stripping the nobility of their right to raise armies, weakening their power while strengthening the crown. In your vision, nobles freed from the burden of maintaining private forces would see their troops disbanded or absorbed by your generals, then redeployed to the empire's key fortresses.

Naturally, your reforms met resistance. But that your gathered strength couldn't overcome it, which you'd anticipated. Yet neither you nor Maggie, ever your steadfast ally, would retreat. A vast empire has its inertia.To push hard in the right direction, even if not enough to derail ancient wheels, was victory enough.

Nobles slandered you. They ignored your decrees, or obeyed with hollow gestures. Slaves never heard your voice where their masters confined them, exploiting them more brutally lest they realize the law now called them men. You clashed endlessly with bureaucrats and nobles. Friction became conflict. Conflict became civil war. War eventually sputtered out through compromises, leaving only scars upon mutual trust.

It seemed endless. The realm you longed for seemed forever out of reach... You'd toppled a Sultan, yet couldn't savor victory's fruit, the jewel-bright prize still hanging above the realm...

How many more challenges must you face? How much of your spine must wear away to taste its sweetness? A hundred? A thousand? Ten thousand? Would your lifetime suffice?

Ha... No matter! You'd try again and again. You and Maggie stood united before the court, glaring down your foes while behind the curtains, your hands clasped tight.

You feared nothing.

ending_238.title: The Realm of People
strings: The Realm of People
The first cry of a Sultan at birth was no louder than that of a slave’s child.

You ascended the Golden Throne, and Riel became the Vizier.

At her first court gathering, Riel stood bewildered. Well-dressed courtiers bowed and offered greetings which only deepened her confusion. But what truly galled her were their honeyed words:

"Your eyes shine like twin moons."

"The hue of your skin is most... refined."

"Your attire today is... ah... remarkable."

Riel's fury mounted until she seized the nearest noble by his embroidered collar. "Moon? What moon?" she demanded. "I've seen the moon, it looks nothing like my damn eyes!" The man stammered, eyes darting everywhere but her face.

Then she understood. Ah, these soft city-dwellers feared to look at her! They flinched from her warrior's muscles, recoiled from the bloodstink still clinging to her, refused to remember how this woman - this slave, this outsider - had led a bandit horde to seat a Sultan on his throne. To them, she might as well have been some demon from beyond the stars.

With a snort, Riel released the trembling noble and turned to you.

"Now I see why you made me Vizier, [player.name]."

Thus began your remaking of the realm from its foundations. You broke the noble's power, shattered the slave chains, decreed all would rise by wit and worth alone. First in the armies, then the bureaucracies, finally the very nobility. Riel stood unwavering at your side, clearing obstacles with threats, terror, and when needed, her own scarred fists. She rounded up the capital's worst cutthroats, beat them senseless one by one, then forged them into her personal guard. Your opponents called them a band of demons who knew only one rule: "[player.name]'s enemies must die."

News of Riel's appointment spread like wildfire through the hinterlands. Her tribal kin came, and the mountain folk, the steppe riders, the coastal fishmen. All who'd been chained as slaves now heard the new Sultan called them the People.

Not monsters, not slaves, not chattel nor commodities, but people - whole, independent, and no different from any other in this realm.

That was a worthy miracle.

ending_239.title: The Guilty Stone
strings: The Guilty Stone
They buried their would-be savior with a sharp stone.

You claimed the Golden Throne, naming Riel, the foreign brute from the Dark Alley, as your Vizier.

This appointment alone would have been outrage enough, but your reforms of abolishing slavery, dismantling noble privilege, proved you weren't content to be just another Sultan. They had expected another wolf to feed, another name to chant in their hollow hymns. Instead, they found a ruler who meant to rule.

The realm convulsed. Slaves and ruined peasants rallied under your banners, sweeping from every territory. They slayed masters and looted freemen's stores. Minor noble and burghers, forced to choose between their livelihoods and loyalty, hired cutthroats to guard what little remained.

Riel fought like a demon for you. She recruited every alley-born killer, crushed noble houses without mercy, gave shelter to runaway slaves... yet still you lacked the strength to break the tradition of this very land. When the riots reached the capital, your royal guards and Riel's ragtag forces couldn't hold the streets. The army, its officers whispering treason, refused your orders. So you took up your sword yourself.

You walked among the mob, calling for calm while cutting down looters until the first stone struck. A jagged rock hurled from the crowd split your brow. As you fell, Riel caught you, shielding your body with her own as more stones rained down

"He tried to save you, you fucking sheep!" she screamed, trying to protect you in her arms. "Can't you tell friend from foe? Or do you like wearing chains?!"

Those were the last words you heard.

ending_240.title: The Howling Wilds
strings: The Howling Wilds
Unexpected allies descend like gods upon the stage.

You ascended the Golden Throne, with Riel, the barbarian from the Dark Alley, as your vizier.

Initially, Riel didn't realize what her title truly meant, not until you started enforcing a series of radical reforms, primarily abolishing slavery.

"Abolishing slavery? The slavers must die, right? Kill them—hang them?" Riel's eyes suddenly lit up, "Let me do it! Let me do it!"

Then, countless uprisings rained down on the Lapis Lazuli floor. Slaves and bankrupt farmers roamed the territories under your banner, attacking slave owners and plundering the Property of free citizens; many minor nobles and middle-class commoners were forced to become your enemies, hiring goons to protect their homes and families...

When the waves of rebellion reached the capital, some high-ranking noble officers incited a Troop that should have resisted the rioters to refuse your orders; this exposed the palace to widespread acts of violence consuming the city. You had been unable to find Riel for days, forcing you to pick up a sword alongside the palace guards.

Suddenly, a strange squad rushed out from the alleyway—they wore no uniforms, held no standard weapons, but each of them, regardless of age or gender, had a swift stride and sharp eyes; they were true warriors.

This group quickly inserted themselves between you and the rioters, led by an older woman draped in feathers and wielding a wooden staff. She stepped out from the ranks, scrutinizing you up and down—and you suddenly saw Riel standing behind her!

"I heard you have supreme authority, yet you don't seem like much..." The old woman's voice was rough and hoarse, with a few cackling laughs, then waved her hand at the rioters, "The young girl said your power was so vast it could provide our people with shelter... she also said you would free all slaves and carve out slavers' livers for us to consume. As long as we help you solve this problem."

Riel frantically signaled you, looking as tame as a fledgling chick beside the old lady.

"Well, let's see, let's see... if the city folk's king lies... then we're going to taste the king's liver."

She struck the ground heavily with her cane, once, twice, thrice.

Her warriors screamed a deafening war cry, then charged at the Mob. Everyone in the city knew the barbarians were cannibalistic. The warriors' painted bodies, human bone necklaces, and strange roars greatly intensified these fearsome legends...

The Mob was instantly scattered. You immediately ordered the arrest of those opposition nobles and treacherous officers who incited the populace, giving their livers to the tribal warriors.

The old woman, being the matriarch, should have the first taste. Her gruesome dining scene on a living person's abdomen with a bloody hearth was so shocking... that no one dared visit that plaza for a long time.

You finally managed to secure the Sultan's throne.

ending_241.title: The Exile Within
strings: The Exile Within
How terrible it is to be exiled from your own palace!

You claimed the Golden Throne, becoming the realm's new Sultan. You raised your allies, cast down your foes, and named Riel the savage as your Vizier. You fought to steer this broken land toward dawn... but can a single hand truly right a capsizing ship?

Your decrees met silent resistance at every turn. Even those who once cheered you now muttered in doubt. You ordered lands measured and divided equally, so the slothful reaped as much as the laboring woman. Was this justice? You demanded all earn their bread by toil, so the sick and pregnant withered in gutters. Was this mercy? You declared slaves equal to masters, stripped nobles of privilege, but who stood with you? Slaves whose eyes and ears had been sealed by their masters? Oh, your supporters packed the court halls. But in the fields, the alleys, the taverns... your name soured on every tongue. Riel fought for you with tooth and claw. Her bandit horde prowled the capital's underbelly, carving loyalty through fear. But they were too few, and the empire too vast...

So you ran. Chased from crisis to crisis, forever stamping out revolts that sprouted like leeches on your skin. The moment you paused, another rebellion's jaws snapped at your heels.

You dared not linger in your own palace. To sit still meant letting guilt gnaw your bones. Though no amount of sweat could straighten this crooked realm, you kept fleeing forward on some self-made exile of atonement...

Perhaps only death will finally let your flesh catch up to your weary soul.

ending_242.title: The Realm of People
strings: The Realm of People
The first cry of a Sultan at birth was no louder than that of a slave’s child.

To take gold and power from one man's pocket and give it to another, that is the work of thieves.

And it is precisely what you did after claiming the throne. You believed rulership should belong not to bloodlines and titles, but to hands calloused by plow and spear. So you stripped the nobility of their monopolies, threw every trade open to free competition. You tore down the caste barriers to imperial examinations. Now any man, woman, or former slave could rise by merit alone. Coin by coin, you emptied the nobles' coffers into the poor's palms that once held nothing, but now could at least fill children's bellies.

Every step met resistance like a wall of spears. But you stood surrounded by loyal blades, and none more surprising than your Vizier, Alim. That former leader of thieves in Dark Alley slipped into his new role as easily as a dagger between ribs. He still wore patched but spotless linens, still had sticky fingers. He was likely to be the only Vizier in history to pick nobles' pockets at council meetings, yet his political instincts were razor-sharp and his suppport were solid.

Three years of setbacks and hard-won victories passed before you'd replaced every key official with reformers. Around you gathered a new breed of talents who poor-born but clear-eyed, ready to bleed for this remade empire.

The tide receded at last. Privilege-stripped nobles found themselves swimming naked, scrambling to adapt. Meanwhile, fierce young minds climbed tooth and nail, knowing their Sultan saw them not as slaves or chattel, but as people.

Your empire flourished. Commoners began hanging your portrait where icons once stood, not as decoration, but as something holy.

ending_243.title: The City Ablaze
strings: The City Ablaze
When your realm burns, you might as well admire the flames.

The nobles did nothing when you overthrew the last Sultan. To them, it was merely exchanging one tyrant for another, swapping the names in their pretty hymns. But when you began your reforms, their indifference turned to shock, then rage, then venomous hatred.

You demanded an end to noble privilege, especially their monopolies. Every trade would now face open competition. This wasn't governance; this was reaching into their pockets and stealing their coins. Brothels (how much gold and sweat had Madam Buthayna spilled for her House of Delights license?), gambling dens, silk-dyeing workshops and goldsmith guilds, all now up for grabs by common hands.

So they tried bribes. They whispered in your courtiers' ears. But your Vizier, Alim, the former leader of thieves, handled bluebloods like a cutpurse handles drunkards: polite, but immovable. You replaced every official with loyalists, then turned your axe toward the local bureaucracies... You weren't playing at rule. You meant to be a great Sultan.

And that simply wouldn't do. To those who profited from the old ways, a reforming Sultan was worse than a tyrant. You were an obstacle.

In your second month, fire erupted across the capital's western quarter. The flames spread unnaturally fast. From the palace, you saw the sky turn orange. Iron Guards sent to quell but could not make it.

Something was wrong. Fire doesn't refuse to die. So you went yourself, steel at your side. Heat lashed your face as you stepped through smoke. Then you saw it: an empty oil cask.

Figures wrapped in wet rags burst from burning buildings. Your guards, watching the flames, reacted too late when assassins' knives found your heart.

ending_244.title: Humble Friends
strings: Humble Friends
An humble friend matters little. But many? That is another matter entirely.

When you toppled the previous Sultan, the Nobles assumed changing rulers meant no more than replacing one jackal with another and revising the preface of lofty compositions. However, when the new Sultan began enacting a series of reforms, they progressed from amazement to anger and finally seethed with hatred.

You demanded the removal of noble privileges, especially exclusive business rights, seeking open competition across all industries. This equated to extracting funds from noble pockets, their largest gains sprouting from these privileged business sectors. Such as Brothels (Ms. Buthayna must've paid a fortune, endured numerous tears and sweat for a license to start the House of Delights!) and gambling houses, in addition to silk dyeing workshops and Gold processing endeavors.

This was unacceptable. For the power holders who benefited from the setup, the country didn't require a progressive Sultan... you were just too bothersome.

In your second month of ascension, a sudden conflagration occurred on one side of the capital. The flames spread sharply, and even within the palace grounds, you could see the sky-high blaze, and groups tasked to extinguish the flames all failed at their attempts.

The incident seemed too strange for the blaze to continue unchecked. Just as you prepared to personally investigate, Alim barged into the Lapis Lazuli Hall with a gang of scoundrels tied up and bound, dragging along some sooty, singed individuals. Their blackened faces and the burnt wooden scent spoke for themselves.

"I've brought you something, oh exalted Sultan..." Alim performed an exaggerated court gesture—"heh, heh, heh... my pups in the city noticed a few individuals lugging oil drums toward the fiery spots... some others reported that these folks were spotted wandering around the Dark Alley with saturated heavy cloaks. Later, one streetwalker recognized one of them as a client, one who recently came into a windfall and bragged about doing something grand to change the country..."

He placed a foot gently on the bound person's body, looking down at him with affection and care.

"Our friends here planned to ignite around the armory, hoping the royal guards would get diverted to extinguish the fire so they could sneak into the palace and attempt regicide, correct? Perhaps if fortune smiles upon them, awaiting the Sultan to oversee the fire-fighting efforts firsthand would be convenient, am I right?"

Listening to him sent a chill up your spine... afterward, you sincerely thanked Alim.

"No need to thank me, oh esteemed Sultan, not at all! It is this city's inconspicuous and humble folks aiding you, for you regard them as humans! They are your inconspicuous friends!"

He waved it off with a smile. Those ash-covered pups proudly pulled back their shoulders.

This marked the last gasp of the dissent nobles, executed under the charge of attempted regicide, securing your throne.

ending_245.title: The Exile Within
strings: The Exile Within
How terrible it is to be exiled from your own palace!

Your decrees met silent resistance at every turn. Even those who once cheered you now muttered in doubt. You ordered lands measured and divided equally, so the slothful reaped as much as the laboring woman. Was this justice? You demanded all earn their bread by toil, so the sick and pregnant withered in gutters. Was this mercy?

So you ran. Chased from crisis to crisis, forever stamping out revolts that sprouted like leeches on your skin. Alim prowled the city's underbelly, his street rats serving as your hands and eyes. Yet what did they know of politics? Honesty and pickpocketing make poor councilors in marble halls.

The moment you paused, another rebellion's jaws snapped at your heels. You dared not linger in your own palace. To sit still meant letting guilt gnaw your bones. Though no amount of sweat could straighten this crooked realm, you kept fleeing forward on some self-made exile of atonement...

Perhaps only death will finally let your flesh catch up to your weary soul.

ending_246.title: The Realm of Sages
strings: The Realm of Sages
This realm is an academy where the path to wisdom is taught.

To overthrow a tyrant, to build a realm, to hand it to sages to rule, then retire to a life of leisure yourself - what could be a sweeter tale?

When you proudly placed Nawfal upon the Sultan's throne, believing the script would unfold as planned, his smile made your gut twist with foreboding...

Upon coronation, Sultan Nawfal immediately established a council. Every noble's voting power would be weighted by the number of souls in their domain. And you? You were made the Speaker of Council, tasked with presenting all motions to the Sultan.

It still sounded like grueling work which need you to mediate disputes, to sooth tempers sparked by the new order. But you accepted. After all, Nawfal was the Sultan. True power remained with him... Didn't it?

Then, the most benevolent and wise Sultan issued a decree surrendering all executive authority to the council! He retained only veto power and the right to call dissolution votes! Of course, he graciously listed his new duties: overseeing construction of the Royal University, establishing the Archives... all tasks he'd have happily done anyway!

This was dumping the entire burden back on you! That cunning bastard! You knew the political rival was vile, but one wearing the crown? Now you had to obey his every whim!

As you raged at Nawfal, he laughed until tears streamed down his face. You'd never seen him so delighted. When his mirth subsided, he clasped your shoulder.

"The best ruler is one who doesn't wish to rule. And though I never desired the Golden Throne... you gave it to me. So [player.name], by that measure, you remain this realm's finest ruler."

Together, you built a wonderful realm.

ending_247.title: Laughter at the End
strings: Laughter at the End
How many would remember your laughter, the joyful, self-mocking, or desperate laughter?

Nawfal became this nation's new Sultan, with you as Vizier, and you established a brand-new realm. Countless muddy, bloodstained hands lifted you to the Golden Throne—kings of the people serving the people: ruler to all yet servant to all.

After coronation, Nawfal launched numerous revolutionary reform policies, completely eradicating the country's slavery system and demanding lords apportion authority per their free citizens' count.

These policies were certainly correct, targeting the root of tyranny—a faction enjoying all the rights while another had none—

Yet, what's right isn't always welcomed.

In the policy implementation phase, discontented courtiers (naturally discontent, since they gained nothing!) deliberately distorted and defiled your intentions; they told the slaves, you are free, meaning you can now seize from free citizens; otherwise, how is it freedom? Then they told the free citizens, those slaves raised the Sultan to the throne, it's a coup, it's unjust! Have you forgotten the former Sultan's benevolence?

Soon, local conflicts began to erupt. Some slaves did not wish to lose their masters, unsure how to embrace freedom; thus, they were first killed by their peers. Subsequently, slaves attacked free citizens and nobles, the latter forming private forces to retaliate; due to the local chaos, urban supplies began to dwindle, with even cities that originally didn't practice slavery seeing their commoners and minor nobles unable to feed their families. Major nobles and lords, already resentful of your abrupt state changes, remained indifferent, refused to lend support, even encouraging defamatory speech against you within their territories.

The situation escalated rapidly, and you and Nawfal exhausted yourselves attempting to explain your true intentions... but the people didn't care. The impoverished felt you failed to deliver what they desired, like unearned gains, revenge against the affluent, trampling on others' rights; while the wealthy realized you threatened their interests and chose silence.

A mob bearing the former Sultan's banner stormed your palace, dragging Nawfal out, beating him to the ground, hanging him on a wooden scaffold erected specifically for him. You were hung an arm's length away from him.

As death approached, you felt no pain, merely a strong desire to laugh.

ending_248.title: The Shears of Fate
strings: The Shears of Fate
Hear me, Great Sultan: fate was truly a pair of shears.

Some called fate a goddess. Others believed it to be cruel dice. But you knew better: fate was a pair of shears.

Nawfal ascended as this land's new Sultan, with you as his Vizier, enacting reforms that shook the empire to its core. The most radical: the total abolition of slavery, and a decree that nobles' power would be measured by the number of free subjects in their domains.

These policies were right, striking at tyranny's root where some were stripped of all power while others hoarded too much.

Yet what is right is not always welcome.

Chaos spread. Some slaves didn't know the meaning of freedom and how to survive without their masters, slain by other slaves. Some slaves turned on freemen and nobles, who retaliated with private armies. Fields lay fallow. Workshops stood empty. All took to plundering!

Cities starved as supply lines collapsed. Petty nobles and urban freemen who had never owned slaves found their children crying with hunger. So they threw open the gates to rioters, blaming the Sultan for everything.

Then they came, bearing the last Sultan's banners. They dragged you and Sultan from your palace, beat you down, and strung you up on scaffolds built just for you. You didn't resist, not from guilt, but from bitter irony... and crushing disappointment.

The rope bit your wrists. The rabble poked your legs with spearpoints, laughing as you twisted in agony. Your death was made slow; you were thirsty, hungry and in pain.

But Fate was a pair of shears.

When moonrise scattered the mob to taverns, shadowy figures overwhelmed your guards. They climbed the scaffold and cut you down with shears.

Half-dead, you were smuggled to the countryside, another corpse dangling in your clothes. Gentle hands stitched your wounds. They parted your cracked lips, pouring in milk and honey. A hundred souls had risked their lives silently...

All whom you'd ever helped. All who knew your true worth.

This was fate. Fate that severed ropes. Fate that cut the thread between malice and its prey. Fate that sheared misfortune. Fate was truly a pair of shears.

ending_249.title: The Hanging Fruit
strings: The Hanging Fruit
Was fighting the only way to make dreams come true? Splendid! You happened to be the finest warrior!

You and Nawfal have taken over this country. This is your victory, and even more so the people's victory.

After ascending to the throne, you immediately began drafting and implementing various reforms with Nawfal, the most significant of which is the abolition of the empire's slavery system. In your vision, the future empire should not even have "Nobles" and people should only rise by their own abilities. As the ancient sages said, "Kings and princes, are they inherently noble?"

Evidently, the reform faced numerous resistances; yet the forces of progress could not break through these obstacles, something you never anticipated. You and Nawfal expected that so many people, so many hands, so many eager eyes—so many souls yearning for freedom and justice—should be enough? But in reality, a vast empire has its inertia... Nawfal put all their strength to push the ancient wheel in the right direction, but the force was insufficient to completely derail it.

The Nobles began to slander Nawfal and attack you, refusing to execute the reform orders. Even when they did, it was just pretense. The slaves could not hear your voice; their masters kept them confined, exploiting them more cruelly, fearing they would realize they are now complete individuals by law. The new government clashed continuously with the bureaucratic system and Noble forces, escalating into local civil wars, which eventually subsided through compromises but left terrifying scars on the trust between you.

It seems all this will never stop; the country you long for seems will never come... even though you have overthrown a Sultan, you cannot enjoy the fruits of victory; those fruits shine like jewels... you can see them, hanging over the country.

Sometimes you and Nawfal have a drink together, and the topic always leads to the same question: How many more challenges must be faced, how many vertebrae worn down, before we can taste its sweetness? A hundred, a thousand, or ten thousand? Is this life enough?

Ha... who cares! Anyway, you'll keep trying, for the hundred and first, the thousand and first, the ten thousand and first time!

Cheers!

ending_250.title: The Realm of Balance
strings: The Realm of Balance
As vessels overflow when filled, and moons must wane when rounded. Balance stands as the wisest design.

At last you ended the Sultan's Game.The people who supported you gazed up, waiting to see what rule would begin under your hand.

Your first act was to wipe fear from their faces. You commanded all messengers to proclaim that your realm would no longer be ruled through terror. You wished for all to stretch their body and mind without fear for their life. You wanted your people to create, to labor, to revel, to love, to rejoice. The suffering of others would stir only your compassion and remorse. Never would you poke people’s bleeding wounds with a stick as the last Sultan had done.

Then you summoned your Vizier, you told him you would abolish slavery throughout the empire. These former slaves would toil as free men, for their own happiness. Next, you announced the formation of a Noble Council, where each noble's voice would be weighted by the number of freemen in his domain.

Those who emancipated their slaves soonest would hold greater sway.

You crushed the nobles' resistance while showering them with favors. You lifted up the oppressed while quietly pruning away the rotten among them. You killed many, indeed, but with these deaths you bought a new world. You did not know if the price was fair. Or perhaps... all necessary deeds were fair.

The freed craved for more. The dispossessed challenge your authority. Balancing these forces is like drawing a line between desire and humanity.

Yet you succeed. You dance upon that razor's edge, never falling into the abyss of indulgence, nor the inferno of tyranny.

ending_251.title: Laughter at the End
strings: Laughter at the End
How many would remember your laughter, the joyful, self-mocking, or desperate laughter?

You became the new Sultan of this land, raised upon the golden throne by countless hands stained with mud and blood. A Sultan from the people, bound to serve the people. You ruled all, yet belonged to all.

After your coronation, your Vizier, [table.宰相.name] and you enacted reforms that shook the empire to its core. The most radical: the total abolition of slavery, and a decree that noble's power would be measured by the number of free subjects in their domains.

These policies were right, striking at tyranny's root where some were stripped of all power while others hoarded too much.

Yet what is right is not always welcome.

Disgruntled officials (of course they were displeased, they gained nothing!) twisted your words. To slaves, they said: "You are free, so take from the freemen! What is freedom otherwise?" To freemen, they whispered: "The Sultan rode to power on slaves' backs, so what sits the throne now but a baseborn usurper?"

Chaos spread. Some slaves didn't know the meaning of freedom and how to survive without their masters, slain by other slaves. Some slaves turned on freemen and nobles, who retaliated with private armies. Cities starved as supply lines frayed. Petty nobles and urban freemen who had never owned slaves found their children crying with hunger. The great nobles, already resentful of your reforms, stood aside. They withheld their soldiers and let slander flourish.

The crisis escalated. You exhausted yourself explaining your true intent...but none listened. The poor cursed you for denying them vengeance, idleness, or the thrill of crushing their betters. The rich said nothing, knowing you meant to take their privileges.
