Then the mob came, bearing the last Sultan's banners. They dragged you from your palace, beat you down, and strung you up on a scaffold built just for you.

As death approached, you felt no pain. Only laughter.

Half-dead, you were smuggled to the countryside, another corpse dangling in your clothes. Gentle hands stitched your wounds. They parted your cracked lips, pouring in milk and honey. A hundred souls had risked their lives silently...

All whom you'd ever helped. All who knew your true worth.

ending_253.title: The Hanging Fruit
strings: The Hanging Fruit
Was fighting the only way to make dreams come true? Splendid! You happened to be the finest warrior!

You led your people into the Lapis Lazuli Palace. That was your victory, but more so theirs.

After coronation, you immediately began drafting reforms with [table.宰相.name]. The most crucial: abolishing the empire's slavery. In your vision, the future empire wouldn't even have "nobles". Every soul should rise by merit alone. As the ancient sage said, "Are rulers and nobles ordained by birth?"

Naturally, your reforms met resistance. But that your gathered strength couldn't overcome it, which was out of your expectation. You and [table.宰相.name] had believed that so many hands, so many fervent eyes, so many souls craving freedom and justice would suffice. Yet a vast empire has its inertia... You pushed hard in the right direction, but not enough to derail ancient wheels.

Nobles slandered you. They ignored your decrees, or obeyed with hollow gestures. Slaves never heard your voice where their masters confined them, exploiting them more brutally lest they realize the law now called them men. You clashed endlessly with bureaucrats and nobles. Friction became conflict. Conflict became civil war. War eventually sputtered out through compromises, leaving only scars upon mutual trust.

It seemed endless. The realm you longed for seemed forever out of reach... You'd toppled a Sultan, yet couldn't savor victory's fruit, the jewel-bright prize still hanging above the realm...

How many more challenges must you face? How much of your spine must wear away to taste its sweetness? A hundred? A thousand? Ten thousand? Would your lifetime suffice?

Ha... No matter! You'd try again and again, a hundred-and-first time, a thousand-and-first, ten-thousand-and-first!

ending_254.title: The Realm of Heroes
strings: The Realm of Heroes
Not only does history remember your name, but the myths that follow shall also bear your tale.

The Sultan fell before you.

You raised your sword high, and the people around you erupted in maddening cheers—an eviscerate hero, a new ruler who defeated the Sultan! This was an unprecedented moment of glory the empire had never known— mere mortals reaching such heights!

Soon, the enormous dragon head was placed above your throne—the empire's most skilled goldsmith created golden reliefs depicting the dragon slaying story, embedded beside the throne—they glared at the officials, scaring some timid ones to their knees the first time they saw the skull!

But you, the most extraordinary hero of mankind, you sat firmly on the throne. You held a longsword tempered by dragon breath, donned in a cloak of dragon scales. Standing beside you was your Vizier, Nawfal. Because your legitimacy seems overwhelmingly strong, the preparations you made for the throne were immensely thorough, the transition of governance was smoother than flipping a fish in a pan.

The Vizier wasn't used to this. They found themselves many tasks, suggesting the abolition of slavery, granting women equal political rights, removing Noble monopolistic rights, and establishing a Noble council—all suggestions the previous Sultan dismissed contemptuously, all seeming hard to execute.

However, when you proposed these suggestions to the officials, there was not a single objection! People stared in amazement at the dragon head, transfixed by your dragon scales... a legendary creature indeed existed, and it was slain by our Sultan! Anything a hero of such stature leads will surely succeed—abolishing slavery, reducing Noble profits, liberating women, forming a council—such compared to slaying a giant dragon are as simple as a child's game!

Thus, you easily and swiftly transformed the country. Ancient traditions were subtly replaced, new rules granted greater liberty to people; more smiles appeared, markets prospered, fewer children went hungry.

To this day, your sculptures still exist all over the continent, and people will always pray to you, hoping you will grant them the courage to overcome setbacks; they knelt before you, and when they stood up, they were filled with strength.

ending_255.title: The Realm of Conquest
strings: The Realm of Conquest
A warrior’s fate is to repeat his deeds of valor until death claims him.

The Sultan fell before you.

You raised your sword high, and the crowds around you erupted into wild cheers—an eviscerate hero, a new ruler who defeated the Sultan! The empire never experienced a more glorious moment—mere mortals reaching an unparalleled realm!

Soon, the colossal dragon head was installed above your throne—the empire's most talented goldsmiths sculpted gold reliefs of the dragon slaying deeds, affixed beside the throne—it eyed the courtiers, some timid ministers collapsed out of fear at their first sight of this skull!

However, the satisfaction from defeating the dragon soon began to wane. You grew restless... every time the court nobles bickered and chittered, and every time Nawfal brought budget and report complaints to you, your discomfort only grew.

At last, you decided to march your army west, seek out a colossal sea monster lurking in a trench—you tallied all worthy hunts, this one closest to the nation!

All your soldiers rejoiced at your decision, while nobles, officials, and ministers stood aghast. Nawfal tried all they could to deter you, "How can a Sultan leave the nation? You still consider yourself just a daredevil seeking glory?!"—But you couldn't wait any longer; a hero who gained the throne through such acts should create ever more heroic deeds!

First was the sea monster, next came the golden-winged serpent, then the Banshee's forest, your troops ravaged through the world's frightful domains; should a local king, lord, or chief impede your passage, you simply annihilated their nation too.

Countless challenges, countless conquests, endless bloodshed! Such a life befits you! You must always run forward, forever fleeing that distant call behind:

"Return—you are the Sultan—you have responsibilities—!"

ending_256.title: The Shrike's Forest
strings: The Shrike's Forest
Slaying a dragon is easy while ruling is not.

The Sultan fell before you.

You raised your sword high, and the crowd roared in frenzy. You were a dragonslayer, a new ruler who had conquered the Sultan! Never before had the empire known such glory, that a mortal could ascend to such heights!

Yet, ruling proved far harder than slaying a dragon. You brought too much change, too swiftly, without securing enough loyal supporters. The nobles seized upon your dragonslayer fame to enrich themselves. They levied higher taxes in your name, claiming the gold was tribute for you. They seized the lands of free folk, declaring them fit for your palaces. They raised private armies, boasting they would aid your conquests...

Their treachery gnawed at you. At last, you struck down one scheming noble, and the rest grew meek as lambs.

Months later, another noble took peasant girls, claiming they were gifts for you... so you killed him too. This time, several courtiers dared protest, calling the punishment too harsh, so you silenced them by executing the least useful among them.

Thus, you learned that bloodshed was the surest way to rule. The more you killed, the smoother your reign. Gallows sprouted in the cities, corpses swaying like grim fruit. Before long, men began calling your capital "The Shrike's Forest".

Your enemies multiplied, your friends dwindled. People feared you - not for the dragon you slew, but for the countless men you butchered. Your halls of Lapis Lazuli fell silent, for none dared speak lest they die. Occasionally, crude pamphlets surfaced among the smallfolk, depicting you as The Dragonslayer Sultan: a winged, fire-breathing monster... so you burned the makers of these pamphlets, as a true dragon would do.

Let them whisper. Let them curse. Were they seated upon your throne, they would fare no better.

ending_257.title: The Realm of Heroes
strings: The Realm of Heroes
Not only does history remember your name, but the myths that follow shall also bear your tale.

The Sultan fell before you.

You raised your sword high, and the crowd roared in frenzy. You were a dragonslayer, a blade who had conquered the Sultan with justice! Never before had the empire known such glory, that a mortal could ascend to such heights!

Soon, the great dragon's head was mounted upon your throne. The empire's finest goldsmiths had forged reliefs of your deed, set into the arms of the seat and it gazed upon the court. Some weak-hearted courtiers, upon first laying eyes on the skull, trembled so badly their knees gave way!

And you, the greatest hero the world has ever known, sat upon that throne. In your hand was a sword tempered in dragonfire, upon your shoulders a cloak of its scales, and at your side stood your Vizier, Adila. Your claim was so unquestionable, your preparations for the throne so thorough, that the transition of power was as smooth as a hot knife through butter.

You had once doubted whether Adila could bear the weight of the Vizier, but actually that was last thing you need to worry about. At once, she set forth sweeping reforms: equal voice for women in council, changes to the imperial succession so that daughters need not wed to claim their birthright, and a new meritocracy for the armies and royal guard: strength alone would decide, not sex, not blood, not race.

Yet when you presented them to the court, not a single voice rose in opposition. The nobles stared, drunk with awe, at the dragon's head, at the scales upon your shoulders... Such a creature had truly existed, and our Sultan had slain it! A man of such greatness was leading us, what could possibly fail? Freeing women? Letting daughters inherit? Breaking the nobles' grip on command? Compared to slaying a dragon, these were but child's play!

And so, swiftly and surely, you and Adila remade the realm. Ancient traditions were deftly replaced, new laws granted greater freedom. Smiles multiplied, markets flourished, fewer children went hungry.

To this day, your statues stand in every corner of the land. People still pray to you, begging for the courage to face their trials. They kneel in reverence, and when they rise again, their eyes burn with newfound strength.

Were it not for your restraint, Adila might have executed several ministers daring enough to rebut her.
