ending_260.title: The Realm of Heroes
strings: The Realm of Heroes
Not only does history remember your name, but the myths that follow shall also bear your tale.

The Sultan has fallen before you.

You raise your sword high above as the masses around you erupt in frenzied cheers—a Dragonslayer hero, a valiant blade that vanquished the Sultan! This is a moment of unparalleled glory the empire has never witnessed; mere mortals reaching such heights!

Soon, the massive dragon's head decorates your throne—a masterpiece of gold engravings crafted by the empire's finest goldsmith captures the epic tale of dragonslaying, set beside your throne—watching over the assembly; those faint of heart among the ministers stumble in awe at their first sight of this head!

And you, the greatest hero among men, sit upon the throne. You wield the longsword tempered by dragon breath and cloak of dragon scales, with your Vizier, Jabal, by your side. Your claim was so unquestionable, your preparations for the throne so thorough, that the transition of power was as smooth as a hot knife through butter.

Jabal has little interest in policy matters—except for one: he believes the nation must encourage the rise of more heroes. So he oversaw the founding of a state-sponsored Adventurers' Guild, accepting commissions from across the empire and the continent beyond. The adventurers gathered there are trained and inspected by him and Adila, and a portion of their earnings is turned over to the state.

When you present this proposal to the ministers, no opposition is voiced! People gaze entranced at the dragon's head, envisioning your draconic conquest... Such magnificent beings truly exist and have been felled by our Sultan! Led by such greatness, success in all pursuits is inevitable— training more heroes? Excellent! The world needs more heroes!

Thus, you swiftly and successfully transform the nation, weaving ancient traditions into new order and granting people more freedom; bringing smiles, prosperity to markets, and reducing hunger.

To this day, your statues dot the continent and people pray for the courage to overcome adversity; they kneel faithfully and rise anew, eyes filled with strength.

ending_261.title: The Realm of Conquest
strings: The Realm of Conquest
A warrior’s fate is to repeat his deeds of valor until death claims him.

The Sultan has fallen before you.

You raise your sword high and the surrounding people burst into a frenzy of cheers—a dragonslayer hero, a new ruler vanquishing the Sultan! A moment of unrivaled brilliance the empire has never experienced, mortals achieving such eminence!

Soon, a massive dragon's head adorns your throne—the empire's finest goldsmith has crafted intricate gold engravings depicting the dragon's tale, set beside your throne—watchful over the assembly; timid ministers stumble in shock at first sight of the head!

However, the triumph over a great dragon quickly dims; restlessness seeps in with each squabble from nobles, each clerk grumbling over budgets and expenditures, each time Jabal disappears again, shirking his share of court duties... This vizier proves to be no help at all. He once proposed founding an Adventurers' Guild, only to be laughed out of the court; afterward, he began avoiding council altogether.

Eventually, you lead your army westward, challenging a mighty sea beast lurking in the trench—a magnificent target nearest your lands!

Warriors rejoice at your decision, while nobles and ministers gape in shock. Having ascended to the Sultan's throne through heroics, must you not pursue more feats of grandeur?

First the sea beast, then the golden feather serpent, and finally the banshee forest, your army ravages through the world's darkest corners; when barriers arise from local kings, lords, or chieftains forbidding passage, you simply obliterate the state.

Challenges unending, conquests innumerable, bloodshed boundless! Such a life befits you! Rush forward evermore; only this escape that distant call:

"Return—you are Sultan—your duties await—!"

ending_262.title: The Shrike's Forest
strings: The Shrike's Forest
Slaying a dragon is easy while ruling is not.

The Sultan fell before you.

You raised your sword high, and the crowd roared in frenzy. You were a dragonslayer, a new ruler who had conquered the Sultan! Never before had the empire known such glory, that a mortal could ascend to such heights!

Yet, ruling proved far harder than slaying a dragon. You brought too much change, too swiftly, without securing enough loyal supporters. The nobles seized upon your dragonslayer fame to enrich themselves. They levied higher taxes in your name, claiming the gold was tribute for you. They seized the lands of free folk, declaring them fit for your palaces. They raised private armies, boasting they would aid your conquests...

Their treachery gnawed at you. At last, you struck down one scheming noble, and the rest grew meek as lambs.

Months later, another noble took peasant girls, claiming they were gifts for you... so you killed him too. This time, several courtiers dared protest, calling the punishment too harsh, so you silenced them by executing the least useful among them.

Thus, you learned that bloodshed was the surest way to rule. The more you killed, the smoother your reign. Gallows sprouted in the cities, corpses swaying like grim fruit. Before long, men began calling your capital "The Shrike's Forest".

Your enemies multiplied, your friends dwindled. People feared you - not for the dragon you slew, but for the countless men you butchered. Your halls of Lapis Lazuli fell silent, for none dared speak lest they die. Occasionally, crude pamphlets surfaced among the smallfolk, depicting you as The Dragonslayer Sultan: a winged, fire-breathing monster... so you burned the makers of these pamphlets, as a true dragon would do.

Let them whisper. Let them curse. Were they seated upon your throne, they would fare no better.

ending_263.title: Bear the Scorn of the Nation
strings: Bear the Scorn of the Nation
Yet still attain happiness.

All the sins you carried, all the darkness of an era, turned to mud and nourished the divinity within your heart. Did you foresee this? Or was it an unintentional?
Along with the insults, curses, blame, and harm, your homeland fell into ruin, you became ragged and wandered afar... yet the splendor of your soul bloomed all the brighter.
People began to tell that the dying regained life at your touch, that greenery sprouted in wastelands along your path, and countless beasts followed, guarded, and listened to your wise voice in the mountains.
Those who longed for ascension and wisdom began to follow you, but only a rare few could stay by your side long—for you always slipped away silently, on an endless journey of suffering.

ending_264.title: The Brightest Star in the Night Sky
strings: The Brightest Star in the Night Sky
As eternal as the world.

Tonight, you rise quietly and gaze upon the land in peace. The wicked game no longer binds you, the tyrant no longer punishes you... Yet you can still hear the messages in people's hearts as they stare at the stars.
If you wish, you may whisper to them now, revealing secrets known only to the stars... for thousands of years, this is how the Star-Souled have secretly shaped the world...
From then on, the North Star gradually gained a strange name: [player.name]. No one can say for sure where it came from, yet countless stories spread across different lands. Stargazers, shepherds, astronomers, fugitives, revolutionaries, explorers... people debate endlessly over the North Star's flickering light, weaving endless tales.

ending_265.title: Blessed Binary Stars
strings: Blessed Binary Stars
You shine together in the night sky.

What a fresh and wonderful thing it is to be a star! Following Lumera—she is now your guiding star—you pick a comfortable spot in the heavens: close enough to Lumera to visit and chat easily, yet not too far from the mortal world, for how else could you check on your friends down there? Oh, what became of them, anyway? You peer down from the clouds, only to find that countless years have passed on earth. Your radiance can no longer find the familiar golden dome of the Sultan's palace!

So this is what it means to be a star—so lonely! You look up at the other stars, worshipped by mortals, believed to rule parts of fate, yet they, too, spin helplessly along their paths, seeming even more powerless than the people kneeling in prayer. Now you finally understand why stars always long to descend to the mortal world!

In your next meeting, you share this thought with Lumera, and she nods earnestly: "Very well! There are so many new things in the world I've never seen. I want to go see if there are new books to read." And so, on an ordinary evening, two shooting stars streak eagerly across the sky. Later generations believe that anyone who sees this sight is blessed, for any wish made then will surely be heard by the stars—and will one day come true.

ending_266.title: Threading the Millennium
strings: Threading the Millennium
Yet it shall finally dry up.

You steal a Sultan Card and flee to the woodland where the wizards who uphold strict neutrality and do not meddle with the true course of history dwell.
For the next thousand years, slowly and steadily, every time the moon rises, you draw the magician's magic from the cards, as if pulling threads of pure gold...
Because of this tax of fate, the collectors who toy with humans are no longer whole, and the game is often interrupted. You pass the eternal hours weaving gifts. You bestow many forms of life upon your loved ones, and weave flying carpets and wings for lost travelers... Throughout a long history, at least three Sultans and one queen have received your works, yet these divine artifacts brought them little luck.
You have had descendants—some born naturally, others born of your weaving... Most leave the forest, taking gifts given or stolen from you, to seek their own lives.
Tonight, the moon rises as usual. You wrap the moonlight with the ever-changing cards, letting strands of golden light slowly condense... You know that one day, you will drain it completely. And you, together with all your gifts, will rejoice at last.

ending_267.title: Silent Dawn
strings: Silent Dawn
Everyone smiles under the sun.

"May 21st, sunny, strong wind, 41°C. Today, we made an archaeological discovery that could upend traditional knowledge! The ruins of an ancient civilization buried deep in the desert! A faulty compass and sandstorms led us here... I'm so excited my hands are still shaking (a smudge where ink leaked)."
"... After a brief exploration, we're certain this was once a massive city. Sand and wind have buried most structures, yet preserved them remarkably intact... We've even found numerous human remains, as if its residents were living moments before being frozen in time by some sudden disaster—a new Pompeii! Larger and better preserved! It's incredible."
"The sandstorm is too fierce; we can only take shelter inside the ancient buildings, sitting among the remains of former inhabitants... So many bodies are seated or lying down, often by windows or building exits... It never fails to unnerve us. What could have claimed so many lives in an instant? The professor reassured us that whatever poison gas or disease it was, thousands of years and sandstorms would have long since neutralized it..."
"The sandstorm is dying down. Once the sun rises, we'll take countless photos! We'll shock the world!"
... The clear record ends abruptly here, leaving only messy scribbles and one repeated word: Bliss.

ending_268.title: Ultimate Creation
strings: Ultimate Creation
She seeks no conquest, yet delights in refining the world.

For the 711th time, you are awakened once more. In your last waking cycle, black towers covered the land, spewing smoke that blotted out the sky... That was Mahir's process to repair the atmosphere. Now, as far as the eye can see, mirror-like plains reflect a crimson sky, as if the world is trapped in eternal dusk... You see no sun, moon, or stars, so you cannot judge your current latitude—and as you think this, an electric pulse transmits information directly into your mind. "Honored Witness [player.name]" Its voice travels along the current into your brain, the only part of you left, fused to this massive cubic creation... In a sense, it is your body; at the very least, you see and hear through its sensors... The land is perfectly flat. From high above, you spot tripod-shelled creatures on the horizon processing floating stones. "In the past 58,424 standard days, we have revised two of your previous feedback: 'It's way too damn bright!' and 'Damn it! All living things on the ground are dead!' Are you feeling better now, honorable Witness?"
"Oh, wonderful! You've done well. Tell your creator the work is done—yours and mine... Can we end this now?" Some part of you must be speaking, though you do not know where. A powerful surge of electricity floods your consciousness, as if someone is yanking a coiled wire inside your brain: "Strong despair detected. Witness [player.name] expresses significant dissatisfaction. Mission incomplete. Analyzing... Semantic match. Hypothesis: 'These aren't even human! I've had enough!' Initiating new objective: Attempting to define... humanity."

ending_269.title: Lively Little Home
strings: Lively Little Home
Why isn't my home a world in itself?

You said, let there be light, and Maggie lit a lamp. It was far too cold outside... so together you put up walls and a roof. Little by little, your room gained a fireplace, tables and chairs, carpets, cups and plates, beds... Where [player.name] labored became the so-called "Yang," and the realm Maggie tended formed the "Yin."
With light and warmth, boundaries, water and dry ground, and the cycle and union of Yin and Yang, the world began to function, slowly expanding with each passing day you lived...

ending_270.title: Perfect Dream
strings: Perfect Dream
A dream has everything you want, except...

.Today Sultan paid you no attention at all in court. It was a peaceful day with no one showing off and no one being beheaded. When the court ended, Lady Fatuna secretly scratched your palm with her fingernail... Too bad you already promised the Aziz you'd all go horse racing on the grassland, and dance with the girls, then get dead drunk—hopefully you won't mix up the order again, and pray Zaki doesn't slip up and tell his mother.
Hey, who dares block [player.name]'s sedan chair? It's Nabhani! And so your group grew, until you had more than ten extra dogs! What can you do... Still, it had its perks: the dogs caught the eye of Miss Shama, the new Ceremony Officer, and you finally got to talk to her! Hehe, the way she looks at you is definitely different from how she looks at other men... Ah, what a perfect day! And yesterday, and tomorrow! Every day brings new hope!

ending_271.title: Perfect Dream
strings: Perfect Dream
If only you could choose never to wake up...

A familiar bell rings outside the door. You let your stuck thoughts fade, set down your quill, and go downstairs to greet Maggie. Alim moves even faster—as a steward, he naturally welcomes the mistress who pays his wages.
Inal bursts in first, grumbling about the trivial rivalries among the court women, the foolish officials, and you, her incompetent husband, wasting money. That fool Mahir publicly showed off the new machine she made with Lord [player.name]! You must have only paid for it, right? Her delay made you miss your chance, and Alim stole the moment to help Maggie out of the sedan chair... but thankfully, her kiss is still yours alone.
Back in the room, while waiting for Habib to prepare dinner, you help Maggie remove her elaborate court jewelry, discussing important events around Sultan and wisely guiding her to solutions (or so you believe). She asks about your latest work... Relax, the sixth volume will be finished by the Summer Solstice! Or let Sultan castrate the useless [player.name]! No matter—I hear Mahir has made the finest replacement...
Your time alone together is brief tonight, for by Maggie's family tradition, you feast with friends on the night of the new moon. In fact, Qais's loud voice already echoes through the parlor walls—hopefully, Nawfal and Faraj won't egg him into ranting rebelliously all evening again.

ending_272.title: Silent Woods
strings: Silent Woods
You failed to create more.

Your world continues to expand, reaching out into the chilling winds. You nurture forests, sculpting them into mysterious forms... Mist swirls, shadows weaving through. The world's hidden truths are etched onto fallen leaves, yet they remain unseen by any.
Time and time again, you shape everything in your possession, yet the creation of a soul eludes you. As the cold intensifies, the wind fades away, until silence lulls you into oblivion, and the cycle begins anew...
Deep within, you cling to the hope that one day, someone might dream of you, infusing their soul into the forest—and with it, heralding an apocalypse.

ending_273.title: Divine Mandate
strings: Divine Mandate
I am the King of Gods.
The King of Gods

ending_274.title: Eternal Covenant
strings: Eternal Covenant
The Eternal Covenant.

ending_275.title: In the Void
strings: In the Void
A deity without worshippers is the most miserable of all.

Your ties to the earth have been entirely severed. To you, this world has transformed into a blurry, ever-shifting canvas as you drift aimlessly... relishing in eternal solitude. You anticipate the moment when a random prayer might utter the name that has long faded into oblivion...

ending_276.title: Utter Severance
strings: Utter Severance
A deity without worshippers is the most miserable of all.

With the demise of your champion, you once again find yourself adrift upon the earth. To you, this world has transformed into a blurry, ever-shifting canvas as you drift aimlessly... relishing in eternal solitude. You anticipate the moment when a random prayer might utter the name that has long faded into oblivion...

ending_277.title: Return to Purity
strings: Return to Purity
You have ascended to the status of a true god.

For more than a millennium, you have reigned over this realm. The prayers of the devout and the memories of your former companions still evoke a stirring within you, serving as reminders of your mortal form known as [player.name]. However, their unwavering devotion has now become a binding force for both of you... In pursuit of a renewed sense of humanity and more human voices, you impel your followers to expand your dominion time and time again, conquering kingdom after kingdom... Each time, those unfamiliar gazes bring moments of clarity. Yet, the ever-growing tide of prayers and dedications intensifies the divine radiance within you.
In the end, the purifying light permeates everything, and the souls of the faithful embody absolute purity—the mortal form of [player.name] fades into the god's heart like a healed wound. As for the fate of this grand empire, the one that once dominated the entire land, how it would eventually face its downfall will remain a mystery, pondered endlessly by future generations of puzzled scholars.

ending_278.title: Eternal Peace
strings: Eternal Peace
May the mundane world never disturb your eternal peace.

You still remember who you are, and what you are. Through the guidance of oracles and revelations, you have devoted immense time and effort to aid your companions in upholding this tumultuous realm—it even saw periods of improvement over certain decades! Yet, you are aware that this status quo cannot last much longer, as a human empire cannot, and should not, rely solely on divine power for its existence...
And so, with the support of other great beings who participated in creation, you readied yourself for the long-awaited repose... Thus, the legend unfolds: at the edge of the ancient empire lies a hidden tomb where the guardian of that realm, [player.name], the Lord of Light, lies dormant. Only when darkness once again shrouds the land can the descendants of heroes awaken Them...

ending_279.title: The Myth of Dreams
strings: The Myth of Dreams
You remain an elusive figure in this reshaped world.

You have melded into the darkness, residing within dreams... However, like wine spilling from an overfilled goblet, or blood trickling from a severed throat, your influence seeps into reality, drop by drop. Is this a result of your own desires, or is it humanity's avarice at play? Not even [player.name] can unveil the answer.
As more mortals draw power from the dream realm, demons, gods, and even stars enter the fray. You are compelled to assign them ranks, grant them dominions and duties... and ultimately, face their challenges.
Whispers of your downfall circulate in the chronicles of the dream realm. Some recount a mighty king ascending to divinity and vanquishing the Lord of Darkness, while others proclaim a formidable priestess wielding love as her blade in this conquest... You fracture into shards, each transforming into a formidable demon deity or an immortal monster, yet none of them carry the name [player.name].

ending_280.title: The Lord of Dreams
strings: The Lord of Dreams
The great one resides within the realm forgotten.

You, alongside your companions who still hold memories of you, have maintained a delicate balance between day and night, between reality and dreams.
Humanity continues to yearn for revelations drawn from dreams, while wizards persist in their quests for power through voyages within dreams... Nonetheless, with your intervention, these practices have gradually faded into the veils of myth and cryptic lore.
In the current era, the world no longer trembles at the thought of being reshaped at the Creator's whims. Their dominion is confined solely within Their own domain, within the realm of dreams. Whispers suggest that [player.name], the Lord of Dreams, occasionally graces mortal dreams—be it to reminisce with former companions or to safeguard the world's forbidden truths.

ending_281.title: Cycles of Tyranny
strings: Cycles of Tyranny
Where shall [player.name] find his place in this grand epic?

On the first night of your era's dawn, you descended into the essence of a trusted companion, using his form as a vessel for your resurrection. With this grand scheme, you forged an immortal realm, a domain where jinns, dragons, merfolks, and even monsters and gods—all conquered by your undying army...
This empire, spanning time and space, endured through countless millennia, and humanity gradually split into two distinct groups: the favored few, blessed with the gift of perpetual resurrection through the cycle, and the mortal throng, relegated to mere servitude.
Yet, who would rise to challenge this eternal dominion...? Who could brave the unyielding might of the undying legions? Amidst the lowly mortals, a whisper took flight, proclaiming that the very first ascended, a champion known as [player.name], was the sole ascended being who favored mortals. One day, he would return from his exile, destined to shatter the tyrannical reign and bring an end to this accursed era...

ending_282.title: A Myriad of Reunions
strings: A Myriad of Reunions
In other lifetimes, we shall always find each other...

On the eve of your new era, the call from your companions, who place their trust and love in you, reaches your ears. Just as you have done countless times across the cycles of the game, the unwavering [player.name] stands resolute against the temptation of power, even the allure of divine power and eternal life...
You have woven your divine essence into the fabric of the future, dispersing it across infinite epochs—not for command or domination, but simply to bestow a parting gift, that [player.name], alongside his companions and beloved ones, would eventually find each other again in any era, in any form they may be reborn into... And as a special reward for yourself, you will retain the memory of each tale from your myriads of reunions...

ending_283.title: The Palace of Dreams
strings: The Palace of Dreams
The gardener of dreams, the tyrant of souls, the wanderer in the garden... The lonely you.

Shortly after dethroning the Sultan, you find Sadani in his harem.

You propose to her that you can pave the way for her child to ascend as the next Sultan, on the condition that she appoints you as the Regent to oversee the kingdom.

Her eyes sparkle momentarily, then dim abruptly...

"But they will question my child's lineage. The Sultan... the late Sultan... the timing of his visit to my chambers and my conception... it simply doesn't add up. I've considered this before, but the nobles just won't lend their support... If you thrust me onto the throne now, all three of us—you, me, and my child—will face certain death."

While her concerns are well-founded, she fails to understand who you truly are... or rather, "what" you truly are.

You unfurl your hand, revealing the tiny clay key to her. It embodies the pinnacle of spiritual achievement, the authority of the enlightened. You could have created an entirely new world with this key, yet you missed the portal it was destined to unlock—or perhaps you consciously veered away from that path. Now, with this immense power in hand, ruling over a mere mortal kingdom is but child's play.

Following this revelation, you outline the blueprint of your future kingdom to Sadani, detailing how you will build the Halcyon Days as vast as the palace itself. You will relentlessly extend its boundaries... witnessing its growth, with blooms sprouting one after the other across its lawns.

Each flower embodies a living dream, an unguarded entity within the dream realm. You reign as the king of this realm of dreams, while all others are but flowers in your garden at best. As you stroll through the garden, plucking at whim, you crush the dreams of others. Disobedient courtiers awaken with their eyes wide, startled from their dreams—they all dream of your colossal figure towering above, gazing down upon them, casually trampling them underfoot. The shattering of their dreams results in maddening agony...

Then, they come to realize that the battleground extends far beyond the confines of the court. They might see political maneuvering as the primary arena in this game of thrones, yet driving a dagger into their core is also a facet of this game, not to mention the torments within their dreams. Amidst these struggles, all they have achieved is the most insignificant victories, while you... you reign as the master. You hold sway over both bodies and spirits.

Initially doubtful of your words, Sadani witnesses the most venerable and hostile noblewomen kneel before her, wailing and pleading. They vow to testify that the child within Sadani's womb indeed carries the late Sultan's lineage. They implore you to cease your torments within their dreams, beseeching that they teeter on the edge of madness.

Despite her uneasiness, Sadani is crowned as the ruler as you foresaw. And you, the Regent by her side, emerge as the true ruler of this kingdom.

Henceforth, the days remain much as they did under the previous Sultan. The populace continues their familiar routines, and all accolades and admiration merely require a shift in recipient. As night falls, you wander in your garden, scanning for any burgeoning weeds, encroaching vines, and thorny plants, uprooting every dream unfit for your empire...

ending_284.title: The Palace of Dreams
strings: The Palace of Dreams
The gardener of dreams, the tyrant of souls, the wanderer in the garden... The lonely you.

You wield a Conquest Card to legitimize your rule, yet as you reveal it, suspicion and contempt fill the faces of all present. Even Zazie, whom you have raised to the throne, schemes to overthrow you. She believes that your motive for placing her on the throne lies solely in the late Sultan's bloodline carried by the child within her womb. Thus, once she secures her position as the mother of the new Sultan, she intends to eliminate you, the Regent, deeming you no longer necessary.

However, be it Zazie, the courtiers, or the soldiers, they all perceive only your earthly form. They remain blind to your true essence, your elevated identity: an enlightened one.

For one who has attained the pinnacle of spiritual achievement, what methods would you use to govern an untamed kingdom...? If your subjects show no gratitude while awake, they might be more obedient in their dreams...

Thus, you build a palace of dreams. Every night, you delve deep into your spiritual domain, observing its vast expanse. You relentlessly extend its boundaries... witnessing its growth, with blooms sprouting one after the other across its lawns.

Each flower embodies a living dream, an unguarded entity within the dream realm. You reign as the king, while all others are but flowers in your garden at best. As you stroll through the garden, plucking at whim, you crush the dreams of others. Disobedient courtiers awaken with their eyes wide, startled from their dreams—they all dream of your colossal figure towering above, gazing down upon them, casually trampling them underfoot. The shattering of their dreams results in maddening agony...

Then, they come to realize that the battleground extends far beyond the confines of the court. They might see political maneuvering as the primary arena in this game of thrones, yet driving a dagger into their core is also a facet of this game, not to mention the torments within their dreams. Amidst these struggles, all they have achieved is the most insignificant victories, while you... you reign as the master. You hold sway over both bodies and spirits.

Zazie remains skeptical of your methods until you personally visit her dream, delicately caressing the golden camellia that represents her before tearing off its petals one after another... The next morning, for the first time, you see Zazie without her usual makeup, rushing to you with disheveled hair, her voice sharp with accusation. "What did you do to me in my dream?!" Undoubtedly, she displays remarkable resilience; other courtiers, after enduring such torment, often remain bedridden for an entire day.

She yields—how could she resist an unseen, supreme power? And so, you, the Regent by her side, emerge as the true ruler of this kingdom.

Henceforth, the days remain much as they did under the previous Sultan. The populace continues their familiar routines, and all accolades and admiration merely require a shift in recipient. As night falls, you wander in your garden, scanning for any burgeoning weeds, encroaching vines, and thorny plants, uprooting every dream unfit for your empire...

ending_285.title: The Palace of Dreams
strings: The Palace of Dreams
The gardener of dreams, the tyrant of souls, the wanderer in the garden... The lonely you.

You wield a Conquest Card to legitimize your rule, yet as you reveal it, suspicion and contempt fill the faces of all present.

Even if it bears the late Sultan's writ of supreme authority, how could one use the Sultan's power to justify overthrowing him? You remain a usurper, a monkey upon the throne, and a traitor without a rightful claim!

At this point, should you assert your dominion by force, you risk becoming enslaved to the kingdom, a deity ensnared within a cage. However... do you not possess a clay key? Even though you do not intend to use it to unlock the gate it was designed for, the spiritual achievements it embodies... You have already attained them.

You are determined to test the power of the spirit. If your subjects show no gratitude while awake, they might be more obedient in their dreams...

Thus, you build a palace of dreams. Every night, you delve deep into your spiritual domain, observing its vast expanse. You relentlessly extend its boundaries... witnessing its growth, with blooms sprouting one after the other across its lawns.

Each flower represents an unguarded dream. You stand as the enlightened one, the most formidable presence within the realm of the spirit, while all others are but flowers in your garden at best. If they possess modest spiritual strength, their blooms might yield a few fruits beneath the leaves—yet you are an entirely different entity. As you stroll through the garden, plucking at whim, you crush the dreams of others.

The next morning, disobedient courtiers awaken with their eyes wide, startled from their dreams—they all dream of your colossal figure towering above, gazing down upon them, casually trampling them underfoot. The shattering of their dreams results in maddening agony... And their terror peaks upon receiving the message from your emissary.

"I cherish the flowers in my garden, as long as they bloom and don't attract pesky insects."

At this moment, they come to realize that the battleground extends far beyond the confines of the court. They might see political maneuvering as the primary arena in this game of thrones, yet driving a dagger into their core is also a facet of this game, not to mention the torments within their dreams. Amidst these struggles, all they have achieved is the most insignificant victories, while you... you reign as the master. You hold sway over both bodies and spirits.

Henceforth, governing the kingdom becomes significantly easier. The days remain much as they did under the previous Sultan. The populace continues their familiar routines, and all accolades and admiration merely require a shift in recipient. As night falls, you wander in your garden, scanning for any burgeoning weeds, encroaching vines, and thorny plants, uprooting every dream unfit for your empire...

ending_286.title: To Set Things Right
strings: To Set Things Right
You have set things right in the history of reality, even if it is just a single page.

To Set Things Right: Unveiling a New Era in [player.name] Research

Today, Nursery National University hosted a prestigious academic symposium led by the university's History Department, drawing experts and scholars from across the globe.

During the symposium's commencement, Professor Juanita, the distinguished President of the History Department at Nursery National University and an esteemed historian and [player.name] researcher, delivered a lecture titled "To Set Things Right."

Here are excerpts from her speech.

"Our gathering today not only commemorates the millennium of [player.name]'s birth but also revolves around a crucial text from an extraordinary archaeological revelation that has captivated the world: [player.name]'s Manuscript. Given our collective expertise in this domain, it is presumed that we are well-versed in the manuscript's contents, necessitating only a brief overview.

This manuscript, spanning over three hundred pages, represents [player.name]'s first personally authored, documentary-style text definitively attributed to him. Regrettably, due to preservation challenges and other factors, a mere thirty pages remain legible today. Among these, a particularly touching passage resonates.

'Today, I returned home, embraced Maggie, and pressed my cheek against hers... Then I lifted Lady Becky from his soft cushion nearest the brazier, taking my place as the master of this household. The wine glasses were already filled to the brim, and the servants presented the hookah... After wetting my throat with wine and stretching my back, I drew near to Maggie, telling her how her husband, with his unmatched cunning, had managed to rid us of a troublesome magician... She chuckled in my arms. She must have fancied me, loved me, been willing to share her life with me, but at that moment, she probably didn't realize how important she was to me or the fact that I had chosen her to set things right.'

This passage marks the manuscript's conclusion. Subsequent to this, the influential courtier, husband, nobleman, and lord appeared to cease documenting his life. Who was this "magician" mentioned in the text? Why did he abruptly stop writing? And most importantly, what does 'to set things right' mean? Despite decades of study on [player.name] with numerous works dedicated to him, he now presents us with a profound mystery after a millennium!

Therefore, we have convened this conference, with the hope that over this four-day symposium, each of us can pool our collective wisdom, engage in dynamic discussions, and endeavor to decipher the significance of the final page of [player.name]'s manuscript. This discovery could upend all our prior conclusions about this influential figure. However, as a scholar and historian, the notion that our entire body of work may have been founded on inaccuracies both unsettles and excites me, as it opens up a vast new realm for exploration.

That concludes my speech. I now pass the microphone to our first speaker. Thank you."

Reporter Argus King will continue reporting on-site discussions from this symposium. Notably, this symposium has been sponsored by Double Cross Technologies.

Reported by Argus Tus.

ending_287.title: Manifestations of Gods
strings: Manifestations of Gods
You have all the time in the cosmos to recall Their names.

The first step in creating a world is to forge the essential tools.

You need to bring forth beings to collaborate in the world's creation, following your grand design. While the original Creator favored embodiments of concepts and laws, you, a solitary soul, yearn for companionship...

Drifting serenely amidst a swirling storm of particles, you extend your hands. Instinctively, you begin to shape the forms of souls from your memory, crafting their likenesses from the particles. Then, with a gentle breath, you bestow a fraction of the Creator's power upon them...

And so, They spring to life. The "gods" of this realm awaken in your hands, gazing up at you. After a fleeting moment of bewilderment, They join you in the act of creation.

ending_288.title: Everything Lies Within These Pages
strings: Everything Lies Within These Pages
You dare to seize all knowledge within your hands? Could a mortal conceive of a more arrogant plan? Yet against all odds, you succeeded!

As you stand before the jubilant crowd that has crowned you their king, observing their thrilled expressions, you feel the stark alienation from them.

How many times has this scene played out before?

You woke up, headed to the palace, tried to stop the Sultan's game, became entangled in it, and strove to bring it to an end...

How many times has this cycle repeated?

And when did you begin to remember everything? You've been pretending that nothing unusual happened, fearing they would deem you insane. Yet, you carried the burden of knowing the fate of each individual. You could only strive to shield a chosen few, while turning a blind eye to others as they turned to ashes in the crucible of destiny...

Perhaps it all began with this tome, you ponder. It was within these pages that you first grasped the concept of the "cycle." During the conversation with Asal, you opened this grand tome that was supposed to be blank, yet... you unearthed the treasures amassed by your former self.

This tome served as both a mooring and a beacon. Amidst the turmoil of myriad worlds, you clung to it resolutely.

And so, time and time again, you achieved extraordinary feats, adding wonders to its pages. Although no promises were given, a lingering sense of anticipation accompanied each addition.

Finally, the last page is now filled, yet no grand revelation emerges as you pen the final words. No miracles unfold as you close its covers. A faint sense of disillusionment creeps in, until you face the jubilant crowd that has crowned you their king—

Instinctively, you raise the tome. It should have weighed heavily in your grasp, but instead, it feels as light as a feather. Almost weightless, it lifts your hand effortlessly as you hear your voice resound boldly as you proclaim.

"In the Sultan's name, I hereby declare: Everything lies within these pages!"

In an instant, radiance emanates from you and the tome. Wherever its light touches, transformations take place, while certain things remain unchanged...

Everything lies within these pages.

ending_289.title: The Realm of Heroes
strings: The Realm of Heroes
Not only does history remember your name, but the myths that follow shall also bear your tale.

ending_290.title: The Realm of Conquest
strings: The Realm of Conquest
A warrior’s fate is to repeat his deeds of valor until death claims him.

ending_291.title: The Shrike's Forest
strings: The Shrike's Forest
Slaying a dragon is easy while ruling is not.

ending_292.title: The Realm of Heroes
strings: The Realm of Heroes
Not only does history remember your name, but the myths that follow shall also bear your tale.

The Sultan has fallen before you.

You raise your sword high above as the masses around you erupt in frenzied cheers—a Dragonslayer hero, a valiant blade that vanquished the Sultan! This is a moment of unparalleled glory that the empire has never witnessed; mere mortals reaching such heights!

Soon, the massive dragon's head decorates your throne—a masterpiece of gold engravings crafted by the empire's finest goldsmith captures the epic tale of dragonslaying, set beside your throne—watching over the assembly; those faint of heart among the courtiers stumble in awe at their first sight of this head!

And you, the greatest hero among men, sit upon the throne. You wield the longsword tempered by dragon breath and cloak of dragon scales, with your Vizier, [Vizier's Name], by your side. Your claim was so unquestionable, your preparations for the throne so thorough, that the transition of power was as smooth as a hot knife through butter.

You swiftly and successfully transform the nation, weaving ancient traditions into a new order and granting people more freedom; bringing smiles, prosperity to markets, and reducing hunger.

To this day, your statues dot the continent and people pray for the courage to overcome adversity; they kneel faithfully and rise anew, eyes filled with strength.

ending_293.title: The Realm of Conquest
strings: The Realm of Conquest
A warrior’s fate is to repeat his deeds of valor until death claims him.

The Sultan has fallen before you.

You raise your sword high and the surrounding people burst into a frenzy of cheers—a dragonslayer hero, a new ruler vanquishing the Sultan! A moment of unrivaled brilliance the empire has never experienced, mortals achieving such eminence!

Soon, a massive dragon's head adorns your throne—the empire's finest goldsmith has crafted intricate gold engravings depicting the dragon's tale, set beside your throne—watchful over the assembly; timid courtiers stumble in shock at first sight of the head!

However, the euphoria of slaying the dragon quickly fades away, replaced by a restlessness that gnaws at you... The ceaseless squabbling among the nobles in the court, the scribes' complaints alongside rustling budgets and tally sheets, and the relentless attacks on [Vizier's Name] by the influential nobles all contribute to your unease. Their disrespect towards the vizier you handpicked feels like a direct affront. Alas, a remedy to this predicament remains elusive to you.

Eventually, you lead your army westward, challenging a mighty sea beast lurking in the trench—a magnificent target nearest your lands!

Warriors rejoice at your decision, while nobles and ministers gape in shock. Having ascended to the Sultan's throne through heroics, must you not pursue more feats of grandeur?

First the sea beast, then the golden feather serpent, and finally the banshee forest, your army ravages through the world's darkest corners; when barriers arise from local kings, lords, or chieftains forbidding passage, you simply obliterate the state.

Challenges unending, conquests innumerable, bloodshed boundless! Such a life befits you! Rush forward evermore; only this escape that distant call:

"Return—you are Sultan—your duties await—!"

ending_294.title: The Shrike's Forest
strings: The Shrike's Forest
Slaying a dragon is easy while ruling is not.

The Sultan has fallen before you.

You raise your sword high and the surrounding people burst into a frenzy of cheers—a dragonslayer hero, a new ruler vanquishing the Sultan! A moment of unrivaled brilliance the empire has never experienced, mortals achieving such eminence!

Yet, ruling proves far harder than slaying a fire dragon. You bring too much change, too swiftly, without securing enough loyal supporters. The nobles seize upon your dragonslayer fame to enrich themselves. They levy higher taxes in your name, claiming the gold is tribute for you. They seize the lands of freeman, declaring them fit for your palaces. They raise private armies, boasting they will aid your conquests...

Their treachery gnaws at you. At last, you strike down one scheming noble, and the rest grow meek as lambs.

Months later, another noble takes peasant girls, claiming they are gifts for you... So you kill him, too. This time, several courtiers dare to protest, calling the punishment too harsh, so you silence them by executing the least useful among them.

Thus, you learn that bloodshed is the surest way to rule. The more you kill, the smoother your reign. Gallows sprout in the cities, corpses swaying like grim fruit. Before long, men begin calling your capital "The Shrike's Forest".

Your enemies multiply, your friends dwindle. People fear you - not for the dragon you slew, but for the countless men you butchered. Your Lapis Lazuli Palace fall silent, for none dares speak lest they die. Occasionally, crude pamphlets surface among the smallfolk, depicting you as the Dragon-Slaying Sultan: a winged, fire-breathing monster... So you burn the makers of these pamphlets, as a true dragon would do.

Let them whisper. Let them curse. Were they seated upon your throne, they would fare no better.

ending_301.title: SacredSacrifice
strings: SacredSacrifice
With flesh as kindling and souls as tinder, you immolated the accursed game

The wicked game was laid to rest forever. All your companions bore witness to your sacred sacrifice. They carried your tale back to the capital, where crowds wept as they praised your name.

Soon every soul who'd ever shared a passing word with you stepped forth - recounting how they'd drunk ale with you, broken bread in taverns, wandered through House of Delights, boasting of confessions whispered and hands clasped in fellowship...

ending_302.title: Happy Ending
strings: Happy Ending
Tempered by dragonfire, guarded by stars

The wicked game was laid to rest forever. The starlight gradually dimmed. The flames failed to consume your soul, yet still, there was the smell of ash.

Your memories were the first to go. Your companions became strange, nameless silhouettes. The ground beneath you shifted, alien. At last, you stood upon a land that extended out into infinity, where you were to wander – without a past, without a destination. None you met seemed to know you.

Until one day, as you passed by a city, you saw a woman standing upon a barbican, her gaze cast stubbornly into the distance. She saw you. As your eyes met, you saw the starlight of tears.

It was Maggie.

Her name lit up your dulled heart. You started to walk towards her. She ran over. As you opened your arms, she fell into your embrace. The dragon’s breath had erased you, yes. Yet the threads of fate had pulled you back to her. Something unnameable stirred and rose from the depths of your soul, and in a moment of profound clarity, you understood: this was happiness.

ending_303.title: The Lone Star
strings: The Lone Star
The lost soul crystallize into the solitary star.

The starlight gradually dimmed. The flames failed to consume your soul, yet still, there was the smell of ash. Your memories were the first to go. 

Your companions became strange, nameless silhouettes. The ground beneath you shifted, alien. At last, all that you were is erased. You stood upon a land that extended out into infinity, a kite lost to the winds, forever searching for the thread that once tethered you – the thread long severed.

ending_401.title: Countless Times
strings: Countless Times

This, too, is a form of victory.
Would you not agree?

You have seen your own deaths – beyond counting. You have fallen in love, with innumerable people. You have woven myriads of machinations. You have seen failure in all its shapes and forms. In this moment, the remorse of ten thousand life times flood you. Yet you know, though time may unwind, you will still take your stand. You will resist the Sultan's Game.

ending_402.title: The Collector
strings: The Collector

This, too, is a form of victory.
Would you not agree?

You grasp your purpose now - the Collector, the Keeper. With magic craft you shall catalogue the crawling things of this earth. All shall be inscribed in the divine game’s cryptic annals. Then your brethren will gather - not as mortal men, but as ancient forebears - to bestow new names upon all creation...

ending_403.title: Coitus Web
strings: Coitus Web
- Thou Art Now Demon

Witcher's Codex - Entry A-208
Name: [player.name]
Titles: Coitus Web, Demon Prince, Patron of Adultery, Master of the 1036th Layer of the Abyss, God-Slayer
Rank: Abyssal Lord
Common Bestowals: Shedding, Extra Limbs, Venom Fangs, Mucous Secretion, Sensory Delusions
Activity: Actively Lures Mortals
This young Abyssal Lord enjoys widespread mortal worship - unsurprising, given his ability to seduce shallow devotees through base sensory pleasures in dreams. Invoking his titles, sigils, or summoning beacons amplifies sensory and hallucinatory magics within his domain. [Warning! Such acts risk drawing his direct attention. Never take it lightly! (See Appendix III: The Green Tower Incident)]
The Coitus Web lacks formal churches. His cultists parasitize other congregations - often those of true gods or potent astral entities. They corrupt high-spiritual-awareness devotees through depraved rituals, or secretly breed "promising seeds" via adulterous unions if existing bloodlines prove inadequate (See Appendix II: Queenie).
When conditions align, an infant of supreme spiritual awareness is conceived through unholy congress steeped in deceit - embodying this Demon Prince's core doctrine: Lust is the web that ensnares souls.
Documented cases (Appendices I, II, IV) reveal these tainted infants become conduits for divine essence, even luring godly avatars into the material plane. Foolish deities mistake this for opportunity, only to meet the Abyssal Lord's fangs. Cultists instantly sacrifice the infant to the Abyss, their prolonged infiltration and blasphemies having already forged the gateway.
The ensuing deicide triggers cascading calamities - earthquakes, plagues, mass casualties - demanding proactive intervention despite its moral quandaries.
Disrupting incomplete rituals can thwart this Lord's schemes. Note: All contaminated lifeforms, including infants and beasts, must be purged without mercy. Even decades-old rituals may resurrect (See Appendix II).
Given his expertise in corruption over combat, forging pacts with this entity is strongly advised against. Long-term peril far outweighs fleeting gains.

ending_404.title: Golden Desolation
strings: Golden Desolation
- Thou Art Now Demon

Witcher's Codex - Entry B-134
Name: [player.name]
Titles: The Golden Desolation, Demon Count, Patron of Miners 
Rank: Archdemon
Common Bestowals: Claws, Bestial Metamorphosis, Transmutation, Metal Dominion, Pactcraft
Activity: Actively lures mortals
As an Archdemo susceptible to summoning, [player.name] peddles his Pact of Desolation to humanity—exchanging vitality and torment for gold. (See Appendix I: Victims exhibit widespread auric ossification, with kin often extracting the tainted gold through grotesque, visceral means.)
Crucially, the scale of these pacts is boundless and exhibits contagious perniciousness. (See Appendix II: National desertification assessments; Appendix I: Early-stage auric corruption detected in victims.) Researches (Appendices I-III), routine evaluations must assess regional rulers and cabinets for susceptibility to the Desolation Pact, including annual monitoring of gold trade, vegetation decay, and medical data. Notably, such pacts remain reversible only while local economies retain capacity to offset their "profits." In such cases, prioritize diplomatic intervention over violence to mitigate fallout. (See Appendix IV: XXXX Desert Reclamation Project.)
All auric byproducts of the Pact bear minor contagious taint and require surveillance and retrieval under radioactive waste disposal protocols, though operatives must enforce strict confidentiality. Collaboration with medical institutions proves critical for early symptom detection and source tracing.
WARNING: Storing over one cubic meter of Desolation Gold in proximity risks coalescence into a [player.name]] avatar - a significant threat.
For witchers maimed (e.g., limb loss), a pact with the Golden Desolation may grant a potent prosthetic. Such bargains are permissible only if the contractor's longevity is not prioritized and must be witnessed and reviewed by at least one Witcher Master. Any profit-driven pact incurs execution.

ending_405.title: Triumphant Carrion
strings: Triumphant Carrion
- Thou Art Now Demon

Witcher's Codex - Entry A-658
Name: [player.name]
Titles: Triumphant Carrion, Ghoul Warlord, Usurper-King, Sovereign of the 861st Abyssal Layer, Regicide Ascendant
Rank: Demon Prince
Common Boons: Summon mundane armaments, Raise ghoul legions, Animate corpses, Command undead, Conjure engines of mass slaughter
Activity: Responds to invocations
In elder days, [player.name]'s influence was oft mistaken for common necromancy, its true scope obscured. The first confirmed case (Appendix I) coincides with 15XX [Redacted] Empire coup records, detailing a general-turned-wight butchering monarchs—a hallmark of Triumphant Carrion's final covenant stage: the pact-bearer becomes marrow-forged legion, returning home to slaughter all bloodkin and former allies, while raising cataclysmic waves of undead.
Modern warfare illuminated clearer signs—dead hosts wielding artillery and repeating arms remain rare... These "bargain-summoned" reinforcements manifest as: ghoul armored divisions hauling siege engines, spectral bomber squadrons darkening skies, or skeleton shock troops deploying alchemical horrors. Upon detection, purge all human combatants involved. Leave no survivors to return home and trigger the covenant's terminal phase.
WARNING: All known pacts with [player.name] inevitably lead to betrayal by the Contracted. Strictly prohibited.

ending_406.title: Suicide Blade
strings: Suicide Blade
- Thou Art Now Demon

Witcher's Codex - B-771
Name: [player.name]
Titles: Suicide Blade, Hundred-Limbed Angel, Blood of Vengeance, Viscount of Damnation
Rank: Archdemon
Common Bestowals: Blood Dominion, Armsmastery, Forgecraft, Blade Conjuration
Activity: Actively seduces mortals
[player.name] whispers to the desperate, binding pacts through scar-tattoos etched in flesh. When fed enough agony and spite, these marks birth crimson weapons from the wielder's own blood. The gifted may even sprend limbs of liquid wrath.
Such blades pierce magical defenses when striking sworn foes, though their bite weakens against ordinary flesh - at first. Once vengeance is claimed, the hatred within seeps into all living beings. Thus, to curb corruption, we must slay the vengeance-drunk before their quest ends, righteous or not.
In dire cases (see Appendix I), [player.name]'s sword-arms burst forth from the pact-bearer's flesh to slaughter freely. Should this occur, Witcher units must retreat without ranged or aerial strikes—direct engagement is folly. Let the abomination exhaust itself.
Suicide Blade's pacts hold grim utility. Most Witchers memorize a crimson blade incantation for final stands. Survivors of such rituals join the Penance Corps, bound in chains.
Lastly, forge weapons from these blood-steel shards against other demons. Unlike mortal hands, these blades submit to containment once their purpose is spent.

ending_501.title: The Song of Silence
strings: The Song of Silence
He fulfilled His very duty.

All turned to white, all turned to silence, all was restored to the world's first dawn... just as the Purist had willed. The world lay like an untouched gift-box, awaiting its master's return.

Many years passed. No life arose upon this planet, the Purist would not suffer souls to defile the Creator's work again.

Then came a silver, egg-shaped vessel. It circled long above the ruins of the fallen empire, venting pale vapors, before extending four slender mechanical legs to alight upon the earth with delicate care.

Strange figures emerged, gray-skinned, wrinkled, with bulbous black eyes, standing half the height of this world's former dwellers. Clad in cumbersome suits, they wielded devices that sent dog-sized silver machines scurrying across the barren land.

Had you understood the tongue of M32-145γ in Andromeda, you'd have heard their bewildered survey of this desolate sphere...

"Precursor civilization found?"

"Yes... layer upon layer, stratum after stratum. The most recent perished some nine hundred solar years past."

"Many layers? Yet no trace of nuclear or solar arrays? Surely they couldn't have been snuffed out each time before reaching the technological singularity?"

"Yet so it appears."

"Oh, how dreadful."

"Agreed. Dreadful indeed."

They scrambled back into their silver egg, pressed a sequence of buttons, and fled in haste.

ending_502.title: Godslayer
strings: Godslayer
- And Yet, Redeemer

The descending god's form had already dissolved into blinding radiance, yet the "god" did not perish, for faith did not vanish with it. Countless zealous devotees still worshipped the scattered rubble and dust of the fallen the Tower of Revelation. The instinct for purification, the obsession with annihilation, still echoed hollowly across the ages. A thousand years, ten thousand years hence, the flames of belief would one day be rekindled, and He would seize that faint chance to descend once more, to destroy this world again...

And so, before nightfall, you left the city, resolved to seek out the near-endless fragments of the god and atone for the boundless sin you had brought upon yourself. But that... is another story. A story without end.

ending_601.title: The God of Wishes
strings: The God of Wishes
His Dream Came True

The Corrupter had coveted the divine throne of the material world for far too long. After millennia of imprisonment, He finally seized His chance. Had He succeeded in destroying the world, what would He have become? The God of Corruption and Chaos? The Eternal God? None could say now...

But Inal's wish tore Him apart. There were so many children in need of help! So many girls suffering! His divine power, His knowledge... everything that could leave a mark upon this world was scattered among all the children, and all the suffering girls yet to come.

Such pitifully thin shreds of divinity, divided among countless souls, could change almost nothing. Perhaps only a sliver of extra courage, the fleeting illusion that wounds hurt less, a stranger's hand more willing to reach out in kindness... But above all, it was the faintest whisper of hope, a wish cradled in the deepest corners of the human heart, urging them to survive...

And so, The Corrupter's wish was granted! He became a true god of this world at last! One with countless worshippers, enduring as long as humanity itself, as eternal as yearning!

..Only, like all wishes, He existed nowhere but in the spaces between breaths, nowhere but in the hearts of those who still dared to dream...

ending_602.title: The Deadline
strings: The Deadline
The thing even the Creator fears.

You have discovered the most wicked ending of all. Truly, there is no one more loathsome than you in Sultan's Game, no one in all the world!

Indeed, because you offered the gifts of the abyss as sacrifice, and because of all your deeds in the game, you have become one of the Cultic Gods.

You sit among the countless idols of chaos, gazing upon the sparks struck from the collisions of human souls, waiting for your chance to seep into the world. And your opportunities are greater than all the rest. Greater than the God of Slaughter, the God of Betrayal, the God of Lies, even the God of Debauchery!

You have become... the God of Deadlines.

You reign over the deadlines of every wretched soul who makes their living by creativity: painters, writers, game writers(what is it anyway?), sculptors, street artisans scraping by, even the little prince in his palace who promised his mother a scribbled portrait. The moment a thought flickers in their minds: "Oh gods, it's due, and I'm not finished!" then you find a crack and slip into the mortal world.

You torment them. You make them obsess over "What if I can't finish it?" until the weight of that dread crushes their will to work. You cunningly strip every last drop of dopamine(what is it anyway?) from their brains, leaving them despondent, guilt-ridden, paralyzed! And then, with malice, you return it to them only after the deadline has passed, letting them drown in the relief of "It's too late now anyway," surrendering to despair. Oh, you are wicked. damn wicked!

And yet, you are worshipped. Remember? The greatest of the Cultic Gods calls himself the Creator. But you? You truly birth creation.As the old saying goes: a borrowed book is the only one read while a draft untouched until the deadline looms. So how many nights and days, under your watchful gaze, have mortals wept, sweated, even bled, just to cross that deadline?

"This part will do, right? That section is weak, but no time to fix it. Another character could be added, but where would the hours come from? Good enough. Good enough! Hit send! Submit!"

Satisfied, brimming with stolen inspiration, you return to the abyss. The other Cultic Gods glare at you, cold and displeased, but powerless. You will torment and reward creators this way for years to come, perhaps forever.

Do you remember the gilded whisper you once planted in the minds of every struggling artist on the brink of their deadline?

"Done is better than perfect. Now fucking do it."

ending_603.title: Corruption
strings: Corruption
At last, He has shaped His own world.

The world was shattered by the Corrupter, ground into ink to feed His stains, into mire to fill His depths...

Souls are trapped in the filth, tearing at each other, lost in waking dreams, wailing and screaming. When the Creator first forged this world, He scooped but a single ladle from such a pit and cast it into existence, and that mere spoonful birthed all this chaos!

Many years have passed.

Then came a silver, egg-shaped vessel of metal, circling long above the ruins of the old empire, spewing pale smoke. It dared not land to the earth that thick with a black, gelatinous substance. And if one looked close, the things trapped within seemed to twitch. So instead, the machine extended a slender cable from its belly, probing deep into the mire.

Had you understood the tongue of Andromeda M32-145γ, you would have heard the small, gray figures with their vast black eyes, murmuring in confusion...

"Traces of a pre-civilization?"

"Perhaps... It's saturated with violent brainwaves, countless brainwaves. Billions. Tens of billions. The things in this gel... they're still alive!"

"Alive? And... what is this gel?"

"Mire."

"What?"

"The signals from the probe... The brainwaves are answering, all at once - 'This is the world. The god's world.'"

"You.you mean this thing is aware of us?!"

"Ascend! Launch! Flee!"

ending_604.title: The Endless Journey
strings: The Endless Journey
Now, at last, we both have time enough.

The Corrupter perished, and with him fell the Magician and the wicked game... Their shattered remnants bled together, leaving one final stain upon your flesh.

In your eyes, that ink pulses still shifting, twisting... and one day, you shall see slaughter, tangled limbs and crowns in the depths. That was the bottomless hunger of men. And from it, the evil shall be born anew.

So before the dawn could break, you slipped from the city, taking only a twisted familiar. None know your path. Some claim you ended the accursed game with your death, snuffing the dark god's last ember of hope. Others whisper you wander still, chasing some frail chance to break the curse, while the god forces game after game upon you... but at least you have your pet. It snaps card after card with ease. It has no true life to extinguish, no true mind to shatter. A vessel to bear this torment, this malice... forever. What a mercy for the world.

ending_999.title: Ending 999
strings:
You make your speech until your mouth feels dry, but it clearly has no impact on the Sultan. Even the Magician pays you no mind. As you come to a stop, exhausted, wondering if your life is about to end, the Sultan suddenly casts you a curious look.
"Verily so," he muses, "A wise monarch should not commit such acts... But neither should a wise monarch abandon his own delights. In which case – why don't you play in my stead? You, my loyal subject, I command you to play this game for me, this Sultan's Game!" He bursts into laughter as you stand there, dumbfounded...

epilogue_2000001.title: Epilogue: Arzu
strings: "Let's see, press here, turn that... Alright, here we go again! Come on, human! Do something to change your fate this time!"

Congratulations! You've successfully escaped from Sultan's Game! This counts as a victorious ending. Yet fate is not set in stone, and as the creators of this story, we sincerely hope you enjoyed the journey and feel inspired to explore more endings.

Whoa! You've uncovered this secret ending. As the creators of this story, we anticipated that only a very few players would make it here - take our hats off to you! We hope you still have the drive to explore more endings.

You did it - it turns out someone actually could! Only a master who fully comprehends all things could reach this destined culmination - take our hats off to you!. Though perhaps... this game still holds secrets even beyond your knowing.

Congratulations! You have emerged victorious in Sultan's Game! This is one of the best endings in the game. As the creators of this story, we sincerely hope you enjoyed the journey and feel inspired to explore more endings.

Congratulations! You have emerged victorious in Sultan's Game! While this may not be the best ending, As the creators of this story, we sincerely hope you enjoyed the fun and feel inspired to explore more endings.
Your deeds now echo in tavern songs, and children brandish sticks as they reenact your dragon-slaying rebellion - the newest game in every muddy courtyard.
Some bards weave your tale into the legend of the King of Flames, and so your old friend dons cloak each night, striving to live up to the mantle you thrust upon.

In time, countless uprisings raise banners embroidered with fire. They chant your name like a battle hymn, as if the very syllables could steel their hearts against impossible odds. It becomes a ritual of defiance, shouted over clashing steel and raised tankards before the charge.

Congratulations! You have emerged victorious in Sultan's Game! This is one of the best endings in the game(or Not?^_^). As the creators of this story, we sincerely hope you enjoyed the journey and feel inspired to explore more endings.

Think you your sins shall be forgotten? People may cease to speak of them out of awe, respect, fear, love... even pity.

But the abyss waits. It is patient. And it always embraces its sinners with tender hands.

After you unveiled the policies of your Realm of Game, Nawfal and some of your supporters vanished. Your spies reported he had withdrawn to his own lands, raising high walls and mustering armies in open rebellion.

At first, you paid it little mind... until more and more began disappearing from your side. First went Nabhani, there were too many had bought Bloodshed Tickets to use on the prostitutes, leaving the House of Delights empty. He left without a word. Then came your usual detractors among the nobility, Qais, for one. After them, the wealthy nobles, even Fatuna, who poured her fortune into backing your enemies! Finally, neighboring realms and tribes once allied to you openly declared for Nabhani’s stronghold, including Fardak. You’d thought he of all people would appreciate your games!

Their betrayals enraged you. Had they not once supported you? All you did was sell cards where people made their own choices!

To draw out the wickedness already festering in their hearts. Was that so wrong? Should it have been left to rot unseen, to fester into venom? No. You refused to accept it. If only Maggie were here... She always knew the right words to soothe hearts. Perhaps her voice could have made them believe you were still worth saving. No, you mustn’t think like that! What was so foul about wickedness, so long as it brought you joy? And so, joyfully, you would destroy them, every last fool who dared oppose you.

You printed Conquest Tickets by the thousands, rewarding any who brought you the heads of rebels. Your realm descended into a rabid, bottom-up war. Thugs dragged in the heads of innocents, swearing they were the "Nawfal". In a single month, you received over three hundred "Nawfal", piling alongside the heads of the liars who brought them.

That was bloodshed. Corpses stacked like harvest sheaves. Yet the rebels' stronghold stood.

Why won’t they die?

You often wondered what Maggie would say, but she was gone. So why did her voice still answer?

You drank deeper, sobered less. The whispers in your ears never ceased.

Time was slipping through your fingers. You kept remembering the words engraved inside that ring: "All things pass." - like his and your reign, like the realm of game and your cruelty, like the good you once held and everything you possessed - all things pass.

And so, in despair, you waited for the next dawn.

After you unveiled the policies of your Realm of Game, Nawfal and some of your supporters vanished. Your spies reported he had withdrawn to his own lands, raising high walls and mustering armies in open rebellion.

At first, you paid it little mind... until more and more began disappearing from your side. First went Nabhani, there were too many had bought Bloodshed Tickets to use on the prostitutes, leaving the House of Delights empty. He left without a word. Then came your usual detractors among the nobility, Qais, for one. After them, the wealthy nobles, even Fatuna, who poured her fortune into backing your enemies! Then neighboring realms and tribes once allied to you openly declared for Nabhani’s stronghold, including Fardak. You’d thought he of all people would appreciate your games!

But the final betrayal cut deepest. Sadani herself joined the revolt. When you confronted her with letters proving her treason, the stubborn former concubine met your gaze without flinching.

"Because you are no longer the man who dared defy the Sultan's Game. Now you are only a villain, nothing more."

And so, in despair, you waited for the next dawn.

When the treachery that doomed you unfolded, your warriors fought with their lives on the line. Some nearly died dragging you from the ambush. Others led desperate cavalry charges to hold back the tide. More still barricaded the palace gates with their own bodies, choosing to perish alongside their foes over surrender.

Yet one man prevented their sacrifice. Not out of cowardice, not from lack of devotion.

"To die here is wasteful," Nawfal told your bleeding champions, "the one we served would not wish us to spend our lives so cheaply. Since traitors loyal to the Sultan slew him, then let there be no more Sultans in this land. We overthrew one before, and we can do it again."

Thus did Nawfal gather your surviving Iron Guards - Nabhani, Jabal, Faris and Riel, Dark Alley's ruler, carving from your former lands a rebel state. Within months, they raised new armies, seized supplies, and struck at the usurper's forces.

Where they marched, people who remembered your rule flocked to their banners. For years they waged their war, your likeness stitched upon every standard. When at last they stormed the Lapis Lazuli Palace, every survivor bore the scars of that long struggle.

Your Iron Guards donned their old vestments once more. Loyalists filled the court again. Nawfal leaned against a pillar, idly turning pages of that book you'd gifted him long ago. For a fleeting moment, time seemed to unwind, as if you might stride through those doors at any instant...

Then Nawfal placed your crown upon the vacant throne in people's sobs. He proclaimed the new order: He would rule as the Vizier, with the Sultan's seat be empty for now.

In later generations, this peculiar reign was remembered as "The Empty Throne."

During the rebellion that led to your demise, your loyal warriors fought valiantly, risking death to save you, leading cavalry in desperate resistance against the enemy, or sacrificing themselves to hold the gates of the Court, determined to die alongside their foes...

Yet there was one who rescued these devoted and valiant warriors, preventing their deaths; not out of cowardice or a lack of concern for you...

"Dying here is too much of a waste," he told them, "We swear allegiance to only one ruler, [player.name]. If he perishes, then this nation should have no further Sultan. We have toppled the Sultan before, and rest assured, we can do it again."

His name was Nawfal. He led your Iron Guard generals—Nabhani, Seliman, Jabal, and Faris—in establishing a provisional government on your territory. Within months, they recruited soldiers, gathered food supplies, and set about attacking nobles allied with Zazie. Wherever they went, commoners who still remembered your deeds joined their cause too.

For years thereafter, this army, adorned with your likeness on its banners, engaged in brutal combat against the rebels, until the day they finally breached the Lapis Lazuli Palace, bearing countless battle scars.

Once more, your Iron Guards donned their old attire, and the loyal gathered before the Court. Nawfal idly leaned against a pillar, reading through the book you gifted him many years ago. Time seemed to rewind, as though nothing had occurred, moments away from you stepping through those palace gates once again...

Amid the people's weeping, Nawfal laid your crown upon the barren golden throne; subsequently, he proclaimed the start of a new dynasty; he is the Vasir, with the Sultan's position yet unfilled.

In future chronicles, this enigmatic dynasty became known as the "Empty Throne."

On the day you set out alone, an unexpected figure followed, like a shadow stripped to instinct, a silent guardian without words. You tried to drive him away. You even tried to kill him. Yet somehow, he always returned, inexplicably alive, lingering at the edges of your path. In the end, you relented. Perhaps, in the moment the tyrant's soul was cleansed, fate had laughably bound the two of you together once more. Or perhaps only when you truly atoned for all the spilled sins would either of you be freed from this endless march through time... No matter. On this long pilgrimage of penance, you did need a companion. A servant. Or, at the very least, you had a place to vent your bitterness without guilty.

Of course you had committed atrocities, and you were the very embodiment of wickedness. People would not soon forget that!

But so long as you kept steering this realm toward prosperity, your past sins mattered little... Beware, though. Should your course ever falter, the masses would not hesitate to drag every last transgression into the light.

A Sultan with blood on his hands made for the best Sultan, didn't he?

[table.宰相.name] died shortly after you.

The two of you remained hanging on the scaffolds, where passersby amused themselves by prodding your corpses with spears.

Before your bodies could fully rot, the great nobles seized control of the leaderless, chaotic realm. They swiftly reinstated every oppressive decree, going even further than the Sultan you had overthrown. Now every slave had to pay a monthly tax for the right to live, lest their masters slaughter them without consequence.

The nobles cheered this cruelty. They crushed the newly freed slaves with brutal fervor, and the slaves fought back with equal fury. The realm descended into a bloody stalemate. Occasionally, people still spoke of you... their voices thick with regret.

Your revolution had ended. But it planted seeds which would bloom, whether in ten years or a hundred.

[table.宰相.name] hung beside you on the scaffold.

Yet the moment the mob stormed in, the Vizier seemed to have lost all will to live. When your rescuers cut the ropes, they found [table.宰相.gender] already gone.

They buried [table.宰相.gender] near your woodland hut. No marker was placed, but a lone pine stood vigil over the grave. It straight as a spear, silent as the grave it guarded.
Quick! Reset it now! That foolish girl's wish is unraveling timelines across a thousand worlds! We've lost too much already! Never again, never play at this cursed ending!

Maggie stood by your every decision. When filth was thrown upon you, she washed the grime from your hair. When the lash fell, she tended your wounds. Her tears had nearly run dry in those days. Her heart ached for you, yet she always smiled, cradling your face and whispering that you were the finest man in the world, the best of husbands.

And when you chose to leave, she followed without hesitation. You could never refuse her, could you? Even as the wind cracked her skin, even as toil roughened her hands, you still held her close, murmuring again and again that she was the finest woman in the world, the best of wives.

epilogue_2000005.title: Epilogue: Bharat
strings: The whereabouts of Bharat and Ansuya are a mystery. Many seek them for various reasons, but all in vain. Perhaps out of gratitude for past kindness or a touch of nostalgia for old stories, they sometimes send anonymous letters; the paper is imbued with the dense scent of the Old Kingdom, containing antiquities as gifts. But when you want to write back, simply hang the letter on the pomegranate tree Maggie planted at your doorstep, and by the next day, the letter disappears.

Bharat and Ansuya have remained silent. Months after you ascending the throne, a nameless shipment arrives by passing ship at your palace.

Exotic treasures from distant lands, accompanied by a single note:

"To the new Sultan, in remembrance of kindness once shown."

Bharat paid his dues in full then vanished like ink in water.

Whispers reached you of his shadow glimpsed in Ansuya's ancestral lands...but you silenced the rumor-bearers with a gaze that stilled their tongues. Some disappearances are meant to stay buried.
