However, what you may not know is that the direct descendants of Jasmine are thriving today as a resilient breed, predominantly found in the Hulur Grassland, with our academy being the proud owners of five of them. The story begins with Lady Maggie personally breeding these horses over three generations. Sensing the weight of time catching up with her, she instructed the ruler of the Hurul domain to allow her foals to roam freely in the grasslands. There, they mingled with local wild horses, giving rise to robust and enduring bloodlines. These horses boast exceptional speed and stamina, all the while maintaining a gentle disposition towards humans. Although they can have a bit of a temper at times, a few carrots are all it takes to soothe them. These horses are truly exceptional, known for their gentle nature and elegance... Ah, sorry... I seem to have gotten carried away talking about horses. Let's just wrap up my presentation here. Thank you all."

During the banquet on the second day, attendees were treated to a screening of the documentary "Lady Mahir: A Genius Inventor Beyond Her Era" in the banquet hall. This film, produced by a research team from Nursery National University focusing on [player.name]'s era, received joint funding from Double Cross Technologies, Nursery National University, and Copport Business College.

The documentary chronicled the remarkable inventions of the renowned inventor Lady Mahir, showcasing her well-known creations such as the hot air balloon and the astronomical telescope, alongside other works that were considered unsuitable for public display. X-ray scans of Lady Mahir's inventions have unveiled significant signs of liquid erosion, a puzzling phenomenon that continues to baffle researchers. Over the course of history, numerous craftsmen have endeavored to replicate her inventions using her research documents, yet the mystery surrounding the "Aether" remains unsolved. This incredible substance seems to be gifted by [player.name] (as repeatedly mentioned in Lady Mahir's research notes as '[player.name] brought me a new batch of stuff.') While this substance appears capable of powering metal-based devices, how it is used and produced remains a mystery.

As the documentary concluded, everyone present witnessed the first public display of Lady Mahir's final invention, "The Sealed Door."

This unique artifact consists of a bronze door with its frame, not attached to any wall or structure. The doorframe is adorned with intricate runes referencing the Purist Order, the Cultic God, the faith of Stars, and other prevalent beliefs of that era. These runes convey notions of "repulsion" and "prohibition," though their exact meanings remain to be deciphered. The Sealed Door can't be opened from any side and features a lock without a keyhole. Despite its exquisite craftsmanship and hollow interior, X-ray scans have revealed significant signs of liquid (possibly "Aether") erosion within.

Unlike Lady Mahir's other inventions, the purpose of this door remains a mystery to all. Some scholars connect it to the artifact "Shattered Dragon Eye" (which was severely damaged at excavation, with only its golden base remaining), suggesting a potential link to dragon lore. After crafting the Sealed Door, Lady Mahir wrote in her journal, "Maybe I'm even greater than a god," and then ceased all her invention works.

Despite mysteries yet to be unraveled, scholars welcomed this artifact with sheer excitement. The representative from Double Cross Technologies announced on the spot that profits from the next 10,000 units of Double Cross Neck & Shoulder Massagers sold would be donated to the research team during [player.name]'s era.

Amidst enthusiastic applause, all attendees returned to the conference hall for the final session of the day.

On the second evening of the symposium, scholars in attendance gathered to enjoy the folk music suite "Ode to Faraj," skillfully performed by twelve musicians from the National Folk Orchestra.

This musical piece was crafted based on the recovered artifact named "Faraj's Music Score." Following the melody, seven dancers from the Arzuna Dance Academy took the stage. Their performance mirrored a traditional dance typically performed during the "Regent's Festival" a millennium ago.

As the performance drew to a close, Professor Mimona delivered the concluding remarks for the symposium's second day.

"These incredible works of art were all funded, created, and disseminated by Faraj, a prominent noble and high lord during [player.name]'s era. Faraj was seen as [player.name]'s most fervent supporter during that era. Even though all of the Regent's followers were known for their loyalty, Faraj's devotion stood out.

He was also an incredibly wealthy lord whose domains would now span three provinces. At the peak of his wealth, his annual earnings matched a tenth of the national treasury. After [player.name] assumed the regency, Faraj devoted most of his efforts towards praising [player.name]. Apart from the captivating dance and music we just enjoyed, he sponsored the publication of at least a dozen books about [player.name] and personally funded the production of commemorative silver coins bearing [player.name]'s portrait. These coins have been unearthed across the empire, suggesting their extensive production and broad circulation.

Faraj himself was an exceptional lord—wise, shrewd, and ruthless toward his adversaries, and it's quite remarkable how deeply he revered the Regent. This vividly paints a picture of how [player.name] was seen as a godlike figure by the people of that time.

Moreover, as we all know, Faraj took his own life after [player.name]'s death due to illness. Despite his age, he personally attended the Regent's funeral, appointed successors for his legacy, then took poison in his mausoleum he had prepared long ago. It's said that his last words were: 'I must leave now. Maybe I'll still make it in time.'

Today, we've thoroughly delved into the influential nobles of [player.name]'s era, and I believe these discussions have offered valuable insights. Tomorrow, we'll shift our focus to discussing the commoners of the empire—traders, scoundrels, thieves, and the like. Make sure to get a good night's rest because tomorrow holds the promise of fruitful exchanges!"

In a relaxed atmosphere, the seminar reached its midpoint. Following group photos with the performers, the attendees returned to the hotel.

Our reporter Argus Tus will continue to cover the symposium's proceedings on the third day.

The conference on the third day was chaired by Associate Professor Rasmi from the History Department of Copport Business College. In his opening statements, he expressed regret for the absence of Professor Topaslar, the college's Chief History Professor, who fell ill with the flu just before the event and had entrusted Rasmi with presenting his paper at the conference.

Associate Professor Rasmi highlighted that during [player.name]'s era, the empire experienced a flourishing trade industry. The capital boasted at least three bustling marketplaces filled with vendors and merchants who, alongside the nobility, played vital roles in the empire's daily affairs. Recent archaeological findings have shed light on their connections to the Regent [player.name], a topic elucidated by Professor Topaslar in his paper.

"Asal and his bookstore 'The Angler' were well-known across the empire. Even today, 'The Angler' brand, featuring Asal's personal signature as its logo, remains a celebrated publishing house. Asal himself gained everlasting fame through his brainchild, the 'Encyclopedia.' This extensive work consists of thirty-nine volumes, documenting a myriad of creatures, events, and artifacts from folklore, alongside accounts of historical figures. The entire publication was made possible solely by [player.name]'s patronage, which is why you'll find the Regent's monogram on each volume's title page, along with the dedication 'In Honor of the Lord of Knowledge.' Although it's still unclear why the Regent decided to patronize a humble bookshop and support such a challenging, time-consuming publishing endeavor, the bond between Asal and [player.name] is undeniable."

When it comes to Bharat, he's often a figure we tend to overlook, probably because his time in the royal capital was rather short, spanning roughly the six months around [player.name]'s rise to regency. But let's not dismiss this fleeting character just yet. This trader, listed as a 'foreign merchant' in the city's records, likely tied the knot with one of the late Supreme Sultan's concubines, possibly Ansuya, as our suspicions now suggest. The royal treasury revealed several exquisite gifts that Bharat offered to the Regent, including an exquisite miniature house crafted of platinum, diamonds, and emeralds. The design, without a roof, symbolized 'may your wishes reach the stars,' a beautiful benediction. The base bore the words: 'To the finest landlord, she also sends her greetings. With gratitude.' Accompanying these treasures were jewels showing signs of wear, crafted in a style favored by the esteemed concubines of the harem during the late Supreme Sultan's reign.

Both Rasma and lead towards the idea that this happened after Bharat's marriage to one of the late Sultan's concubines. He returned all the jewels the late Sultan had gifted to his wife back to the palace, a gesture of remarkable integrity that showcased the confidence of the newlywed. Bharat believed he could provide his wife with even finer jewels, while she considered him a husband superior to the late Sultan. Of all the concubines, the only one eligible to wear such top-tier jewelry and possibly linked to Bharat was Ansuya (as both of them were from the same tribe). The only unfortunate part is that we haven't quite figured out what type of 'lord' a 'landlord' exactly is.

As for Malkina, she was already a well-known figure in the aristocratic women's social circles for her talents in embroidery and makeup artistry even before [player.name] ascended to the regency. When her master rose to power as the actual ruler of the empire, Malkina was appointed as the official court embroiderer. We've unearthed adorned with her distinctive eye-shaped monogram, once worn by the Grand Vizier, the Regent, and Lady Maggie. Speaking of which, our academy proudly possesses four of these garments, originally housed in the Copport Lord Museum. Incidentally, Copport was established as a port city during [player.name]'s regency by an anonymous merchant guild.

Moreover, we've discovered widespread worship dedicated to Lady Malkina within the capital and neighboring major domains. Archaeological findings revealed exquisite wooden and cotton needle cushions in various styles, all inscribed with the words: 'May my needle move as swiftly as Lady Malkina's.' Additionally, we've discovered Malkina figurines with basic features like a nose, eye sockets, and lips. These figurines allowed her followers to practice their makeup skills by applying pigments as they pleased. Though the details remain unclear, it's likely that this form of worship originated from [player.name]'s personal support, or at least spread with his tacit approval.

Lastly, let's talk about Lady Jenna, the best jeweler in the capital. Her life was even more closely intertwined with [player.name]'s. Handpicked by the Regent as the court jeweler, she designed and crafted jewelry for him, his family, and his trusted nobles within the Lapis Lazuli Palace. While extensive research has been devoted to this master jeweler who shaped the empire's fashion trends, a recent revelation stands out: Jenna has crafted seven sets of jewelry for [player.name] during her lifetime. Scans revealed inscriptions inside each set, marking different periods in [player.name]'s life.

The first set, crafted from gold and rubies, features three medium-sized gems. 'To My Friends and My Kind Employer,' symbolizing Jenna's early bond with [player.name].

The second set, crafted from gold and sapphires, boasts a large sapphire and inscribed 'Jewels for an Influential Courtier,' reflecting [player.name]'s service to the Supreme Sultan.

The third set, crafted from gold, diamonds, emeralds, sapphires, amethysts, citrine, jade, pearls, and other precious gems, is inscribed 'Master of the Empire,' believed to be worn by [player.name] upon ascending to the regency.

The fourth set, crafted from platinum, diamonds and sapphires, bears the inscription, 'Ten Years Have Passed,' serving as a poignant memento of [player.name]'s tenth year of reign.

The fifth set, crafted from precious metals, rubies, emeralds, and buffalo bone, bears the inscription 'For the Unbreakable.' We believe that this was a gift marking [player.name]'s anniversary with Lady Maggie, as it features a pair of gold bracelets designed to interlock—a symbol of marital unity back then. Interestingly, this set also marks the debut of buffalo bone in upscale jewelry.

The sixth set, crafted entirely from gold without gemstones, consists of a belt, an armlet, and a pair of earrings engraved with 'The Thirtieth Year,' evidently marking the thirtieth year of the Regent's reign. Perhaps by this point, both [player.name] and Jenna had grown weary of opulence. This set was presented in a beautiful ox bone case.

The seventh set, crafted from gold and diamonds, introduced the legendary diamond '[player.name]'s Heart,' a 320-carat masterpiece meticulously set within pure gold supports, resembling molten gold cascading over its crystalline surface. This colossal diamond, the empire's most prized possession, is now showcased at the National Museum.

Inscribed on this jewelry set (besides '[player.name]'s Heart,' this set includes a large diamond ring named '[player.name]'s Eye and an ebony staff adorned with gold) is the phrase: 'Perfection from Fate's Repeated Polishing.' At the time of crafting this jewelry, Jenna must have been elderly and gravely ill, as she passed away shortly after its completion. By then, [player.name] too, was likely in his later years, as only then would he have received such an exceptional staff as a gift.

In conclusion, the lives of these four artisans and merchants unfolded alongside [player.name]'s grandeur, all influenced by this exceptional regent. As they departed this world, I believe they all must have felt they had truly lived a fulfilling life. That concludes my presentation. Thank you all."

This speech garnered enthusiastic applause, prompting attendees to rise from their seats and flock to Associate Professor Rasmi for further insights. Many were moved to tears by the presentation—myself included.

On the third day of the symposium, Mr. Bakula, a researcher from the Capital Institute of Social Sciences and History, shared his latest thesis, titled "Riel: From Slave Girl to Matriarch."

During his presentation, Mr. Bakula showcased detailed images of Riel's crown, a treasured artifact passed down through generations within the Kur community (once disparagingly labeled as "barbarians" a thousand years ago). This ornate crown was adorned with feathers from various rare birds and decorative beads made from human bones. Following this display, Mr. Bakula then exhibited a set of primitive iron shackles.

"These are the standard shackles used in the empire's slave markets a thousand years ago, designed for the toughest slaves. Riel, a sturdy Kur woman recently captured, found herself imprisoned in a cage with these very restraints by the slavers. It must have been a dreadful experience for her, much like a wolf ensnared in a trap.

For reasons still unclear to us, [player.name], after penning his 'To Set Things Right' journal, started frequenting the slave market. As my colleague mentioned earlier, he might have been in search of Kaya and also bought Riel, an unpopular slave. Later, he revisited the market and liberated several other female Kur slaves, whose identity document fragments are still preserved in the museum. Back then, freed slaves would often fold their identity papers into small squares, tuck them into leather pouches, and wear them around their necks.

Following this, Riel began to make a name for herself in the capital. Unfortunately, since neither Riel nor her kin could read or write, there are no written records about her. Still, we can catch glimpses of her struggles through the accounts of others. Over three consecutive nights, guards rushed to intervene in clashes between a group of barbarian women, likely including Riel and her allies, and a local gang known as the Jackals.

After [player.name]'s rise to the Regent, Riel grew bolder in her actions. For a long period—possibly up to a decade—she relentlessly targeted and eliminated slavers. By beheading a hundred slavers, she earned the title of matriarch and the feathered crown we showcased earlier. She also smashed numerous sets of shackles similar to the ones we saw earlier.

There have been numerous records from scribes detailing slavers petitioning the Regent against bandits' attacks on their slave trades, but the Regent took no action. In the tenth year of his regency, [player.name] declared that slave trading would no longer receive protection from imperial forces or law, declaring, 'Those who seek to steal others' freedom must be prepared to have their own freedom and lives taken.' Following this decree, while slaves were still a common sight, raids on Kur, steppe dwellers, and nomadic settlements for slaves significantly decreased. Of course, the success of this policy was inseparable from the fact that the most influential and cruel slavers had been decimated by Riel and her comrades over the past decade.

(More introductions.)

To wrap up this presentation, I'd like to share a bit about myself. I belong to the Kur, or as the city dwellers labeled us a millennium ago, the 'barbarians.' When I was young, raw liver was a common dish at our table, quite tasty actually... Not human liver, of course, but seasoned sheep liver. My mother used to tell me stories of Riel the Matriarch, and she always ended with the same words. 'We owe Riel and [player.name] a lot. Without them, we wouldn't be here, I wouldn't have met your father—who just can't stomach raw liver—and you wouldn't be here.'

In [player.name]'s time, my father would have been considered a 'city dweller.' During those story sessions, he always agreed with my mother, saying, 'Enslaving others is just plain wrong. If anyone tries to take away your freedom, you must fight back.'

Now I'm thirty-four. I once made a feather crown from chicken and crow feathers found on the ground, something every Kur kid probably did. I can read Riel's name in two different languages. And most importantly, I've never been enslaved.

That wraps up my presentation. Thank you for your attention."

Hassan is a renowned figure in history, known for his compilation "Three Hundred Rubaiyat of Hassan," which is recommended as supplementary reading material for primary and middle school students in our country. Regarded as one of the most illustrious poets in history, Hassan was highlighted in several papers during the symposium, including the ones below.

"Old Hassan's Lamblet," authored by Mr. Sahaadin, a celebrated poet, lyricist, writer, and the recipient of the prestigious Hassan Award. His presentation offered a glimpse into Hassan's carefree and unconstrained life through the perspective of his legendary pet sheep, Lamblet.

"The End of Poetry: Hassan and the Political Situation of [player.name]'s Era," authored by Ms. Lumerian, a visiting professor from the Literature Department at Nursery National University. Through in-depth analysis of historical sources, she unveiled a different aspect of the poet—not just a master of verse but also a cunning strategist who used poetry as a tool to refute [player.name]'s rivals within the court.

"On the Complexity of Hassan", authored by Bitter Wine, the President of the Laurel Poets Society and a distinguished poet, historian, and sociologist. In his paper, he delved into the historical mysteries surrounding Hassan, including the unexplained longevity of his pet sheep and his sudden disappearance. (Hassan lived a healthy life until Regent [player.name] passed away. Estimated to be at least a century old, Hassan and his faithful companion Lamblet, who far outlived a sheep's typical lifespan, vanished without a trace following the Regent's funeral.) Bitter Wine also discussed a collection of poems titled 'The Fate Rectified,' composed during Hassan's later years.

Within this collection, known for its obscurity and mysterious themes, Hassan penned, 'The game of destiny spins, Shredded like paper by youthful delight. With hands, eyes, a heart, a soul that grins, To set things all right.' Bitter Wine suggested that while these cryptic verses might contain historical inaccuracies, their mystical undertones were undeniably captivating. He also shared that his alias "Bitter Wine" was inspired by Hassan's famous lines: 'Drink fate's wine, Bitter yet true, Brew with heart, sweetness ensue.'

It is worth noting that the young scholar, who had interrupted the conference multiple times earlier, raised his hand once more, but the host refused to pass him the microphone this time. Following Bitter Wine's presentation, the young scholar had a lengthy discussion with the elderly poet.

On the third day of the symposium, Professor Dauma, the President of Nursery National University and a distinguished legal scholar, delivered a lecture titled "On the Essence of Nursery." She delved into the shared roots of Nursery and Nursery National University, reflecting on the eventful history that spanned a thousand years. Here are some excerpts from her speech.

"A thousand years ago, creating the institution known as the 'Nursery' was a daring move for the people of that time. Back then, literacy rates were extremely low, and the ability to write was almost a luxury reserved for the upper class. However, [player.name] insisted that every young beggar, vagrant, orphan, and thief in his Nursery not only learn to read and write but also acquire survival skills for a harsh world. After ascending to the regency, [player.name] continued to invest resources into his Nursery—he would teach there himself alongside his trusted courtiers like Nawfal and Vizier, reserving esteemed positions in his court for Nursery graduates who had come of age.

To attribute [player.name]'s actions purely to benevolence would be underestimating this legendary politician. [player.name] decreed that only kids from the lowest social echelons be admitted to the Nursery. Those with household servants or parents owning gold ornaments were deemed unsuitable. Following his initial success, he established similar academies in major cities and standardized the curricula.

Then, in the seventeenth year of his rule, he announced a groundbreaking reform in the empire's bureaucratic system—all officials must pass standardized exams for appointment and promotion, with the exam content closely aligned with the subjects taught in the Nursery academies. This news sent shockwaves through the aristocracy, as their children had never faced such selection processes. The exam subjects—ranging from accounting, writing, math, history, to logic—were entirely foreign to them. As a result, many nobles shed their gold accessories, dismissed servants, and disguised themselves as commoners to enroll their children in the Nursery. This reform became known as the 'Gold's Downfall' for this very reason.

Through the Nursery and the reforms, [player.name] took about twenty years to gradually replace most officials in the bureaucracy with young men lacking noble lineage. These individuals showed nearly fervent loyalty to him and naturally rejected the uneducated offspring of nobles. Throughout [player.name]'s reign, at least four Viziers originated from the Nursery, and many courtiers debating in court were former classmates there.

Now looking at it from a contemporary standpoint, especially from the perspective of an aged legal scholar like myself, [player.name]'s methods were remarkably innovative for the era. He set a 'bar' for officials and enforced consequences—those failing the exams would be banished from the court. These actions pushed everyone in the bureaucratic system to better themselves so that they could maintain their positions. Moreover, he sidelined the supporters of the traditional nobility while safeguarding the interests of its most skilled members, like Lord Zaki, Lord Nawfal, and Lord Faraj. In doing this, he sent a clear message throughout the empire—the Regent valued wisdom over lineage.

This is what I mean by the 'essence of the Nursery' in my title. By establishing the Nursery, [player.name] gradually reshaped the empire's social structure. As we know, he progressively abolished slavery by supporting Riel in secret, and through the Nursery, he further blurred the boundary between commoners and nobles, which resulted in the empire's most thriving, lively, and inclusive decades. Moreover, each one of us present here today, and every individual living in this country, has benefited from [player.name]'s legacy. Prior to him, the world was teeming with dragons, Cultic Gods, sorcerers, creatures haunting the night, and shackles binding hands, yet he banished them all.

What was once called a 'Nursery' a millennium ago is now known as the 'university.'

To conclude this speech, I'd like to share a quote from a distinguished writer and journalist. 'In our humanity lies the power of storytelling, separating us from mere beasts. Through shared history and myths, we weave the fabric of our community, thriving within its embrace. Gratitude to yesterday, for it molds our tomorrow.'

Truly, gratitude to yesterday. Gratitude to [player.name] and that fateful day when he chose to gather together those children who were struggling to find enough to eat. Gratitude to you, [player.name]. And gratitude to you all, my dear colleagues."

Professor Dauma's speech received enthusiastic applause, with all attendees standing up from their seats.

After the round of applause, the attendees headed to the banquet hall for lunch.

During lunch, Mr. Kustasa, Vice President of the Capital Academy of Social Sciences and History, a distinguished authority in institutional and social history, shared his latest research findings in a presentation titled "The Pack in the Shadows: Dark Alleys and the Poor in [player.name]'s Era."

In an engaging twist, he incorporated a captivating performance into his presentation—actors reenacted scenes of Alim and his accomplices engaging in theft. Dressed as thieves from a thousand years ago, the actors encircled a pot-bellied "noble lord," snatching silk scarves, jewel-encrusted rings, gold bracelets, and coin pouches from him... As the audience burst into laughter, one of the actors suddenly emptied a large bundle onto the floor, revealing cell phones, watches, wallets, and makeup bags. As attendees scrambled to retrieve their belongings, it became apparent that while the audience was engrossed in the performance, the real show was unfolding in the shadows!

"Well, my dear colleagues, what you just experienced is precisely the tactic Alim and his thieves were experts in. They'd start with a few small-time crooks stealing things from a flashy 'victim,' pretty much like a school of small fish going after a big one. Sometimes, they'd even make it obvious, leaving loopholes or starting loud arguments on purpose. Once they had everyone's attention, the more experienced members of the gang would swoop in and start swiping from the crowd. This age-old trick still works like a charm today, so if you ever see a heated argument or fight going down, try not to get too caught up in it.

Back to the point, it seems Alim had a personal connection with the Regent [player.name]. Records from that time reveal that Alim brought many kids, like beggars and young thieves known as 'pups,' to the Nursery founded by [player.name] himself. Despite his role as a notorious ringleader in the Dark Alley, Alim seemed to understand that stealing wasn't the way to go. So whenever he could, he'd steer those children to places he believed held more promise.

What's more, we have good reason to believe that the tie between Alim and [player.name] went deeper. It's possible that this seasoned thief acted as [player.name]'s mouthpiece in the Dark Alley. After [player.name] assumed the regency, the poor folks in the Dark Alley started receiving monthly aid in the form of food and money. However, there was a catch—they had to contribute to public works, tasks like digging wells, cleaning streets, and managing waste, all overseen by none other than Alim. Clearly, this cunning dog didn't foot the bill for these tasks on his own, so the most logical conclusion is that he dipped into the Regent's coffer to keep things running smoothly.

Additionally, we have another crucial piece of evidence linking the thief to the Regent. In the ruins believed to be Alim's 'kennel,' archaeologists uncovered a gold ring found in an unmarked grave holding the remains of a man in his sixties. The ring's inner surface displayed [player.name]'s monogram, clearly indicating it was a gift from the Regent rather than stolen loot, as even for Alim, snatching a ring from the Regent's hand would have been an impossible feat. Now, picture this: Upon learning the sad news of his friend Alim the Old Dog's demise, the grief-stricken Regent removed a ring from his own finger and handed it to a messenger with instructions to place it in the grave.

Back then, the law forbade thieves and prostitutes from having proper burial grounds. Alim's pups, who laid him to rest, likely kept quiet about the Regent's gold ring hidden away in the tomb. Hence, the golden ring, concealed within the unmarked grave, evaded the covetous eyes of grave robbers, staying intact for a thousand years.

Now, here's a question: how on earth did [player.name], born into nobility, brought up in an aristocratic household, and quickly climbing the ranks as an influential courtier, manage to forge a strong bond with a thief like Alim? This raises yet another puzzle shrouding [player.name]. As hinted at time and again during our discussions, '[player.name] seemed to know everything from the beginning.' Well, looks like my humble research adds another subtle glint to this Regent's aura of enigma."

This lively lunchtime episode sparked academic conversations. Amidst discussions, all attendees returned to the conference venue.

In the afternoon of the third day, Ms. Ibrani, a professor in the History Department at Sunier University, focusing on migration, hygiene, and poverty history, shared her most recent paper, titled "Raed, Vagrants, and the Empire."  "Raed stands out as another captivating figure from [player.name]'s era. She was the leader of all vagrants within the capital, portrayed in historical records as a bold, defiant woman with decayed teeth and wielding a mace. During an era of turmoil caused by the empire's rapid expansion, droves of vagabonds sought refuge in the capital, and their survival relied entirely on finding shelter under Raed's protective wings. Our findings indicate that those under Raed's care had survival rates four to six times higher than the average across the empire.  Here comes the question: how did Raed make such a sheer difference between life and death? The answer uncovers a fascinating twist—Raed seemed to share a personal bond with [player.name] himself. In Lord Nawfal's diary—hat tip to his faithful journaling—we discovered this note: '[player.name] set up a meeting for me with Ra. She refused to visit the palace, so I went to the slums.'  While 'Ra' in this context could refer to someone else, the subsequent references to 'she' and the term 'slums' strongly hint that 'Ra' can only be Raed. Therefore, based on Lord Nawfal's records, it was the Regent himself who arranged the meeting between him and Raed, and he agreed to personally visit the slums—a place that hardly befits Lord Nawfal's status as the Grand Vizier.  This brief message ignites our curiosity: How did the Regent get to know Raed? And given that Lord Nawfal shortened Raed to 'Ra' here, does this suggest that Raed's complete name appeared earlier in the diary, perhaps on those worn-out pages? If that's the case, did the Grand Vizier have a personal connection with this Leader of the Vagrants? And why?  With these lingering questions in mind, we delved deeper into Raed's story and found a surprising revelation—Raed was, in fact, literate. We discovered a number of counterfeit identity papers—documents typically reserved for freed slaves—among the excavated tombs for vagrants. Moreover, we realized that Raed possessed considerable wealth. In the early years of [player.name]'s regency, she invested in shops and housing across the capital to shelter vagrants and offer them business opportunities. In other words, Raed, a literate, wealthy woman with ties to the Regent, had countless reasons to live a lavish life like a princess, but she chose to stay with the vagrants, tending to their needs and paving paths to brighter futures for them.  The exact location of Raed's tomb has been long lost to history. All we can figure is that at some point during the later years of [player.name]'s reign, she led her followers to a desolate domain where she spent her final days. She brought numerous groundbreaking ideas to the empire, the most notable being the creation of commercial spaces specifically run by the homeless. These establishments stood the test of time for the next thousand years. It's common knowledge that during the empire's many future crises, the people managing these spaces stepped up to assist those in need.  More importantly, Raed transformed the concept of the term 'vagrants.' Instead of feeling ashamed of their status, these wanderers united and worked together purposefully. In time, they would become influential figures in historical events on numerous occasions."  Professor Ibrani's presentation received enthusiastic applause. Given the limited research on Raid, the audience was thrilled by the scholarly insights she provided.

At the conference, researcher Sirhak Pamuti from the Whetted Grassland Foundation delivered a presentation titled "Sirshana and the Homeland People During [player.name]'s Era". Delving into the extensive historical archives of [player.name]'s era, he focused on a lesser-known figure of that time—Sirshana, the Homeland prince recognized as the "Roaming Swordsman."

"Princess Sirshana didn't want to live the life of a prince. Despite having many supporters, they chose to live in the Dark Alley, leading a carefree and scandalous life. Nonetheless, his senior attendants dutifully followed the Homeland's protocols, carefully recording Sirshana's growth, words, deeds, and decisions. These records were passed down among the Homelanders and eventually became esteemed cultural relics of the Whetted Grassland Foundation about 91 years ago."

Sirhak presented visual materials of this invaluable ancient text from a millennium ago.

"Through these pages, we can vividly follow Prince Sirshana's life. The first line on the opening page means, 'The virtuous shall not be forgotten.' This book documents a crucial event closely related to the theme of this symposium, an event that the Whetted Grassland Foundation has yet to fully comprehend to this day. I'm sharing it here, hoping to gain valuable insights from my colleagues."

Following this, Sirhak displayed a line elegantly written text, underscored by thick black lines, suggesting the scribe had eagerly highlighted this sentence.

"'On that fateful day, [player.name] simply called out the name Sirshana. Who leaked His Highness's true identity? Who did it? Who exactly betrayed us?!' The scribe must have been in a state of sheer panic—fearing that the revelation of the prince's identity would lead to manhunts and massacres they had endured before. Thankfully, their worst fears didn't come true. After [player.name] assumed the role of the Regent, Sirshana and his followers, who had already fled to distant lands, were brought back. In the court, Sirshana was officially appointed the lord of a prosperous domain. This appointment is also documented in these records."

To emphasize his point, Sirhak revealed a message written in gold powder, featuring a crucial word written in multiple languages: "Whetted Grassland." The page was adorned with numerous stars bearing human faces, believed to represent the Stars revered in the Homeland.

"When Prince Sirshana received the Kabalua Domain, he renamed it 'Whetted Grassland.' This name originally referred to a desolate area overgrown with switchgrasses in the capital. For reasons unknown to us, Sirshana selected this name. Following this, nearly all the surviving Homelanders openly migrated to this domain. There, Sirshana ruled as their monarch. The people there were almost free from the empire's laws, only needing to pay taxes on time and fulfill their military duties. In the Whetted Grassland, Sirshana reinstated the Homeland's practices, traditions, beliefs, and culture. This domain brought solace to the Homeland survivors. For years to come, the Whetted Grassland firmly backed [player.name] and his empire.

As Sirhak wrapped up his presentation, he posed his question once more.

"So, how did [player.name] discover Prince Sirshana's true identity? Logically, he had no ties to a random swordsman roaming the Dark Alley, so why did he suddenly grant a fiefdom to him? Wasn't he concerned about potential opposition from the Homelanders? Didn't he worry that Sirshana might intend to seize the throne? His decisions and actions imply he was familiar with Sirshana as if they were old friends... but we all know that's completely impossible. I eagerly await insights from my esteemed colleagues, and if needed, our foundation is ready to disclose more historical records about Prince Sirshana and the Whetted Grassland.

The audience engaged in a lively debate on this subject for forty minutes. During the lively discussion, the young scholar, who had repeatedly interrupted the conference, once again shouted, "As I said, he just knew everything!" and was subsequently escorted out of the venue.

During the banquet on the third day, a heated debate unfolded between Mr. Biller, the High Priest of the Order of Pure Light and Grace, and Mr. Shaharu, the General Manager of Liberation Bloom Labor Dispatch Co, Ltd. To the intrigued audience, they sought to prove the prominence of their respective deities during [player.name]'s era.

High Priest Biller highlighted that after [player.name]'s rise to the regency, Iman, the High Priest of the Purist at the time, was summoned to the Lapis Lazuli Palace and served at the Regent's side until the end of his days. In addition, unearthed manuscripts revealed records of nobles petitioning for divine blessings, indicating the persuasive influence of the Purist Order. It was rumored that these blessings, accompanied by the priests' own excruciating pain, possessed the miraculous power to instantly heal any wound.

On the other hand, Manager Shaharu argued that such blessings were precisely the evidence that the Purist faith was fake. "Healing wounds by whipping and cutting others? This masochistic ritual sounds like something out of a fever dream! It just shows that the so-called faith of the Purist Order was more of a mass hysteria during the reign of the Supreme Sultan! A cruel aristocratic game masquerading as a religion."

Enraged by Manager Shaharu's remarks, Priest Biller knelt in a plea to the Purist for divine retribution against the defiler. Five minutes later, he rose to his feet again, pointing out that the Cult worshipped by Manager Shaharu was no different in terms of collective delusion and brutality. He mentioned the deity's consumption of human souls and the reported deaths of numerous cultists within "stone chambers." He then posed a sharp question: if Shaharu dismissed the Purist's healing abilities as delusions, how could he rationalize the Cult's cannibalistic rituals? "The suffering our priests endured brought solace to others, but those cultists? What good came from their deaths?"

Manager Shaharu, clearly prepared for this question, showcased a collection of paintings, books, and photographs, attributing them to the creative inspirations ignited by the meditations in stone chambers, herbal initiations, and mystical tattoos provided by Liberation Bloom. He mentioned a number of esteemed artists, writers, singers, and politicians who regularly sought Liberation Bloom's services to explore their inner selves and forge connections with a higher realm, guided by the Cult's core tenet "the unknowable descends through me." "With this belief, the human soul evolves from a mere burden into a vessel of infinite potential."

In response, High Priest Biller dismissed Manager Shaharu's arguments, highlighting that the Order of Pure Light and Grace had experienced many similar instances. He mentioned how followers participated in rituals like jasmine perfume baths, mica flake trials, and pillar prayers to achieve inner peace, resulting in souls that were akin to "snow-washed surfaces—pure, light, and tranquil." Meanwhile, he expressed skepticism about the enlightenment claimed by Cult followers. "Have there been rumors about the Cult using an herbal mixture with hallucinogens and anesthetics? Given their effects, I wouldn't be shocked by anything they might do." To reinforce his point, High Priest Biller presented a document unsuitable for the banquet atmosphere, detailing certain... excrement-related activities conducted by Liberation Bloom followers.

Manager Shaharu deemed this a direct personal affront, insisting that these activities bore no connection to [player.name] and were thus unsuitable for such a setting.

High Priest Billar asserted these activities were closely linked to [player.name], citing Iman's role as the Regent's trusted confidant. He pointed out that Iman engaged in daily conversations with [player.name], a detail recorded in the court scribe's accounts.

In response, Shaharu Manager emphasized [player.name]'s connections with Badriyyah, the Cult's leader at the time. He presented an archaeological report documenting Cult worship practices, unearthed in the remains of a slaughterhouse on the capital's outskirts, stating that the slaughterhouse was constructed after [player.name]'s ascension to the regency, likely tailored to accommodate followers of the Cult. He further argued that the unique Liberation Bloom symbol was purportedly designed by Badriyyah herself and subsequently adopted by all her followers. Correspondence among nobles from that time period even verified that [player.name] bore the same mark. "Doesn't this point to a connection between Badriyyah and [player.name]? Would he allow just any woman to mark his skin? He was the Regent!"

Once again, High Priest Biller chuckled dismissively at this claim. "Are you out of your mind, Manager Shaharu, to bring this up? Records from the Order show that they actually supposed the spread of the Liberation Bloom symbol, believing it could sever the commoners' ties to the Cultic God. Doesn't this prove that [player.name] aimed to free everyone from the manipulation of the Cult's so-called god?"

Manager Shaharu burst into laughter at this statement. "Come on, keep going! What happened after the Order threw their support behind Liberation Bloom?" Seeing his opponent's face turn pale, Shaharu pressed further, citing merchant correspondence from that era. "Indeed, [player.name] demanded that the chief priests and followers of the Order bear this very symbol. Following this, the priests lost the ability to commune with their god. However, they insisted that the symbol had nothing to do with the situation—for if it did, it would mean their god, also affected by the symbol, were nothing different from those worshipped by the Cult! Instead, they suggested the Regent's tyrannical rule enraged the god, causing them to withdraw their blessings. But in truth, during [player.name]'s reign, peace and prosperity thrived. If that was tyranny, what did the Order perceive as a just rule? Care to enlighten us, High Priest Biller?"

In response, High Priest Billar insisted that being an exceptional regent did not necessarily make him an outstanding religious leader. He criticized [player.name]'s decree for all Order priests to bear the defiled markings, adamantly stating that the loss of divine communication couldn't have been caused by a blockage of the Purist's divine power—how could that even be possible? "The Purist stands as the one true god, existing at the core of the universe. They have always been present—They merely shifted Their gaze to other realms for a while. Yes, They will return, hence why every follower of the Order of Pure Light and Grace keeps a 1001-year countdown clock. The Purist will return once the clock hits zero."

High Priest Biller's statement evoked another burst of laughter from Manager Shaharu. "Oh, right. The countdown has been reset three times: three centuries ago, one century ago, and two decades ago, right? Your god sure takes their sweet time, don't they?"

High Priest Billar chuckled in agreement. "I couldn't agree more, Mr. Shaharu. Waiting for a god's prophesied return seems a lot more dignified than smearing feces on oneself."

As High Priest Biller spoke those words, Manager Shaharu lunged forward, grabbing the High Priest by the hair—it was a wig. The High Priest staggered, arms flailing, and tumbled to the ground, now bald-headed, shouting, "Police! Where are the police?!" Then, two of the High Priest's attendants rushed in, knocking Manager Shaharu to the ground. A waiter present, a supporter of Liberation Bloom, joined the scuffle and struck one of the attendants with a food tray. The brawl continued until police officers arrived twelve minutes later and separated both parties.

As High Priest Biller and Manager Shaharu were eventually escorted away, the audience applauded the extraordinary "debate" they had witnessed.

The final day of the conference was chaired by Ms. Chiola, Vice President of Arzuna Dance Academy and a well-known dance artist.

Following a brief introduction, Ms. Chiola welcomed Ms. Menes, a respected writer and historian, to start the first session of the day—"Maggie: The Unchanged One."

Ms. Menes started her presentation by highlighting a commonly known fact—Maggie and [player.name] did not have any children. Consequently, after the Regent and she passed away in succession, state power was entrusted to a group of "councilors" handpicked by [player.name] during his lifetime. This has long been seen as the greatest lament of the [player.name] era, leading many to ponder: if these two remarkable individuals had left behind an heir, what direction might the empire have veered towards?

"I don't think [player.name] ever planned to have children," Ms. Menes expressed, "Lady Maggie probably became unable to conceive after a miscarriage. Despite this, [player.name], acting as the Regent, remained faithful to one wife throughout his life, an uncommon practice for the time. If he truly wanted heirs, he could have taken concubines, and as a traditional noblewoman, Lady Maggie wouldn't have objected.

Given that such a natural scenario didn't happen, it's reasonable to infer that [player.name] intentionally chose not to have an heir. He trusted the empire to those without so-called blue blood, understanding that if he had his own heirs, the power struggle would erupt before they could even speak. He was also aware that his heirs might not uphold his political ideals—how could he ensure that future generations would think as he did?

As a great politician and a great man, [player.name] focused on securing the loyalty of his current followers. Therefore, he spent years training and guiding his trusted young followers, instructing them to share his vision. Then, with confidence, he entrusted the empire to them. Even long after his demise, his decision continued to profoundly shape the kingdom. I venture to say that there is no other place in the world where democracy bloomed so early.

Now, let's circle back to Lady Maggie.

As we've discussed at length in this symposium, [player.name], following his 'To Set Things Right' manuscript, reshaped the destinies of many with remarkable efficiency, leading them all towards brighter futures. Among them, Lady Maggie stood as a constant amidst the whirlwind of change. Despite [player.name]'s supreme authority, she remained steadfast in her ways. At the end of each busy day, the Regent sought solace in Maggie's company, sharing a casual chat over a hookah. Just as a ship navigates turbulent waters, relying on the unwavering light of a lighthouse, so too did the captain of the empire find strength in her constancy.

In conclusion, while we rightfully praise [player.name]'s heroic feats, let's not forget the steadfast presence behind his brilliance. Lady Maggie stood faithfully beside this extraordinary Regent. Her love was gentle, enduring, and unwavering—it never changed."

Thank you, my dear colleagues."

The second session on the fourth day featured a presentation by Professor Mimona, who offered a unique perspective, "[player.name]'s Servants."

In his study, Professor Mimona explored the origins, lineage, education levels, divisions of labor, and management structures of the key attendants within [player.name]'s household. Additionally, drawing from the latest archaeological findings, Professor Mimona traced the life trajectories of [player.name]'s several key attendants.

"Even to this day, a thousand years later, we are still puzzled by the motivations behind [player.name]'s sudden decision to purchase the noble title Murad Tus for his servant Zephyr and recommend Zephyr to Jawad, another influential courtier. Historical records offer us a glimpse: Zephyr, namely Murad Tus, was instantly captivated by Lady Arumina at first sight. In return, Lady Arumina, too, fell in love with Zephyr upon seeing his charming running. The rest won't need much elaboration—even now, on occasions like Valentine's Day, we see products featuring the names of this couple, while romantic phrases like 'A gentle bite is a sign of love' have become cliche.

Another perplexing truth is the Regent's another sudden decision, following this note "To Set Things Right", to grant freedom to both Inal, Lady Maggie's dowry slave girl, and Aziz, the Regent's own attendant. He even granted Aziz the authority to recruit his own servants, leading to his personal guards being primarily from Aziz's clan. Inal later became the court's chief lady-in-waiting and married Aziz at the age of twenty-five—a rather late age for a first marriage back then. This delay was reportedly due to her overwhelming responsibilities that left little room for romance. Following their marriage, Aziz and Inal raised at least seven children, as history records show that Lady Maggie once requested the court ceremonial officer to host a 'banquet for the mother of seven.' From the guest list, we can see that at least one of Inal's children was named 'Mae,' a clear gesture of respect to Lady Maggie.

As for Gullis, once known as the 'sharp-eyed slave' in [player.name]'s household, he gained freedom around the time of the 'To Set Things Right' note. After that, Gullis faithfully served [player.name] until the eleventh year of [player.name]'s regency, then he left the court. We believe he likely traveled northward, returning to his homeland. Archaeologists recently unearthed a tribal chieftain's boundary marker near the remains of the highlanders' settlement, engraved with Gullis's name and the phrase 'Friend of the Regent.' It might seem a bit audacious for a former slave to claim friendship with the Regent... but as a new chieftain returning to his tribe after more than a decade of wandering, Gullis likely needed such endorsement from the highest authority.

In conclusion, by examining the life paths of these former slaves, we can catch a glimpse of [player.name]'s nature: a man who is highly perceptive, knowledgeable, and deeply caring about the well-being of all."

Professor Mimona's insights were responded to with rounds of applause. Here, as the author of this article, I'd like to share a personal note. My last name is Tus, a name that seemed to appear out of thin air after [player.name]'s reign. This name appears to be a fictitious noble title devised by [player.name], who assigned it to the servant once known as Zephyr through methods like falsification and bribery.

While the reasons behind this decision remain a mystery, as the offspring of Murad Tus and Lady Alumina, a lineage our family has always cherished, I must express my most sincere gratitude to [player.name], my ancestor's former master and unwavering friend.

Reported by Argus Tus, Nursery National University.

During the lunch break of the fourth day, the development team of the video game "Sultan's Game" presented an exquisite trailer titled "Supernatural Elements of [player.name]'s Era." As we all know, Sultan's Game is a video game based on the actual historical events during [player.name]'s era, immersing players in an alternate world where [player.name] didn't "set things right."

The trailer showcases popular supernatural elements from [player.name]'s era, including dragons and jinns, drawing inspiration from historical accounts that mention [player.name] being accompanied by three jinn attendants named Veesa, Endry, and Iliona. While traditional historians tend to interpret these "jinns" as metaphors for influential courtiers close to [player.name], their exact counterparts remain a mystery.

The developers speculate that these jinns might have been foreigners with distinct appearances compared to the locals. Through historical research, the developers discovered that those jinns worshipped a certain queen. This discovery aligns with the discoveries made during the excavation of the Lapis Lazuli Palace: archaeologists unearthed a shattered golden cage shaped like human ribs, wrapped in layers of silk, and locked within a separate small chamber. The base of the cage was inscribed with the word "Queen," while the inner bottom panel was delicately etched with three names repeatedly—Veesa, Endry, and Iliona, the very names of the three jinns.

If a "queen" was indeed imprisoned within the cage, only a few dozen centimeters tall, what did those carved names signify? Did they symbolize resentment, a thirst for vengeance, or something entirely different? The cage shows signs of violent twisting and breaking. Drawing from this detail, the developers weaved tales involving the jinns and their queen into the game. Now, you can easily find Sultan's Game on Steam and immerse yourself in a bizarre world teeming with jinns, magic, dragons, tyrants, and sinister cards brought by a certain magician.

But let's leave fantasy as it is. As displayed in the trailer, after [player.name]'s era, all traces of supernatural phenomena vanished from the empire's records. The Regent likely set a clear boundary in his realm, keeping out all things supernatural.

As the trailer concluded, Sultan's Game developers brought in a cosplayer portraying the Supreme Sultan to engage with the audience, and this amusing interlude received positive responses. The audience agreed that video games could be an effective tool to spark the young people's interest in history, offering a novel way to disseminate knowledge for media and content creators in today's world.

In the afternoon of the last day, Ms. Chiola introduced the audience to the touring performance, "Arzuna: Dance of the Sun"—a grand spectacle entirely staged by the faculty and students of Arzuna Dance Academy, featuring dances meticulously restored from Lady Arzuna's ancient records.

"Lady Arzuna is believed to be one of the earliest recorded dancers and the most exceptional of her time. Not only was she passionate about dancing, but she was also dedicated to creating new dance forms. She left behind an illustrated manuscript titled 'Dance of the Sun,' a priceless treasure even today. I believe that every dancer in our land has perused this manual, where each movement is depicted with precise illustrations, comprehensible even to those who are unable to read. The last dance featured in the book is the Dance of the Sun, a choreography with a mysterious topic. Today, I'm excited to share some discoveries about the dance.

Arzuna and [player.name] shared the same father, while their mothers had never met in their lifetimes. It is likely that [player.name]'s intended for this concubine and her daughter to remain secluded within the domain, far from the capital where his legitimate wife lived. However, upon ascending to the regency, [player.name] abruptly visited his younger sister.

This sudden visit happened around the time of the 'To Set Things Right' journal. The future Regent brought Arzuna to the capital, welcomed her into his own household, introduced her as 'my sister' to all, and promptly started her education in reading, writing, and etiquette. Moreover, he arranged for the leading dancer from the House of Delights to accompany her. Such gestures were rare for a brother towards his sister in that era, and even now.

These discoveries were found from the House of Delights' ledgers, documents related to [player.name]'s household, and correspondences among lords. While we lack details about Arzuna's feelings back then, it's conceivable that she experienced fear and anxiety, unsure of the intentions of this brother she had never met before. However, with the companionship of the skilled dancer by her side, she gradually adapted to her new life. Given her exceptional intellect, literacy skills and court etiquette posed no challenge to her. However, why did the Regent arrange such courses for her? Arzuna must have considered this question as well, likely believing that her brother had chosen a husband who would advance his own career.

However, after [player.name] assumed the regency, his decision once again surprised Arzuna. He hired the dancer who had been accompanying Arzuna, handpicked two skilled painters, dispatched a group of Honor Guards led by the Honor Guard Nabhani, and then instructed Arzuna to travel across the continent 'to witness and remember all the dances of the land,' a line that now adorns the title page of the book 'Dance of the Sun.' Nabhani must have enjoyed this assignment, given that historical accounts mention his personal luggage alone filling up four carriages. Along the journey, Nabhani left behind at least thirty tales of heroic rescues. For this, Arzuna even composed a dance in honor of this dashing swordsman, titled 'He Has Come.'

Now, let's set aside the historical details and allow our mind to drift for a while. If you were in Arzuna's shoes, riding in that carriage toward the distant horizon, what would you feel about the new life? Just a few months earlier, she was trapped within her domain, keeping vigil at her mother's grave. Etched on the tombstone was a haunting inscription. 'She waited, but he never came. Now, beneath the soil, she has all the time to wait.' You can sense the coldness in these words.

At first, Arzuna must have resented [player.name], who had a complete family, a promising future, and an ideal life that she lacked. But then suddenly, her brother brought her to the capital. There, she encountered new experiences, expanded her knowledge, and was even granted the freedom to pursue her passions. Then, in the blink of an eye, her brother ascended to the throne, and she became a princess. And in another instant, she found herself seated in a grand carriage beside her trusted companion—her brother asked her to chase the sun on the voyage, to witness and remember every dance.

Let's not forget the fact that Arzuna was a young lady back then. All the turmoils she had experienced before paled in comparison to the whirlwind changes of the past few months. During the journey, as the carriage wheels rolled, her legs swayed while she engaged in casual conversations with the dancer and the Honor Guard, directing the painters to capture each moment of the dancer's movements... Arzuna must have felt a mix of bewilderment and joy at that point. As her journey continued, her bewilderment faded while her joy blossomed. Eventually, when she believed she had understood herself completely, she sprang off the carriage, gathered all her comrades, and performed the Dance of the Sun.

This dance requires the participation of eleven performers: one portraying Arzuna, another as her dancer friend, one as Nabhani, two as painters, five as other guards, and the final one, symbolizing the sun itself. Throughout the dance, Arzuna depicts the entirety of her life's journey, starting with anguish, confusion, animosity, and desolation. Then, she becomes enveloped in the sun's warm embrace. Each of her companions interprets their own unique roles: Nabhani brandishes his sharp blade, the painters sketch the world's landscapes, and the dancer reveals love's mysteries through the fluid motions of her waist... The world unfurls before Arzuna, and in that moment, she realizes how much she missed in the past and how much she can achieve in the future! Thus, at the climax, the 'sun' rises, and all performers extend their arms to embrace its radiance... As the sun sets, performers lie down and sleep, except for Arzuna, who rises, standing at the center stage. She delicately extracts a new sun from her chest, symbolizing a fresh beginning. Indeed, the sun may rise and set, but the essence of the sun remains settled in everyone's heart.

For all dancers, myself included, portraying Arzuna in the Dance of the Sun is the highest honor they can imagine. The sheer variety of movements, the depth of emotion, and the precision of posture required for this role far surpass those of any other character in the dance. Time and again, we strive to merge our spirits with that of Arzuna, who danced a thousand years ago. In the silence of the night, we rise, draw forth the miniature sun from our chests, and present it to the world. This is Arzuna's dance to the sun, a dance from [player.name]'s sister to her beloved brother, and a dance offered to the world by countless generations of dancers."

As applause filled the air, Ms. Chiola concluded her speech with elegance. "Arzuna: Dance of the Sun" is still on tour today. You can get tickets through major ticketing agencies. Don't pass up the chance if you're a true art lover.

The final presentation of the symposium was delivered by Ms. Hajur, a researcher in astronomical history at the National Planetarium, titled "Lumera and Fardak: Secrets Hidden in the Stellar Trajectories."

"Back in my student days, every exam week, my classmates would playfully construct a Lumera altar using white pebbles in our dormitory and engage in a bit of worship, believing this ritual would help them remember the knowledge needed for their exams. Lumera, the Regent [player.name]'s adopted daughter, was renowned for her exceptional memory, not to mention her extraordinary achievement of having a constellation named after her. This constellation, particularly brilliant in autumn, sits adjacent to Perseus, consisting of four prominent stars (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, and Delta Lumera) alongside Beta and Gamma Fardak. With a touch of imagination, one can almost visualize these stars forming the shape of a lady holding a book.

From the imperial records, we can glimpse into how constellation Lumera came into existence. [player.name]'s funeral was overseen by Lady Lumera, who was the head librarian of the royal library at the time. Serenely holding the late Regent's crown, she led the procession into his mausoleum. After the funeral, she stepped out of the mausoleum, gazed up at the night sky, and addressed the crowd with composure, 'I've lingered in this realm for too long.' With arms raised high, she whispered cryptic incantations. Suddenly, a fierce gale materialized out of thin air, compelling other mourners to cower on the ground. As for Lumera herself, she was lifted steadily by the wind, ascending into the heavens... until she merged with the stars above.

On that very evening, the royal astronomers recorded the sudden appearance of the Lumera constellation.

I understand how wild this account may seem, but prior to this incident, no astronomical records from any corner of the world had ever mentioned this particular constellation. On that particular day, astronomers worldwide marveled at this 'newcomer' in the sky, with at least ten nations interpreting it as an auspicious sign. Subsequently, the empire's astronomers sent letters detailing the event to their peers globally, and their accounts were met with widespread acknowledgment. This explains why many languages have named this constellation 'Lumera,' although it is also known by other monikers such as 'The Regent's Daughter' or 'The Book-Reading Lady.'

The constellation 'Fardak,' which I mentioned earlier, is another newcomer that appeared around a thousand years ago. It appears dimmer than Lumera and can only be spotted with the naked eye during autumn and spring. This constellation is also associated with a legend recorded in the empire's official annals. Fardak was once a prince of a tribal state that had surrendered to the empire. He arrived in the capital as a diplomatic hostage and later crossed paths with Lady Lumera. After his father's death, Fardak assumed the leadership of his tribe, starting to manage tribal affairs. Nonetheless, he spent three months each year in the capital—more specifically, in Lady Lumera's library.

In the seventh year of [player.name]'s regency, Lumera and Fardak married, a rare and joyous event that sparked grand celebrations across the empire. Fardak's tribe, too, rejoiced in this union, crafting numerous stone sculptures and erecting a grand white stone altar in honor of Lumera, renowned for her wisdom and passion for books. Legend has it that Lumera herself insisted on two elements in all her sculptures: a book and a star.

Following their wedding, Lumera and Fardak started their migratory journey together. Every year, they spent three months together in Fardak's palace, another in Lumera's palace—specifically, that of her adoptive father [player.name]'s—and the remaining six months apart in their respective palaces. This matrimonial routine mirrored the movements of the celestial bodies, as their corresponding constellations graced the night sky for six months each year, visible to the naked eye.

Whether this extraordinary union brought joy to them remains a mystery to us, distant observers from a millennium later, but they seemed genuinely content during their time. A vast, or rather, an immense correspondence between the couple has been uncovered so far, detailing every facet of their lives during the six months they spent apart. It is said that the messengers shuttling between their royal residences even blazed a new trail that endures to this day.

Fardak's ascension was slightly later than Lumera's. Astronomical records indicate that the Fardak constellation joined Lumera's celestial company two decades later. During those intervening years, Fardak dutifully fulfilled his duties as the tribal leader, overseeing the seamless assimilation of his realm into the empire before peacefully passing away in his sleep at a ripe old age. The appearance of the Fardak constellation aligns almost perfectly with the documented demise of King Fardak in history. People of that era interpreted the constellation as a man wearing a crown, gazing towards Lumera—a depiction that likely resonated with Fardak's desire. Perhaps before leaving the world, his beloved Lumera whispered to him, 'Fear not, my dear. Our love shall endure for eternity.'

The two constellations shining upon us narrate tales from a thousand years past—tales of love, duty, and passion... inscribed in the heavens by the stars. As an astronomer, I am deeply honored to offer my humble insights on the constellations of Lumera and Fardak, especially as my modest contribution draws this symposium to a close. Once again, my heartfelt gratitude extends to the organizers and the generous sponsor, Double Cross Technologies, for making this enlightening gathering possible."

Ms. Hajur's presentation received a warm round of applause. As Ms. Hajur was about to leave the venue, an unexpected turn of events unfolded: The young scholar, who had repeatedly interrupted the presentations, made a return to the conference hall, accompanied by a group of experts, including the representative from Double Cross Technologies, Mr. Bitter Wine, Professor Mimona, and others.

"Let's not rush to conclude this symposium without hearing from this young man," Professor Mimona proposed, "Honestly, it could be quite enlightening."

Even though the agenda was to conclude the conference with a banquet, all attendees agreed to listen to what the young scholar had to share.

The final impromptu presentation of the symposium was delivered by [player.name], a history enthusiast and amateur writer, titled "The Rectified World."

"Hello, everyone. I've been eager to speak at this conference, but it seems not everyone in academic circles welcomes disruptive facts. Well, my name is [player.name], a gift from my history-loving mother. Among all historical figures, she held a special admiration for [player.name], and because of my name, my friends nicknamed me 'Regent.' Girls named 'Adila' would ask me where they could find their dragon, while those named 'Maggie' wouldn't give me the time of day...

Here, as a history enthusiast and [player.name] himself, I'm earnestly asking to consider this question: What exactly did [player.name] set right?

Sure, we could talk about all the details that were fixed. Over the past four days, we've touched on so many changes, like how our world no longer has the Supreme Sultan, dragons, gods, jinns, slavery, or noble privileges. The world that [player.name] set right is essentially the world we're living in today.

"We've been accepting this fact in retrospect. We assume that if these things don't exist in the world today, they didn't exist a thousand years ago either. We brush off ancient records related to these elements, calling them fabrications because of 'the limitations of knowledge back then.' But what if this 'ordinary' world we're used to is precisely the outcome of a certain miracle? If we see things this way, we'll naturally reach an inevitable conclusion, don't you agree?"

Yes, here's the conclusion. [player.name] reshaped the world into what we see today. He banished all oppressors that used to haunt the ancient world, whether they were mortals or higher beings. He forbade any mystical forces; he forced mortals to rely on their own strength to survive; he uprooted all sources of prayer; he eradicated all oppressive traditions.

And because of all that, we're now in a safe and 'dull' world where we can rely on ourselves and truly live like humans. We have to rely on our own strength, so we've replaced divine power with technology. We have to treat each other as equals, so we've come together in nations, ruling with caution. We've figured out how to approach tomorrow with good sense and logic, because we grew up in a yesterday that [player.name] set right."

Let's be real: the world we live in today is exactly the result of a miracle orchestrated by [player.name]. He gained unfathomable power and thereby saw firsthand what would have happened if he hadn't 'set things right.' Without such foresight, he might have dismissed the magician, who would later draw the empire into her cruel game, just like in that video game! Without his intervention, the pregnant Sadani would've been drowning in fear and despair, Lady Arumina would've missed her perfect match, and Sirshana would've run away from his responsibilities instead of facing them with courage... On the other hand, [player.name] graciously allowed the last whispers of the mystic age to linger around him—Hassan's mysterious longevity, Lumera's merging with the stars, and even perhaps assistance from Iman and Badriyyah. Isn't Lady Mahir's masterpiece, 'The Sealed Door,' the best proof of that?

It's only when we acknowledge that all these oddities were actually orchestrated by [player.name] that things start to make sense.

I understand, you might think I'm spouting nonsense because you're dazzled by the marvels he brought about. You don't buy into the idea that humans can predict the future, and you scoff at the notion of dragons and the Stars... Well, you're welcome to stick to your beliefs, but I'm standing firm in my conclusion.

[player.name] is the one who set things right. He's the real architect of this very world. I mean, seriously! His name is [player.name], a weird name that never showed up in history before him! Haven't you ever thought about that?

Well, that's my take, and now I'm off to enjoy a meal on the house. Thanks, everyone."

Girls named 'Adila' would ask me where they could find their dragon, while those named 'Maggie' wouldn't give me the time of day...

Here, as a history enthusiast and [player.name] himself, I'm earnestly asking to consider this question: What exactly did [player.name] set right?
